document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify new genetic susceptibility loci for invasive epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) by performing a comprehensive meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (GWAS). The investigation included data from general population EOC cases and controls, as well as BRCA1/2 mutation carriers. Six novel EOC susceptibility loci were discovered, and their potential functional roles were characterized through eQTL analysis, epigenetic profiling, gene expression and DNA copy number assessments, and in vitro transcriptional assays, with the ultimate goal of improving EOC risk prediction.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic Risk Factor Identification and Functional Genomics Analysis (via Genome-Wide Association Studies, Meta-analysis, and In Vitro Transcriptional Assays)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on identifying genetic risk factors for EOC, not a therapeutic intervention. A meta-analysis of approximately 11-11.4 million genetic variants was performed using data from 15,397-15,437 EOC cases (including 9,627 serous EOC), 30,816-30,845 controls, 15,252 BRCA1 mutation carriers (2,462 with EOC), and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers (631 with EOC). Genome-wide significance for associations was set at p<5	10^-8. Functional analyses included gene expression analysis for 91 coding genes and mRNA expression for 316 complete tumors (Z-score threshold of 2), DNA copy number analysis for 481 serous EOC samples, and an in vitro luciferase reporter assay performed by co-transfecting 800 ng of luciferase constructs and 50 ng of pRL-TK Renilla into 8 	 10^4 iOSE4 normal ovarian cells. Methodological details included sample exclusion for genotyping call rate <95% and SNP exclusion based on imputation accuracy (r^2 <0.25-0.3) or minor allele frequency (MAF <0.005-0.01). Imputation utilized 90 MCMC iterations and specific buffer regions. No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic treatment were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). CFU assay medium contained 100 ng/mL recombinant murine stem cell factor, 10 ng/mL recombinant murine interleukin-3, 10 ng/mL recombinant human interleukin-6, and 3 U/mL human erythropoietin, with endothelial cell assays using 100 ng/mL vascular endothelial growth factor. In vivo analysis included mouse embryos at E10.0, E11, E12, E14, with fractionation of endothelial cells based on CD61 expression (CD61 high, CD61 low, and CD61 − subpopulations). document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Refined machine learning-derived predictive score; Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Stratified subclinical atherosclerosis risk subgroups and predicted atherosclerosis progression; associated with CVD risk.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Stratified combined SLE-P/SLE-NP cohorts (n=142) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.84. Predicted 3-year atherosclerosis progression in female postpubertal patients with juvenile-onset SLE (n=36) with an AUC of 0.79. Identified distinct high and low subclinical atherosclerosis risk subgroups in a 'real-world' setting of unscanned adult patients with SLE (n=38). Showed high accuracy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stratification of subclinical atherosclerosis risk and prediction of its progression in female SLE patients; comprehensive assessment of CVD risk incorporating key metabolomic and clinical indicators.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined cohorts of SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, postpubertal patients with juvenile-onset SLE (for 3-year progression prediction), unscanned adult SLE patients in a 'real-world' setting; subclinical plaque status and atherosclerosis progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Could improve CVD risk assessment/management in female patients with SLE across age, identify patients for enhanced CVD risk monitoring/treatment, and potentially guide lifestyle and clinical management by highlighting modifiable metabolites. Provides highly accurate prediction for plaque status and CVD risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Key and significant metabolite hits within the tryptophan pathway (pathway significantly influenced by hemp fiber supplementation, p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main metabolite of serotonin, often used as an indicator of serotonin turnover.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-dose hemp fiber supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects altered serotonin metabolism and activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for a two-phase randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigating the efficacy and acceptability of high-frequency, low-load Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) in UK military personnel with lower limb musculoskeletal injuries where persistent pain is the primary limiting factor. Phase One will compare 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) BFR-RT over one week to determine the most effective and acceptable pressure for pain reduction. Phase Two will then compare this optimal BFR-RT protocol against usual care over three weeks to evaluate its impact on pain modulation, function, and other rehabilitation outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) compared to standard rehabilitation (usual care).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Phase One involves 7 BFR-RT sessions over 5 days (1 week) comparing 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) (n=28). Each session for the affected limb includes unilateral leg press and knee extension, performed at 20% of 1-Repetition Maximum (1RM) with a protocol of 1 set of 30 repetitions followed by 3 sets of 15 repetitions, with 30-second rest between sets (continuous inflation) and a 3-minute reperfusion period between exercises. Phase Two involves 21 BFR-RT sessions over 15 days (3 weeks) for the BFR group (n=26), utilizing the optimal LOP determined in Phase One. The control group in Phase Two receives usual care. The study aims to compare high vs. low BFR pressures (40% vs. 80% LOP) and their acceptability, but as this is a protocol document, no dose-response results are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of consuming cow's milk versus an energy-matched carbohydrate solution on recovery markers and performance in twenty female team-sport athletes following repeated simulated team games (STGs). The findings indicated that 500 mL of milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function (peak torque for knee extension and flexion), sprint performance (5m and 10m), and perceptions of stress, and helped reduce muscle soreness and tiredness, particularly after the first STG. However, for many other physiological and performance markers (e.g., CK, hsCRP, LOOHs, PCs, CMJ, HR, RPE), the effects were mostly unclear or trivial, with milk showing no clear benefit after the second STG.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional intervention (consumption of cow's milk vs. an energy-matched carbohydrate solution) combined with a multi-stage physical activity protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 500 mL of either cow's milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g protein, 25.5 g carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat) or an energy-matched carbohydrate solution (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 53.6 g carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat) immediately following each of two simulated team games (STG1 and STG2). The 17 g protein from milk was noted to be below the recommended 20 g threshold for maximal protein synthesis stimulation. The exercise protocol involved two ~30 minute halves of intermittent running with sprints, agility, and jumps, separated by a 10-minute half-time, with a 48-hour recovery period between STG1 and STG2. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the nutritional interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Benefit for MILK (possible-likely; ES = 0.40 to 0.58) following STG1. Overall positive effect of milk on post-exercise muscle function was small to moderate, but performance remained below baseline at 96 h. A within-group decrease was observed from STG1 to STG2, but between-group (MILK vs. CHO) comparisons were unclear. Average 5m sprint time was ~1.37s during STG, slower than isolated sprints (~1.20s).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of explosive power, acceleration, and short-distance speed.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery from repeated simulated team games (STGs), within-group changes from STG1 to STG2, and between-group comparison of MILK vs. CHO.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Directly indicates recovery of speed and acceleration, which are vital components of team-sport performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of post-exercise milk consumption (500 mL) versus an energy-matched carbohydrate drink on recovery from a repeated sprinting and jumping protocol in female team-sport athletes. The strenuous protocol successfully induced muscle damage, leading to post-exercise decreases in muscle function (peak torque, countermovement jump, sprint performance, rate of force development) and increases in subjective muscle soreness and tiredness. Milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function, particularly for peak torque (knee extension/flexion at 180°/s) and countermovement jump height, and reduced perceived stress (DALDA B) at various time points (24h, 48h, 72h) post-exercise. The study concluded that milk may be a valuable recovery intervention for female team-sport athletes following this type of exercise, although its effects on serum creatine kinase, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, reactive strength index, and some sprint performances were unclear.

The milk protein dose (17g) was noted to be potentially suboptimal for maximal protein synthesis compared to other studies. No dose-response comparisons were conducted, as a single volume of 500 mL was used for both interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study protocol investigates the effects of early spironolactone therapy on exercise capacity, clinical worsening, and vascular inflammation in 70 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without right ventricular failure. It aims to assess changes in functional performance (6-minute walk distance, VO2 max), plasma markers of vascular inflammation, gene expression profiles in PBMCs and PAECs, neurohormonal axis activation (sympathetic nervous system, RAAS, sex hormone metabolism), and right ventricular structure and function using advanced imaging techniques, while also monitoring for safety biomarkers like serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Spironolactone therapy (Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Early treatment with spironolactone will be administered for 24 weeks in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial. The initial dose is 25 mg once daily, escalating to 50 mg daily after week 6 if serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine does not increase >50% from baseline. Dose adjustments and discontinuation are strictly tied to safety monitoring, including stopping if serum potassium increases to 5.3-5.9 mEq/L, discontinuing if it remains ">="5.3 mEq/L on two consecutive draws or immediately if ">="6.0 mEq/L, or if serum creatinine increases >50% from baseline. No formal dose-response comparisons are reported within this protocol, although drug-drug interactions with PAH-specific therapies were considered.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Change in placebo-corrected 6-minute walk distance will be measured at 24 weeks; the study is powered to detect an effect size of 0.9 for the difference in change from baseline between the spironolactone and placebo groups (at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05, with at least 84% power). This biomarker is known to significantly decrease with worsening NYHA/WHO functional class in PAH patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Assesses submaximal exercise capacity, functional status, and overall physical endurance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early spironolactone therapy in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without clinical right ventricular failure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary endpoint to evaluate improvement in exercise capacity and incidence of clinical worsening in PAH patients, and a predictor of mortality in PAH.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify new genetic susceptibility loci for invasive epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) by performing a comprehensive meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (GWAS). The investigation included data from general population EOC cases and controls, as well as BRCA1/2 mutation carriers. Six novel EOC susceptibility loci were discovered, and their potential functional roles were characterized through eQTL analysis, epigenetic profiling, gene expression and DNA copy number assessments, and in vitro transcriptional assays, with the ultimate goal of improving EOC risk prediction.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic Risk Factor Identification and Functional Genomics Analysis (via Genome-Wide Association Studies, Meta-analysis, and In Vitro Transcriptional Assays)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on identifying genetic risk factors for EOC, not a therapeutic intervention. A meta-analysis of approximately 11-11.4 million genetic variants was performed using data from 15,397-15,437 EOC cases (including 9,627 serous EOC), 30,816-30,845 controls, 15,252 BRCA1 mutation carriers (2,462 with EOC), and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers (631 with EOC). Genome-wide significance for associations was set at p<5	10^-8. Functional analyses included gene expression analysis for 91 coding genes and mRNA expression for 316 complete tumors (Z-score threshold of 2), DNA copy number analysis for 481 serous EOC samples, and an in vitro luciferase reporter assay performed by co-transfecting 800 ng of luciferase constructs and 50 ng of pRL-TK Renilla into 8 	 10^4 iOSE4 normal ovarian cells. Methodological details included sample exclusion for genotyping call rate <95% and SNP exclusion based on imputation accuracy (r^2 <0.25-0.3) or minor allele frequency (MAF <0.005-0.01). Imputation utilized 90 MCMC iterations and specific buffer regions. No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic treatment were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with higher risk, specifically for the serous EOC subtype, at genome-wide significance (p=3.0	10^-8 in meta-analysis for serous EOC); not significant for all invasive EOC (p=6.8	10^-6). The most significantly associated SNP was rs116133110.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: GPX6 encodes an antioxidant enzyme; while its specific role in cancer is not detailed, this locus contributes specifically to serous epithelial ovarian cancer subtype susceptibility.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Susceptibility to serous EOC in a meta-analysis including OCAC and BRCA1/BRCA2 carriers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an increased genetic predisposition to serous EOC; its incorporation into risk assessment tools can improve clinical risk predictions for BRCA1/2 mutation carriers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially reported as elevated; later found to be inconsistent and influenced by confounding factors
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially reported elevated in serum, plasma, and leukocytes of HD individuals, with plasma levels correlating with proximity to diagnosis. Subsequent studies failed to replicate these findings due to high biological variability and confounding factors (stress, depression, smoking, low weight, pollution, diet).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD) progression, oxidative stress, and confounding factors like stress, depression, smoking, weight, pollution, and diet.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Initially thought to be a disease severity marker for HD, but its high variability and susceptibility to confounding factors question its validity as a reliable marker of disease state.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the oxidative stress and genotoxicity in gas station refueling workers exposed to long-term, low levels of atmospheric BTEX in Nanning, China, comparing them to office workers. It found significantly higher BTEX levels in refueling areas, which, despite being generally below occupational limits, were associated with reduced antioxidant capacity (lower T-SOD and GSH) and increased oxidative stress (higher MDA and 8-OHdG) and DNA damage (higher micronucleus rate, tail moment, and Olive tail moment) in refueling workers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Long-term occupational exposure to BTEX (Benzene, Toluene, Ethylbenzene, Xylenes) compounds in gas station refueling workers, compared to office workers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Long-term occupational exposure to low levels of atmospheric BTEX, with refueling workers exposed for an average of 8.7 years. BTEX concentrations in refueling areas were significantly higher than in office areas (p < 0.001), with mean ambient air concentrations including Benzene (60.03 vs 16.86 µg/m3), Toluene (317.76 vs 89.93 µg/m3), Ethylbenzene (113.85 vs 12.09 µg/m3), m-xylene (40.91 vs 28.44 µg/m3), p-xylene (57.51 vs 10.62 µg/m3), and o-xylene (37.18 vs 15.67 µg/m3). These levels were generally below current occupational exposure limits, but fixed environmental monitoring may underestimate actual exposure. No specific dose-response analysis for individual BTEX compounds was reported in human subjects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in refueling workers compared to office workers (p = 0.025 to z = -6.047, p < 0.001); however, after controlling for confounding factors (age, gender, years of exposure, smoking, and drinking habits), 8-OHdG levels were significantly lower in refueling workers than in office workers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of oxidative DNA damage, reflecting lesions in DNA structure and indicating DNA adduct formation by free radicals.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Long-term occupational exposure to low levels of BTEX in gas station refueling workers compared to office workers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased oxidative DNA damage, potentially associated with genotoxicity and increased disease risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of total dietary antioxidant intake and capacity on body antioxidant mechanisms and exhaustive exercise-induced oxidative damage in ultra-endurance athletes. It examined physiological responses, including oxidative stress biomarkers (8-iso PGF2a, TOS, TAS, OSI) and lactate levels, during and after a combined cycling and treadmill exhaustive exercise protocol. Key findings indicated that higher dietary antioxidant intake was negatively correlated with pre-exercise total oxidant status and post-exercise increases in 8-iso PGF2a, while positively correlating with post-exercise increases in total antioxidant status and blood lactate concentrations. A higher dietary antioxidant capacity also positively influenced antioxidant defense and blood lactate removal (in both sexes) and running time to exhaustion (in males), but did not affect post-exercise heart rate recovery or perceived exertion.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Exercise and Dietary Antioxidant Intake Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ultra-endurance athletes underwent an acute exhaustive exercise protocol comprising 45 minutes on a cycle ergometer at 65% VO2max, immediately followed by a treadmill test at 75% VO2max to volitional exhaustion (median running time ~26-27 min, RPE 19). Dietary antioxidant intake was assessed using the Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP) assay, with a median intake of 16.6-17.2 mmol/day, categorized as moderate-to-high. The study focused on correlation analysis between habitual dietary intake and exercise responses, rather than controlled dietary intervention or dose-response comparisons for exercise intensity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. The study also explored genetic associations with cerebellar gray matter volume, linking several genetic variants to cardiovascular disease and other health indicators.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study characterized pediatric Philadelphia-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients with kinase fusions in Japan, identifying 29 such patients from a cohort of 373. These patients presented with distinct clinical features including male predominance (22/7), older mean age at onset (8.8 years), high mean white blood cell count at diagnosis (94,200/μl), and a high proportion of National Cancer Institute high-risk (NCI-HR) cases. Genetic analysis revealed various kinase fusions (ABL1, PDGFRB, JAK2, IgH-EPOR, NCOR1-LYN, CRLF2) and a high prevalence of IKZF1 deletion (16/22 patients). Kinase fusion-positive patients demonstrated inferior outcomes, including high rates of prednisolone poor response (44.8%), induction failure (12.9%), and significantly inferior 5-year event-free survival rates (48.6±9.7%) compared to fusion-negative patients, suggesting clinical similarities to Ph+ ALL and underscoring the need for advanced stratification and targeted therapies.

However, specific drug doses, durations, or detailed regimens for any treatment were not provided or directly investigated within this study; the heterogeneity of protocols was noted as a limitation. The study focused on clinical outcomes in relation to kinase fusion status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. ESCC patients underwent surgery or endoscopic resection, and IEN patients underwent endoscopic resection for sample collection, but no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were investigated, as the study's primary aim was diagnostic and prognostic marker development.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of significant difference indicates that APOBEC gene mutation status is independent of the cfDNA methylation-based subtyping in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screening in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells, primarily Nalm6 B-ALL, to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of panobinostat resistance and action. Key findings reveal mitochondrial activity as a driver of panobinostat resistance and SIRT1 expression as a critical determinant of sensitivity. Panobinostat treatment abrogates mitochondrial activity in ALL cells, contributing to resistance, while enhancing mitochondrial function (via rosiglitazone or SIRT1 overexpression) sensitizes ALL cells to panobinostat by activating the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. The investigation identifies the SIRT1-mitochondria-PMAIP1 pathway as central to panobinostat response and suggests that higher SIRT1 expression or mitochondrial hyperactivity could indicate patient benefit from panobinostat therapy. The study also details various methods used, including cell culture, gene modulation techniques, drug sensitivity assays, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and flow cytometry.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily investigated Panobinostat, a pan-histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, often in combination with genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening or SIRT1 modulation. Other HDAC inhibitors (chidamide, vorinostat) and conventional chemotherapeutic agents (l-asparaginase, cytarabine, 6-mecaptopurine, vincristine, dexamethasone, daunorubicin) were mentioned for comparative or contextual analysis. Rosiglitazone, a PPAR   γ activator, was used to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and enhance panobinostat sensitivity.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Panobinostat was frequently used at 10 nM for durations of 24 hours (for RNA sequencing, combination treatments) or 14 days (for CRISPR screening), leading to 60-80% cell death and significant proliferation inhibition in Nalm6 cells. Gradient concentrations were employed for drug sensitivity assays. Rosiglitazone was administered at 31.25 µM for 24 or 48 hours. Dose-response comparisons for panobinostat sensitivity were analyzed using Sanger GDSC1 IC50 data across 576 diverse cancer cell lines. document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in pre-transplant patients (mean: 533.50 ± 98.13 pg/ml) compared to healthy controls (mean: 1049.29 ± 150.42 pg/ml, p < 0.0001). Post-transplant patients showed recovery (mean: 878.87 ± 96.26 pg/ml), tending to return towards healthy levels. Levels in AR patients (mean: 629.50 ± 107.90 pg/ml) were significantly lower than transplant excellent patients (mean: 837.21 ± 124.72 pg/ml, p < 0.001) and healthy controls (p < 0.001). ITBL patients also showed significantly lower levels than transplant excellent patients (p < 0.01) and healthy controls (p < 0.001). matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential non-invasive, early diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for liver transplant complications (AR, ITBL) and effectiveness monitoring, reflecting disorders of glycolipid metabolism and overall liver function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reliable ALCs are used to validate flow cytometry data; no specific quantification of observed changes or normal limits are cited in this text.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Validates flow cytometry data and provides valuable insights into phenotypic and functional immune reconstitution; deviations are indicative of changes in overall immune status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. The key finding is that obesity largely explains the observed association between IR and AN, with no direct causal relationship found between IR and AN when obesity is accounted for, highlighting AN's utility as a non-invasive clinical marker for obesity-driven cardiometabolic risk and its ability to predict future Type 2 Diabetes risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating cardiometabolic risk factors and a diagnostic marker
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention or dose administered. Data was collected from 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children aged 6–17 years from a family-based cohort, focusing on associations and the utility of Acanthosis Nigricans as a screening tool for cardiometabolic risk factors, including extensive clinical tests and interviews on medical history, demographic, phenotypic, and environmental variables.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Skin (clinical assessment, visual assessment of epidermal thickening, primarily axillae, posterior neck fold, flexor skin surfaces, and umbilicus)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Clinical visual assessment / severity score (quasi-quantitative trait)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: correlated (positive with BMI, HOMA-IR, CRP, WC; negative with HDL-C, PFS); higher prevalence with obesity/prediabetes/MS
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Heritability of AN-q was 0.75 (p<0.0001); h² for AN severity score was 0.75 ± 0.11 (P < 3.6 x 10⁻¹²). Positively/significantly correlated with BMI, HOMA-IR, and CRP (p<0.05). Negatively correlated with HDL-C and PFS (p<0.05). Prevalence 33% in the study population. Severity scores range 0–5. Occurrence of AN increased by obesity status: normal weight (11%), overweight (53%), and obese (65%); by prediabetes status (47%); and by MS status (67%). Children with AN are approximately 9/10 times more likely to be obese/overweight, 6 times more likely to have MS, and 2 times more likely to have prediabetes. Phenotypic correlations (ρP) with CMRFs ranged from -0.35 (with PFS) to 0.66 (with WC). Genetic correlations (ρG) ranged from -0.57 (with PFS) to 0.79 (with WC). Obesity is a direct contributor to AN, which itself is a compound marker of complex cardiometabolic risk.

Its pathogenesis may involve activation of insulin-like growth factor-1 receptors or fibroblast growth factor receptors by excess insulin.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Observational study in non-diabetic Mexican American children, examining causal relationships between AN, obesity, and insulin resistance; association with obesity, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome (MS), and cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strong correlate of obesity and a marker of insulin resistance, associated with various cardiometabolic risk factors. It is a compound marker of metabolic risk and a valuable, simple non-invasive clinical tool for pediatric screening of cardiometabolic risks (e.g., Type 2 Diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia).

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Predicts Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression as strongly as plasma pTau-181. Most significantly associated with cerebrovascular disease. Individuals with AD had approximately two years of additional CognitionBrain aging (P value meta = 9.23 × 10−36). A standard deviation increase conferred a 34% increased risk (P value meta = 1.03 × 10−15) of a clinically relevant two-point increase in CDR-SB within five years. Significantly predicted brain volume in multiple AD-sensitive regions. Had the highest adjusted hazard ratio (1.57; P = 8.95 × 10−3) for dementia progression among AD biomarkers. A standard deviation increase (approximately four years) in brain age gap conferred between 15-50% increased all-cause mortality risk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects accelerated biological aging and potential dysfunction of the brain and vascular system; predicts molecular brain aging and brain aging phenotypes related to cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Human lifespan aging, specifically for the brain and vasculature; association with cerebrovascular disease and all-cause mortality; Alzheimer's Disease (AD) status, cognitive decline, dementia progression, brain volume changes; neurodegenerative diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression independently from and as strongly as plasma pTau-181. Associated with increased risk of cerebrovascular disease and all-cause mortality. Stronger association with AD status, risk of future dementia progression, and brain volume changes in AD-sensitive regions. Provides molecular information about brain aging not captured by other approaches.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed predictive models using a novel machine learning pipeline to identify viable intrauterine pregnancies (Live Normally Sited Pregnancies, LNSP) in symptomatic women, differentiating them from combined adverse outcomes (CAO) such as miscarriage, pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). The models integrate serum metabolite levels (untargeted 1H NMR profiling) with plasma hormone concentrations (β-hCG and progesterone) and clinicodemographic data, finding that a composite biomarker provides superior predictive accuracy (0.79). The aim is to offer a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic test to reduce diagnostic burden and improve outcomes in early gestation by accurately identifying LNSP and excluding conditions associated with maternal morbidity and mortality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker identification and predictive model development using machine learning, untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, and hormone assays.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 370 symptomatic pregnant women (≤10 weeks gestation), presenting with abdominal pain and/or vaginal bleeding. A single blood sample was collected upon first emergency presentation; plasma was used for β-hCG and progesterone concentration measurements, and serum for untargeted metabolomic profiling. Nine key metabolite signals were identified. Random forest models were constructed and compared: a model using metabolite signals alone yielded 0.68 accuracy, β-hCG and progesterone alone yielded 0.71 accuracy, and the combined model achieved the best predictive accuracy of 0.79. Model performance was assessed using an independent validation cohort. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic accuracy for pregnancy outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were lower in Live Normally Sited Pregnancies (LNSP) compared to combined adverse outcomes (CAO), implying higher levels in CAO. Specifically, levels were increased in tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP), consistent with previous findings differentiating tEP from LNSP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Short-chain fatty acid, involved in energy metabolism and gut microbiome activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early pregnancy outcomes (LNSP vs. combined adverse outcomes (CAO)), particularly differentiating tEP.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a key metabolite in a composite biomarker for discriminating viable intrauterine pregnancies from adverse pregnancy outcomes; potential biomarker for differentiating tubal ectopic pregnancy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels were the most significant metabolite positively correlated for overweight/obesity in ICU patients, and elevated/statistically associated with obesity/overweight in general COVID-19 patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in amino acid, carbohydrate, lipid, and general metabolism pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 patients admitted to ICU or generally with overweight/obesity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with overweight/obesity in severe COVID-19 patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated Acetyl CoA levels were observed, resulting from increased cellular ketogenic amino acids (KAAs) and simultaneous fatty acid  -oxidation. This may slow carbohydrate breakdown and increase the availability of fatty acids for the TCA cycle.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key intermediate in metabolism, linking glycolysis, fatty acid oxidation, and the TCA cycle.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following FOPS ingestion, particularly during exercise and recovery, linked to KAA conversion and fatty acid  -oxidation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a shift towards increased fatty acid utilization for energy, helping to spare carbohydrate metabolism and optimize energy supply, thereby enhancing exercise adaptations and potentially improving health and sports performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: hiPSC, hESC, somatic cells, Mouse iPSC

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently up-regulated in early and late passage cells of both hiPSC lines (by ESI-MS e) and confirmed by Western blot analysis. All selected proteins were confirmed to be up-regulated in hiPSC and hESC compared to somatic cells. Found to be up-regulated in mouse iPSC (previous study). Included in a panel of markers confirmed to be differentially expressed in analyzed hiPSCs compared to somatic cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly stated, inferred as related to metabolism and potentially pluripotency. Involved in iPSC biology (up-regulated in mouse iPSC).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Proposed novel pluripotency marker identification and validation. Mouse iPSC biology and as a component of the hiPSC protein marker panel.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate novel pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs. Marker for iPSC state.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Leukaemia (AML), patient-derived xenografts, Inducible THP-1 cells, primary IDH1 R132-mutated purified AML blasts, primary IDH1-mutant AML cells in NSG xenografts, Glioma samples, cells transduced with shRNA (leukemic cells)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Synthetic lethal interaction (loss of function), Gene expression level, Protein inhibition sensitivity (IC50), Cell growth/viability, Engraftment

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lethal (when both IDH1 mutation and ACACA defect are present); higher (expression); increased (sensitivity); lower/defective (cell growth/viability, engraftment)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Defects in both are lethal to a cell; validated using gene targeting and patient-derived xenografts. Differentially overexpressed in IDH1-mutant AML (1.5–2.0-fold increase in gene expression) and glioma (P value=0.008) compared to IDH1 wild-type. Selective reduction in cell viability with 2 µM TOFA. Pharmacological inhibition caused reduction in cell growth (P=0.0001 vs -dox; P<0.0001 vs IDH1 wild-type +dox). IC50 1.1 µM in IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts versus 6 µM in IDH1 wild-type (P value=0.01). Knockdown by shRNA (P value=0.001) or CRISPR/Cas9 targeting (P value<0.001) caused growth defect. Reduced engraftment of leukaemic cells (P value=0.025) in xenografts. Knockdown efficiency by shRNA constructs was determined by quantitative real-time PCR and western blotting.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Rate-limiting enzyme in fatty acid synthesis, involved in metabolic processes. Acts as a synthetic lethal partner for IDH1 mutation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MiSL-predicted synthetic lethal partner of IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma; pharmacological inhibition with TOFA; gene knockdown/CRISPR targeting in IDH1-mutant AML cells, and targeted knockdown via shRNA lentiviral vectors in IDH1-mutated AML samples.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A bona fide synthetic lethal partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML with direct clinical implications, indicating a novel druggable target with potential antiproliferative activity for IDH1-mutant cancers, accelerating precision oncology.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between groups 55 days after starting the dietary intervention (p < 0.002).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of acute and long-term (16 weeks) heavy resistance exercise, with and without angiotensin II type I receptor blocker (losartan) supplementation, on serum C-terminal agrin fragment (CAF) levels in healthy older men. The findings indicate that 16 weeks of exercise alone did not affect CAF, but losartan supplementation led to an increase in CAF levels. Conversely, a single bout of heavy resistance exercise acutely lowered serum CAF. The study emphasizes drug interaction and the timing of blood sampling relative to exercise as crucial factors influencing CAF turnover and interpretation in neuromuscular research.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Heavy resistance exercise and Angiotensin II Type I Receptor Blocker (Losartan)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise (1EX) consisted of a single bout of unilateral heavy resistance exercise targeting the quadriceps muscles (5 sets of 12 concentric repetitions at 70% 1RM followed by 4 sets of 6 eccentric repetitions at 110% 1RM). Losartan (100 mg daily) or placebo was administered from Day -10 to Day 7 for 1EX. Long-term exercise (48EX) involved 48 sessions over 16 weeks (3 sessions/week) of progressive heavy resistance exercise, with loads gradually increasing from 67% to 86% of 1RM, 3 to 5 sets, and 15 to 6 repetitions. Losartan for 48EX was 50 mg/day for the first week, then 100 mg/day for the remaining 15 weeks. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either exercise or medication regarding biomarker outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single bout of unaccustomed heavy resistance exercise (unilateral leg extensions).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the expression characteristics of cuproptosis markers, oxidative stress indexes, copper metabolism, and hepatic fibrosis in Wilson disease patients, concluding that conventional chelation therapy significantly improves these abnormal markers and may reverse hepatic fibrosis progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Conventional chelation therapy using sodium dimercaptosulphonate (DMPS)

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive fine-mapping analysis of 150 breast cancer risk regions using dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls of European ancestry). It identified 352 independent risk signals, containing 13,367 credible causal variants (CCVs), with 191-205 high-confidence signals and 191 likely target genes. The investigation revealed that CCVs were significantly over-represented in active gene regulatory regions, open chromatin, actively transcribed genes, and transcription factor binding sites. The study also found signals differentially associated with ER-positive and ER-negative breast cancer, and prioritized target genes through integrated computational approaches like PAINTOR and INQUISIT, collectively explaining up to 23.6% of the familial relative risk. Furthermore, it included eQTL analyses in normal and tumor breast tissue to link genetic variants with gene expression changes, and explored the enrichment of CCVs with various genomic features and their impact on specific biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic fine-mapping, risk profiling, and functional genomics analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is a genetic association and fine-mapping analysis, not an interventional therapy. It utilized dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls) of European ancestry, analyzing over 639,000 genetic variants (SNPs, deletion/insertions, CNVs with MAF ">= 0.1% or 0.005%") across 150-152 previously defined risk regions. Methodologies included stepwise multinomial logistic regression, Bayesian approaches (PAINTOR), and a gene prioritization pipeline (INQUSIT). Statistical thresholds like conditional p-values (< 10^-6 for strong evidence, < 10^-4 for moderate) and False Discovery Rate (FDR 5%) were applied. eQTL analyses involved linear regression with specific covariates, and functional characterization included enrichment analysis with histone marks and TFBS motifs (FIMO p-value threshold 10^-3). No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were reported.
