document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially increased significantly with cadmium exposure, but showed clear and significant recovery/reversibility after reduction in exposure.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), increasing with urinary Cd in 1998, and exceeding age-adjusted cut points (14.6 mg/g creatinine in 1998, 21.7 mg/g creatinine in 2006). Post-reduction, mean levels in 2006 significantly decreased from baseline (p < 0.01) in highly polluted areas for both sexes. A clear recovery was observed, independent of UCd value, with no exposure-response relation in 2006 compared to 1998, and a significant decline in prevalence of elevated albumin (p < 0.05 for UCd > 5  5g/g creatinine groups).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A major plasma protein whose excessive excretion in urine (albuminuria) signifies compromised glomerular filtration barrier integrity and glomerular damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure and its reduction over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in a human population.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates glomerular dysfunction and damage. The Cd-mediated increase in urinary albumin excretion is a reversible effect, suggesting temporary damage that resolves after substantial reduction in exposure.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported in this document chunk. Intended to measure change.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported in this document chunk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Maintains osmotic pressure, transport protein.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General health monitoring.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of nutritional status, liver function, and systemic inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Generally, a transport protein and maintains osmotic pressure. Used to adjust calcium levels.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 120 minutes of treadmill running at 70% V̇o2max with or without carbohydrate ingestion.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not explicitly detailed as an indicator, but used to adjust calcium levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Protein deficiency decreases blood proteins, especially of albumin; low protein intake seems to decrease the rate of albumin synthesis (61). Decreased or elevated plasma albumin requires contextualization in athletes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major blood protein, maintains critical body functions, associated with human growth hormone (GH) concentrations (101)
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Protein deficiency, low protein intake, athletes training or competing, tracking athletes
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Helps gauge protein status; low levels may indicate insufficient protein intake. Requires careful contextualization for athletes as levels may relate to GH or other health issues beyond simple protein status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated a chemically defined, serum-free protocol for the in vitro transdifferentiation of pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells into functional hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) over five days. The research examined morphological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional changes, concluding that successful transdifferentiation, facilitated by extracellular matrix proteins like fibronectin or laminin, is independent of serum.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro pancreatic progenitor cell transdifferentiation to hepatocyte-like cells
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Clonal pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells were cultured for five days in a differentiation medium containing 100 nM Dexamethasone, 10 ng/ml Oncostatin M, 20 ng/ml HGF, 20 ng/ml FGF-2, 1% ITS+ (insulin, transferrin, selenous acid), 0.2% BSA, 4.4 mM nicotinamide, 1 µM copper sulphate, 30 µg/ml ascorbic acid, and 1 µg/ml heparin. Cells were grown on uncoated plastic, laminin-coated (2 µg/cm2), or fibronectin-coated (5 µg/cm2) substrata, with or without 5% FBS supplementation. The study primarily focused on the effectiveness of serum-free conditions facilitated by ECM proteins, rather than dose-response comparisons for individual components, finding no significant difference in transdifferentiation potential between fibronectin and laminin substrata.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: AR42J-B13 cells (gene expression), Cell culture supernatant of AR42J-B13 cells (secreted protein)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA expression) and Secreted Protein Level (ELISA)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: mRNA was upregulated to varying degrees. Undifferentiated cells did not secrete albumin, but clear albumin secretion was demonstrated in the supernatant of all experimental groups exposed to differentiation medium.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major protein synthesized and secreted by the liver, essential for transport and maintaining oncotic pressure, serving as a key hepatocyte marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pancreas-to-liver transdifferentiation under serum-free conditions, in response to differentiation medium.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a conversion towards a hepatocyte phenotype, confirming liver-specific protein synthesis and mature hepatocyte-like cell function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In normal range.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of renal function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following dietary intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates normal renal function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether pre-exercise ascorbic acid supplementation influenced antioxidant defenses, glucose metabolism, inflammation, and muscle damage in untrained healthy adults following a single bout of moderate-intensity cycling. Findings indicated that ascorbic acid supplementation reduced plasma Malondialdehyde (MDA) and increased Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP), while also modulating glucose levels and attenuating exercise-induced changes in albumin and total protein. While moderate-intensity cycling led to an increase in red blood cell Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) activity and low-grade muscle damage (Total Creatine Kinase), it did not induce systemic inflammation or lipid peroxidation. Ascorbic acid supplementation appeared to mitigate the exercise-induced increase in SOD activity but did not significantly prevent muscle damage or affect other inflammatory/damage markers such as hsCRP, LDH, CK-MB, GPx, or Catalase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supplementation combined with a single bout of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects received 1000 mg of ascorbic acid (or placebo) orally 5 minutes prior to a 30-minute indoor cycling session. Exercise intensity was set at 65–75% of maximum heart rate, which was predicted by an age-based equation. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either ascorbic acid or exercise intensity.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher immediately after exercise in placebo, returning to baseline by 30 minutes; no significant change with ascorbic acid supplementation
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated immediately after exercise in placebo (P<0.05) and significantly (p=0.049) returned to baseline at 30 min post-exercise. This increase was not observed with ascorbic acid supplementation, indicating no difference between pre-, post-, and 30 min post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Maintains plasma oncotic pressure and transports various substances in the blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute aerobic exercise (indoor cycling) in untrained healthy adults, with or without ascorbic acid supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute physiological responses to exercise, potentially related to fluid shifts or metabolic demand. Ascorbic acid attenuated these changes, potentially promoting adequate hydration status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, prospective observational study investigated whether vitamin D metabolites (25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) and Vitamin D Binding Protein (VDBP), along with their ratios, could predict preeclampsia (PE) in women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM). The study found that higher concentrations of 1,25(OH)2D, lower concentrations of VDBP, and elevated 1,25(OH)2D/VDBP ratios in the second and third trimesters were significantly associated with and predictive of subsequent PE, while 25(OH)D, the standard metric for vitamin D status, did not predict PE.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal Prospective Observational Study on Preeclampsia Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons. Biomarker concentrations and clinical data were collected at three gestational visits: V1 (~12 weeks), V2 (~22 weeks), and V3 (~32 weeks). The study enrolled 151 women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM) and 24 non-diabetic controls, rigorously phenotyped and free of proteinuria and hypertension at enrolment. The primary analysis compared 23 T1DM women who developed preeclampsia (PE) with 24 matched T1DM women who remained normotensive. A secondary analysis compared normotensive T1DM women with non-diabetic controls. The cohort was largely vitamin D insufficient or deficient.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not explicitly reported for PE prediction
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Circulating levels were measured and used for calculating free and bioavailable vitamin D concentrations. No specific effect on PE status was reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: General transport protein, contributes to maintaining oncotic pressure, and binds various substances including vitamin D metabolites. It's a lower affinity carrier for vitamin D metabolites (10-15%).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal prospective pregnancy study in women with Type 1 Diabetes and/or Preeclampsia, primarily used for calculating free and bioavailable vitamin D forms.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential modulator of vitamin D bioavailability and a factor in preeclampsia pathophysiology, primarily relevant for calculations of free/bioavailable vitamin D.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between iron status and renal outcomes, specifically progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), in 111 pre-dialysis patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven Diabetic Nephropathy (DN). It found that reduced serum transferrin is an independent predictor of ESRD, and identified increased iron and transferrin deposition in renal tubular epithelial cells of DN patients, suggesting a pathological role for altered iron metabolism in disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the prognostic value of iron status and related biomarkers in Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. Serum markers were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, immunoradiometric assay, and colorimetric methods. Additionally, histological analysis involved immunohistochemical staining for transferrin and Perl's blue staining for iron in kidney biopsy specimens from DN patients and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or active treatments were investigated; the study focused on correlation and predictive value.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower baseline concentrations in ESRD patients compared to non-ESRD patients. Lower concentrations observed in patients with lower serum transferrin quartiles and positively correlated with baseline serum transferrin (r=0.69, P<0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Maintains osmotic pressure, transports various substances in the blood. Main protein in human blood plasma, maintains osmotic pressure, and transports various substances; a marker of nutritional status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in T2DM patients with Diabetic Nephropathy (DN); T2DM with biopsy-proven DN.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels are associated with ESRD, indicating poorer nutritional status or liver/kidney dysfunction; positively correlated with serum transferrin. Indicator of nutritional status; lower levels suggest poor nutritional status, consistent with lower transferrin. Transferrin has a shorter half-life, making it a more sensitive marker for early protein depletion than albumin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Time effect (  time = 53.53 g·L⁻¹ [42.35, 64.72]), but no effect of Group or Supplement.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein, plays roles in transport and maintaining oncotic pressure.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During and after exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects exercise-related changes but is not significantly influenced by OC use or NAC supplementation beyond these acute exercise effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the work-recovery cycle and temporal variation of kidney strain, muscle injury, hydration, and inflammation biomarkers in 20 male sugarcane workers exposed to repeat heat stress and strenuous manual labor, despite a workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. It assessed biomarker dynamics across work shifts and different recovery periods (18h vs 42h post-shift). The study found marked cross-shift kidney and muscle strain, alongside an accumulation of systemic inflammation over the work week, with recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers being similar for both recovery durations. The findings highlight the importance of biomonitoring for occupational populations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study investigated the impact of occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor, specifically sugarcane cutting, on worker health, with an applied workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. This intervention included a maximum six-hour workday, hourly mandated rest breaks in the shade, easy access to cool water, and electrolyte solutions (300 mL bolis/bags containing sugar, sodium chloride, and potassium phosphate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 20 male sugarcane workers were observed over 4 days, covering work shifts and recovery periods (18h and 42h post-shift). Workload intensity ranged from 55-58%HR max, with daily average Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) between 26-29 °C, which was considered cooler than normal for a harvest period. Workers consumed approximately 8 L of water and four 300 mL electrolyte bags daily. Work shifts averaged around 5 hours, with Monday shifts showing higher workload intensity and heat stress. Recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers were found to be similar between 18 hours and 42 hours of rest (p > 0.27), indicating no significant difference in recovery duration comparison within this timeframe.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during work shifts) and lower (during recovery)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01), with greater increases observed during Monday work shifts (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein involved in maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting various substances; also an indicator of systemic stress or hydration status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Work shifts, particularly Monday work shifts, and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can reflect hydration status through hemoconcentration during work shifts and indicates systemic physiological response to acute exertion.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were uniformly undetectable or very low.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A major plasma protein; its presence in urine in significant amounts typically indicates kidney damage (impaired filtration).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout work and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates healthy kidney filtration function, suggesting no significant kidney damage or pathology resulted from the work-recovery cycles and heat stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Patients with atherosclerotic plaques (SLE-P) had higher albumin levels compared to plaque-free patients (SLE-NP).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein involved in maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting various substances; can act as an acute phase reactant.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Subclinical atherosclerosis in women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with the presence of subclinical atherosclerotic plaques in SLE patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between dietary vitamin intake, specific blood biomarkers, and muscle activation in 61 Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) patients. It found that albumin consistently predicted muscle activation in both arm and leg muscles. Vitamin B9 positively predicted leg muscle activation, while vitamin A negatively predicted it, with potential toxicity at higher intakes. The B6/protein ratio showed inconsistent effects, negatively predicting arm muscle activation but positively predicting leg activation. Among other blood biomarkers, PON1 positively predicted arm muscle activation, whereas BuChE and haptoglobin negatively predicted leg muscle activation. CRP, Vitamin C, and Vitamin D were not found to be significant predictors of muscle activation in this cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational cross-sectional study investigating dietary habits and biomarkers in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no specific therapeutic interventions or experimental doses administered. Dietary intake of B vitamins (B1, B2, B6, B12, folate, niacin), vitamins C, A, D, and E, and the B6/protein ratio were assessed using a seven-day dietary record, Food Frequency Questionnaire, and 24-hour recalls in 61 ALS patients. Blood concentrations of butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE), albumin, haptoglobin, C-reactive protein (CRP), and paraoxonase 1 (PON1) were determined. Basal muscle activation was measured using surface electromyography. Patients were under riluzole treatment as an inclusion criterion, not an intervention. No dose-response comparisons were made for treatments, but effects of estimated vitamin intake levels and ratios (e.g., B6/protein) on muscle activation were analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Positively predicted for both arm and leg muscle activation.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Arm muscle activation: r = 0.10-0.22,   = 0.18; Leg muscle activation: r = 0.10-0.26,   = 0.31. Higher levels associated with increased muscle activation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein involved in transport and osmotic pressure maintenance; a reliable indirect biomarker of nutritional status, muscle mass, and a potential biomarker of muscle function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clinical assessment of muscle function alterations or disease progression, and prediction of arm and leg muscle activation in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Most consistent positive predictor of muscle activation in ALS patients, indicating nutritional status and muscle mass.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the tissue origins of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in healthy mice using tissue-specific knockout models and its utility as a biomarker following paracetamol (APAP) overdose in both mice and humans. It found that cfDNA predominantly originates from blood cell lineages in healthy mice. Following APAP overdose, total and hepatocyte-derived cfDNA, as well as ALT and AST levels, significantly increased in mice (peaking at 8 hours), while albumin and bilirubin remained unaffected. In human APAP overdose patients, total cfDNA and liver-specific cfDNA (via methylation analysis) also significantly increased, especially in those with biochemical evidence of liver injury, demonstrating cfDNA's potential as a clinical biomarker for distinguishing overdose patients, assessing liver injury severity, and monitoring treatment efficacy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Paracetamol (APAP) Overdose; N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mice received intraperitoneal (IP) APAP at 350 mg/kg body weight, with samples collected at 8, 24, and 48 hours post-dosing (optimal cfDNA peak at 8 hours, liver damage most severe at 24 hours). Human patients presented with APAP overdose, with a subset receiving N-acetylcysteine (NAC) at 500-900 mg/kg body weight 20-40 hours after initial overdose. Patient groups were stratified by liver injury severity (normal vs. raised ALT); no specific APAP dose comparisons were performed in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Unaffected by APAP dosing. Normal range for serum albumin is 40–60 g/l.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein involved in maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting various substances, indicative of liver synthetic function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: APAP dosing in C57BL/6 mice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the absence of overt liver failure following APAP dosing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower liver synthesis function markers (albumin (ALB))

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main protein in blood plasma, produced by the liver, essential for maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting substances.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-liver transplantation in transplant, acute rejection (AR), and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL) patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired liver synthesis function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower levels in patients with HCC (P < 0.0001). Cirrhotic SVRs had higher serum ALB concentrations than cirrhotic chronic patients (P = 0.0053), but lower levels than non-cirrhotic SVRs (P = 0.0023). No difference detected between non-/cirrhotic chronic HCV patients. Lower levels associated with HCC risk (P = 0.0156–0.001). Demonstrated lower prognostic performance (suboptimal) for HCC risk compared to new predictors, showing nearly normal levels among SVRs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein synthesized by the liver, essential for maintaining oncotic pressure and transporting substances. Low levels indicate impaired liver synthesis or malnutrition. Indicator of liver synthetic function and severity of liver damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of liver functional class in cirrhotic patients. Comparison of HCC patients vs non-malignant patients; between non-/cirrhotic chronic HCV patients; cirrhotic SVRs vs cirrhotic chronic patients and non-cirrhotic SVRs. Non-malignant cirrhosis, chronic HCV patients, HCC risk, SVRs, and cirrhotic patients with mild fibrotic grades. Used as a criterion for the Child-Pugh score.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower concentration contributes to a higher Child-Pugh score, indicating more severe liver dysfunction and prognosis in cirrhosis. Lower levels indicate impaired liver synthetic function or malnutrition, common in advanced liver disease and HCC. Higher levels in SVRs suggest improved liver function. Associated with HCC risk, but had limited/suboptimal predictive power for HCC development compared to other markers, especially in SVRs with normal levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 36-hour survival training, which included moderate to low physical activity and complete sleep deprivation, on oxidative stress and muscle damage biomarkers in young, healthy men. The training impaired enzymatic antioxidant defense (GPx, SOD), increased lipid peroxidation (LHs), and induced muscle damage (CK). A subsequent 12-hour recovery period, including overnight sleep, was found to be sufficient to normalize these markers and restore blood prooxidant-antioxidant homeostasis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Survival Training (combined with moderate to low intensity physical activity and sleep deprivation)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 36-hour survival training regimen for young, healthy men, involving moderate to low physical activity such as a 12-km march, 6 hours of rowing, 4 hours of kayaking, running, swimming, climbing, solving special tasks, and navigation in wild terrain. Ambient temperatures ranged from 8°C at night to 30°C during the day. The average heart rate was 80-90 beats/min (40-45% age-predicted HR max), with individual variations from 70-80 beats/min during march to 120-130 beats/min during rowing or kayaking. Participants experienced complete sleep deprivation and consumed approximately 3800 ± 120 kcal daily. This was followed by a 12-hour recovery period, including overnight sleep. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes documented at any of the analyzed time points.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A major plasma protein with antioxidant properties, crucial for maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting various substances.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During 36-hour survival training with sleep deprivation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its stability suggests no dehydration, hemoconcentration, or significant liver dysfunction experienced by participants.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing

Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased ~10% (ranging from 10-14%) during the short recovery period (SRecover), returning to basal levels during long recovery (LRecover). The increase occurred at the same ratio as creatinine in response to exercise, though with a slight delay.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major blood protein, sensitive marker of volemia and fluid balance, related to hydration status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol induced metabolic stress, observed during short and long recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with metabolic stress and hydration changes; confirms changes in blood volume/volemia, potentially indicating a last escape of water from the blood in response to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An increase in the levels of nonenzymatic plasma antioxidants (albumins) was observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The most abundant protein in plasma, serving as a carrier molecule and possessing antioxidant properties.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy nonathletes (n=10) after a single WBC session (-130°C, 3 min) with no exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to enhanced systemic antioxidant capacity and overall plasma stability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No differences observed between groups following 12 weeks of supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The most abundant protein in human blood plasma, important for maintaining osmotic pressure, transporting substances, and acting as a protein reserve.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed before and after the 12-week supplementation period of daily protein combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of nutritional status, liver function, and systemic inflammation. Used to check protein intake and renal function, with no adverse effects noted.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No exercise effect was shown for albumin-adjusted calcium in the PBO trial (P = 0.871). No immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding observed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In normal range, but with a tendency for reduction in the verum group while increasing in the placebo group; difference between groups reduced (p = 0.083, ES = 0.521).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of renal function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following dietary intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates normal renal function, with a tendency for improvement in the verum group.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased from day 7 to day 14 in cisplatin-injured rats. Was not significantly greater than background levels in rats that received cell therapy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of albuminuria, reflecting kidney damage (impaired reabsorption of albumin).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of albuminuria in cisplatin-injured nude rats treated with CD133+ or CD133- cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher ratio indicates increased albuminuria and kidney injury. Absence of significant increase in cell-treated groups indicates amelioration of injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Remained constant during rest, but increased significantly by ~16-fold (1600%) (from 0.16  1 0.03 to 2.47  1 0.41  5mol/L; p < .001; effect size = 1.4) in response to CCombat exercise. It dropped during short recovery and reached basal levels within 48 hours (long recovery). Microalbuminuria (MA) ranged from 0.45 to 4.5  5mol over a 24-hour period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Assesses kidney permeability to albumin, reflecting changes in glomerular filtration caused by exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intensive CCombat exercise and subsequent hydration status changes, observed during short and long recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as an early, sensitive, easy, and inexpensive biomarker for evaluating hydration status changes and acute kidney impairment during intensive exercise, potentially mitigating chronic renal dysfunction and aiding human performance assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Prevalence rate was 36.3%. Positively correlated with cIMT (P < 0.05) and identified as a risk factor for carotid intima-media thickening (P < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Gene targeting using TALENs, in vitro human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation, and in vivo mouse embryo analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GATA2w/eGFP reporter was generated in H1 hESCs via gene editing (TALENs, electroporation of 1 μg linearized vector and 2.5 μg of each TALEN plasmid into 1 × 10^6 H1 cells, puromycin selection at 0.5 μg/mL, and Cre recombinase (400 ng per 1 × 10^6 cells) for cassette removal). In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). CFU assay medium contained 100 ng/mL recombinant murine stem cell factor, 10 ng/mL recombinant murine interleukin-3, 10 ng/mL recombinant human interleukin-6, and 3 U/mL human erythropoietin, with endothelial cell assays using 100 ng/mL vascular endothelial growth factor. In vivo analysis included mouse embryos at E10.0, E11, E12, E14, with fractionation of endothelial cells based on CD61 expression (CD61 high, CD61 low, and CD61 − subpopulations). No specific dose-response comparisons for differentiation conditions or therapeutic interventions were reported beyond qualitative observations of effect.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: GATA2/eGFP+ HECs (sorted from hESC blood differentiation at day 8).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Enriched in the eGFP+ cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Critical gene for normal function of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) or HSC niche.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Transcriptome analysis of GATA2/eGFP+ HECs during hESC blood differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its enrichment indicates a functional hematopoietic stem cell characteristic in GATA2/eGFP+ HECs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated urinary proteins responsive to acute eccentric calf-raise exercise in healthy males, identifying an N-terminal fragment of titin. The urinary titin fragment significantly increased 96 hours post-exercise and correlated strongly with established blood biomarkers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion), proposing its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Eccentric Calf-Raise Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute, single-leg calf-raise exercise (right leg) involving repetitive eccentric muscle contractions. The protocol consisted of 10 sets of 40 repetitions (total 400 repetitions) with 3-minute rest between sets, performed at 60 counts/min. Ankle joint range of motion was maintained between 20° dorsiflexion and 15° plantar flexion, with an exercise load approximately half the subject's body weight. Samples were collected before and up to 96 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant correlations between changes in urinary titin fragment concentrations and changes in serum ALD after acute eccentric exercise. Positive correlation between titin fragment and ALD at 48 h (r = 0.98, p < 0.01), and titin fragment at 48 h and ALD at 72 h (r = 0.94, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established marker of muscle damage, indicating muscle cell injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After acute eccentric exercise; exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences (p > 0.05) between time points (T1, T2, T3) nor between control and intervention groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in glycolysis, indicator of muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6 weeks of CrossFit® exercise with/without Tribulus Terrestris supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Muscle damage biomarker; TT supplementation had no significant impact on this specific marker of muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased the age gap association with dementia severity (FIBA-); expressed in astrocytes. Proposed as a CSF biomarker for AD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Expressed in astrocytes, involved in brain metabolism; proposed as a CSF biomarker for AD.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's disease, cognitive decline, brain aging mechanisms.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Involved in brain aging, but its contribution (or higher levels) decreases the model's association with dementia severity. Proposed as a CSF biomarker for AD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single bout of moderate-intensity continuous exercise, specifically at lactate threshold (LT) intensity, on renal hemodynamics and kidney injury biomarkers in middle-aged men. The main findings indicate that this type of exercise effectively maintains renal blood flow (RBF), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and filtration fraction (FF), and crucially, does not induce renal injury based on biomarker analysis. However, transient changes were noted in renal cross-sectional area and resistance indices, along with an increase in plasma noradrenaline in the recovery phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of 30 minutes of aerobic exercise was performed using a cycle ergometer, precisely at lactate threshold (LT) intensity (corresponding to 36% VO2max). The study involved middle-aged men (38 	 8 years) with well-maintained renal function (eGFR 	 60 ml/min/1.73m2). Renal hemodynamics and biomarker levels were evaluated at rest, immediately after exercise, and during 30-minute and 60-minute recovery phases. Participants were allowed free hydration during and after the experiment. No dose-response comparisons or chronic effects were investigated in this acute study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes at any point compared with before exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS), involved in the regulation of fluid and electrolyte balance and renal hemodynamics.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Continuous exercise at LT intensity and recovery phase.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Demonstrates that moderate-intensity continuous exercise does not activate the RAS system, which results in no significant increase in FF.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to characterize circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) in the plasma of patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) compared to healthy controls. Key findings include significantly higher plasma NfL and GFAP in RRMS patients, with GFAP also elevated in NMOSD patients. RRMS patients exhibited lower EV density and increased mean EV size compared to controls, with larger EVs (>150nm) primarily contributing to this. Furthermore, specific EV surface markers (CD29, CD31, CD40, CD44, CD49c, CD69) showed changes in RRMS patients, notably correlating negatively with NfL/GFAP levels and positively with time since the last relapse, suggesting their potential as biomarkers for disease stabilization and reduced immune cell activity, independent of current treatments.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing biomarkers in patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD) undergoing existing pharmacological treatments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 96 participants (52 RRMS, 19 NMOSD, 10 MOGAD, 15 healthy controls). RRMS patients received natalizumab (n=33), dimethylfumarate/glatiramer acetate (n=12), or no treatment (n=7). NMOSD patients were treated with rituximab, and MOGAD patients had various heterogeneous treatments. While existing treatments were noted, no specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated by the study itself. Biomarker measurements were performed using SIMOA, SP-IRIS, cryo-EM, Western blotting, NTA, and multiplex flow cytometry. The study concluded that current treatments did not significantly influence the observed EV marker levels or composition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detection of Alix was performed as an intravesicular marker, but no quantitative data on its level or change are provided; it serves as a general EV marker.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intravesicular marker, commonly used to characterize and confirm the presence of extracellular vesicles.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characterization of plasma EVs in patients with RRMS, AQP4-positive NMOSD, MOG-positive MOGAD, and healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the presence and helps confirm the identity of extracellular vesicles.
