document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers to differentiate Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases in human patients. The findings indicated that methylation levels of OPCML and HOXD9 in serum cfDNA were significantly higher in CCA patients compared to those with other biliary diseases. The study concluded that OPCML and HOXD9, especially when combined, demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity, making them promising differential biomarkers for CCA, improving diagnostic accuracy and preventing misdiagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based differential diagnosis using cfDNA methylation analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on evaluating serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 as diagnostic biomarkers. Methylation levels were quantified using methylation-sensitive high-resolution melting (MS-HRM) assay on bisulfite-modified serum cfDNA (20 µL, <1 µg), with detection limits of 1.56% (lower) and 50% (upper). Their potency was evaluated using ROC curves. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported, as this was a diagnostic study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Abnormally elevated in both CCA and other biliary disease groups; no significant difference between groups (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme indicative of liver or bone disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Ineffective for differentiating CCA from other biliary diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. The investigation focused on age-dependent differences in scaffold properties and their influence on BM-MSC osteogenic differentiation, rather than dose-response comparisons of a therapeutic agent.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) cultured on decellularized bone scaffolds and in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased activity and staining intensity in all BM-MSC/scaffold/DBCM combinations compared to controls. BM-MSCs (both young and old donor) cultured on old donor bone scaffolds or in old donor DBCM consistently showed significantly higher ALP activity and staining intensity compared to young donor bone or DBCM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key enzyme marker of early osteoblast differentiation and bone mineralization.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Osteogenic differentiation of young and old donor BM-MSCs seeded on human decellularized bone scaffolds from young or old donors, and in conditioned media derived from these scaffolds.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced early osteogenic commitment and differentiation, demonstrating superior osteoinductive capacity of older donor bone and its conditioned media.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational cohort study, conducted in a non-diabetic hypertensive population (N=14,393), investigated the prospective relationship between baseline and changing serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels and the risk of new-onset diabetes and impaired fasting glucose (IFG). The study found that higher serum ALP levels, both at baseline and with increasing levels over time, are significantly associated with an increased risk of new-onset diabetes and IFG. This association is particularly strong in individuals with lower total homocysteine (<10 µmol/L) or higher fasting glucose (≥5.9 mmol/L) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antihypertensive treatment (Enalapril ± Folic Acid, or other antihypertensive drugs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily oral doses of 10 mg enalapril and 0.8 mg folic acid (single pill combination) or 10 mg enalapril only, as part of the primary study, and other antihypertensive medications were used. This study was an observational cohort analysis of biomarker associations, not an intervention to modify ALP. It investigated the relationship between baseline serum biomarker levels (ALP, tHcy, FG) and incident diabetes, including a dose-response evaluation for baseline ALP levels and changes in ALP levels over a median follow-up of 4.5 years. Specific thresholds for effect modifiers were identified as lower tHcy (< 10 µmol/L) and higher FG (≥ 5.9 mmol/L).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean serum ALP: 100 IU/L (SD, 30.5), median: 96 IU/L; normal range: 20–140 IU/L. Per SD increment, adjusted OR for new-onset diabetes was 1.07 (95% CI: 1.01, 1.14), and for new-onset IFG was 1.07 (95% CI: 1.02, 1.14). Compared to ALP < 96 IU/L, ALP ≥ 96 IU/L had adjusted ORs of 1.13 (95% CI: 1.00, 1.27) for new-onset diabetes and 1.13 (95% CI: 1.02, 1.27) for new-onset IFG. A positive association was also found between ALP and change in FG levels (per SD increment, adjusted β, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.06). For changes in ALP levels, persistently high ALP (≥ 96 IU/L at baseline and exit) had an adjusted OR of 1.57 (95% CI: 1.36, 1.81) for new-onset diabetes, while increased ALP (< 96 IU/L at baseline and ≥ 96 IU/L at exit) had an adjusted OR of 1.97 (95% CI: 1.61, 2.42). The association was stronger in participants with total homocysteine (tHcy) < 10 µmol/L (adjusted OR, 1.24; 95% CI: 1.10, 1.40) or fasting glucose (FG) ≥ 5.9 mmol/L (adjusted OR, 1.16; 95% CI: 1.07, 1.27).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme involved in dephosphorylation, found in liver, bone, kidney, and intestine, playing roles in bone mineralization, lipid transport, and phosphate homeostasis. It is a generally accepted clinical marker of hepatic or bone disease, and it contributes to vascular calcification, endothelial dysfunction (by reducing nitric oxide bioavailability), and increased inflammation status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prospective relation with new-onset diabetes and impaired fasting glucose in hypertensive adults over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, particularly when baseline and changes in ALP levels are modified by total homocysteine and fasting glucose levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher baseline serum ALP levels and an increase in ALP levels over time indicate an increased risk of new-onset diabetes and impaired fasting glucose (IFG) in hypertensive patients. This risk is particularly elevated in individuals with lower baseline tHcy or higher baseline FG levels. Optimizing ALP levels may be a strategy for primary diabetes prevention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Significant increases after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.79). Increased after PS phase or intense soccer exercises; augmented following PS phase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in bone formation, liver function, and tissue repair processes; marker related to muscle damage and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after intense physical exertion (PS phase) or intense soccer exercises, including acute exercise 12 hours before blood draw.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased bone turnover, tissue repair processes, muscle damage, and inflammation resulting from acute exercise; adaptative changes in the whole organism and metabolism, informing optimal management of stimulus/recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased acutely, with a recovery trend
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased acutely during exercise (up to 50% in post-exercise samples), with a recovery trend during short recovery sessions. During long recovery, Athlete 1 showed a more pronounced decrease than Athlete 2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in liver, bone, kidney, and digestive tract.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, short and long recovery), systemic stress response.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Control for hepatic and biliary health; can indicate liver or bone issues, suggesting a systemic stress response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of liver or bone disease, relevant for monitoring general health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between routine plasma biomarker levels and recovery efficiency in elite professional soccer players over an entire eleven-month competitive match season, including seasonal variations and differences based on player position and cumulative match time. It concluded that a panel of AST, CK, LDH, and creatinine can effectively monitor recovery, adaptation, and overtraining risk, particularly in active positions like midfielders who may also be prone to iron and magnesium deficiencies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competitive professional soccer matches and regular intense training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An eleven-month competitive season, comprising 44 league and cup matches (23 autumn, 21 spring), typically one to two matches per week. Fasting capillary blood samples were collected 17-24 hours after each match. The study compared player positions (midfielder/defender vs. goalie/substitute, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups), noting significant differences in cumulative match time and physical demands. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for training intensity, but adaptation to increasing training load was observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varied over time (increase in autumn, decrease in spring)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were found between midfielder/defender and goalie/substitute groups. However, activity varied significantly over time: generally increasing in the autumn round (R=0.18-0.29, P<=0.05 for various groups) and subsequently decreasing in the spring round (R=-0.25 to -0.60, P<=0.05 for various groups).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in ATP metabolism, amino acid catabolism, and hydrolysis of fats across cell membranes, potentially leaking from skeletal muscles. It also indicates bone metabolism, liver function, and various other metabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout an eleven-month professional competitive soccer match season, including post-match recovery and regular intense training. Changes were observed across autumn and spring rounds, and were correlated with cumulative game time in midfielder/defender, goalie/substitute, midfielder, and defender groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suitable for recovery efficiency monitoring, its changes over time may indicate adaptation to training load. It can also reflect dynamic changes in bone turnover or liver function across competitive phases, and post-effort activity could signal early symptoms of vitamin B6 and niacin deficiency. Monitoring could help prevent overreaching or overtraining.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated alterations in serum levels of tumor, cardiac, liver, and renal function markers, alongside the IL-18 rs1946518 polymorphism, in patients with breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers (BC, CRC, PCa), and myocardial infarction (MI), compared to healthy controls. It revealed significantly elevated tumor markers (CA 15-3, CA 19-9, CEA, TPSA) in cancer patients, which serve as efficient early detection biomarkers. Cardiac markers (hs-cTnT, CK-MB) were specific to MI and largely unchanged in cancer. Liver and renal markers (ALP, AST, ALT, urea, creatinine) showed varied elevations, particularly in CRC and PCa, suggesting their utility as alternative diagnostic indicators. The IL-18 -607 C/A polymorphism was identified as a risk factor for PCa (AA genotype and A allele), and also showed an Odds Ratio of 1.75 for BC, while A/C heterozygotes were linked to increased CRC risk and C allele homozygotes offered protection against CRC.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker and Genetic Polymorphism Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study focused on assessing diagnostic biomarker levels and genetic polymorphisms in various patient groups and healthy controls, without any therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in CRC/PCa, unchanged in BC
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly elevated/significantly increased in Colorectal Cancer (CRC) and Prostate Cancer (PCa) patients compared with the control group (P<0.001). Unchanged in Breast Cancer (BC) patients compared to healthy individuals. Efficient biomarker for CRC (AUC = 0.85) and PCa (AUC = 0.91). ALP velocity appears to be a strong independent predictor of bone metastases and overall survival in men with increased PSA levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in liver and bone metabolism, a marker for liver health and bone activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Breast Cancer (BC), Colorectal Cancer (CRC), and Prostate Cancer (PCa) patients compared to healthy controls; liver injury and biochemical abnormalities in cancer patients; predicting BC relapse; predicting bone metastases and overall survival in men with increased PSA levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Efficient and valuable hepatic biomarker for early detection of CRC and PCa; also a good tumor marker for metastatic/different stages of BC. ALP velocity predicts bone metastases and overall survival in PCa. Less effective than CA15-3 for BC relapse prediction alone, but their combination is best. Unchanged in BC patients for diagnosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Fluctuated; generally unchanged over 10 weeks in female groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fluctuated, with activity varying by competitive distance and sex. No significant differences between female sprint and long-distance groups were observed over 10 weeks.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in liver, bone, kidney, and digestive tract, generally involved in various metabolic processes like bone formation and liver function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Evaluating usefulness in professional long-distance and sprint swimming, particularly during a 10-week preparatory training stage and post-physical effort recovery profiles.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potentially useful for assessing post-training effort, but not explicitly stated as part of the effective panel or as a specific performance/health indicator.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased after 4 months of treatment with soy peptides compared with placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in bone metabolism, liver function, and other processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy peptides supplementation for 4 months (in the context of Olympic female gymnasts).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potentially indicates changes in bone metabolism or overall health status related to long-term supplementation and physical activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of biomarker-based screening for the early detection of AL amyloidosis in intermediate/high-risk MGUS patients. It demonstrates that longitudinal monitoring, particularly in a cohort of 4742 MGUS patients with altered FLCr, significantly increases the timely identification of pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis, leading to earlier treatment, limited organ involvement, and significant recovery of organ function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening and monitoring strategy for AL amyloidosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Systematically integrated since 2012 in a single-center longitudinal cohort of 4742 MGUS patients, with a median follow-up of 4 years. Specifically, 1375 patients (28.9%) with altered FLCr underwent sequential biomarker monitoring. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focuses on a diagnostic screening strategy rather than a therapeutic intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 1 out of 22 (4.5%) pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis patients with liver involvement and in 2 out of 38 (5.3%) MGUS cases without AL, raising suspicion of initial pre-symptomatic organ involvement.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening for pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis liver involvement or other liver pathologies in MGUS patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of potential liver involvement in AL amyloidosis, suggesting the need for further diagnostic workup. In cases where AL was ruled out, it indicated conditions such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single case study (N=1) involved longitudinal observation over 6 months, with data collected across five study visits (M0, M1, M3, M4, M6) following four acute sexual violence (SV) events (including vaginal rape and revictimization prior to M3 and M5 visits). Data collection included surveys, blood draws, cervicovaginal exams, and self-collected diurnal saliva samples. Integrated support protocols were provided, but no active interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and applied a novel site-specific Multiple Reaction Monitoring Mass Spectrometry (MRM MS) method to map the human plasma glycome in 97 healthy volunteers (ages 21 to 84 years old). The research characterized 159 common glycopeptides, revealing 796 significant inter- and intra-protein glycan associations, many of which were previously unknown. The investigation further identified 13 glycopeptides associated with gender and 41 glycopeptides associated with age, including specific pro-inflammatory glycans and general IgM levels. A highly accurate age prediction model was successfully constructed and validated using a subset of five age-associated glycopeptides, demonstrating the potential for glycan biomarkers in clinical applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Glycan Profiling Method Development and Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the development and application of Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) mass spectrometry for highly precise site-specific glycan monitoring from plasma samples of 97 healthy volunteers (ages 21 to 84 years). No therapeutic intervention or specific dose was applied, as the focus was on characterizing the human glycome and developing biomarker and age prediction models.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly altered by gender (FDR < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery Method: Nano-omics integrative proteomics workflow utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas for glioblastoma (GB).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved inducing murine glioblastoma by stereotactic injection of 50,000 GL261 cells into the striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Liposomes (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000) were prepared at a final lipid concentration of 25 mM and administered intravenously at a lipid dose of 0.125 mM/g body weight (equivalent to 5 mg/kg doxorubicin-loaded liposomes) 10 minutes prior to blood collection in mice. In human validation, ex vivo nanoparticle corona analysis was performed on pre-operative plasma samples from 10 high-grade glioma patients. Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. Matched resected tumor tissue from human patients was analyzed by LCM-coupled LC:MS/MS. No specific dose-response comparisons for nanoparticle application or tumor cell inoculation were reported for therapeutic purposes, as the focus was on biomarker discovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as one of the 116 differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) across all three time points (D7, D14, D18), grouped within Clusters 4 and 6, which exhibited progressively increasing or decreasing plasma levels as tumour burden increased.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and applied a novel site-specific Multiple Reaction Monitoring Mass Spectrometry (MRM MS) method to map the human plasma glycome in 97 healthy volunteers (ages 21 to 84 years old). The research characterized 159 common glycopeptides, revealing 796 significant inter- and intra-protein glycan associations, many of which were previously unknown. The investigation further identified 13 glycopeptides associated with gender and 41 glycopeptides associated with age, including specific pro-inflammatory glycans and general IgM levels. A highly accurate age prediction model was successfully constructed and validated using a subset of five age-associated glycopeptides, demonstrating the potential for glycan biomarkers in clinical applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Glycan Profiling Method Development and Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the development and application of Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) mass spectrometry for highly precise site-specific glycan monitoring from plasma samples of 97 healthy volunteers (ages 21 to 84 years). No therapeutic intervention or specific dose was applied, as the focus was on characterizing the human glycome and developing biomarker and age prediction models.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery and characterization for intervertebral disc degeneration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved proteomic profiling and histological grading of human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissues and matched plasma from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy. IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood plasma; Intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue (specifically Nucleus Pulposus)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in plasma, higher in tissue
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In plasma, A2M was reduced in donors with severe degeneration (LFC = -0.79, AUC = 0.79 or 0.78), showing moderate accuracy in distinguishing mild from severe IVD degeneration (Log2 fold change below -0.5, p < 0.05). In IVD tissue, A2M increased with degeneration severity, showing an opposite trend to plasma, and tissue levels exhibited a weak correlation with plasma levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protease inhibitor with antioxidative and anti-inflammatory roles, inhibiting degradation enzymes and promoting protective matrix genes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Plasma and IVD tissue samples from individuals with severe degenerated IVD compared to mild degenerated IVD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential plasma biomarker for IVD degeneration progression, showing a moderate negative correlation with histological grade. However, it may not serve as a sole plasma biomarker due to complex and weakly correlated tissue changes. May play a protective role in the IVD, and its altered levels may impair disc function and contribute to pathogenesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Changes in stress levels are being investigated (in current study protocol); results not yet available.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes from baseline will be collected and analyzed; assessed via SalivaBio Collection Aid (Salimetrics) from morning collections.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of sympathetic nervous system activity and stress response; enzyme involved in carbohydrate digestion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week probiotic intervention; morning collection during baseline visit; probiotic intervention and post-intervention treadmill endurance testing in non-elite runners.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of stress; expected to indicate stress responses and potentially digestive function, in the context of probiotic intervention and exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the functional implications of heterogeneity in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), focusing on an endodermally biased pluripotent substate. Using a GATA6-GFP reporter line and single-cell functional/transcriptomic analyses, the research identified distinct, interconvertible hESC substates defined by differential expression of GATA6 and SSEA3. GATA6-positive hESCs, while retaining long-term self-renewal and pluripotency (often alongside OCT4 and SOX2 co-expression), exhibited a higher propensity and bias towards spontaneous endoderm and mesoderm differentiation, with downregulation of ectodermal genes. SOX17 was identified as a potential driver for this endoderm-biased substate.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Embryonic Stem Cell (hESC) Substate Characterization and Differentiation Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized the Shef4 hESC line, which was genetically modified with a GATA6-GFP reporter via Zinc Finger Nuclease-mediated homologous recombination. Cells were cultured in KO/SR on MEF feeders or E8 medium. hESC substates, defined by differential GATA6 and SSEA3 expression (e.g., 3+/6-, 3+/6L, 3+/6H, 3-/6+), were isolated by Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS). These sorted cells were subjected to single-cell cloning, gene expression analysis (qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing), high-content clonogenic assays, and differentiation protocols, including a spin-embryoid body (EB) system, without external therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for differentiation-inducing factors. The focus was on intrinsic marker expression and resultant lineage bias.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: EBs from hESC subsets; hESC fractions (cluster 8)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked upregulation in EBs from GATA6-expressing subsets (3+/6L, 3+/6H). Higher expression in cells within 3+/6H and 3-/6+ fractions (cluster 8).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Endoderm-associated gene, marker for more mature endoderm.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: hESC subset differentiation using spin-EB system; single-cell RNA sequencing.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bias toward endoderm differentiation, specifically more mature endoderm.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated a novel automatic time-resolved fluorescence immunoassay utilizing lectin-modified macromolecular lipid magnetic spheres (LCA-MMLs) for the rapid and accurate detection of the serum Alpha-fetoprotein-L3 variant (AFP-L3). The method aimed to improve the differential diagnosis of liver cancer from other liver diseases (chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis), demonstrating that AFP-L3 is a more accurate and specific biomarker for liver cancer diagnosis and prognosis compared to total AFP.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Assay Development and Validation for Liver Cancer
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The diagnostic method involved preparing lectin-modified macromolecular lipid magnetic spheres (LCA-MMLs) using lentil lectin derivatives (LCA-HQ, 2.5 mg), cholesterol (0.5 mg), and magnetic particles (0.5 mg). This was coupled with an automatic time-resolved fluorescence immunoassay for detecting serum Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and its variant, AFP-L3. The method demonstrated high AFP-L3 recovery efficiency (>90%) with no significant difference (p>0.05) compared to manual micro-affinity column methods, and an enrichment ability correlation coefficient γ=0.985. Clinical evaluation was performed on 1150 serum samples from healthy individuals, chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and liver cancer patients. The assay offers short detection time and automated operation, and as a diagnostic tool, no therapeutic dose comparisons were applicable.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in liver cancer patients and also in other liver diseases.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum levels were significantly higher in liver cancer patients compared to healthy individuals (P<0.05), and also elevated in chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis patients. Content in the hepatitis group was significantly higher than the cirrhosis group (P<0.05). The AUC (95% CI) for differential diagnosis was 0.743 ± 0.031, which was statistically less accurate than AFP-L3 (p<0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A general tumor marker commonly used for liver cancer diagnosis, but its serum levels can also be elevated in benign liver diseases like cirrhosis and hepatitis. Approximately 35% of primary liver cancer patients may have normal AFP levels (<400 ng/mL).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clinical diagnosis and differential diagnosis of liver cancer, chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and healthy subjects.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Less accurate and specific than AFP-L3 for the differential diagnosis of liver cancer, primarily due to its elevation in benign liver conditions and normal levels in a substantial percentage of liver cancer patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with HCC than in non-malignant patients (P < 0.0001). Chronic HCV patients had significantly higher AFP levels than SVRs (P < 0.0001). Cirrhotic patients in each group had higher levels than non-cirrhotic patients (P < 0.0001 for all). Levels in SVRs were significantly lower than in treatment-naïve HCV patients. Can remain within normal limits (≤ 10 ng/mL) in approximately 30% of HCC patients. Positively correlated with peripheral Cldn1/TGF-β (HCC, non-malignant cirrhotic, non-cirrhotic). Positively correlated with IL-12 (non-malignant cirrhotic) and with IL-10 and IL-12 (non-cirrhotic). Inversely correlated with sCD163 (non-cirrhotic). Demonstrated lower prognostic performance (suboptimal) for HCC risk compared to new predictors.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Glycoprotein produced primarily by the fetal liver and yolk sac; elevated levels in adults can indicate liver damage, regeneration, or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is widely used as a tumor marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment in HCV-related HCC patients and other patient groups. Comparison of HCC patients vs non-malignant patients; chronic HCV patients vs SVRs; cirrhotic vs non-cirrhotic patients. HCC prediction, DAA-SVR, chronic HCV patients, and non-malignant patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Commonly used as a tumor marker for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Elevated levels are a marker for HCC, also associated with active chronic HCV and cirrhosis. Although considered a 'gold standard' for HCC, its reliability may be compromised in patients with normal levels, particularly in cirrhotic DAA-SVRs, indicating a need for more specific predictors. Demonstrated considerable prognostic capacity (Fisher’s exact test: sensitivities 88–99.41%, specificities 82.14–97.92%), but showed suboptimal prognostic capacity in SVRs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the clinical utility of multimodal alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) profiling from cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and circulating tumor cells (CTCs) using a novel bead-based liquid biopsy platform for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The aim was to enhance diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring, concluding that this combined approach provides superior accuracy and clinical information compared to conventional serum AFP, particularly for detecting recurrence and stratifying treatment response and overall survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) treatments, including radiofrequency ablation (RFA), trans-arterial chemoembolization (TACE), surgical resection, and radiotherapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on biomarker monitoring of existing HCC treatments. Patients received individualized treatments based on clinical judgment, with samples collected after the first treatment cycle. No specific dose, intensity, duration, or dose-response comparisons were reported for any therapeutic modality.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene abundance quantification (qPCR) of AFP genomic DNA fragments

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in HCC patients, significantly decreased post-treatment in responders, reliably captured recurrence events, associated with shorter RFS (trend)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly greater diagnostic accuracy (p < 0.0001, AUC = 0.998) distinguishing HCC from non-cancerous individuals; median log10(2−∆Ct) 0.53 ± 0.12 (HCC) vs. -0.34 ± 0.10 (non-cancerous); post-treatment log change -0.18 ± 0.27 (responders) vs. 0.14 ± 0.12 (non-responders, p = 0.008, AUC=0.743); increased levels tended to correlate with shorter RFS (19.4 months vs. 27.6 months, p = 0.162, not significant), with increases observed at recurrence and decreases post-successful treatment; exhibited superior diagnostic sensitivity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A tumor marker for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that reflects tumor burden, activity, growth, angiogenesis, immune modulation, and cell turnover, derived from circulating tumor DNA.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis, prognosis, and longitudinal treatment monitoring in HCC; distinguishing HCC patients from non-cancerous individuals; assessing therapeutic response and recurrence-free survival (RFS); detecting recurrence.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Offers superior diagnostic capabilities and accuracy for monitoring treatment response compared to serum AFP; a reliable indicator for patient prognosis and recurrence monitoring; enhances overall HCC management.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Circulating Tumor Cells (CTCs) isolated from the peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) layer
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein expression assessment via immunohistochemistry and cell enumeration (AFP+ CTC counts)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: High specificity for HCC, detected only in HCC patients pre-treatment, detected only in non-responders post-treatment, strongly associated with adverse overall survival, higher counts in patients with ascites
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean 0.36 ± 0.67 CTCs/mL in HCC patients (none in non-cancerous, p = 0.114, AUC=0.628); post-treatment, average 0.63 ± 0.96 cells/mL in non-responders (p = 0.002, 36.8% positivity) vs. none in responders (AUC=0.684); 57.1% of patients with detectable post-treatment AFP+CTCs succumbed (p = 0.001 for OS); no significant RFS difference (p = 0.988); limited abundance and modest capture efficiency (~70%). Higher counts observed in patients with ascites but not correlated with metastatic burden.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents viable tumor cells providing genetic and phenotypic information, indicative of tumor burden, metastatic potential, and treatment response in HCC.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring in HCC; identifying non-responders; predicting overall survival; pre-treatment assessment for ascites; longitudinal monitoring during treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides high specificity for HCC diagnosis and identifying non-responders; strong indicator for adverse overall survival post-treatment; accurately reflects treatment outcomes; useful as an adjunctive marker, though limited by low abundance and detection sensitivity.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Limited sensitivity and specificity; no statistically significant difference for diagnosis; decreased levels post-treatment associated with better overall survival, but inconsistent trends for RFS; no correlation with pathological features
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Diagnostic sensitivity of 70.1% and specificity of 89.8% for overall HCC (>20 ng/mL), dropping to 49.3% for early-stage HCC (AUC=0.62), and 44% specificity when AFP>20 ng/mL without tumors; median concentration 6.73 ± 3.82 ng/mL (HCC) vs. 5.07 ± 2.53 ng/mL (non-cancerous, p = 0.538, AUC=0.564); post-treatment log change -0.07 ± 0.11 (responders) vs. -0.04 ± 0.07 (non-responders, p = 0.354, AUC=0.567); increased levels showed a non-significant trend for longer RFS (26.2 months vs. 21.9 months, p = 0.381); no correlation with tumor stage, multicentricity, tumor size, lymphovascular invasion, cirrhosis, or ascites.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A conventional tumor marker implicated in HCC growth, angiogenesis, and immune modulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Routine diagnosis and prognostic evaluation of HCC; monitoring response to cancer treatments; pre-treatment assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Limited utility due to low sensitivity and specificity, especially in early-stage HCC; poor discriminative and predictive performance for diagnosis and treatment response; not a reliable indicator of baseline pathological features or tumor burden.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Multiple metabolic pathways were enriched with hemp fiber intake.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolism of an essential omega-3 fatty acid, involved in inflammatory responses and cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hemp fiber intake, leading to enrichment of this pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates modulation of essential fatty acid metabolism, potentially influencing inflammatory processes and overall health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnosis of Sport-related Concussion (SRC) using proteomic profiling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from concussed and non-concussed collegiate athletes within 48 hours post-injury, with analyses conducted for acute (0-6 hours) and subacute (7-48 hours) phases. A highly multiplexed proteomic DNA aptamers assay targeting 1305 plasma proteins was used. The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly less abundant after SRC (P<0.05). After 6 hours post-injury, individual plasma SNCA showed an AUC of 0.875 (95%CI: 0.794–0.957); combination with EPB41 provided an AUC of 1.000.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the molecular relevance of GBA1 pathogenic variants (N370S and L444P) in Gaucher disease (GD) patients (GD1, GD3) on Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT), GBA1 carriers, and healthy subjects by analyzing glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb1), α-synuclein mRNA, total protein, and oligomer levels. Key findings included significantly elevated Lyso-Gb1 levels in GD patients and neuronopathic GD, substantially higher α-synuclein mRNA levels in GD3 patients and L444P carriers, but no statistically significant differences in total α-SNCA protein or oligomer levels between groups after multiple comparison adjustment. The research also explored correlations with disease severity, GBA1 variants, aging, and ERT impact, suggesting links to Parkinson's disease risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients (65 total: 47 GD1, 18 GD3) were treated with ERT. Doses varied, generally ranging from 15–60 U/kg, with an average of 30 U/kg bm/every other week. While Lyso-Gb1 showed a varied correlation with ERT dosing (the coefficient of determination (R2) for treatment response dropped to 0.16 for high doses >35 U/kg bm/every other week), no consistent dose-response comparisons were reported for all analyzed markers. Blood samples were collected during annual clinical follow-up visits.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Non-significant but consistently lower levels of AD biomarkers were observed when using stimulated saliva methods. Direct spitting should be avoided due to stimulatory effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the transferability and performance of European-derived Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS) across diverse global populations, demonstrating consistent associations with AD risk and biomarkers and improved prediction in non-European ancestries when including the APOE region, while also detailing the comprehensive methodological framework for generating these scores.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Application, evaluation, and methodological development of Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study developed and evaluated polygenic scores (PGS) for Alzheimer's disease (AD). PGS ALZ was derived from 83 independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) excluding the APOE locus, and an APOE-inclusive PGS was also generated. Associations were assessed across various PGS ALZ strata (e.g., 0–2% vs. 98–100% relative to 40–60% reference). Cross-ancestry polygenic risk scores (PRS COMB) were constructed using the Bayesian PRS-CSx method, integrating GWAS summary statistics from European, African American, Latin American, and East Asian populations, and evaluated across different sparseness values and both with and without the APOE region. Methodological details included stringent variant quality control (e.g., R^2 < 0.3 excluded), imputation with TOPMed reference panel, ancestry determination, population structure adjustment using principal components (first 14 PCs), and clumping criteria (P-value threshold of 1 x 10^-3 and R^2 of 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study found that while bone turnover markers (CTX and BAP) decreased in both K citrate and placebo groups, K citrate significantly enhanced these beneficial effects, particularly in a subgroup of patients with pre-existing low-grade acidosis (low urine pH and/or low potassium and citrate excretion). K citrate also improved urinary pH, citrate, and potassium excretion. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Potassium Citrate (K citrate) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Daily oral supplementation with 30 mEq of K citrate (in two tablets) for 6 months. This was administered in addition to daily calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹) for all subjects (K citrate and placebo groups). The K citrate treatment showed significant benefits in subjects with evidence of low-grade acidosis (low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH) compared to the placebo, with significant changes observed as early as 3 months. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported, and adherence rates were approximately 90% for both groups.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed accumulative increases, rising during matches (more in the second match than the first) and continuing into recovery. Athlete 1 spiked 275% compared to initial levels during long recovery, while Athlete 2 had a 1.5-fold increase. At long recovery, both athletes reached ~75 mmol/L, roughly 50% above the upper normal limit. Peak was found during long recovery, displaying a delayed response compared to lactate. The protocol-induced increase matched with an increase in urate in Athlete 2, but not in Athlete 1.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition Day (during matches and recovery, particularly long recovery).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a classic marker of exercise intensity, corroborating high-intensity competition and suggesting cumulative strain. Indicates metabolic stress and potentially different primary sources of ammonium production between athletes (amino acid deamination vs. purine cycle), with prolonged elevation suggesting incomplete recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated algorithms using serum biomarkers Amphiregulin (AREG), ST2, and REG3α to predict 12-month nonrelapse mortality (NRM) in patients with acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. The algorithms effectively discriminated NRM risk, with ST2+REG3α proving most accurate for Minnesota standard-risk GVHD and posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-CY) prophylaxis patients, while AREG alone was superior for Minnesota high-risk GVHD patients. These biomarker algorithms are valuable for enhancing clinical risk stratification, guiding GVHD clinical trial design, and informing treatment intensification or de-escalation strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT) and subsequent treatment for Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD); systemic corticosteroid treatment; JAK1 inhibition by itacitinib monotherapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients underwent allogeneic HCT and developed acute GVHD, receiving topical and/or systemic therapy for acute GVHD, including systemic corticosteroids or posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-CY)-based prophylaxis. Itacitinib was used as monotherapy in some cases for low-risk biomarker scores. The study focused on biomarker algorithm performance for risk prediction and treatment guidance, not specific therapeutic dose regimens or dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An algorithm containing only AREG more accurately risk-stratified patients with Minnesota high-risk GVHD. Serum concentrations were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and expressed in picograms per milliliter (pg/mL). Algorithms predicted 12-month NRM probability (0.001 to 0.999). AREG was an independent discriminator of 12-month NRM alone or in pairwise combination and remained a significant predictor when combined with ST2 and REG3α. The AREG algorithm created an 18% difference in 12-month NRM between risk groups. It stratified patients receiving systemic treatment for GVHD (12% vs 30%, P < .001) and patients with lower GI GVHD at diagnosis (8% vs 45%, P < .001). The AREG algorithm was slightly better than ST2+REG3α for patients with Minnesota high-risk GVHD, classifying 7% more patients correctly.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD) diagnosis following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT), specifically in patients with Minnesota high-risk GVHD, lower GI GVHD, systemic treatment for GVHD, and for general GVHD risk stratification.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictor of risk for 6-month and 12-month nonrelapse mortality (NRM) and overall survival (OS); prognostic biomarker superior to the Minnesota risk system for high-risk GVHD; aids in stratifying patients into low- and high-risk groups for NRM and OS; identifies patients at high/low risk for NRM; indicates suitability for tailored therapy for GVHD; appropriate for guiding GVHD clinical trial design and informing treatment strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated a chemically defined, serum-free protocol for the in vitro transdifferentiation of pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells into functional hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) over five days. document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively explores Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) as crucial mediators of intercellular communication, highlighting their dual roles in health and disease. It examines their potential as personalized diagnostic biomarkers across various conditions including viral infections, cancer, neurological, kidney, autoimmune, metabolic, and pro-thrombotic diseases. The document also investigates EVs as promising therapeutic agents, drug delivery vehicles, and regenerative therapeutics, discussing their involvement in disease pathogenesis (e.g., spreading misfolded proteins, facilitating viral replication) and their protective functions (e.g., neuroprotection, inflammation regulation, aggregate prevention, tissue repair). Challenges in EV isolation, standardization, and clinical translation are also addressed.
