document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screening in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells, primarily Nalm6 B-ALL, to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of panobinostat resistance and action. Key findings reveal mitochondrial activity as a driver of panobinostat resistance and SIRT1 expression as a critical determinant of sensitivity. Panobinostat treatment abrogates mitochondrial activity in ALL cells, contributing to resistance, while enhancing mitochondrial function (via rosiglitazone or SIRT1 overexpression) sensitizes ALL cells to panobinostat by activating the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. The investigation identifies the SIRT1-mitochondria-PMAIP1 pathway as central to panobinostat response and suggests that higher SIRT1 expression or mitochondrial hyperactivity could indicate patient benefit from panobinostat therapy. The study also details various methods used, including cell culture, gene modulation techniques, drug sensitivity assays, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and flow cytometry.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily investigated Panobinostat, a pan-histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, often in combination with genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening or SIRT1 modulation. Other HDAC inhibitors (chidamide, vorinostat) and conventional chemotherapeutic agents (l-asparaginase, cytarabine, 6-mecaptopurine, vincristine, dexamethasone, daunorubicin) were mentioned for comparative or contextual analysis. Rosiglitazone, a PPAR   γ activator, was used to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and enhance panobinostat sensitivity.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Panobinostat was frequently used at 10 nM for durations of 24 hours (for RNA sequencing, combination treatments) or 14 days (for CRISPR screening), leading to 60-80% cell death and significant proliferation inhibition in Nalm6 cells. Gradient concentrations were employed for drug sensitivity assays. Rosiglitazone was administered at 31.25 µM for 24 or 48 hours. Dose-response comparisons for panobinostat sensitivity were analyzed using Sanger GDSC1 IC50 data across 576 diverse cancer cell lines. No specific doses or dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for other HDAC inhibitors or conventional chemotherapeutic agents.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Nalm6 cells, REH cells, SEM cells

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased (by rosiglitazone + panobinostat); increased (by SIRT1 overexpression + panobinostat); decreased (by SIRT1 disturbance + panobinostat)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Rosiglitazone combined with panobinostat 'led to more apoptosis than control or either drug alone'; in REH cells, combination resulted in 'more cell death than that what was achieved by either drug alone (13.72% and 1.78%, respectively) or the addition of the 2 (28.93%)'. SIRT1 OE cells exhibited the 'highest proportion of apoptosis', whereas SIRT1 disturbed cells exhibited the 'lowest proportion of apoptosis' compared to control cells when treated with panobinostat.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined treatment of rosiglitazone and panobinostat, or panobinostat treatment with modulated SIRT1 expression in ALL cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased apoptosis indicates enhanced therapeutic efficacy and overcoming panobinostat resistance in ALL cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly higher with eIF3a silencing; significantly lower with eIF3a overexpression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly greater (p < .01) in eIF3a-silenced cells, and significantly lower (p < .05) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Programmed cell death, crucial for removing damaged or cancerous cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: eIF3a silencing or overexpression in CRC cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased apoptosis indicates induction of cancer cell death, a desirable therapeutic outcome, while lower apoptosis promotes malignancy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Gradual and late rise associated with PGD3 at T48–72 h. Elevated levels also observed at T24–48 h post-lung transplant in patients with PGD3 in previous studies. Temporal changes were significantly associated with PGD3 at T48–72h (before and after adjusting for multiple testing in the non-overlap weighted cohort).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell death marker; indicates apoptosis (caspase-cleaved cytokeratin 18).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-lung transplant reperfusion (T24–48h, T48–72h), associated with PGD3.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a phased onset of apoptosis and increased cellular apoptosis/tissue damage associated with severe PGD (PGD3).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the role of PPARγ1, specifically its K154/155 acetylation site, as a molecular switch in oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary adenocarcinoma tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and metastasis. Using in vitro cell models, in vivo mouse xenograft models, and human breast cancer patient datasets, the research demonstrated that K154/155 acetylation is essential for promoting tumor growth, de novo lipogenesis, and cancer stem cell characteristics, while also regulating cellular apoptosis and autophagy. The acetylation status was found to determine genome-wide DNA binding site selection, shifting from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) binding, and influencing transcriptional programs for growth factor signaling. Furthermore, gene signatures reflecting acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis (PASS1 and PASS2) showed predictive value for survival outcomes and distant metastasis-free survival in various breast cancer subtypes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Molecular mechanism investigation focusing on PPARγ1 post-translational modification (acetylation) and the functional consequences of genetic variants (wild-type vs. acetylation-defective mutants)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparing wild-type PPARγ1 with specific genetic variants (acetylation-defective mutants K154/155Q, K154/155A, an acetylation mimic K154/155R, and a sumoylation site mutant K77R) expressed in various breast cancer cell lines (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src) and in vivo in mouse xenograft models and transgenic mice with inducible Pparγ1 deletion. Experiments often involved subcutaneous injection of 1 x 10^6 cells. No dose-response comparisons of external therapeutic agents were reported; the focus was on the impact of specific molecular modifications and genetic manipulations, with the K154/155Q mutant demonstrating a significant ~90% reduction in tumor growth.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the feasibility and biological correlations of simultaneously quantifying perfusion, permeability, and novel contrast leakage effects in brain gliomas using dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) with a single contrast injection. Key findings demonstrate that dynamic SAGE-EPI enables the simultaneous assessment of these parameters, providing new metrics that correlate with previous treatment exposure, IDH status, and Ki67 expression, offering advantages like shorter scan times and reduced contrast agent use, and revealing distinct differences in contrast agent dynamics and tissue properties between treatment-naïve and recurrent gliomas, as well as between IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype tumors. document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed predictive models using a novel machine learning pipeline to identify viable intrauterine pregnancies (Live Normally Sited Pregnancies, LNSP) in symptomatic women, differentiating them from combined adverse outcomes (CAO) such as miscarriage, pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). The models integrate serum metabolite levels (untargeted 1H NMR profiling) with plasma hormone concentrations (β-hCG and progesterone) and clinicodemographic data, finding that a composite biomarker provides superior predictive accuracy (0.79). The aim is to offer a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic test to reduce diagnostic burden and improve outcomes in early gestation by accurately identifying LNSP and excluding conditions associated with maternal morbidity and mortality.

A single blood sample was collected upon first emergency presentation; plasma was used for β-hCG and progesterone concentration measurements, and serum for untargeted metabolomic profiling. Nine key metabolite signals were identified. Random forest models were constructed and compared: a model using metabolite signals alone yielded 0.68 accuracy, β-hCG and progesterone alone yielded 0.71 accuracy, and the combined model achieved the best predictive accuracy of 0.79. Model performance was assessed using an independent validation cohort. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic accuracy for pregnancy outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

Patients showed a leftward shift of the lactate curve from CPET 1 to CPET 2 (P < 0.001), while controls showed a rightward shift (P < 0.001). [La a ] at GET did not differ significantly from controls on CPET 1 in patients, and showed no significant differences between CPETs in patients, but was significantly reduced in controls on CPET 2 (P = 0.008). A diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore) was established using a specific formula involving five N-glycans (m/z 1606, 1769, 2074, 2118, 2423) and a cut-off of -0.0955 points. No therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated in the UC group compared with the levels in the healthy volunteer (HV) and prostate cancer (PC) groups (p = 0.0001). Upregulation observed in Prostate Cancer (PC) patients. Contributes to the dNGScore formula with a positive coefficient (0.4941).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: N-glycosylation profile on immunoglobulins, modulating their structure and potentially their biological activity. Its aberrant level may indicate altered glycan processing due to disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Serum N-glycan profiling for urothelial carcinoma (UC) detection and Prostate Cancer (PC) diagnosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with UC detection (decreased levels) and potentially a candidate for prostate cancer detection (upregulated levels). Contributes to the overall diagnostic accuracy of the dNGScore.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of aberrant N-glycosylation profiles of serum immunoglobulins (Igs) for urothelial carcinoma (UC), including bladder cancer (UCB) and upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). It identified five UC-associated aberrant N-glycan changes, notably the accumulation of asialo-bisecting GlcNAc type N-glycans in UC patients. A novel diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore), derived from a combination of these five N-glycans, demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (92.8% sensitivity, 97.2% specificity, AUC 0.969) for discriminating UC patients from healthy volunteers and prostate cancer patients, outperforming traditional diagnostic methods like urine cytology and hematuria. The dNGScore also showed utility in detecting urine cytology-negative cases and was associated with UCB invasiveness.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification (N-glycomics analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on diagnostic biomarker discovery, not therapeutic doses. High-throughput N-glycomics was used to quantify 32 types of N-glycan levels on serum immunoglobulins from 10-μL aliquots of purified Ig fractions. A diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore) was established using a specific formula involving five N-glycans (m/z 1606, 1769, 2074, 2118, 2423) and a cut-off of -0.0955 points. No therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Asialo bisecting GlcNAc with core fucosylated N-glycan (m/z 2118)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated in the urothelial carcinoma (UC) group (p = 0.0001), but not detectable in healthy volunteer (HV) and prostate cancer (PC) groups. Accumulation was more of a UTUC-specific phenomenon than UCB. Contributes to the dNGScore formula with a negative coefficient (-3.2460).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: N-glycosylation profile on immunoglobulins, hypothesized to be formed by β1,4-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase (GnT-III) activity in UC patients. Its aberrant level indicates altered glycan processing.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Serum N-glycan profiling for urothelial carcinoma (UC) detection, particularly for distinguishing UTUC from UCB.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strong diagnostic indicator for urothelial carcinoma, as its presence and upregulation are specific to UC patients and undetectable in controls. Potentially an indicator for UTUC-specific characteristics. Contributes significantly to the dNGScore.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as an influential factor in group differentiation (VIP score between 1.04 and 1.75), contributing to the overall reduction in amino acids in the PFF group. Notable differences were observed between groups at 98 days (p < 0.002). Its inclusion in classic models (age, BMI, waist circumference, or cholesterol) significantly increased AUC from 76.7-78% to 100% (approaching significance).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Non-essential amino acid involved in protein synthesis, metabolism, and metabolic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention, differentiating metabolic profiles between groups at 55 and 98 days, and used in predictive models to assess intervention impact from baseline to day 98.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to different health statuses, influencing group differentiation, and identified as a relevant metabolite that significantly improves the predictive power of statistical models for assessing dietary intervention impact.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significant seasonal changes; changes were similar to CK, showing significant decreases.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant changes observed for the whole group (n=24) over the one-year training cycle. Changes were similar to CK, which decreased significantly from T1-T2 (-160.9 U/L) and T3-T4 (-292.7 U/L).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, indicative of liver and muscle health, and associated with muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training cycle in young soccer players, competitive and pre-season training, and adaptation to applied training loads.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of muscle damage or liver stress; elevated levels suggest tissue injury due to intense physical activity, reflecting adaptations to soccer training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and delayed effects of the 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT) on biomarkers of muscle damage (creatinine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase), inflammation (C-reactive protein), and subjective perceptions of fatigue, recovery, and muscle soreness (DOMS, RPE, PRS) in healthy male amateur team sports players. Findings indicate that the 5mSRT significantly increased muscle damage and inflammation markers, as well as DOMS and RPE, while reducing PRS. The study concluded that a 72-hour recovery period was generally sufficient for fatigue recovery, with biomarker levels returning towards baseline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 5mSRT consisted of 6 repetitions of 30-second maximal shuttle sprints, with 35-second recovery periods between each sprint. Participants ran the greatest possible distance within 30 seconds by shuttling between cones at increasing distances (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m, etc.). Blood samples and perceptual scores were taken at rest, 5 minutes post-exercise, and 72 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons for varying test intensities or durations were reported within the protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased acutely post-exercise, then returned towards baseline.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased from pre-5mSRT (18.0  1 4.4 IU/L) to post-5mSRT (21.7  1 6.2 IU/L, p < 0.001). Levels decreased to 15.0  1 4.7 IU/L at 72 h post-5mSRT, returning towards baseline (p < 0.001 compared to post-5mSRT).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, found in striated muscle. It serves as a marker of muscle and liver damage; simultaneous changes with CK, LDH, and ALAT typically indicate muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute effect of 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT)-induced muscle damage and fatigue, with assessment at 5 minutes and 72 hours post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of exercise-induced muscle damage and fatigue. Return to baseline within 72 hours suggests recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage in trained individuals.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase observed only after the third bout of exhaustive exercise (p<0.05), with no differences in baseline values before bouts or in post-exercise values after the first and second bouts. Percentage increase was several dozen-times lower than cf n-DNA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in various tissues, including muscle, liver, and heart; elevated levels in blood are markers of tissue damage, involved in amino acid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In response to the third bout of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level and cellular processes leading to leakage of biomolecules from mitochondria following exhaustive exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences (p > 0.05) between time points (T1, T2, T3) nor between control and intervention groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme indicative of muscle, liver, and cardiac damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6 weeks of CrossFit® exercise with/without Tribulus Terrestris supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle, liver, and cardiac damage; TT supplementation had no significant impact on this marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated sex differences in biomarkers of end-organ damage (Creatinine (CR), estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Creatine Kinase (CK), Alanine-Transaminase (ALT), and Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST)) and their time course following exertional heat stroke (EHS) in 62 active-duty service members. Findings indicate that women exhibited significantly lower peak values for kidney (CR) and muscle (CK) damage biomarkers compared to men, with ALT and AST also being similar or lower in women during recovery, suggesting women may be less susceptible to organ injury from EHS despite similar recorded core temperatures or potential higher actual peak temperatures due to pre-measurement cooling.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exertional Heat Stroke (EHS) and subsequent active cooling interventions
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on Exertional Heat Stroke (EHS) events where individuals received active cooling interventions (ice sheets, cold-water immersion, chilled saline) prehospital and en route to the emergency department. While recorded peak body core temperatures were similar between sexes (women: 41.11°C (40.06, 41.67); men: 41.11°C (40.28, 41.72), P = 0.57), active cooling was initiated prior to temperature recording more frequently in women (91%) than men (57%), suggesting actual peak temperatures might have been higher for women. No specific dose-response comparisons for EHS severity or cooling interventions were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: no initial statistical significance for peak, then lower in women at later time points
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peak AST did not reach statistical significance (women: 66 U·L−1; men: 142 U·L−1, P = 0.069). However, women showed significantly lower AST than men for later recovery time points (time bins 5 and 6), and men had significantly higher absolute and relative AST and mean difference from upper limit from 21 to 32.99 h post-EHS.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in various tissues, including liver and muscle, indicating cellular damage when elevated in blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exertional heat stroke (EHS) in otherwise healthy humans (military personnel) during acute phase and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severity of liver and muscle damage; lower levels during recovery in women suggest less severe organ damage following EHS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median levels significantly higher in cirrhotic patients within both non-malignant groups (P = 0.0051 for chronic HCV, P < 0.0001 for SVRs). Significantly elevated in HCC patients compared to healthy controls, SVRs, and chronic HCV (P < 0.0001). Non-cirrhotic SVRs had lower AST levels than cirrhotic HCV (P = 0.0003) and cirrhotic SVRs (P < 0.0001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Liver enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, also found in heart and muscle cells. Elevated levels indicate liver or muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of liver health and fibrosis, particularly in HCV patients. Comparison among cirrhotic non-malignant patients, HCC patients, SVRs, chronic HCV, and controls; comparison between cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic groups. Used as a component in the FIB-4 index formula.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate liver inflammation or damage; significantly higher in HCC and cirrhotic patients. Lower levels in non-cirrhotic SVRs suggest better liver health post-treatment. Levels are used as part of the FIB-4 index to assess liver fibrosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased acutely, with a recovery trend
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased acutely during exercise (up to 50% in post-exercise samples), with a recovery trend during short recovery sessions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, present in liver and muscle cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, short recovery), systemic stress response.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can indicate muscle or liver strain/damage from exercise, suggesting a systemic stress response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, found in liver, heart, muscle, and other tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in the context of a study involving half-marathon running and potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Commonly used marker for liver damage or muscle injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between routine plasma biomarker levels and recovery efficiency in elite professional soccer players over an entire eleven-month competitive match season, including seasonal variations and differences based on player position and cumulative match time. It concluded that a panel of AST, CK, LDH, and creatinine can effectively monitor recovery, adaptation, and overtraining risk, particularly in active positions like midfielders who may also be prone to iron and magnesium deficiencies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competitive professional soccer matches and regular intense training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An eleven-month competitive season, comprising 44 league and cup matches (23 autumn, 21 spring), typically one to two matches per week. Fasting capillary blood samples were collected 17-24 hours after each match. The study compared player positions (midfielder/defender vs. goalie/substitute, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups), noting significant differences in cumulative match time and physical demands. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for training intensity, but adaptation to increasing training load was observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher initially, then consistently decreased over time, lower in spring vs. autumn
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally higher in midfielder/defender groups, especially midfielders, compared to goalie/substitute groups. AST levels consistently decreased significantly over time and with cumulative game time across all player subgroups and seasonal rounds (negative correlation ranging from R=-0.32 to -0.50, P<=0.05). Activity was significantly lower in the spring round compared to the autumn round across all positions. While generally increasing after an endurance effort, the long-term trend in this study was a decrease.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism (catalyzes transamination) and is stimulated by cortisol. It serves as an indicator of liver disease, muscle damage, metabolic stress, and recovery processes, reflecting both liver and muscle integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout an eleven-month professional competitive soccer match season, including post-match recovery (17-24 hours post-match), regular intense training, and after endurance efforts. Comparisons were made between different player positions (midfielder/defender, goalie/substitute, individual midfielder and defender subgroups), considering cumulative game time, seasonal variations (autumn vs. spring rounds), and adaptation to training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An appropriate and useful biomarker for monitoring recovery efficiency, metabolic response to exercise, and adaptation to training, as it is less affected by other factors and has lower interindividual variability than CK. It indicates physiological stress and muscle damage levels, suggesting higher strain in active positions, and its decrease over time often suggests adaptation or reduced tissue stress/damage. Monitoring AST can help prevent overreaching or overtraining and can appear earlier than CK in assessing recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the tissue origins of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in healthy mice using tissue-specific knockout models and its utility as a biomarker following paracetamol (APAP) overdose in both mice and humans. It found that cfDNA predominantly originates from blood cell lineages in healthy mice. Following APAP overdose, total and hepatocyte-derived cfDNA, as well as ALT and AST levels, significantly increased in mice (peaking at 8 hours), while albumin and bilirubin remained unaffected. In human APAP overdose patients, total cfDNA and liver-specific cfDNA (via methylation analysis) also significantly increased, especially in those with biochemical evidence of liver injury, demonstrating cfDNA's potential as a clinical biomarker for distinguishing overdose patients, assessing liver injury severity, and monitoring treatment efficacy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Paracetamol (APAP) Overdose; N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mice received intraperitoneal (IP) APAP at 350 mg/kg body weight, with samples collected at 8, 24, and 48 hours post-dosing (optimal cfDNA peak at 8 hours, liver damage most severe at 24 hours). Human patients presented with APAP overdose, with a subset receiving N-acetylcysteine (NAC) at 500-900 mg/kg body weight 20-40 hours after initial overdose. Patient groups were stratified by liver injury severity (normal vs. raised ALT); no specific APAP dose comparisons were performed in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in APAP-dosed mice, peaking at 8 hours post-dosing (normal range for serum AST is 0–35 IU/l).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in liver and other tissues, indicating tissue damage, particularly hepatocellular damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: APAP-induced acute liver injury in C57BL/6 mice and APAP overdose patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for liver function and indicator of acute tissue damage, particularly liver damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: higher liver enzyme markers (AST)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in liver, heart, muscle, and kidney, released into blood upon tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-liver transplantation in acute rejection (AR) patients, associated with worse liver function.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver cell damage and worse liver function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated alterations in serum levels of tumor, cardiac, liver, and renal function markers, alongside the IL-18 rs1946518 polymorphism, in patients with breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers (BC, CRC, PCa), and myocardial infarction (MI), compared to healthy controls. It revealed significantly elevated tumor markers (CA 15-3, CA 19-9, CEA, TPSA) in cancer patients, which serve as efficient early detection biomarkers. Cardiac markers (hs-cTnT, CK-MB) were specific to MI and largely unchanged in cancer. Liver and renal markers (ALP, AST, ALT, urea, creatinine) showed varied elevations, particularly in CRC and PCa, suggesting their utility as alternative diagnostic indicators. The IL-18 -607 C/A polymorphism was identified as a risk factor for PCa (AA genotype and A allele), and also showed an Odds Ratio of 1.75 for BC, while A/C heterozygotes were linked to increased CRC risk and C allele homozygotes offered protection against CRC.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker and Genetic Polymorphism Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study focused on assessing diagnostic biomarker levels and genetic polymorphisms in various patient groups and healthy controls, without any therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in PCa, unchanged in BC
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in Prostate Cancer (PCa) patients compared with the control group, with an AUC value of 0.76 for detecting PCa. Unchanged in Breast Cancer (BC) patients compared to healthy individuals.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Liver function enzyme, involved in amino acid metabolism, general indicator of tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Breast Cancer (BC) and Prostate Cancer (PCa) patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Good indicator for detecting PCa. Unchanged in BC patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme found in the liver, heart, muscle, and kidney; elevated levels indicate tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of liver or muscle damage; relevant for monitoring potential drug toxicity or disease impact.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change during the study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hepatic function, marker of liver or muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During the CCombat study (entire protocol and recovery).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable hepatic function and muscle integrity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Fluctuated; increased activity in professional athletes; lower inter-individual variability compared to CK
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fluctuated, with activity varying by competitive distance and sex. Increased activity in professional athletes is associated with muscle cell release. No significant differences were observed in male groups over 10 weeks. Shows lower inter-individual variability compared to CK. Correlated with CK activity (male groups, FS group) and urea concentration (regardless of sex).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in muscles, liver, and other tissues; auxiliary diagnostic marker for muscle damage and can indicate liver or muscle cell integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-training recovery and during a 10-week preparatory training stage in professional long-distance and sprint swimmers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: In athletes, indicates muscle cell release rather than liver pathology. Important for training and recovery decisions, especially with CK due to lower inter-individual variability. Can clarify if increased urea is diet-related or training-load consequence. Recommended for an optimal monitoring panel.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant differences observed across PGI/PGII quartiles (P < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, often indicating liver health or tissue damage when elevated in the blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Stratification by Pepsinogen Ratio (PGI/PGII) quartiles.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of liver function and potential liver damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated a multilayer perceptron (MLP) machine learning model for the early postnatal differential diagnosis of choledochal cysts (CC) and cystic biliary atresia (CBA). The model utilized routinely available clinical parameters, including biochemical markers (Total bile acid, Total bilirubin, γ-glutamyl transferase, Aspartate aminotransferase, Alanine aminotransferase, Direct bilirubin, and Taurodeoxycholate) and ultrasonographic measurements (Longitudinal and Transverse diameters of cysts), from a retrospective cohort of 319 patients. The MLP model achieved high diagnostic performance (95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and AUC of 0.990 for differentiating CBA from CC), aiming to facilitate timely surgical intervention for CBA and improve patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Model Development (Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective study involved the analysis of clinical features from 319 patients (< 60 days old at surgery) with hepatic hilar cysts (274 CC, 45 CBA) treated between 2011 and 2022. It focused on developing a diagnostic model rather than a therapeutic intervention. Biochemical markers and ultrasonographic measurements were compared, and key diagnostic features were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Eleven machine learning models were developed and compared, with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) model showing optimal performance: 95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.990. The model utilized seven routine clinical parameters (GGT, TBA, DBIL, TBIL, ALT, LDC, and TDC) as input variables. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the congenital biliary atresia (CBA) group than in the choledochal cysts (CC) group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in the liver, heart, muscle, and kidney; elevated levels often indicate liver cell damage. Indicator of hepatocellular injury or damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of Cystic Biliary Atresia (CBA) vs. Choledochal Cysts (CC) in early infancy; preoperative assessment for patients with hepatic hilar cysts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver cell damage, contributing to the differentiation of CBA from CC.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly different between SBMA and controls (P_adj < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme found in various tissues including liver, heart, muscle, and kidney; indicates tissue damage when elevated.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Adult male patients with SBMA compared to age-matched healthy controls (NIH cohort).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates tissue damage; differences linked to SBMA may suggest multi-organ involvement or muscle damage.
