document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated Nogo-B protein expression in liver tissues and its plasma levels in patients with liver cirrhosis, correlating them with various clinical parameters. Findings indicated that Nogo-B is highly expressed in fibrotic/cirrhotic liver tissues and its plasma levels are significantly elevated in cirrhotic patients, showing a positive correlation with Child-Pugh scores and liver fibrosis stage. The research suggests that plasma Nogo-B could serve as a novel surrogate marker for assessing liver functional reserve.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on liver cirrhosis progression and biomarker correlation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention. It involved 24 patients with fibrotic/cirrhotic liver specimens (12 Metavir F2, 12 Metavir F4) and 10 healthy controls for immunohistochemical analysis of liver tissue. For plasma Nogo-B analysis, 301 patients with hepatic cirrhosis (comprising 152 with hepatitis B cirrhosis, 83 with alcoholic cirrhosis, and 66 with primary biliary cirrhosis) and 153 healthy controls were enrolled. Patients were further classified into Child-Pugh classes A, B, and C to assess correlation with disease severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant correlation with plasma Nogo-B concentrations (r = 0.112, P = 0.052).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Liver inflammatory marker, indicates hepatocellular damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of liver inflammation in patients with hepatic cirrhosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects inflammation of liver; lack of correlation with Nogo-B suggests Nogo-B does not reflect active inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Improved after 14 months of pioglitazone and ezetimibe. Altered due to depression, excess eating, and lowered physical activity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Liver enzyme, indicator of liver cell damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After pioglitazone and ezetimibe treatment, associated with depression, excess eating, lowered physical activity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates liver damage; improvement suggests therapeutic efficacy and disease improvement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of low (0.625 mg) and high (2.5 mg) doses of phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation on full squat performance, muscle damage, protein breakdown, metabolic response, and perceived exertion in resistance-trained males. It concluded that high-dose PC favorably influenced squat performance, reduced active muscle perceived exertion, and attenuated muscle damage compared to placebo, suggesting an ergogenic effect primarily with the higher dose.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation during resistance training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received oral phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation 45 minutes before exercise, with conditions including a low dose (LD) of 0.625 mg, a high dose (HD) of 2.5 mg, and a placebo (PLA) of maltodextrin. The resistance exercise protocol involved full squat sets of 3x8 repetitions at 70% 1RM, with lifting velocity monitored. The high dose (HD) demonstrated superior biochemical and mechanical anti-fatigue effects compared to the low dose and placebo, indicating a dose-response relationship where higher doses were more effective.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower for High Dose (HD) PC compared to Placebo (PLA). PLA resulted in higher AST concentrations at 24-h post than HD (p = 0.02). Significant differences between conditions for AST post-values (p = 0.03). HD exhibited lower levels of AST than PLA after 24 hours.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism and found in various tissues including muscle; elevated levels in blood typically indicate muscle or cellular damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 24-hour post-resistance training (full squat) recovery after high-dose phenylcapsaicin supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower AST concentrations at 24-h post-exercise indicate reduced muscle damage and inflammation, suggesting improved recovery and less mechanical stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Used for assessment of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD) markers

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in amino acid metabolism, indicative of liver cell damage when elevated
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD) markers
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator for assessing the status of Chronic Liver Disease (CLD)

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers to differentiate Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases in human patients. The findings indicated that methylation levels of OPCML and HOXD9 in serum cfDNA were significantly higher in CCA patients compared to those with other biliary diseases. The study concluded that OPCML and HOXD9, especially when combined, demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity, making them promising differential biomarkers for CCA, improving diagnostic accuracy and preventing misdiagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based differential diagnosis using cfDNA methylation analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on evaluating serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 as diagnostic biomarkers. Methylation levels were quantified using methylation-sensitive high-resolution melting (MS-HRM) assay on bisulfite-modified serum cfDNA (20 µL, <1 µg), with detection limits of 1.56% (lower) and 50% (upper). Their potency was evaluated using ROC curves. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported, as this was a diagnostic study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Abnormally elevated in both CCA and other biliary disease groups; no significant difference between groups (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme indicative of liver or muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Ineffective for differentiating CCA from other biliary diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in cirrhotic patients within both non-malignant groups (P = 0.0015 for chronic HCV, P < 0.0001 for SVRs). Significantly elevated in HCC patients compared to healthy controls, SVRs, and chronic HCV (P < 0.0001). Median AST/ALT ratio was lower in both chronic HCV and non-cirrhotic SVRs patients than in cirrhotic patients (P < 0.00001).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison among cirrhotic non-malignant patients, HCC patients, SVRs, chronic HCV, and controls; comparison between cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated ratio indicates more severe liver damage, possibly suggestive of cirrhosis or HCC. A lower ratio in non-cirrhotic patients indicates less severe liver disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Riociguat (Drug Treatment)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients with early treatment-naïve diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis were randomized to receive riociguat (n=60) or placebo (n=61) for 52 weeks. Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in changes from baseline to week 14 between riociguat and placebo groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthase, impacting NO bioavailability and vascular function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in dcSSc patients from baseline to week 14.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Levels are elevated in diffuse SSc, but no change was observed with riociguat treatment, suggesting no direct impact on its levels or the overall NO-sGC-cGMP pathway engagement via ADMA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between groups 55 days after starting the dietary intervention (p < 0.002).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthase, impacting endothelial function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention at 55 days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentiating metabolite indicating the impact of the dietary intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Atherosclerosis risk signature (UCLH-40, comprising serum metabolites and clinical traits)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Metabolomic analysis and machine learning-derived predictive signature

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Predicted the presence or absence of subclinical atherosclerosis; Components collectively contribute to discriminating SLE patients with plaques from those without.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Classified SLE-P patients and outperformed established CVD risk assessment tools (QRISK3, Framingham Risk Score), routine lipid profiles, and clinical features alone. Validated in a second adult female SLE cohort (n=98) predicting plaque status with moderate accuracy (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.79). Signature derived from top variables appearing in models with AUROC >0.7. The weighted score for predicting subclinical atherosclerosis-risk was derived from the validated UCLH-40 using Youden statistic and Autoscore analysis.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Assessment and prediction of subclinical atherosclerosis risk in female SLE patients; diverse biological roles, including lipoprotein metabolism, amino acid metabolism, glycolysis, and ketone body metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Female patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with or without subclinical atherosclerosis; discrimination of subclinical atherosclerotic plaques in female SLE patients (SLE-P vs. SLE-NP cohorts) and assessment of CVD risk.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improves prediction of subclinical atherosclerosis risk in female SLE patients compared to established CVD risk scores, identifying patients who may benefit from enhanced monitoring or intervention. Predicts subclinical atherosclerosis risk and can be used to stratify patients based on this risk in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

document_context_data.document_summary: This surveillance report details malaria cases in the United States in 2018, reporting a 15.6% decrease in confirmed cases from 2017 while noting an overall increase since 1972, with 98.1% being imported cases predominantly from Africa and P. falciparum as the most common species. It describes comprehensive surveillance methodologies, diagnostic tests, and molecular analyses for antimalarial drug resistance markers, particularly for P. falciparum against pyrimethamine, sulfadoxine, chloroquine, and mefloquine, with no resistance markers for atovaquone or artemisinin. The report also investigates chemoprophylaxis adherence (found to be poor), treatment patterns for uncomplicated and severe malaria, and emphasizes the critical importance of prompt diagnosis, appropriate treatment with CDC guidelines, and continuous surveillance to prevent local transmission.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Malaria prevention (chemoprophylaxis, including Tafenoquine), diagnosis (microscopy, PCR, RDTs), and treatment for both uncomplicated and severe malaria (oral antimalarials like atovaquone-proguanil, artemether-lumefantrine, quinine; parenteral IV artesunate for severe malaria), alongside molecular surveillance for antimalarial drug resistance.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Chemoprophylaxis adherence was poor among U.S. residents with imported malaria in 2018, with 24.5% reporting use and 95.0% demonstrating non-adherence or inconsistent regimens, often due to forgetting or prematurely stopping. Tafenoquine offers an abbreviated schedule for eligible adults. For treatment, IV artesunate became the first-line for severe malaria in April 2019, replacing IV quinidine gluconate, though 52.1% of severe cases in 2018 did not receive guideline-appropriate treatment. Uncomplicated malaria treatments varied, with 91.7% receiving appropriate care, and primaquine was often used for P. vivax/P. ovale relapse prevention, though sometimes inappropriately. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported, but treatment choice was emphasized based on species, severity, patient factors (e.g., pregnancy), and CDC guidelines.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood specimens; Whole blood specimens; Plasmodium falciparum parasites (DNA)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Antimalarial drug resistance marker testing (identification of genetic polymorphisms); Gene sequence polymorphisms; Evaluation of resistance genes

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specimens tested contained a marker for atovaquone resistance (0% of 106 P. falciparum-positive specimens). No markers of resistance were identified in 96 (87.3%) specimens evaluated. Identified at codons I258M and Y268S in the pfcytb gene.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates potential reduced efficacy of atovaquone due to specific genetic mutations in Plasmodium falciparum cytochrome b (PFCytB), a component of the electron transport chain targeted by the drug.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Molecular surveillance of P. falciparum positive malaria cases in the United States, 2018; Detection of antimalarial drug resistance in imported P. falciparum malaria cases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Guides treatment decisions; absence of resistance markers suggests continued susceptibility to atovaquone, identifying drug-susceptible foci.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels highest in subphenotype 2. Precise quantification not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates myocardial stretch/stress and fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort, particularly defining Subphenotype 2.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are associated with subphenotype 2, which is linked to significantly worse patient outcomes (HR 3.43 (1.76–6.69) compared to subphenotype 1).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mouse heart tissue, Neonatal Rat Cardiomyocytes (NRCMs)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (with CRAMP treatment); higher (in CRAMP deficiency)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced in the TAC model upon mCRAMP peptide treatment. Decreased mRNA expression levels in AngII-treated NRCMs with CRAMP. Further increased in AngII-induced HF in mCRAMP knockout mice.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone involved in regulating blood pressure and fluid balance, often upregulated in response to cardiac stress and hypertrophy; a biomarker of cardiac hypertrophy.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: TAC-induced heart failure (HF) with mCRAMP peptide supplementation; AngII-treated neonatal rat cardiomyocytes with CRAMP; AngII-induced heart failure in mCRAMP knockout mice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced expression indicates attenuated cardiac stress and hypertrophy. Increased expression indicates exacerbated HF.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic modifier investigation; Observational longitudinal study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is observational and investigates an intrinsic genetic factor, not an active therapeutic intervention. The 'dose' refers to the additive effects of the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage (0, 1, or 2 G alleles), which was modeled as a continuous variable. The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). No deviations from an additive effect were observed (heterozygosity indicator P > 0.05), and no traditional dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In GRN symptomatic carriers longitudinally: better attention/processing speed scores (β for slope per G allele: 0.28, 95% CI: 0.09, 0.46; corrected P: 0.02). The C9orf72 group also showed more generalized protective effects on cognition longitudinally, including these domains.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Ability to focus concentration and efficiently process information, components of cognitive function critical for daily activities.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage in symptomatic GRN and C9orf72 carriers longitudinally.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher scores indicate better attention and processing speed, crucial cognitive functions often impacted in FTD, suggesting better cognitive preservation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Auditory-verbal short-term memory assessment in Turkish speakers, an agglutinative language with high morpheme-to-word ratio.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates cognitive impairment in short-term memory, particularly affected by the linguistic structure of agglutinative languages.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the role of PPARγ1, specifically its K154/155 acetylation site, as a molecular switch in oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary adenocarcinoma tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and metastasis. Using in vitro cell models, in vivo mouse xenograft models, and human breast cancer patient datasets, the research demonstrated that K154/155 acetylation is essential for promoting tumor growth, de novo lipogenesis, and cancer stem cell characteristics, while also regulating cellular apoptosis and autophagy. The acetylation status was found to determine genome-wide DNA binding site selection, shifting from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) binding, and influencing transcriptional programs for growth factor signaling. Furthermore, gene signatures reflecting acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis (PASS1 and PASS2) showed predictive value for survival outcomes and distant metastasis-free survival in various breast cancer subtypes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Molecular mechanism investigation focusing on PPARγ1 post-translational modification (acetylation) and the functional consequences of genetic variants (wild-type vs. acetylation-defective mutants)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparing wild-type PPARγ1 with specific genetic variants (acetylation-defective mutants K154/155Q, K154/155A, an acetylation mimic K154/155R, and a sumoylation site mutant K77R) expressed in various breast cancer cell lines (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src) and in vivo in mouse xenograft models and transgenic mice with inducible Pparγ1 deletion. Experiments often involved subcutaneous injection of 1 x 10^6 cells. No dose-response comparisons of external therapeutic agents were reported; the focus was on the impact of specific molecular modifications and genetic manipulations, with the K154/155Q mutant demonstrating a significant ~90% reduction in tumor growth.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Restraint of autophagy/mitophagy in K154/155Q expressing tumors indicates altered cellular metabolism, potentially hindering tumor cell survival and growth.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study longitudinally analyzed T and B cell receptor repertoire transcripts in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of COVID-19 patients to understand the dynamic immune response across different disease stages compared to healthy controls. Key findings include markedly diminished TCR repertoires (reduced unique TCR reads, TRA, and TRB percentages) during early severe disease, which recovered during convalescence, with TRB expression suggested as a reliable indicator for recovery. BCR repertoires showed increased IgH, IgK, and IgL proportions, isotype switching, a transient but dramatic early IgA expansion, and dominant B cell clonal expansion with decreased diversity following recovery from infection, alongside an early IgM to IgG isotype switch.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Natural SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study observed the natural progression of SARS-CoV-2 infection in patients, analyzing peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples at various time points (e.g., D4-7, D8-15, D17-22 after symptom onset) and comparing them to healthy controls. No therapeutic intervention, controlled dose, or dose-response comparisons were administered or investigated; the focus was on the temporal dynamics of the immune response to the infection itself.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dominant B cell clonal expansion with decreased diversity occurred following recovery from infection. Many dominant clones and lower diversity compared to healthy controls were found in ICU patients in early infection.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates dynamic immune response during COVID-19 recovery; evaluates emergent host immunity to SARS-CoV-2. Changes in adaptive immune response, specifically concerning B cell repertoire diversity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: drastically reduced numbers in severe COVID-19; numbers normalized in patients who have recovered or are convalescent.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Adaptive immune response; antibody production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A common feature in patients with severe COVID-19; lymphopenia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Cell counts/frequency, Immunoglobulin production, B-cell activating factor (BAFF) overproduction

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: B cells recover more slowly than innate immune cells post-TCT. Prolonged low levels are observed during the first 3 months post-TCT; however, early reconstitution of B cells (>25/μL within 100 days) is an immune predictor for reduced NRM. A higher frequency of B-cell precursors and early B cells in the first year post-TCT is linked to a lower incidence of both acute and chronic GVHD, while delayed reconstitution correlates with GVHD development. B cells overproducing B-cell activating factor (BAFF) are associated with cGVHD and NRM.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the 'real-world' eligibility of unselected, symptomatic outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HF-REF) for sacubitril/valsartan treatment, using criteria from the PARADIGM-HF trial. It found that 34-76% of these patients are eligible, with eligibility significantly influenced by background ACEI/ARB dosing. The most common reasons for ineligibility were low natriuretic peptide levels, followed by low blood pressure, renal dysfunction (low eGFR), and hyperkalemia, which collectively accounted for 20-30% of exclusions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sacubitril/valsartan (eligibility assessment against enalapril/ACEI/ARB)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on evaluating patient eligibility for sacubitril/valsartan based on PARADIGM-HF trial criteria, considering different background ACEI/ARB doses. Patients were deemed potentially eligible if they were on an ACEI or ARB dose equivalent to at least 10 mg enalapril daily, with further consideration for tolerating up-titration to 20 mg enalapril daily during an active run-in phase. The study did not report specific sacubitril/valsartan doses but observed its comparative effect on renal impairment and hyperkalemia during follow-up against enalapril. Eligibility varied depending on these background ACEI/ARB dose thresholds.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in eligible patients; lower levels lead to ineligibility.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Ineligibility thresholds were BNP < 150 pg/ml (or NT-proBNP < 600 pg/ml), or for patients hospitalized for HF in the preceding 12 months, BNP < 100 pg/ml (or NT-proBNP < 400 pg/ml). This was the most common reason for ineligibility, affecting 13.7% to 16.1% of patients depending on the background ACEI/ARB dose (e.g., 14.9% or 462 of 3099 patients in the ">=10mg enalapril equivalent group). Higher concentrations are associated with greater absolute risk reduction from sacubitril/valsartan treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized discovery metabolomics and lipidomics to investigate plasma glycosphingolipids and other lipid metabolites as potential biomarkers for distinguishing aggressive from indolent prostate cancer (PCa) in treatment-naïve African-American and European-American men. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screening in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells, primarily Nalm6 B-ALL, to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of panobinostat resistance and action. Key findings reveal mitochondrial activity as a driver of panobinostat resistance and SIRT1 expression as a critical determinant of sensitivity. Panobinostat treatment abrogates mitochondrial activity in ALL cells, contributing to resistance, while enhancing mitochondrial function (via rosiglitazone or SIRT1 overexpression) sensitizes ALL cells to panobinostat by activating the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. The investigation identifies the SIRT1-mitochondria-PMAIP1 pathway as central to panobinostat response and suggests that higher SIRT1 expression or mitochondrial hyperactivity could indicate patient benefit from panobinostat therapy. The study also details various methods used, including cell culture, gene modulation techniques, drug sensitivity assays, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and flow cytometry.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Panobinostat was frequently used at 10 nM for durations of 24 hours (for RNA sequencing, combination treatments) or 14 days (for CRISPR screening), leading to 60-80% cell death and significant proliferation inhibition in Nalm6 cells. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates targeting RARA overexpression with tamibarotene, a selective RARα agonist, in combination with azacitidine in newly diagnosed unfit non-APL acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) patients. It demonstrates that RARA-positive patients respond significantly better to tamibarotene plus azacitidine, achieving high complete remission rates, rapid response onset, and improved survival. The study also explores RARA overexpression's association with monocytic features and its link to venetoclax resistance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tamibarotene plus azacitidine combination therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In a phase 2 clinical study (NCT02807558), azacitidine was administered at 75 mg/m2 (intravenously or subcutaneously) daily on days 1-7, followed by oral tamibarotene at 6 mg/m2 per day (divided doses twice daily) on days 8-28, with each treatment cycle lasting 28 days. This combination was evaluated in 51 newly diagnosed unfit AML patients (22 RARA-positive, 29 RARA-negative). Hypertriglyceridemia was a frequent, manageable, and reversible high-grade nonhematologic adverse event. No dose-response comparisons were reported for tamibarotene plus azacitidine. document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Patients with atherosclerotic plaques (SLE-P) had lower disease activity compared with plaque-free patients (SLE-NP).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pluripotency marker identification and proteome coverage expansion using MALDI MS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a novel, minimally invasive approach using hair follicle (HF) gene expression, specifically a four-gene panel (Bmp2, Daam2, Plaat1, Prss27), to assess and classify tissue thyroid hormone (TH) action. Investigating amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism (AIH) in human patients and a TH action indicator (THAI) mouse model, the study found that amiodarone treatment significantly attenuates tissue TH action under hyperthyroid conditions, leading to a mismatch between elevated serum TH levels and attenuated tissue hyperthyroidism, suggesting a protective effect of amiodarone against thyrotoxicosis at the tissue level.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Amiodarone treatment and Thyroid Hormone Status Modulation (Hypothyroid, Euthyroid, Hyperthyroid, T4 Administration)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human patients were treated with amiodarone for at least 4 weeks prior to sampling, with comparisons made between hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid groups; specific human amiodarone doses were not reported. In the mouse model, amiodarone was administered at 1.35 g/kg in chow for 8 weeks, and T4 was administered intraperitoneally at 166.7 ng/bwg/day for 2 days to induce hyperthyroidism. Amiodarone was shown to prevent T4-induced TH action elevation in mouse tissues. Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism affected up to 10% of patients, and AIH affected 1% of patients. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for amiodarone or T4.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Regulated by both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism; specifically 2.7- to 6.5-fold higher in hyperthyroid cases compared to hypothyroid cases.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression level is highly influenced by TH status and correlated with serum-based TH status. Part of a 4-gene model that showed high predictive performance for tissue TH status.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Human tissue TH signaling assessment across hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid states, particularly in amiodarone treatment or discrepancies between serum and tissue TH levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Allows assessment of tissue TH action/status, reflecting serum-based TH status at the tissue level. document_context_data.document_summary: This study prospectively evaluated mesenteric fibrosis (MF) in small intestinal neuroendocrine neoplasms (SINENs) using a multidimensional approach correlating radiological, surgical, and histological findings. The NETest-fibrosome demonstrated high accuracy in detecting microscopic MF, with APLP2, BNIP3L, CD59, and CTGF individually showing significant predictive capabilities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the development and validation of computationally efficient Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models for predicting epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) risk. The research specifically focuses on penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and Bayesian frameworks (S4, LDPred). It evaluates their predictive performance and association strength for non-mucinous EOC in the general population across European, East Asian, and African ancestries, as well as in BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers, concluding that S4 and lasso models provide improved risk prediction and risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) Modeling for Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (EOC) Risk Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study developed and validated multiple computational Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models, including penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and Bayesian frameworks (S4, LDPred). Models were built using individual-level genotype data and summary statistics derived from meta-analyses. For example, the S4 model utilized up to 27,240 Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs), while LDPred explored various fractions of associated variants (0.001 to 1.0). Performance was assessed by comparing predictive accuracy (e.g., AUC), association strength (Odds Ratios, Hazard Ratios), and estimated cumulative risk across different models, ancestries (European, East Asian, African), and in BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers. No traditional therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for a physical agent were applicable or reported; the focus was on comparing the efficacy and performance of different statistical modeling approaches.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association of common germline genetic variants, particularly those exhibiting differential allelic expression (DAE), with breast and ovarian cancer risk in a large cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association of common germline genetic variants, particularly those exhibiting differential allelic expression (DAE), with breast and ovarian cancer risk in a large cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. It identified a new modifier locus at 11q22.3 significantly associated with breast cancer risk, specifically in BRCA1 carriers, and explored potential functional implications through eQTL and chromatin analyses. While several other SNPs showed nominal associations with breast or ovarian cancer risk and specific breast cancer subtypes (ER-negative/ER-positive), most associations did not retain statistical significance after multiple testing correction.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic Association Study and Epidemiological Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational epidemiological study involving genetic risk assessment, not a therapeutic intervention. It analyzed ~320 genotyped SNPs and additional imputed SNPs across a cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. Statistical significance was set at p < 1.5 × 10^-4 after Bonferroni adjustment for multiple testing, and imputation considered SNPs with r^2 > 0.30. eQTL analysis was performed using gene expression data from normal and tumor breast tissues. No dose-response comparisons were reported as it is not a treatment study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the development and validation of computationally efficient Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models for predicting epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) risk. The research specifically focuses on penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and Bayesian frameworks (S4, LDPred). It evaluates their predictive performance and association strength for non-mucinous EOC in the general population across European, East Asian, and African ancestries, as well as in BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers, concluding that S4 and lasso models provide improved risk prediction and risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) Modeling for Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (EOC) Risk Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study developed and validated multiple computational Polygenic Risk Score (PRS) models, including penalized logistic regression (lasso, elastic net, stepwise) and Bayesian frameworks (S4, LDPred). Models were built using individual-level genotype data and summary statistics derived from meta-analyses. For example, the S4 model utilized up to 27,240 Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs), while LDPred explored various fractions of associated variants (0.001 to 1.0). Performance was assessed by comparing predictive accuracy (e.g., AUC), association strength (Odds Ratios, Hazard Ratios), and estimated cumulative risk across different models, ancestries (European, East Asian, African), and in BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers. No traditional therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for a physical agent were applicable or reported; the focus was on comparing the efficacy and performance of different statistical modeling approaches.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genetic material (DNA, inferred from carrier status); Genomic data (genetic predisposition)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with cumulative risk of ovarian cancer. PRS HGS AUC estimate for BRCA2 carriers (AUC = 0.667); lasso and S4 models showed slightly better AUCs in BRCA2 carriers. Cumulative risk of ovarian cancer by age 80 modulated by PRS, with risks for 10th and 90th percentiles detailed in supplementary tables.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Encodes a tumor suppressor protein involved in DNA repair by homologous recombination, maintaining genomic integrity. Pathogenic variants impair this function, leading to increased cancer risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Ovarian cancer risk assessment in individuals with genetic predisposition; Contextual group for evaluating the predictive performance of new Polygenic Risk Score models for EOC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a significantly increased lifetime risk of developing ovarian cancer, which can be further stratified by polygenic risk scores; Significant indicator of hereditary EOC risk; population for whom improved risk stratification is highly valuable.
