document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the expression and role of bone marrow stromal protein 2 (BST2) in bone metastatic breast cancer across cell lines, tumor tissues, and patient serum. Findings consistently demonstrated significant upregulation of BST2 in bone metastatic breast cancer, correlating with increased cancer cell migration and proliferation, thereby identifying BST2 as a potential biomarker for early detection and a contributor to bone metastasis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Investigation and Functional Characterization
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparative analysis of BST2 expression levels in various breast cancer cell lines, human tumor tissues, and patient serum (comparing bone metastatic, non-bone metastatic, and normal states). In vitro functional studies included experimental induction of BST2 expression in breast cancer cells. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were applicable or reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human breast cancer cell lines (e.g., MDA-231BO, MDA-231, MCF-10A), human breast tumor tissues, and human blood serum.
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA expression via microarray and RT-PCR), Protein Level (Western blot, immunohistochemistry, ELISA), and Functional Activity (Cell Migration, Cell Proliferation/Cell Cycle Progression).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The BST2 gene showed overexpression via cDNA microarray in bone metastatic breast cancer cell lines (MDA-231BO) compared to primary (MDA-231), with expression ratios ranging from 3.2 to 4.9. Gene and protein expression were significantly increased (P < 0.01 for mRNA) in bone metastatic breast cancer cell lines (MDA-231BO) compared to normal and non-bone metastatic lines via RT-PCR and Western blot. In human breast tumor tissues (TMA), 55% (11/20) of bone metastatic cases showed increased BST2 protein expression compared to 3.3% (1/30) of non-bone metastatic and 0% (0/8) of normal tissues (p < 0.0001). Serum BST2 levels measured by ELISA were significantly higher (P < 0.0001) in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis (mean absorption value 0.51 ± 0.15) compared to those without metastasis (0.24 ± 0.11) and healthy controls (0.22 ± 0.05), demonstrating 84% sensitivity and 93% specificity for metastasis. Furthermore, in vitro studies showed that induced BST2 expression in MDA-231 breast cancer cells led to significantly increased cell migration and an increased S-phase cell population, indicating higher cell proliferation (P < 0.01 for both); apoptosis was unchanged (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A transmembrane glycoprotein and bone marrow stromal protein that functions as a cell growth factor, mediating IL-6 response gene expression via the STAT3 pathway. It is involved in cell-cell interaction, tumor invasion, progression, and promotes breast cancer cell migration and proliferation, potentially contributing to osteoclastic bone destruction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Investigation of bone metastasis formation in human breast cancer; includes differential expression analysis comparing bone metastatic versus non-bone metastatic breast cancer cell lines, tumor tissues, and patient serum, as well as in vitro studies modulating BST2 expression to observe effects on breast cancer cell migration and proliferation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: BST2 is a promising sensitive and specific biomarker for the detection and diagnosis of early bone metastases in breast cancer, both in tissue and serum. Its upregulation is strongly associated with bone metastatic breast cancer and indicates a critical role in disease progression by promoting increased cancer cell migration and proliferation, thereby contributing to the metastatic potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified exclusively by MALDI MS. Listed as a widely used hiPSC/hESC marker.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly stated, inferred as related to pluripotency maintenance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pluripotency marker identification and proteome coverage expansion using MALDI MS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in SCT players (12.5            3.7) compared to CON (17.0            4.1; p = 0.003) at post-camp.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait at the post-camp period of pre-season training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: May be an early indicator of altered kidney function in SCT players, while a higher ratio in CON suggests chronic dehydration in control players during training camp, emphasizing the importance of fluid balance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

While no significant changes were observed in fecal pH, water content, ammonia, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), or plasma/urine malondialdehyde levels, the supplementation led to an increased abundance of the Bacteroidetes phylum and a decrease in health-related gut bacteria such as Roseburia, Blautia, and Bifidobacterium longum, suggesting a potentially negative impact on gut microbiota balance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in the MSC group on day 14 compared to control. Gradually decreased over the first 28 days in both groups. Positively correlated with lung fibrosis intensity on weeks 24 (r = 0.457, p ≤ 0.005) and 48 (r = 0.449, p ≤ 0.005).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 pneumonia after MSC therapy.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests reduced inflammatory response, improved maturation of neutrophils, and attenuation of the inflammatory process linked to lung fibrosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case-control study investigated plasma levels of 16 trace elements and 27 AMD-associated genetic variants in 236 individuals with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and 236 age-matched controls. The primary findings revealed significantly elevated plasma levels of barium and cadmium, and reduced levels of chromium in nAMD patients, suggesting that an imbalance of these trace elements, influenced by environmental and lifestyle factors, may play a role in nAMD pathogenesis. No association was found between the AMD-associated genetic variants and trace element levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational biomarker association study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Plasma levels of 16 trace elements (including arsenic, barium, calcium, cadmium, cobalt, chromium, copper, iron, magnesium, manganese, molybdenum, lead, antimony, selenium, vanadium, and zinc) were quantitatively measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in 236 nAMD patients and 236 age-matched controls. Two additional elements (Al, Ni) were initially measured but excluded due to inadequate accuracy/reproducibility. This was a cross-sectional, observational study, and no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported or applicable. Patients with nAMD may have received past anti-angiogenic drug injections, but details regarding dose, intensity, or duration were not the focus of this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean plasma concentrations were 1.35 μg/L (SD 0.71) in nAMD patients and 1.15 μg/L (SD 0.63) in controls (P = 0.001). In a multifactorial binary logistic regression model, Ba showed an Odds Ratio (OR) of 1.55 per μg/L for nAMD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Trace element involved in the regulation of oxidative stress and cellular antioxidant defense mechanisms. Can inhibit potassium channels and Na/K pump in RPE cells, potentially reducing blood flow in the choroid and molecular transport across RPE membranes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), with a trend towards association with antihypertensive drug usage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a potential role in nAMD pathogenesis, possibly through effects on blood flow and RPE function. May serve as a biomarker for disease risk and progression, and is associated with increased odds of having nAMD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the acute and 1-week effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on cardiovascular performance, autonomic control, endothelial function, and a range of molecular biomarkers (inflammatory, hormonal, oxidative stress, nitric oxide synthesis, and mitochondrial regulation) in physically inactive postmenopausal women (aged 50-70) with systemic arterial hypertension, both at rest, during submaximal aerobic exercise, and throughout recovery. The aim is to provide nutritional recommendations for optimizing cardiovascular health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with nitrate-rich beetroot juice combined with standardized submaximal aerobic exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice will be administered acutely at 140 mL (800 mg nitrate) on the first day, followed by a daily dose of 70 mL (400 mg nitrate) for 6 subsequent days. A placebo (nitrate-free) juice will serve as control. Exercise consists of a 40-minute treadmill session at a speed corresponding to 65-70% of VO2peak. The study employs a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled design with a 7-day washout period between intervention protocols. Previous research indicated lower doses (200-400 mg nitrate) were insufficient for acute cardiovascular effects, leading to the optimized dosages used here. Additionally, 40 g of whey protein will be provided before executing experimental protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased as a result of physical exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates blood pressure in response to changes in blood pressure.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Physical exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to better blood pressure regulation and is a valuable strategy for hypertensive patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of heart rate-matched (HR-matched) or work rate-matched (WR-matched) hypoxic interval exercise on post-exercise cardiac autonomic and cardiovascular responses compared to normoxic exercise in moderately trained men. Findings indicate that HR-matched hypoxic exercise mimicked post-exercise autonomic responses of normoxic exercise without inducing significant post-exercise hypotension (PEH) or impairing cardiac baroreflex sensitivity (cBRS). Conversely, WR-matched hypoxic exercise resulted in delayed cardiac autonomic recovery, a temporary decrease in cBRS, and prolonged PEH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hypoxic and Normoxic Interval Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed three interval-type exercise sessions (5x5-min work intervals; 1-min passive recovery) after a 5-min warm-up at 50% WR@VT1. Normoxic exercise (N) was at 80% of the work rate (WR) at the first ventilatory threshold (mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 139±10 bpm, ~75%HRmax). Hypoxic exercise (FiO2 = 14.2%, simulating ~3000m altitude) was performed either at the same absolute WR as N (H-WR, WR-matched: mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 154±11 bpm, ~83%HRmax) or at the same absolute HR as N (H-HR, HR-matched: mean WR 144±18 W, mean HR 138±9 bpm, ~75%HRmax). This resulted in a -21.1±9.3% reduction in WR for H-HR compared to N, and a higher HR (by ~15 bpm) for H-WR compared to N. Recovery was seated under normoxic conditions, with assessments at POST-15, POST-45, POST-60, and POST-90 minutes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased at POST-15 after all exercise sessions (time effect, p < 0.05) for both positive (n+) and negative (n-) sequences.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the frequency of baroreflex-mediated responses to blood pressure changes, indicating compensatory mechanisms.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery after Normoxic (N), HR-matched Hypoxic (H-HR), and WR-matched Hypoxic (H-WR) exercise sessions, at POST-15.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An increase suggests a more frequent occurrence of baroreflex sequences during early recovery, indicating an active compensatory mechanism to regulate blood pressure.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week concurrent endurance and strength training intervention on microRNA expression and Line-1 methylation in capillary blood of sedentary, healthy adults. It aimed to develop a miRNA-based 'fitness score' to assess individual responses to diet, metabolism, and exercise, identifying significantly altered miRNAs and anthropometric data, and their correlations with genetic polymorphisms (ACE, ACTN3, FTO), dietary intake, fluid intake, and stress levels, ultimately providing information for assessing individual health, performance, and recovery.

No specific intensity levels, frequencies, or detailed exercise modalities were provided, and no dose-response comparisons were reported. A healthy, age- and sex-matched control group (n=20) received no intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 3-year longitudinal study characterized the central vein sign (CVS) profiles in newly developing white matter lesions in Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients. It found that most new lesions were CVS+ (68%) and established that younger age and a higher baseline CVS+ percentage are associated with an increased likelihood of new CVS+ lesion development, thereby identifying CVS as a predictive radiologic biomarker for MS disease activity and informing clinical decisions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing the Central Vein Sign (CVS) as a diagnostic imaging biomarker in the context of Multiple Sclerosis lesion development and progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study followed adults with MS and healthy controls for a median of 3.1 years (Q1–Q3: 0.7–6.3 years). MRI scans were conducted on 3T Siemens or Philips scanners using specific submillimeter T2*-weighted, 3D millimetric T1-weighted MPRAGE/MP2RAGE, and 3D millimetric T2-weighted FLAIR sequences. The study did not involve specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons, though retrospective observations of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) changes were noted.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole brain MRI assessment of MS patients
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Imaging-based characteristic/predictor, quantified as a percentage of lesions that are CVS+.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Individuals with only new CVS+ lesions had a higher baseline CVS+ percentage compared with the other groups. The likelihood of CVS+ lesion development increased with higher baseline CVS+ percentage (OR = 1.5 per 10% increase in baseline CVS+ percentage, 95% CI = 1.1–1.9).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A diagnostic and prognostic imaging marker in Multiple Sclerosis, reflecting underlying venular inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Risk factor for CVS-stratified new lesion formation in MS patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher baseline CVS+ percentage is an indicator of ongoing disease activity and a predictor of future new CVS+ lesion formation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (hiPSCs), Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESCs), somatic cells

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Included in the list of 982 proteins up-regulated by at least 1.5-fold in hiPSCs compared to parental somatic cells, identified with >95% confidence and a maximum false discovery rate of 2%. Consistently up-regulated in early and late passage cells of both hiPSC lines (by ESI-MS e) and confirmed by Western blot analysis. All selected proteins were confirmed to be up-regulated in hiPSC and hESC compared to somatic cells. Quantification confirmed by Western blot analysis in the study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transmembrane glycoprotein; involved in cell adhesion, migration, and extracellular matrix remodeling; previously not used for hiPSC selection. Cell surface marker, associated with stemness maintenance and regulation of pluripotency.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of proteomic profiles during reprogramming of somatic cells to hiPSCs and between hiPSCs and hESCs. Proposed novel pluripotency marker identification and validation. Stemness maintenance and regulation of pluripotency in hESC and hiPSC, as a candidate for a protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential candidate for hiPSC surface marker, indicating pluripotency and stem cell identity. Candidate novel pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs. Potential marker for hiPSC characterization and quality control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, involved in allergic and inflammatory reactions.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of allergic reactions or inflammatory conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at T3 (congested period) compared with T2 and T1 (0.002 < p < 0.04, -0.78 < ES < -0.40); increases found throughout the observation period (both uncongested and congested). Individually, most players (n = 13) presented higher values at T3 compared to T1 and T2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Granulocyte involved in allergic and inflammatory responses, including histamine release.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout observation periods (congested and uncongested) of elite soccer match play.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Changes may indicate immune activation or stress related to intense training and competition, or allergic responses due to overall physiological stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negative large correlation with CMJ-free hands performance (r = -0.51, p = 0.008).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell involved in allergic reactions and inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase; correlation with Countermovement Jump (CMJ) performance.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower basophil percentage associated with better CMJ performance, suggesting certain inflammatory responses might negatively impact explosive power.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (with STING activation), lower (with IRE1α inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated in TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group (p < 0.05). Significantly downregulated by IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-apoptotic protein that promotes programmed cell death.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); modulated by STING activation (2'3'-cGAMP) or IRE1α inhibition (Kira6).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its upregulation indicates increased activation of apoptotic pathways, contributing to neuronal death. Its downregulation suggests reduced neuronal apoptosis and potential neuroprotection.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased by eIF3a silencing; downregulated by eIF3a overexpression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was increased (p < .01) upon eIF3a silencing and downregulated (p < .01) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-apoptotic protein, promotes apoptosis by inducing mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: eIF3a silencing or overexpression in CRC cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased levels indicate promotion of apoptosis; downregulation indicates inhibition of apoptosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inhibited the expression of the Bax gene.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nicorandil treatment in rats with ischemic heart failure (animal model context).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduces myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis by inhibiting cardiomyocyte apoptosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (with STING activation), higher (with IRE1α inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated in TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group (p < 0.01). Significantly upregulated by IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An anti-apoptotic protein that inhibits programmed cell death.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); modulated by STING activation (2'3'-cGAMP) or IRE1α inhibition (Kira6).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its downregulation indicates reduced cellular protection against apoptosis. Its upregulation suggests reduced neuronal apoptosis and potential neuroprotection.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased by eIF3a silencing; increased by eIF3a overexpression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was decreased (p < .01) upon eIF3a silencing and increased (p < .01) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels contribute to cancer cell death, while increased levels promote cancer cell survival.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic modifier investigation; Observational longitudinal study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is observational and investigates an intrinsic genetic factor, not an active therapeutic intervention. The 'dose' refers to the additive effects of the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage (0, 1, or 2 G alleles), which was modeled as a continuous variable. The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). No deviations from an additive effect were observed (heterozygosity indicator P > 0.05), and no traditional dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In C9orf72 symptomatic group longitudinally: stronger protective effect on behavior. No protective effects observed in GRN groups. The symptomatic C9orf72 group was the only group demonstrating additive protective effects of rs1990622 G on behaviour longitudinally.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved behavioral scores indicate a reduction in behavioral symptoms associated with FTD and better behavioral health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: rTMS could enhance high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Enhancement by rTMS might adjust neural communication within frontal-limbic circuits, improving mood stabilization and impulse control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

Only few shPW1 cells were detected in the muscle 1 month after injection. Majority of Ctl AdmMABs were localized in the interstitium after 6 h, whereas the shPW1 AdmMABs were still within the blood vessels. Very few labelled nuclei were associated with myofibres in the shPW1 AdmMABs-injected mice (1 month).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly elevated at baseline, showing a tendency toward improvement or slight recovery in some groups (e.g., young individuals), but with a high probability of sustained elevation.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), exceeding age-adjusted cut points (0.890 mg/g creatinine in 1998, 1.028 mg/g creatinine in 2006). Levels increased overall in some individuals (p < 0.01 in 2006). While some slight recovery was suggested (especially in young individuals), there was little evidence of complete recovery. Elevated  2-microglobulin in 1998 was a strong predictor for elevated levels in 2006 (OR = 24.8; 95% CI: 11.2, 55.3), significantly higher than for albumin (OR = 3.0) and NAG (OR = 2.6). Individuals with baseline urinary  2-microglobulin > 300  5g/g creatinine experienced a greater decline in eGFR after 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates renal tubular damage and impaired kidney function. It is a strong prognostic factor and a robust predictor of persistent and future tubular dysfunction, being more informative than NAG.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for a two-phase randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigating the efficacy and acceptability of high-frequency, low-load Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) in UK military personnel with lower limb musculoskeletal injuries where persistent pain is the primary limiting factor. Phase Two involves 21 BFR-RT sessions over 15 days (3 weeks) for the BFR group (n=26), utilizing the optimal LOP determined in Phase One. The control group in Phase Two receives usual care. document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study investigated the ergogenic effects of acute pre-exercise homemade chicken broth (CB) ingestion, rich in histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) like carnosine and anserine, on high-intensity cycling performance in recreationally-trained men. The study found a significant 5.2% improvement in 8-minute time trial mean power and elevated plasma carnosine and anserine levels following CB supplementation. The supplement was administered 25-40 minutes prior to an 8-minute high-intensity cycling time trial, following a warm-up. No dose-response comparisons were made, only CB versus placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the tissue origins of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in healthy mice using tissue-specific knockout models and its utility as a biomarker following paracetamol (APAP) overdose in both mice and humans. document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. Rehydration involved consuming either electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) or standard purified water (CON), with an equal volume equivalent to 2% of pre-exercise body weight (approximately 20 mL/kg), administered within 30 minutes. This was followed by a 120-minute (2-hour) recovery period. No dose-response comparisons or variations in rehydration volume/rate were reported beyond the two water types.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational cohort study utilized data from the ARIC study over 25 years to investigate whether middle-age serum sodium levels, as a proxy for habitual hydration, are associated with accelerated biological aging, chronic diseases (including heart failure, dementia, chronic lung disease, stroke, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and atrial fibrillation), and premature mortality. The study concluded that serum sodium levels exceeding 142 mmol/l, or outside the optimal 138–142 mmol/l range, are associated with increased risks of these adverse outcomes, suggesting that optimal hydration may slow the aging process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hydration Status Assessment (Observational Cohort Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational cohort study with no direct therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons. Habitual hydration status was inferred from fasting serum sodium concentrations, averaged from Visits 1 and 2 of the ARIC study participants. The normal serum sodium reference range was 135–146 mmol/l. The study identified specific thresholds: levels >142 mmol/l were associated with increased risk for chronic diseases and accelerated biological aging, and >144 mmol/l with elevated risk of premature mortality. The lowest risks were observed for serum sodium in the range of 138–142 mmol/l. Participants with serum sodium outside the 135–146 mmol/l range, plasma glucose >140 mg/dL, or BMI >35 kg/m2 were excluded.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher BA was associated with increased risk of chronic diseases (HR = 1.70, 95% CI:1.50–1.93) and premature mortality (HR = 1.59, 95% CI 1.39–1.83). Participants with serum sodium >142 mmol/l had up to 50% higher odds of being biologically older than their chronological age. For premature mortality, risk was 54% or 59% higher in the highest quartile (Q4) of BA and BA-Age compared to the lowest (Q1). For chronic diseases, biologically older participants (Q3 and Q4 of BA-Age) had up to 44% higher risk than the Q1 group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of an individual's physiological age compared to their chronological age, reflecting accumulated damage and functional decline over time and the overall speed of the aging process.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Calculated at middle-age (visit 2) in ARIC study participants and correlated with long-term outcomes, including premature mortality and development of chronic diseases up to ages 70–90 years, and its cross-sectional association with serum sodium levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A better predictor of future premature mortality and degenerative changes (chronic diseases) than chronological age, indicating accelerated aging and higher physiological deterioration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study develops and validates the GeroSense deep neural network model, which uses deep longitudinal phenotyping of wearable sensor data (physical activity patterns) to provide a high-quality and cost-effective alternative for Biological Age Acceleration (BAA) determination. The model's BAA metric quantifies human health state, predicts morbidity risk, and is associated with life expectancy, mortality, chronic diseases, life-shortening lifestyles, and COVID-19 incidence. The study also reveals that organism state recovery time (resilience), derived from BAA fluctuations, is an independent marker of aging and mortality, with its divergence increasing with chronological age.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Deep Learning Computational Modeling (GeroSense BAA model) for Biological Age Acceleration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The GeroSense BAA model was trained using deep neural networks on physical activity data (steps per minute) from wearable devices (smartphones, smartwatches) from 103,830 one-week longitudinal samples and 2,599 samples up to 2 years long. This input data, derived from 100Hz raw acceleration, was used for daily BAA predictions, with averaging over several weeks improving accuracy. The model was designed to decouple BAA from seasonal variations. The study focused on model development and validation for biomarker assessment; no interventional doses or dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Derived metric from wearable sensor data (physical activity patterns/steps per minute from smartphones/smartwatches)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Computational model output (Deep Artificial Neural Network), serving as a biological clock based on mortality risk

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher BAA is associated with increased morbidity and mortality risk, decreased resilience; comparable to blood-based BAA models; unchanged during COVID-19 lockdown
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exhibited superior association with life-expectancy over average daily steps; comparable association with lifestyles and diseases to blood-based models. Activity-based models' signal-to-noise ratio improved by averaging longer tracks, detecting chronic diseases/smoking effects similar to blood-based PhenoAge/DOSI. ROC AUC 0.60-0.61 for morbidity and 0.60-0.62 for mortality prediction. BAA distributions were indistinguishable between smartphone and smartwatch data (p=2E-5). BAA increase during COVID-19 lockdown was less significant (p>1E-10) than physical activity. Excess BAA predicted increased COVID-19 incidence risk (HR=2.4, p=4E-2). Recovery rate decreased age-dependently, vanishing at ages exceeding 100 years. Expressed in years of healthy life expectancy gained or lost.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Quantitative characterization of aging and indicator of morbidity risk; quantifies human health and biological aging; dynamic variable characteristic of stress, indicating an organism's ability to recover its equilibrium state (resilience); biological clock based on mortality risk, a measure of overall stress level and dynamic stability.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Deep neural networks trained on wearable 'steps per minute' for predicting morbidity/life expectancy; applicable for health risk assessment, life insurance, associations with chronic/non-chronic diseases, smoking, COVID-19 infection, aging process, and response to natural stresses/diseases. Predicted daily from 7 previous days of continuous step counts per minute from wearable devices; longitudinal analysis of BAA fluctuations and resilience across age cohorts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides a high-quality, cheap alternative for BAA determination, superiorly associated with life-expectancy; capable of detecting chronic disease effects comparable to blood-based biomarkers. Predicts death/disease incidence, acts as a superior indicator of life expectancy, and signifies organismal resilience and recovery rate from stress. Elevated BAA is associated with increased COVID-19 risk, indicating loss of resilience and approaching loss of dynamic stability, contributing to fatality.
