document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at 1 day and 3 days after TBI (p < 0.001). Cl-amidine treatment significantly decreased extravasation at 1 day (p < 0.05) and 3 days (p < 0.01) post-TBI compared to vehicle. Quantification by spectrophotometry at OD 620 nm.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Directly indicates BBB disruption, a critical pathological event in TBI that aggravates secondary injury. Attenuation by Cl-amidine indicates reduced secondary brain injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased from pre to post in all groups. Combined and progestin-only HC users returned to baseline, while naturally menstruating females remained significantly lower at recovery than pre
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Body fat % was significantly higher in naturally menstruating females than progestin-only HC users at pre (p=0.049). All three groups significantly decreased from pre to post (p<0.001). Combined HC users and progestin-only HC users returned to baseline after a significant increase (p<0.001) from post to recovery. Naturally menstruating females had significantly lower body fat % at recovery than pre (p=0.001) despite a significant increase from post to recovery (p<0.001). A significant group*time interaction observed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar reductions experienced by both sexes during the 21-week competition preparation and weight-loss period.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. The primary finding was that ALK water significantly reduced high-shear whole blood viscosity and enhanced its restoration to pre-exercise baseline levels compared to CON water, while other markers like plasma osmolality, bioimpedance, and body mass showed no significant difference.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral rehydration therapy after exercise-induced dehydration, comparing electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) with standard purified water (CON).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants exercised in a warm environment (30 °C, 70% relative humidity) until a 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight loss was achieved due to perspiration (mild dehydration). Rehydration involved consuming either electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) or standard purified water (CON), with an equal volume equivalent to 2% of pre-exercise body weight (approximately 20 mL/kg), administered within 30 minutes. This was followed by a 120-minute (2-hour) recovery period. No dose-response comparisons or variations in rehydration volume/rate were reported beyond the two water types.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: While 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight was lost during exercise-induced dehydration and 2% body weight was replaced during rehydration, no significant difference in body mass change was observed between electrolyzed high-pH water and standard purified water during the recovery period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Directly reflects the net fluid balance of the body, indicating the degree of dehydration or rehydration, and total body water losses and gains.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post exercise-induced dehydration during a 2-hour recovery period following rehydration with high-pH alkaline water compared to standard purified water.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary and accurate indicator for quantifying dehydration level and monitoring rehydration effectiveness; however, in this study, it did not differentiate between the two rehydration methods.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility and limitations of Body Mass Index (BMI) compared to Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)-derived percent body fat and fasting leptin and insulin levels for diagnosing and classifying obesity in adults. It concluded that BMI significantly underestimates obesity prevalence, especially in women and with advancing age, due to its inability to distinguish lean from fat mass. The study proposed new, lower gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) and found that leptin levels, unlike insulin, enhance the accuracy of BMI estimates for adiposity, particularly in women and when DXA is unavailable. The integration of leptin and DXA is suggested for more precise obesity characterization and management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Comparison and Biomarker Analysis for Obesity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional study conducted a retrospective review of BMI calculations, DXA scans, and fasting blood levels of leptin and insulin from 9,088 adults between 1998 and 2009. Measurements for BMI, DXA (providing simultaneous muscle, bone mass, and adiposity data), and blood work (fasting leptin and insulin drawn between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm) were taken within 3 weeks of each other. The study evaluated and compared the accuracy and classification rates of these metrics for obesity, proposing new gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) based on body fat and leptin corrections. No therapeutic intervention dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Calculated from whole-body anthropometric measurements (height and weight)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean BMI was 27.3 (SD = 5.9). BMI characterized 26% of subjects as obese, while DXA indicated 64% were obese. 39% of subjects classified as non-obese by BMI were found to be obese by DXA. BMI misclassified 25% of men and 48% of women. The study proposes a better cutpoint for obesity with BMI is 24 for females and 28 for males. Applying these new cutoffs, 64.1% of American women would be classified as obese, compared to current NHANES estimates of 35.5% (BMI >30 kg/m2).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indirect, imprecise mathematical estimate of body fat based on height and weight, failing to distinguish lean body mass from fat mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Obesity classification in adults and population health policy, particularly when compared against more accurate measures like DXA and leptin.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An inaccurate obesity classification method that systematically underestimates obesity prevalence and adiposity, especially in women and with advancing age, contributing to failed treatment and underestimation of associated comorbidities (e.g., hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes). Less precise than direct adiposity measures in predicting medical comorbidities, although improved cut-points can enhance prediction of all-cause mortality.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Remained unchanged throughout the 6-week study duration.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of overall body weight and adiposity status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following dietary intervention with micronutrient supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests the intervention did not influence overall body weight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the sex-specific relationships among total serum cholinesterase activity (CS), high-sensitive cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), and traditional hemodynamic parameters of autonomic nervous system function during exercise in apparently healthy individuals. Key findings include a positive association between serum CS and hs-cTnT detection in women, an inverse association in men, and sex-dependent predictions of exercise-hemodynamic changes and metabolic impairment by CS, providing insights for cardiovascular disease risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study using Cardiac Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent a standard Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST) according to the Bruce protocol. The study was observational, investigating associations between biomarkers and hemodynamic changes during this test; no specific therapeutic 'dose' or 'duration' of an intervention was applied or compared. Hypertensive reactions were defined as peak SBP > 205 mm/Hg in men and > 187 mm/Hg in women. Heart rate recovery rate was calculated from peak rate to recovery time.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Not applicable (calculated from height and weight)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Trend analysis revealed elevated BMI across sex-specific quartiles of CS in men (p for trend = 0.019) and women (p for trend = 0.018).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body fatness, used to categorize individuals into weight status categories (e.g., underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed during routine annual checkups, and evaluated in relation to cholinergic status.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher BMI is a risk factor for various health conditions, including metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, prospective observational study investigated whether vitamin D metabolites (25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) and Vitamin D Binding Protein (VDBP), along with their ratios, could predict preeclampsia (PE) in women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM). The study found that higher concentrations of 1,25(OH)2D, lower concentrations of VDBP, and elevated 1,25(OH)2D/VDBP ratios in the second and third trimesters were significantly associated with and predictive of subsequent PE, while 25(OH)D, the standard metric for vitamin D status, did not predict PE.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal Prospective Observational Study on Preeclampsia Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons. Biomarker concentrations and clinical data were collected at three gestational visits: V1 (~12 weeks), V2 (~22 weeks), and V3 (~32 weeks). The study enrolled 151 women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM) and 24 non-diabetic controls, rigorously phenotyped and free of proteinuria and hypertension at enrolment. The primary analysis compared 23 T1DM women who developed preeclampsia (PE) with 24 matched T1DM women who remained normotensive. A secondary analysis compared normotensive T1DM women with non-diabetic controls. The cohort was largely vitamin D insufficient or deficient.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in T1DM women with PE (DM+PE+) than in normotensive T1DM women (DM+PE−) at the initial study visit.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A measure of body fat based on height and weight, used to classify individuals into weight categories.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Initial study visit in pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM), associated with preeclampsia (PE) risk.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of obesity, which is a risk factor for preeclampsia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of low (LV-HIIT) and high (HV-HIIT) volumes of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on vascular-endothelial function, oxidative stress, and atherosclerosis markers in patients after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The 16-week supervised HIIT programs, regardless of volume, led to a volume-dependent enhancement in endothelial function (FMD) and a decrease in oxidative stress (ox-LDL). A reduction in vascular wall thickness (cIMT) was also observed, with LV-HIIT proving sufficient to initiate favorable adaptations and reduce cardiovascular risk. The study also assessed anthropometric and other cardiovascular markers, comparing HIIT groups to an active control.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Unsupervised Physical Activity Recommendations (Active Control, AC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) with two volumes: Low Volume (LV-HIIT) and High Volume (HV-HIIT), and an Active Control (AC) group. LV-HIIT involved 8 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-minute total session. HV-HIIT involved 16 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-40 minute total session. Both supervised HIIT groups exercised 2 non-consecutive days per week for 16 weeks (32 sessions) on treadmills and cycle ergometers, with intensity individualized based on cardiorespiratory fitness, ventilatory thresholds, beat-to-beat HR, and the Böarg scale. The AC group received individualized recommendations for unsupervised physical activity, advised to perform at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity 5–7 days per week for 16 weeks. FMD and ox-LDL changes were volume-dependent (HV-HIIT showing greater effects), while cIMT reduction was similar between LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT, indicating a volume-independent effect for cIMT and confirming LV-HIIT's effectiveness.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: LV-HIIT group exhibited a mild reduction (-1.6 ± 0.9%, p = 0.046). Body mass remained unaffected in all groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of body fatness and overall body composition relative to height, used to assess obesity-related health risks.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 16-week Low-Volume High-Intensity Interval Training (LV-HIIT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates improved body composition, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health and reduces risks associated with obesity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-sectional Study for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the 2019 general physical examination of 3,280 rural Chinese residents aged 45 years and older. No experimental interventions or therapeutic doses were administered; the study focused on observational correlations between biomarkers and cIMT. It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Participants categorized as underweight (<18.5 kg/m  ), normal (18.5-24 kg/m  ), overweight (24-28 kg/m  ), and obese (  28 kg/m  ).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates healthy weight for height.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional health examination.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with various health risks including metabolic disorders and cardiovascular diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of early first-trimester tubular (urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1) and glomerular (eGFR) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). It concluded that elevated first-trimester urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc) and, to a lesser extent, eGFR, are associated with increased PE risk. Notably, uNGALcc, especially when combined with clinical factors like BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin, significantly improved PE prediction, indicating subclinical renal tubular and glomerular dysfunction as early markers of PE, while urinary KIM-1 and plasma NGAL were not predictive.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on diagnostic biomarker assessment for preeclampsia risk prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a prospective observational cohort study enrolling pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) and normotensive pregnant women without diabetes. Biomarkers were assessed at three gestational visits: V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks), V2 (21.7  1 1.4 weeks), and V3 (31.4  1 1.5 weeks), with primary focus on first-trimester (V1) values for preeclampsia (PE) prediction. Study groups included women with T1DM who developed PE (DM+PE+), T1DM women who remained normotensive (DM+PE-), and normotensive women without diabetes (DM-). All T1DM subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria at V1. No active intervention or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic/prognostic utility. Analysis included samples with specific attention to leukocyte-negative urine samples.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in DM+PE+ than in DM+PE 2 at V1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body composition and overall health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and subsequent Preeclampsia (DM+PE+), compared to those without Preeclampsia (DM+PE 2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as a covariate in the mathematical model to predict PE risk; associated with distinguishing clinical characteristics between DM+PE+ and DM+PE 2 groups at V1.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week (3-month) food-based vitamin D3 fortification intervention on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, bone turnover markers (Osteocalcin, Bone specific Alkaline Phosphatase, Procollagen type 1 amino-terminal propeptide, C-terminal crosslinked telopeptide of type 1 collagen), and muscle strength (handgrip, knee extension, chair-standing) in 143 women of Danish and Pakistani origin, aged 18-50 years, living in Denmark and at risk of vitamin D deficiency. Despite a significant increase in serum 25(OH)D concentrations in the fortified groups, the intervention did not result in significant changes in bone turnover markers or muscle strength. Baseline characteristics including anthropometrics and vitamin D status were also assessed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Food-based vitamin D fortification
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 12-week (3-month) randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled winter intervention trial. The intervention group (143 women) received 30 μg vitamin D3/day (analyzed as 29 μg/day total vitamin D content) through fortified daily foods (150g yoghurt, 60g cheese, 1 egg, 1 small crisp-bread); the placebo group received similar non-fortified products. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and the study noted potential insufficient power to detect changes in secondary endpoints.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in women of Pakistani origin
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: slightly higher in women of Pakistani origin compared to Danish origin (P < 0.001)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body mass relative to height, associated with body composition and health risks.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline comparison between women of Danish and Pakistani origin.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates ethnic disparities in body mass index, potentially linked to metabolic health risks.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.18) or without pDPN group (P = 0.19); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.24).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body fatness and overall body composition status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change in overall body composition.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls; positively associated with AGEs in the entire cohort and in control subjects

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body fatness and obesity
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis; correlation with AGEs in general population and healthy controls
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes and glycemic control/insulin resistance

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: RAISE-ETP patients had a higher mean BMI (27.06 [6.85]) compared to EUFEST patients (22.04 [3.17]). In RAISE-ETP, patients with an increase in CDSS scores (+\u0394CDSS) at 6 months had a significantly higher baseline BMI; specific quantitative difference for this association is not detailed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body composition, energy balance, and metabolic health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline characteristic of patients in RAISE-ETP and EUFEST clinical trials; associated with an increase in depressive symptoms (+\u0394CDSS) at 6 months in RAISE-ETP.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with various health outcomes; in this context, it serves as a patient characteristic linked to psychopathological variables and predictive of changes in clinical depression scores.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study established robust reference intervals for plasma dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated Matrix Gla-Protein (dp-ucMGP) in a metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population using the IDS-iSYS Ina Ktif assay. It investigated dp-ucMGP's utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The findings indicate a significant stepwise increase in plasma dp-ucMGP levels from healthy individuals to those with DM without DKD, and further to those with DKD. Higher dp-ucMGP levels were associated with renal function decline and demonstrated predictive value for DKD diagnosis and progression, showing similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting renal function decline. Additionally, the study explored associations of dp-ucMGP with various clinical parameters in healthy volunteers, noting gender differences and correlations with BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study (Observational)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on establishing reference intervals and evaluating the diagnostic potential of plasma dp-ucMGP across different health states (healthy, diabetes mellitus, diabetic kidney disease). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted within this study. However, the document discusses external studies on Vitamin K2 supplementation (e.g., 6 weeks of daily supplementation or 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days) as a potential therapy impacting dp-ucMGP levels.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher; increasing BMI was associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increasing BMI was associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP in a regression model in both HVs and participants with DM. Significant (albeit mild) correlations observed. Increased from low to high tertile of dp-ucMGP (Swiss study).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body fatness and overall body composition, associated with metabolic health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General health assessment in healthy volunteers and participants with diabetes; metabolically healthy Caucasian population.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Risk factor for metabolic conditions; its increase is associated with higher dp-ucMGP levels, suggesting a potential link between weight status, vitamin K status, and long-term vascular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. The key finding is that obesity largely explains the observed association between IR and AN, with no direct causal relationship found between IR and AN when obesity is accounted for, highlighting AN's utility as a non-invasive clinical marker for obesity-driven cardiometabolic risk and its ability to predict future Type 2 Diabetes risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating cardiometabolic risk factors and a diagnostic marker
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention or dose administered. Data was collected from 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children aged 6–17 years from a family-based cohort, focusing on associations and the utility of Acanthosis Nigricans as a screening tool for cardiometabolic risk factors, including extensive clinical tests and interviews on medical history, demographic, phenotypic, and environmental variables.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole body (derived from anthropometric measurements of height and weight)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: positively correlated; identified as a direct contributor and attenuator of other relationships
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively/significantly correlated with AN-q (p<0.05). High rates of overweight (19.1%) and obesity (34%) were found in the study population. AN-q exhibited a linear trend with BMI (ANOVA for linear trend p < 0.001). A partial mediation model where BMI explained the relationship with both HOMA-IR and AN-q simultaneously had a better goodness-of-fit. BMI was associated with AN-q and HOMA-IR, mediating most of the associations with CMRFs. BMI had a partial effect, not only on IR and AN, but also on inflammation, blood pressure, lipids and physical fitness. Obesity (measured by BMI) is a direct contributor to AN, hyperinsulinemia, and other CMRFs; attenuation by BMI is shown for various phenotypic functions (e.g., hsCRP, triglycerides).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of body fatness and obesity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Observational study in non-diabetic Mexican American children, examined as a cardiometabolic risk factor; association with AN-q, HOMA-IR, and cardiometabolic risk factors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of overweight/obesity; identified as a primary driver of cardiometabolic risk, directly influencing insulin resistance, AN, inflammation, blood pressure, lipids, and physical fitness, with effects often mediating other factors. Directly linked to increased cardiometabolic risk, AN, and hyperinsulinemia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. The primary finding was that ALK water significantly reduced high-shear whole blood viscosity and enhanced its restoration to pre-exercise baseline levels compared to CON water, while other markers like plasma osmolality, bioimpedance, and body mass showed no significant difference.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral rehydration therapy after exercise-induced dehydration, comparing electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) with standard purified water (CON).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants exercised in a warm environment (30 °C, 70% relative humidity) until a 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight loss was achieved due to perspiration (mild dehydration). Rehydration involved consuming either electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) or standard purified water (CON), with an equal volume equivalent to 2% of pre-exercise body weight (approximately 20 mL/kg), administered within 30 minutes. This was followed by a 120-minute (2-hour) recovery period. No dose-response comparisons or variations in rehydration volume/rate were reported beyond the two water types.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean values for vital signs were similar between the high-pH alkaline water and standard water groups, with no clinically significant abnormal values observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of thermoregulation and metabolic state.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise rehydration with alkaline water compared to control water.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly affected by the type of rehydration water (alkaline vs. control) in this context, suggesting no differential impact on thermoregulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of the body's internal temperature.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of fever, inflammation, and recovery from COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: The STEPWISE randomized controlled trial investigated the effectiveness of a group-based structured lifestyle education program for weight reduction in adults with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or first-episode psychosis. The 12-month intervention aimed to promote clinically relevant weight loss and improve physical activity, diet, and biomedical measures. However, the study found no significant difference in mean weight reduction between the intervention and control groups (mean difference 0.0 kg, P=0.963), and no significant changes in physical activity, dietary intake, or biochemical measures were observed. Ultimately, the intervention was neither clinically nor cost-effective for weight management in this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Structured lifestyle education program (STEPWISE)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 12-month STEPWISE intervention comprised a foundation course of four weekly 2.5-hour group sessions, followed by bi-weekly 10-minute 1:1 telephone support contacts, and three additional 2.5-hour group booster sessions at approximately 4, 7, and 10 months post-randomization. The total intended intervention duration was approximately 25.5 hours, with a maximum of 17.5 hours of face-to-face contact. Participant adherence varied, with a mean attendance of 2.7 foundation sessions and 1.4 booster sessions; 53.6% attended ">"=3 foundation sessions and ">"=1 booster session, while 17.4% attended no sessions. Support was primarily via telephone. The study reported no significant difference in weight reduction between the intervention and control ('treatment as usual') groups and found no association between total contact time and weight loss. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported within the trial, though intervention intensity was discussed relative to other studies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: No significant differential change between intervention and control groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean reduction of 0.47 kg in the intervention group and 0.51 kg in the control group (difference = 0.0 kg, 95% CI -1.6 to 1.7, P = 0.963). Weight reduction increased by 0.8 kg per 10 additional years of age (95% CI 0.0 to 1.5 kg, P = 0.042). Participants with schizoaffective disorder had greater mean weight loss (-2.7 kg) compared to first-episode psychosis (-0.3 kg) or schizophrenia (+0.01 kg; P = 0.023).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents overall energy balance and an indicator of metabolic health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Weight management during a 12-month STEPWISE intervention in individuals with mental health conditions (schizoaffective disorder, first-episode psychosis, schizophrenia).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary indicator of the intervention's effectiveness for weight reduction and overall health status in the studied population.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in both groups following 14 days of HDBR, with no significant difference between groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall body mass, indicative of energy balance and fluid status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 14 days of Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR) with or without an exercise countermeasure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General health status; significant decrease can indicate fluid loss or catabolism during bed rest.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CON players experienced greater body weight loss (−1.3            1.1 kg; −1.0            0.9% body weight) and % body weight changes compared to SCT players (−0.9            0.9 kg; −0.8            0.8% body weight; all p < 0.001) during pre-season training camp.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of fluid balance during physical activity, reflecting net fluid loss from the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NCAA Division I American football players during pre-season training camp practices under hot and humid conditions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: SCT players exhibited less body weight loss, suggesting an improved fluid balance compared to CON players during pre-season training camp practices, potentially due to better hydration practices or physiological adaptations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Acute decrease; greater than −2% body mass

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects changes in total body water, mainly due to water losses (sweating, urination).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Evaluation of degree of dehydration; taken before exercise in a euhydrated state.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Greater than −2% body mass is linked to decreases in exercise/sport performance, cognitive function, mood, and increases in risk of exertional heat illness or exertional heatstroke for individuals exercising in hot and humid environments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase observed in both pDPN group (P < 0.01) and without pDPN group (P < 0.0001); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.28). Overall significant gain (P < 0.005).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: General physiological parameter reflecting metabolic status and energy balance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intensive glycemic control (with exenatide/pioglitazone or insulin) over a 1-year follow-up in type 2 diabetes patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a side effect of the intensive glycemic control regimen, as weight gain can be associated with certain diabetes treatments. Bodyweight gain was negatively associated with corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD), with every 2-kg increase in bodyweight corresponding to a 1 fiber/mm decrease in CNFD (P = 0.0501).

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to evaluate bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome (NS) to understand their bone status and explore genotype-phenotype correlations. It revealed increased bone resorption in NS patients, evidenced by significantly elevated serum C-telopeptides of type I collagen (CTX) levels, and a non-significant increase in RANKL. The study also discussed the influence of RAS/MAPK signaling pathway alterations and SHP2 protein on osteoclastic activity and the effects of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment on bone parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Case-Control Study evaluating bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome, including an analysis of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment effects.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional, case-control study compared 28 children with Noonan Syndrome to 35 healthy controls. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was administered to the main cohorts. Within the NS cohort, some subjects had received or were receiving rhGH therapy, but no specific dosages, duration, or dose-response comparisons for rhGH treatment were reported, and no significant differences in bone parameters were found between treated and untreated subjects in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference found between NS patients and controls. A positive correlation was observed between BMD Z-score and BALP levels (r = 0.640; p = 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone formation marker secreted by osteoblasts, reflecting osteoblast activity and involvement in mineralization.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children with Noonan Syndrome (NS), including correlation with bone mineral density.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not a significant indicator of altered bone formation in this cohort in direct comparison to controls, but higher levels are associated with better bone mineral density.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study found that while bone turnover markers (CTX and BAP) decreased in both K citrate and placebo groups, K citrate significantly enhanced these beneficial effects, particularly in a subgroup of patients with pre-existing low-grade acidosis (low urine pH and/or low potassium and citrate excretion). K citrate also improved urinary pH, citrate, and potassium excretion. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Potassium Citrate (K citrate) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Daily oral supplementation with 30 mEq of K citrate (in two tablets) for 6 months. This was administered in addition to daily calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹) for all subjects (K citrate and placebo groups). The K citrate treatment showed significant benefits in subjects with evidence of low-grade acidosis (low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH) compared to the placebo, with significant changes observed as early as 3 months. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported, and adherence rates were approximately 90% for both groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased significantly in both K citrate and placebo groups. In patients with low 24h-citrate excretion at baseline, a 30% mean decrease was observed at 6 months. A 25% reduction was evident in patients with low fasting-morning urine citrate, and a 25% reduction in patients with low fasting-morning urine pH. Changes in BAP in the last three-month period were significantly different only in subjects with a low pH in fasting-morning urine. More pronounced decrease after K citrate supplementation was observed in subjects with low urine pH and/or low citrate excretion, compared to calcium and vitamin D alone. These changes were similar to those observed after antiresorptive drugs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of bone formation, reflecting the activity of osteoblasts (bone-forming cells) and bone matrix maturation. It is an isoenzyme of alkaline phosphatase specific to osteoblasts.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: K citrate (30 mEq day   ⁻¹) supplementation for 6 months, combined with calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹), in postmenopausal women with osteopenia, particularly those with low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH at baseline, and those receiving calcium and vitamin D treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A decrease indicates reduced bone formation. In the context of accelerated bone loss with increased turnover, a reduction in both resorption and formation markers suggests a rebalancing of bone remodeling towards a healthier state and a beneficial effect on bone health. Reflects bone remodeling unit (BRU) activity and correlates with bone loss. Considered a useful tool for assessing response to anti-osteoporotic drugs, with decreased levels indicating opposition to bone loss progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week (3-month) food-based vitamin D3 fortification intervention on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, bone turnover markers (Osteocalcin, Bone specific Alkaline Phosphatase, Procollagen type 1 amino-terminal propeptide, C-terminal crosslinked telopeptide of type 1 collagen), and muscle strength (handgrip, knee extension, chair-standing) in 143 women of Danish and Pakistani origin, aged 18-50 years, living in Denmark and at risk of vitamin D deficiency. Despite a significant increase in serum 25(OH)D concentrations in the fortified groups, the intervention did not result in significant changes in bone turnover markers or muscle strength. Baseline characteristics including anthropometrics and vitamin D status were also assessed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Food-based vitamin D fortification
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 12-week (3-month) randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled winter intervention trial. The intervention group (143 women) received 30 μg vitamin D3/day (analyzed as 29 μg/day total vitamin D content) through fortified daily foods (150g yoghurt, 60g cheese, 1 egg, 1 small crisp-bread); the placebo group received similar non-fortified products. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and the study noted potential insufficient power to detect changes in secondary endpoints.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant change after 12 weeks of vitamin D fortification (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of bone turnover, particularly bone formation, reflecting bone remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12-week intervention with vitamin D fortified foods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone formation activity and overall bone health. Lack of significant change suggests the intervention did not notably affect bone formation, possibly due to adequate baseline vitamin D status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 2-year prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in bone remodeling and turnover markers in children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from diagnosis through chemotherapy. It revealed that ALL onset significantly slows bone remodeling, with significantly lower bone turnover markers at diagnosis compared to controls. During chemotherapy, particularly the induction phase, these markers increased, suggesting a recovery of bone turnover, and a potential balance in active bone remodeling by the end of therapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Risk-adapted multiagent antileukemic chemotherapy, specifically for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), including Glucocorticoid (GC) therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 2-year prospective longitudinal study involved chemotherapy according to international AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 and ESPhALL 2017 protocols, with patients stratified by risk (standard, intermediate, high). The treatment included induction, reinduction/delayed intensification (two phases of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy), and a maintenance phase. Blood sampling was conducted at 5 time points (T0-T4) from diagnosis until treatment cessation. No specific numerical drug dosages were reported, but it was noted that different glucocorticoid doses did not significantly alter bone marker profiles after intensive therapy phases.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: initially lower at diagnosis compared to controls, then increased during treatment
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower at diagnosis compared to controls (p < 0.001), then showed a significant increase during treatment from 26.7 µg/L at onset to 67.6 µg/L at T3 (p = 0.004), particularly at T0-T1 (end-of-induction).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme marker specifically reflecting osteoblast activity and bone formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls, and during treatment phases (T0-T4, especially during induction T0-T1, and up to T3).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates decreased bone formation at the onset of leukemia, followed by an increase during induction chemotherapy, reflecting changes in osteoblast activity and overall slowed bone remodeling, suggesting an attempt at bone turnover recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute response of serum sclerostin and bone turnover biomarkers (B-ALP, CTX) to a single session of whole-body vibration (WBV) exercise, both with and without blood flow restriction (BFR), in healthy untrained adult males. The findings indicated that adding BFR to WBV did not significantly affect serum sclerostin or CTX levels up to 24 hours post-exercise. However, a differential response was observed for bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (B-ALP), which was significantly lower 24 hours post-exercise in the combined WBV and BFR group compared to WBV alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Whole-body Vibration (WBV) exercise with and without Blood Flow Restriction (BFR)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two experimental conditions: (i) WBV alone, consisting of ten 1-minute bouts of whole-body vibration (30 Hz frequency, 2 mm peak-to-peak displacement, 3.6 g peak acceleration) with 30-second recovery between bouts. Participants stood barefoot in an isometric semi-squat position (130° knee angle). (ii) WBV with lower-body Blood Flow Restriction (BFR). For the WBV+BFR condition, a 13-cm-wide pneumatic cuff was applied to each thigh and inflated to 110 mmHg (estimated ~60% blood flow restriction) for the entire 1-minute duration of each vibration bout, with full deflation during the 30-second recovery intervals. No dose-response comparisons for varying WBV parameters or BFR pressure were reported within the study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (with WBV+BFR compared to WBV alone)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A significant condition × time interaction was observed (p<0.001; ηp2=0.49). Serum B-ALP values at 24 hours post-exercise were significantly higher following whole-body vibration (WBV) alone compared to combined whole-body vibration and blood flow restriction (WBV+BFR) (p=0.028, d=0.31).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of bone formation, reflecting osteoblast activity in bone mineralization and overall bone remodeling activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute bout of whole-body vibration (WBV) compared to combined Whole-body Vibration and Blood Flow Restriction (WBV+BFR), specifically 24 hours post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Significantly lower B-ALP with combined WBV+BFR compared to WBV alone at 24 hours post-exercise suggests that adding BFR to WBV may not provide an additive or beneficial osteogenic effect, and might even acutely reduce bone formation indicated by this marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. The investigation focused on age-dependent differences in scaffold properties and their influence on BM-MSC osteogenic differentiation, rather than dose-response comparisons of a therapeutic agent.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Structural assessment (3D analysis of micro-CT images)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Various changes related to density, surface area, and interconnectedness
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Older donor bone exhibited altered microarchitecture, including lower bone volume/total volume (BV/TV), higher trabecular separation (Tb.Sp), lower trabecular number (Tb.N), and reduced trabecular lattice interconnectedness, indicating increased porosity compared to young donor bone. Trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) showed no significant change.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Provides detailed information on bone morphology, including topography, pore size, and porosity, which influence cell infiltration and osteoinduction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of decellularized bone allograft structural properties based on donor age (young vs. old).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Crucial for predicting the mechanical stability and osteoinductive capacity of the scaffold; age-related differences may impact clinical applicability, with increased porosity in older bone potentially being beneficial for cell integration.
