document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated plasma glycoprotein non-metastatic melanoma protein B (gpNMB) and glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) concentrations in a cohort of patients with Gaucher disease (GD1, GD3, GD1-PD), idiopathic Parkinson's disease (IPD), and GBA heterozygous PD, alongside healthy controls. The primary aim was to explore gpNMB's relationship to Gaucher disease severity, clinical phenotypes (neurological, pulmonary, liver disease, monoclonal gammopathy), and treatment status. Findings revealed significantly elevated plasma gpNMB levels in Gaucher disease patients compared to controls (mean: 200.9 vs. 35.1 ng/ml), which remained high even after prolonged enzyme replacement therapy. Higher gpNMB concentrations were notably associated with splenectomy, pulmonary disease, liver disease (including fibrosis and cirrhosis), and monoclonal gammopathy. Additionally, gpNMB levels were elevated in Parkinsonism patients with type 1 GD compared to GBA1 heterozygotes or IPD (p=0.0001). The study also highlighted gpNMB's good diagnostic performance for GD (AUC 0.894), and its significant positive correlations with other established GD biomarkers (GlcSph, Chitotriosidase, CCL18, ACE), suggesting its potential as a supportive biomarker for residual disease activity, disease complications, and clinical stratification, although it does not differentiate between neuronopathic GD subtypes or idiopathic PD. The study also reviewed other diagnostic markers like acid β-glucosidase activity and GBA1 mutation analysis, noting their utility and limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) and Substrate Reduction Therapy (SRT), including macrophage-targeted enzyme therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients received ERT or SRT for varying durations: mean 14.6 ± 6.9 years (range: 1–29 years) for ERT, and 10.1 ± 7.5 years (range: 6 months–23 years) for SRT. Plasma gpNMB concentrations showed an inverse correlation with treatment duration during the first 5 years of specific therapy (rho= -0.470, p= 0.024) but no correlation after 10 years. gpNMB levels remained elevated in GD1 patients on ERT for over 5 years, and no statistical difference was observed between treated GD1 and GD3 patients. Glucosylsphingosine concentrations declined with ERT or SRT. No explicit dose-response comparisons for ERT or SRT were reported, though it was noted that therapeutic response may vary across Gaucher disease subtypes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Weakly correlated with gpNMB concentrations (rho: 0.337, p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Clinical assessment tool to quantify the extent of Gaucher cell infiltration and disease impact on bone marrow, often derived from imaging.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Gaucher Disease patients, particularly in the late treatment phase.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Represents disease severity in bone marrow; its weak correlation with gpNMB suggests gpNMB may not be a strong indicator of this specific severity measure in treated patients, possibly due to late treatment phase.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Bone mineral density assessment (standardized score); Bone Mineral Density

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes were observed in either COMP group from PRE to MID or in any group from MID to POST. Scores remained stable for female COMP participants (from 0.68 	0.85 to 0.68 	0.84) and for male COMP participants (from 0.75 	1.13 to 0.74 	1.15 / 0.78 	1.02). This stability was observed despite low energy availability and reduced IGF-1 levels during the 21-week competition preparation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates bone health and strength, serving as a standardized measure of deviation from age and sex-matched norms. Strength training is known to protect bone mineral content and density.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During the 21-week competition preparation period involving low energy availability and reduced IGF-1 levels, and during the subsequent recovery phase.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A stable Z-score indicates maintenance of bone health, suggesting that a 21-week weight loss period may not negatively impact bone mineral density in physique athletes, potentially due to engagement in extensive strength training. This is important for long-term health and injury prevention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Overall bone mass / Bone mineral density

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Loss of overall bone mass, reduction in bone mineral density (e.g., osteopenia) (cited in 12).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant brain edema observed at 1 and 3 days after TBI (p < 0.001). Significantly decreased by Cl-amidine treatment at 1 day (p < 0.05) and 3 days (p < 0.001) post-TBI compared to vehicle.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in both nicorandil and conventional treatment groups (P < 0.05); more significantly decreased in the nicorandil group compared to conventional treatment (P < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: \u03b3 Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS)

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the regulation of 23 blood-based biomarkers (including CK, IL-6, IL-17A, S100A8, BDNF, CD163, IL-1ß, and LDH) in 35 male elite athletes (badminton and soccer players) across different recovery-stress states. The primary aim was to identify markers responsive to habitual loading microcycles compared to recovered states. Key findings indicated that Creatine Kinase (CK), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) were generally higher in non-recovered states. S100A8 levels were significantly lower in non-recovered badminton players, while Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) levels were lower in non-recovered soccer players. Statistical trends were also observed for CD163 and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1ß). The study concludes that these discipline-specific biomarker responses are potentially useful for monitoring exercise and recovery to prevent overtraining and injury, though further validation is needed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise Training / Habitual Loading Microcycles
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared blood biomarker levels in elite male athletes (badminton and soccer players) during two states: 'recovered' (REC, after at least one day of rest from exercise) and 'non-recovered' (NOR, after a habitual loading microcycle). The habitual loading involved intensive, sport-specific training. For badminton players, this included four consecutive days with up to two sessions per day (50-310 min of moderate to intensive exercise daily). For soccer players, it involved high-intensity sessions with strenuous small-sided games, with at least two sessions within 48 hours. Blood samples for the NOR state were taken 12-16 hours after the last training session. The specific training content within microcycles varied and was not precisely controlled, reflecting real-world conditions. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training loads were reported within the context of the main findings, although external references to other exercise bouts (e.g., marathon, duathlon, interval training) were used to characterize biomarker behavior generally.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In soccer players, significantly lower in non-recovered (NOR) state (32,199.5  1 6058.8 pg/mL) compared to recovered (REC) state (33,907.4  1 5795.7 pg/mL) (p = 0.043; mean difference -1707.9 pg/mL, 95% CI [-3354.1, -61.7]). This contrasts with transient increases typically seen after acute exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A growth factor regulating development, maintenance, and plasticity of neuronal networks; a key component of the hypothalamic pathway and supports neuronal growth, survival, and differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-recovered state after a habitual loading microcycle in soccer players, contrasting with acute exercise responses but consistent with longer-term intense aerobic training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a sport-specific biomarker alteration in soccer players, potentially related to neurotrophic support and recovery processes, mediating positive effects of regular physical activity on central nervous system structure and function, and useful for monitoring recovery-stress cycles.

document_context_data.document_summary: Investigation of the relationship between serum levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and the number of T2/FLAIR lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, finding an inverse correlation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Biomarker Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Comparison between 28 MS patients (18-50 years old, median 38) and 28 healthy controls (19-49 years old, median 33). BDNF levels measured by ELISA. T2/FLAIR lesions quantified by MRI. No therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced in MS patients (median 1160 pg/mL, range 352.6-2640) compared to healthy controls (median 1640 pg/mL, range 632.4-4268; P = 0.03, Mann-Whitney test). Negatively correlated with T2/FLAIR lesions (r = -0.41; P = 0.02, Spearman correlation test).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neurotrophin related to neuronal development and survival; has a putative protective role in neurodegenerative diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients, specifically in correlation with the number of T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions identified by MRI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: May be a promising biomarker for MS disease activity and progression; indicates potential reduced neuroprotection and is inversely associated with demyelination and neuronal damage as reflected by T2/FLAIR lesion load.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. It further characterized 56 proteins with sustained changes, linking them to cardiometabolic traits and responses to a 20-week aerobic exercise training program. The research aimed to biochemically characterize acute exercise protein kinetics, finding enrichment for coagulation-related proteins post-exercise and MYC targets, and noting both concordant and discordant protein responses between acute and chronic exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute treadmill exercise and chronic aerobic exercise training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise consisted of symptom-limited treadmill stress testing in 75 middle-aged adults, following a standard Bruce protocol with plasma protein quantification at baseline, peak exercise (mean 90% predicted peak heart rate, 9.6 METs), and 1-hour post-exercise. Chronic exercise involved a 20-week aerobic training program with three sessions per week, with intensity and duration gradually increased based on individual VO2max. Acute exercise intensity and duration varied, making it difficult to effectively analyze specific exertion thresholds or dose-response comparisons for the acute protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changed (false discovery rate < 0.05) and showed sustained higher levels at both peak exercise and 1-h post-exercise, with a concordant direction of change.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Secreted protein and known exerkine related to exercise and cardiometabolic traits.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute treadmill exercise (peak and 1-h post-exercise)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with cardiometabolic traits and a promising candidate for further investigation as a circulating biomarker and exercise-responsive factor.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increases promoted by 30 minutes of treadmill Cardiovascular Exercise (CE) at vigorous intensity. No changes observed in the resting control group. No significant associations with post-exercise improvements in a sensorimotor adaptation task. Significantly larger increases following HIIT compared to MICT after 25 minutes of treadmill CE. Significant increases also observed following a maximal treadmill graded exercise test. Greater BDNF elevation when walking at moderate intensity for 30 minutes compared to walking at light intensity. The HIIT group showed significantly greater increases in basal BDNF concentrations following 12 weeks of training compared to MICT.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neuronal growth, survival, and synaptic plasticity, promoting neuroplasticity and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute bouts of vigorous-intensity treadmill CE, 25 minutes treadmill CE (HIIT vs MICT), 30 minutes moderate vs light intensity walking, and 12 weeks of chronic cycling (HIIT vs MICT) post-stroke.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests acute and chronic neurotrophic support for neuroplasticity, with higher intensities and HIIT eliciting greater increases. Higher levels are potentially linked to neuroplasticity and recovery, though acute upregulation does not always translate to immediate functional improvements.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Compared to 5 minutes of treadmill walking at light intensity, 5 minutes of moderate-intensity treadmill or vigorous-intensity ergometry did not elicit significantly larger increases in BNDF levels. Compared to a group undergoing standard therapeutic activity, 10 weeks of vigorous-intensity treadmill training did not induce any acute or chronic significant change in basal BDNF levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neuronal growth, survival, and synaptic plasticity, promoting neuroplasticity and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute bout of 5 minutes treadmill walking (light vs moderate intensity) or vigorous-intensity ergometry post-stroke; and 10 weeks of vigorous-intensity treadmill training post-stroke.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that very short durations, even at higher intensities, might not be sufficient to elicit significantly larger acute BDNF increases, and chronic vigorous-intensity training might not consistently alter basal BDNF levels or acute responses in stroke survivors, highlighting variability in chronic effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week daily curcumin supplementation (2g/day) on inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), blood count, and brain-derived neurotropic factor (BDNF) levels in middle-aged amateur long-distance runners. Overall, curcumin supplementation did not significantly affect CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, or blood count. However, IL-1β levels unexpectedly increased in the curcumin group, while BDNF levels showed a notable 21% increase in the curcumin group, contrasting a 5% decrease in the placebo group.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Curcumin supplementation alongside regular endurance training and an incremental treadmill running test.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 6-week daily supplementation of 2g curcumin extract. Each dose consisted of two capsules (500mg turmeric extract standardized to 95% curcumin, 10mg black pepper extract standardized to 95% piperine per capsule) taken twice daily. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but effects were compared between curcumin and placebo groups during specific exercise trials and recovery periods.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher (Curcumin group vs. Placebo, and absolute increase in CUR group); no overall statistical significance.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: BDNF levels increased by 21% in the curcumin-supplemented group at rest after 6 weeks of supplementation, whereas the placebo group showed a 5% decrease. While significant differences were observed across time points (rest, 3 min post-test, 1 h post-test) in both groups, the overall effect of curcumin on BDNF was not statistically significant, despite the notable percentage increase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in neuronal development, learning, memory, and neuroprotection; neurotrophin widely distributed throughout the nervous system, with release triggered by endurance exercises.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week curcumin supplementation (2g/day) in middle-aged amateur long-distance runners during a preparatory training period, measured at rest, 3 minutes post-test, and 1 hour post-test.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Curcumin supplementation led to a notable increase in BDNF levels, suggesting potential support for nervous system health and neuroprotection in endurance athletes, despite the lack of overall statistical significance across all measurements.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the discovery of novel traumatic brain injury (TBI) biomarkers using autoimmune profiling in both rat models and human patients. It details methodologies for sample preparation, protein analysis via 2D gel electrophoresis, immunoprofiling, and the development of an immunosorbent electrochemiluminescence assay (IEA) for peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6). The main findings establish PRDX6 as a candidate TBI biomarker, showing its astrocytic expression, TBI-induced autoantibody reactivity in rats, gender differences in baseline human plasma levels, and a significant, persistent approximately fourfold elevation of circulating PRDX6 in humans following mild-to-moderate TBI, which is proportional to injury severity and independent of imaging findings. The study also acknowledges S100B and GFAP as other relevant TBI indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) injury model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human TBI was observed as mild-to-moderate (median GCS 15), with plasma collected at 4-24 hours and 2-7 days post-injury; no direct manipulation or controlled dose was applied, though PRDX6 response correlated with injury severity. In rat models, severe CCI injury was induced using a stereotaxic impactor with a 5 mm impactor at a 20-degree angle to a depth of 2 mm at 5 m/sec with a dwell time of 500 msec to maximize autoimmune response. No specific dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported for either human TBI or rat CCI, beyond PRDX6 response proportionality in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Concentrated in platelets. Serum levels are elevated over those measured in corresponding plasma due to release from platelets during coagulation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established brain biomarker. Human platelets function as circulating repositories for it. Involved in neuronal health and growth.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Coagulation process; normal physiological conditions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An established brain biomarker; can indicate platelet release during coagulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes the IMPROVE trial, a four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating a novel home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training program (along with individual components and controls) on cognitive function, physical performance, mood, and quality of life in older (≥50) ICU survivors with delirium. The study aims to identify improvements and understand the underlying pathophysiology, hypothesizing beneficial changes in neurotrophic factors (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), and a reduction in inflammatory (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, CRP) and glial activation (S-100β, GFAP) biomarkers, as well as investigating AD-related markers like APOE genotype and Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training delivered via Internet-based videoconference. The study also investigates individual components (physical exercise only, cognitive training only) and control interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a four-arm randomized controlled trial. Active cognitive training involves facilitator-led online modules (Posit Science, Inc. Brain HQ) for 45 minutes, 2 days/week for 3 months. Active physical exercise is multi-modal, seated aerobic and progressive resistance training for 45 minutes, 3 times/week for 3 months, delivered via videoconference at moderate intensity (RPE 5-6 on a 10-point scale). Control groups receive matched frequency cognitive control modules and gentle seated stretching. This protocol does not report dose-response comparisons, focusing on comparisons between the four distinct intervention arms.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hypothesized increase due to combined physical and cognitive training; specific quantitative data not reported as this is a study protocol describing intent to measure changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Functions as a neurotrophic factor, mediating neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal survival, enhancing neural proliferation and neuroplasticity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined physical exercise and cognitive training intervention in older ICU survivors with delirium-induced cognitive impairment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cognitive function, neural function, and brain health, associated with potential for recovery from post-ICU cognitive impairment and delaying Alzheimer disease/dementias. Maximizes effects of cognitive stimulation and is a potential therapeutic target.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol details a prospective observational longitudinal study to develop and validate the Imperial Comprehensive Cognitive Assessment in Cerebrovascular Disease (IC3), a novel digital tool for detecting post-stroke cognitive deficits. The study aims to recruit 300 acute stroke patients and longitudinally investigate the relationship between cognition, psychosocial status, MRI brain imaging, and various blood biomarkers (including NFL, GFAP, brain-derived tau, phosphorylated tau forms, Aβ42/40 ratio, apolipoprotein E genotype, and polygenic risk scores) over 12 months post-ictus. The overarching goal is to identify reliable multimodal recovery indicators, patients at risk of progressive cognitive decline, and facilitate personalized therapy allocation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational longitudinal study for post-stroke cognitive impairment monitoring, biomarker identification, and validation of a novel digital cognitive assessment tool (IC3).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a 12-month longitudinal observational design involving repeated measures collected at baseline (0-15 days post-stroke), 3, 6, and 12 months post-ictus. It includes a digital cognitive assessment (IC3) comprising 22 tasks, lasting 60-70 minutes, administered via web-browser. Blood samples are collected from 200 patients and MRI imaging from 300 patients (at 3 and 12 months), along with 50 age-matched controls. No therapeutic dose comparisons are reported as it is an observational and diagnostic tool development protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aimed to be quantified over the first year after stroke and related to MRI measures and cognitive/functional outcomes; not yet reported as it describes a study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced plasma levels were observed with statistically significant differences between the two diets (p < 0.05). Consistent decreases occurred from baseline to 55 days (p < 0.05) and continued until day 98 (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) important for muscle growth, energy, tissue repair, and overall metabolic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention combining macronutrients, with effects measured from baseline to 98 days across PF and PFF groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to different health statuses and indicates metabolic changes, particularly in muscle protein turnover and energy status, due to dietary intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels are informative about protein synthesis, nutrition, and fatigue; supplementation can increase rates of protein synthesis and degradation in resting human muscle.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) crucial for protein synthesis, muscle repair, energy production, and skeletal muscle protein synthesis signaling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Protein synthesis, nutrition, fatigue, muscle repair, BCAA supplementation, diet, stress, disease states, monitoring resting amino acids across a season.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can reveal information about protein synthesis, nutrition, and fatigue, aiding in optimizing fueling strategies and indicating muscle status; direct effects on skeletal muscle protein synthesis signaling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated a stepwise, serum- and feeder-free protocol for differentiating human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) into hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) and red blood cells (RBCs). document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between dietary vitamin intake, specific blood biomarkers, and muscle activation in 61 Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) patients. It found that albumin consistently predicted muscle activation in both arm and leg muscles. Vitamin B9 positively predicted leg muscle activation, while vitamin A negatively predicted it, with potential toxicity at higher intakes. The B6/protein ratio showed inconsistent effects, negatively predicting arm muscle activation but positively predicting leg activation. Among other blood biomarkers, PON1 positively predicted arm muscle activation, whereas BuChE and haptoglobin negatively predicted leg muscle activation. CRP, Vitamin C, and Vitamin D were not found to be significant predictors of muscle activation in this cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational cross-sectional study investigating dietary habits and biomarkers in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no specific therapeutic interventions or experimental doses administered. Blood concentrations of butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE), albumin, haptoglobin, C-reactive protein (CRP), and paraoxonase 1 (PON1) were determined. Basal muscle activation was measured using surface electromyography. Patients were under riluzole treatment as an inclusion criterion, not an intervention. No dose-response comparisons were made for treatments, but effects of estimated vitamin intake levels and ratios (e.g., B6/protein) on muscle activation were analyzed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated plasma glycoprotein non-metastatic melanoma protein B (gpNMB) and glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) concentrations in a cohort of patients with Gaucher disease (GD1, GD3, GD1-PD), idiopathic Parkinson's disease (IPD), and GBA heterozygous PD, alongside healthy controls. The primary aim was to explore gpNMB's relationship to Gaucher disease severity, clinical phenotypes (neurological, pulmonary, liver disease, monoclonal gammopathy), and treatment status. Findings revealed significantly elevated plasma gpNMB levels in Gaucher disease patients compared to controls (mean: 200.9 vs. 35.1 ng/ml), which remained high even after prolonged enzyme replacement therapy. Higher gpNMB concentrations were notably associated with splenectomy, pulmonary disease, liver disease (including fibrosis and cirrhosis), and monoclonal gammopathy. Additionally, gpNMB levels were elevated in Parkinsonism patients with type 1 GD compared to GBA1 heterozygotes or IPD (p=0.0001). The study also highlighted gpNMB's good diagnostic performance for GD (AUC 0.894), and its significant positive correlations with other established GD biomarkers (GlcSph, Chitotriosidase, CCL18, ACE), suggesting its potential as a supportive biomarker for residual disease activity, disease complications, and clinical stratification, although it does not differentiate between neuronopathic GD subtypes or idiopathic PD. The study also reviewed other diagnostic markers like acid β-glucosidase activity and GBA1 mutation analysis, noting their utility and limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) and Substrate Reduction Therapy (SRT), including macrophage-targeted enzyme therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients received ERT or SRT for varying durations: mean 14.6 ± 6.9 years (range: 1–29 years) for ERT, and 10.1 ± 7.5 years (range: 6 months–23 years) for SRT. Plasma gpNMB concentrations showed an inverse correlation with treatment duration during the first 5 years of specific therapy (rho= -0.470, p= 0.024) but no correlation after 10 years. gpNMB levels remained elevated in GD1 patients on ERT for over 5 years, and no statistical difference was observed between treated GD1 and GD3 patients. Glucosylsphingosine concentrations declined with ERT or SRT. No explicit dose-response comparisons for ERT or SRT were reported, though it was noted that therapeutic response may vary across Gaucher disease subtypes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant positive correlation with plasma gpNMB concentrations (rho = 0.574, p < 0.001 and rho = 0.584, p < 001). GlcSph showed correlation with CCL-18-PARC concentrations and declines after institution of ERT or SRT.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chemokine involved in immune regulation and fibrosis, often elevated in lysosomal storage diseases and associated with macrophage activity. It reflects the singular inflammatory process that characterizes Gaucher disease, attributed to pathological macrophages undergoing alternative-type activation (M2 activation).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Gaucher disease.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker associated with Gaucher disease pathology; its positive correlation with gpNMB suggests a shared or related biological pathway, possibly involving macrophage activity. Established biomarker for the diagnosis and clinical monitoring of Gaucher disease; reflects inflammatory processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated before OCP treatment (part of 7 DETs with p < 0.01); increased after elagolix treatment (part of 42 DETs with similar significance levels)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine, regulates proliferation and invasion of endometriotic cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Before OCP treatment and after elagolix treatment in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure and suspected endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Present in peritoneal fluid of endometriosis cases, regulates proliferation and invasion via PI3K/AKT pathway; elevated in PF of infertile women with endometriosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Catheter ablation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression levels were significantly upregulated in the persistent AF group relative to SR control and paroxysmal AF groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine that recruits monocytes/macrophages, promoting inflammation and fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differentiated fibrocytes from persistent Atrial Fibrillation patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased expression in persistent AF fibrocytes suggests their contribution to local inflammation and recruitment of immune cells, exacerbating the pro-fibrotic environment in persistent AF.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Concentration remained unchanged in response to hyperacute serum treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory chemokine involved in immune cell recruitment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hyperacute serum treatment after IL-1β stimulation in an in vitro OA tissue model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Continued presence indicates ongoing inflammatory signaling that was not inhibited by the hyperacute serum treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: high levels in cases with severe disease compared to patients with uncomplicated SARS

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine, involved in inflammatory pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19; inflammatory pathway leading to cytokine storm.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with severe disease; attributed to cause acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) leading to pulmonary fibrosis and death.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Convalescent Plasma Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Critically ill COVID-19 patients were randomized to receive two units of high-titer, ABO-compatible convalescent plasma (total volume approximately 550 mL 
G
 150 mL) administered within 48 hours of randomization, or usual care. While no overall benefit was found (OSFD-21 OR 0.91 (0.74

1.11), mortality OR 1.01 (0.80

1.29)), differential treatment effects were observed across identified subphenotypes: subphenotype-1 showed lower hospital mortality with plasma (37.6% vs 40.5% in usual care), whereas subphenotypes-2 and -3 showed higher mortality with plasma (35.4% vs 24.1% for subphenotype-2; 34.1% vs 29.7% for subphenotype-3). No specific dose-response comparisons for plasma were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Elevated in subphenotype-3 (implied exaggerated inflammation). Significantly higher in non-survivors overall, and higher in seropositive subphenotype-1 patients. Lower in seropositive subphenotype-3 patients. Used to characterize subphenotypes.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in non-survivors; higher in seropositive subphenotype-1; lower in seropositive subphenotype-3. Not quantified in relation to treatment effect on biomarker levels directly; used to define subphenotype patterns.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a patient's immunological subphenotype which predicts differential response to convalescent plasma therapy and clinical outcomes; represents a heightened early innate immune response state; varies by serostatus within different subphenotypes; associated with higher hospital mortality and distinguishes specific COVID-19 subphenotypes. Subphenotype patterns (2 and 3) associated with worse outcomes/poorer plasma response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in SRS1 than SRS2 (FDR <0.05) in both GAinS and VANISH.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory chemokine, involved in immune cell recruitment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between SRS1 and SRS2 subphenotypes in sepsis patients from GAinS and VANISH cohorts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation indicates a pro-inflammatory state (SRS1 subphenotype) in sepsis patients, which is associated with worse clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.
