document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a distinct 4-biomarker panel (CXCL9, ST2, MMP-3, OPN) for cGVHD shown to correlate with disease activity. Also, identified individually for cGVHD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine; involved in leukocyte trafficking and immune responses, particularly Th1 responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Component of a panel correlating with chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease (cGVHD) disease activity; also identified as an individual biomarker for cGVHD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Concentration; Chemokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects; prominently in the acute SDD+C group compared to other groups. Significant increase in acute febrile phase compared to healthy controls (P < 0.05). Positively linked with IL-6, MIP-1β, IL-15, and RANTES.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine involved in immune cell trafficking and inflammation, acting as a chemoattractant for activated T lymphocytes and NK cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute febrile phase of dengue infection (healthy controls, dengue patients); correlated with other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Might be involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and may be a potential marker for severity in dengue patients. Also identified as a biomarker for dengue severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the clinical relevance and efficacy of collagen X breakdown product (CXM) as a blood-based biomarker for endochondral long bone fracture repair in both healthy individuals and patients with tibia or femur fractures. It characterized CXM expression patterns, stability across demographics (age, sex), correlation with other bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, osteocalcin, leptin, sclerostin), and its utility in predicting healing prognosis (early, normal, delayed). The findings showed CXM levels are low in healthy individuals, peak around 25-35 days post-fracture, can be reliably measured via dried blood spots, and offer an earlier, quantitative indication of healing compared to traditional radiographic methods, supporting its prospective use in fracture studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of natural long bone fracture repair, with a secondary analysis of a Vitamin D3 supplementation trial (VitaShock).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on observing biomarker changes in patients with acute closed or low-grade open tibial or femoral shaft fractures (Gustilo type I or II, AO/OTA type 42), without applying a specific therapeutic dose as an intervention. For the secondary analysis of the VitaShock trial, multiple Vitamin D3 dosing strategies were assessed, but specific dose details were not provided, and no significant difference in CXM response was found compared to placebo. Longitudinal blood samples were collected at various standard-of-care clinical visits over a period up to 48 weeks post-fracture.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increases during acute fracture healing, elevated at 6 weeks post-injury, positively correlates with CXM
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: r = 0.40, p < 0.0001 (with CXM). Strongest correlation occurred at 6 weeks (r = 0.50, p < 0.0001). Elevated levels at 6 weeks post-injury.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone resorption marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute fracture healing, particularly at 6 weeks post-fracture.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with early radiological healing at 12 weeks. An indicator of bone resorption activity during fracture healing, with a strong association with CXM levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates current and potential blood and urine biomarkers for osteoarthritis (OA), focusing on markers derived from type II collagen and aggrecan to reflect joint tissue turnover. The review details their molecular targets, measurement methods, and diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic utility in assessing cartilage degradation, bone turnover, and disease progression, including responses to treatments. It highlights both established and preclinical markers, emphasizing the complexities of cleavage sites, the need for multi-protease inhibition strategies, and further biomarker validation, while noting a continued lack of operationalized in vitro diagnostics and markers for patient endotyping.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Osteoarthritis (OA) biomarker investigation, Doxycycline treatment, Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT), Cathepsin K inhibition, Collagen hydrolysate supplementation, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced remodeling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic dose or intervention protocols are primarily reported, as this is a narrative review focusing on biomarkers for Osteoarthritis and their utility in drug development and patient management. However, some treatments were mentioned: Doxycycline was investigated in a randomized controlled trial in 120 obese knee OA patients (specific dose/duration not detailed). Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) was examined for its effect on knee OA patients (specific dose not detailed). Cathepsin K inhibition reduced CTX-I by more than 90% (specific inhibitor dose/duration not reported). Collagen hydrolysate administration led to a modest decrease in CS846 and an elevation in PIIANP (specific dose/duration not reported). No dose-response comparisons were generally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced more than 90% by Cathepsin K inhibition.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone resorption biomarker, generated by Cathepsin K activity on type I collagen.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clinical development of Cathepsin K inhibitors for osteoporosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone resorption levels; serves as a pharmacodynamic biomarker for Cathepsin K inhibitor efficacy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar between groups at rest. Significantly decreased 5 minutes (-19%, p < 0.001) and 1 hour post-exercise (-24%, p < 0.001) in both groups, then returned to baseline by 24 hours post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biochemical marker of bone resorption, reflecting the breakdown of type I collagen in bone.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest and acutely (5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours) post-plyometric exercise in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No difference at rest suggests no resting bone resorption difference between groups. The acute post-exercise decrease indicates a transient reduction in bone resorption, contributing to an overall anabolic bone response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study found that while bone turnover markers (CTX and BAP) decreased in both K citrate and placebo groups, K citrate significantly enhanced these beneficial effects, particularly in a subgroup of patients with pre-existing low-grade acidosis (low urine pH and/or low potassium and citrate excretion). K citrate also improved urinary pH, citrate, and potassium excretion. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Potassium Citrate (K citrate) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Daily oral supplementation with 30 mEq of K citrate (in two tablets) for 6 months. This was administered in addition to daily calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹) for all subjects (K citrate and placebo groups). The K citrate treatment showed significant benefits in subjects with evidence of low-grade acidosis (low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH) compared to the placebo, with significant changes observed as early as 3 months. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported, and adherence rates were approximately 90% for both groups.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Carboxy-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased significantly in both K citrate and placebo groups. In patients with low 24h-citrate excretion at baseline, a 30% mean decrease was observed at 6 months. A 35% reduction was evident in patients with low fasting-morning urine citrate, and a 30% reduction in patients with low fasting-morning urine pH. Changes induced by K citrate were more evident from three to six months and statistically significant in subgroups with low baseline pH and low citrate excretion. These changes were similar to those observed after antiresorptive drugs, with a reduction greater than 30% correlating with a significant decrease in osteoporotic fracture incidence.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of bone resorption, indicating the breakdown of type I collagen, a major structural component of bone matrix, and reflecting osteoclast activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: K citrate (30 mEq day   ⁻¹) supplementation for 6 months, combined with calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹), in postmenopausal women with osteopenia, particularly those with low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH at baseline, and those receiving calcium and vitamin D treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A decrease indicates reduced bone resorption, suggesting improved bone health and potential reduction in osteoporosis progression. Considered a useful tool for assessing response to anti-osteoporotic drugs and recommended by international committees as a reference marker for bone resorption. Reflects bone remodeling unit (BRU) activity and correlates with bone loss.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated everolimus (an mTORC1 inhibitor) as a treatment for progressive NF2-related vestibular schwannomas (VS), evaluating its impact on tumor volume, growth rate, hearing outcomes, and quality of life over 52 weeks. The findings indicate that 3-month volumetric imaging can serve as an early biomarker to predict long-term sensitivity to everolimus, which demonstrated a cytostatic effect by decreasing VS growth rates, stabilizing tumors, and improving time to progression, while generally maintaining hearing and quality of life, despite not achieving significant tumor shrinkage in all cases.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Everolimus (mTORC1 inhibitor), with some cases also involving Bevacizumab as a subsequent or alternative treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral everolimus was administered daily for 52 weeks (12 months) to NF2 patients with progressive VS. Adult participants (18+) received 10 mg/day, and adolescents (16-17) received 3 mg/day. Doses could be reduced (e.g., to 5 mg/day for adults) due to toxicity, such as grade 3+ or grade 2 oral ulcers. While no formal dose-response comparisons were reported, the treatment period was continuous for 52 weeks, with some patients re-challenged with everolimus after discontinuation, and others receiving bevacizumab if everolimus failed to control growth.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 11 of 15 non-target tumors (including C1 root schwannoma) were stable during the study period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of tumor proliferation and growth in secondary tumor sites.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Everolimus treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disease progression in secondary tumors and treatment efficacy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Genetic factor implicated in neurodegenerative diseases like ALS and FTD.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic studies in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) cohorts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to evaluate and verify the diagnostic value of serum exosomal miRNAs, particularly miR-193b-5p and miR-511-5p, in sepsis and septic shock. It identified miR-193b-5p as a potential diagnostic biomarker, associated with inflammation and immune regulation, and a protective factor against sepsis and septic shock progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification and Disease State Analysis (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved an initial screening cohort of serum exosomal miRNA sequencing on patients with sepsis (n=6), septic shock (n=6), and healthy controls (n=3). This was followed by validation using qRT-PCR in a larger cohort of 90 participants, comprising 30 patients with sepsis, 30 with septic shock, and 30 general surgery patients serving as controls. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours of ICU admission. Comparisons were made between disease groups and controls to identify diagnostic biomarkers and understand disease progression; no specific therapeutic dose or dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathological landscape, subclonal evolution, and dynamics of gene fusions, specifically KMT2A/AFDN and a novel CCDC32/CBX3, along with chimeric RNA variants, in 16 adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) patients undergoing treatment. It aimed to understand treatment resistance and relapse mechanisms by monitoring cytogenetic, RNA-seq, and genome-wide changes from diagnosis to relapse. The research identified the CCDC32/CBX3 fusion as a new therapeutic vulnerability that promotes cell cycle progression and contributes to AML pathogenesis and treatment resistance, highlighting its prognostic significance and the necessity of advanced molecular profiling for cryptic gene fusion detection.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (including high-dose cytarabine (HIDAC) and (7+3) induction chemotherapy) and Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (for Patient 7).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient 7 received HIDAC chemotherapy followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient 20 received (7+3) induction chemotherapy followed by HIDAC consolidation. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study primarily focused on biomarker monitoring and molecular changes rather than specific treatment efficacy across different doses. The study also included functional validation of gene fusion in vitro, which is not a treatment per se but part of the investigation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Bone marrow samples (AML patients), MV4-11 AML cell line, MYCN non-amplified neuroblastoma samples, primary/metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma, astrocytes, prostate cell line (in vitro).
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene fusion detection (RNA-sequencing, Quantitative PCR, PCR, Sanger DNA sequencing, long-read RNA sequencing, FISH), Gene transcript expression (qPCR), Molecular profiling, Gene expression level (overexpression in cell line), in vitro knockdown.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Persisted/Unchanged in patients, higher upon overexpression in cell line, lower upon knockdown in vitro
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Persisted or remained unchanged in AML patient 7 throughout diagnosis and relapse. Detected in 4 out of 16 AML patients (25% frequency) with breakpoints in exon 1 of CBX3 and exon 2 of CCDC32. Ectopic overexpression in MV4-11 AML cells resulted in higher gene transcript levels and was experimentally demonstrated to promote cell cycle progression. In vitro knockdown reduced cell proliferation and motility.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Novel gene fusion associated with specific chromosomal breakpoints; promotes cell cycle progression, contributing to AML pathogenesis and treatment resistance; reduces cell proliferation and motility upon knockdown; potential role in modulating wild-type CCDC32 and CBX3 gene expression. Previously reported in MYCN non-amplified neuroblastoma and papillary thyroid carcinoma.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Newly diagnosed, refractory, and relapsed AML patients (with KMT2A rearrangement and FLT3-Mutated AML), functional validation in MV4-11 AML cells, and referenced in MYCN non-amplified neuroblastoma and papillary thyroid carcinoma.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Novel prognostic and predictive biomarker associated with AML pathogenesis, treatment resistance, relapse, and poor clinical outcomes. It suggests a potential oncogenic role in subclonal evolution. Its detection highlights the necessity of advanced molecular profiling (like RNA-seq) for cryptic gene fusions, indicating a novel therapeutic vulnerability and prognostic significance for AML relapse risk and disease aggressiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the expression, secretion, and subcellular localization of Anterior Gradient 2 (AGR2) in normal bladder urothelium and various cancer types, particularly bladder cancer, to assess its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target. Key findings reveal that normal bladder cells express AGR2 but do not secrete it into urine or blood, whereas urothelial carcinoma cells secrete AGR2 and can localize it on their cell surface. While AGR2 expression is often lost or reduced in primary bladder tumors, it can be higher in lymph node metastases and is detectably secreted into the urine of bladder cancer patients. This differential secretion and localization, rather than expression alone, is critical for AGR2's utility as a bladder cancer biomarker. However, AGR2 expression in primary bladder tumors did not correlate with patient survival.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the systemic innate immune response, specifically focusing on neutrophil phenotypes, as biomarkers to monitor exercise-induced immune changes during repetitive, prolonged walking over consecutive days (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches). It found that prolonged exercise leads to an initial systemic innate immune response, characterized by the mobilization and activation of various neutrophil phenotypes, followed by adaptation or partial normalization in subsequent days. Crucially, increased neutrophil activation, marked by high CD11b expression, was consistently associated with impaired physical feeling, slower walking speed, and a higher degree of physiological stress, suggesting its potential as a valuable marker for monitoring immune system changes and detecting overtraining.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression significantly correlated with CD11b and CD35 (R^2 > 0.80; P < 0.0001), implying an increase as a neutrophil activation marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Selected highly migrating Mesenchymal Stem Cell subpopulation (sMSC).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased expression in sMSC compared to oMSC.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Glycoprotein receptor involved in angiogenesis and cell proliferation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Selection of highly migrating sMSC subpopulation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with superior migration potential of sMSC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and characterized a responsive human triple-culture model of the air-blood barrier, integrating distinct macrophage phenotypes (M1, M2 wound-healing, M2 regulatory) derived from THP-1 monocytes to mimic in vivo alveolar macrophage features. The research investigated their immunological impact, particularly on epithelial barrier function and inflammatory responses in both A549/ISO-HAS-1 and H441/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture systems. It demonstrated that the M1 macrophage model induced a severe inflammatory-like response, characterized by impaired epithelial barrier integrity and increased pro-inflammatory markers, making it suitable for modeling inflammatory lung diseases. Conversely, the M2 models (M2wh and M2reg) exhibited a non-inflammatory or pro-regenerative profile, maintaining barrier integrity and thus providing a foundation for establishing a quiescent, physiological air-blood barrier model. The study also detailed the specific biomarker profiles of these differentiated macrophage subtypes and their varied responses to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation within the triple-culture system, highlighting cell line-specific differences in inflammatory outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro differentiation of human monocytic leukemia cell line THP-1 into M1 (classically activated), M2wh (wound-healing), and M2reg (regulatory) macrophage phenotypes, followed by their integration into a human triple-culture air-blood barrier model. The model consisted of alveolar epithelial cells (A549 or NCI H441) and microvascular endothelial cells (ISO-HAS-1) cultured on Transwell filter membranes. Immunological impact was subsequently assessed via Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: THP-1 cells were differentiated for 48h using specific cytokine cocktails: for M1 macrophages, 50 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 25 ng/ml TNFα; for M2wh macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, 35 ng/ml IL-4, and 20 ng/ml IL-13; for M2reg macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 20 ng/ml IL-10. Dexamethasone (1 µM) was also used in some contexts. The differentiated macrophages were seeded onto the epithelial layer of the co-culture system. Cell culture media contained 10% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS), which was reduced to 5% for the triple cultures. The triple cultures were stimulated apically with 1 µg/ml LPS (end concentration) and incubated for 24h. No explicit dose-response comparisons for LPS or macrophage cell numbers were reported; the focus was on comparing responses across macrophage phenotypes and with/without LPS stimulation.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: decreased for M1; unchanged for M2wh and M2reg
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Unstimulated THP-1 cells showed 83 ± 13% positive expression. M1 macrophages exhibited a marked reduction to 23 ± 18% positive cells. M2wh (85 ± 12%) and M2reg (86 ± 6.5%) macrophages preserved similar expression levels compared to unstimulated THP-1 cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cell surface integrin, often associated with dendritic cells and some macrophage subsets, and antigen-presenting capability.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro differentiation of THP-1 cells into M1, M2wh, and M2reg macrophage phenotypes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Helps differentiate the M1 phenotype, which shows a reduction in CD11c, from the M2wh/M2reg and unstimulated cells, which maintain expression, thereby indicating distinct differentiation states and suggesting a reduction in dendritic cell-like features for M1, consistent with alveolar macrophage features for M2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein expression level (immunohistology, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: More than 65% of cells in primary cultures expressed CD133; GFP+CD133+ sorted population had 91.36% ± 9.17% purity. Localized in Bowman's capsule and apical surface of scattered tubular cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker for kidney progenitor cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characterization of human kidney-derived cells in culture and in tissue sections.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the presence and purity of renal progenitor cell populations, crucial for cell-based therapies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to identify surface markers for human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived erythropoietin (EPO)-producing cells (hiPSC-EPO cells) generated via a feeder-free differentiation protocol. It confirmed that EPO production was within the normal range and demonstrated that CD140b and CD73 expression levels, and the rates of CD140b+CD73+ cells, are correlated with EPO levels, thereby identifying them as beneficial cell surface markers for the purification of hiPSC-EPO cells.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) differentiation protocol for generating erythropoietin (EPO)-producing cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: hiPSCs were cultured in a feeder-free system, initially on iMatrix-511 coated plates in StemFit medium. For differentiation, cells were dissociated and seeded on Matrigel-coated plates at 5.0 	 10^4 cells	cm^-2. The protocol involved a two-stage medium system: Stage 1 included RPMI 1640, B27 supplement, recombinant human/mouse/rat activin A (100 ng	mL^-1), 1 μm CHIR99021 (with 10 µm Y-27632 for the initial 24 hours). Stage 2 consisted of KnockOut DMEM, penicillin/streptomycin (25 U	mL^-1), 20% KnockOut Serum Replacement, 1% DMSO, 2 mm L-glutamine, 1% nonessential amino acid, and 100 μm β-mercaptoethanol. Cells were cultured until day 13 for analysis, with EPO secretion peaking on this day. No dose-response comparisons or variations in differentiation parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression levels of CD140b are correlated with the level of EPO (R=0.871, P=0.024) and EPO concentration in supernatant (R=0.985, P<0.001). Rates of CD140b+ cells also correlated with EPO in supernatant (R=0.943, P<0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell surface marker; suggested as a marker for renal and hiPSC-derived EPO-producing cells, involved in cell identification.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identification and characterization of hiPSC-EPO cells during a feeder-free differentiation protocol for purification by cell sorting.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a specific marker for hiPSC-EPO cells, critical for optimizing EPO production and cell counts for transplantation in regenerative medicine, and useful for cell sorting and purification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Gene targeting using TALENs, in vitro human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation, and in vivo mouse embryo analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GATA2w/eGFP reporter was generated in H1 hESCs via gene editing (TALENs, electroporation of 1 μg linearized vector and 2.5 μg of each TALEN plasmid into 1 × 10^6 H1 cells, puromycin selection at 0.5 μg/mL, and Cre recombinase (400 ng per 1 × 10^6 cells) for cassette removal). In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the systemic innate immune response, specifically focusing on neutrophil phenotypes, as biomarkers to monitor exercise-induced immune changes during repetitive, prolonged walking over consecutive days (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches). It found that prolonged exercise leads to an initial systemic innate immune response, characterized by the mobilization and activation of various neutrophil phenotypes, followed by adaptation or partial normalization in subsequent days. Crucially, increased neutrophil activation, marked by high CD11b expression, was consistently associated with impaired physical feeling, slower walking speed, and a higher degree of physiological stress, suggesting its potential as a valuable marker for monitoring immune system changes and detecting overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive prolonged walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in prolonged walking over 3 consecutive days as part of a public walking event (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches), covering 30, 40, or 50 km/day at a self-selected pace. Exercise intensity on day 1 averaged 65% of maximum heart rate. While the study involved varying distances, no explicit dose-response comparisons for immune markers were reported between different daily distances. However, increased neutrophil activation (high CD11b expression) was associated with slower walking speeds (approx. 4.1-4.2 km/h across days) and predominantly occurred in participants walking 30 km (66% of this group).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased significantly from 4.58 (3.33–5.70) × 10^6 /ml at day 1 to 3.12 (2.41–4.57) × 10^6 /ml (P < 0.0001) after day 2 of prolonged walking.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a shift in neutrophil populations during sustained exercise, with its decrease being the main reason for the overall decrease in total neutrophil count, suggesting a dynamic immune response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

Significantly upregulated with PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.01). Significantly decreased with STING antagonist C-176 (p < 0.01).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the regulation of 23 blood-based biomarkers (including CK, IL-6, IL-17A, S100A8, BDNF, CD163, IL-1ß, and LDH) in 35 male elite athletes (badminton and soccer players) across different recovery-stress states. The primary aim was to identify markers responsive to habitual loading microcycles compared to recovered states. Key findings indicated that Creatine Kinase (CK), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) were generally higher in non-recovered states. S100A8 levels were significantly lower in non-recovered badminton players, while Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) levels were lower in non-recovered soccer players. Statistical trends were also observed for CD163 and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1ß). The study concludes that these discipline-specific biomarker responses are potentially useful for monitoring exercise and recovery to prevent overtraining and injury, though further validation is needed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise Training / Habitual Loading Microcycles
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared blood biomarker levels in elite male athletes (badminton and soccer players) during two states: 'recovered' (REC, after at least one day of rest from exercise) and 'non-recovered' (NOR, after a habitual loading microcycle). The habitual loading involved intensive, sport-specific training. For badminton players, this included four consecutive days with up to two sessions per day (50-310 min of moderate to intensive exercise daily). For soccer players, it involved high-intensity sessions with strenuous small-sided games, with at least two sessions within 48 hours. Blood samples for the NOR state were taken 12-16 hours after the last training session. The specific training content within microcycles varied and was not precisely controlled, reflecting real-world conditions. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training loads were reported within the context of the main findings, although external references to other exercise bouts (e.g., marathon, duathlon, interval training) were used to characterize biomarker behavior generally.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed a statistical trend (p = 0.069) across all athletes in differentiating recovery and non-recovered states. Significant increases were observed 3 hours after marathon and half-marathon races, with a more pronounced increase after a full marathon, generally decreasing to baseline within 48 hours.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Expressed on macrophages and monocytes, involved in preventing hemoglobin-induced toxicity during hemolysis, possesses anti-inflammatory properties, and provides protective mechanisms against oxidative stress and myocardial damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise recovery cycle in athletic populations, particularly after prolonged running (marathon, half-marathon) and strenuous exercise loads.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential marker for athletic monitoring, reflecting anti-inflammatory and protective responses following prolonged and strenuous exercise, though requiring confirmation due to trend-level significance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and characterized a responsive human triple-culture model of the air-blood barrier, integrating distinct macrophage phenotypes (M1, M2 wound-healing, M2 regulatory) derived from THP-1 monocytes to mimic in vivo alveolar macrophage features. The research investigated their immunological impact, particularly on epithelial barrier function and inflammatory responses in both A549/ISO-HAS-1 and H441/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture systems. It demonstrated that the M1 macrophage model induced a severe inflammatory-like response, characterized by impaired epithelial barrier integrity and increased pro-inflammatory markers, making it suitable for modeling inflammatory lung diseases. Conversely, the M2 models (M2wh and M2reg) exhibited a non-inflammatory or pro-regenerative profile, maintaining barrier integrity and thus providing a foundation for establishing a quiescent, physiological air-blood barrier model. The study also detailed the specific biomarker profiles of these differentiated macrophage subtypes and their varied responses to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation within the triple-culture system, highlighting cell line-specific differences in inflammatory outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro differentiation of human monocytic leukemia cell line THP-1 into M1 (classically activated), M2wh (wound-healing), and M2reg (regulatory) macrophage phenotypes, followed by their integration into a human triple-culture air-blood barrier model. The model consisted of alveolar epithelial cells (A549 or NCI H441) and microvascular endothelial cells (ISO-HAS-1) cultured on Transwell filter membranes. Immunological impact was subsequently assessed via Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: THP-1 cells were differentiated for 48h using specific cytokine cocktails: for M1 macrophages, 50 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 25 ng/ml TNFα; for M2wh macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, 35 ng/ml IL-4, and 20 ng/ml IL-13; for M2reg macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 20 ng/ml IL-10. Dexamethasone (1 µM) was also used in some contexts. The differentiated macrophages were seeded onto the epithelial layer of the co-culture system. Cell culture media contained 10% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS), which was reduced to 5% for the triple cultures. The triple cultures were stimulated apically with 1 µg/ml LPS (end concentration) and incubated for 24h. No explicit dose-response comparisons for LPS or macrophage cell numbers were reported; the focus was on comparing responses across macrophage phenotypes and with/without LPS stimulation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Flow-cytometric analysis showed negative expression for all differentiated THP-1 models (M1, M2wh, M2reg).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro differentiation of THP-1 cells into M1, M2wh, and M2reg macrophage models.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of expression suggests that the differentiated THP-1 models, particularly M2wh and M2reg, do not fully acquire this typical M2 marker, indicating potential limitations in mirroring in vivo M2 phenotypes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed an integrative multi-platform meta-analysis of gene expression profiles from Affymetrix and Illumina datasets in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients and healthy controls to identify novel, robust diagnostic biomarkers. The analysis revealed 5 commonly differentially expressed genes and 28 novel 'gained' genes, suggesting their significant potential for early PDAC diagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Integrative meta-analysis of gene expression data for biomarker identification and diagnostic prediction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gene expression data from two independent cohorts of PDAC patients (Affymetrix: 18 PDAC patients; Illumina: 36 PDAC patients) and 18 healthy controls were integrated. Profiling was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) using Affymetrix GeneChip® Human Gene ST 1.0 Arrays and Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 Expression BeadChip microarray platforms. Data were integrated using an empirical Bayesian methodology (ComBat) for batch effect removal, and differential expression was analyzed with limma software, identifying genes with p<0.01 and at least 1.5-fold differential expression. The analysis identified 5 commonly differentially expressed genes (with individual ROC curve AUC > 0.9) and 28 novel 'gained' genes, which could discriminate PDAC patients from controls with an average sensitivity of 74.8% and specificity of 73.3% for individual gained genes, 100% sensitivity and 94% specificity for combined common genes, and 91% sensitivity and 87% specificity for combined gained genes. No dose-response comparisons were applicable as it is a diagnostic biomarker identification study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Gene targeting using TALENs, in vitro human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation, and in vivo mouse embryo analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GATA2w/eGFP reporter was generated in H1 hESCs via gene editing (TALENs, electroporation of 1 μg linearized vector and 2.5 μg of each TALEN plasmid into 1 × 10^6 H1 cells, puromycin selection at 0.5 μg/mL, and Cre recombinase (400 ng per 1 × 10^6 cells) for cassette removal). In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). CFU assay medium contained 100 ng/mL recombinant murine stem cell factor, 10 ng/mL recombinant murine interleukin-3, 10 ng/mL recombinant human interleukin-6, and 3 U/mL human erythropoietin, with endothelial cell assays using 100 ng/mL vascular endothelial growth factor. In vivo analysis included mouse embryos at E10.0, E11, E12, E14, with fractionation of endothelial cells based on CD61 expression (CD61 high, CD61 low, and CD61 − subpopulations). No specific dose-response comparisons for differentiation conditions or therapeutic interventions were reported beyond qualitative observations of effect.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: GATA2/eGFP+ HECs and GATA2/eGFP- ECs (hESC blood differentiation).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Preferably marked GATA2/eGFP- ECs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell surface marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Validation of differentially expressed surface markers in hESC blood differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a potential marker for non-hemogenic ECs, aiding in their discrimination from HECs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and characterized a responsive human triple-culture model of the air-blood barrier, integrating distinct macrophage phenotypes (M1, M2 wound-healing, M2 regulatory) derived from THP-1 monocytes to mimic in vivo alveolar macrophage features. The research investigated their immunological impact, particularly on epithelial barrier function and inflammatory responses in both A549/ISO-HAS-1 and H441/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture systems. It demonstrated that the M1 macrophage model induced a severe inflammatory-like response, characterized by impaired epithelial barrier integrity and increased pro-inflammatory markers, making it suitable for modeling inflammatory lung diseases. Conversely, the M2 models (M2wh and M2reg) exhibited a non-inflammatory or pro-regenerative profile, maintaining barrier integrity and thus providing a foundation for establishing a quiescent, physiological air-blood barrier model. The study also detailed the specific biomarker profiles of these differentiated macrophage subtypes and their varied responses to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation within the triple-culture system, highlighting cell line-specific differences in inflammatory outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro differentiation of human monocytic leukemia cell line THP-1 into M1 (classically activated), M2wh (wound-healing), and M2reg (regulatory) macrophage phenotypes, followed by their integration into a human triple-culture air-blood barrier model. The model consisted of alveolar epithelial cells (A549 or NCI H441) and microvascular endothelial cells (ISO-HAS-1) cultured on Transwell filter membranes. Immunological impact was subsequently assessed via Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: THP-1 cells were differentiated for 48h using specific cytokine cocktails: for M1 macrophages, 50 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 25 ng/ml TNFα; for M2wh macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, 35 ng/ml IL-4, and 20 ng/ml IL-13; for M2reg macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 20 ng/ml IL-10. Dexamethasone (1 µM) was also used in some contexts. The differentiated macrophages were seeded onto the epithelial layer of the co-culture system. Cell culture media contained 10% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS), which was reduced to 5% for the triple cultures. The triple cultures were stimulated apically with 1 µg/ml LPS (end concentration) and incubated for 24h. No explicit dose-response comparisons for LPS or macrophage cell numbers were reported; the focus was on comparing responses across macrophage phenotypes and with/without LPS stimulation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Flow-cytometric analysis showed negative expression for all differentiated THP-1 models (M1, M2wh, M2reg).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A typical marker for alternatively activated macrophages (M2wh and M2reg).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro differentiation of THP-1 cells into M1, M2wh, and M2reg macrophage models.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of expression suggests that the differentiated THP-1 models, particularly M2wh and M2reg, do not fully acquire this typical M2 marker, indicating potential limitations in mirroring in vivo M2 phenotypes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (with Cl-amidine, with STING inhibition), lower (with PAD4 overexpression)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Upregulated mRNA expression level by Cl-amidine (p < 0.01). Downregulated by PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.05). Upregulated by STING antagonist C-176 (p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A mannose receptor and marker for the anti-inflammatory (M2-like) microglial/macrophage phenotype, involved in tissue repair and resolution of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, PAD4 overexpression, or STING inhibition.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anti-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation, supporting repair. Its upregulation suggests a promotion of protective responses, while downregulation indicates an imbalance towards pro-inflammatory responses.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated a stepwise, serum- and feeder-free protocol for differentiating human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) into hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) and red blood cells (RBCs). It specifically examined the effect of enforced HOXB4 expression on this process. While HOXB4 activation increased the production of multipotent HPCs (peaking around days 6-10, characterized by CD34, CD43, and Runx1C-GFP expression) and immature erythroid cells, it ultimately failed to promote the maturation, efficient enucleation, or expansion of adult-like RBCs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enforced expression of HOXB4 in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized a tamoxifen-inducible HOXB4-ER T2 expression system within H1 hESCs, under a CAG promoter. HOXB4 activation was induced with tamoxifen for varying durations: 10 days for HPC assessment, days 10-24 for RBC maturation, or days 0-24 for overall differentiation and expansion. This was integrated into a multi-step, serum- and feeder-free differentiation protocol lasting at least 17 days, involving sequential addition of various growth factors and cytokines (e.g., BMP4, VEGF, Wnt3a, Activin A, GSK-3 2 inhibitor VIII, FGF- 1, SCF, IGF2, TPO, Heparin, IBMX, Hydrocortisone, Flt3L, IL-3, IL-11, EPO, IGF1) at specific concentrations and time points. No quantitative dose-response comparisons for either HOXB4 activation or the overall differentiation protocol were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Cell surface marker expression (proportion of cells)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No effect of tamoxifen on the overall proportion of erythroid cells that expressed CD235a at day 24.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cell surface marker for erythroid cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: HOXB4 activation during later stages of hESC differentiation (days 10-24) to assess RBC maturation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates presence of erythroid cells; no change suggests HOXB4 does not alter overall erythroid cell production.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Primary cultures of human renal cells

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All CD133+ cells co-expressed CD24, but only 70% of CD24+ cells expressed CD133.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Co-expressed marker with CD133 in renal progenitor cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characterization of primary renal cell cultures to define progenitor cell populations.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Helps in the comprehensive characterization and definition of renal progenitor cell subsets.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (via flow cytometry phenotype analysis)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression is increased after 72-hour mitogen stimulation, making the 'positive population' clearer; precise quantification of change not reported, but used for empirical determination of positive populations.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates T-cell activation, functioning as a baseline-expressed activation marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 72-hour mitogen stimulation, in the context of immune monitoring programs for human TCT recipients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates immune activation; baseline expression observed in both patient and healthy donor cells is not necessarily a cause for immediate concern, but changes upon stimulation help define positive populations for accurate monitoring.
