document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study investigated the ergogenic effects of acute pre-exercise homemade chicken broth (CB) ingestion, rich in histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) like carnosine and anserine, on high-intensity cycling performance in recreationally-trained men. The study found a significant 5.2% improvement in 8-minute time trial mean power and elevated plasma carnosine and anserine levels following CB supplementation. However, the ergogenic effect was not mediated by changes in acid-base balance or red blood cell glutathione status, indicating alternative mechanisms may be at play.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute pre-exercise nutritional supplementation (homemade chicken broth or placebo soup)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested either 8 mL/kg body weight of homemade chicken broth (CB), providing 46.4 mg/kg body weight of total histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) (specifically 15.6 mg/kg BW carnosine and 30.8 mg/kg BW anserine), or an equivalent volume of a placebo soup. The supplement was administered 25-40 minutes prior to an 8-minute high-intensity cycling time trial, following a warm-up. No dose-response comparisons were made, only CB versus placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased post-exercise (p < 0.05, and p = 0.011 for interaction effect) after chicken broth supplementation compared to placebo, reaching 372.7 nmol/L at 5 min recovery post-exercise from a basal pooled plasma concentration of 23.34     ± 2.78 nmol/L. The increase in plasma carnosine was 50 times lower compared to plasma anserine, contributing to an almost 700-fold increase in total plasma HCDs (from 30 nmol/L to 20 µmol/L).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A histidine-containing dipeptide (HCD) involved in intracellular pH buffering, antioxidant activity, and oxidative stress control. It is degraded by serum carnosinase-1 (CN1).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise (53 min after supplementation) following acute pre-exercise chicken broth ingestion and an 8-minute high-intensity cycling time trial.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated circulating levels are associated with potential ergogenic effects and improved high-intensity exercise performance through attenuation of acidosis and/or oxidative stress in blood. Its accumulation in plasma is interrelated with anserine accumulation and overall improved exercise performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of low (LV-HIIT) and high (HV-HIIT) volumes of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on vascular-endothelial function, oxidative stress, and atherosclerosis markers in patients after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The 16-week supervised HIIT programs, regardless of volume, led to a volume-dependent enhancement in endothelial function (FMD) and a decrease in oxidative stress (ox-LDL). A reduction in vascular wall thickness (cIMT) was also observed, with LV-HIIT proving sufficient to initiate favorable adaptations and reduce cardiovascular risk. The study also assessed anthropometric and other cardiovascular markers, comparing HIIT groups to an active control.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Unsupervised Physical Activity Recommendations (Active Control, AC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) with two volumes: Low Volume (LV-HIIT) and High Volume (HV-HIIT), and an Active Control (AC) group. LV-HIIT involved 8 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-minute total session. HV-HIIT involved 16 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-40 minute total session. Both supervised HIIT groups exercised 2 non-consecutive days per week for 16 weeks (32 sessions) on treadmills and cycle ergometers, with intensity individualized based on cardiorespiratory fitness, ventilatory thresholds, beat-to-beat HR, and the Böarg scale. The AC group received individualized recommendations for unsupervised physical activity, advised to perform at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity 5–7 days per week for 16 weeks. FMD and ox-LDL changes were volume-dependent (HV-HIIT showing greater effects), while cIMT reduction was similar between LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT, indicating a volume-independent effect for cIMT and confirming LV-HIIT's effectiveness.

Noteworthy, yet slight, alterations compared to the active control group (ANOVA p = 0.019). Manifest atherosclerosis is indicated by values > 0.8 mm.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates a decrease in the progression of atherosclerosis, mitigating cardiovascular risk and lowering the likelihood of future cardiovascular events such as stroke and myocardial infarction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates current and potential blood and urine biomarkers for osteoarthritis (OA), focusing on markers derived from type II collagen and aggrecan to reflect joint tissue turnover. The review details their molecular targets, measurement methods, and diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic utility in assessing cartilage degradation, bone turnover, and disease progression, including responses to treatments. It highlights both established and preclinical markers, emphasizing the complexities of cleavage sites, the need for multi-protease inhibition strategies, and further biomarker validation, while noting a continued lack of operationalized in vitro diagnostics and markers for patient endotyping.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Osteoarthritis (OA) biomarker investigation, Doxycycline treatment, Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT), Cathepsin K inhibition, Collagen hydrolysate supplementation, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced remodeling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic dose or intervention protocols are primarily reported, as this is a narrative review focusing on biomarkers for Osteoarthritis and their utility in drug development and patient management. However, some treatments were mentioned: Doxycycline was investigated in a randomized controlled trial in 120 obese knee OA patients (specific dose/duration not detailed). Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) was examined for its effect on knee OA patients (specific dose not detailed). Cathepsin K inhibition reduced CTX-I by more than 90% (specific inhibitor dose/duration not reported). Collagen hydrolysate administration led to a modest decrease in CS846 and an elevation in PIIANP (specific dose/duration not reported). No dose-response comparisons were generally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Highly elevated after traumatic injury and moderate to high with impact exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the turnover of the cartilage oligomeric matrix protein.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic injury; impact exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates cartilage oligomeric matrix protein turnover; elevated levels are associated with cartilage stress or damage from traumatic injury and impact exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and optimized a novel Quantum Dot-Linked Immunoassay (QLISA) for the sensitive and multiplex detection of biochemical markers, using spectroscopic QD-analyte complex measurements in a microvolume liquid droplet format on a glass microslide. The method significantly enhanced detection sensitivity and multiplexing capabilities for limited sample volumes, demonstrating 10 to 40 times stronger fluorescence signals compared to standard 96-well plate QLISAs and enabling the detection of lower analyte concentrations for model analytes such as Cartilage Oligomeric Matrix Protein (COMP) and human Growth Hormone (hGH).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Development and optimization of a Quantum Dot-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (QLISA) for sensitive and multiplex biomarker detection in a microvolume format.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The method utilized microvolume liquid droplets (2  5L samples) on a glass microslide, achieving 10 to 40 times stronger fluorescence signals compared to standard 96-well plate QLISAs. Analyte concentrations tested included COMP and hGH at 5 nM, 25 nM, and 50 nM. Optimization involved alkaline immune-complex disassembling solutions (e.g., 10 mM NaOH + 0.5% SDS or 50 mM NaOH + 0.5% SDS) for 5 minutes, followed by PBS dilution. Various concentrations of biotinylated antibodies (e.g., biotin-anti-hGH: 10 nM, 20 nM) and QDs (e.g., QD625: 20 nM, QD655, QD605, QD525) were used, with fluorescence intensity measurements using an excitation wavelength of 400 nm. Detection limits ranged from 50 fM (QD625) to 2 pM (QD525), significantly improving detectability especially in multiplex analysis where 96-well plate formats struggled to distinguish concentrations.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: In vitro assay system (model recombinant protein in buffered solutions and microvolume liquid droplets on a glass microslide)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level Detection and Quantification (via Quantum Dot-Linked Immunoassay, QLISA)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected and quantified across 5 nM, 25 nM, and 50 nM concentrations. Microvolume detection significantly increased FL signal strength and sensitivity (10-40 times stronger than 96-well QLISAs), with detection limits from 50 fM (QD625) to 2 pM (QD525). Specific increases in MFI with PBS dilution were 1.36-fold for 50 nM, 2.13-fold for 25 nM, and 2.5-fold for 5 nM (all P  1 0.001). For 50 nM COMP, microvolume detection showed a 5.5 times higher MFI compared to 96-well format (P  1 0.0001). A 14.4-fold difference from blank was achieved for 3.125 nM in microslide vs. 1.3-fold in 96-well. Singleplex detection yielded 14.5-fold and duplex 3.1-fold ratios to blank in microvolume for 50 nM COMP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A noncollagenous extracellular matrix protein primarily found in cartilage, mediating its structure and integrity; used as a model analyte for immunoassay development and associated with inflammatory and degenerative age-related joint diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Optimization and validation of a microvolumetric Quantum Dot-Linked Immunoassay (QLISA) for multiplex detection of protein analytes, involving immune-complex disassembling solutions, PBS dilution, and comparison between 96-well plate and glass microslide formats.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a model biomarker to demonstrate the enhanced sensitivity and multiplexing capabilities of the QLISA method; it is relevant for potential diagnostic applications for musculoskeletal conditions, indicating joint health/damage, and can aid in the diagnosis and characterization of inflammatory and degenerative age-related joint diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Riociguat (Drug Treatment)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients with early treatment-naïve diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis were randomized to receive riociguat (n=60) or placebo (n=61) for 52 weeks. Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (between groups); fold-change correlated with mRSS change
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in mRNA levels did not differ significantly between riociguat and placebo groups from baseline to week 14. However, fold-changes showed a modest correlation (0.306) with change in mRSS from baseline to week 52 in the riociguat group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Extracellular matrix protein, involved in matrix remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in dcSSc patients from baseline to week 14/52.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change in mRNA levels due to treatment, but a modest correlation with mRSS changes suggests it could be a potential indicator of skin fibrosis progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the expression patterns and prognostic value of the thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP)/nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome pathway and its related genes (IL1B, CASP1) in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Analyzing microarray data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), transcriptome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), and qRT-PCR data from a Jinan University (JNU) validation cohort, the study found that TXNIP and IL1B were generally upregulated, while CASP1 showed variable expression in AML patients compared to healthy individuals. Crucially, lower expression, particularly the co-expression, of TXNIP, NLRP3, and IL1B was consistently associated with a more favorable prognosis and longer overall survival (OS) in AML patients, indicating their potential as prognostic biomarkers and targets for novel AML therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prognostic Biomarker Analysis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study analyzing endogenous gene expression patterns in AML patients across multiple public (GEO: GSE13159, GSE12417; TCGA) and institutional (JNU) datasets. The study compared expression levels between AML patients and healthy individuals, and correlated expression patterns with patient outcomes (overall survival, restricted mean survival time). Patients were categorized into high and low expression groups based on median gene expression levels. No experimental intervention, therapeutic doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported or investigated.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: AML patient data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (GSE13159), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database, and Peripheral Blood (PB) samples from Jinan University (JNU) database, compared with Healthy Individuals.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially downregulated in AML patients (GSE13159); significantly higher in AML patients in JNU dataset; variable expression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated in AML patients (P = 0.038 in GSE13159); not statistically significant in GSE12417 (P = 0.356). Significantly higher in AML patients compared to HIs (P = 0.014) in JNU dataset.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of the NLRP3 inflammasome; self-cleavage of pro-caspase-1 forms activated CASP1, which then cleaves pro-IL-1β and pro-IL-18 into their active mature forms, inducing inflammation and cell death (pyroptosis).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients; Expression levels in AML patients compared to healthy individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests dysregulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) patients; involved in activating inflammatory cytokines and pyroptotic cell death; variable expression, but low co-expression with other markers is prognostic.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated (p < 0.001) in the TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group compared to the TBI + Cl-amidine group at 3 days after TBI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key executioner caspase in the apoptotic pathway, involved in programmed cell death.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP in Cl-amidine-treated TBI mice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its upregulation indicates increased apoptotic cell death and loss of neuroprotection.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to establish comprehensive reference intervals for novel circulating biomarkers of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and hepatic regeneration in healthy human volunteers. It investigated intra- and interindividual variability, as well as diurnal variation, to provide robust data for interpreting exploratory clinical DILI studies and assisting biomarker qualification by regulatory authorities.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study for establishing reference intervals of circulating biomarkers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved serum sample collection from 227 healthy volunteers in a cross-sectional study (single sample). Additionally, 25 subjects underwent weekly serial sampling over 3 weeks, and 23 subjects had intensive 24-hour blood sampling every 3 hours after a 10-h overnight fast and standardized meals. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved, as the focus was on establishing reference intervals and assessing natural variability in healthy subjects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reference intervals established; consistent levels observed, not significantly influenced by demographic factors; intra-individual variability non-significant.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference intervals based on the 97.5% quantile (90% CI). No significant fixed effects of sex, age, height, weight, BMI, or ethnicity were observed. Mean ccK18 levels were consistent with previous studies. Intra-individual variability found to be non-significant, with no significant impact of diurnal variation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Monitors apoptotic-necrotic dynamics, reflecting the degree of hepatocellular necrotic and/or apoptotic injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Establishing reference ranges in healthy human volunteers, characterizing natural variability, diurnal variation, and assessing its stability across demographic factors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identifies hepatocellular necrotic and/or apoptotic injury. Stable levels across various demographic factors and low intraindividual variability support the establishment of universal reference intervals for DILI prediction and hepatic regeneration assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. The aim was to evaluate systemic and muscle-related stress responses and recovery patterns, comparing biomarkers at 1 day (R+1) and 15 days (R+15) post-landing with pre-flight values and age-matched controls. Findings revealed a strong spaceflight-induced stress response in muscle tissue, leading to a proinflammatory state, with inflamma-miRs and myo-miR-206 mediating systemic recovery, and significant inter-individual differences in biomarker responses were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 6-month International Space Station (ISS) spaceflight exposure with in-flight countermeasure training, followed by a post-flight recovery period.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two crewmembers were exposed to approximately 6 months of spaceflight. Samples were collected pre-flight (76-79 days before) and post-flight at 1 day (R+1 / 24 hours) and 15 days (R+15) after landing. Individual molecular responses varied significantly between the two crewmembers, with crewmember A generally showing more persistent changes. Specifics of in-flight countermeasure training dose were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons for spaceflight duration were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher; increased (+23% and +50%) in crewmember A after landing (R+1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A stress and antioxidant protein.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-spaceflight (R+1).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates differences in stress and antioxidant proteins post-spaceflight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether pre-exercise ascorbic acid supplementation influenced antioxidant defenses, glucose metabolism, inflammation, and muscle damage in untrained healthy adults following a single bout of moderate-intensity cycling. Findings indicated that ascorbic acid supplementation reduced plasma Malondialdehyde (MDA) and increased Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP), while also modulating glucose levels and attenuating exercise-induced changes in albumin and total protein. While moderate-intensity cycling led to an increase in red blood cell Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) activity and low-grade muscle damage (Total Creatine Kinase), it did not induce systemic inflammation or lipid peroxidation. Ascorbic acid supplementation appeared to mitigate the exercise-induced increase in SOD activity but did not significantly prevent muscle damage or affect other inflammatory/damage markers such as hsCRP, LDH, CK-MB, GPx, or Catalase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supplementation combined with a single bout of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects received 1000 mg of ascorbic acid (or placebo) orally 5 minutes prior to a 30-minute indoor cycling session. Exercise intensity was set at 65–75% of maximum heart rate, which was predicted by an age-based equation. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either ascorbic acid or exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activity remained unchanged independent of treatment (p>0.05, implied).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An antioxidant enzyme that catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, protecting cells from oxidative damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute aerobic exercise (indoor cycling) in untrained healthy adults, with or without ascorbic acid supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No acute impact on Catalase activity observed, suggesting this exercise bout or ascorbic acid supplementation did not alter its activity under these conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased the activity of renal antioxidant enzymes (catalase).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Renal antioxidant enzyme.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nicorandil treatment in a rat model of unilateral partial ureteral obstruction (animal model context).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduces oxidative stress and improves glomerular and tubulointerstitial damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher catalase (CAT) activity was observed after the control exercise bout than after the exercise bout preceded by a WBC session.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An antioxidant enzyme that converts hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen, protecting cells from oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional volleyball players (n=18) after 40-min submaximal physical exercise preceded by a single WBC session (-130°C, 2 min) vs. control exercise bout without WBC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: WBC may mitigate exercise-induced increases in CAT activity, contributing to antioxidant effects and a more balanced oxidative response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activity was preserved and neither affected by anserine dose, post-exercise time-course, nor interaction effects. No significant difference compared to placebo (d = 0.1 and 0.2 for ANS-LD and ANS-HD vs. PLA, respectively).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cellular antioxidant defense, catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, involved in oxidation-reduction pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Anserine supplementation following an exercise challenge (time to exhaustion).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests maintained levels of this antioxidant enzyme and contributes to preserving cellular homeostasis, potentially influencing the role of GSH, GSSG, and GSH/GSSG.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (p < 0.05) activity after melatonin supplementation (e.g., 15 mg for 3 days pre-exercise or general increases in expression/activity).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Antioxidant enzyme that catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, protecting cells from oxidative damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation (e.g., 15 mg before physical activity or general indirect antioxidant mechanisms) in highly trained athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved antioxidant capacity and enhanced protection against exercise-induced oxidative stress, contributing to reduced oxidative stress and improved cellular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over study investigated the effects of acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake on exercise-induced changes in antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress, inflammation, nitric oxide (NO) production, exercise performance, and recovery in well-trained male cyclists. Findings showed acute CF intake increased systemic epicatechin levels and total antioxidant capacity (TEAC/UA and UA), but did not significantly affect exercise-induced lipid peroxidation (MDA), inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), or NO production markers (L-arginine/ADMA, citrulline). While CF intake showed a tendency for improved late-stage performance in the first time trial, overall exercise performance and recovery were not significantly enhanced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake and cycling exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received an acute dose of either 903.75 mg of cocoa flavanols (CF) or a placebo (15 mg CF) in chocolate milk prior to exercise. The exercise protocol involved two 30-minute time trials (TT1 and TT2) performed at a workload equivalent to 75% of peak power output, separated by a 100-minute passive recovery. No explicit dose-response comparisons were conducted beyond the high-CF vs. placebo design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not significantly differ between CF and placebo (PL) intake or between different time points (no main effect of time or trial observed).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A monomeric flavanol component of cocoa, measured to assess systemic exposure to cocoa flavanols.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following consumption of CF-content chocolate milk during exercise trials.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact observed in this study context regarding CF intake or exercise on its serum concentration, indicating limited or no absorption/effect compared to epicatechin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in acute HF patients (AUC 0.616, P<0.001; 90.59% specificity, 29.03% sensitivity), negatively correlated with NT-proBNP (R=-0.174, P=0.030), with a cutoff of 1203.525 pg/ml. Also decreased in saliva from NYHA class I/II HF patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Human cathelicidin peptide (analogue of CRAMP) involved in antimicrobial activity, immunomodulation, wound healing, chemoattraction, cell proliferation, cell migration, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal-transition, angiogenesis, inflammation, innate/adaptive immune response, and potential cardiac protection.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Heart Failure (HF) patients, NYHA class I/II HF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential novel diagnostic biomarker for acute HF; decreased circulating levels are associated with acute HF and observed in early-stage HF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated cord blood LL37 levels in preterm neonates and their association with preterm complications, particularly bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Findings indicate that LL37 levels are lower in preterm infants compared to term neonates, positively correlate with gestational age, decrease after prenatal/antenatal steroid administration, and that higher cord blood LL37 acts as an independent protective factor against the development and severity of BPD, potentially mediated by its negative association with the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prenatal steroid administration (investigated as a factor affecting LL37 levels)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Prenatal/antenatal steroid administration in preterm neonates was associated with decreased cord blood LL37 levels. No specific dosage, duration, or dose-response comparisons for the steroid treatment itself were reported in the context of its effect on LL37.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (in preterm neonates compared to term neonates and in BPD patients); higher (in serum post-birth, with increasing gestational age, and as a protective factor against BPD); decreased (after prenatal steroid administration); negatively correlated (with IL-6)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in preterm neonates than term neonates (P = 0.01). Serum LL37 levels 48–72 hours after birth in preterm were higher than cord blood (P = 0.01, n = 75). Positively correlated with gestational age (R = 0.347, P <0.0001; lower gestational age associated with lower LL37, B = 45.560, p = 0.004, n = 134). Decreased after antenatal steroid administration (B = -126.695, p = 0.027, n = 134). Cord blood levels were lower in neonates who developed BPD (p = 0.001); higher levels were an independent protective factor for BPD and associated with less severe BPD (n = 102). Negatively correlated with IL-6 concentration (R = -0.391, p <0.0001, n = 102). All measurements were performed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Human cathelicidin, a major antimicrobial peptide that plays a significant role in innate immunity, inflammation-induced tissue repair, and overall human immune defense. It promotes preterm pulmonary development and mediates protection against BPD, potentially by inhibiting pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Preterm birth and gestational development; postnatal adaptation (48-72 hours post-birth); prenatal/antenatal steroid administration; development and severity of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) in preterm neonates; perinatal inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in preterm neonates are associated with increased susceptibility to sepsis, excessive inflammatory responses, and a higher risk of BPD. Higher cord blood levels are an independent protective factor against developing BPD and are associated with less severe BPD, indicating improved respiratory outcomes. Postnatal increases may reflect adaptation to the extrauterine environment. Antenatal steroid use reduces LL37 levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently up-regulated in early and late passage cells of both hiPSC lines (by ESI-MS e) and confirmed by Western blot analysis. All selected proteins were confirmed to be up-regulated in hiPSC and hESC compared to somatic cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly stated, inferred as related to cellular processes and pluripotency.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Proposed novel pluripotency marker identification and validation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate novel pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: May reduce or prevent amyloid beta (A ) plaque deposition.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Primary Age-Related Tauopathy (PART) pathology compared to Alzheimer's Disease (AD) pathology.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with resistance to A  plaque deposition in PART individuals.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between thalamic volume and heart rate recovery following an orthostatic challenge in older adults from The Irish Longitudinal Study on Aging (TILDA). It consistently found that smaller thalamic volume is associated with slower heart rate recovery, suggesting that thalamic structural integrity is a potential risk marker for autonomic dysfunction, cardiovascular events, and sudden cardiac death, while also differentiating its contribution from other subcortical brain regions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Orthostatic Challenge (Active Standing Test)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in this observational study underwent an active stand protocol where they lay supine for 10 minutes, then stood quickly and remained standing for 3 minutes. Beat-to-beat heart rate and blood pressure were monitored, with heart rate recovery (HRR) specifically measured between 10 and 30 seconds post-standing (HRR 10|30s). This study focused on correlating brain volume with physiological response, thus no therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Interaction with HRR 10|30s was significantly different from the thalamus x HRR 10|30s interaction.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: B = 0.03; CI 95 0.01–0.04; p < .001 when compared to thalamus interaction.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Part of the basal ganglia, involved in goal-directed behavior, learning, and executive functions; also plays a role in autonomic regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with heart rate recovery after an orthostatic challenge, evaluated in a model including other subcortical regions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to autonomic regulation, with a differentiated role compared to the thalamus in heart rate response to standing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated endogenous Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with rtPA, aiming to determine its association with functional outcome and compare its levels to healthy controls and at 3 months post-stroke. Key findings indicate that plasma GLP-1 levels are elevated in acute stroke patients compared to healthy individuals and remain stable at 3 months, but these endogenous levels were not associated with functional outcome. document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Influences epigenetic age estimation and can reflect underlying immune status or health conditions, potentially impacting disease risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Shortened cell cycle duration (p < .05) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The time required for a cell to complete one round of division.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overexpression of eIF3a in CRC cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shortened cell cycle duration indicates accelerated cell division, contributing to enhanced cancer cell proliferation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated a stepwise, serum- and feeder-free protocol for differentiating human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) into hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) and red blood cells (RBCs). It specifically examined the effect of enforced HOXB4 expression on this process. While HOXB4 activation increased the production of multipotent HPCs (peaking around days 6-10, characterized by CD34, CD43, and Runx1C-GFP expression) and immature erythroid cells, it ultimately failed to promote the maturation, efficient enucleation, or expansion of adult-like RBCs.

This was integrated into a multi-step, serum- and feeder-free differentiation protocol lasting at least 17 days, involving sequential addition of various growth factors and cytokines (e.g., BMP4, VEGF, Wnt3a, Activin A, GSK-3 2 inhibitor VIII, FGF- 1, SCF, IGF2, TPO, Heparin, IBMX, Hydrocortisone, Flt3L, IL-3, IL-11, EPO, IGF1) at specific concentrations and time points. No quantitative dose-response comparisons for either HOXB4 activation or the overall differentiation protocol were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Superior migration potential compared to oMSC; siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown in sMSC decreased migration potential down to the oMSC level. Significantly more sMSC than oMSC migrated to the tumors and were detectable within the tumor tissue in vivo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the role of PPARγ1, specifically its K154/155 acetylation site, as a molecular switch in oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary adenocarcinoma tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and metastasis. Using in vitro cell models, in vivo mouse xenograft models, and human breast cancer patient datasets, the research demonstrated that K154/155 acetylation is essential for promoting tumor growth, de novo lipogenesis, and cancer stem cell characteristics, while also regulating cellular apoptosis and autophagy. The acetylation status was found to determine genome-wide DNA binding site selection, shifting from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) binding, and influencing transcriptional programs for growth factor signaling. Furthermore, gene signatures reflecting acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis (PASS1 and PASS2) showed predictive value for survival outcomes and distant metastasis-free survival in various breast cancer subtypes.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparing wild-type PPARγ1 with specific genetic variants (acetylation-defective mutants K154/155Q, K154/155A, an acetylation mimic K154/155R, and a sumoylation site mutant K77R) expressed in various breast cancer cell lines (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src) and in vivo in mouse xenograft models and transgenic mice with inducible Pparγ1 deletion. Experiments often involved subcutaneous injection of 1 x 10^6 cells. No dose-response comparisons of external therapeutic agents were reported; the focus was on the impact of specific molecular modifications and genetic manipulations, with the K154/155Q mutant demonstrating a significant ~90% reduction in tumor growth.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytotoxic and immunomodulatory effects of chemotherapeutic agents (cisplatin, oxaliplatin, pemetrexed) on malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) cell lines, both alone and in allogeneic co-culture with healthy donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). The primary aim was to assess the impact of these agents on the expression of immune checkpoints (PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3) and their ligands (PD-L1, PD-L2, galectin-9) to inform rational combination strategies with immune checkpoint blockade. While chemosensitivity varied by cell line (e.g., NCI-H2818 more sensitive to cisplatin and oxaliplatin, no response to pemetrexed), the expression of immune checkpoints and their ligands on MPM cells and PBMCs was mostly downregulated or unaltered, with only TIM-3 on PBMC co-cultured with NCI-H2731 showing significant alteration after cisplatin treatment. The findings generally showed no clear trend or significant changes, highlighting interexperimental variability and suggesting complex interactions relevant for designing optimal immunotherapy combination schedules.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Desired inhibitory concentrations (IC values: IC20, IC40, IC50, IC60) for cisplatin, oxaliplatin, and pemetrexed were determined via SRB-assay across three MPM cell lines (NCI-H2818, NCI-H2795, NCI-H2731). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. The aim was to evaluate systemic and muscle-related stress responses and recovery patterns, comparing biomarkers at 1 day (R+1) and 15 days (R+15) post-landing with pre-flight values and age-matched controls. Findings revealed a strong spaceflight-induced stress response in muscle tissue, leading to a proinflammatory state, with inflamma-miRs and myo-miR-206 mediating systemic recovery, and significant inter-individual differences in biomarker responses were observed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Post-exercise levels increased after each bout, reaching similar levels (around 450-462*10^3 GE/mL). Significant increases (p<0.05) were observed after the second (from 229±216 to 450±228*10^3 GE/mL) and third bouts (from 173±120 to 462±314*10^3 GE/mL). The first percentage increment was lower than subsequent ones, and the overall exercise-induced increase was much lower than cf n-DNA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively investigates the potentials, pitfalls, and practical applications of blood-based biomarkers for objective individualized monitoring of training load, recovery, and health status in elite sports. It evaluates the utility and limitations of established markers like creatine kinase (CK), lactate, C-reactive protein (CRP), urea, myoglobin, and various leukocyte populations, detailing their physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise, kinetics, and implications for muscle damage, immune function, and inflammation. The document also addresses methodological considerations, confounding variables, the need for individual reference ranges, and statistical approaches for interpreting biomarker changes, concluding with recommendations for best practices in their sport-specific use.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-based biomarker monitoring in conjunction with physical exercise and training load management in elite sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review focuses on the application and interpretation of blood-based biomarkers for athlete monitoring across various exercise loads, including strenuous, resistance, high-intensity, submaximal, acute physical stress, soccer matches, ultradistance races, and long-term intensive endurance exercise. Biomarker responses are noted to depend on exercise modality, intensity, duration, and individual factors such as ethnicity and body composition. While specific exercise regimens like 30 minutes of endurance running (65% vs 85% of VO2max) showed CRP increases, no single standardized dose-response is consistently reported or compared across all biomarkers. The document emphasizes the need for individual reference levels, standardized collection, and careful consideration of confounding variables, particularly in managing workload by adjusting training when physiological parameters exceed baseline.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Could detect the onset of overtraining (long-term decrement in performance capacity) in a resistance training setting, although the definition of overtraining was not actually met in the specific study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly detailed in the text, but levels are associated with cellular stress and damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Resistance training setting
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential indicator for the onset of overtraining, but with limited demonstration and validation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time course of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and conventional muscle damage markers in response to mechanically demanding muscle-damaging drop jump exercise without significant metabolic stress in healthy males. It found that cfDNA levels increased acutely and with a delayed response up to 72 hours post-exercise, correlating strongly with primary muscle damage indicators (low-frequency fatigue, MVIC torque, P20/P100 torque) and delayed-onset muscle soreness. This suggests cfDNA is a sensitive marker for acute loss of muscle function after mechanical stress, offering insights into primary and secondary muscle damage responses.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Muscle-damaging exercise (Drop Jumps)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fourteen participants performed 50 intermittent drop jumps once, from heights of approximately 0.5 m (ranging from 30.37 ± 5.55 cm to 36.39 ± 6.83 cm) with 20-second rest intervals between each jump. This protocol was designed to be mechanically demanding, inducing sufficient primary and secondary muscle damage, without placing the organism under significant metabolic stress. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels increased acutely from 0.97 ± 0.19 to 1.5 ± 0.21 ng/mL (log10 scale, P < 0.01) immediately post-exercise, normalizing by 90 min. Significant delayed increases were also observed after 6 h (1.25 ± 0.25 ng/mL, P < 0.01), 12 h (1.29 ± 0.27 ng/mL, P < 0.01), 48 h (1.26 ± 0.41 ng/mL, P < 0.05), and 72 h (1.42 ± 0.55 ng/mL, P < 0.01), recovering by 96 h. Moderate increases (approximately 5-fold) were noted.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Circulating nucleic acids released from cells into the bloodstream, reflecting cell injury/death (passive release) or active cellular secretion; involved in aseptic inflammatory responses and immune cell activation. It is a pro-inflammatory, load-dependent marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Muscle-damaging exercise (50 intermittent drop jumps) performed without significant metabolic stress; changes in response to severe primary and secondary muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A sensitive and comprehensive marker for acute loss of muscle function (primary muscle damage) and secondary muscle damage. The initial elevation likely reflects primary muscle damage, while secondary increases may indicate local inflammation.
