matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Short-term powdered tart cherry supplementation surrounding a half-marathon run and 48-h recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced physiological stress and muscle catabolism, as well as an improved anabolic/catabolic balance during and after endurance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased, dynamic responses, negatively correlated with miR-133a
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant changes for Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) protocols, with peak values observed 0 h post-exercise (p < 0.05). Plasma levels were increased in response to Maximum Strength (MS) protocol, peaking after 24 h recovery (p < 0.05). Showed a significant negative correlation with miR-133a (R = -0.53, p = 0.04).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Catabolic stress hormone involved in stress response, muscle breakdown, and anabolic-catabolic balance. Also associated with gains in type II fiber area.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Resistance Training, specifically Muscular Strength Endurance (SE), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH), and Maximum Strength (MS) protocols.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for monitoring training responses and neuromuscular adaptations, indicating physiological stress response to exercise, and potentially stressful training (overreaching). Also associated with muscle structural adaptation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Chronically elevated levels, consistently high during chronic stress or dysregulation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone and catabolic hormone; inhibits protein synthesis, blocks anabolic signaling, and is immunosuppressive; involved in endocrine regulation and long-term dysregulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Long-term dysregulation, overtraining, chronic stress, fatigue, performance decrements, and endocrine regulation of muscle adaptations during training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Integrates with other markers for health/overtraining status; chronically elevated levels indicate catabolic state, impeding muscle mass maintenance and recovery, and signaling chronic stress, fatigue, and performance decrements, and increased overtraining risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a single 6g dose of citrulline malate (CM) supplementation on muscle recovery after a high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session in untrained young adult men, examining functional, metabolic, anabolic, and physiological markers. The findings concluded that CM supplementation does not improve the muscle recovery process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Citrulline Malate (CM) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single oral dose of 6 g of citrulline malate (CM) was administered 60 minutes pre-workout, dissolved in 200 mL water. Participants then performed a single session of high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) consisting of 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions at 90% of 10RM for leg press and hack squat exercises, with 2 min rest between sets and exercises, performed with a 1s concentric:2s eccentric cadence. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and no significant treatment × time interaction was found for any measured variables, indicating CM did not improve recovery compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific significant changes or treatment × time interactions were reported for individual cortisol levels with CM supplementation versus placebo; only the Testosterone:Cortisol ratio was analyzed for significance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glucocorticoid stress hormone that plays a catabolic role, involved in glucose metabolism, immune response, and regulation of stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blood samples collected pre- and post-exercise, and immediately after muscular fatigue tests (24, 48, and 72 h after RE session) during CM or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Catabolic hormone level, often reflecting physiological stress and potentially hindering recovery or adaptation if elevated chronically.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Hormone concentration, HPA axis activity (cortisol awakening response, morning levels)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, elevated activity, or unchanged (depending on measurement type/study)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: HPA axis hyperactivity reported in early HD. Elevated salivary cortisol awakening response (CAR) found in premanifest HD mutation carriers. Morning cortisol levels were higher in premanifest HD subjects compared to symptomatic HD subjects. Shows circadian rhythmicity, requiring standardized sampling.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, involved in stress response, metabolism, and mood regulation; also a stress hormone.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD mouse models, various patient stages); HPA axis activity; circadian rhythm.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates potential hyperactivity of the HPA axis in the premanifest stage of HD, which may contribute to depressive symptoms. Its levels show circadian rhythmicity, necessitating standardized sampling times for reliable measurement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: decreased in ITG, significantly higher in CG
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In CG, significantly increased from T1: 15.4 ± 3.2 mg/dL to T2: 19.3 ± 6.1 mg/dL, representing a 24.74 ± 25.84% increase (p = 0.005). In ITG, decreased non-significantly from T1: 16.2 ± 5.9 mg/dL to T2: 15.1 ± 2.3 mg/dL, representing a -13.54 ± 13.61% change (p > 0.05). The increase in CG was significantly greater than the change in ITG (p < 0.05). Moderate to high negative correlations were observed with sFe (r = −0.596; p = 0.011), Hb (r = −0.910; p < 0.001), and FER (r = −0.962; p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone involved in catabolic processes, anti-anabolic actions related to protein turnover, and modulation of exercise-induced inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España) with 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels indicate higher effort-induced stress and inadequate recovery; lower levels indicate better stress modulation, muscle repair/regeneration, and optimal recovery for future performances.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the circadian rhythmicity and diurnal variation of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and healthy controls. It found that sST2 exhibits a distinct diurnal rhythm with lower values in the morning and peaks in the late afternoon. The study also compared sST2's rhythmicity to N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), which showed no diurnal rhythm, and to melatonin and cortisol, which demonstrated expected circadian patterns. These findings highlight the impact of diurnal variation on the clinical interpretation and management of sST2 levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker diurnal variation and circadian rhythm analysis for clinical monitoring and interpretation guidance
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from 16 HFrEF patients and 16 controls at seven specific time points (9 a.m., 1 p.m., 5 p.m., 9 p.m., 1 a.m., 5 a.m., and 9 a.m.) over a 24-hour period. The study focused on observational biomarker patterns and did not involve therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or standardized conditions for physical activity, meals, light exposure, or sleep duration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exhibited an intact and expected diurnal pattern in all subjects, peaking during the early morning (modal value: 9 a.m.) with values diametrically opposite to melatonin.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulator of circadian rhythms; main endocrine product of the central clock.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diurnal variation in chronic heart failure patients (HFrEF) and healthy controls, used as a control for circadian rhythms.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the presence of normal, intact circadian rhythms and preserved neurohumoral circadian output in the study subjects, serving as a positive control for the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: no immediate change, then decreased, then increased
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No immediate change after exercise (F2.33 = 99.89; p < 0.001 for main effect), decreased 3 hours after (p < 0.001), then increased again 24 hours after, remaining increased compared to pre-exercise levels (p < 0.001). Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC < 0.75 or ICC = 0.70).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glucocorticoid stress hormone involved in metabolism, immune response, and physiological adaptation; stress hormone.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 60-min continuous endurance exercise bouts; endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the general physiological stress response and recovery processes following endurance exercise, but suggests limited suitability due to moderate reliability for reliable monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in relation to some metrics, lower in others
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with CMJ values (+1.441). Negatively associated with VO2 max values (-0.974) in predictive regression models (p < 0.001 for overall models). Used as a predictor in significant regression equations for fitness parameters (R2 adjusted up to 0.930).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, strong indicator of catabolic metabolism, involved in energy metabolism and immune response; modified by physical stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer playing/training, pre-seasonal training, analyzed for its predictive ability on fitness parameters (CMJ, VO2 max).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels predict improved explosive vertical jump ability. Lower levels predict better aerobic capacity. Its direct correlation with an optimal fitness level is not always automatic, but it indicates acute/prolonged physical stress response. Useful tool in early detection of overtraining, especially when considered in ratio with testosterone; used to predict fitness parameters.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (from 14.7 to 17.0 μg/dL) and at 30 min post-exercise for all participants (p<0.01). Experienced participants exhibited significantly higher concentrations both post-exercise (p=0.001) and at 30 min post-exercise (p=0.036) compared to novice participants. Novice participants' cortisol was significantly higher than pre-exercise only at 30 min post-exercise (p=0.045). Significantly correlated with the number of rounds performed (r = 0.53; p = 0.010).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, regulates metabolism and immune responses; a primary stress hormone involved in metabolism, immune regulation, and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT), comparison between novice and experienced participants. Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Acute response to single CrossFit 'Cindy' workout.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute physiological stress response to intense exercise. Higher levels in experienced participants suggest greater overall work performed, and prolonged high levels following high-intensity exercise warn of potential negative health outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 4-month omega-3 supplementation on cellular aging-related biomarkers (telomerase, cortisol, and inflammatory cytokines) in sedentary, overweight, middle-aged adults following a laboratory speech stressor. Omega-3 supplementation was found to alter telomerase and IL-10 stress reactivity by protecting against post-stress declines, and to reduce overall cortisol and IL-6 levels during stress, suggesting a stress-buffering effect that may slow accelerated aging and reduce depression risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Omega-3 Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily doses of either 2.5 g/d omega-3 (2085 mg EPA, 348 mg DHA), 1.25 g/d omega-3 (1042.5 mg EPA, 174 mg DHA), or a placebo for 4 months, involving 6 pills (3 g oil) per day. A dose-response was observed, where the 2.5 g/d dose significantly lowered overall cortisol and IL-6 levels, while both omega-3 doses prevented post-stress declines in telomerase and IL-10 levels compared to placebo.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower overall levels during stressor with high-dose omega-3; rose in response to stressor across all participants
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Omega-3 supplementation lowered total cortisol levels throughout the stressor in a dose-response manner (p=0.04). The 2.5 g/d group had a significant 19% lower overall cortisol levels compared to the placebo group (p=0.01). The 1.25 g/d group did not differ significantly from placebo (p=0.29). Cortisol reactivity, measured by AUCi, was not significantly impacted (p=0.44).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary stress hormone, mediating the body's 'fight or flight' response and involved in various physiological processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Total cortisol levels during and after a laboratory speech stressor (Trier Social Stress Test) in sedentary, overweight, middle-aged adults, following 4 months of omega-3 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower stress-induced cortisol release indicates a potential to prevent common chronic diseases and depression, and is associated with longer telomeres. Exaggerated cortisol responses are associated with shorter telomeres.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study investigating the biobehavioral impacts of sexual violence victimization and revictimization, integrated with support protocols for the participant.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single case study (N=1) involved longitudinal observation over 6 months, with data collected across five study visits (M0, M1, M3, M4, M6) following four acute sexual violence (SV) events (including vaginal rape and revictimization prior to M3 and M5 visits). Data collection included surveys, blood draws, cervicovaginal exams, and self-collected diurnal saliva samples. Integrated support protocols were provided, but no active interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Hormone Concentration (including Cortisol Awakening Response, CAR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dysregulated and dampened over time, with a distinctive Cortisol Awakening Response (CAR) observed only at M0. The diurnal profile was dysregulated within the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis; specific quantitative data beyond these descriptions were not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of stress response and adaptation, part of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, and involved in circadian rhythm (Cortisol Awakening Response) in response to ACTH and stress stimuli.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Repeat sexual violence victimization and revictimization over a 6-month longitudinal assessment period within The THRIVE Study, associated with trauma and chronic stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates dysregulation and dampened/attenuated activity of the HPA axis, mirroring neuroendocrine consequences of intense, chronic stress and trauma. This suggests a compromised stress response and impairment of cortisol production regulation, linked to adverse mental health. Monitoring is valuable in coordination with mental health changes during repeated sexual trauma, with potential considerable consequences for downstream physiological systems and contribution to allostatic load.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Changes in stress levels are being investigated (in current study protocol); results not yet available.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes from baseline will be collected and analyzed; assessed via SalivaBio Collection Aid (Salimetrics) from morning collections.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary stress hormone involved in regulating metabolism, inflammation, and immune responses; mediates physiological stress response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week probiotic intervention; morning collection during baseline visit; probiotic intervention and post-intervention treadmill endurance testing in non-elite runners.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of stress; expected to indicate physiological stress levels, potentially affected by probiotic supplementation and endurance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marginally elevated; noted as the only abnormality in the study cohort.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A stress hormone involved in regulating metabolism, immune response, and stress response; if chronically elevated, it may contribute to bone loss.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General health status of the study cohort, assessed after a short break in the training season. Assessment in elite male rowers undergoing high or low calcium dietary interventions and intense rowing exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Ongoing elevated cortisol may contribute toward bone loss, independent of low energy availability. The marginal elevation was noted as an abnormality in the cohort, but not directly linked to the calcium intervention effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at T2 (pT1–T2 = 0.03, pT2–T3 < 0.01); no significant difference between T1 and T3 (pT1–T3 = 0.16). Statistically significant differences were noted between baseline (T1), shortly after the ultramarathon (T2), and after recovery (T3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone involved in the body's stress response, energy regulation, and immune response; an important part of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis with immunosuppressive effects.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running), immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2), and during recovery (T3).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological stress response and recovery status in athletes. Offers potential for innovative monitoring of exercise and recovery. A significant negative correlation with blood procalcitonin and CRP at baseline suggests decreased inflammatory markers due to cortisol's immunosuppressive effect.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased from T1 to T2 (pT1–T2 < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone that regulates metabolism, immune response, and sympathetic nervous system activity; an important part of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis with immunosuppressive effects.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running) and immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a significant systemic physiological stress response to prolonged extreme exercise. Offers potential for innovative monitoring of exercise and recovery. A significant negative correlation with blood procalcitonin and CRP at baseline suggests decreased inflammatory markers due to cortisol's immunosuppressive effect.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative literature review investigates biosensor approaches for continuous, real-time in vivo monitoring of molecular markers relevant to performance and health status. It highlights the limitations of current technologies and proposes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors as a generalizable, minimally invasive solution. The review details the development, validation, and attributes (generalizability, selectivity, reversibility, stability) of EAB sensors for detecting diverse targets (drugs, metabolites, hormones, proteins) in complex biological fluids and tissues. It also addresses the technological hurdles for subcutaneous placement, the correlation between interstitial fluid and systemic concentrations, and their potential for monitoring stress indicators (e.g., cortisol) and HPA/HPG axis hormones to assess overtraining syndromes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) Sensor Technology for Real-time In Vivo Molecular Monitoring
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This narrative literature review discusses the development and application of Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) sensors for continuous, real-time in vivo molecular monitoring, without an applied 'dose' in the traditional sense as it is a review of technology. EAB sensors, including 75-µm-diameter, 3-mm-long versions, have been tested in live rats for plasma monitoring (jugular vein) for up to 12 hours with few-second to sub-second resolution and clinically relevant precision. They are also adapted for minimally invasive subcutaneous placements (microneedles, indwelling needles) for interstitial fluid monitoring (e.g., brain, tumor, dermal ISF). The review highlights the importance of seconds-resolved time resolution and nanomolar limits of detection for hormones (achieved for LH and NGAL, micromolar for others). Time delays between subcutaneous ISF and plasma concentrations (e.g., 5-12 min for glucose, ~17 min for vancomycin) and correlations (strong for cortisol, <6% error for glucose) are noted, influenced by target properties. No dose-response comparisons for sensor parameters or monitoring duration were explicitly reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased secretion during stress; exhibits complex temporal patterns, including ultradian, circadian, and stress-induced oscillations, with high variability.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels in saliva and blood are strongly correlated. Typically rises ~3-5 min after HPA axis activation, peaking ~30 min later. Ultradian (every 60 min), circadian (decreases during day), and stress-induced (within minutes) oscillations are observed. Social and emotional experiences can account for over 70% of variation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary end product of the HPA axis; mediates stress response, energy mobilization, increased arousal and vigilance, inhibition of nonessential anabolic activity, and regulation of various physiological functions.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Stress, HPA (hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal) axis activity, acute response to stress, social and emotional experiences, monitoring of cumulative stress and insufficient recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of stress and HPA axis function; dysregulation associated with overtraining, functional over-reaching, and non-functional overreaching syndromes; contributes to adaptations during acute stress; relevant for monitoring cumulative stress and insufficient recovery and performance status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Some studies reported fluctuations related to SP, and findings were contradictory regarding its effect. Whey protein reduced cortisol's increase during recovery, while SP's specific impact was not consistently quantified.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, involved in glucose metabolism, immune function, and catabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein supplementation in active individuals and athletes; during recovery after exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Inconsistent effects mean no clear indication of benefit or detriment for recovery, muscle adaptation, or stress response from this review.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in exercise group, lower in control group
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were increased in the exercise group and decreased significantly in the control group following 14 days of bed rest intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glucocorticoid hormone involved in stress response, glucose metabolism, immune function, and inflammation regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 14 days of bed rest intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of stress response and adaptation; changes can reflect physiological strain (exercise group) or altered adrenal function/reduced metabolic demand (control group) during bed rest.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (males), upward trend (females, not significant), unchanged (females)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in male COMP during competition preparation (p < 0.05, PRE to MID). Increased significantly in male COMP from MID to POST (p < 0.05), but not significantly different from CTRL. Female athletes showed an upward trend during competition preparation, though not statistically significant. No significant changes were observed in female groups across the study for specific time points.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key stress hormone (glucocorticoid) involved in glucose metabolism, immune response, and inflammation regulation. It is generally catabolic, and its elevation is typically linked to low energy availability (LEA).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) and the subsequent recovery phase in physique athletes, suggesting an adaptive response to energy stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels in males indicate increased physiological stress, potentially promoting catabolism and impairing recovery. A persistent increase during recovery suggests ongoing physiological stress. Stability or non-significant changes in females may indicate different stress coping mechanisms.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Altered, with significant alterations observed in response to training and competition loads. Levels can be continually elevated, with more pronounced increases after consecutive matches. Specific direction of alterations caused by chronic training load remains unclear, and levels show variability. Contributes to hormonal strain.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Catabolic stress hormone involved in physiological adaptation, stress response, and anabolic/catabolic balance, reflecting metabolic strain and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Physiological loads from intensive training, competition loads (TL and CL), training load-induced stress across competitive seasons, and periods of fixture congestion in professional male team sport athletes. Used for chronic fatigue monitoring.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects measurable physiological strain, catabolic state, and hormonal strain. Provides useful information for athlete monitoring to detect dysfunctional physiological responses and indicate increased stress and fatigue, though with limitations due to variability. Useful for balancing stress and recovery, indicating physiological adaptation, and helping curtail risks of overtraining, injury or disease. Interpretation as part of the testosterone/cortisol ratio requires sex-specific considerations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dysregulations, including significant associations with alterations in salivary cortisol, are linked to AD development and progression, cognitive decline, and neurodegeneration. Levels increase with physical activity and mental/cognitive stressors. Morning awakening salivary cortisol is decreased in patients with insomnia. Subject to diurnal fluctuations and a high awakening response. Levels were higher when collected using cotton rolls, indicating measurement interference.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, involved in hormonal, metabolic, and endocrinological changes, and regulates metabolism, immune response, and sleep-wake cycles.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease development and progression, preclinical stages, physical activity, mental/cognitive stressors, sleep disturbances (insomnia), diurnal variations, and saliva collection methods (cotton rolls).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential non-invasive diagnostic biomarker for AD, indicating hormonal, metabolic, and endocrinological changes, and stress response. Requires careful timing and control of pre-analytical variables (activity, mental state, time of day, collection materials) for accurate assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased post-exercise in all groups (p < 0.001), but no significant trial differences were found between supplementation groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone involved in the regulation of metabolism, immune response, and physiological stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-2.25 h intensive cycling, following 2-week hemp fiber (high/low dose) or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of physiological stress response; the increase reflects exercise-induced stress, but hemp fiber had no effect on the acute stress response differences to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then decreased rapidly during recovery
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Rose sharply after both matches, mirroring ACTH pattern, with elevations up to 3-fold. Specifically, Athlete 1 increased by 40% after match 1 and 165% after match 2; Athlete 2 increased by 130% after match 1 (reaching upper limit of 0.690 µmol/L) and 222% after match 2. Short recovery sessions consistently promoted significant reductions; the increase for Athlete 2 after the second match lasted for a shorter time compared to Athlete 1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary systemic stress hormone (glucocorticoid) involved in regulating metabolism, immune response, and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition Day (during/post-matches), short recovery sessions, intense competitive exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates significant physiological stress and HPA axis activation, with recovery during short rest periods. Essential for understanding immune response and glycemic regulation in sports. Higher levels suggest a more pronounced stress response; individuals with heightened hormonal stress responses may benefit from additional recovery days or alternative recovery modalities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced in untrained CD group (9.89 	 2.05 	/dL vs. PLAC 11.76 	 2.21 	/dL; p < 0.05) and in trained CD group (8.32 	 2.17 	/dL vs. PLAC 10.46 	 2.72 	/dL; p < 0.05). Overall, statistically significant improvements indicating alleviated stress.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary stress hormone, involved in catabolism, energy metabolism, immune regulation, and stress response; elevated levels can hinder muscle growth and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation (5g daily for 8 weeks) combined with progressive resistance training; post-resistance training recovery; modulation of the Hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis by CD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced physiological stress and catabolic responses, facilitating post-exercise recovery, mitigating fatigue, and improving overall well-being.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in response to both EXE and EXO trials, exhibiting a gradual rise and reaching peak concentrations in the recovery phase (EXE: p < 0.001 at 38°C; EXO: p < 0.01 at 38.5°C). A greater increase was observed in the EXE trial compared to the EXO trial.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary stress hormone involved in regulating metabolism, immune response, and fight-or-flight reactions, mediating stress responses through the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Heat stress (EXE and EXO trials) induced by core temperature increases, with samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments up to 39°C and subsequent decrease until 37.5°C, particularly during heating and recovery phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the physiological stress response to thermal challenges and recovery dynamics. Reflects slower HPA axis activation compared to the SNS, with higher levels in EXE reflecting greater overall physiological stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Statistically unchanged over time in all groups, but generally higher in combined HC users compared to other groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged throughout the investigation (pre, post ~23 weeks of LEA, and recovery) in all groups, with no significant main effect for time (F=0.953, p=0.391) or group*time interaction (F=0.654, p=0.626). However, overall, cortisol was significantly higher in combined HC users than in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females (significant main effect for group, F=21.452, p<0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary glucocorticoid stress hormone, regulated by the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis. It is involved in regulating metabolism, immune response, inflammation, and maintaining blood pressure, acting as a catabolic hormone
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by diet and physical training in female physique athletes, with a comparative analysis across combined hormonal contraceptive users, progestin-only hormonal contraceptive users, and naturally menstruating females at pre, post, and recovery time points
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Statistically unchanged levels across groups over time suggest maintained HPA axis homeostasis despite LEA, or adaptive mechanisms. However, the generally higher concentrations in combined HC users indicate a differential baseline stress response, which is relevant for metabolic regulation, muscle tissue remodeling, and overall physiological stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Significant increases after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.63). Intensification of training demands translates to a rise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A primary stress hormone involved in regulating metabolism, immune response, and inflammation; indicates catabolic status and psychophysiological stress response to external stimulus.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after intense physical exertion and intensification of training demands.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects physiological stress response to intense physical activity; indicates catabolic status; important for evaluating anabolic/catabolic balance and managing stimulus/recovery to minimize illness/injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased by 27% in response to exercise during short recovery (SRecover), returning to basal levels during long recovery (LRecover).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, involved in physiological stress response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During short and long recovery periods following CCombat exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of physiological stress response to intensive exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Area Under the Curve of Cortisol

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the experienced group compared to novice participants (p=0.004). Significant acute perturbations; significantly different from pre-exercise (p < 0.05); significantly greater than post-30min and post-24h (p < 0.05); significantly greater than post-30min (p < 0.05); significantly greater than pre-exercise only for ALL and EXP (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An integrative measure of the total physiological stress response as indicated by cortisol levels over a period.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following a single 'Cindy' HIFT workout session, with differential responses between experienced and novice participants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the overall magnitude of the physiological stress response over time to high-intensity exercise, potentially correlating with training status or recovery.
