document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 30 mL of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) or an energy-matched placebo twice per day (8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.) for eight consecutive days, including four days pre-trial and throughout the trial period. The MC contained 73.5 mg 7L 91 cyanidin-3-glucoside, 178.8 gallic acid equivalent 7L 91 total phenolic content, and a TEAC of 0.58 trolox equivalents 7L 91. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The MC group showed faster recovery; CMJ decrease was significantly attenuated at 24 h (5%, p=0.022) and 48 h (6%, p=0.017) versus placebo. Overall faster recovery in MC group (p<0.05). (Time: F(1,4)=30.320, p<0.001,  72=0.684; Group: F(1,2)=7.336, p=0.017,  72=0.345; Interaction: F(1,4)=3.334, p=0.028,  72=0.193).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures lower body power and explosiveness
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity (adapted Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test) with MC supplementation vs. placebo, observed over 72 h post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates restoration of lower body power and functional capacity, showing MC reduces performance decline and accelerates recovery after strenuous exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of consuming cow's milk versus an energy-matched carbohydrate solution on recovery markers and performance in twenty female team-sport athletes following repeated simulated team games (STGs). The findings indicated that 500 mL of milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function (peak torque for knee extension and flexion), sprint performance (5m and 10m), and perceptions of stress, and helped reduce muscle soreness and tiredness, particularly after the first STG. However, for many other physiological and performance markers (e.g., CK, hsCRP, LOOHs, PCs, CMJ, HR, RPE), the effects were mostly unclear or trivial, with milk showing no clear benefit after the second STG.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional intervention (consumption of cow's milk vs. an energy-matched carbohydrate solution) combined with a multi-stage physical activity protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 500 mL of either cow's milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g protein, 25.5 g carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat) or an energy-matched carbohydrate solution (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 53.6 g carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat) immediately following each of two simulated team games (STG1 and STG2). The 17 g protein from milk was noted to be below the recommended 20 g threshold for maximal protein synthesis stimulation. The exercise protocol involved two ~30 minute halves of intermittent running with sprints, agility, and jumps, separated by a 10-minute half-time, with a 48-hour recovery period between STG1 and STG2. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the nutritional interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Trivial effects were seen for CMJ within-group (STG1 to STG2) for both MILK and CHO. A trivial outcome was observed for STG1 vs. STG2 between MILK vs. CHO (-0.8  
	± 6.8% vs. -0.4  
	± 3.3%). A comparison of CMJ from STG1 to STG2 revealed no clear benefit of MILK. CMJ height was approximately 80% of the isolated jump height during the STG.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measure of lower body power, explosiveness, and neuromuscular efficiency.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery from simulated team-sport games (STG1 and STG2) after cow's milk consumption, and between-group comparison of MILK vs. CHO.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lower body power, muscle recovery, and fatigue status, affecting jump performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), inflammatory indices, hematological markers, and performance decline in soccer players following a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). The LIST protocol induced transient changes in immune cells, inflammatory markers, and declines in performance. BC supplementation demonstrated potential in mitigating some EIMD, improving recovery of muscle power (SQJ), and attenuating post-exercise increases in inflammatory markers (CRP, CK, IL-6) compared to pre-supplementation and/or whey protein, suggesting better maintenance of performance and reduced post-exercise EIMD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Bovine Colostrum (BC) and Whey Protein (WP) supplementation in conjunction with a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A low-dose of 3.2 g/day of either bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) was administered for 6 weeks to soccer players. This consisted of 8 capsules x 400 mg per capsule. The LIST protocol was performed pre- and post-supplementation. No dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported, as only one dose was used; however, comparisons were made between pre- and post-supplementation responses, and directly between the BC and WP groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower (sustained significant decline of ~8 to 10% from 24 to 48 h post-LIST). BC supplementation did not significantly affect CMJ kinetics, with similar declines observed for LIST 1 and LIST 2 in both groups. The stretch-shortening cycle in CMJ might mask negative performance effects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures lower body explosive power and reactive strength, incorporating eccentric-concentric muscle actions.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute muscle fatigue and decline in athletic performance following strenuous exercise; BC did not significantly improve it in this study, potentially due to methodological factors masking effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This placebo-controlled, double-blind, six-arm crossover study investigated the effects of a single 60 mg Cannabidiol (CBD) supplementation versus placebo after an intensive resistance training protocol (designed to induce muscle damage) on skeletal muscle regeneration and performance in healthy, well-trained participants. The study measured muscle damage biomarkers (Creatine Kinase and Myoglobin) and neuromuscular performance (1RM Back Squat and Countermovement Jump) at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. While overall effects were small, CBD significantly attenuated increases in CK and Myo concentrations and aided in the recovery of 1RM Back Squat performance after 72 hours, but showed no significant effect on Countermovement Jump performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cannabidiol (CBD) supplementation following an intensive strength training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Participants underwent an intensive strength training protocol consisting of three sets of 12 back squats at 70% of 1RM with 150 seconds rest, and three sets of 15 drop jumps from a 45 cm box landed in a deep squat with 60 seconds rest. A single dose of 60 mg CBD solubilisat or a placebo drink was consumed directly after exercise, with effects monitored at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. Absolute strength values and training loads averaged 118.6 
± 22.6 kg. The study did not include dose-response comparisons for CBD, nor did it investigate chronic supplementation or endurance training effects, and it was suggested that the protocol might not have induced sufficient power reduction for CMJ.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes observed at any time or over the course of the study, and no significant differences between groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of explosive lower body power and neuromuscular function, reflecting the ability to rapidly produce force and height in a vertical jump.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After intensive resistance training and single CBD supplementation, compared to placebo, measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours during recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an individual's explosive muscular power and readiness for explosive movements. The lack of observed change suggests that either the training protocol did not induce sufficient power reduction or the test might not be ideal for this specific outcome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of post-exercise milk consumption (500 mL) versus an energy-matched carbohydrate drink on recovery from a repeated sprinting and jumping protocol in female team-sport athletes. The strenuous protocol successfully induced muscle damage, leading to post-exercise decreases in muscle function (peak torque, countermovement jump, sprint performance, rate of force development) and increases in subjective muscle soreness and tiredness. Milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function, particularly for peak torque (knee extension/flexion at 180°/s) and countermovement jump height, and reduced perceived stress (DALDA B) at various time points (24h, 48h, 72h) post-exercise. The study concluded that milk may be a valuable recovery intervention for female team-sport athletes following this type of exercise, although its effects on serum creatine kinase, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, reactive strength index, and some sprint performances were unclear.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional intervention (Milk vs. Carbohydrate drink)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants immediately consumed either 500 mL of milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g Protein, 25.5 g Carbohydrate, 5.0 g Fat) or 500 mL of an energy-matched carbohydrate drink (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g Protein, 53.6 g Carbohydrate, 0.0 g Fat) following a whole-body sport and exercise protocol designed to induce muscle damage (15x20m maximal sprints and 8 sets of 10 plyometric jumps). The milk protein dose (17g) was noted to be potentially suboptimal for maximal protein synthesis compared to other studies. No dose-response comparisons were conducted, as a single volume of 500 mL was used for both interventions.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (post-exercise), significantly attenuated by milk (less decrease).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Post-exercise decreases in CMJ height were observed. Baseline: MILK 26.7 "+/-" 2.7 cm, CHO 26.7 "+/-" 3.5 cm. At B-24h: MILK 

−1.1 "+/-" 5.2% vs. CHO 

−9.7 "+/-" 15.1% (very likely moderate benefit, ES = 0.70). At B-48h: MILK 

−1.8 "+/-" 4.6% vs. CHO 

−9.6 "+/-" 8.1% (likely moderate benefit, ES = 0.67). At B-72h: MILK 

−0.6 "+/-" 2.1% vs. CHO 

−10.0 "+/-" 13.7% (likely small benefit, ES = 0.47). Milk attenuated losses in CMJ height.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indication of lower body power and neuromuscular coordination, reflecting explosive strength.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage from sprinting and jumping.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle fatigue and power output, serving as a marker for recovery from muscle damage. Recovery of CMJ is essential for many athletic activities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of various post-exercise recovery strategies (active recovery, cold water immersion, massage, and passive recovery) on subjective and objective fatigue markers in 46 recreational male runners after a competitive half-marathon. The findings indicate that cold water immersion and massage were effective in improving subjective fatigue measures, such as muscle soreness and perceived recovery/stress, compared to passive recovery. However, active recovery was largely ineffective or even detrimental, worsening subjective recovery and negatively impacting certain objective markers (creatine kinase, free-testosterone). Overall, none of the recovery interventions demonstrated beneficial effects on objective physiological markers of fatigue.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise recovery interventions (Active Recovery (ACT), Cold Water Immersion (CWI), Massage (MAS), and Passive Recovery (PAS)) following a half-marathon race.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
46 recreational male runners completed a competitive half-marathon (average time 107-116 min, 86.2%-92.9% of anaerobic threshold, 450 m altitude climb). Within 15 minutes post-race, a single application of one of four recovery protocols was performed: Passive Recovery (PAS) was 15 min sitting at rest; Active Recovery (ACT) was 15 min sub-maximal jogging at 60% anaerobic threshold; Cold Water Immersion (CWI) involved 15 min of lower limb immersion up to the iliac crest in 15 
	1
	C water, with circular leg motions every 2 min; and Massage (MAS) consisted of 20 min of classical sports massage (effleurage, petrissage, friction), split into 5 min per leg in prone and supine positions, performed by certified sports scientists. No dose-response comparisons for the overall half-marathon intensity or the recovery interventions were explicitly reported, though the CWI protocol was chosen based on existing dose-response evidence.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Cold water immersion (CWI) resulted in lower CMJ performance immediately post-recovery compared to passive recovery (PAS) (ES = -0.98), indicating a harmful effect. Measurements were taken 24 h before, immediately after recovery, and 24 h after the race.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of lower body power, explosive strength, and overall neuromuscular function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following a half-marathon race, specifically after cold water immersion.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the recovery of athletic performance capacity and neuromuscular function; lower height indicates reduced power and potentially inadequate recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of pre- versus post-exercise branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation on muscle recovery, delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP), muscle damage indicators (CK), and neuromuscular performance (CMJ) after resistance training in healthy untrained males. Resistance training induced DOMS and elevated inflammatory factors and muscle proteins. Post-exercise BCAA supplementation was generally more effective than pre-exercise supplementation in alleviating DOMS symptoms and reducing inflammatory factors (IL-6, CRP). While some findings indicated BCAA supplementation, particularly post-exercise, could reduce muscle soreness and inflammation markers, other analyses noted no significant effect on neuromuscular recovery (CMJ) or blood lactate levels, and mixed findings for CK between specific timing comparisons.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation combined with resistance training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: BCAA capsules at 40 mg/kg with a leucine:isoleucine:valine ratio of 2:1:1. Supplementation was administered either 30 minutes before resistance training or immediately after. The resistance training program, lasting one hour, included 90% 10RM weighted knee extensions, vertical jumps, and continuous frog jumps, designed to induce delayed-onset muscle soreness. The study focused on comparing the timing of BCAA intake (pre- vs. post-exercise) rather than varying the BCAA dosage.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Neuromuscular performance measure / Jump height measurement

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (between groups, but showed within-group recovery over time)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were found between BCAA supplementation groups (pre/post) and placebo groups for CMJ height during the 48-hr recovery period (p > .05). However, within both BCAA and placebo groups, CMJ height significantly increased from 30 min post-exercise to 24 hr and 48 hr recovery time points (e.g., BCAA group at 24 hr: 37.30 ± 4.45 vs 30 min: 34.72 ± 4.48; p < .001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Evaluates lower limb explosive power and neuromuscular function, often used to assess the recovery state of muscle power and performance capacity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery after resistance training (including deep squats), comparing different BCAA supplementation timings and placebo groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neuromuscular fatigue and recovery state; BCAA supplementation did not significantly enhance or alter the overall neuromuscular recovery compared to placebo or between timing regimens.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes between the three test sessions (T1, T2, T3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Explosive strength and power generation, particularly lower body, including the stretch-shortening cycle.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Competitive soccer periods (T1 to T3, including uncongested and congested periods).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lower body power. No change suggests stable power or a lack of significant impact from workload on this specific performance metric.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively investigates the underlying genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) regulation, including promoter mutations, methylation, and microRNAs. It elucidates hTERT's critical role in oncogenesis and cancer cell limitless self-renewal, exploring its clinical impacts as a diagnostic, prognostic, and potential therapeutic biomarker in telomerase-dependent cancers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This review focuses on the molecular mechanisms of hTERT regulation and its implications as a cancer biomarker and potential therapeutic target, including the discussion of an ongoing clinical trial for miR-34a mimics.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: As a comprehensive review, no specific therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were experimentally applied or detailed; rather, it discusses the potential of hTERT regulatory mechanisms and microRNAs as therapeutic targets, with a mention of a Phase I clinical trial for miR-34a mimics (NCT01829971) without dose specifics.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Associated with poor prognosis and responsiveness to drugs targeting DNA or H3K27 methylation
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific quantitative data provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An epigenetic modification pattern affecting tumor prognosis and drug responsiveness.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Ependymomas, specifically CIMP tumors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with poor prognosis in ependymomas and indicates responsiveness to specific DNA or H3K27 methylation targeting drugs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated blood-derived DNA methylation-based prediction models, including epigenetic scores (epi-LIBRA, epi-CAIDE) and a Multivariate Methylation Risk Score (MMRS), to assess and predict cognitive impairment and dementia (including AD and MCI) in various independent cohorts. The MMRS showed notable predictive capacity for MCI and prospective cognitive decline in AD and Parkinson's disease, and enhanced prediction when combined with traditional biomarkers, though individual epi-CAIDE and epi-LIBRA models performed poorly for AD and MCI status prediction. The study also detailed data preprocessing for various dementia risk factors, CSF biomarkers (amyloid- , tau, p-tau), whole blood DNA methylation profiling, and polygenic scores, aiming to investigate cognitive status and dementia.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Model Development and Validation using Epigenetic Markers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the development and validation of DNA methylation-based predictive models (including MMRS, epi-CAIDE, epi-LIBRA) for cognitive impairment and dementia. Whole blood genome-wide DNA methylation data, genotyping, and CSF biomarkers were utilized from various cohorts (EXTEND, EMIF-AD MBD, PPMI, ADNI, BASE-II) with different age ranges (40-75,  60 years). Models were constructed using machine learning techniques (e.g., ElasticNet, Random Forest, sPLS-DA, RF-RFE) with hyperparameter optimization via cross-validation. The study focused on predictive modeling and model performance comparisons, rather than therapeutic interventions or traditional dose-response relationships.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: CpGs/Genes associated with AMPA glutamate receptor clustering
matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Whole-blood (derived from DNA methylation data); Gene Ontology Analysis
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Ontology term enrichment; DNA Methylation sites contributing to molecular scores

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most overrepresented (Unadjusted P = 4.2e-4). Genes associated with CpGs contributing to the best-performing MMRS model were significantly overrepresented in the 'AMPA glutamate receptor clustering (GO:0097113)' GO term and include known dementia-related genes (e.g., APOE, DLG1, NLGN1, SHANK3, SHISA6, SHISA7, SSH1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Synaptic plasticity, learning, and memory. Dysregulation can contribute to neurodegenerative diseases. AMPA glutamate receptors are crucial for synaptic transmission; their increased removal from the post-synaptic membrane is associated with AD pathology. Methylation changes at these sites, even when measured in the blood, may resemble alterations that occur in the AD-affected brain.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Most overrepresented GO term by the union of CpGs used in 10 risk factor models contributing to MMRS-MCI. Key contributors to the MMRS model, providing biological meaning to the model's predictive capacity for cognitive impairment and dementia. Associated with molecular changes relevant to AD pathology.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a crucial molecular pathway implicated in MCI prediction by the MMRS model, potentially linked to synaptic dysfunction. Their involvement suggests the MMRS model captures biologically relevant mechanisms of dementia pathophysiology (e.g., synaptic dysfunction), enhancing the model's interpretability and potential for targeted intervention strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels observed in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls. Higher levels were associated with negative prognosis in urine, and also positively correlated with arterial hypertension and obesity/overweight in serum.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in energy metabolism (cellular energy storage and supply) and arginine and proline metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls, patient prognosis, arterial hypertension, and obesity/overweight.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for COVID-19 infection, prognosis, and associated with metabolic changes and comorbidities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as an influential factor in group differentiation (VIP score between 1.04 and 1.75), contributing to the overall reduction in amines (alongside amino acids) in the PFF group. Its inclusion in classic models (age, BMI, waist circumference, or cholesterol) significantly increased AUC from 76.7-78% to 100% (approaching significance).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Compound involved in energy storage and supply in cells, particularly muscle cells, and serves as an amine in metabolic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention, differentiating metabolic profiles between groups at 55 and 98 days, and used in predictive models to assess intervention impact from baseline to day 98.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to different health statuses, influencing group differentiation, and identified as a relevant metabolite that significantly improves the predictive power of statistical models for assessing dietary intervention impact.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between groups 55 days after starting the dietary intervention (p < 0.002).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Creatine is involved in energy storage; Choline is a precursor for acetylcholine and a methyl donor.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention at 55 days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentiating metabolite indicating the impact of the dietary intervention.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Creatine Kinase: Gefunden in 9 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute exhaustive exercise / Symptom-limited incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single session of acute exhaustive exercise was performed by 28 male chronic heart failure (CHF) participants (mean age 59.07  1 1.79 years). The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels (Table 3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased muscle damage following acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated circulating myomesin 3 fragments as a novel biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage, finding that plasma levels significantly increased 96 hours after acute eccentric exercise in humans and positively correlated with established muscle damage biomarkers (CK, Mb, LDH) and muscle symptoms (tenderness, DOMS).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Eccentric Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention involved nine healthy males performing 10 sets of 40 repetitions of one-leg calf-raise exercise (total 400 repetitions) with a load corresponding to half their body weight. Ankle ROM was maintained between 20 0 dorsiflexion and 15 0 plantar flexion, at a speed of 60 counts/min (1 repetition/s); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed a significant increase after the eccentric calf-raise exercise. Percent changes positively correlated with myomesin 3 fragments (R = 0.602, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytosolic enzyme that leaks into the blood following sarcolemma damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute eccentric exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Established biomarker for muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: After 1-month of treatment, there was no significant difference in CK levels between the high-effective Δhs-CRP (%) group (100.12 ± 55.76 U/L) and the low-effective group (100.62 ± 88.01 U/L, p = 0.198).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme found predominantly in muscle and brain tissue; catalyzes the interconversion of creatine and phosphocreatine, essential for energy storage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Statin-based lipid-lowering strategies after 1-month of treatment in patients post-PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels can indicate muscle injury or damage; no significant change suggests the treatments did not induce significant muscle damage in this patient cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Montmorency cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained cyclists undergoing three consecutive days of high-intensity simulated road cycle racing. Findings consistently showed that MC attenuated post-exercise oxidative stress, indicated by lower lipid hydroperoxides (LOOH), and inflammatory responses, evidenced by reduced interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), compared to a placebo. No significant effect was found on muscle damage markers (creatine kinase) or other cytokines (TNF-α, IL-8, and IL-1-β). This suggests that MC is effective in combating oxidative and inflammatory cascades induced by metabolically strenuous exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency Tart Cherry Concentrate (MC) Supplementation in conjunction with a high-intensity, simulated road cycling exercise protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Trained cyclists consumed 30 mL of Montmorency cherry concentrate or a placebo twice daily (8 am, 6 pm) for seven consecutive days (4 days pre-trial and throughout the 3-day trial period). The exercise protocol involved three consecutive days (days 5, 6, and 7 of supplementation) of a 109-minute simulated road cycling race, which included 66 sprints (5, 10, or 15 seconds) and specific time trials (2x2 min, 1x5 min). No dose-response comparisons for the MC supplement or exercise intensity were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No group or interaction effects were found for CK; no significant differences were apparent between MC and PLA groups. However, a significant main effect for time was observed (F(1,7) = 3.213, p = 0.007), indicating a small mean increase of 77 U/I across the trial period, reflecting a very small overall increase in CK.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme primarily found in muscle cells, released into the bloodstream upon muscle damage, thus serving as a marker for muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Responses to repeated days high-intensity stochastic cycling; MC supplementation did not significantly affect CK levels compared to placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Minimal to no significant impact on muscle damage (as indicated by CK) observed with MC supplementation, suggesting the exercise stress was primarily metabolic rather than mechanically damaging, and MC did not attenuate this particular marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 30 mL of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) or an energy-matched placebo twice per day (8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.) for eight consecutive days, including four days pre-trial and throughout the trial period. The MC contained 73.5 mg 7L 91 cyanidin-3-glucoside, 178.8 gallic acid equivalent 7L 91 total phenolic content, and a TEAC of 0.58 trolox equivalents 7L 91. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased overall, but unchanged between groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The trial significantly increased CK in both groups (F(1,4)=10.243, p=0.004,  72=0.423), with peak values of 1200 IU/L at 24 h. However, no significant group or interaction effects were found, indicating no protective effect of MC on CK compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme primarily found in muscle cells, released upon muscle damage, indicating muscle fiber integrity or injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Muscle damage markers following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity (adapted Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test) with MC supplementation vs. placebo, involving heavy eccentric load.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates level of muscle damage; lack of group difference suggests MC supplementation did not significantly mitigate this specific marker of muscle damage following this strenuous exercise protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated urinary proteins responsive to acute eccentric calf-raise exercise in healthy males, identifying an N-terminal fragment of titin. The urinary titin fragment significantly increased 96 hours post-exercise and correlated strongly with established blood biomarkers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion), proposing its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Eccentric Calf-Raise Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute, single-leg calf-raise exercise (right leg) involving repetitive eccentric muscle contractions. The protocol consisted of 10 sets of 40 repetitions (total 400 repetitions) with 3-minute rest between sets, performed at 60 counts/min. Ankle joint range of motion was maintained between 20° dorsiflexion and 15° plantar flexion, with an exercise load approximately half the subject's body weight. Samples were collected before and up to 96 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased on and after 48 h after exercise. Positive correlations with urinary titin fragment percentage change at 48 h (r = 0.98, p < 0.01) and 72 h (r = 0.79, p < 0.05; r = 0.81, p < 0.01). CK activities at 48 h correlated with DOMS at 48 h (r = 0.93, p < 0.01) and 72 h (r = 0.80, p < 0.05). Negative correlation between percentage changes in CK activity at 72 h and torque post exercise (r = -0.74, p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established marker of muscle damage, indicating muscle cell injury or integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After eccentric exercise; exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level; correlated with DOMS and reduced muscle strength.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive study investigated alpha-synuclein (αSN) as a potential diagnostic and monitoring biomarker for Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM). It evaluated αSN immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies and its concentration in serum and muscle homogenates, comparing IBM patients to other myopathies and healthy controls. The findings suggest αSN immunoreactivity in muscle is a promising diagnostic marker, while serum αSN levels could serve as a monitoring biomarker, correlating with disease duration and clinical severity in IBM. The study also explored the diagnostic utility of other established and emerging biomarkers in IBM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational/Diagnostic Biomarker Investigation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved a multimodal assessment of alpha-synuclein (αSN) levels and immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies, muscle tissue homogenates, and serum samples from various cohorts. Muscle biopsies (N=63, including 19 IBM, 21 other inflammatory myopathies, 20 other myopathies, 3 healthy controls) were analyzed by immunohistochemical staining. Serum samples (N=156, including 11 IBM, 25 other inflammatory myopathies, 53 hereditary myopathies, 30 mitochondriopathies, 37 healthy controls) were assessed by ELISA. Muscle homogenates were also examined (N=17 IBM, N=19 other inflammatory myopathies, N=5 hereditary myopathies, N=2 healthy controls). IBM patients were stratified by disease severity (IBMFRS) and disease duration for serum αSN analysis. No interventional dose or therapeutic comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic and monitoring biomarker evaluation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: IIM patients had higher CK activity than all other groups (specific values not provided in this excerpt). Correlated significantly with IBMFRS (r = 0.803, p = 0.012) in IBM patients. Showed a trend towards significant correlation with αSN concentrations (r = 0.62, p = 0.06) in IBM patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism, primarily found in muscle; elevated levels often indicate muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis/characterization of Inflammatory Myopathies (IIM) and correlation with IBM severity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher activity in IIM patients compared to other groups. In IBM, it correlates with IBMFRS, suggesting its utility as an indicator of muscle damage severity or disease burden.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of wearing exercise compression stockings (CS) on intramuscular pressure (IMP), muscle tissue oxygenation, and early blood biomarkers for muscle damage (myoglobin, creatine kinase) in the tibialis anterior muscle during a 10-km treadmill run in healthy recreational runners. Findings indicated that CS use significantly elevated IMP, reduced muscle tissue oxygenation, and increased serum myoglobin, suggesting non-beneficial muscle effects and no prevention of early exercise-induced muscle damage. Creatine kinase levels and systemic blood pressure remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise with Compression Stockings
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty healthy recreational runners performed two identical 10-km treadmill runs at a self-selected speed (10-12 km/h, no inclination) in a randomized crossover design, once with knee-high compression stockings (manufacturer-stated 25 mmHg at ankle) and once without. The intervention involved wearing CS during rest, running, and a post-run recovery period. No dose-response comparisons for compression levels were conducted, only with/without CS comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in post-running early serum creatine kinase concentration was observed between using CS and not using CS. The 	 change in median serum CK concentration (n = 13) was 0.7 (	17.6 to 6.0) 		kat/L with CS and 0.6 (	9.3 to 6.0) 		kat/L without CS. Normal reference intervals for serum CK are 0.6	3.5 		kat/L in women and 0.6	6.7 		kat/L in men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme primarily found in muscle cells; elevated levels in blood indicate muscle damage or injury. Levels can be elevated for up to 48 hours post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured directly after a 10-km treadmill run, comparing conditions with and without exercise compression stockings.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of significant change suggests no observable early exercise-induced muscle damage as measured by this biomarker under the given conditions, indicating CS did not reduce levels compared to without CS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No differences observed between groups following 12 weeks of supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme primarily found in muscle cells; elevated levels typically indicate muscle damage or strenuous exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed before and after the 12-week supplementation period of daily protein combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of muscle damage or breakdown; no change suggests the exercise protocol did not induce significant muscle damage, or protein did not modulate it differently between groups.

biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significant seasonal changes, characterized by a significant decrease in activity.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant changes observed for the whole group (n=24) over the one-year training cycle, with significant decreases in activity from T1-T2 (-160.9 U/L) and T3-T4 (-292.7 U/L). A significant (p < 0.001) time interaction showed a more dynamic drop in the supplemented group (GS, -374.0 U/L) than in the placebo group (GP, -223.9 U/L) between T3 and T4.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme crucial for muscle energy storage and production, released into blood upon muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training cycle in young soccer players, during competitive and pre-season periods, reflecting muscle adaptation to training loads, influenced by vitamin D supplementation and endogenous synthesis during spring and summer.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary and strong indicator of muscle damage and recovery status from physical exertion. Lower concentrations suggest muscle adaptation to training loads, while a more dynamic drop in the supplemented group suggests a positive effect of supplementation in combination with endogenous vitamin D synthesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled study investigated the acute effects of collagen hydrolysate (CH) and dairy protein (DP) supplementation on recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) induced by 30 minutes of downhill running in recreationally active males. The study found that while downhill running significantly increased muscle damage (Creatine Kinase) and inflammation markers (Interleukin-6, High-sensitivity C-reactive protein), along with muscle soreness and reduced muscle function, neither post-exercise consumption of 25g CH nor DP for three days significantly improved these indices of EIMD compared to an isoenergetic placebo during the acute recovery period.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional supplementation (Collagen Hydrolysate, Dairy Protein) and Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage (Downhill Running)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Muscle damage was induced by 30 minutes of downhill running on a -15% slope at 80% of VO2max speed. Participants consumed either 25 g of collagen hydrolysate protein, 25 g of dairy protein, or an isoenergetic placebo. Each serving was consumed two hours before the pre-exercise measures and then at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-downhill run measures. The supplements were isoenergetic and flavour-matched. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either the exercise or the nutritional supplements. It was suggested that a longer CH supplementation duration (e.g., 9 days prior to exercise) might be necessary for beneficial effects, contrasting with the acute post-exercise use in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Significantly higher due to exercise-induced muscle damage (time effects, p 

#x2264; 0.001, ηp2 = 0.531). Levels peaked at 24 hours post-exercise for all groups, before returning towards baseline at 72 hours. No significant group or interaction effects were observed with collagen hydrolysate or dairy protein supplementation (all p > 0.05) compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism of muscle; its release into blood indicates cellular damage, primarily used as a biomarker for muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) from 30 minutes of downhill running.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage and integrity after strenuous exercise, with elevated levels associated with reduced performance and disruption of daily activities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and evaluated a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol in collegiate athletes, demonstrating that it significantly enhances the recovery of cardiovascular and biochemical biomarkers (heart rate, lactic acid, and creatine kinase) compared to regular training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 4-week intervention included a Taekwondo-specific HIIT protocol compared to a control group receiving regular Taekwondo training. The HIIT was structured in two phases: Weeks 1-2 involved six rounds of four kicking techniques (21s work, 12s rest, 1.75:1 WRR) at 85% HRmax; Weeks 3-4 increased to eight rounds of the same techniques (24s work, 8s rest, 3:1 WRR) at 90% HRmax. Both phases included 1-minute rest between rounds. The control group performed regular Taekwondo training (90 min/session, 5 times/week) at 70-80% HRmax. Significant differences were observed between the groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant (p ">= 0.05) post-intervention reductions and faster recovery were observed in the HIIT group compared to the control group. The HIIT group showed significant changes at E5 and E24 within the group, and significant differences at PostE5 and PostE24 between groups, indicating rapid CK recovery. Detection range for CK was 10-2000 U/L, with a coefficient of variation ">= 1.5%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in cellular energy metabolism, released into the bloodstream upon muscle damage and sarcolemmal injury, serving as a biomarker for muscle damage and fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery during and after a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved muscle recovery capacity, suggesting reduced muscle damage and faster repair, which contributes to better force production and physical performance, though CK is an indirect and variable marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of varying intensities of a single session of aerobic exercise on serum markers of lipid peroxidation (MDA) and muscle damage (CK) in sedentary males, concluding that moderate to high-intensity exercise significantly increases MDA and CK levels, while low-intensity exercise is suggested for adaptation and damage prevention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Single-session aerobic exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed 20 minutes of aerobic treadmill running at low (40% VO2 max), moderate (60% VO2 max), or high (80% VO2 max) intensities. Intensity levels significantly affected both MDA (P=0.001) and CK (P=0.003) post-test, with increasing intensity leading to increased amounts of both markers. Specifically, MDA levels significantly differed between control and all intensity levels, but not among the intensity levels themselves. CK levels significantly differed between control and moderate/high intensity levels, but not between control and low intensity, and no significant differences were observed among the intensity levels themselves.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly affected by aerobic exercise intensity [F(3, 45) = 5.455, P = 0.003] post-test. Amounts increased with increasing intensity. Significant differences were found between the control group (M = 101.60, SD = 43.71 U/L) and participants in the moderate and high intensity levels, but not between control and low intensity. The highest amount was measured in the high intensity level (M = 216.38, SD = 85.62 U/L), though no significant difference was found among the intensity levels themselves.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Muscle enzyme that leaks into circulation, serving as an indicator of muscle damage due to disruption of cell membrane integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-test after a single session of aerobic exercise with varying intensities (low, moderate, high) in sedentary males.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage, with elevated serum levels associated with disruption of sarcomeric Z-disk and leakage from muscle cells, particularly after moderate to high-intensity aerobic exercise. Low intensity is recommended for prevention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No changes in the values of selected immune system parameters: muscle enzymes: creatine kinase (CK) were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme primarily found in muscle, whose elevated levels in blood indicate muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Italian national rugby team members (n=10) after cryotherapy (5 sessions/week, once a day, -110°C/2 min).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant muscle damage or recovery effect was detected by this cryotherapy protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A carbohydrate/protein drink, which was rich in BCAAs, did not have an effect on creatine kinase levels; a leucine/carbohydrate beverage did not affect serum creatine kinase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme primarily found in muscle cells, elevated levels in blood are a common marker for muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following eccentric quadriceps contractions or 6 sets of heavy back squats.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage; no effect of BCAA-CHO suggests muscle fibers were damaged irrespective of supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-weeks of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) pre-loading on markers of inflammation (hsCRP, IL-6), muscle damage (CK), perceived muscle soreness, tissue tenderness, and lower limb performance (squat jump peak power, hamstring flexibility) in endurance-trained female runners after a single bout of downhill running (DHR). MIPS consumption attenuated inflammation (hsCRP) three days post-DHR but did not significantly impact perceived soreness, muscle damage markers, or other performance measures.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS, NO-Shotgun®) and eccentric exercise (Downhill Running, DHR).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) was consumed daily for 28 days (4 weeks) prior to a single bout of DHR, and 30 minutes before post-testing. One serving of MIPS was 21g. A control group received an isocaloric (28g maltodextrin) placebo. The DHR protocol involved a 60-minute run at a -10% gradient, at 75% VO2max (average speed 12.03  ± 0.4 km/hr). No dose-response comparisons for either the supplement or DHR protocol were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed main effects of time (p = 0.05), with a significant increase from baseline to immediately post-DHR (p=0.02) and peak increases at 24 h post-DHR. MIPS consumption did not significantly affect CK levels compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme released from damaged muscle cells, widely used as an indicator of muscle injury and cellular integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage and the recovery status following strenuous eccentric exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), inflammatory indices, hematological markers, and performance decline in soccer players following a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). The LIST protocol induced transient changes in immune cells, inflammatory markers, and declines in performance. BC supplementation demonstrated potential in mitigating some EIMD, improving recovery of muscle power (SQJ), and attenuating post-exercise increases in inflammatory markers (CRP, CK, IL-6) compared to pre-supplementation and/or whey protein, suggesting better maintenance of performance and reduced post-exercise EIMD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Bovine Colostrum (BC) and Whey Protein (WP) supplementation in conjunction with a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A low-dose of 3.2 g/day of either bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) was administered for 6 weeks to soccer players. This consisted of 8 capsules x 400 mg per capsule. The LIST protocol was performed pre- and post-supplementation. No dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported, as only one dose was used; however, comparisons were made between pre- and post-supplementation responses, and directly between the BC and WP groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (3- to 4-fold increase, peaked at 24-48h) after LIST. BC supplementation resulted in a faster recovery compared to pre-supplementation kinetics (trial × time: p = 0.056) and a trend for lower iAUC in the BC group compared to WP [WP: 18,785 (4651–41,357) U h/L, BC: 8842 (4807–14,802) U h/L, p = 0.081]. Lower elevations were statistically significant 24h after LIST in the BC group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme released from damaged muscle cells into circulation, serving as a primary indicator of muscle cell damage and integrity loss.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitored for 72 hours post-Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) to assess exercise-induced muscle damage and the effects of 6-week low-dose bovine colostrum supplementation, comparing pre- and post-supplementation and against whey protein.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a primary indicator of exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD). Lower levels or faster recovery suggest reduced muscle damage and potential mitigation of EIMD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the protective effects of 5-minute non-damaging downhill walking (DW) or level walking (LW) preconditioning against muscle damage induced by a subsequent 40-minute DW in healthy young men. The key finding was that 5-minute preconditioning DW significantly attenuated markers of muscle damage, including maximal knee extension strength reduction, plasma creatine kinase activity, and muscle soreness, following the 40-minute damaging DW, suggesting its utility for preparing for strenuous activities like trekking.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Preconditioning Downhill Walking (DW) and Level Walking (LW) exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Untrained young men were allocated to control, 5-min preconditioning Downhill Walking (PRE-DW), or 5-min preconditioning Level Walking (PRE-LW) groups (n=12/group). PRE-DW and PRE-LW performed their respective 5-min bouts (treadmill, 5 km/h, 10% body mass load; DW at -28% slope) one week prior to the main exercise. The main exercise for all groups was 40-min Downhill Walking (treadmill, -28% slope, 5 km/h, 10% body mass load). The 5-min preconditioning bouts induced no significant changes in measured variables. The 5-min preconditioning DW significantly attenuated muscle damage (47-64%) from the 40-min DW, while 5-min LW did not provide a protective effect. No explicit dose-response comparisons were performed for different preconditioning durations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes were observed after 5-min DW or 5-min LW preconditioning. After 40-min DW, control group showed peak CK of 635.5  1 306.0 U/L (P<0.05) and PRE-LW group showed peak CK of 639.6  1 405.4 U/L (P<0.05), remaining elevated for 72h. Normal reference range is 24-195 U/L. The PRE-DW group showed an attenuated peak CK of 339.3  1 148.4 U/L (P<0.05 compared to control/PRE-LW), representing a 47-64% smaller magnitude of change in peak values compared to the control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy metabolism within muscle cells; its leakage into plasma indicates muscle cell membrane damage and injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured before and after 5-min preconditioning (Downhill Walking or Level Walking) and before/24/48/72 h after 40-min damaging Downhill Walking.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated plasma CK activity is a primary indicator of muscle cell membrane damage, associated with delayed onset muscle soreness and prolonged recovery. Attenuated increases signify a protective effect against extensive muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: dynamic responses, peak at 24h for SE/MH, peak at 0h for MS
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peak values observed after 24 h recovery (p < 0.05) for Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) protocols, and 0 h post-exercise (p < 0.05) for Maximum Strength (MS) protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme and conventional marker of muscle damage and integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Resistance Training, specifically Muscular Strength Endurance (SE), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH), and Maximum Strength (MS) protocols.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for monitoring training responses, neuromuscular adaptations, and recovery phases, indicating muscle damage or breakdown induced by exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase (p<0.05) after each bout of exhaustive exercise, without normalization during the 72-hour resting period. Baseline values before bouts showed a significant upward trend (162±63 U/L before 1st bout vs 301±131 U/L before 3rd bout, p<0.05). Percentage increment was always many times lower than cf n-DNA.
