document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: After 1-month of treatment, there was no significant difference in Cr levels between the high-effective Δhs-CRP (%) group (81.50 ± 35.20 μmol/L) and the low-effective group (80.85 ± 26.23 μmol/L, p = 0.871).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product of creatine metabolism by muscles, filtered by the kidneys and excreted in urine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Statin-based lipid-lowering strategies after 1-month of treatment in patients post-PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as a marker of kidney function; stable levels suggest healthy renal function or no adverse renal effects from the treatments in this patient cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Determined by Jaffe reaction method and used to standardize urine spot samples, ensuring all urinary parameters were adjusted for dilution.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, excreted at a relatively constant rate; commonly used to adjust for urine dilution in spot samples.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used for standardizing urinary biomarker measurements in environmental cadmium exposure studies.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Essential for accurate assessment of other urinary kidney function markers by accounting for urine dilution variability.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In 2006, serum creatinine concentration was significantly higher in the highly polluted area compared to other areas (p < 0.01). Serum creatinine data was only available for 2006.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, used as an indicator of kidney function; elevated levels suggest impaired renal clearance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-cessation of cadmium exposure (8-year follow-up) for assessing overall renal function.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates kidney function; higher levels suggest potential kidney impairment, especially in highly polluted areas, serving as a crucial indicator for diagnosing chronic kidney disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased 19% over pre-run values in placebo during recovery, and 6% in tart cherry group. Significant attenuations over time (p=0.047) and group differences (p=0.007), with significantly attenuated serum creatinine 60-min post-run in tart cherry group compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of kidney function and muscle breakdown/catabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Short-term powdered tart cherry supplementation surrounding a half-marathon run and 48-h recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced muscle catabolism and potentially better muscle preservation following endurance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase after each bout of exhaustive exercise. Baseline values did not differ between bouts. Post-exercise plasma concentrations increased, but percentage increment was always many times lower than cf n-DNA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism; elevated levels can indicate muscle breakdown or altered renal function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After each of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can indicate muscle damage, metabolic stress, and renal system exertion resulting from strenuous exercise, with increases possibly due to lower clearance during strenuous exercise and/or exercise-induced catabolism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study found that while bone turnover markers (CTX and BAP) decreased in both K citrate and placebo groups, K citrate significantly enhanced these beneficial effects, particularly in a subgroup of patients with pre-existing low-grade acidosis (low urine pH and/or low potassium and citrate excretion). K citrate also improved urinary pH, citrate, and potassium excretion. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Potassium Citrate (K citrate) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Daily oral supplementation with 30 mEq of K citrate (in two tablets) for 6 months. This was administered in addition to daily calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹) for all subjects (K citrate and placebo groups). The K citrate treatment showed significant benefits in subjects with evidence of low-grade acidosis (low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH) compared to the placebo, with significant changes observed as early as 3 months. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported, and adherence rates were approximately 90% for both groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product of muscle metabolism, serves as an indicator of kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: K citrate supplementation in postmenopausal women with osteopenia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of renal function.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Low daily excretion (baseline).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product; often used to normalize the excretion rates of other urine analytes due to its relatively constant excretion. Nutritional marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: K citrate supplementation in postmenopausal women with osteopenia. Assessment of dietary acid load in osteopenic women reporting low/moderate animal protein and abundant plant food consumption.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as a reference for excretion rates of other urine analytes; indicator of kidney function. Low excretion proved scarce dietary acid load.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between routine plasma biomarker levels and recovery efficiency in elite professional soccer players over an entire eleven-month competitive match season, including seasonal variations and differences based on player position and cumulative match time. It concluded that a panel of AST, CK, LDH, and creatinine can effectively monitor recovery, adaptation, and overtraining risk, particularly in active positions like midfielders who may also be prone to iron and magnesium deficiencies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competitive professional soccer matches and regular intense training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An eleven-month competitive season, comprising 44 league and cup matches (23 autumn, 21 spring), typically one to two matches per week. Fasting capillary blood samples were collected 17-24 hours after each match. The study compared player positions (midfielder/defender vs. goalie/substitute, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups), noting significant differences in cumulative match time and physical demands. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for training intensity, but adaptation to increasing training load was observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, increased over time, and varied by group/season
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally higher in midfielder/defender groups compared to goalie/substitute groups, particularly in midfielders, with concentration increasing significantly over time during the season (e.g., in midfielder/defender group, goalie/substitute autumn round, midfielders spring round). It showed a slight but significant positive correlation with cumulative match-time in midfielder/defender groups (R=0.24-0.25, P<=0.05) and goalies/substitutes (R=0.26, P<=0.05), and a stronger positive correlation in midfielders (R=0.17-0.41, P<=0.05). However, a negative correlation was observed in defenders (R=-0.28, P<=0.05) with cumulative game time.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product of muscle metabolism and creatine breakdown, indicating muscle mass, kidney function, and general health status. It is involved in water-electrolyte balance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout an eleven-month professional competitive soccer match season, including post-match recovery (17-24 hours post-match), regular intense training, and competition. Comparisons were made between midfielder/defender and goalie/substitute groups, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups, considering cumulative game time and seasonal variations (autumn vs. spring rounds).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful biomarker for monitoring recovery periods and efficiency, reflecting muscle mass, creatine turnover, and kidney stress from intense physical activity. It indicates dynamic changes in muscle metabolism and hydration status over the season, suggesting adaptation or increased demands depending on player position and game time. Its lower interindividual variability makes it a good indicator for assessing recovery, adaptation, and reducing overtraining risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific plasma microRNAs (miR-34a, miR-224, miR-452) and Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) in women with diabetes and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction (LVDD) or Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF), including cohorts with impaired renal function or a history of preeclampsia. The study found distinct patterns of miR expression and Ang-2 levels associated with microvascular injury in these conditions, highlighting their relevance, particularly in women. Methodologies included echocardiography, standard blood testing, RNA isolation for microRNA profiling, and ELISA for specific plasma proteins.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study, diagnostic assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on diagnostic assessment and biomarker identification for naturally occurring cardiovascular conditions (LVDD and HFpEF) in the context of diabetes. No therapeutic interventions or dose administrations were performed or compared; the study examined existing biomarker levels in patient cohorts.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Levels measured, but direction of change relative to activity not reported.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not quantified for change in this context.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker for kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used in the calculation of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) for cardiovascular risk assessment in patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used to assess kidney function, a key indicator for cardiovascular health and risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between iron status and renal outcomes, specifically progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), in 111 pre-dialysis patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven Diabetic Nephropathy (DN). It found that reduced serum transferrin is an independent predictor of ESRD, and identified increased iron and transferrin deposition in renal tubular epithelial cells of DN patients, suggesting a pathological role for altered iron metabolism in disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the prognostic value of iron status and related biomarkers in Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. Serum markers were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, immunoradiometric assay, and colorimetric methods. Additionally, histological analysis involved immunohistochemical staining for transferrin and Perl's blue staining for iron in kidney biopsy specimens from DN patients and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or active treatments were investigated; the study focused on correlation and predictive value.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher baseline levels in ESRD patients compared to non-ESRD patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in T2DM patients with Diabetic Nephropathy (DN).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher baseline levels are associated with increased risk of progression to ESRD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multi-country feasibility study, part of the ISN 0by25 trial, investigated the implementation of a comprehensive program for recognizing and managing community-acquired acute kidney injury (AKI) and acute kidney disease (AKD) in low-resource settings (Bolivia, Nepal, Malawi). The program combined point-of-care (POC) serum creatinine and urine dipstick testing with an education and training program for healthcare providers and teleconsultations with referral hospital physicians. The study demonstrated the feasibility of this approach in improving early identification and management of kidney disease in high-risk primary care patients, leading to reduced hospitalization rates and influencing management, despite high baseline rates of kidney dysfunction and mortality. The intervention facilitated the identification of more AKI patients, including more severe cases, compared to an observation phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A comprehensive intervention program combining healthcare provider education and training, point-of-care (POC) serum creatinine and urine dipstick testing, mobile digital technology-enabled teleconsultations, and fluid therapy for the recognition and management of Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The program was structured in a 4-month observation phase, a 2-month training phase, and a 6-month intervention phase. Healthcare providers and physicians in community health centers received training on AKI risk assessment, recognition, POC test use (serum creatinine and urine dipstick), interpretation, and management protocols, including the STOP AKI protocol, with real-time guidance via teleconsultation from referral hospital physicians. POC testing for serum creatinine was performed at enrollment and re-measured at 7 days, 1, 3, and 6 months follow-up, along with urine dipstick tests for proteinuria. During the intervention phase, patients received more fluids (both oral and intravenous; 75% received fluid therapy) compared to the observation phase, leading to reduced hospitalization (59% vs 49%, p<0.001). No specific quantitative doses for fluids or detailed dose-response comparisons for the educational intervention or testing frequency were reported, as the study focused on feasibility.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Used diagnostically for AKI definition: increase by >=26.5 µmol/l within 48 hours, or increase to >1.5 times baseline within 7 days. For AKI recovery: complete (returned to or below enrollment value) or partial (lower than peak but higher than enrollment). At 1 month, serum creatinine was lower than at enrollment in 84% (336/402) of AKI patients (no history of CKD) and 85.5% (241/282) of AKD patients. Over 66% of patients had kidney abnormalities based on initial POC test, and over 40% of AKI patients showed a decline, suggesting resolving AKI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product of muscle metabolism; a key indicator of glomerular filtration rate, kidney function, and potential damage or recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis, risk assessment, recognition, management, and monitoring of community-acquired Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), Acute Kidney Disease (AKD), and Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) in primary healthcare settings within low-resource countries (Bolivia, Nepal, Malawi), including assessment of recovery and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary diagnostic marker for AKI, AKD, and CKD, indicating impaired kidney function, damage, or recovery. Elevated levels predict higher risk for AKI, CKD progression, hospitalization, and mortality. Declining levels can indicate resolving AKI or kidney impairment of unknown chronicity (AKD).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated alterations in serum levels of tumor, cardiac, liver, and renal function markers, alongside the IL-18 rs1946518 polymorphism, in patients with breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers (BC, CRC, PCa), and myocardial infarction (MI), compared to healthy controls. It revealed significantly elevated tumor markers (CA 15-3, CA 19-9, CEA, TPSA) in cancer patients, which serve as efficient early detection biomarkers. Cardiac markers (hs-cTnT, CK-MB) were specific to MI and largely unchanged in cancer. Liver and renal markers (ALP, AST, ALT, urea, creatinine) showed varied elevations, particularly in CRC and PCa, suggesting their utility as alternative diagnostic indicators. The IL-18 -607 C/A polymorphism was identified as a risk factor for PCa (AA genotype and A allele), and also showed an Odds Ratio of 1.75 for BC, while A/C heterozygotes were linked to increased CRC risk and C allele homozygotes offered protection against CRC.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker and Genetic Polymorphism Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study focused on assessing diagnostic biomarker levels and genetic polymorphisms in various patient groups and healthy controls, without any therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Unchanged in Breast Cancer (BC) patients compared to healthy individuals. AUC value of 0.7 for detecting PCa.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Renal function marker, waste product of muscle metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Breast Cancer (BC) and Prostate Cancer (PCa) patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Good indicator for detecting PCa. Unchanged in BC patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of CDH1, CDH2, MCP-1, and PAI-1 mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles (EVs) for predicting early-stage diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main findings indicate that CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression in blood EVs was significantly downregulated with the development of DN (overt and incipient stages) compared to diabetic patients without DN, suggesting a renoprotective effect and their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. These mRNAs inversely correlated with markers of kidney damage like creatinine and albuminuria. In contrast, CDH1 mRNA showed no significant change across groups, and while PAI-1 mRNA decreased in some diabetic groups, its diagnostic utility for early DN was not clearly established, according to the authors' results. The study also explored the expression of these and other related biomarkers in urine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 196 participants (35 overt DN, 53 incipient DN, 62 DM, and 46 healthy controls) with type 2 diabetes. The study focused on characterizing mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles and other clinical markers across different stages of diabetic nephropathy and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CDH2 mRNA level inversely correlated with creatinine (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.370, p < 0.001). MCP-1 mRNA had negative correlations with creatinine (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.361, p < 0.001). Incipient DN group had higher concentration than DM group (p = 0.001), but no significant difference compared to control (p = 0.151). CDH2 mRNA expression level could be estimated from creatinine (unstandardized coefficient = -2.673, p < 0.001). MCP-1 mRNA expression level could be estimated from creatinine level (unstandardized coefficient = -3.024, p = 0.010).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function. Elevated levels suggest impaired kidney function, and are inversely correlated with potential renoprotective markers.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic Nephropathy / Diabetic Mellitus.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Inversely correlated with CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA levels, reflecting kidney function and severity of renal injury. Acts as a predictor of CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product produced from muscle metabolism; indicator of kidney function
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes and potential kidney dysfunction

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single bout of moderate-intensity continuous exercise, specifically at lactate threshold (LT) intensity, on renal hemodynamics and kidney injury biomarkers in middle-aged men. The main findings indicate that this type of exercise effectively maintains renal blood flow (RBF), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and filtration fraction (FF), and crucially, does not induce renal injury based on biomarker analysis. However, transient changes were noted in renal cross-sectional area and resistance indices, along with an increase in plasma noradrenaline in the recovery phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of 30 minutes of aerobic exercise was performed using a cycle ergometer, precisely at lactate threshold (LT) intensity (corresponding to 36% VO2max). The study involved middle-aged men (38 	 8 years) with well-maintained renal function (eGFR 	 60 ml/min/1.73m2). Renal hemodynamics and biomarker levels were evaluated at rest, immediately after exercise, and during 30-minute and 60-minute recovery phases. Participants were allowed free hydration during and after the experiment. No dose-response comparisons or chronic effects were investigated in this acute study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes in serum creatinine level at any point.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product from muscle metabolism, excreted by the kidneys; its concentration is commonly used to estimate kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate impaired kidney function or potential kidney injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not specified in this chunk

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not specified in this chunk
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CrossFit workout and Tribulus Terrestris supplementation
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not specified in this chunk

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Moderate effects on modulating creatinine; non-significant decreases (p > 0.05) in some studies, but significant decreases (p < 0.05) were reported in others (e.g., with 6 mg single-dose after exercise).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product from muscle metabolism, primarily used as an indicator of kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation in highly trained athletes for renoprotection against intense exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary indicator of kidney function and muscle metabolic status; modulated levels may reflect changes in muscle turnover or renal processing, improving kidney function and demonstrating cytoprotective properties.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma, Serum (Fluid from clinical laboratory test)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly different between SBMA and controls (P_adj < 0.05). Decreased abundance in plasma and significantly correlated with higher thigh MRI muscle fat fraction (MFF). Showed correlations with SBMA muscle MRI and the SBMAFRS.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product from muscle metabolism; typically indicates kidney function but also influenced by muscle mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Existing fluid biomarker used in SBMA clinical studies. Assessed in adult male patients with SBMA compared to age-matched healthy controls (NIH cohort).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle atrophy and fat infiltration in SBMA, correlating with disease severity, muscle MRI findings, and functional assessments (SBMAFRS).

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the work-recovery cycle and temporal variation of kidney strain, muscle injury, hydration, and inflammation biomarkers in 20 male sugarcane workers exposed to repeat heat stress and strenuous manual labor, despite a workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. It assessed biomarker dynamics across work shifts and different recovery periods (18h vs 42h post-shift). The study found marked cross-shift kidney and muscle strain, alongside an accumulation of systemic inflammation over the work week, with recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers being similar for both recovery durations. The findings highlight the importance of biomonitoring for occupational populations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study investigated the impact of occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor, specifically sugarcane cutting, on worker health, with an applied workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. This intervention included a maximum six-hour workday, hourly mandated rest breaks in the shade, easy access to cool water, and electrolyte solutions (300 mL bolis/bags containing sugar, sodium chloride, and potassium phosphate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 20 male sugarcane workers were observed over 4 days, covering work shifts and recovery periods (18h and 42h post-shift). Workload intensity ranged from 55-58%HR max, with daily average Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) between 26-29 °C, which was considered cooler than normal for a harvest period. Workers consumed approximately 8 L of water and four 300 mL electrolyte bags daily. Work shifts averaged around 5 hours, with Monday shifts showing higher workload intensity and heat stress. Recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers were found to be similar between 18 hours and 42 hours of rest (p > 0.27), indicating no significant difference in recovery duration comparison within this timeframe.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01). Cross-shift changes were similar to previously reported values, showing worsening pre-shift levels over a work week. Changes were similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, filtered and excreted by the kidneys; used as a marker for kidney glomerular filtration and function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting) in a weekly work-rest cycle, despite RSH intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates daily kidney strain, recovery capacity, and can reflect hydration status or muscle breakdown. Worsening pre-shift levels suggest a decline in kidney function and can forecast end-of-harvest kidney function. Biomonitoring is advised before a work shift.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Differing levels (lower in urine, higher in unspecified fluid) observed in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls. Lower levels in urine associated with negative outcome/poor prognosis. Identified as a key discriminating molecule.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product of muscle metabolism, indicator of kidney function and muscle mass; general metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls, and prognosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for COVID-19 infection, differentiating patients from controls, and associated with sarcopenia and negative prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant alterations, direction not explicitly stated but linked to muscle damage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Linked to exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise-induced muscle damage, training load changes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Quantifies biochemical responses to training load changes; reflects measurable physiological strain and muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased, then returned toward pre-exercise values
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased acutely after matches (17-35% increases), with a quick return to pre-exercise values during short recovery sessions, mirroring hematocrit kinetics.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product from muscle metabolism, reflects kidney function and muscle turnover
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match), acute exercise, short recovery sessions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute physiological stress from exercise and renal perfusion during exercise, showing observed differences not solely due to volemia changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product generated from muscle metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CD constituents in animal studies, potentially associated with delaying the onset of exercise-induced fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction may suggest improved metabolic efficiency or reduced muscle breakdown, contributing to delayed fatigue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased significantly in both sexes; consistently higher in males
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels increased significantly from baseline to 30 months in both sexes (females: p=0.009; males: p=0.001). Males consistently exhibited higher baseline values and higher levels throughout the study (p < 0.001). Age correlated positively with creatinine levels in both males and females (p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product from muscle metabolism, used as an indicator of kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates renal function, suggesting subtle sex-based differences in renal adaptation post-infection/vaccination. Consistent with known sex-based physiological differences (muscle mass, glomerular filtration dynamics), with higher baseline in males reflecting pronounced acute physiological burden and earlier alterations in renal parameters.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated sex differences in biomarkers of end-organ damage (Creatinine (CR), estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Creatine Kinase (CK), Alanine-Transaminase (ALT), and Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST)) and their time course following exertional heat stroke (EHS) in 62 active-duty service members. Findings indicate that women exhibited significantly lower peak values for kidney (CR) and muscle (CK) damage biomarkers compared to men, with ALT and AST also being similar or lower in women during recovery, suggesting women may be less susceptible to organ injury from EHS despite similar recorded core temperatures or potential higher actual peak temperatures due to pre-measurement cooling.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exertional Heat Stroke (EHS) and subsequent active cooling interventions
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on Exertional Heat Stroke (EHS) events where individuals received active cooling interventions (ice sheets, cold-water immersion, chilled saline) prehospital and en route to the emergency department. While recorded peak body core temperatures were similar between sexes (women: 41.11°C (40.06, 41.67); men: 41.11°C (40.28, 41.72), P = 0.57), active cooling was initiated prior to temperature recording more frequently in women (91%) than men (57%), suggesting actual peak temperatures might have been higher for women. No specific dose-response comparisons for EHS severity or cooling interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Women had significantly lower peak CR (1.39 mg·dL−1) compared to men (1.75 mg·dL−1, P < 0.01). Women also showed significantly lower creatinine for time bins 1-5 (P < 0.05), and men exhibited greater mean difference from the upper limit and higher absolute and relative increases following EHS.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolic waste product and indicator of kidney function, filtered by the kidneys.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exertional heat stroke (EHS) in otherwise healthy humans (military personnel) during acute phase and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severity of kidney and potential muscle damage; lower levels in women suggest less severe organ injury and may contribute to shorter hospitalization after EHS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between serum S100B protein levels and disease severity in hospitalized Covid-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infected) patients. It revealed that increased S100B serum concentrations significantly correlate with Covid-19 disease severity, intensity of care, inflammatory processes, and several inflammatory and organ damage markers, suggesting S100B as a novel biomarker for monitoring disease course and prognosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on the progression of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Covid-19) in hospitalized patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received standard care following WHO guidelines. Disease severity was quantified using a Covid-score and categorization into High Intensity Care (HIC) or Low Intensity Care (LIC) wards. No specific intervention doses or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant correlation observed with S100B levels (p < 0.01) in the subgroup of patients with high levels of ALT (> 40 IU/L, n = 19).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Organ damage marker (implied as kidney damage).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: SARS-CoV-2 infection (Covid-19 patients), specifically in the subgroup with high ALT levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a possible independent association with liver and/or kidney damage, contributing to Covid-19 severity assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased in recovery; fluctuated with training load
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A decrease in recovery concentration was observed in all groups. Generally a fairly stable variable dependent on sex, but fluctuations are commonly related to training load, aerobic/anaerobic metabolism, competition length, and competitive season stage. Correlation with CK activity was found in male swimmers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product from muscle metabolism, primarily filtered by the kidneys, and a marker of kidney function, used for monitoring recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring athletes' recovery periods, particularly during a 10-week preparatory training stage in professional long-distance and sprint swimmers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates training load, aerobic/anaerobic metabolism, competition length, and stage of competitive season. Convergent with CK in determining skeletal muscle microdamages and energy costs. Useful for monitoring recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Significant increases after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.66). Increased after PS phase or intense soccer exercises.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolic waste product of muscle metabolism; indicator of muscle breakdown and kidney function; associated with training intensity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after intense physical exertion (PS phase) or intense soccer exercises.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with greater match and training intensities; suggests increased muscle turnover or breakdown following physical stress; indicates physiological response to intense exercise and adaptative changes in the whole organism and metabolism, informing optimal management of stimulus/recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased ~10-11% in blood in response to the CCombat protocol, returning to basal levels within 24 hours. The increase was at the same ratio as albumin in response to exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolite of creatine, serving as an indicator of renal filtration and glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol induced metabolic stress, impacting renal filtration; observed at the end of exercise and during recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impairment or reduction of renal filtration (GFR) due to intensive exercise, though interpretation can be complex due to muscle damage effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in both nicorandil and conventional treatment groups (P < 0.05); significantly more decreased in the nicorandil group compared to conventional treatment (P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Traditional indicator of renal function and glomerular filtration rate.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nicorandil treatment for Type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects improved renal function in Type I CRS patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective study analyzed 4054 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to investigate the association of preoperative red blood cell distribution width (RDW) and hemoglobin-to-RDW ratio (HRR) with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). The findings demonstrated that elevated RDW and decreased HRR were robustly and independently associated with a higher risk of CA-AKI, suggesting their utility for early risk identification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Coronary Angiography (CAG) or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) involving contrast media administration.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study retrospectively analyzed 4054 patients undergoing CAG or PCI. Patients received contrast media as part of standard clinical practice. Excessive contrast media was defined as exceeding a calculated maximum dose (5 mL × weight (kg)/Scr at baseline (mg/dL)). However, no dose-response comparisons for RDW or HRR associations with varying contrast media doses or procedural specifics were reported in relation to CA-AKI risk.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased (with higher RDW); Decreased (with higher HRR)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased proportionally with RDW (multivariable β = 2.496, 95% CI = 1.784–3.208, p < 0.001). Decreased with increasing HRR (multivariable β = -3.559, 95% CI = -4.243 to -2.875, p < 0.001). Defined as an increase in Scr levels >0.5 mg/dL (44.2 μmol/L) or an increase in Scr ratio >25% post-procedure.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function; its elevation signifies acute kidney injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following Coronary Angiography (CAG) or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI), used as a diagnostic criterion for Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CA-AKI).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary diagnostic criterion for CA-AKI.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study protocol investigates the effects of early spironolactone therapy on exercise capacity, clinical worsening, and vascular inflammation in 70 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without right ventricular failure. It aims to assess changes in functional performance (6-minute walk distance, VO2 max), plasma markers of vascular inflammation, gene expression profiles in PBMCs and PAECs, neurohormonal axis activation (sympathetic nervous system, RAAS, sex hormone metabolism), and right ventricular structure and function using advanced imaging techniques, while also monitoring for safety biomarkers like serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Spironolactone therapy (Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Early treatment with spironolactone will be administered for 24 weeks in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial. The initial dose is 25 mg once daily, escalating to 50 mg daily after week 6 if serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine does not increase >50% from baseline. Dose adjustments and discontinuation are strictly tied to safety monitoring, including stopping if serum potassium increases to 5.3-5.9 mEq/L, discontinuing if it remains ">="5.3 mEq/L on two consecutive draws or immediately if ">="6.0 mEq/L, or if serum creatinine increases >50% from baseline. No formal dose-response comparisons are reported within this protocol, although drug-drug interactions with PAH-specific therapies were considered.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Renal insufficiency defined as serum creatinine rise ">50% of baseline", leading to drug discontinuation. Will be measured one week after initiating therapy or a dose increase and then serially.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Waste product from muscle metabolism, used as an indicator of kidney function and glomerular filtration rate.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring safety and tolerability during spironolactone therapy in PAH patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates risk of renal insufficiency, a potential adverse effect of spironolactone requiring dose adjustment or discontinuation and removal from the protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in both protein and placebo groups after 12 weeks (P Time < 0.001), but no between-group differences were observed. Used for participant exclusion criteria (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m^-1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A waste product from muscle metabolism, used as a marker for kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of kidney function (inversely related to eGFR); can be influenced by changes in muscle mass or high protein intake. No adverse effect on renal function was noted.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A measure of how well the kidneys filter blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Key indicator of kidney function and chronic kidney disease.
