document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Interaction between neuronal oscillations (phase, amplitude, power modulation)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: altered, disrupted, corrected, over-activated, inhibited-activated, weakened
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Altered in neurological disorders (PD, AD); over-activated pattern before \u03b3 neuromodulation transitioned to inhibited-activated during stimulation, then remained significantly weakened post-stimulation compared to initial state.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Organizes neural activity, impacts neurotransmitter release, synaptic plasticity, brain network synchronization; regulates cognition and behavior.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neurological disorders (PD, AD); psychiatric disorders; \u03b3 neuromodulation interventions; noradrenergic, dopaminergic, and cholinergic systems modulation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Underlying mechanism for motor and cognitive deficits in neurological disorders; linked to corticostriatal function and higher-order cognitive activities in psychiatric disorders; diagnostic and therapeutic tool; alleviates cognitive and behavioral symptoms.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute response of serum sclerostin and bone turnover biomarkers (B-ALP, CTX) to a single session of whole-body vibration (WBV) exercise, both with and without blood flow restriction (BFR), in healthy untrained adult males. The findings indicated that adding BFR to WBV did not significantly affect serum sclerostin or CTX levels up to 24 hours post-exercise. However, a differential response was observed for bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (B-ALP), which was significantly lower 24 hours post-exercise in the combined WBV and BFR group compared to WBV alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Whole-body Vibration (WBV) exercise with and without Blood Flow Restriction (BFR)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two experimental conditions: (i) WBV alone, consisting of ten 1-minute bouts of whole-body vibration (30 Hz frequency, 2 mm peak-to-peak displacement, 3.6 g peak acceleration) with 30-second recovery between bouts. Participants stood barefoot in an isometric semi-squat position (130° knee angle). (ii) WBV with lower-body Blood Flow Restriction (BFR). For the WBV+BFR condition, a 13-cm-wide pneumatic cuff was applied to each thigh and inflated to 110 mmHg (estimated ~60% blood flow restriction) for the entire 1-minute duration of each vibration bout, with full deflation during the 30-second recovery intervals. No dose-response comparisons for varying WBV parameters or BFR pressure were reported within the study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significant inhibition of cutaneous reflexes

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Characterizes mechanisms associated with neurophysiological integrity and neuroplasticity in spinal networks
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 5 weeks of light-intensity upper-limb ergometry training
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Resulted in more normalized amplitudes between the paretic and non-paretic sides, suggesting restoration of imbalances and potential for improved motor function post-stroke.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Riociguat (Drug Treatment)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients with early treatment-naïve diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis were randomized to receive riociguat (n=60) or placebo (n=61) for 52 weeks. Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by 94 (78)% (from 7.22 ± 2.57 to 12.92 ± 5.24 pmol/ml) with riociguat vs. 10 (39)% (from 7.44 ± 3.34 to 7.50 ± 3.02 pmol/ml) with placebo by week 14 (P < 0.001). Elevated levels correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetic variables, but showed no clear relationship with mRSS change in the riociguat group.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pharmacodynamic engagement of riociguat with the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway, suggesting potential improvement in vascular function and antifibrotic/anti-inflammatory effects. No clear predictive value for mRSS response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly reduced by eIF3a silencing; significantly increased by eIF3a overexpression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was significantly reduced (p < .01) upon eIF3a silencing and significantly increased (p < .01) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: eIF3a silencing or overexpression in CRC cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates inhibition of cell cycle progression, contributing to suppressed cancer cell proliferation, while an increase promotes it.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Downregulated (control AdmMABs and with PW1), Maintained high (shPW1 AdmMABs), Upregulated (in absence of PW1)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Control AdmMABs downregulated cycE in DM; cycE levels remained high in the shPW1 AdmMABs. Marked decrease in cycE expression in response to PW1 (in fibroblasts). CCNE1 and CCNE2 were upregulated in the absence of PW1 (microarray). Sustained cycE expression observed in the absence of PW1. Inhibition of CyclinE-cdk2 activity by Roscovitin treatment was sufficient to rescue MyoD protein in growing shPW1 cells.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myogenic differentiation, regulation of MyoD activity, cell cycle exit. Absence of PW1 in MABs, co-transfection experiments in NIH3T3 cells, inhibition of CyclinE-cdk2 activity in shPW1 cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels indicate ongoing MyoD degradation and impaired differentiation, whereas downregulation is necessary for proper myogenesis. document_context_data.document_summary: This study evaluated and compared the regenerative potential of different blood-derived products (EDTA-PRP, Citrate-PRP, and hyperacute serum [hypACT]) in a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model over 21 days. Key assessments included metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression (SOX9, COL2AB, COL1A1, MMP3, P21), and extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and quality, using 1% or 5% concentrations of the products. HypACT consistently demonstrated superior and more stable results for cartilage-related gene expression and tissue quality. In contrast, Citrate-PRP showed negative effects on ECM production, chondrocyte presence, and gene expression, which was partly attributed to anticoagulants and extensive platelet accumulation. Metabolic activity generally showed no significant differences among the blood products compared to controls, though some variations were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-derived products: hyperacute serum (hypACT), leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with EDTA (EPRP), and leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with trisodium citrate (CPRP).

HypACT showed stable effects across both 1% and 5% concentrations. For EPRP, 1% was favored over 5% due to better glycosaminoglycan deposition and lower platelet accumulation, with concentration influencing specific gene expressions (SOX9, MMP3, COL2AB, COL1A1). CPRP at both 1% and 5% concentrations resulted in poor tissue quality and no increase in COL2AB production, with extensive platelet accumulation observed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Blood protein expression (surrogate biomarker generated by DNAmGrimAge clock)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific quantitative data reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Surrogate biomarker for blood protein expression, contributing to the DNAmGrimAge clock's predictive power.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis of epidemiological cohort data as part of DNAmGrimAge clock output.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Part of a panel of biomarkers used by the DNAmGrimAge clock to predict health and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single bout of moderate-intensity continuous exercise, specifically at lactate threshold (LT) intensity, on renal hemodynamics and kidney injury biomarkers in middle-aged men. The main findings indicate that this type of exercise effectively maintains renal blood flow (RBF), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and filtration fraction (FF), and crucially, does not induce renal injury based on biomarker analysis. However, transient changes were noted in renal cross-sectional area and resistance indices, along with an increase in plasma noradrenaline in the recovery phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of 30 minutes of aerobic exercise was performed using a cycle ergometer, precisely at lactate threshold (LT) intensity (corresponding to 36% VO2max). The study involved middle-aged men (38 	 8 years) with well-maintained renal function (eGFR 	 60 ml/min/1.73m2). Renal hemodynamics and biomarker levels were evaluated at rest, immediately after exercise, and during 30-minute and 60-minute recovery phases. Participants were allowed free hydration during and after the experiment. No dose-response comparisons or chronic effects were investigated in this acute study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes in serum cystatin C level at any point.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A protein produced by all nucleated cells, filtered by the glomeruli; used as a marker of kidney function, often considered more sensitive than creatinine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate impaired kidney function or potential kidney injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the work-recovery cycle and temporal variation of kidney strain, muscle injury, hydration, and inflammation biomarkers in 20 male sugarcane workers exposed to repeat heat stress and strenuous manual labor, despite a workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. It assessed biomarker dynamics across work shifts and different recovery periods (18h vs 42h post-shift). The study found marked cross-shift kidney and muscle strain, alongside an accumulation of systemic inflammation over the work week, with recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers being similar for both recovery durations. The findings highlight the importance of biomonitoring for occupational populations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study investigated the impact of occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor, specifically sugarcane cutting, on worker health, with an applied workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. This intervention included a maximum six-hour workday, hourly mandated rest breaks in the shade, easy access to cool water, and electrolyte solutions (300 mL bolis/bags containing sugar, sodium chloride, and potassium phosphate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 20 male sugarcane workers were observed over 4 days, covering work shifts and recovery periods (18h and 42h post-shift). Workload intensity ranged from 55-58%HR max, with daily average Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) between 26-29 °C, which was considered cooler than normal for a harvest period. Workers consumed approximately 8 L of water and four 300 mL electrolyte bags daily. Work shifts averaged around 5 hours, with Monday shifts showing higher workload intensity and heat stress. Recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers were found to be similar between 18 hours and 42 hours of rest (p > 0.27), indicating no significant difference in recovery duration comparison within this timeframe.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01). Cross-shift increases were more pronounced than creatinine, especially during Monday shifts (p = 0.02), and similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A sensitive protein marker for kidney glomerular filtration, independent of diet, muscle, and physical activity, synthesized at a constant rate.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting) in a weekly work-rest cycle, despite RSH intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates daily kidney strain and acute kidney stress. It is a valuable cross-shift and cross-harvest marker of kidney strain, particularly useful due to its independence from muscle catabolism. Biomonitoring is advised before a work shift.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant changes observed in the AD group compared with controls, measured by mass spectrometry and confirmed by ELISA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in proteinase inhibition, potentially inflammation or neuroprotection.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) group compared to controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Discriminator for AD, indicating disease-related changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in both nicorandil and conventional treatment groups (P < 0.05); significantly more decreased in the nicorandil group compared to conventional treatment (P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of renal function, particularly glomerular filtration rate.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nicorandil treatment for Type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects improved renal function in Type I CRS patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly by ~240-250% (~3.4-fold) (from 1.7  1 0.1 to 5.7  1 0.5 mg/L; p < .001; effect size = 2.4) in response to the CCombat protocol, quickly returning to basal levels within the first hour of recovery. Post-CCombat CysC negatively correlated with pre-exercise creatinine (r s -0.71), and showed both negative (r s -0.50 at 60 min) and positive (r s 0.53 at 24 h) correlations with urinary albumin (HuA).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein that reflects glomerular filtration rate (GFR), considered a sensitive biomarker of kidney function, less affected by diet or muscle mass than creatinine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol-induced metabolic stress, observed at the end of exercise and during early to long recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Sensitive indicator of kidney function changes and glomerular filtration impairment due to intensive exercise and metabolic stress; indicates transient albumin permeability and albuminuria.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific plasma microRNAs (miR-34a, miR-224, miR-452) and Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) in women with diabetes and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction (LVDD) or Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF), including cohorts with impaired renal function or a history of preeclampsia. The study found distinct patterns of miR expression and Ang-2 levels associated with microvascular injury in these conditions, highlighting their relevance, particularly in women. Methodologies included echocardiography, standard blood testing, RNA isolation for microRNA profiling, and ELISA for specific plasma proteins.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study, diagnostic assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on diagnostic assessment and biomarker identification for naturally occurring cardiovascular conditions (LVDD and HFpEF) in the context of diabetes. No therapeutic interventions or dose administrations were performed or compared; the study examined existing biomarker levels in patient cohorts.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Levels measured, but direction of change relative to activity not reported.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not quantified for change in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels highest in subphenotype 2. Precise quantification not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Implicated in renal dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort, particularly defining Subphenotype 2.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are associated with subphenotype 2, which is linked to significantly worse patient outcomes (HR 3.43 (1.76–6.69) compared to subphenotype 1).

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as an influential factor in group differentiation (VIP score between 1.04 and 1.75), contributing to the overall reduction in amino acids in the PFF group. Statistically significant differences were observed between groups at baseline, 55 days (p < 0.002), and 98 days (p < 0.002). Its inclusion in classic models (age, BMI, waist circumference, or cholesterol) significantly increased AUC from 76.7-78% to 100% (approaching significance).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Amino acid involved in protein synthesis and antioxidant defense, also playing a role in metabolic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention, differentiating metabolic profiles between groups at baseline, 55, and 98 days, and used in predictive models to assess intervention impact from baseline to day 98.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to different health statuses, influencing group differentiation, and identified as a relevant metabolite that significantly improves the predictive power of statistical models for assessing dietary intervention impact.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased upon sorafenib exposure.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Precursor of glutathione (GSH), involved in the xCT system and transsulfuration pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Upon sorafenib exposure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Likely due to upregulation of the xCT system and/or increased endogenous cysteine synthesis, contributing to antioxidant defense and ferroptosis resistance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the immediate effects of a single 20-minute Yogic Breathing (YB) session, specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam from the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, on salivary pro-inflammatory biomarkers in healthy volunteers. The study found that YB significantly reduced salivary levels of IL-1β, IL-8, and MCP-1 compared to an attention control group, with these reductions often observed at multiple time points and leading to more stable cytokine values over time.

document_context_data.document_summary: This article updates the redox theory of aging, proposing that aging results from a decline in gene-exposome interaction plasticity due to cumulative exposure memory. It emphasizes the critical role of redox networks, particularly thiol/disulfide balance (e.g., plasma cystine to glutathione ratio), as an interface between an individual and the environment, influencing health, disease etiology, and resilience. The theory links compromised redox networks to increased oxidative stress biomarkers like hydroxynonenal and reactive carbonyls, and discusses the predictive power of the plasma CySS/GSH ratio for all-cause mortality in conditions like coronary artery disease, while also exploring implications for regenerative medicine, multimorbidity, and personalized health management.

It discusses observational findings and the predictive power of naturally occurring biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated a chemically defined, serum-free protocol for the in vitro transdifferentiation of pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells into functional hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) over five days. The research examined morphological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional changes, concluding that successful transdifferentiation, facilitated by extracellular matrix proteins like fibronectin or laminin, is independent of serum.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro pancreatic progenitor cell transdifferentiation to hepatocyte-like cells
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Clonal pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells were cultured for five days in a differentiation medium containing 100 nM Dexamethasone, 10 ng/ml Oncostatin M, 20 ng/ml HGF, 20 ng/ml FGF-2, 1% ITS+ (insulin, transferrin, selenous acid), 0.2% BSA, 4.4 mM nicotinamide, 1 µM copper sulphate, 30 µg/ml ascorbic acid, and 1 µg/ml heparin. Cells were grown on uncoated plastic, laminin-coated (2 µg/cm2), or fibronectin-coated (5 µg/cm2) substrata, with or without 5% FBS supplementation. The study primarily focused on the effectiveness of serum-free conditions facilitated by ECM proteins, rather than dose-response comparisons for individual components, finding no significant difference in transdifferentiation potential between fibronectin and laminin substrata.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive study investigated alpha-synuclein (αSN) as a potential diagnostic and monitoring biomarker for Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM). It evaluated αSN immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies and its concentration in serum and muscle homogenates, comparing IBM patients to other myopathies and healthy controls. The findings suggest αSN immunoreactivity in muscle is a promising diagnostic marker, while serum αSN levels could serve as a monitoring biomarker, correlating with disease duration and clinical severity in IBM. The study also explored the diagnostic utility of other established and emerging biomarkers in IBM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational/Diagnostic Biomarker Investigation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved a multimodal assessment of alpha-synuclein (αSN) levels and immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies, muscle tissue homogenates, and serum samples from various cohorts. Muscle biopsies (N=63, including 19 IBM, 21 other inflammatory myopathies, 20 other myopathies, 3 healthy controls) were analyzed by immunohistochemical staining. Serum samples (N=156, including 11 IBM, 25 other inflammatory myopathies, 53 hereditary myopathies, 30 mitochondriopathies, 37 healthy controls) were assessed by ELISA. Muscle homogenates were also examined (N=17 IBM, N=19 other inflammatory myopathies, N=5 hereditary myopathies, N=2 healthy controls). IBM patients were stratified by disease severity (IBMFRS) and disease duration for serum αSN analysis. No interventional dose or therapeutic comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic and monitoring biomarker evaluation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. document_context_data.document_summary: This study characterized pediatric Philadelphia-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients with kinase fusions in Japan, identifying 29 such patients from a cohort of 373. These patients presented with distinct clinical features including male predominance (22/7), older mean age at onset (8.8 years), high mean white blood cell count at diagnosis (94,200/μl), and a high proportion of National Cancer Institute high-risk (NCI-HR) cases. Genetic analysis revealed various kinase fusions (ABL1, PDGFRB, JAK2, IgH-EPOR, NCOR1-LYN, CRLF2) and a high prevalence of IKZF1 deletion (16/22 patients). Kinase fusion-positive patients demonstrated inferior outcomes, including high rates of prednisolone poor response (44.8%), induction failure (12.9%), and significantly inferior 5-year event-free survival rates (48.6±9.7%) compared to fusion-negative patients, suggesting clinical similarities to Ph+ ALL and underscoring the need for advanced stratification and targeted therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy for B-Cell Precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (BCP-ALL)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients were treated under various conventional chemotherapy clinical trial protocols (e.g., JACLS-ALL02, TCCSG, CCLSG, KYCCSG studies), which included initial prednisolone (PSL) therapy. Some patients received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs like imatinib, dasatinib) are discussed as potential targeted therapies for kinase fusion-positive patients. However, specific drug doses, durations, or detailed regimens for any treatment were not provided or directly investigated within this study; the heterogeneity of protocols was noted as a limitation. The study focused on clinical outcomes in relation to kinase fusion status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an observational cross-sectional study. Its primary objective is to assess the reliability of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and immune cell reactivity, alongside perceived pain and pressure pain thresholds, through nine repeated measurements in workers exposed to constant real-life occupational workloads. Secondary aims include assessing correlations between these biomarkers and pain measures, and comparing levels between groups with higher and lower upper-extremity physical workloads. The study also details screening for metabolic parameters to ensure participant eligibility and ultimately aims to clarify the predictive role of these biomarkers in the development of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and to inform work-related stress-recovery concepts.

Participants will undergo nine repeated measurements of blood samples and pain assessments once every two weeks. The study assesses reliability and compares biomarker levels between these workload groups, rather than evaluating a therapeutic dose-response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates the utility of T cell Receptor Excision Circles (TRECs) and other markers (TCR diversity, CD31, PTK7) for monitoring thymic output and T-cell reconstitution after allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT). It examines TRECs as a predictive marker for post-HSCT complications like infections, relapse, and Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD), and for clinical outcomes including overall survival. The study also explores clinical factors influencing TREC levels, such as recipient age, conditioning regimen, stem cell source and dose, and pre-transplant thymic activity, and discusses TREC's broader diagnostic utility in congenital immunodeficiencies, HIV infection, and autoimmune diseases, advocating for its inclusion in post-HSCT follow-up.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily discusses various conditioning regimens employed in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT), including total body irradiation, cyclophosphamide, busulfan, non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC), and anti-T cell serotherapy, aimed at preventing graft rejection and reducing relapse risk. It notes that a higher dose of CD34+ peripheral blood stem cells (e.g., >10^7 per kg body weight) has been associated with higher TREC levels, suggesting a dose threshold. Immunosuppressive drugs like corticosteroids and cyclosporine are mentioned in the context of GVHD prevention and treatment. However, specific dose-response relationships for HSCT or its components are not consistently reported, and the findings are often contradictory across studies due to variations in protocols and lack of randomized trials. The document focuses on monitoring applications rather than detailing specific therapeutic intervention doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected earlier than TREC in patients receiving double cord blood grafts. A significant association with TREC was reported 6 months after transplantation. Efficiency of CMV clearance was higher in patients with TREC levels above 2000 copy/µg DNA.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery after double cord blood transplantation (CBT); assessment of CMV clearance.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with CMV clearance efficiency and improved overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in post-transplant patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in the low LPC 20:0 group (p<0.05); negatively correlated with TAG 54:4-FA22:4 and TAG 56:5-FA22:4 (correlation coefficient >0.85). Given these TAGs are significantly higher in severe/fatal patients, cytotoxic T cell count is inferred to be lower in severe and fatal COVID-19.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune cells responsible for killing infected or cancerous cells; crucial for immune response and host defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease severity and prognosis; patients with low LPC 20:0 levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired immune state or dysregulation in COVID-19 patients, potentially influenced by lipid metabolism; association with COVID-19 severity and prognosis; lower levels inferred and observed in severe/fatal outcomes, suggesting compromised cellular immunity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly from 6.5  1 0.6 to 79.4  1 21.3  5mol/L (p < .001) in response to intensive CCombat exercise, with increases ranging from 22 to 5.4-fold in 15 of 16 athletes, decreasing during recovery. High variability was observed among athletes, with elevated levels noted at +24 h in one individual.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker of coagulation and fibrinolysis, also an indicator of muscle integrity and damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intensive CCombat exercise and subsequent recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological stress response, muscle damage, or coagulation activity, emphasizing the need for individualized analysis due to high variability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase I/II clinical trial investigated the safety and efficacy of intravenously administered acellular human amniotic fluid (hAF) in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients with respiratory symptoms. The primary aim was to assess the impact of hAF on markers of systemic inflammation and coagulation. The study concluded that hAF administration did not result in statistically significant differences in safety or most inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, LDH) compared to placebo, although under specific analysis conditions (including last recorded values for early discharge patients), D-dimer and IL-6 showed statistically significant increases in the hAF group. Overall, hAF did not demonstrate a significant benefit in reducing inflammation or improving clinical outcomes, despite showing safety for intravenous administration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intravenous administration of sterile filtered, acellular human amniotic fluid (hAF)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 10 cc of sterile processed acellular hAF was administered intravenously once daily for up to 5 consecutive days (median 5 doses, IQR 3, 5). The hAF was sourced from a single donor per dose and underwent processing via filtration, purification, and sterilization to meet sterility guidelines. No significant dose-response comparisons were reported, and the efficacy was primarily compared against a saline placebo group. The study authors hypothesized that the tested dose might have been insufficient or administered too late in the disease course.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not statistically different from baseline to Day 6 compared to placebo under standard analysis. However, when including last recorded values for early discharge patients, a statistically significant increase was observed in the hAF group compared to placebo (hAF: 0.1 [-0.1, 0.2] vs placebo: -0.1 [-0.4, 0]; p = 0.04).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Fibrin degradation product, an indicator of activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis systems, and often elevated during systemic inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Changes from baseline to Day 6 following daily intravenous hAF or placebo administration in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients, with specific consideration for early discharge patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with thrombotic activity and inflammation; generally showed no significant impact, but a statistically significant increase in the hAF group was noted under specific measurement conditions (early discharge patients).

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels, increased ~two-fold in COVID-19 patients in uncomplicated (1.2-1.9 ng/ml) and complicated (1.8-3.8 ng/ml) phases compared to healthy individuals (<1 ng/ml). Levels in the complicated phase were elevated compared to the uncomplicated phase but remained below the upper limit of the normal range for Caucasians. Low D-dimer formation was associated with uPA downregulation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A byproduct of fibrinolysis of cross-linked fibrinogen, serving as a coagulation/fibrinolysis factor that indicates fibrin degradation and reflects activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease progression (uncomplicated and complicated phases) in Japanese patients, and uPA downregulation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An indicator of coagulation system and fibrinolysis activation. Elevated levels indicate moderate coagulation activation and are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. Lower levels in Japanese COVID-19 patients potentially indicate a lower thrombosis risk and may identify 'fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown' patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: stable overall; elevated in females at 30 months
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels remained stable over time in the overall cohort (p=0.905). However, females showed significantly higher values than males at the 30-month (T3) endpoint (p=0.024), with lower values recorded in males at endpoint.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Fibrin degradation product, indicating activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis, often associated with thrombotic events.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates coagulation status and thrombotic risk, suggesting distinct sex-specific patterns in thrombo-inflammatory response, with females showing delayed coagulative resolution and males potentially faster recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between serum S100B protein levels and disease severity in hospitalized Covid-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infected) patients. It revealed that increased S100B serum concentrations significantly correlate with Covid-19 disease severity, intensity of care, inflammatory processes, and several inflammatory and organ damage markers, suggesting S100B as a novel biomarker for monitoring disease course and prognosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on the progression of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Covid-19) in hospitalized patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received standard care following WHO guidelines. Disease severity was quantified using a Covid-score and categorization into High Intensity Care (HIC) or Low Intensity Care (LIC) wards. No specific intervention doses or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positive and significant correlation observed with S100B (p < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a novel, minimally invasive approach using hair follicle (HF) gene expression, specifically a four-gene panel (Bmp2, Daam2, Plaat1, Prss27), to assess and classify tissue thyroid hormone (TH) action. Investigating amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism (AIH) in human patients and a TH action indicator (THAI) mouse model, the study found that amiodarone treatment significantly attenuates tissue TH action under hyperthyroid conditions, leading to a mismatch between elevated serum TH levels and attenuated tissue hyperthyroidism, suggesting a protective effect of amiodarone against thyrotoxicosis at the tissue level.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Amiodarone treatment and Thyroid Hormone Status Modulation (Hypothyroid, Euthyroid, Hyperthyroid, T4 Administration)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human patients were treated with amiodarone for at least 4 weeks prior to sampling, with comparisons made between hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid groups; specific human amiodarone doses were not reported. In the mouse model, amiodarone was administered at 1.35 g/kg in chow for 8 weeks, and T4 was administered intraperitoneally at 166.7 ng/bwg/day for 2 days to induce hyperthyroidism. Amiodarone was shown to prevent T4-induced TH action elevation in mouse tissues. Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism affected up to 10% of patients, and AIH affected 1% of patients. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for amiodarone or T4.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Regulated by both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism; specifically 2.7- to 6.5-fold higher in hyperthyroid cases compared to hypothyroid cases.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression level is highly influenced by TH status and correlated with serum-based TH status. Part of a 4-gene model that showed high predictive performance for tissue TH status.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of tissue thyroid hormone signaling and action (TH-responsive gene).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Human tissue TH signaling assessment across hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid states, particularly in amiodarone treatment or discrepancies between serum and tissue TH levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Allows assessment of tissue TH action/status, reflecting serum-based TH status at the tissue level. It is part of a 4-gene panel used to categorize tissue TH status, serving as a complementary tool for clinical scenarios with unexplained discrepancies between routine serum parameters and clinical symptoms, and aids in treatment decisions for amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism.
