document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of consuming cow's milk versus an energy-matched carbohydrate solution on recovery markers and performance in twenty female team-sport athletes following repeated simulated team games (STGs). The findings indicated that 500 mL of milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function (peak torque for knee extension and flexion), sprint performance (5m and 10m), and perceptions of stress, and helped reduce muscle soreness and tiredness, particularly after the first STG. However, for many other physiological and performance markers (e.g., CK, hsCRP, LOOHs, PCs, CMJ, HR, RPE), the effects were mostly unclear or trivial, with milk showing no clear benefit after the second STG.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional intervention (consumption of cow's milk vs. an energy-matched carbohydrate solution) combined with a multi-stage physical activity protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 500 mL of either cow's milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g protein, 25.5 g carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat) or an energy-matched carbohydrate solution (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 53.6 g carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat) immediately following each of two simulated team games (STG1 and STG2). The 17 g protein from milk was noted to be below the recommended 20 g threshold for maximal protein synthesis stimulation. The exercise protocol involved two ~30 minute halves of intermittent running with sprints, agility, and jumps, separated by a 10-minute half-time, with a 48-hour recovery period between STG1 and STG2. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the nutritional interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive power of Neuroimmune Guidance Cue (NGC) gene expression profiles from peripheral blood monocytes for classifying cardiovascular disease (CVD) patients versus healthy individuals. Utilizing various machine learning methods, including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and Stochastic Gradient Boosting, the research aimed to identify key biomarkers for CVD prediction. The findings indicated that expression levels of SEMA6B, SEMA6D, and EPHA2 in circulating monocytes were predictive of CVD outcomes, with machine learning models demonstrating high accuracy and sensitivity in discriminating between healthy individuals and CVD patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Predictive modeling for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction using machine learning on biomarker expression profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved profiling transcriptomes of purified CD14+ monocytes from 368 subjects in the CIRCULATING CELLS study cohort, utilizing 60 mL EDTA blood samples with stringent RNA quality control (RIN > 9) and Illumina BeadStation for hybridization. Various machine-learning methods (including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, Stochastic Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, Partial Least Square, Bagged CART, and Random Forest) were applied to gene expression data to classify CVD patients and healthy individuals. Model performances were compared, with linear discriminant analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and stochastic gradient boost models yielding perfect or near-perfect sensibility and specificity, and some models achieving up to 100% accuracy in classification. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on predictive modeling and biomarker analysis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as one of the three most important features by Linear Discriminant Analysis and Naïve Bayesian models for classifying CVD patients and healthy individuals.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed an integrative multi-platform meta-analysis of gene expression profiles from Affymetrix and Illumina datasets in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients and healthy controls to identify novel, robust diagnostic biomarkers. The analysis revealed 5 commonly differentially expressed genes and 28 novel 'gained' genes, suggesting their significant potential for early PDAC diagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Integrative meta-analysis of gene expression data for biomarker identification and diagnostic prediction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gene expression data from two independent cohorts of PDAC patients (Affymetrix: 18 PDAC patients; Illumina: 36 PDAC patients) and 18 healthy controls were integrated. Profiling was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) using Affymetrix GeneChip® Human Gene ST 1.0 Arrays and Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 Expression BeadChip microarray platforms. Data were integrated using an empirical Bayesian methodology (ComBat) for batch effect removal, and differential expression was analyzed with limma software, identifying genes with p<0.01 and at least 1.5-fold differential expression. The analysis identified 5 commonly differentially expressed genes (with individual ROC curve AUC > 0.9) and 28 novel 'gained' genes, which could discriminate PDAC patients from controls with an average sensitivity of 74.8% and specificity of 73.3% for individual gained genes, 100% sensitivity and 94% specificity for combined common genes, and 91% sensitivity and 87% specificity for combined gained genes. document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. ESCC patients underwent surgery or endoscopic resection, and IEN patients underwent endoscopic resection for sample collection, but no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were investigated, as the study's primary aim was diagnostic and prognostic marker development.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the role of PPARγ1, specifically its K154/155 acetylation site, as a molecular switch in oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary adenocarcinoma tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and metastasis. Using in vitro cell models, in vivo mouse xenograft models, and human breast cancer patient datasets, the research demonstrated that K154/155 acetylation is essential for promoting tumor growth, de novo lipogenesis, and cancer stem cell characteristics, while also regulating cellular apoptosis and autophagy. The acetylation status was found to determine genome-wide DNA binding site selection, shifting from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) binding, and influencing transcriptional programs for growth factor signaling. Furthermore, gene signatures reflecting acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis (PASS1 and PASS2) showed predictive value for survival outcomes and distant metastasis-free survival in various breast cancer subtypes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Molecular mechanism investigation focusing on PPARγ1 post-translational modification (acetylation) and the functional consequences of genetic variants (wild-type vs. acetylation-defective mutants)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparing wild-type PPARγ1 with specific genetic variants (acetylation-defective mutants K154/155Q, K154/155A, an acetylation mimic K154/155R, and a sumoylation site mutant K77R) expressed in various breast cancer cell lines (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src) and in vivo in mouse xenograft models and transgenic mice with inducible Pparγ1 deletion. Experiments often involved subcutaneous injection of 1 x 10^6 cells. No dose-response comparisons of external therapeutic agents were reported; the focus was on the impact of specific molecular modifications and genetic manipulations, with the K154/155Q mutant demonstrating a significant ~90% reduction in tumor growth.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates age-dependent DNA methylation (DNAm) changes, focusing on the gain of methylation at Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)-bound low-methylated regions (LMRs) in embryonic stem cells, somatic mitotic cells, and various human and mouse tissues. It proposes the novel 'PRC2-AgeIndex' as a universal, assay-agnostic, and pan-tissue biomarker of cellular and epigenetic aging, demonstrating its utility in quantifying the effects of anti-aging interventions like caloric restriction and partial reprogramming, and distinguishing cellular age and passage number.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of aging and biomarker development; investigation of interventions including caloric restriction, rapamycin treatment, and epigenetic reprogramming.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved observational comparisons of DNA methylation profiles across various ages (0-103 years in humans, 2-22 months in mice) and cell types (CD4+ T-cells, epidermis, hepatocytes, fibroblasts). Interventions included long-term caloric restriction in old mice, rapamycin treatment in old mice (no significant change observed), and partial epigenetic reprogramming in mouse skin via Yamanaka Factors. Cell passaging experiments in human fibroblasts (neonatal and old, P2-P8) were also conducted, along with EZH2 ChIP-Seq. No detailed therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported for interventions, with a primary focus on age-dependent and cell replication-dependent epigenetic changes and biomarker validation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mammalian tissues; human CD4+ T-cells, human epidermis (sun-exposed and sun-protected skin), primary human fibroblasts (neonatal and old, passaged), murine hepatocytes, various somatic mitotic cells.
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Epigenetic modification (methylation gain/loss); average DNA methylation level, specifically at low-methylated regions (LMRs) highly bound by PRC2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Observed gain of methylation in PRC2-bound LMRs with age, representing approximately 90% of age-dependent DNAm gain genome-wide. Specifically, 95% of high-PRC2 LMRs in T-cells and 83% in epidermis were hypermethylated with age among the top 1000 LMRs with highest PRC2 binding in hESCs, with similar but lower trends in mice. Old sun-exposed epidermis samples showed significantly higher methylation than sun-protected ones. A consistent gain of DNAm at high-PRC2 LMCs was seen with age across datasets, with a very high correlation with passage number in primary human fibroblasts and in various cancer types. No significant DNAm gain was observed in post-mitotic oligodendrocytes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression and potential for gene silencing, particularly at regulatory regions (LMRs) where PRC2 binding maintains hypomethylation; a key indicator in the aging process and cell replication, and a marker of physiological aging.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Age-dependent changes across mammalian tissues and somatic mitotic cells (0-103 years in humans, 2-22 months in mice), influenced by environmental factors like sun exposure, cell replication, and cell passaging in primary fibroblasts, and in cancer samples versus post-mitotic oligodendrocytes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Recognized as one of the most reliable biomarkers of aging across mammalian tissues; its age-dependent gain, amplified in mitotic cells and cancer, is linked to cellular aging and contributes to functional dysregulation via aberrant gene expression. These DNAm changes are robust indicators of chronological and biological age, crucial for the development of the 'PRC2-AgeIndex'.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes a multi-round Delphi expert consensus process to identify and prioritize 14 key biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies. The identified biomarkers encompass physiological, inflammatory, functional, and genetic/epigenetic domains. The study outlines the methodology, discusses the suitability of biomarkers for different intervention durations, and identifies future research needs regarding biomarker standardization and early life application, concluding with a preference for composite biomarkers due to the complexity of aging.

treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study utilized a 3-round online Delphi method, starting with 116 experts in Round 1 and concluding with 60 experts in Round 3, out of 460 invited international panel members. Consensus for statements was defined as ">=70%" agreement, with "51-69%" indicating moderate agreement and "

	<=50%" leading to removal. Initially, 460 biomarkers were suggested, leading to 20 being appraised in detail. The consensus level for the 14 recommended biomarkers ranged from 70% to 98%. The identified biomarkers were deemed more suitable for medium- (3-6 months) and long-term (">=6 months") interventions, and less suitable for acute or short-term ("<3 months") interventions, as short-term changes are likely homeostatic responses with limited long-term significance for aging. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were investigated as this was a consensus-building study on biomarker utility.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study focused on developing and validating novel enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) for apolipoprotein AII (apoAII) isoforms, particularly the apoAII-ATQ/AT ratio, as diagnostic biomarkers for early-stage pancreatic cancer and for identifying individuals at high risk for pancreatic malignancy. Plasma and serum samples were collected from various cohorts, including healthy controls and patients with pancreatic cancer (e.g., IDACP across stages), other pancreatic diseases, and gastroenterologic conditions. The analytical procedures involved specific sample preparation steps for MS (e.g., 50 µl plasma, desalting, elution, spotting) and dilution protocols for ELISAs (e.g., 1/5000 dilution for apoAII-AT/ATQ, absorbance at 450 nm). Diagnostic performance was assessed using AUC values, sensitivity, and specificity, with comparisons against established markers like CA19-9 and DUPAN-2. A linear logistic regression model was used for a combination biomarker. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were performed or reported.

AUC for distinguishing IDACP (cohort-2) was 0.917, with stage-specific AUCs: stage-I (0.812), stage-II (0.850), stage-III (0.892), stage-IV (0.964). AUC values for distinguishing patients from healthy controls in other conditions ranged from 0.437 (SCNs) to 0.775 (MCNs). Did not identify patients at high risk for pancreatic cancer in the present study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document outlines the protocol for the PROSAP-A randomized controlled trial, investigating the effects of preoperative insomnia treatment (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia or Sleep Education Therapy) on acute and long-term postoperative pain control, brain health, and physical recovery in patients undergoing total knee or hip arthroplasty. document_context_data.document_summary: This study develops and validates the GeroSense deep neural network model, which uses deep longitudinal phenotyping of wearable sensor data (physical activity patterns) to provide a high-quality and cost-effective alternative for Biological Age Acceleration (BAA) determination. The model's BAA metric quantifies human health state, predicts morbidity risk, and is associated with life expectancy, mortality, chronic diseases, life-shortening lifestyles, and COVID-19 incidence. The study also reveals that organism state recovery time (resilience), derived from BAA fluctuations, is an independent marker of aging and mortality, with its divergence increasing with chronological age.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Deep Learning Computational Modeling (GeroSense BAA model) for Biological Age Acceleration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The GeroSense BAA model was trained using deep neural networks on physical activity data (steps per minute) from wearable devices (smartphones, smartwatches) from 103,830 one-week longitudinal samples and 2,599 samples up to 2 years long. This input data, derived from 100Hz raw acceleration, was used for daily BAA predictions, with averaging over several weeks improving accuracy. The model was designed to decouple BAA from seasonal variations. The study focused on model development and validation for biomarker assessment; no interventional doses or dose-response comparisons were reported.

Decreased levels are associated with increased COVID-19 risk; less efficient than GeroSense BAA in scoring infection risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of various post-exercise recovery strategies (active recovery, cold water immersion, massage, and passive recovery) on subjective and objective fatigue markers in 46 recreational male runners after a competitive half-marathon. The findings indicate that cold water immersion and massage were effective in improving subjective fatigue measures, such as muscle soreness and perceived recovery/stress, compared to passive recovery. However, active recovery was largely ineffective or even detrimental, worsening subjective recovery and negatively impacting certain objective markers (creatine kinase, free-testosterone). Overall, none of the recovery interventions demonstrated beneficial effects on objective physiological markers of fatigue.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise recovery interventions (Active Recovery (ACT), Cold Water Immersion (CWI), Massage (MAS), and Passive Recovery (PAS)) following a half-marathon race.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
46 recreational male runners completed a competitive half-marathon (average time 107-116 min, 86.2%-92.9% of anaerobic threshold, 450 m altitude climb). Within 15 minutes post-race, a single application of one of four recovery protocols was performed: Passive Recovery (PAS) was 15 min sitting at rest; Active Recovery (ACT) was 15 min sub-maximal jogging at 60% anaerobic threshold; Cold Water Immersion (CWI) involved 15 min of lower limb immersion up to the iliac crest in 15 
	1
	C water, with circular leg motions every 2 min; and Massage (MAS) consisted of 20 min of classical sports massage (effleurage, petrissage, friction), split into 5 min per leg in prone and supine positions, performed by certified sports scientists. No dose-response comparisons for the overall half-marathon intensity or the recovery interventions were explicitly reported, though the CWI protocol was chosen based on existing dose-response evidence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant associations described between alterations in salivary DHEA and the development or progression of AD, including preclinical disease stages. Dysregulations associated with cognitive decline, neurodegeneration, AD-related pathology, and AD-related behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential non-invasive and easily accessible diagnostic biomarker for AD, indicating hormonal, metabolic, and endocrinological changes associated with the disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and delayed effects of the 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT) on biomarkers of muscle damage (creatinine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase), inflammation (C-reactive protein), and subjective perceptions of fatigue, recovery, and muscle soreness (DOMS, RPE, PRS) in healthy male amateur team sports players. Findings indicate that the 5mSRT significantly increased muscle damage and inflammation markers, as well as DOMS and RPE, while reducing PRS. The study concluded that a 72-hour recovery period was generally sufficient for fatigue recovery, with biomarker levels returning towards baseline.

Participants ran the greatest possible distance within 30 seconds by shuttling between cones at increasing distances (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m, etc.). Blood samples and perceptual scores were taken at rest, 5 minutes post-exercise, and 72 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons for varying test intensities or durations were reported within the protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

The MC contained 73.5 mg 7L 91 cyanidin-3-glucoside, 178.8 gallic acid equivalent 7L 91 total phenolic content, and a TEAC of 0.58 trolox equivalents 7L 91. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time course of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and conventional muscle damage markers in response to mechanically demanding muscle-damaging drop jump exercise without significant metabolic stress in healthy males. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

A significant negative interaction between %CST and APOE4 status was observed (  = -0.297; P = 0.002), which survived Bonferroni correction. In APOE4 carriers only, %CST was negatively associated with dentate gyrus (  = -0.410; 95%CI[-0.440;-0.379]; P = 0.018).

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests increased or more efficient brain oxygen utilization in response to HIIT, indicating potential neural adaptations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study established robust reference intervals for plasma dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated Matrix Gla-Protein (dp-ucMGP) in a metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population using the IDS-iSYS Ina Ktif assay. It investigated dp-ucMGP's utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The findings indicate a significant stepwise increase in plasma dp-ucMGP levels from healthy individuals to those with DM without DKD, and further to those with DKD. Higher dp-ucMGP levels were associated with renal function decline and demonstrated predictive value for DKD diagnosis and progression, showing similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting renal function decline. Additionally, the study explored associations of dp-ucMGP with various clinical parameters in healthy volunteers, noting gender differences and correlations with BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study (Observational)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on establishing reference intervals and evaluating the diagnostic potential of plasma dp-ucMGP across different health states (healthy, diabetes mellitus, diabetic kidney disease). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted within this study. However, the document discusses external studies on Vitamin K2 supplementation (e.g., 6 weeks of daily supplementation or 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days) as a potential therapy impacting dp-ucMGP levels.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in DKD and DM without DKD compared to HVs; higher in decliners than non-decliners; increased with renal function deterioration and CKD stages; higher in patients on hemodialysis; higher in females than males; associated with increasing BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin (in HVs); negatively correlated with eGFR and rate of change in renal function; positively correlated with uACR; reduced by vitamin K2 supplementation (discussed from other studies).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference Intervals (RIs) for metabolically healthy Caucasian adults were <300–532 pmol/L. Median values: 318 pmol/L (HVs), 434 pmol/L (DM without DKD), 729 pmol/L (DKD). For identification of participants with DKD, AUC was 0.842 (95%CI:0.799–0.880; p < 0.001); optimum cut-off >557 pmol/L. Among patients with DM, LN dp-ucMGP showed a negative correlation with eGFR (r = −0.7041; p < 0.001) and with the rate of change in renal function (%change) (r = −0.4509; p < 0.001), and a positive correlation with LN uACR (r = 0.3392; p < 0.001). Males: 301 (299–518) pmol/L vs. Females: 365 (299–698) pmol/L (p = 0.004). Discussed reductions with Vitamin K2 supplementation: 27% reduction with 6 weeks of supplementation; 10.7% reduction with 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix Gla-protein (MGP) is a potent inhibitor of vascular calcification. dp-ucMGP is an inactive form, and its plasma concentration is considered an indicator of vascular vitamin K status and insufficiency. It is involved in regulating arterial calcification and is associated with vascular health and kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Establishment of normative data in metabolically healthy Caucasian adults; diagnosis and prognosis in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD); assessment of renal function decline; associations with gender, smoking status, BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, haemoglobin, iPTH, NT-proBNP, Sodium, and SBP. Also discussed in the context of hemodialysis, chronic heart failure, arterial stiffness, and vitamin K2 supplementation (based on external studies).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for identifying adults at high risk for vascular disease in the context of progressive DKD. Demonstrates similar ability to uACR in detecting participants with DM and renal function decline. Considered a marker of effective Vitamin K supplementation and is associated with combined cardiovascular disease or mortality. In healthy individuals, it shows gender-specific differences and associations with indicators of metabolic health, inflammation, liver, and thyroid function. High levels indicate vitamin K insufficiency, and interventions targeting high plasma dp-ucMGP may slow vascular calcification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study investigating the biobehavioral impacts of sexual violence victimization and revictimization, integrated with support protocols for the participant.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single case study (N=1) involved longitudinal observation over 6 months, with data collected across five study visits (M0, M1, M3, M4, M6) following four acute sexual violence (SV) events (including vaginal rape and revictimization prior to M3 and M5 visits). Data collection included surveys, blood draws, cervicovaginal exams, and self-collected diurnal saliva samples. Integrated support protocols were provided, but no active interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slight decrease at M1; increased adverse mental health at M3 (compared to M1); decrease (improvement) at M4; continuation of improved state at M6.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects self-reported symptoms associated with depressive states, indicating emotional distress and mood disturbances.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Repeated sexual violence victimization, proximity to victimization events, and contextual factors like a 'recovery' period or change in environment (return from college).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates level of psychological distress and impact of trauma on emotional well-being; changes suggest coping, recovery, or exacerbation of symptoms related to life events.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated brain and blood biomarker signatures in both rat models exposed to repetitive low-level blast and human veterans exposed to IED blasts, aiming to identify antemortem evidence of tauopathy and neuronal injury related to neurobehavioral syndromes. Key findings include chronic increases in hyperphosphorylated tau (p-tau) immunoreactivity and abnormal perivascular p-tau accumulation in specific brain regions of blast-exposed rats from 6 weeks to 12 months post-injury. In human veterans, a significant subset (50%) with multiple blast exposures exhibited excessive cortical [18F]AV1451 tau ligand retention, indicating tauopathy, which correlated with higher circulating plasma neurofilament light (NfL) levels, suggesting neuronal injury. The study also explored cortical diffusivity analysis and [18F]AV45 amyloid PET imaging, finding no significant amyloid pathology but identifying microstructural cortical disruption linked to tau pathology. Additionally, increases in stathmin 1 in the amygdala of blast-exposed animals were associated with increased anxiety. The findings collectively suggest a link between blast injury, tauopathy, neuronal injury, and associated neurobehavioral complaints, highlighting potential biomarkers for diagnosing long-term neuropsychiatric sequelae of mTBI.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blast exposure (Mild Traumatic Brain Injury - mTBI)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Rats received three repetitive low-level blast exposures (74.5 kPa/10.8 psi, 4.8 ms duration, 175.8 kPa ms impulse) administered one per day for 3 consecutive days using a shock tube. Human veterans reported histories of multiple blast exposures from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), ranging from 1 to 50 or more, all associated with at least one mTBI. The study primarily focused on the effects of these exposures rather than varying doses, and no dose-response comparisons were reported. Diagnostic procedures included MRI (3-Tesla Siemens Biograph MR system) and PET imaging (370 MBq [18F]AV45 and 370 MBq [18F]AV1451 injected, with image acquisition approximately 60-80 min post-injection for 20 min durations).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Veterans reported significantly higher levels of depression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mental health status, specifically related to mood and affect.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between veterans and age-matched comparison group.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates higher prevalence or severity of depression symptoms in the veteran group, a common comorbidity or consequence of blast-related trauma.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. It also examined changes in cognitive function (attention, executive function, memory, visual ability, fine motor skills, reaction), psychological scores (anxiety, depression), and various blood biochemical markers (Estradiol, prolactin, FSH, LH, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin). The study compared patients before, one week after, and six months after completing chemotherapy to healthy controls. Key findings revealed widespread chemotherapy-induced abnormalities in resting state networks, which partly recovered by six months post-chemotherapy. These altered functional connectivities were correlated with cognitive assessment scores and blood biochemical indexes, suggesting RSNs as potential biomarkers for chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and for guiding rehabilitation. Baseline analyses also showed higher metabolic markers and psychological/cognitive scores in patients compared to controls, along with a high incidence of chemotherapy-induced amenorrhea.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (for breast cancer patients, some also received endocrine therapy)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Postoperative chemotherapy was administered to breast cancer patients, typically in six to eight courses. While specific drug names or dosages were not detailed, follow-up assessments were consistently conducted before (baseline), one week after completing, and six months after completing chemotherapy. Some patients (35.3%) also received endocrine therapy after chemotherapy, but no concurrent radiotherapy or endocrine therapy was given during chemotherapy. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the breast cancer group than in the healthy control group at baseline (P = 0.002), although these scores were within the normal range. Scores continued to increase one week after chemotherapy but decreased over time after the end of chemotherapy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects psychological distress and emotional state, with suggested competitive interactions with cognition.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline assessment and post-chemotherapy emotional changes and recovery in breast cancer patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of mental health status and psychological burden. Initial high scores indicate distress, and subsequent decrease is speculated to benefit cognitive function recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: DEPRESSION decreased in male COMP from MID to POST (p < 0.05), though not significantly different from CTRL. No significant changes were observed in female groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects feelings of sadness, despondency, and low mood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Across the MID to POST phase in male and female physique athletes and control groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A decrease indicates an improvement in mood and reduction in depressive symptoms during the recovery phase. Stability in females suggests consistent depression levels, indicating different psychological responses compared to males.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated blood-derived DNA methylation-based prediction models, including epigenetic scores (epi-LIBRA, epi-CAIDE) and a Multivariate Methylation Risk Score (MMRS), to assess and predict cognitive impairment and dementia (including AD and MCI) in various independent cohorts. The MMRS showed notable predictive capacity for MCI and prospective cognitive decline in AD and Parkinson's disease, and enhanced prediction when combined with traditional biomarkers, though individual epi-CAIDE and epi-LIBRA models performed poorly for AD and MCI status prediction. The study also detailed data preprocessing for various dementia risk factors, CSF biomarkers (amyloid- , tau, p-tau), whole blood DNA methylation profiling, and polygenic scores, aiming to investigate cognitive status and dementia.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Model Development and Validation using Epigenetic Markers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the development and validation of DNA methylation-based predictive models (including MMRS, epi-CAIDE, epi-LIBRA) for cognitive impairment and dementia. Whole blood genome-wide DNA methylation data, genotyping, and CSF biomarkers were utilized from various cohorts (EXTEND, EMIF-AD MBD, PPMI, ADNI, BASE-II) with different age ranges (40-75,  60 years). Models were constructed using machine learning techniques (e.g., ElasticNet, Random Forest, sPLS-DA, RF-RFE) with hyperparameter optimization via cross-validation. The study focused on predictive modeling and model performance comparisons, rather than therapeutic interventions or traditional dose-response relationships.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified by mean absolute SHAP values as a predominant driver (rank among top 4).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Epigenetic marker contributing to depression risk, influencing cognitive impairment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Factor predominantly driving the best-performing MMRS-MCI (RF-RFE) model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a significant epigenetic contribution to MCI prediction, reflecting mental health's role.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the functional implications of heterogeneity in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), focusing on an endodermally biased pluripotent substate. Using a GATA6-GFP reporter line and single-cell functional/transcriptomic analyses, the research identified distinct, interconvertible hESC substates defined by differential expression of GATA6 and SSEA3. GATA6-positive hESCs, while retaining long-term self-renewal and pluripotency (often alongside OCT4 and SOX2 co-expression), exhibited a higher propensity and bias towards spontaneous endoderm and mesoderm differentiation, with downregulation of ectodermal genes. SOX17 was identified as a potential driver for this endoderm-biased substate.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Embryonic Stem Cell (hESC) Substate Characterization and Differentiation Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized the Shef4 hESC line, which was genetically modified with a GATA6-GFP reporter via Zinc Finger Nuclease-mediated homologous recombination. Cells were cultured in KO/SR on MEF feeders or E8 medium. hESC substates, defined by differential GATA6 and SSEA3 expression (e.g., 3+/6-, 3+/6L, 3+/6H, 3-/6+), were isolated by Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS). These sorted cells were subjected to single-cell cloning, gene expression analysis (qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing), high-content clonogenic assays, and differentiation protocols, including a spin-embryoid body (EB) system, without external therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for differentiation-inducing factors. The focus was on intrinsic marker expression and resultant lineage bias.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked upregulation in EBs from GATA6-expressing subsets (3+/6L, 3+/6H, 3-/6+).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mesoderm-associated gene.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: hESC subset differentiation using spin-EB system.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bias toward mesoderm differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the function of microRNA-137 (miR-137) and Developmental endothelial locus-1 (Del-1) expression in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells and tissues using various molecular and cellular assays. It found that miR-137 inhibits cancer progression by directly targeting and regulating Del-1, acting as a tumor suppressor and suggesting its potential as a novel therapeutic and diagnostic biomarker for TNBC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Investigation and molecular manipulation of gene expression regulation (miRNA overexpression/inhibition, siRNA knockdown) for triple-negative breast cancer progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Experimental manipulation included transient transfection of miR-137 mimics (1, 10, or 25 pmol) or inhibitors, and small-interfering RNAs (siRNA) for Del-1 knockdown (1 or 25 pmol) or overexpression plasmids (100 ng or 2 µg) in MDA-MB-231 and Hs578T triple-negative breast cancer cell lines using Lipofectamine. Comparative analysis of miR-137 levels in tumor tissues and Del-1 levels in plasma was performed in 30 TNBC patients relative to normal controls. While specific concentrations were used for in vitro experiments, no dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were explicitly reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Breast cancer cell lines (MDA-MB-231, MCF7, SK-BR3, T-47D), normal breast epithelial cells (MCF10A), plasma from breast cancer patients (including 30 TNBC patients), TNBC tissue, cell culture medium.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic and prognostic marker for early breast cancer; indicates tumor progression and oncogenesis; promotes proliferation, migration, and invasion of TNBC cells; its regulation by miR-137 is crucial for TNBC therapeutic strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in severe patients compared to mild patients, and significantly higher in fatal patients compared to survival patients. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of aberrant N-glycosylation profiles of serum immunoglobulins (Igs) for urothelial carcinoma (UC), including bladder cancer (UCB) and upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). It identified five UC-associated aberrant N-glycan changes, notably the accumulation of asialo-bisecting GlcNAc type N-glycans in UC patients. A novel diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore), derived from a combination of these five N-glycans, demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (92.8% sensitivity, 97.2% specificity, AUC 0.969) for discriminating UC patients from healthy volunteers and prostate cancer patients, outperforming traditional diagnostic methods like urine cytology and hematuria. The dNGScore also showed utility in detecting urine cytology-negative cases and was associated with UCB invasiveness.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification (N-glycomics analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on diagnostic biomarker discovery, not therapeutic doses. High-throughput N-glycomics was used to quantify 32 types of N-glycan levels on serum immunoglobulins from 10-μL aliquots of purified Ig fractions. A diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore) was established using a specific formula involving five N-glycans (m/z 1606, 1769, 2074, 2118, 2423) and a cut-off of -0.0955 points. No therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Diagnostic capability; generally lower in UC patients
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Discriminated UC patients from HV and PC patients with 92.8% sensitivity and 97.2% specificity. The AUC for dNGScore was 0.969 for UC detection, superior to urine cytology (AUC 0.707) and hematuria (AUC 0.892). Significantly lower in UC patients (UCB and UTUC) than in the non-UC group (HVs and PC) (p = 0.0001). At -0.0955 points cut-off, negative predictive value was 96.1%. Associated with invasiveness of UCB.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A combined diagnostic indicator reflecting aberrant N-glycosylation patterns on immunoglobulins in urothelial carcinoma, reflecting disease-associated immunoreactions and altered glycan biosynthetic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Detection of Urothelial Carcinoma (UC), including UCB and UTUC, using a composite serum biomarker.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Highly sensitive and specific diagnostic biomarker for urothelial carcinomas, outperforming traditional diagnostic methods and capable of detecting patients negative for hematuria and urine cytology. Useful for early diagnosis of UCB and for identifying urine cytology-negative UC cases, and associated with UCB invasiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the clinical utility of serum N-glycan profiling using glycoblotting and mass spectrometry as novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for Germ Cell Tumors (GCT). It aimed to assess whether a newly developed N-glycan score could improve GCT detection and prognosis, particularly in patients negative for conventional tumor markers, and identify those at high risk of relapse. The study demonstrated that the N-glycan score is a practical method for GCT detection and prognosis, showing a higher score in GCT patients and associating with advanced disease and poor prognosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This study involved N-glycan profiling and analysis for the diagnostic and prognostic assessment of Germ Cell Tumors (GCT), focusing on biomarker identification rather than therapeutic intervention.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Comprehensive N-glycan structural analysis was performed on sera from 54 untreated GCT patients and 103 age-adjusted healthy volunteers using glycoblotting and mass spectrometry, identifying 70 types of BOA-labeled N-glycans. Optimal cutoff concentration values were established for candidate N-glycans, leading to the creation of a diagnostic N-glycan score (based on five N-glycans: m/z 2379, 2337, 1709, 3865, 3195) and a prognostic N-glycan score (based on four N-glycans: m/z 2890, 3195, 3560, 3865). The study did not involve therapeutic dose or treatment comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Composite score based on the number of specific N-glycans (m/z 2379, 2337, 1709, 3865, 3195) above cutoff concentration values

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher score indicates presence of GCT
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the GCT group compared to healthy volunteers (5.0 vs. 1.0, P < 0.001). Accuracy for predicting GCT was significant with an area-under-the-curve (AUC) value of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.81–0.94, P < 0.001), using an optimal cutoff of 2.5 points (81% sensitivity, 80% specificity). It detected 10 of 12 (83%) patients with negative conventional tumor markers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Integrates information from five specific N-glycans (m/z 2379, 2337, 1709, 3865, 3195) to reflect altered protein glycosylation patterns associated with the presence of germ-cell tumors.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis of Germ Cell Tumors (GCT) in patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A practical diagnostic method for GCT, indicating the presence of tumors and proving particularly effective for GCT detection in patients who are negative for conventional tumor markers (detecting 83% of such cases).
