document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of heart rate-matched (HR-matched) or work rate-matched (WR-matched) hypoxic interval exercise on post-exercise cardiac autonomic and cardiovascular responses compared to normoxic exercise in moderately trained men. Findings indicate that HR-matched hypoxic exercise mimicked post-exercise autonomic responses of normoxic exercise without inducing significant post-exercise hypotension (PEH) or impairing cardiac baroreflex sensitivity (cBRS). Conversely, WR-matched hypoxic exercise resulted in delayed cardiac autonomic recovery, a temporary decrease in cBRS, and prolonged PEH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hypoxic and Normoxic Interval Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed three interval-type exercise sessions (5x5-min work intervals; 1-min passive recovery) after a 5-min warm-up at 50% WR@VT1. Normoxic exercise (N) was at 80% of the work rate (WR) at the first ventilatory threshold (mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 139±10 bpm, ~75%HRmax). Hypoxic exercise (FiO2 = 14.2%, simulating ~3000m altitude) was performed either at the same absolute WR as N (H-WR, WR-matched: mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 154±11 bpm, ~83%HRmax) or at the same absolute HR as N (H-HR, HR-matched: mean WR 144±18 W, mean HR 138±9 bpm, ~75%HRmax). This resulted in a -21.1±9.3% reduction in WR for H-HR compared to N, and a higher HR (by ~15 bpm) for H-WR compared to N. Recovery was seated under normoxic conditions, with assessments at POST-15, POST-45, POST-60, and POST-90 minutes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: At rest, DAP significantly increased at POST-60 in H-HR (MD 7 mmHg, p=0.002) compared to PRE. During squat-stand (SS) manoeuvres, DAP significantly decreased at POST-45 in H-WR (MD -4 mmHg, p=0.035) and increased at POST-90 in H-HR (MD 5 mmHg, p=0.017) compared to PRE.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the minimum pressure exerted on the arteries between heartbeats, reflecting vascular resistance and maintaining blood flow during diastole.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery at rest and during repeated squat-stand manoeuvres following HR-matched Hypoxic (H-HR) and WR-matched Hypoxic (H-WR) exercise sessions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Changes suggest altered peripheral vascular resistance or cardiac output during recovery and orthostatic challenge, indicating varying cardiovascular regulation responses and potentially impacting cardiovascular recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of wearing exercise compression stockings (CS) on intramuscular pressure (IMP), muscle tissue oxygenation, and early blood biomarkers for muscle damage (myoglobin, creatine kinase) in the tibialis anterior muscle during a 10-km treadmill run in healthy recreational runners. Findings indicated that CS use significantly elevated IMP, reduced muscle tissue oxygenation, and increased serum myoglobin, suggesting non-beneficial muscle effects and no prevention of early exercise-induced muscle damage. Creatine kinase levels and systemic blood pressure remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise with Compression Stockings
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty healthy recreational runners performed two identical 10-km treadmill runs at a self-selected speed (10-12 km/h, no inclination) in a randomized crossover design, once with knee-high compression stockings (manufacturer-stated 25 mmHg at ankle) and once without. The intervention involved wearing CS during rest, running, and a post-run recovery period. No dose-response comparisons for compression levels were conducted, only with/without CS comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in these values were found for subjects running with CS and without CS.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Systemic arterial pressure during ventricular relaxation, serving as an indicator of overall cardiovascular function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured before and after a 10-km treadmill run, with and without compression stockings.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Unchanged diastolic blood pressure indicates no significant systemic cardiovascular effect of compression stockings during running.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: decreased in non-pDPN group, unchanged in pDPN group
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.39); significant decrease in without pDPN group (P < 0.0001); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.30).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular health, representing the pressure in arteries between heartbeats.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improvement in cardiovascular health (lower diastolic blood pressure) in the group without pDPN, but no change in the pDPN group.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular health and arterial pressure
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of low (LV-HIIT) and high (HV-HIIT) volumes of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on vascular-endothelial function, oxidative stress, and atherosclerosis markers in patients after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The 16-week supervised HIIT programs, regardless of volume, led to a volume-dependent enhancement in endothelial function (FMD) and a decrease in oxidative stress (ox-LDL). A reduction in vascular wall thickness (cIMT) was also observed, with LV-HIIT proving sufficient to initiate favorable adaptations and reduce cardiovascular risk. The study also assessed anthropometric and other cardiovascular markers, comparing HIIT groups to an active control.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Unsupervised Physical Activity Recommendations (Active Control, AC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) with two volumes: Low Volume (LV-HIIT) and High Volume (HV-HIIT), and an Active Control (AC) group. LV-HIIT involved 8 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-minute total session. HV-HIIT involved 16 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-40 minute total session. Both supervised HIIT groups exercised 2 non-consecutive days per week for 16 weeks (32 sessions) on treadmills and cycle ergometers, with intensity individualized based on cardiorespiratory fitness, ventilatory thresholds, beat-to-beat HR, and the Böarg scale. The AC group received individualized recommendations for unsupervised physical activity, advised to perform at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity 5–7 days per week for 16 weeks. FMD and ox-LDL changes were volume-dependent (HV-HIIT showing greater effects), while cIMT reduction was similar between LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT, indicating a volume-independent effect for cIMT and confirming LV-HIIT's effectiveness.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased by -9.1 ± 5.1% (p = 0.0007) in LV-HIIT and -10.2 ± 6.3% (p = 0.0015) in HV-HIIT. No significant changes were observed in the AC group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the pressure exerted by blood on artery walls when the heart rests between beats, reflecting cardiovascular health and hypertension risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 16-week High-Intensity Interval Training (LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates improved cardiovascular health and reduced hypertension risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-sectional Study for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the 2019 general physical examination of 3,280 rural Chinese residents aged 45 years and older. No experimental interventions or therapeutic doses were administered; the study focused on observational correlations between biomarkers and cIMT. It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hypertension was defined as DBP    90 mmHg.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures arterial pressure during heart relaxation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional health examination.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of hypertension and increased risk of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the pressure in arteries when the heart rests between beats.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health and general physiological status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. The primary finding was that ALK water significantly reduced high-shear whole blood viscosity and enhanced its restoration to pre-exercise baseline levels compared to CON water, while other markers like plasma osmolality, bioimpedance, and body mass showed no significant difference.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral rehydration therapy after exercise-induced dehydration, comparing electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) with standard purified water (CON).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants exercised in a warm environment (30 °C, 70% relative humidity) until a 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight loss was achieved due to perspiration (mild dehydration). Rehydration involved consuming either electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) or standard purified water (CON), with an equal volume equivalent to 2% of pre-exercise body weight (approximately 20 mL/kg), administered within 30 minutes. This was followed by a 120-minute (2-hour) recovery period. No dose-response comparisons or variations in rehydration volume/rate were reported beyond the two water types.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean values for vital signs were similar between the high-pH alkaline water and standard water groups, with no clinically significant abnormal values observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key indicator of cardiovascular function and fluid status, reflecting arterial pressure during heart relaxation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise rehydration with alkaline water compared to control water.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly affected by the type of rehydration water (alkaline vs. control) in this context, suggesting no differential impact on immediate cardiovascular stability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 2-year prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in bone remodeling and turnover markers in children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from diagnosis through chemotherapy. It revealed that ALL onset significantly slows bone remodeling, with significantly lower bone turnover markers at diagnosis compared to controls. During chemotherapy, particularly the induction phase, these markers increased, suggesting a recovery of bone turnover, and a potential balance in active bone remodeling by the end of therapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Risk-adapted multiagent antileukemic chemotherapy, specifically for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), including Glucocorticoid (GC) therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 2-year prospective longitudinal study involved chemotherapy according to international AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 and ESPhALL 2017 protocols, with patients stratified by risk (standard, intermediate, high). The treatment included induction, reinduction/delayed intensification (two phases of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy), and a maintenance phase. Blood sampling was conducted at 5 time points (T0-T4) from diagnosis until treatment cessation. No specific numerical drug dosages were reported, but it was noted that different glucocorticoid doses did not significantly alter bone marker profiles after intensive therapy phases.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower at diagnosis compared to controls
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls (p < 0.0001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inhibits the Wnt/β-catenin pro-osteoblastogenic pathway, which is crucial for osteoblast differentiation and bone formation, thus regulating osteoblastogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in ALL children at diagnosis suggest altered bone formation signaling and dysregulation of bone formation pathways, potentially contributing to suppressed bone turnover observed in a context of overall slowed bone remodeling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. It further characterized 56 proteins with sustained changes, linking them to cardiometabolic traits and responses to a 20-week aerobic exercise training program. The research aimed to biochemically characterize acute exercise protein kinetics, finding enrichment for coagulation-related proteins post-exercise and MYC targets, and noting both concordant and discordant protein responses between acute and chronic exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute treadmill exercise and chronic aerobic exercise training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise consisted of symptom-limited treadmill stress testing in 75 middle-aged adults, following a standard Bruce protocol with plasma protein quantification at baseline, peak exercise (mean 90% predicted peak heart rate, 9.6 METs), and 1-hour post-exercise. Chronic exercise involved a 20-week aerobic training program with three sessions per week, with intensity and duration gradually increased based on individual VO2max. Acute exercise intensity and duration varied, making it difficult to effectively analyze specific exertion thresholds or dose-response comparisons for the acute protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not specified numerically; exhibited similar direction of change to previous findings at peak exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: WNT signaling modulator.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Peak acute exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Exercise-responsive.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: sHEI administered.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline visit (Visit 3).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Baseline dietary patterns that may influence primary and secondary outcome measures.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery Method: Nano-omics integrative proteomics workflow utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas for glioblastoma (GB).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved inducing murine glioblastoma by stereotactic injection of 50,000 GL261 cells into the striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Liposomes (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000) were prepared at a final lipid concentration of 25 mM and administered intravenously at a lipid dose of 0.125 mM/g body weight (equivalent to 5 mg/kg doxorubicin-loaded liposomes) 10 minutes prior to blood collection in mice. In human validation, ex vivo nanoparticle corona analysis was performed on pre-operative plasma samples from 10 high-grade glioma patients. Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. Matched resected tumor tissue from human patients was analyzed by LCM-coupled LC:MS/MS. No specific dose-response comparisons for nanoparticle application or tumor cell inoculation were reported for therapeutic purposes, as the focus was on biomarker discovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 115 DAPs identified at D7 (p < 0.05), increasing to 206 at D14, and 417 at D18. The majority of DAPs were upregulated in tumour-bearing mice. A group of 116 DAPs showed differential abundance across all three time points, with some exhibiting progressively increasing or decreasing plasma levels as tumour burden increased.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects alterations in the plasma proteome in response to brain tumour growth, indicating shedding of tumour-related proteins into the bloodstream.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal monitoring of GL261-bearing mice across three stages of tumour growth (D7, D14, D18) using nanoparticle-enabled proteomic analysis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests distinct proteomic changes at different stages of tumour progression, highlighting the importance of longitudinal studies for capturing dynamic changes associated with GB progression; identifies potential molecular pathways that could serve as sources for peripheral blood biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. ESCC patients underwent surgery or endoscopic resection, and IEN patients underwent endoscopic resection for sample collection, but no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were investigated, as the study's primary aim was diagnostic and prognostic marker development.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 153 genes showed significant differential expression (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05) when comparing methylation-dominant and methylation-poor groups. A total of 3221 significant genes (Padj<0.1, BH method) were selected, with 920 genes upregulated in the methylation-dominant cluster and 2301 genes upregulated in the methylation-poor cluster.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of cellular processes, reflecting transcriptional activity and pathway involvement. Methylation-dominant group showed enrichment in cell division-related pathways (organelle fission, nuclear division, mitotic nuclear division, chromosome segregation). Methylation-poor group showed enrichment in immune-related pathways (T-cell activation, mononuclear cell differentiation, lymphocyte differentiation).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Catheter ablation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a higher percentage of fibrocytes with myofibroblast characteristics in persistent AF patients, suggesting active fibrotic processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated a multilayer perceptron (MLP) machine learning model for the early postnatal differential diagnosis of choledochal cysts (CC) and cystic biliary atresia (CBA). The model utilized routinely available clinical parameters, including biochemical markers (Total bile acid, Total bilirubin, γ-glutamyl transferase, Aspartate aminotransferase, Alanine aminotransferase, Direct bilirubin, and Taurodeoxycholate) and ultrasonographic measurements (Longitudinal and Transverse diameters of cysts), from a retrospective cohort of 319 patients. The MLP model achieved high diagnostic performance (95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and AUC of 0.990 for differentiating CBA from CC), aiming to facilitate timely surgical intervention for CBA and improve patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Model Development (Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective study involved the analysis of clinical features from 319 patients (< 60 days old at surgery) with hepatic hilar cysts (274 CC, 45 CBA) treated between 2011 and 2022. It focused on developing a diagnostic model rather than a therapeutic intervention. Biochemical markers and ultrasonographic measurements were compared, and key diagnostic features were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Eleven machine learning models were developed and compared, with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) model showing optimal performance: 95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.990. The model utilized seven routine clinical parameters (GGT, TBA, DBIL, TBIL, ALT, LDC, and TDC) as input variables. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

The study concluded that OPCML and HOXD9, especially when combined, demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity, making them promising differential biomarkers for CCA, improving diagnostic accuracy and preventing misdiagnosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery Method: Nano-omics integrative proteomics workflow utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas for glioblastoma (GB).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved inducing murine glioblastoma by stereotactic injection of 50,000 GL261 cells into the striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Liposomes (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000) were prepared at a final lipid concentration of 25 mM and administered intravenously at a lipid dose of 0.125 mM/g body weight (equivalent to 5 mg/kg doxorubicin-loaded liposomes) 10 minutes prior to blood collection in mice. In human validation, ex vivo nanoparticle corona analysis was performed on pre-operative plasma samples from 10 high-grade glioma patients. Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. Matched resected tumor tissue from human patients was analyzed by LCM-coupled LC:MS/MS. No specific dose-response comparisons for nanoparticle application or tumor cell inoculation were reported for therapeutic purposes, as the focus was on biomarker discovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility and limitations of Body Mass Index (BMI) compared to Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)-derived percent body fat and fasting leptin and insulin levels for diagnosing and classifying obesity in adults. It concluded that BMI significantly underestimates obesity prevalence, especially in women and with advancing age, due to its inability to distinguish lean from fat mass. The study proposed new, lower gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) and found that leptin levels, unlike insulin, enhance the accuracy of BMI estimates for adiposity, particularly in women and when DXA is unavailable. The integration of leptin and DXA is suggested for more precise obesity characterization and management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Comparison and Biomarker Analysis for Obesity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional study conducted a retrospective review of BMI calculations, DXA scans, and fasting blood levels of leptin and insulin from 9,088 adults between 1998 and 2009. Measurements for BMI, DXA (providing simultaneous muscle, bone mass, and adiposity data), and blood work (fasting leptin and insulin drawn between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm) were taken within 3 weeks of each other. The study evaluated and compared the accuracy and classification rates of these metrics for obesity, proposing new gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) based on body fat and leptin corrections. No therapeutic intervention dose-response comparisons were reported.

DXA indicated that 64% of subjects were obese, compared to 26% by BMI, providing simultaneous measurements of muscle, bone mass, and body adiposity. Obesity cut-points used include American Society of Bariatric Physicians (ASBP) guidelines (≥25% for men, ≥30% for women) and World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines (≥25% for men, ≥35% for women).

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered a better and more accurate reference standard than BMI for adiposity and obesity diagnosis. It allows for more precise characterization and management of obesity, including identifying 'normal weight obese' individuals and sarcopenic obesity. This is crucial as sarcopenic obesity exacerbates BMI misclassifications and is associated with increased risk for impaired gait, disability, falls, fractures, and other medical comorbidities (e.g., hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, hypertension, and diabetes). Its use may represent a reasonable transition in public health policy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Control AdmMabs gave rise to dystrophin expressing fibres 1 month after injection. No dystrophin expression was observed following systemic injection of shPW1 AdmMABs. ShPW1 AdmMABs restored dystrophin expression in the injected area (intramuscular).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. ESCC patients underwent surgery or endoscopic resection, and IEN patients underwent endoscopic resection for sample collection, but no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were investigated, as the study's primary aim was diagnostic and prognostic marker development.

Sensitivities improved from 70% to 87% for ESCC and 50% to 62% for precancerous lesions. Increased detection rates: 62% for IENs, 78% for stage I, 83% for stage II, and 93% for stage III ESCCs, maintaining specificities >95%. Potential increase in 5-year overall survival rates by 33.87% to 41.95%; annual application at IEN stage could increase 5-year survival by 6.9% (40.22% vs 33.37% for ESCC-cfMeth).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the functional implications of heterogeneity in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), focusing on an endodermally biased pluripotent substate. Using a GATA6-GFP reporter line and single-cell functional/transcriptomic analyses, the research identified distinct, interconvertible hESC substates defined by differential expression of GATA6 and SSEA3. GATA6-positive hESCs, while retaining long-term self-renewal and pluripotency (often alongside OCT4 and SOX2 co-expression), exhibited a higher propensity and bias towards spontaneous endoderm and mesoderm differentiation, with downregulation of ectodermal genes. SOX17 was identified as a potential driver for this endoderm-biased substate.

The focus was on intrinsic marker expression and resultant lineage bias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnosis of Sport-related Concussion (SRC) using proteomic profiling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from concussed and non-concussed collegiate athletes within 48 hours post-injury, with analyses conducted for acute (0-6 hours) and subacute (7-48 hours) phases. A highly multiplexed proteomic DNA aptamers assay targeting 1305 plasma proteins was used. The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly more abundant after SRC (P<0.05). After 6 hours post-injury, individual plasma EPB41 showed an AUC of 0.956 (95%CI: 0.902–1.000); combination with SNCA provided an AUC of 1.000.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential erythrocyte membrane component, stabilizing the spectrin-actin cytoskeleton, and plays an essential role in the central nervous system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sport-related concussion (SRC) diagnosis, particularly >6 hours post-injury.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A highly accurate plasma diagnostic biomarker for concussion in athletes, especially when combined with alpha-synuclein. Previously, decreased levels were associated with neurological impairments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: CD133+ and CD133- human kidney cell populations

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CD133- cells expressed noticeably lower levels of Epcam compared with CD133+ cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Epithelial marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differentiation between epithelial-like (CD133+) and mesenchymal-like (CD133-) human kidney cell populations.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an indicator to distinguish the epithelial characteristics of isolated kidney cell populations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (hiPSCs) and Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESCs) compared to parental somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Included in the list of 982 proteins up-regulated by at least 1.5-fold in hiPSCs compared to parental somatic cells, identified with >95% confidence and a maximum false discovery rate of 2%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell surface marker; involved in cell adhesion and signaling; well-known embryonic stem cell (ESC) marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of proteomic profiles during reprogramming of somatic cells to hiPSCs and between hiPSCs and hESCs.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of pluripotency and stem cell identity; identified as a potential hiPSC surface marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive power of Neuroimmune Guidance Cue (NGC) gene expression profiles from peripheral blood monocytes for classifying cardiovascular disease (CVD) patients versus healthy individuals. Utilizing various machine learning methods, including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and Stochastic Gradient Boosting, the research aimed to identify key biomarkers for CVD prediction. The findings indicated that expression levels of SEMA6B, SEMA6D, and EPHA2 in circulating monocytes were predictive of CVD outcomes, with machine learning models demonstrating high accuracy and sensitivity in discriminating between healthy individuals and CVD patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Predictive modeling for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction using machine learning on biomarker expression profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved profiling transcriptomes of purified CD14+ monocytes from 368 subjects in the CIRCULATING CELLS study cohort, utilizing 60 mL EDTA blood samples with stringent RNA quality control (RIN > 9) and Illumina BeadStation for hybridization. Various machine-learning methods (including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, Stochastic Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, Partial Least Square, Bagged CART, and Random Forest) were applied to gene expression data to classify CVD patients and healthy individuals. Model performances were compared, with linear discriminant analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and stochastic gradient boost models yielding perfect or near-perfect sensibility and specificity, and some models achieving up to 100% accuracy in classification. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on predictive modeling and biomarker analysis.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Circulating monocytes (Peripheral Blood Monocytes, specifically CD14-positive monocytes)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Differential expression for classification; its knockdown attenuated atherosclerotic lesion development
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression levels were of predictive value for cardiovascular disease outcome. Machine learning models, particularly stochastic gradient boosting, identified it as the 'third most important feature' (P<0.05 for overall model performance).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neuroimmune guidance cue; directs cell and axon migration during neural development; involved in pathological immune responses, leukocyte trafficking, and atherosclerosis pathogenesis. Promotes the adhesion and differentiation of monocytes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Classification of cardiovascular disease patients versus healthy individuals using various machine learning methods (e.g., Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, Stochastic Gradient Boosting); implicated in atherosclerosis pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictive biomarker for cardiovascular disease outcome and susceptibility to progression; promotes monocyte adhesion and differentiation; its knockdown attenuated atherosclerosis, indicating a significant role in disease development and a potential health indicator.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive fine-mapping analysis of 150 breast cancer risk regions using dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls of European ancestry). It identified 352 independent risk signals, containing 13,367 credible causal variants (CCVs), with 191-205 high-confidence signals and 191 likely target genes. The investigation revealed that CCVs were significantly over-represented in active gene regulatory regions, open chromatin, actively transcribed genes, and transcription factor binding sites. The study also found signals differentially associated with ER-positive and ER-negative breast cancer, and prioritized target genes through integrated computational approaches like PAINTOR and INQUISIT, collectively explaining up to 23.6% of the familial relative risk. Furthermore, it included eQTL analyses in normal and tumor breast tissue to link genetic variants with gene expression changes, and explored the enrichment of CCVs with various genomic features and their impact on specific biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic fine-mapping, risk profiling, and functional genomics analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is a genetic association and fine-mapping analysis, not an interventional therapy. It utilized dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls) of European ancestry, analyzing over 639,000 genetic variants (SNPs, deletion/insertions, CNVs with MAF ">= 0.1% or 0.005%") across 150-152 previously defined risk regions. Methodologies included stepwise multinomial logistic regression, Bayesian approaches (PAINTOR), and a gene prioritization pipeline (INQUSIT). Statistical thresholds like conditional p-values (< 10^-6 for strong evidence, < 10^-4 for moderate) and False Discovery Rate (FDR 5%) were applied. eQTL analyses involved linear regression with specific covariates, and functional characterization included enrichment analysis with histone marks and TFBS motifs (FIMO p-value threshold 10^-3). No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the role of fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4), particularly adipocyte-released e-FABP4, in clear cell Renal Cell Carcinoma (ccRCC) progression and its correlation with peri-renal adipose tissue. It demonstrates that FABP4 serum levels and e-FABP4 in adipocyte conditioned media are significantly higher in ccRCC patients. In vitro experiments showed that recombinant FABP4 significantly promotes ccRCC cell migration and ERK phosphorylation, while adipocyte-released factors (other than FABP4) also enhance ACHN cell proliferation. These findings highlight FABP4 as a driver of ccRCC progression and a potential noninvasive biomarker and therapeutic target.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Investigation of FABP4's role in renal cancer progression through in vitro studies using recombinant FABP4, adipocyte-conditioned media (Ad-CM) from ccRCC patients and healthy donors, and the FABP4 inhibitor BMS309403, alongside analysis of patient serum biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In vitro experiments involved recombinant FABP4 (specifically at 10000 pg/mL), Adipocyte-Conditioned Medium (Ad-CM) from ccRCC patients and healthy donors, and the FABP4 inhibitor BMS309403. Cells were treated for proliferation and migration assays, with Mitomycin C (10 µg/mL) used to halt proliferation in scratch assays. While specific concentrations were provided for some reagents, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were generally not reported. Patient serum FABP4 levels were also compared between ccRCC patients and healthy donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: FABP4 effect was associated with an increased ERK phosphorylation. Both Ad-CM from ccRCC and recombinant FABP4 treatment significantly increased ERK phosphorylation. FABP4 inhibitor mitigated ERK phosphorylation induced by Ad-CM from ccRCC and recombinant FABP4 in both cell lines. Quantitative statistical data not provided beyond qualitative description of significance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key signaling event and crucial transducer of extracellular signals, regulating cellular processes such as proliferation, differentiation, cell shape, and motility; involved in coordinating cell movement, and plays a pivotal role in extracellular FABP4 signaling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: FABP4 effect in 786-O and ACHN renal cancer cell lines, activation by Ad-CM from ccRCC, and mitigation by FABP4 inhibitor, mediating enhanced motility of ccRCC cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with FABP4-mediated cell migration and progression of ccRCC, indicates increased ccRCC cell motility and metastatic spread, a key factor in cancer progression.
