document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: same as healthy controls, very different
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were the same as those in healthy controls. Levels were unique for all grades of histological findings, showing an inverse relationship with healthy controls but without statistical difference. The correlation with all grades of histological findings also showed an inverse relationship with no statistical difference. Serum levels were very different from those of the other cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, MCP-1, G-CSF, leptin); no significant difference in plasma levels reported in NASH patients treated with melatonin (cited study).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Appetite-stimulating hormone, involved in energy homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) patients, all grades of histological findings (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Levels are not significantly different from healthy controls in NASH and show a non-significant inverse relationship with histological findings, suggesting it may not be a direct indicator for NASH progression. Potentially associated with more severe NAFLD (cited study); important cytokine in NASH requiring further research.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the discovery of novel traumatic brain injury (TBI) biomarkers using autoimmune profiling in both rat models and human patients. It details methodologies for sample preparation, protein analysis via 2D gel electrophoresis, immunoprofiling, and the development of an immunosorbent electrochemiluminescence assay (IEA) for peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6). The main findings establish PRDX6 as a candidate TBI biomarker, showing its astrocytic expression, TBI-induced autoantibody reactivity in rats, gender differences in baseline human plasma levels, and a significant, persistent approximately fourfold elevation of circulating PRDX6 in humans following mild-to-moderate TBI, which is proportional to injury severity and independent of imaging findings. The study also acknowledges S100B and GFAP as other relevant TBI indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) injury model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human TBI was observed as mild-to-moderate (median GCS 15), with plasma collected at 4-24 hours and 2-7 days post-injury; no direct manipulation or controlled dose was applied, though PRDX6 response correlated with injury severity. In rat models, severe CCI injury was induced using a stereotaxic impactor with a 5 mm impactor at a 20-degree angle to a depth of 2 mm at 5 m/sec with a dwell time of 500 msec to maximize autoimmune response. No specific dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported for either human TBI or rat CCI, beyond PRDX6 response proportionality in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI induces the expression of autoantibodies against GFAP and its breakdown products. GFAP protein levels increase in blood in response to TBI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Highly expressed in astrocytes and a constituent of blood. Autoantibodies against GFAP are induced by TBI.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate TBI biomarker; autoantibodies against GFAP are indicative of TBI.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, natural history study investigated Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) patients (mild, moderate, severe) and healthy controls, aiming to determine if extracellular vesicle (EV) concentrations of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light (NfL), measured 1 year post-injury, could distinguish patient groups and correlate with TBI severity or 1-year and long-term recovery outcomes (GOS-E). The study found that blood-derived EV GFAP and NfL concentrations were generally higher in TBI patients 1 year post-injury compared to controls, correlating with injury severity and poorer 1-year recovery outcomes, although EV GFAP also showed an association with long-term improvement. Attempts to quantify EV UCH-L1 and EV tau were unsuccessful due to insufficient data quality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and its long-term biomarker profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Biomarker measurements were performed 1 year after TBI, with patient groups classified by TBI severity (mild, moderate, severe). This was a natural history study, and no specific therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated in moderate (mean 54.1, SD 31.6, p < 0.001) and severe TBI (mean 66.7, SD 33.2, p < 0.001) compared to controls (mean 25.7, SD 15.5). Higher in severe TBI compared to mild TBI (mean 40.2, SD 24.3, p = 0.023). Mild TBI showed a non-significant trend for higher concentrations than controls (p = 0.054). Diagnostic utility (AUROC) for severe TBI vs controls: 0.88 (95% CI 0.74–1.0); moderate TBI vs controls: 0.86 (95% CI 0.74–0.97). Higher EV GFAP was associated with lower 1-year GOS-E (  = -0.644, p = 0.033) but also associated with long-term improvement in GOS-E (  = 0.604, p = 0.028).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Astrocytic cytoskeleton protein released after astrocytic cell death; an indicator of astrocytic cell impairment following TBI.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) ranging from mild to severe, assessed 1 year post-injury and up to 5 years post-injury for long-term outcomes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Discriminates TBI patients from controls and across TBI severities. Indicates TBI presence and is related to injury severity. Associated with worse 1-year clinical outcomes (lower GOS-E) but also with long-term improvement in GOS-E, suggesting its utility as a chronic biomarker for TBI and astrocytic impairment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported, this is a study protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An intermediate filament protein specific to astrocytes, released upon astrocyte activation or injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of astrocyte injury and disease activity in neuroinflammatory conditions, highlighted as an exploratory outcome for NMOSD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced in patients with MCI and AD in some studies, while others reported higher levels in AD patients. Levels significantly correlated with AD biomarkers, including Aβ42, IL-1β, and caspase-8. Plasma levels are altered by acute food intake.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Astrocytic biomarker associated with neuroinflammation in AD.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) diagnosis, neuroinflammation; measurements sensitive to acute food intake.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for distinguishing controls from MCI or AD, but with conflicting findings across studies for direction of change. Its measurement can be sensitive to acute food intake, highlighting the importance of pre-analytical controls.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes the IMPROVE trial, a four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating a novel home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training program (along with individual components and controls) on cognitive function, physical performance, mood, and quality of life in older (≥50) ICU survivors with delirium. The study aims to identify improvements and understand the underlying pathophysiology, hypothesizing beneficial changes in neurotrophic factors (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), and a reduction in inflammatory (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, CRP) and glial activation (S-100β, GFAP) biomarkers, as well as investigating AD-related markers like APOE genotype and Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training delivered via Internet-based videoconference. The study also investigates individual components (physical exercise only, cognitive training only) and control interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a four-arm randomized controlled trial. Active cognitive training involves facilitator-led online modules (Posit Science, Inc. Brain HQ) for 45 minutes, 2 days/week for 3 months. Active physical exercise is multi-modal, seated aerobic and progressive resistance training for 45 minutes, 3 times/week for 3 months, delivered via videoconference at moderate intensity (RPE 5-6 on a 10-point scale). Control groups receive matched frequency cognitive control modules and gentle seated stretching. This protocol does not report dose-response comparisons, focusing on comparisons between the four distinct intervention arms.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hypothesized decrease due to combined physical and cognitive training; specific quantitative data not reported as this is a study protocol describing intent to measure changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of glial dysfunction and astrocyte activation, indicating astrogliosis, central nervous system injury, neuroinflammation, and neurotoxicity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined physical exercise and cognitive training intervention in older ICU survivors with delirium-induced cognitive impairment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates brain injury, glial activation, and neuroinflammation; a hypothesized decrease suggests reduced astrocyte/microglial activation, improved brain structure, and may contribute to delaying Alzheimer disease/dementias. Higher levels are associated with increased delirium risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute blood protein levels of Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP), Ubiquitin C-terminal Hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1), Neurofilament Light Chain (NF-L), and tau in US military cadets after concussions incurred during combative training. It aimed to validate these biomarkers for concussion diagnosis and management in military settings, given the challenges of traditional symptom-based assessments for mild traumatic brain injury (TBI). The findings revealed significant acute increases in GFAP and UCH-L1, with GFAP showing more prolonged elevation and NF-L levels indicating persistent differences, suggesting ongoing axonal injury and potentially incomplete biological recovery despite symptom resolution. These patterns were largely consistent with those observed in sport-associated concussions, while tau levels showed no significant changes in this specific context.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Concussion sustained during combative training exercises
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concussions occurred during combative training exercises (e.g., boxing, self-defense, martial arts) among military service academy cadets. This multicenter prospective case-control study compared 67 concussed cadets to 36 matched contact-control cadets who participated in the same training but did not incur a concussion. Biomarker levels were assessed at baseline, acute postinjury (<6 hours), 24-48 hours postinjury, asymptomatic postinjury, and 7 days after return to activity. No specific dose or intensity of head impacts was quantified, and no dose-response comparisons for concussion severity were reported, as the 'dose' refers to the concussion event itself.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increases compared with baseline and contact-control group. Mean difference in natural log values was 0.34 (95% CI, 0.18-0.50; P < .001) at the acute postinjury point (<6 hours). Levels remained high at 24- to 48-hour postinjury (mean difference in ln values, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.06-0.38; P = .007) and asymptomatic postinjury points (mean difference in ln values, 0.21; 95% CI, 0.05-0.36; P = .01), indicating persistence for several days. Lower limit of quantification was 0.467 pg/mL.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Brain injury-associated protein, indicating underlying pathophysiological changes and longer-lasting increases after concussion and mild traumatic brain injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute concussion incurred during combative training among US military service academy cadets, with measurements taken at acute, 24-48 hours, and asymptomatic postinjury time points, showing persistent elevation for several days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential biomarker for concussion diagnosis, injury identification, and recovery assessment in military combative training, indicating acute brain injury. Its persistent elevation suggests incomplete biological recovery despite symptom resolution, potentially informing return-to-activity decisions. It is also associated with positive CT and MRI findings in mild TBIs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Serum, cerebral and transcerebral circulation (net exchange via arterial and internal jugular venous sampling)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked elevations (P < 0.05 vs. baseline) in net cerebral output (v > a). Output was more pronounced in normoxic normoventilation (NX) compared to hyperoxic hyperventilation (HX) (P < 0.05 vs. HX). More marked elevations in arterial concentrations during hyperoxic (HX) apnea. A relationship was observed between elevated PaCO2 and decreased GFAP gradient in HX (r = -0.638, P = 0.047). Peak concentrations were generally below pathologic thresholds.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intermediate filament protein predominantly expressed by astrocytes; indicator of astrocyte activation, damage, and general gliovascular reactivity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Maximal dry apnea and breath-hold diving (during apnea) under normoxic and hyperoxic conditions, particularly severe apneic hypoxemia-hypercapnia (NX condition) and elevated PaCO2 in HX apnea.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of blood-brain barrier permeability and glio-vascular damage; reflects increased neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, identifying hemodynamic stress and hypoxemia's contribution to BBB disruption. Indicates a rapid increase in BBB permeability, but peak concentrations were generally below traumatic brain injury thresholds.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study (cross-sectional analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional observational study utilizing baseline data from 129 community-dwelling cognitively healthy older adults (aged 65+) enrolled in the Age-Well trial. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered; the study focused on analyzing associations between naturally occurring biological markers and neuroimaging values.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (concentration, measured via SIMOA, log transformed for analysis)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A significant positive interaction between %CST and APOE4 status was observed (  = 0.225; P = 0.012), though this did not survive Bonferroni correction. In APOE4 carriers only, higher %CST tended to be associated with higher plasma GFAP level (P = 0.071).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Related to neurodegeneration and Alzheimer's disease (AD) physiopathology, serving as a marker for astrocyte activation and glial reactivity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline data collection and interaction with APOE4 status in cognitively healthy older adults.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neurodegeneration and AD physiopathology risk, astrocyte activation, potentially reflecting neuroinflammation and brain aging.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnosis of Sport-related Concussion (SRC) using proteomic profiling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from concussed and non-concussed collegiate athletes within 48 hours post-injury, with analyses conducted for acute (0-6 hours) and subacute (7-48 hours) phases. A highly multiplexed proteomic DNA aptamers assay targeting 1305 plasma proteins was used. The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Differentially abundant, confirming previous findings regarding plasma proteins in SRC. Recognized as a diagnostic marker for mTBI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of astroglial damage following mild traumatic brain injuries (mTBIs).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sports-Related Concussion (SRC) assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Recognized diagnostic marker for mTBI; potential candidate biomarker for concussion; used to determine necessity of CT scans.

document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevations in blood levels observed in military Service Members (SMs) with blast exposure. Not specifically quantified in the provided text; its increase represents a potential marker of astroglial injury.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Potential blood marker of astroglial injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blast exposure in military SMs during training events.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Facilitates identification of astroglial injury, elucidates pathophysiological mechanisms related to brain trauma, and serves as a potential biomarker for brain injury assessment and risk stratification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol details a prospective observational longitudinal study to develop and validate the Imperial Comprehensive Cognitive Assessment in Cerebrovascular Disease (IC3), a novel digital tool for detecting post-stroke cognitive deficits. The study aims to recruit 300 acute stroke patients and longitudinally investigate the relationship between cognition, psychosocial status, MRI brain imaging, and various blood biomarkers (including NFL, GFAP, brain-derived tau, phosphorylated tau forms, Aβ42/40 ratio, apolipoprotein E genotype, and polygenic risk scores) over 12 months post-ictus. The overarching goal is to identify reliable multimodal recovery indicators, patients at risk of progressive cognitive decline, and facilitate personalized therapy allocation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational longitudinal study for post-stroke cognitive impairment monitoring, biomarker identification, and validation of a novel digital cognitive assessment tool (IC3).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a 12-month longitudinal observational design involving repeated measures collected at baseline (0-15 days post-stroke), 3, 6, and 12 months post-ictus. It includes a digital cognitive assessment (IC3) comprising 22 tasks, lasting 60-70 minutes, administered via web-browser. Blood samples are collected from 200 patients and MRI imaging from 300 patients (at 3 and 12 months), along with 50 age-matched controls. No therapeutic dose comparisons are reported as it is an observational and diagnostic tool development protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Aimed to be characterized over the first year after stroke; specific direction not yet reported as it describes a study design.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aimed to be quantified over the first year after stroke and related to MRI measures and cognitive/functional outcomes; not yet reported as it describes a study design.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker and indicator of astrocytic activation and neuroaxonal injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-stroke cognitive outcome and recovery trajectory over the first year after stroke; after acute stroke; post-stroke period.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Aimed to identify novel biomarkers associated with poststroke cognitive outcome and recovery trajectory, and as an indicator of astrocytic activation and neuroaxonal injury; will be analyzed to describe dynamics after acute stroke and its relationship with continuous outcome measures like cognitive scores at 1 year; expected to yield novel findings concerning its role in determining cognitive outcomes post-stroke.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to characterize circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) in the plasma of patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) compared to healthy controls. Key findings include significantly higher plasma NfL and GFAP in RRMS patients, with GFAP also elevated in NMOSD patients. RRMS patients exhibited lower EV density and increased mean EV size compared to controls, with larger EVs (>150nm) primarily contributing to this. Furthermore, specific EV surface markers (CD29, CD31, CD40, CD44, CD49c, CD69) showed changes in RRMS patients, notably correlating negatively with NfL/GFAP levels and positively with time since the last relapse, suggesting their potential as biomarkers for disease stabilization and reduced immune cell activity, independent of current treatments.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing biomarkers in patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD) undergoing existing pharmacological treatments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 96 participants (52 RRMS, 19 NMOSD, 10 MOGAD, 15 healthy controls). RRMS patients received natalizumab (n=33), dimethylfumarate/glatiramer acetate (n=12), or no treatment (n=7). NMOSD patients were treated with rituximab, and MOGAD patients had various heterogeneous treatments. While existing treatments were noted, no specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated by the study itself. Biomarker measurements were performed using SIMOA, SP-IRIS, cryo-EM, Western blotting, NTA, and multiplex flow cytometry. The study concluded that current treatments did not significantly influence the observed EV marker levels or composition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) than in healthy controls (HCs) (Figure 2, A and B), suggesting gliosis. A significant increase in NMOSD compared with HCs (Figure 2B) indicates astrocytopathy. No significant difference for GFAP z-score between RRMS, NMOSD, and MOGAD groups (Figure 2A). Preliminary GFAP z-scores were adjusted for age and sex based on a large reference database.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intermediate filament protein in astrocytes, released into circulation after astrogliosis (astrocytic damage/injury response) in the CNS.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Astrocytic injury/response and disease activity in the CNS of patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) and Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), but not Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered a potential surrogate biomarker of astrogliosis and disease activity in demyelinating diseases of the CNS, indicating gliosis in RRMS and astrocytopathy in NMOSD. Useful for following disease activity and linked to a negative correlation with certain EV markers in RRMS, suggesting an association with low disease activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantified with a customized Neurology 4-plex A platform. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intermediate filament protein found in astrocytes, indicating astrocyte activation and neuroinflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Plasma AD biomarker analysis in study populations 2 and 3.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential blood-based biomarker for neuroinflammation and astrogliosis in AD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study, part of the Concussion Assessment, Research, and Education (CARE) Consortium, investigated the utility of plasma biomarkers (total tau, GFAP, and Nf-L) for predicting return-to-sport (RTS) duration following sport-related concussion (SRC) in collegiate athletes. It aimed to differentiate athletes returning to sport in less than 14 days versus 14 days or more post-injury. The findings indicated that higher total tau concentrations at 24-48 hours post-injury and at symptom resolution, and lower GFAP concentrations acutely post-injury, were associated with a protracted RTS (>=14 days). Nf-L was not significantly associated with RTS duration in this cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery and return-to-sport (RTS) trajectories.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 127 NCAA collegiate athletes who sustained an SRC. Plasma biomarker levels (total tau, GFAP, Nf-L) were measured at baseline, 0-21 hours, 24-48 hours post-injury, and at the time of symptom resolution. The study compared biomarker concentrations between athletes who returned to sport in less than 14 days versus those who took 14 days or more; no therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in athletes with protracted Return-to-Sport (RTS) (>=14 days) compared to those with shorter RTS (<14 days).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Acutely post-injury, mean plasma GFAP was 4.72 [0.12] pg/mL for the <14 days RTS group vs 4.39 [0.11] pg/mL for the >=14 days RTS group (P = .04). This implies lower GFAP in the longer RTS group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Released from astrocytes; an indicator of brain injury, potentially glial activation, commonly associated with more severe gradients of injury in mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acutely post-Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery monitoring in collegiate athletes, specifically comparing return to sport duration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with RTS duration; lower levels were counterintuitively associated with protracted RTS in this cohort compared to prior mTBI studies, suggesting complex release kinetics or different injury characteristics in SRC. Its individual discriminatory power was not significant.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Apnea generally increased gCBF. Relative increase was greater in hyperoxic (HX) (206 ± 52%) vs. normoxic (NX) (83 ± 22%) due to consistently lower perfusion at baseline in HX.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Perfusion of the brain, delivering oxygen and nutrients.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Apnea (Normoxic and Hyperoxic).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Compensatory elevation in cerebral blood flow during severe asphyxia, secondary to hypercapnia/hypoxemia-induced pial artery dilation and severe arterial hypertension.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic modifier investigation; Observational longitudinal study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is observational and investigates an intrinsic genetic factor, not an active therapeutic intervention. The 'dose' refers to the additive effects of the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage (0, 1, or 2 G alleles), which was modeled as a continuous variable. The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). No deviations from an additive effect were observed (heterozygosity indicator P > 0.05), and no traditional dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In GRN symptomatic carriers: better global cognitive performance at baseline (β per G allele: 2.16, 95% CI: 2.27, 5.61, corrected P: 2.59 × 10^-5). In C9orf72 symptomatic group longitudinally: stronger protective effect on overall cognitive functions. No effects on global cognitive measures were observed in MAPT carriers. The rs1990622 A allele was associated with greater decline in MMSE score (β = 0.969, P = 0.001 in FTD; β = 0.123, P = 0.019 in Parkinson’s disease).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects overall mental abilities including thinking, reasoning, memory, and problem-solving, indicative of brain health and neuronal integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT mutations) in presymptomatic and symptomatic carriers, modified by TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates cognitive and behavioral health; better scores or maintained function suggest a protective effect against FTD progression, improved functional outcomes, and better cognitive preservation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study (cross-sectional analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional observational study utilizing baseline data from 129 community-dwelling cognitively healthy older adults (aged 65+) enrolled in the Age-Well trial. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered; the study focused on analyzing associations between naturally occurring biological markers and neuroimaging values.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain White Matter (global, frontal, and temporal regions)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Structural neuroimaging (Kurtosis Fractional Anisotropy from DKI MRI)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower (  = -.230; P = .010) in association with higher %CST, particularly in frontal and temporal regions. Result survived Bonferroni correction.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects microstructural complexity and integrity of white matter, indicating axonal organization and myelination.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with higher %CST levels in cognitively healthy older adults.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered white matter microstructure, potentially related to age-related changes or early neurodegenerative processes, and compromised white matter integrity linked to neurodegeneration or AD physiopathology.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

Treatment with CD133+ or CD133- cells significantly reduced FITC-sinistrin t1/2 by day 7 (improving GFR), to a similar degree between cell groups, compared to cisplatin-injured controls. While improved, renal function was not fully restored to baseline by day 14. Cisplatin typically causes a 20-40% reduction in GFR.
