matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured during fasting, pre-warm-up, post-cycling Time Trial (TT), and during recovery following nutritional intervention and exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic status and energy availability; unchanged levels suggest no direct impact on these parameters by the intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for the body's cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of current blood sugar levels, relevant for diabetes and metabolic stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Exercise-induced changes are being investigated (in current study protocol).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes from baseline will be collected and analyzed; measured via Contour®Next EZ blood glucose monitor at rest, 5 min into treadmill test, every 2-3 min until exhaustion, and 3 min after test completion.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells, regulated by metabolic processes and fuel use patterns during exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week probiotic intervention during endurance treadmill test; collected during V̇O2 max and time-to-exhaustion tests.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects metabolic response to exercise and energy status, influencing running performance and fuel use patterns during running.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative literature review investigates biosensor approaches for continuous, real-time in vivo monitoring of molecular markers relevant to performance and health status. It highlights the limitations of current technologies and proposes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors as a generalizable, minimally invasive solution. The review details the development, validation, and attributes (generalizability, selectivity, reversibility, stability) of EAB sensors for detecting diverse targets (drugs, metabolites, hormones, proteins) in complex biological fluids and tissues. It also addresses the technological hurdles for subcutaneous placement, the correlation between interstitial fluid and systemic concentrations, and their potential for monitoring stress indicators (e.g., cortisol) and HPA/HPG axis hormones to assess overtraining syndromes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) Sensor Technology for Real-time In Vivo Molecular Monitoring
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This narrative literature review discusses the development and application of Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) sensors for continuous, real-time in vivo molecular monitoring, without an applied 'dose' in the traditional sense as it is a review of technology. EAB sensors, including 75-µm-diameter, 3-mm-long versions, have been tested in live rats for plasma monitoring (jugular vein) for up to 12 hours with few-second to sub-second resolution and clinically relevant precision. They are also adapted for minimally invasive subcutaneous placements (microneedles, indwelling needles) for interstitial fluid monitoring (e.g., brain, tumor, dermal ISF). The review highlights the importance of seconds-resolved time resolution and nanomolar limits of detection for hormones (achieved for LH and NGAL, micromolar for others). Time delays between subcutaneous ISF and plasma concentrations (e.g., 5-12 min for glucose, ~17 min for vancomycin) and correlations (strong for cortisol, <6% error for glucose) are noted, influenced by target properties. No dose-response comparisons for sensor parameters or monitoring duration were explicitly reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Levels in subcutaneous ISF parallel plasma levels with a time delay.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Subcutaneous glucose levels parallel plasma glucose levels with a time delay of 5 to 12 min and an error of less than 6%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Energy metabolism regulation; primary energy source for the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Continuous glucose monitoring; comparison between subcutaneous ISF and plasma levels; general health and performance monitoring.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of health and performance status; commercially available sensor for continuous monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-week oral garlic supplementation on 40-km cycling time trial performance, whole-body energy metabolism, exercise-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in healthy adult males. Findings indicate that garlic supplementation significantly enhanced total antioxidant capacity and attenuated oxidative stress (MDA), inflammatory response (TNF-α), and some markers of muscle damage (LDH and UA at specific time points), but it did not improve cycling performance or overall whole-body energy metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral garlic extract supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 1000 mg/day for 4 weeks (28 consecutive days) in a single-blind crossover design. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as a single dose was used.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences observed between garlic and placebo trials (p > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cellular metabolism and a blood energy biomarker for exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 4-wk garlic supplementation during a 40-km cycling challenge
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used to assess energy metabolism and substrate utilization during exercise; garlic supplementation had no observed effect.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed predictive models using a novel machine learning pipeline to identify viable intrauterine pregnancies (Live Normally Sited Pregnancies, LNSP) in symptomatic women, differentiating them from combined adverse outcomes (CAO) such as miscarriage, pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). The models integrate serum metabolite levels (untargeted 1H NMR profiling) with plasma hormone concentrations (β-hCG and progesterone) and clinicodemographic data, finding that a composite biomarker provides superior predictive accuracy (0.79). The aim is to offer a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic test to reduce diagnostic burden and improve outcomes in early gestation by accurately identifying LNSP and excluding conditions associated with maternal morbidity and mortality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker identification and predictive model development using machine learning, untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, and hormone assays.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 370 symptomatic pregnant women (≤10 weeks gestation), presenting with abdominal pain and/or vaginal bleeding. A single blood sample was collected upon first emergency presentation; plasma was used for β-hCG and progesterone concentration measurements, and serum for untargeted metabolomic profiling. Nine key metabolite signals were identified. Random forest models were constructed and compared: a model using metabolite signals alone yielded 0.68 accuracy, β-hCG and progesterone alone yielded 0.71 accuracy, and the combined model achieved the best predictive accuracy of 0.79. Model performance was assessed using an independent validation cohort. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic accuracy for pregnancy outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: While identified as significantly perturbed in tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP) versus live normally-sited pregnancy (LNSP) in a previous study, it was not significantly different in the cohort examined in this study between tEP and LNSP controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolite, the primary energy source for cellular processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP) and live normally-sited pregnancy (LNSP) controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not validated as a differentiating biomarker in this specific cohort, despite conflicting findings from previous research.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and optimized a portable, economical, and sensitive biosensor for rapid thrombin activity detection, leveraging a blood coagulation-inspired fibrin hydrogel system with a personal glucometer readout; the principle involves thrombin-mediated fibrinogen cleavage and invertase immobilization, and the method's analytical performance, selectivity, and reliability in serum samples were thoroughly evaluated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Development and optimization of a portable biosensor and in vitro enzymatic assay for thrombin activity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The biosensor was optimized for thrombin detection, achieving a linear range of 0–0.8 U/mL with an LOD of 0.04 U/mL. Optimal conditions included a fibrinogen concentration of 10.0 mg/mL, thrombin-fibrinogen incubation for 5.0 min, invertase concentration of 1.0 mg/mL, sucrose concentration of 7.5 mg/mL, and invertase-sucrose incubation for 5.0 min at an enzymatic reaction temperature of 40–50 °C. Recovery rates in serum samples ranged from 92.8% to 107.7%, and repeatability was 7.0% RSD. The study focused on diagnostic method development, so no therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: As thrombin activity increases, the amount of glucose produced by sucrose hydrolysis decreases, leading to a decreased glucometer readout (P sample). The change in readout (ΔP = P blank - P sample) is calculated.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A monosaccharide sugar, produced by the hydrolysis of sucrose by invertase.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: The terminal detectable product in the biosensor assay, providing the quantitative signal readout for the personal glucometer, inversely indicating thrombin activity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The direct measurable output signal of the assay, serving as the quantitative indicator of thrombin activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly different between SBMA and controls (P_adj < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Adult male patients with SBMA compared to age-matched healthy controls (NIH cohort).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General health indicator; differences linked to SBMA may suggest metabolic alterations associated with the disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) for COVID-19 (AUC=0.91). Higher levels positively correlated with longer hospital stay (p=0.043) in COVID-19 patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source, involved in energy metabolism and associated with glycerolipid metabolism and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 diagnosis and duration of hospital stay.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A key diagnostic biomarker for COVID-19 and associated with longer hospitalization and severe COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes a multi-round Delphi expert consensus process to identify and prioritize 14 key biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies. The identified biomarkers encompass physiological, inflammatory, functional, and genetic/epigenetic domains. The study outlines the methodology, discusses the suitability of biomarkers for different intervention durations, and identifies future research needs regarding biomarker standardization and early life application, concluding with a preference for composite biomarkers due to the complexity of aging.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Expert consensus methodology (Delphi method) for identifying biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies (nutritional, lifestyle, or pharmacological).
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study utilized a 3-round online Delphi method, starting with 116 experts in Round 1 and concluding with 60 experts in Round 3, out of 460 invited international panel members. Consensus for statements was defined as ">=70%" agreement, with "51-69%" indicating moderate agreement and "

	<=50%" leading to removal. Initially, 460 biomarkers were suggested, leading to 20 being appraised in detail. The consensus level for the 14 recommended biomarkers ranged from 70% to 98%. The identified biomarkers were deemed more suitable for medium- (3-6 months) and long-term (">=6 months") interventions, and less suitable for acute or short-term ("<3 months") interventions, as short-term changes are likely homeostatic responses with limited long-term significance for aging. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were investigated as this was a consensus-building study on biomarker utility.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Achieved "

	<=50%" agreement in expert panel consensus.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells, serving as a physiological marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Considered for assessment of the aging process.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic health and diabetes risk, but deemed less specific for aging by the expert panel.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly (acute rise) by 35-50% above initial concentrations during matches, due to liver glucose output exceeding systemic uptake.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cellular metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (during matches, triggered by acute exercise).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased energy demand during exercise, with the body mobilizing glucose to meet these demands, demonstrating a classic glycemic response to exercise and the high-intensity nature of a BVb competition day.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not explicitly reported as a change; its baseline level served as a variable in machine learning models.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Specific quantitative data or changes were not reported in the provided chunks; it was included as a blood-based biomarker in predictive models for depressive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells and central to carbohydrate metabolism and blood sugar regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used as a baseline blood-based biomarker in secondary analysis of EUFEST and RAISE-ETP trials, collected from patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, for inclusion in machine learning models predicting depressive symptoms and episodes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General indicator of metabolic health; used as a variable to evaluate its contribution to predicting depressive symptoms or post-psychotic depressive episodes in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells, crucial for metabolic function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CD administration in mice following resistance exercise, facilitating recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased concentrations suggest improved energy availability, beneficial for sustained performance and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes the development, optimization, and validation of a portable, low-cost, and 3D-printed electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor capable of simultaneously detecting glucose and lactate in real serum. The biosensor integrates interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) within a bipolar electrochemical system and leverages a smartphone-based readout, demonstrating high sensitivity, reproducibility, and accuracy within physiologically relevant ranges, thereby offering a scalable and field-deployable solution for point-of-care metabolic monitoring and biomedical diagnostics.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Development, fabrication, optimization, and validation of a 3D-printed electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor for diagnostic purposes.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The biosensor was fabricated using dual-extrusion FDM 3D printing (0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer height, 40 mm/s printing speed, 220 °C nozzle, 60 °C heated bed, 100% infill) and featured six pairs of interdigitated electrodes. Operational parameters were optimized for voltage (3-10 V, with signal saturation observed beyond optimal), luminol concentration (4 mM), pH, and enzyme concentrations (glucose oxidase at 10 mg/mL, lactate oxidase at 50 U/mL, with 90-120 s incubation). This optimization led to detection limits of 0.1 mM for glucose (linear range 0.1-5.0 mM) and 80 µM for lactate (linear range 0.1-4.0 mM), with real serum recovery rates of 95–102%. Interdigitated electrodes provided approximately a 2.5-fold increase in luminescence signal compared to planar electrodes. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported as the study focused on diagnostic device performance.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Real human serum and target analyte solutions (for biosensor characterization).
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: ECL Signal Intensity Measurement (Enzyme-coupled Electrochemical Luminescence Biosensing for concentration detection/monitoring).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ECL signal intensity is directly proportional to glucose concentration, quantified in Relative Light Units (RLU) and measured via smartphone camera. The sensor exhibited a detection limit of 0.1 mM, a linear range from 0.1 mM to 5.0 mM, and 95-102% recovery rates in real serum. In human serum, it measured 4.55 mM compared to 4.70 mM by a clinical method (96.80% accuracy), demonstrating reproducible and reliable quantification across varying concentrations.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cells, central to carbohydrate metabolism, and an indicator of metabolic status and physiological stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Real-time monitoring for chronic diseases, sepsis, trauma, and physiological stress scenarios, validated through the development and characterization of a 3D-printed, smartphone-integrated ECL biosensor in analyte solutions and human serum.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Critical for assessing metabolic status, detecting physiological stress, and diagnosing systemic complications, providing sensitive, rapid, and reliable quantification for real-time medical diagnostics and monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not significantly change during either EXE or EXO trials.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for cellular function and metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Heat stress (EXE and EXO trials) induced by core temperature increases, with samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments up to 39°C and subsequent decrease until 37.5°C.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable glucose homeostasis despite thermal challenge.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change before (rest), during, or after (recovery) the entire CCombat protocol. Post-CCombat glucose showed a positive correlation with post-CCombat lactate (r s 0.52) and a negative correlation with post-CCombat urea (r s -0.50).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source, involved in energetic metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Before, during, and after the CCombat exercise protocol (up to 96 hours).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable energy substrate availability and adequate metabolic balance during CCombat training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar at baseline between groups, and no significant changes were reported over time or between groups during the supplementation period (non-fasted >11 mmol/L was an exclusion criterion).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized discovery metabolomics and lipidomics to investigate plasma glycosphingolipids and other lipid metabolites as potential biomarkers for distinguishing aggressive from indolent prostate cancer (PCa) in treatment-naïve African-American and European-American men. The findings indicate that specific glycosphingolipid species, particularly trihexosylceramide and tetrahexosylceramide, along with other sphingolipids and triglycerides, are significantly associated with PCa aggressiveness. A five-sphingolipid signature demonstrated promising diagnostic accuracy comparable to or exceeding PSA, suggesting their utility as novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and highlighting their role in related metabolic networks and genetic alterations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated plasma glycoprotein non-metastatic melanoma protein B (gpNMB) and glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) concentrations in a cohort of patients with Gaucher disease (GD1, GD3, GD1-PD), idiopathic Parkinson's disease (IPD), and GBA heterozygous PD, alongside healthy controls. The primary aim was to explore gpNMB's relationship to Gaucher disease severity, clinical phenotypes (neurological, pulmonary, liver disease, monoclonal gammopathy), and treatment status. Findings revealed significantly elevated plasma gpNMB levels in Gaucher disease patients compared to controls (mean: 200.9 vs. 35.1 ng/ml), which remained high even after prolonged enzyme replacement therapy. Higher gpNMB concentrations were notably associated with splenectomy, pulmonary disease, liver disease (including fibrosis and cirrhosis), and monoclonal gammopathy. Additionally, gpNMB levels were elevated in Parkinsonism patients with type 1 GD compared to GBA1 heterozygotes or IPD (p=0.0001). The study also highlighted gpNMB's good diagnostic performance for GD (AUC 0.894), and its significant positive correlations with other established GD biomarkers (GlcSph, Chitotriosidase, CCL18, ACE), suggesting its potential as a supportive biomarker for residual disease activity, disease complications, and clinical stratification, although it does not differentiate between neuronopathic GD subtypes or idiopathic PD. The study also reviewed other diagnostic markers like acid β-glucosidase activity and GBA1 mutation analysis, noting their utility and limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) and Substrate Reduction Therapy (SRT), including macrophage-targeted enzyme therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients received ERT or SRT for varying durations: mean 14.6 ± 6.9 years (range: 1–29 years) for ERT, and 10.1 ± 7.5 years (range: 6 months–23 years) for SRT. Plasma gpNMB concentrations showed an inverse correlation with treatment duration during the first 5 years of specific therapy (rho= -0.470, p= 0.024) but no correlation after 10 years. gpNMB levels remained elevated in GD1 patients on ERT for over 5 years, and no statistical difference was observed between treated GD1 and GD3 patients. Glucosylsphingosine concentrations declined with ERT or SRT. No explicit dose-response comparisons for ERT or SRT were reported, though it was noted that therapeutic response may vary across Gaucher disease subtypes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated by more than 200-fold on average in untreated GD1 patients compared with healthy controls. Declines after institution of ERT or SRT. Statistically significant positive correlation with plasma gpNMB concentrations (rho = 0.584, p < 0.001).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the molecular relevance of GBA1 pathogenic variants (N370S and L444P) in Gaucher disease (GD) patients (GD1, GD3) on Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT), GBA1 carriers, and healthy subjects by analyzing glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb1), α-synuclein mRNA, total protein, and oligomer levels. Key findings included significantly elevated Lyso-Gb1 levels in GD patients and neuronopathic GD, substantially higher α-synuclein mRNA levels in GD3 patients and L444P carriers, but no statistically significant differences in total α-SNCA protein or oligomer levels between groups after multiple comparison adjustment. The research also explored correlations with disease severity, GBA1 variants, aging, and ERT impact, suggesting links to Parkinson's disease risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients (65 total: 47 GD1, 18 GD3) were treated with ERT. Doses varied, generally ranging from 15–60 U/kg, with an average of 30 U/kg bm/every other week. While Lyso-Gb1 showed a varied correlation with ERT dosing (the coefficient of determination (R2) for treatment response dropped to 0.16 for high doses >35 U/kg bm/every other week), no consistent dose-response comparisons were reported for all analyzed markers. Blood samples were collected during annual clinical follow-up visits.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In GD patients, plasma concentrations were markedly increased above the cut-off level (12–14 ng/mL), with all GD patients having levels above this threshold (GD1 median 71.5 ng/mL, GD3 median 64.6 ng/mL; p > 0.05 for GD1 vs GD3). This was significantly higher than GBA1 variant carriers (median 7.51 ng/mL, p < 10^-9) and healthy controls (8.49 ng/mL, p < 10^-8). Elevated levels were observed in one healthy subject and seven GBA1 carriers. GD patients homozygous for L444P had higher levels (median, 184.5 ng/mL) than N370S (median, 143.1 ng/mL). Brain levels were 22–51 times higher in GD3 and 38–694 times higher in GD2 compared to healthy individuals, while GD1 brain levels were within the normal range. The biomarker correlates with disease severity and its correlation with ERT treatment response varied, with R2 dropping to 0.16 for high doses (>35 U/kg bm/every other week). Correlation with age was also reported in supplementary materials.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Deacylated form of glucosylceramide (Gb1) that accumulates due to β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) enzyme deficiency in Gaucher disease. It is a diagnostic marker for GD, reflects disease severity, and is useful for treatment monitoring. It directly interacts with and stabilizes α-synuclein oligomers in the lysosomal compartment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Gaucher disease (GD, including GD1, GD2, GD3) patients, GBA1 pathogenic variant carriers (L444P, N370S, and unknown variants), and healthy controls, in the context of Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) and correlation with age.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Most reliable biomarker for GD diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Elevated levels indicate GD presence, reflect disease severity, and may contribute to neuronopathic GD neurological manifestations. It is a potential factor in α-synuclein accumulation and is linked to Parkinson's disease development, correlating with elevated α-synuclein levels in neurons and promoting α-SNCA oligomer formation.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the intricate short- and long-term dynamics of glucosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb1) in Gaucher Disease (GD) patients undergoing Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT), combining an eight-year longitudinal study with an analysis of immediate post-infusion effects. It found a rapid and significant short-term reduction in lyso-Gb1 levels post-ERT infusion (average 17% decrease), reaffirming ERT's immediate efficacy. However, long-term (up to 8 years) analysis revealed statistically insignificant year-to-year variability but high individual variability, especially between GD type 1 and type 3 patients, suggesting biomarker instability between infusions and highlighting limitations for its use as a consistent long-term indicator of disease severity or treatment outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: ERT involved biweekly (every other week) administration of imiglucerase (Cerezyme®) or velaglucerase alfa (VPRIV®), with typical doses of 30 U/kg/EOW for type 1 Gaucher Disease (GD1) and 60 U/kg/EOW for type 3 Gaucher Disease (GD3). Short-term effects were observed by measuring biomarker levels immediately before and 30 minutes after infusion. Long-term observations spanned up to 8 years within this study, though patients generally received ERT for a minimum of 15 to a maximum of 28 years. No specific dose-response comparisons or modifications accounting for long-term variability were reported within the study's findings.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower acutely post-ERT infusion; largely stable/fluctuating but statistically unchanged over long-term annual monitoring, with high individual variability.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Short-term (30 minutes post-infusion): average decrease of 17% (p < 0.0001). Long-term (up to 8 years): statistically insignificant year-to-year variability (p > 0.05 for paired t-test after correction), but high individual variability. Coefficients of variation were 34% for GD type 1 patients and 23% for GD type 3 patients (p = 0.0003), indicating lower long-term variability in GD3.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolic marker indicating substrate accumulation in Gaucher disease pathology due to β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) deficiency. It is a product of glucosylceramide (Gb1) deacylation, reflecting an imbalance in sphingolipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Gaucher Disease (GD) management in patients undergoing Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT), specifically examining immediate responses (30 minutes post-infusion) and long-term dynamics (up to 8 years) during stable therapy for GD type 1 and type 3 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Traditionally used as an indicator of β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) deficiency, disease severity, and Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) treatment response. Its rapid acute reduction (17% within 30 minutes) indicates immediate ERT efficacy in reducing substrate accumulation. However, the study highlights that while GD type 3 patients exhibit less long-term variability than GD type 1 patients, the biomarker's overall instability between infusions, high individual variability, and lack of consistent long-term correlation with GD severity or treatment outcomes challenge its role and suggest a need for refinement in clinical application, especially considering limitations of Dried Blood Spot (DBS) testing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to establish comprehensive reference intervals for novel circulating biomarkers of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and hepatic regeneration in healthy human volunteers. It investigated intra- and interindividual variability, as well as diurnal variation, to provide robust data for interpreting exploratory clinical DILI studies and assisting biomarker qualification by regulatory authorities.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study for establishing reference intervals of circulating biomarkers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved serum sample collection from 227 healthy volunteers in a cross-sectional study (single sample). Additionally, 25 subjects underwent weekly serial sampling over 3 weeks, and 23 subjects had intensive 24-hour blood sampling every 3 hours after a 10-h overnight fast and standardized meals. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved, as the focus was on establishing reference intervals and assessing natural variability in healthy subjects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reference intervals established; levels significantly influenced by BMI; lower intra- and interindividual variability compared to previous reports; no significant diurnal impact.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference intervals based on the 97.5% quantile (90% CI). BMI was identified as a significant fixed effect from linear modelling. Intra-individual variability found to be non-significant, and no significant diurnal variation. No significant intra- or interindividual variation across the study, in contrast to previously reported problems.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enriched in the liver, acting as a mechanism-based biomarker of liver injury and regeneration; indicator of mitochondrial dysfunction; potential liver-specific alternative to ALT.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Establishing healthy reference intervals in human volunteers, assessing intra- and interindividual variability and diurnal variation, and identifying the effect of BMI on serum levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential to improve DILI prediction and hepatic regeneration assessment. Reference intervals should account for BMI to reduce variability and improve interpretation, especially due to visceral fat influencing liver function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the tissue origins of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in healthy mice using tissue-specific knockout models and its utility as a biomarker following paracetamol (APAP) overdose in both mice and humans. It found that cfDNA predominantly originates from blood cell lineages in healthy mice. Following APAP overdose, total and hepatocyte-derived cfDNA, as well as ALT and AST levels, significantly increased in mice (peaking at 8 hours), while albumin and bilirubin remained unaffected. In human APAP overdose patients, total cfDNA and liver-specific cfDNA (via methylation analysis) also significantly increased, especially in those with biochemical evidence of liver injury, demonstrating cfDNA's potential as a clinical biomarker for distinguishing overdose patients, assessing liver injury severity, and monitoring treatment efficacy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Paracetamol (APAP) Overdose; N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mice received intraperitoneal (IP) APAP at 350 mg/kg body weight, with samples collected at 8, 24, and 48 hours post-dosing (optimal cfDNA peak at 8 hours, liver damage most severe at 24 hours). Human patients presented with APAP overdose, with a subset receiving N-acetylcysteine (NAC) at 500-900 mg/kg body weight 20-40 hours after initial overdose. Patient groups were stratified by liver injury severity (normal vs. raised ALT); no specific APAP dose comparisons were performed in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all human APAP overdose patients (including those with normal ALT); correlated with total cfDNA (Spearman correlation 0.85, p-value < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme indicating mitochondrial damage, involved in glutamate metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: APAP overdose in human patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Novel APAP overdose biomarker measuring mitochondrial damage. Increased GLDH in patients with normal ALT suggests the damage may originate from tissues other than the liver.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Anserine significantly affected GPT (p < 0.05, main treatment effects), with ANS-HD inducing slight but significant elevations (p < 0.05) compared to ANS-LD or PLA. GPT levels remained within the normal range (~10–40 U/L), with 'transient increased GPT levels' noted.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell damage biomarker, particularly associated with liver or muscle damage; enzyme released into blood upon cellular damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-dose anserine supplementation following an exercise challenge (time to exhaustion).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevations suggest anserine (at high dose) might be associated with an augmented exercise-induced adaptive response and recovery, rather than detrimental damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Primary kidney cancer tumor samples (TCGA data); VHL-deficient and isogenic VHL-restored RCC4 cell lines, inferred from tumour genomic data and cell line shRNA data
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Amplification (Copy Number Alteration), Gene Expression Level, Cell Viability Reduction (upon siRNA targeting), Gene identified as a synthetic lethal partner

measured_effect.direction_of_change: selectively amplified in presence of VHL mutation; increased expression with amplification; differentially overexpressed in VHL-mutant kidney cancer; significant reduction in cell viability upon targeting with siRNAs
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: GLS was selectively amplified only in the presence of the VHL mutation (HI-HI Boolean implication). GLS amplification resulted in increased expression of GLS. GLS was differentially overexpressed in VHL-mutant compared to VHL-wild-type kidney cancer. Targeting GLS with siRNAs showed a significant reduction in cell viability in VHL-deficient RCC4 cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Functions in the glutaminase pathway, crucial for cell metabolism and growth, forms a synthetic lethal interaction with VHL mutation, and is involved in metabolic processes (glutaminolysis).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: VHL mutation in kidney cancer, identified as a candidate SL partner via MiSL amplification pipeline, and experimentally validated.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Constitutes a previously known mutation-specific Synthetic Lethal partner for VHL mutation in kidney cancer, suggesting that targeting GLS with siRNAs could be a therapeutic strategy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased (no specific quantification).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Amino acid, part of patterns indicating fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Athletes; associated with fatigue and suboptimal training capacity; monitoring resting amino acids across a season.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with fatigue and suboptimal training capacity; may serve as biomarker of muscle quality/status.

The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated a chemically defined, serum-free protocol for the in vitro transdifferentiation of pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells into functional hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) over five days. The research examined morphological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional changes, concluding that successful transdifferentiation, facilitated by extracellular matrix proteins like fibronectin or laminin, is independent of serum.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro pancreatic progenitor cell transdifferentiation to hepatocyte-like cells
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Clonal pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells were cultured for five days in a differentiation medium containing 100 nM Dexamethasone, 10 ng/ml Oncostatin M, 20 ng/ml HGF, 20 ng/ml FGF-2, 1% ITS+ (insulin, transferrin, selenous acid), 0.2% BSA, 4.4 mM nicotinamide, 1 µM copper sulphate, 30 µg/ml ascorbic acid, and 1 µg/ml heparin. Cells were grown on uncoated plastic, laminin-coated (2 µg/cm2), or fibronectin-coated (5 µg/cm2) substrata, with or without 5% FBS supplementation. The study primarily focused on the effectiveness of serum-free conditions facilitated by ECM proteins, rather than dose-response comparisons for individual components, finding no significant difference in transdifferentiation potential between fibronectin and laminin substrata.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Undifferentiated cells were uniformly GS-negative. GS was expressed in a proportion of cells in all experimental groups cultured under hepatocyte differentiation conditions.
