document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of consuming cow's milk versus an energy-matched carbohydrate solution on recovery markers and performance in twenty female team-sport athletes following repeated simulated team games (STGs). The findings indicated that 500 mL of milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function (peak torque for knee extension and flexion), sprint performance (5m and 10m), and perceptions of stress, and helped reduce muscle soreness and tiredness, particularly after the first STG. However, for many other physiological and performance markers (e.g., CK, hsCRP, LOOHs, PCs, CMJ, HR, RPE), the effects were mostly unclear or trivial, with milk showing no clear benefit after the second STG.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional intervention (consumption of cow's milk vs. an energy-matched carbohydrate solution) combined with a multi-stage physical activity protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 500 mL of either cow's milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g protein, 25.5 g carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat) or an energy-matched carbohydrate solution (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 53.6 g carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat) immediately following each of two simulated team games (STG1 and STG2). The 17 g protein from milk was noted to be below the recommended 20 g threshold for maximal protein synthesis stimulation. The exercise protocol involved two ~30 minute halves of intermittent running with sprints, agility, and jumps, separated by a 10-minute half-time, with a 48-hour recovery period between STG1 and STG2. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the nutritional interventions.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: trivial for MILK (within-group); likely lower for CHO (within-group); trivial (between-group)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Trivial effects were seen for HR within-group (STG1 to STG2) for MILK. HR was likely lower in STG2 for CHO (within-group). Between-group comparison of HR for MILK vs. CHO showed a trivial outcome.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular activity and physiological response to exercise or stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Within-group changes from STG1 to STG2 for both MILK and CHO, and between-group comparison of MILK vs. CHO.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of physiological strain, exercise intensity, or recovery status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported in this document chunk. Intended to measure change.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Registered continuously by 12-lead ECG during spiroergometry.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiac activity and cardiovascular response to stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Spiroergometry, graded exercise test.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects cardiovascular fitness and physiological stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over study investigated the effects of acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake on exercise-induced changes in antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress, inflammation, nitric oxide (NO) production, exercise performance, and recovery in well-trained male cyclists. Findings showed acute CF intake increased systemic epicatechin levels and total antioxidant capacity (TEAC/UA and UA), but did not significantly affect exercise-induced lipid peroxidation (MDA), inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), or NO production markers (L-arginine/ADMA, citrulline). While CF intake showed a tendency for improved late-stage performance in the first time trial, overall exercise performance and recovery were not significantly enhanced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake and cycling exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received an acute dose of either 903.75 mg of cocoa flavanols (CF) or a placebo (15 mg CF) in chocolate milk prior to exercise. The exercise protocol involved two 30-minute time trials (TT1 and TT2) performed at a workload equivalent to 75% of peak power output, separated by a 100-minute passive recovery. No explicit dose-response comparisons were conducted beyond the high-CF vs. placebo design.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (due to exercise), unchanged (by CF intake)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased during both TT1 and TT2 (main effect of time: F = 841.38; p < 0.001). Acute CF intake had no effect on heart rate (no main effect of trial or interaction effect).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Physiological response indicating cardiovascular workload and intensity of exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During exhaustive exercise (two 30-min time trials) following acute cocoa flavanol intake in well-trained cyclists.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects cardiovascular intensity and physiological stress during exercise; suggests no impact of CF on exercise physiological demand.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased only in the verum group (p = 0.027, ES = 0.256).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of cardiac function; reflects the number of heartbeats per unit of time, indicator of cardiac load and autonomic nervous system activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following dietary intervention with micronutrient supplementation and oral magnesium administration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an improvement in cardiac function and reduced cardiac load and improved cardiovascular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proof-of-concept study investigated whether a single session of High-Intensity Training (HIT) could restore impaired counterregulatory hormonal, symptomatic, and cognitive responses to subsequent insulin-induced hypoglycemia in people with type 1 diabetes and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH). The findings supported the hypothesis that IAH develops as a habituated response, demonstrating that HIT significantly amplified adrenaline responses and total symptom awareness during subsequent hypoglycemia, although it also led to a significant prolongation of cognitive reaction time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity training (HIT) compared to controlled rest
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single HIT session lasting 20 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down, with 4 x 30-second cycle sprints at 150% of maximum wattage (V̇O2peak assessment) interspersed with 2-minute recovery periods. Participants aimed for >90% peak heart rate. This was directly compared to 20 minutes of seated rest, and no dose-response comparisons for HIT were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: marked rise

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of physiological response to acute stress or exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following a single episode of High-Intensity Training (HIT) intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms the acute physiological impact and effectiveness of the HIT intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and evaluated a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol in collegiate athletes, demonstrating that it significantly enhances the recovery of cardiovascular and biochemical biomarkers (heart rate, lactic acid, and creatine kinase) compared to regular training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 4-week intervention included a Taekwondo-specific HIIT protocol compared to a control group receiving regular Taekwondo training. The HIIT was structured in two phases: Weeks 1-2 involved six rounds of four kicking techniques (21s work, 12s rest, 1.75:1 WRR) at 85% HRmax; Weeks 3-4 increased to eight rounds of the same techniques (24s work, 8s rest, 3:1 WRR) at 90% HRmax. Both phases included 1-minute rest between rounds. The control group performed regular Taekwondo training (90 min/session, 5 times/week) at 70-80% HRmax. Significant differences were observed between the groups.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cardiovascular System (measured via Polar HR monitor)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Faster recovery/normalization post-exercise and reduced HR at work.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant (p ">= 0.05) differences observed between groups in both exercise and recovery heart rates post-intervention. The HIIT group showed significant pre-to-post intervention improvements in recovery HR (R1HR, R2HR, R3HR) and exercise HR (E1, E3, E5, E7, E9) at all time points, unlike the control group. Post-intervention, the HIIT group had significantly lower recovery and exercise HRs compared to the control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of cardiovascular function, oxygen delivery, and an indicator of exertion and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery during and after a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cardiovascular recovery capacity and fitness, suggesting better adaptation to physical demands, reduced fatigue, and enhanced competition readiness in taekwondo athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of different cycling exercise intensities (70% and 90% of ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and cadences (30-110 rpm) on cardiopulmonary, metabolic, and skeletal muscle oxygenation responses in healthy participants. While higher intensity and cadence led to increased cardiorespiratory and metabolic activity, skeletal muscle oxygenation (measured by tissue saturation index and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis was not substantially affected, suggesting it may not be a primary factor in self-selected cadence at moderate exercise intensity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cycling Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed cycling exercise at two intensities (70% and 90% of the ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and five cadences (30, 50, 70, 90, and 110 rpm), with each bout lasting 4 minutes in a randomized sequence, interspersed with active recovery. While cardiopulmonary and metabolic responses increased with higher intensity (90% Tvent) and higher cadences (especially 110 rpm), skeletal muscle oxygenation (TSI and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis showed no significant dose-response across the tested intensities or cadences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Approximately 20 bpm higher at 90% Tvent than at 70% Tvent (P < 0.05) across all cadences. At 110 rpm, HR (150 
						14 bpm at 70% Tvent; 166 
						10 bpm at 90% Tvent) was significantly higher compared to lower cadences (P < 0.002). Returned to resting levels after active recovery periods.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular effort, physiological strain, and workload, reflecting the body's response to oxygen demand during exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cycling at different exercise intensities (70% vs 90% Tvent) and cadences (30-110 rpm), including post-active recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased cardiovascular demand and exercise intensity with higher workload and cadences, with effective recovery between bouts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of heart rate-matched (HR-matched) or work rate-matched (WR-matched) hypoxic interval exercise on post-exercise cardiac autonomic and cardiovascular responses compared to normoxic exercise in moderately trained men. Findings indicate that HR-matched hypoxic exercise mimicked post-exercise autonomic responses of normoxic exercise without inducing significant post-exercise hypotension (PEH) or impairing cardiac baroreflex sensitivity (cBRS). Conversely, WR-matched hypoxic exercise resulted in delayed cardiac autonomic recovery, a temporary decrease in cBRS, and prolonged PEH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hypoxic and Normoxic Interval Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed three interval-type exercise sessions (5x5-min work intervals; 1-min passive recovery) after a 5-min warm-up at 50% WR@VT1. Normoxic exercise (N) was at 80% of the work rate (WR) at the first ventilatory threshold (mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 139±10 bpm, ~75%HRmax). Hypoxic exercise (FiO2 = 14.2%, simulating ~3000m altitude) was performed either at the same absolute WR as N (H-WR, WR-matched: mean WR 183±19 W, mean HR 154±11 bpm, ~83%HRmax) or at the same absolute HR as N (H-HR, HR-matched: mean WR 144±18 W, mean HR 138±9 bpm, ~75%HRmax). This resulted in a -21.1±9.3% reduction in WR for H-HR compared to N, and a higher HR (by ~15 bpm) for H-WR compared to N. Recovery was seated under normoxic conditions, with assessments at POST-15, POST-45, POST-60, and POST-90 minutes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: During work rate-matched hypoxic exercise (H-WR), HR was higher (~83%HRmax) compared to normoxic exercise (N, ~75%HRmax), an increase of approximately 15 bpm (p < 0.001). After exercise, a progressive decrease in HR is observed due to cardiac parasympathetic reactivation and sympathetic withdrawal.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiac activity and cardiovascular effort, mediating responses to meet metabolic needs during exercise and decreasing post-exercise due to autonomic recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During work rate-matched hypoxic exercise (H-WR) compared to normoxic exercise (N), and during post-exercise recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological stimulation, cardiovascular stress during exercise, and the impact of exercise on autonomic recovery. Higher HR in H-WR suggests a greater physiological challenge.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: minimum 85% of age-predicted maximal HR (220 minus age) for maximal effort criterion; 85% of V̇O2 max HR to set treadmill speed for endurance test; HR collected throughout tests.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular workload and physiological response to exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During V̇O2 max treadmill test and time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Criterion for determining true maximal effort and exercise exhaustion; used to set exercise intensity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-of-day-dependent physiological, physical, and psychological responses of higher-weight men to a Walking Football Match (WFM). Findings revealed that evening WFM led to significantly lower glycemia, mean blood pressure (MBP), and heart rate recovery after 1 minute (HRR60s) compared to morning sessions, suggesting potential safety and metabolic benefits for higher-weight individuals when exercising in the evening. Most other parameters, including HRV, lactate, SpO2, and various physical performance metrics, showed no significant diurnal variation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Walking Football Match (WFM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a single session of 5 vs. 5 Walking Football Matches (WFM) on artificial turf fields. Each session lasted approximately one hour, comprising a 10-min warm-up, two 20-min playing periods separated by a 10-min passive recovery, and a 5-min cool-down. Matches were performed in randomized order, either in the morning (6:30 a.m. - 8:30 a.m.) or in the evening (5:00 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.), with 7 days between sessions. The activity was classified as moderate intensity (4.85-4.9 METs), with participants averaging around 2500-2600 steps per session and a cadence of approximately 63.8 steps/min. The study primarily focused on time-of-day effects, with no explicit dose-response comparisons regarding WFM intensity or duration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference between the two TODs for mean HR (p = 0.40, d = 0.19) and HR max (p = 0.60, d = 0.03). Mean HR during WFM: 133.54 beat/min in the morning and 136.54 in the evening.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiac activity and exercise intensity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During Walking Football Match, comparing morning vs. evening sessions in higher-weight men.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates level of physical activity and cardiovascular exertion during exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Effectively inhibited adriamycin-induced decreases in heart rate.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cardiac function indicator.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nicorandil treatment in an adriamycin-induced heart failure rat model (animal model context).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Effectively improves cardiac function during heart failure.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased with time during fixed-intensity cycling. Not different between Supplement or Group. Peak heart rate for WomenNC during placebo 1-km TT was 187 beat·min⁻¹ [182, 192], during NAC 186 beat·min⁻¹ [181, 191]. For WomenOC during placebo 1-km TT was 185 beat·min⁻¹ [179, 190], during NAC 185 beat·min⁻¹ [180, 191]. Not statistically different between groups in placebo or NAC trial.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular effort and physiological response to exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During fixed-intensity cycling and 1-km cycling time trial.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects cardiovascular demand during exercise, with no significant differences observed between groups or with NAC supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. The primary finding was that ALK water significantly reduced high-shear whole blood viscosity and enhanced its restoration to pre-exercise baseline levels compared to CON water, while other markers like plasma osmolality, bioimpedance, and body mass showed no significant difference.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral rehydration therapy after exercise-induced dehydration, comparing electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) with standard purified water (CON).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants exercised in a warm environment (30 °C, 70% relative humidity) until a 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight loss was achieved due to perspiration (mild dehydration). Rehydration involved consuming either electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) or standard purified water (CON), with an equal volume equivalent to 2% of pre-exercise body weight (approximately 20 mL/kg), administered within 30 minutes. This was followed by a 120-minute (2-hour) recovery period. No dose-response comparisons or variations in rehydration volume/rate were reported beyond the two water types.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean values for vital signs were similar between the high-pH alkaline water and standard water groups, with no clinically significant abnormal values observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiovascular demand and physiological stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise rehydration with alkaline water compared to control water.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly affected by the type of rehydration water (alkaline vs. control) in this context, indicating no differential cardiovascular stress response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated cardiovascular hemodynamic responses to peak exercise in individuals with and without Multiple Sclerosis (MS), specifically comparing groups with similar aerobic capacities (peak VO2) and stratifying by fitness levels. The core finding suggests that when individuals with and without MS have comparable peak VO2, their hemodynamic responses to peak exercise are similar. This implies that fitness, rather than the MS disease process itself, is a primary determinant of hemodynamic responses to exercise in this population. Additionally, unfit individuals with MS showed higher blood pressure compared to their fit MS counterparts, a difference not seen in control groups, highlighting the importance of fitness for health outcomes in MS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal incremental cycle ergometer exercise test to volitional exhaustion
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent maximal incremental cycle ergometer exercise tests to volitional exhaustion, following a protocol tailored for individuals with MS. Hemodynamic variables (heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure) were monitored at baseline, during warmup, at specific stages (e.g., 15W, 30W), and every other minute thereafter until peak exertion. The study focused on assessing peak aerobic capacity (peak VO2) and comparing hemodynamic responses at this maximal effort level between groups with similar peak VO2, and between pre-existing 'fit' and 'unfit' individuals. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities were reported beyond the incremental progression to maximal effort, as the primary aim was to compare groups at similar peak VO2.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher from baseline to peak exercise in both MS and control groups; however, overall MS group showed less increase over time, attributed to age. No significant difference in age/sex-matched sub-analysis.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased similarly from baseline to peak exercise in both MS and control groups. A significant group by time interaction (p < 0.01) indicated less HR change over time in the MS group compared to controls, which was accounted for by age. This interaction was no longer significant (p = 0.98) in an age/sex-matched subset. Unfit individuals (both MS and CON) also showed less HR change over time with a significant time*group interaction compared to their fit counterparts.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the number of heartbeats per minute, indicating the heart's response to physiological demand and regulating cardiovascular output and oxygen delivery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a maximal incremental cycle ergometer exercise test in individuals with and without MS, including comparisons between fit and unfit subgroups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects cardiovascular response and adaptive capacity to exercise. Attenuated HR response, especially in unfit groups, suggests compromised cardiorespiratory fitness. While historically suggesting autonomic impairment in MS, current findings suggest age, rather than disease, as a factor when fitness is matched.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not quantified as significant in this study.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During incremental exercise testing, altitude training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased (P < 0.05) post-intervention in the intervention group compared to baseline and control.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of autonomic nervous system function, cardiovascular recovery, and fitness post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) during or after rehabilitation training/aerobic exercise therapy in CAD patients after PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher HRR1 indicates improved cardiovascular recovery, autonomic regulation, and fitness, associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular events.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of total dietary antioxidant intake and capacity on body antioxidant mechanisms and exhaustive exercise-induced oxidative damage in ultra-endurance athletes. It examined physiological responses, including oxidative stress biomarkers (8-iso PGF2a, TOS, TAS, OSI) and lactate levels, during and after a combined cycling and treadmill exhaustive exercise protocol. Key findings indicated that higher dietary antioxidant intake was negatively correlated with pre-exercise total oxidant status and post-exercise increases in 8-iso PGF2a, while positively correlating with post-exercise increases in total antioxidant status and blood lactate concentrations. A higher dietary antioxidant capacity also positively influenced antioxidant defense and blood lactate removal (in both sexes) and running time to exhaustion (in males), but did not affect post-exercise heart rate recovery or perceived exertion.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Exercise and Dietary Antioxidant Intake Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ultra-endurance athletes underwent an acute exhaustive exercise protocol comprising 45 minutes on a cycle ergometer at 65% VO2max, immediately followed by a treadmill test at 75% VO2max to volitional exhaustion (median running time ~26-27 min, RPE 19). Dietary antioxidant intake was assessed using the Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP) assay, with a median intake of 16.6-17.2 mmol/day, categorized as moderate-to-high. The study focused on correlation analysis between habitual dietary intake and exercise responses, rather than controlled dietary intervention or dose-response comparisons for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant interaction was observed between dietary antioxidants and post-exercise HR recovery.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflection of autonomic nervous system activity and cardiovascular fitness during recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exhaustive exercise recovery, relation to dietary antioxidant capacity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of exercise performance and post-exercise recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery (VO2Rec) measures, especially VO2T12.5% (time to recover 12.5% of peak VO2), in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. The study suggests its regular inclusion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing protocols.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Pharmacological treatment (Aficamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Aficamten was administered for 24 weeks in a phase 3 randomized controlled trial, compared against placebo. Doses were individualized to achieve the lowest effective dose, targeting a Valsalva Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Gradient (LVOT-G) <30 mm Hg while maintaining a left ventricular ejection fraction ">=\u00ad50%. Specific daily dosages (mg) and dose-response comparisons were not detailed, but treatment led to proportional improvements in cardiac function and biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 44% recovery in individuals with VO2 T 12.5% ">=35 seconds versus 41% in those with <35 seconds, 2 minutes after exercise (P =0.82). HR is 43% recovered 2 minutes after exercise. Tertiles of VO2 T 12.5% show no difference in percentage of HR recovered by 2 minutes among the 3 groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the rate at which heart rate returns to baseline after exercise, indicative of autonomic nervous system function. Number of heartbeats per minute, reflecting cardiac workload.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 2 minutes after incremental ramp exercise, stratified by VO2 T 12.5% duration. Post-peak exercise recovery; comparison with VO2 Rec.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No difference in HR recovery patterns suggests that impaired central cardiac function (e.g., SV recovery) rather than autonomic control of heart rate is the primary driver of prolonged VO2 T 12.5%. Impaired HR recovery is observed in patients with HFpEF; however, VO2 Rec provides independent insight into a patient		s hemodynamic status, suggesting HR recovery alone is not sufficient for comprehensive assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between thalamic volume and heart rate recovery following an orthostatic challenge in older adults from The Irish Longitudinal Study on Aging (TILDA). It consistently found that smaller thalamic volume is associated with slower heart rate recovery, suggesting that thalamic structural integrity is a potential risk marker for autonomic dysfunction, cardiovascular events, and sudden cardiac death, while also differentiating its contribution from other subcortical brain regions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Orthostatic Challenge (Active Standing Test)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in this observational study underwent an active stand protocol where they lay supine for 10 minutes, then stood quickly and remained standing for 3 minutes. Beat-to-beat heart rate and blood pressure were monitored, with heart rate recovery (HRR) specifically measured between 10 and 30 seconds post-standing (HRR 10|30s). This study focused on correlating brain volume with physiological response, thus no therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cardiovascular system (measured via noninvasive digital photoplethysmography)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Physiological response measurement (change in beat-to-beat heart rate over time)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Slower/impaired recovery is associated with smaller thalamic volume; faster recovery with larger thalamic volume.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Heart rate recovery (HRR 10|30s) was calculated as the difference in heart rate between 10 and 30 seconds after standing. Slower HRR was observed with smaller thalamic volume, quantified as -1.4 bpm slower per 1 cm^3 thalamic volume (95% CI -2.01 to -0.82; p < .001) and a mean of -2.7 bpm slower in participants with smaller thalamic volumes (95% CI -3.89 to -1.61; p < .001). Conversely, HRR was 2.1-2.7 beats per minute faster in the highest tertile of thalamic volume. Specifically, the mean decline in HRR 10|30s was -5.75 bpm for the smallest thalamic volume tertile versus -8.51 bpm for the largest tertile. A 1 bpm slower HRR was linked to a 10% increased risk of all-cause mortality.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Heart rate recovery is a crucial indicator of autonomic function, cardiovascular risk, and homeostatic flexibility, reflecting the efficiency of the autonomic nervous system (vagal and sympathetic activation) in restoring cardiovascular homeostasis after a physiological stressor like an orthostatic challenge.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to an orthostatic challenge (standing up from a resting position) in older adults, and its association with thalamic volume and overall aging.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Heart rate recovery is a reliable indicator of autonomic function, cardiovascular risk, and homeostatic flexibility. Slower or attenuated HRR is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events, all-cause mortality, and sudden cardiac death, predicting cardiac mortality and reflecting central autonomic control and dysfunction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-of-day-dependent physiological, physical, and psychological responses of higher-weight men to a Walking Football Match (WFM). Findings revealed that evening WFM led to significantly lower glycemia, mean blood pressure (MBP), and heart rate recovery after 1 minute (HRR60s) compared to morning sessions, suggesting potential safety and metabolic benefits for higher-weight individuals when exercising in the evening. Most other parameters, including HRV, lactate, SpO2, and various physical performance metrics, showed no significant diurnal variation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Walking Football Match (WFM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a single session of 5 vs. 5 Walking Football Matches (WFM) on artificial turf fields. Each session lasted approximately one hour, comprising a 10-min warm-up, two 20-min playing periods separated by a 10-min passive recovery, and a 5-min cool-down. Matches were performed in randomized order, either in the morning (6:30 a.m. - 8:30 a.m.) or in the evening (5:00 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.), with 7 days between sessions. The activity was classified as moderate intensity (4.85-4.9 METs), with participants averaging around 2500-2600 steps per session and a cadence of approximately 63.8 steps/min. The study primarily focused on time-of-day effects, with no explicit dose-response comparisons regarding WFM intensity or duration.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in the evening compared to the morning
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in the evening than in the morning (p = 0.048; d = 0.47); overall values were lower in the evening compared to the morning. Previous study reported 27 ± 7 bpm in morning, 29 ± 7 bpm in evening among hypertensive men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects cardiac autonomic function, post-exercise cardiac autonomic recovery, and sympathetic activity, indicating cardiovascular fitness/recovery capacity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-Walking Football Match (WFM) recovery, comparing evening vs. morning sessions in higher-weight men.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates safety of exercise and is correlated with mortality risk (low HRR values). Lower HRR60s values in the evening compared to the morning suggest that evening exercise practice could be safer for individuals with higher weight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the sex-specific relationships among total serum cholinesterase activity (CS), high-sensitive cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), and traditional hemodynamic parameters of autonomic nervous system function during exercise in apparently healthy individuals. Key findings include a positive association between serum CS and hs-cTnT detection in women, an inverse association in men, and sex-dependent predictions of exercise-hemodynamic changes and metabolic impairment by CS, providing insights for cardiovascular disease risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study using Cardiac Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent a standard Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST) according to the Bruce protocol. The study was observational, investigating associations between biomarkers and hemodynamic changes during this test; no specific therapeutic 'dose' or 'duration' of an intervention was applied or compared. Hypertensive reactions were defined as peak SBP > 205 mm/Hg in men and > 187 mm/Hg in women. Heart rate recovery rate was calculated from peak rate to recovery time.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Measured during exercise ECG stress test

measured_effect.direction_of_change: inversely correlated (to CS values in women)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Calculated as absolute values of heart rate upon recovery minus peak rate divided by the recovery time (min). In women, heart rate recovery after exercise was inversely correlated to CS values, with decreasing CS levels evident between heart rate recovery quartiles (Fig. 1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the speed at which the heart rate returns to normal after exercise, indicating autonomic nervous system function and cardiovascular fitness.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitored after a cardiac exercise ECG stress test (Bruce protocol).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictor of worse cardiovascular prognosis. A faster heart rate recovery indicates better cardiovascular health and parasympathetic tone.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively explores Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) as crucial mediators of intercellular communication, highlighting their dual roles in health and disease. It examines their potential as personalized diagnostic biomarkers across various conditions including viral infections, cancer, neurological, kidney, autoimmune, metabolic, and pro-thrombotic diseases. The document also investigates EVs as promising therapeutic agents, drug delivery vehicles, and regenerative therapeutics, discussing their involvement in disease pathogenesis (e.g., spreading misfolded proteins, facilitating viral replication) and their protective functions (e.g., neuroprotection, inflammation regulation, aggregate prevention, tissue repair). Challenges in EV isolation, standardization, and clinical translation are also addressed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study characterized the longitudinal development of kidney size (length and volume) in pediatric Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) patients. It aimed to evaluate the association of early height-adjusted estimated total kidney volume (haeTKV), particularly measurements within the first 18 months of life, with kidney survival, identifying it as a clear prognostic marker for kidney survival. The study also detailed statistical methodologies for estimating annual eGFR loss and haeTKV increase in children, including those on Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT).

A specific focus was placed on height-adjusted estimated total kidney volume (haeTKV) in the first eighteen months of life. Mean annual increase of haeTKV was estimated by a linear regression of haeTKV versus age.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: haeTKV reflects kidney enlargement due to fibrocystic changes, which is a key characteristic of ARPKD and indicative of disease progression and severity. It also functions as a prognostic marker for kidney survival.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) progression, specifically longitudinal changes during childhood and adolescence, initial measurements in the first eighteen months of life, stratified by age, genetic variants, and CKD stage. Also includes longitudinal assessment of haeTKV versus age in children and children undergoing Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the severity and progression of kidney disease in ARPKD. It is a strong potential prognostic marker for kidney survival in childhood and adolescence, particularly when measured in the first 18 months of life (haeTKVmax18), and can identify patients at heightened risk of early kidney failure or progression to KRT for clinical studies.
