biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Synthese: Hier wuerde die konsolidierte Zuverlaessigkeits-Zusammenfassung stehen.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in the low LPC 20:0 group (p<0.05); negatively correlated with PC 14:0-18:1 (correlation coefficient >0.85). Given PC 14:0-18:1 is significantly lower in the acute stage of severe patients, helper T-cell count is inferred to be higher in the acute stage compared to recovery in severe COVID-19 patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune cells that activate other immune cells, central to coordinating adaptive immune responses; crucial for immune response and host defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute vs. recovery stages in severe COVID-19 patients; patients with low LPC 20:0 levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired immune state or dysregulation in COVID-19 patients, potentially influenced by lipid metabolism; association with disease stage in severe COVID-19; inferred higher levels in acute severe stages compared to recovery, potentially reflecting immune dysregulation.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Hematocrit: Gefunden in 10 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All immune-related complete blood counts demonstrated significant changes over time (p<0.001), but no significant changes between groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proportion of red blood cells in total blood volume.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in the context of a study involving half-marathon running and potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects blood viscosity, oxygen transport efficiency, and hydration status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Revealed a tendency to increase in response to exercise; attributed to dehydration.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells; indicative of blood viscosity and hydration status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After each bout of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological response to exercise-induced water loss/dehydration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: transient decrease followed by no change
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased by approximately 5% during the second rest day (Rest2d) attributed to hydration restoration. It did not change (ranging from 43% to 45%) during the CCombat protocol (0 140 min) or during short (up to 120 min) or long (up to 48 h) recovery. Changes correlated highly with natremia during resting (-48h and -24h), with r s values of 0.65.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of blood volume (volemia), hemoconcentration, and blood water content.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-exercise, during CCombat exercise, and during short/long recovery periods, with observations during initial rest days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects changes in blood volume/volemia and is used as a tool for hydration follow-up in exercise; a decline can be attributed to hydration restoration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased at T1 compared to T0 (p<0.0001); not significantly different to T0 at T2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) at engraftment time point T1
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates red blood cell system status and recovery post-alloSCT, related to blood viscosity and oxygen delivery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased acutely following matches and returned toward pre-exercise baseline levels quickly during short recovery. Levels remained predominantly below initial values throughout the protocol, except post-match 1, showing similar patterns for both athletes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Volume percentage of red blood cells, indicating blood viscosity and oxygen-carrying capacity
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, short recovery), acute exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indirectly assesses acute blood volume changes (hemoconcentration/dilution) due to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally elevated in hyperoxic (HX) compared to normoxic (NX) conditions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Volume percentage of red blood cells in blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline in Hyperoxic (HX) conditions compared to Normoxic (NX) apnea.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Likely reflects (apnea-induced) splenic contraction and/or plasma volume contraction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells, related to oxygen-carrying capacity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase in professional soccer players, assessed at baseline and post-PS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not reported in this study, but generally an indicator of oxygen-carrying capacity and endurance performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Approximately 1.8% higher in CON than CAL (P < 0.001). Increased by ~2.3% from baseline at the end of EX1, then decreased by 7.8% during recovery. Generally increased during exercise and decreased during recovery in both conditions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates red blood cell volume and is used to estimate fluid shifts and for hemoconcentration adjustment of other markers.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During strenuous rowing exercise (EX1, EX2) and recovery periods, with or without preexercise calcium intake (CAL vs CON). Also used to adjust bone turnover marker concentrations for hemoconcentration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates changes in blood volume due to fluid shifts, relevant for adjusting other biomarker concentrations. The reported difference between conditions was 'unlikely to be practically important' for Hct itself.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No alterations or differences were found during or after the 6-week supplementation protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells, indicating blood viscosity and oxygen-carrying capacity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day) combined with a CrossFit training program.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that the supplementation and training program did not negatively impact blood component levels, maintaining health and performance potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slightly different between each severity group in acute and convalescent phases, but no significant difference reported. No quantitative data was given beyond 'slightly different'.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the proportion of blood volume that is occupied by red blood cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute and convalescent phases of dengue infection across MDF, SDD-C, and SDD+C severity groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Severity of dengue does not significantly influence hematocrit changes in the tested patients.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Hematocrit (HCT): Gefunden in 7 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant differences observed between different time points, specifically a significant decrease in the placebo group (GP).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the proportion of red blood cells in blood volume.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Competitive season and pre-season sports training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects red blood cell mass and potential changes in hydration or erythropoiesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Showed different patterns of changes across all groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Different patterns of changes in the RBC-related parameters of hematocrit (HCT) were found in all groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Volume percentage of red blood cells in blood, reflecting red blood cell mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional swimming training period.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides important information about the general health of athletes; observed fluctuations were within general population reference limits.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over study investigated the effects of acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake on exercise-induced changes in antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress, inflammation, nitric oxide (NO) production, exercise performance, and recovery in well-trained male cyclists. Findings showed acute CF intake increased systemic epicatechin levels and total antioxidant capacity (TEAC/UA and UA), but did not significantly affect exercise-induced lipid peroxidation (MDA), inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), or NO production markers (L-arginine/ADMA, citrulline). While CF intake showed a tendency for improved late-stage performance in the first time trial, overall exercise performance and recovery were not significantly enhanced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake and cycling exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received an acute dose of either 903.75 mg of cocoa flavanols (CF) or a placebo (15 mg CF) in chocolate milk prior to exercise. The exercise protocol involved two 30-minute time trials (TT1 and TT2) performed at a workload equivalent to 75% of peak power output, separated by a 100-minute passive recovery. No explicit dose-response comparisons were conducted beyond the high-CF vs. placebo design.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported as a direct outcome of the intervention.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Measured for plasma volume correction, but direct effects or quantitative changes due to intervention/exercise are not reported as primary outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells; used to correct for plasma volume changes during analysis of other biomarkers.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured at various time points during exercise trials to correct biochemical data for plasma volume shifts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Essential for accurate interpretation of other biomarker concentrations by accounting for changes in plasma volume during exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in relation to some metrics, higher in others
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively associated with 10m sprint values (-0.056) and RSA values (-1.822). Positively associated with VO2 max values (+1.505) in predictive regression models (p < 0.001 for overall models).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates red blood cell volume, relates to oxygen transport capacity, considered an adaptive response to increasing training loads.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer players' 10m sprint, RSA, and VO2 max performance after strenuous pre-seasonal training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels predict better 10m sprint efficiency and repeated sprint ability. Higher levels predict better aerobic capacity. Its increase following prolonged training is debated.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (p < 0.001), decreased 3 hours after (p < 0.001), and remained significantly different compared to pre-exercise at 24 hours (p < 0.002). Demonstrated good reliability (ICC = 0.78).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High reliability, suggesting suitability as a blood-based biomarker for monitoring physiological exercise response and recovery status in endurance athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in ITG (prevented decline in CG)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ITG showed significant increases, from T1: 46.3 ± 2.6% to T2: 49.7 ± 2.0%, representing a 7.32 ± 3.92% increase (p < 0.05). CG showed a decline from T1: 44.6 ± 2.5% to T2: 44.1 ± 3.0%, representing a -1.17 ± 3.78% change. Group-by-time interaction was significant (p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Percentage of red blood cells in the blood, indicating oxygen-carrying capacity and blood viscosity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España) with 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with oxygen delivery capacity and physical performance; contributes to optimal recovery levels and endurance capacity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: RBC parameters, iron metabolism markers (transferrin, ferritin, serum iron), plasma viscosity, and IgM/IgG levels generally remained unchanged. Significant decreases (p < 0.05) were observed in WBC count, neutrophils, and lymphocytes after acute 10 mg melatonin 2h post-exercise. Plasma IgA levels significantly increased (p < 0.05) after 100 mg for 4 weeks.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Hematopoietic Stem Cell (HSC) proliferation and associated gene regulators (e.g., TAL1, RUNX1, CREB1, SPI1, GATA1, ACKR1, ALAS2, FOXO3, BCL2L1)
matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Bone Marrow (and mobilization to circulation) / Leukocytes

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Leukocyte-skewed augmentation in HSC proliferation from bone marrow. Differential expression for various gene transcripts: TAL1, RUNX1, CREB1, leukocyte producing HSC regulators (altered); SPI1 (higher); GATA1, ACKR1, hemoglobin production genes, FOXO transcription factors, anti-apoptotic transcription factors (lower). All recovered to baseline during weight regain.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates the generation and differentiation of all blood cell types, including immune cells, by controlling HSC proliferation, survival, and lineage commitment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense weight loss period (prolonged energy deprivation and intense exercise).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed differentiation in the erythroid lineage, induced activity of myeloid and lymphoid progenitor cell lines, increased metabolic stress on HSCs, augmented ROS-induced apoptosis, and potential acceleration of HSC aging, all contributing to immune system dysregulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified among 890 (99%) of 900 genes with significant positive correlations (Pearson coefficient, Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05) between cfRNA and wbRNA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with myeloid cell transcription.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of cfRNA and wbRNA profiles in patients with MIS-C, moderate to severe COVID-19, or controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Demonstrates complementary information between cfRNA and wbRNA, providing a more complete picture of host response and cell dynamics.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All immune-related complete blood counts demonstrated significant changes over time (p<0.001), but no significant changes between groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in the context of a study involving half-marathon running and potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and can reflect endurance potential or anemia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Revealed a tendency to increase in response to exercise; attributed to dehydration.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After each bout of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates oxygen carrying capacity and potential dehydration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between iron status and renal outcomes, specifically progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), in 111 pre-dialysis patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven Diabetic Nephropathy (DN). It found that reduced serum transferrin is an independent predictor of ESRD, and identified increased iron and transferrin deposition in renal tubular epithelial cells of DN patients, suggesting a pathological role for altered iron metabolism in disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the prognostic value of iron status and related biomarkers in Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. Serum markers were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, immunoradiometric assay, and colorimetric methods. Additionally, histological analysis involved immunohistochemical staining for transferrin and Perl's blue staining for iron in kidney biopsy specimens from DN patients and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or active treatments were investigated; the study focused on correlation and predictive value.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower baseline concentrations in ESRD patients compared to non-ESRD patients. Lower concentrations observed in patients with lower serum transferrin quartiles and positively correlated with baseline serum transferrin (r=0.39, P<0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport. Main protein of red blood cells, responsible for oxygen transport in the blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in T2DM patients with Diabetic Nephropathy (DN); T2DM with biopsy-proven DN.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels are associated with ESRD; positively correlated with serum transferrin, suggesting a link between iron status, anemia, and kidney disease progression. Indicator of overall health and nutritional status; lower levels may suggest anemia or poor nutritional status, consistent with lower transferrin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in hemoglobin levels between baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Changes between baseline and FUP6 in various heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, HFrEF) after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential change or impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study, suggesting it is not a key differential indicator in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls
