matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes; elevated levels might suggest dehydration or other conditions

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes or specific effects reported related to the intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment in elite male rowers undergoing high or low calcium dietary interventions and intense rowing exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No specific performance or health indicator was reported related to the calcium intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased at T1 compared to T0 (p=0.0009); not significantly different to T0 at T2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport in red blood cells
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) at engraftment time point T1
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates red blood cell system status and recovery post-alloSCT, related to oxygen carrying capacity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen throughout the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CD administration in mice following resistance exercise, facilitating recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased concentrations suggest enhanced oxygen transport capacity, which is beneficial for endurance and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significant seasonal changes; significant increase at the end of autumn (T2) and decrease in the placebo group.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant changes observed for the whole group (n=24) over the one-year training cycle (p < 0.001, pη[1] = 0.38 for GS, 0.37 for GP). A significant increase was noted at the end of autumn (T2) when 25(OH)D was low, and a significant decrease was observed in the placebo group (GP). No significant effect of vitamin D supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport in red blood cells, crucial for cellular oxygenation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training cycle in young soccer players under high training loads (competitive/pre-season), influenced by seasonal changes, 8-week vitamin D supplementation, and home isolation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates oxygen-carrying capacity of blood, relevant for athletic performance and fatigue. Changes primarily reflect training loads, with decreases potentially indicating adaptation or stress, and insufficient training loads during isolation not improving cellular oxygenation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Females <12 g·d⁻¹; males <13 g·dL⁻¹ (for anemia diagnosis). Functional iron deficiency defined as <11.5 g·dl⁻¹.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Efficiently transports oxygen to exercising muscle tissue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Iron deficiency; anemia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Insufficient levels impair oxygen transport and endurance performance; required for diagnosis of anemia. Supplementation is known to correct low levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. It also examined changes in cognitive function (attention, executive function, memory, visual ability, fine motor skills, reaction), psychological scores (anxiety, depression), and various blood biochemical markers (Estradiol, prolactin, FSH, LH, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin). The study compared patients before, one week after, and six months after completing chemotherapy to healthy controls. Key findings revealed widespread chemotherapy-induced abnormalities in resting state networks, which partly recovered by six months post-chemotherapy. These altered functional connectivities were correlated with cognitive assessment scores and blood biochemical indexes, suggesting RSNs as potential biomarkers for chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and for guiding rehabilitation. Baseline analyses also showed higher metabolic markers and psychological/cognitive scores in patients compared to controls, along with a high incidence of chemotherapy-induced amenorrhea.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (for breast cancer patients, some also received endocrine therapy)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Postoperative chemotherapy was administered to breast cancer patients, typically in six to eight courses. While specific drug names or dosages were not detailed, follow-up assessments were consistently conducted before (baseline), one week after completing, and six months after completing chemotherapy. Some patients (35.3%) also received endocrine therapy after chemotherapy, but no concurrent radiotherapy or endocrine therapy was given during chemotherapy. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased slightly from baseline (t0) to one week post-chemotherapy (t1), and significantly increased from t1 to t2 (six months post-chemotherapy; P = 0.003).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport in blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Changes after chemotherapy in breast cancer patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of red blood cell count and oxygen-carrying capacity, reflecting general health status and potential chemotherapy-induced effects. No direct correlation to cognitive function outcomes is provided for these specific changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally elevated in hyperoxic (HX) compared to normoxic (NX) conditions.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline in Hyperoxic (HX) conditions compared to Normoxic (NX) apnea.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Likely reflects (apnea-induced) splenic contraction and/or plasma volume contraction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged after PS phase; positively correlated
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences after the PS phase observed, except for PLT. Moderate positive correlation with VAMEVAL test (r = 0.44, 95%CI: 0.05; 0.71). Positive moderate correlation with 10-meter sprint split (r = 0.42, p = 0.032).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Responsible for oxygen transport in the blood; indicator of endurance capacity and internal training load.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after an intense training phase; correlation with VAMEVAL test and 10-meter sprint performance.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates endurance capacity and internal training load; higher levels associated with improved aerobic fitness and VAMEVAL performance; higher levels associated with slower 10-meter sprint times (counterintuitive but reported); monitoring is crucial for superior aerobic performance and overall physical readiness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This surveillance report details malaria cases in the United States in 2018, reporting a 15.6% decrease in confirmed cases from 2017 while noting an overall increase since 1972, with 98.1% being imported cases predominantly from Africa and P. falciparum as the most common species. It describes comprehensive surveillance methodologies, diagnostic tests, and molecular analyses for antimalarial drug resistance markers, particularly for P. falciparum against pyrimethamine, sulfadoxine, chloroquine, and mefloquine, with no resistance markers for atovaquone or artemisinin. The report also investigates chemoprophylaxis adherence (found to be poor), treatment patterns for uncomplicated and severe malaria, and emphasizes the critical importance of prompt diagnosis, appropriate treatment with CDC guidelines, and continuous surveillance to prevent local transmission.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Malaria prevention (chemoprophylaxis, including Tafenoquine), diagnosis (microscopy, PCR, RDTs), and treatment for both uncomplicated and severe malaria (oral antimalarials like atovaquone-proguanil, artemether-lumefantrine, quinine; parenteral IV artesunate for severe malaria), alongside molecular surveillance for antimalarial drug resistance.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Chemoprophylaxis adherence was poor among U.S. residents with imported malaria in 2018, with 24.5% reporting use and 95.0% demonstrating non-adherence or inconsistent regimens, often due to forgetting or prematurely stopping. Tafenoquine offers an abbreviated schedule for eligible adults. For treatment, IV artesunate became the first-line for severe malaria in April 2019, replacing IV quinidine gluconate, though 52.1% of severe cases in 2018 did not receive guideline-appropriate treatment. Uncomplicated malaria treatments varied, with 91.7% receiving appropriate care, and primaquine was often used for P. vivax/P. ovale relapse prevention, though sometimes inappropriately. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported, but treatment choice was emphasized based on species, severity, patient factors (e.g., pregnancy), and CDC guidelines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: <7g/dL.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport; its level indicates the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Manifestation of severe malaria, specifically acute kidney injury and severe anemia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severe anemia, which is a key criterion for classifying a malaria case as severe, and a significant contributor to morbidity and mortality.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No alterations or differences were found during or after the 6-week supplementation protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day) combined with a CrossFit training program.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that the supplementation and training program did not negatively impact oxygen transport capacity or blood component levels, maintaining health and performance potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ significantly among all the groups investigated.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport throughout the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison among HCC, non-malignant, and control groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant indicator of differential oxygen-carrying capacity among the studied groups, despite differences in RBC counts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hb < 13 g/dL in 20% of women (optimal: 13.0-15.0 g/dL) and Hb < 14 g/dL in 60% of men (optimal: 14.0-17.0 g/dL).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport in blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Aging population.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anemia in old age and is associated with increased hospitalization and mortality risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then returned toward baseline; predominantly below initial values after recovery
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Matches induced acute raises, which returned toward baseline during short recovery 1 and 2. Levels remained predominantly below initial values throughout the protocol, except post-match 1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, short recovery)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indirectly assesses acute blood volume changes due to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar between groups at CPET 1 and CPET 2 initially. However, it decreased by 0.7 g/dL in both study groups from CPET 1 to CPET 2, a reduction that could explain an expected mean reduction in peak VO2 of 0.68 mL/kg/min.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary protein responsible for oxygen transport from the lungs to the body's tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest before CPET 1 and within 90 seconds after peak exercise on CPET 1 and CPET 2, and between CPETs, in female ME/CFS patients and healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Consistent levels initially suggest no differential acute changes in oxygen carrying capacity due to exercise or underlying health conditions. The observed reduction between CPETs indicates a decreased oxygen-carrying capacity, which contributes to reduced peak oxygen uptake and overall exercise capacity in both groups, but is relevant for understanding performance changes.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Hemoglobin (Hb): Gefunden in 10 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant changes (P > 0.05) in hematological parameters were observed throughout the experiment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that transports oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues and carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, indicating stable oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood under the study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over study investigated the effects of acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake on exercise-induced changes in antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress, inflammation, nitric oxide (NO) production, exercise performance, and recovery in well-trained male cyclists. Findings showed acute CF intake increased systemic epicatechin levels and total antioxidant capacity (TEAC/UA and UA), but did not significantly affect exercise-induced lipid peroxidation (MDA), inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), or NO production markers (L-arginine/ADMA, citrulline). While CF intake showed a tendency for improved late-stage performance in the first time trial, overall exercise performance and recovery were not significantly enhanced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake and cycling exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received an acute dose of either 903.75 mg of cocoa flavanols (CF) or a placebo (15 mg CF) in chocolate milk prior to exercise. The exercise protocol involved two 30-minute time trials (TT1 and TT2) performed at a workload equivalent to 75% of peak power output, separated by a 100-minute passive recovery. No explicit dose-response comparisons were conducted beyond the high-CF vs. placebo design.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Concentration used for plasma volume correction

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported as a direct outcome of the intervention.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Measured for plasma volume correction, but direct effects or quantitative changes due to intervention/exercise are not reported as primary outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport; used to correct for plasma volume changes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured at various time points during exercise trials to correct biochemical data for plasma volume shifts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Essential for accurate interpretation of other biomarker concentrations by accounting for changes in plasma volume during exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study established robust reference intervals for plasma dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated Matrix Gla-Protein (dp-ucMGP) in a metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population using the IDS-iSYS Ina Ktif assay. It investigated dp-ucMGP's utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The findings indicate a significant stepwise increase in plasma dp-ucMGP levels from healthy individuals to those with DM without DKD, and further to those with DKD. Higher dp-ucMGP levels were associated with renal function decline and demonstrated predictive value for DKD diagnosis and progression, showing similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting renal function decline. Additionally, the study explored associations of dp-ucMGP with various clinical parameters in healthy volunteers, noting gender differences and correlations with BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study (Observational)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on establishing reference intervals and evaluating the diagnostic potential of plasma dp-ucMGP across different health states (healthy, diabetes mellitus, diabetic kidney disease). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted within this study. However, the document discusses external studies on Vitamin K2 supplementation (e.g., 6 weeks of daily supplementation or 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days) as a potential therapy impacting dp-ucMGP levels.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Variable (higher in HVs, lower in DM); increasing haemoglobin was associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP in HVs, while decreasing haemoglobin was associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP in participants with DM.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: As described in direction of change.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells that transports oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General health assessment in healthy volunteers and participants with diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of oxygen-carrying capacity and anemia. Its association with dp-ucMGP varies between healthy individuals and those with diabetes, potentially indicating different pathophysiological links.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Iron-containing protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and anemia.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (p < 0.001), decreased 3 hours after (p < 0.001), and remained significantly different compared to pre-exercise at 24 hours. Demonstrated excellent reliability (ICC = 0.86).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High reliability, suggesting suitability as a blood-based biomarker for monitoring physiological exercise response and recovery status in endurance athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a computational model to explain and predict changes in red blood cell parameters (RDW-CV%, Hb, MCV) during iron and folate deficiencies, highlighting RDW-CV% as an early and useful indicator for both conditions, especially in resource-limited settings for detecting folate deficiency to prevent foetal damage, and suggesting its inclusion in routine blood analyses.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Computational diagnostic modeling for nutritional deficiencies.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A computer model simulated red blood cell (RBC) formation and destruction, assuming a 120-day RBC lifespan. It used standard haematological parameters (normal Hb lower limit 110 g/l, upper normal RDW-CV% 15%) and specific parameters for normal haemopoiesis (RBC/day 40000, MCV 90, SD of MCV 10, MCH 30), iron-deficient haemopoiesis (RBC/day 30000, MCV 60, SD of MCV 7, MCH 18), and folate-deficient haemopoiesis (macrocytic pattern). Simulations ran for up to 180 days, incorporating shifts between normal and deficient states to predict changes in blood parameters. No direct therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported within the study, as it focused on diagnostic prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower limit of normal for adult women is 110 g/l. In early iron deficiency and short-term folate deficiency, levels decrease but often remain initially within the normal range (e.g., 111 g/l after 50 days of iron deficiency in the model). Hb is also low in anaemia of thalassaemia and when iron is the limiting nutrient in combined iron and folate deficiency.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main protein in red blood cells responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early iron deficiency, short-term folate deficiency, anaemia of thalassaemia, and iron deficiency (as a limiting nutrient in combined deficiencies).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary indicator of anaemia. When near the lower limit of normal and combined with a high RDW-CV%, it can predict iron or folate deficiency. Its decrease signals underlying deficiencies or other haematological conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in ITG (prevented decline in CG)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ITG showed significant increases, from T1: 14.7 ± 0.9 g/L to T2: 16.6 ± 0.5 g/L, representing a 13.04 ± 5.64% increase (p < 0.05). CG showed a slight decrease or minimal change from T1: 15.1 ± 0.8 g/L to T2: 15.0 ± 1.2 g/L, representing a -0.41 ± 3.32% change. Group-by-time interaction was significant (p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells, crucial for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España) with 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Critical for physical performance and oxygen delivery, preventing fatigue associated with reduced oxygen transport; contributes to optimal recovery levels and endurance capacity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive study investigated alpha-synuclein (αSN) as a potential diagnostic and monitoring biomarker for Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM). It evaluated αSN immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies and its concentration in serum and muscle homogenates, comparing IBM patients to other myopathies and healthy controls. The findings suggest αSN immunoreactivity in muscle is a promising diagnostic marker, while serum αSN levels could serve as a monitoring biomarker, correlating with disease duration and clinical severity in IBM. The study also explored the diagnostic utility of other established and emerging biomarkers in IBM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational/Diagnostic Biomarker Investigation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved a multimodal assessment of alpha-synuclein (αSN) levels and immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies, muscle tissue homogenates, and serum samples from various cohorts. Muscle biopsies (N=63, including 19 IBM, 21 other inflammatory myopathies, 20 other myopathies, 3 healthy controls) were analyzed by immunohistochemical staining. Serum samples (N=156, including 11 IBM, 25 other inflammatory myopathies, 53 hereditary myopathies, 30 mitochondriopathies, 37 healthy controls) were assessed by ELISA. Muscle homogenates were also examined (N=17 IBM, N=19 other inflammatory myopathies, N=5 hereditary myopathies, N=2 healthy controls). IBM patients were stratified by disease severity (IBMFRS) and disease duration for serum αSN analysis. No interventional dose or therapeutic comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic and monitoring biomarker evaluation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated Hb concentrations observed in all examined tissue homogenate samples; Hb concentration was higher in muscle tissue homogenates compared to serum samples. A slight correlation with αSN was suggested in diseased cohort (r=0.525), but no correlation was observed in healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of haemolysis, which can confound α-synuclein measurements in tissue homogenates.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measurement in muscle homogenates and serum samples during analysis of α-synuclein in Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM) patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels in muscle homogenates indicate haemolysis, necessitating adjustment (e.g., log-αSN/Hb ratio) to accurately reflect actual αSN concentration in muscle cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported in the study findings.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General indicator of blood oxygen-carrying capacity and overall health status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A similar pattern was observed for hemoglobin (Hb) concentration as for RBC counts (highest in middle of study for females, and at beginning and end for males).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional swimming training period.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the sex-specific relationships among total serum cholinesterase activity (CS), high-sensitive cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), and traditional hemodynamic parameters of autonomic nervous system function during exercise in apparently healthy individuals. Key findings include a positive association between serum CS and hs-cTnT detection in women, an inverse association in men, and sex-dependent predictions of exercise-hemodynamic changes and metabolic impairment by CS, providing insights for cardiovascular disease risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study using Cardiac Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent a standard Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST) according to the Bruce protocol. The study was observational, investigating associations between biomarkers and hemodynamic changes during this test; no specific therapeutic 'dose' or 'duration' of an intervention was applied or compared. Hypertensive reactions were defined as peak SBP > 205 mm/Hg in men and > 187 mm/Hg in women. Heart rate recovery rate was calculated from peak rate to recovery time.

Pre-diabetic women presented higher CS values than healthy ones (1447.8 +/- 296.8 vs. 1355.58 +/- 289.711 for CS, p = 0.03).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similarly increased in both UA and placebo groups (~4–5% increase, both p < 0.05 versus baseline). No difference between groups (p = 0.877).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following an altitude training camp (with or without UA supplementation).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved oxygen-carrying capacity, contributing to physiological adaptation to a robust training stimulus, but not specific to UA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Gene targeting using TALENs, in vitro human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation, and in vivo mouse embryo analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GATA2w/eGFP reporter was generated in H1 hESCs via gene editing (TALENs, electroporation of 1 μg linearized vector and 2.5 μg of each TALEN plasmid into 1 × 10^6 H1 cells, puromycin selection at 0.5 μg/mL, and Cre recombinase (400 ng per 1 × 10^6 cells) for cassette removal). In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). CFU assay medium contained 100 ng/mL recombinant murine stem cell factor, 10 ng/mL recombinant murine interleukin-3, 10 ng/mL recombinant human interleukin-6, and 3 U/mL human erythropoietin, with endothelial cell assays using 100 ng/mL vascular endothelial growth factor. In vivo analysis included mouse embryos at E10.0, E11, E12, E14, with fractionation of endothelial cells based on CD61 expression (CD61 high, CD61 low, and CD61 − subpopulations). No specific dose-response comparisons for differentiation conditions or therapeutic interventions were reported beyond qualitative observations of effect.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: CFU-erythrocyte derived from GATA2/eGFP+ HECs and HPCs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expressed in CFU-erythrocyte.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Adult hemoglobin component (beta-globin).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Erythroid differentiation from GATA2/eGFP+ HECs and HPCs during hPSC blood differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates that GATA2/eGFP+ HECs could give rise to HPCs representing definitive hematopoietic systems.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective study analyzed 4054 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to investigate the association of preoperative red blood cell distribution width (RDW) and hemoglobin-to-RDW ratio (HRR) with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). The findings demonstrated that elevated RDW and decreased HRR were robustly and independently associated with a higher risk of CA-AKI, suggesting their utility for early risk identification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Coronary Angiography (CAG) or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) involving contrast media administration.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study retrospectively analyzed 4054 patients undergoing CAG or PCI. Patients received contrast media as part of standard clinical practice. Excessive contrast media was defined as exceeding a calculated maximum dose (5 mL × weight (kg)/Scr at baseline (mg/dL)). document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between different physical activity (PA) patterns and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index in US adults, using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007-2018. The main findings indicate that regularly active individuals experience a substantial and significant reduction in the TyG index, offering sustained metabolic benefits. While weekend warriors and insufficiently active individuals show some improvement compared to inactive counterparts, they do not achieve comparable benefits to those who are regularly active. The association between PA and the TyG index in the regularly active group was more pronounced in males, individuals with higher education levels, and those without diabetes. A significant, non-linear, and negative relationship between weekly total PA and the TyG index was observed in non-inactive individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Activity (PA) patterns and Sedentary time
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physical activity was assessed via a questionnaire covering frequency and duration (minimum 10 uninterrupted minutes) of vigorous and moderate pursuits during a typical week. An aggregate PA score was computed (2 * vigorous PA + moderate PA). Participants were categorized into four groups: inactive (no PA), insufficiently active (< 150 min/week overall PA), weekend warriors (WWs, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in 1 or 2 sessions), and regularly active (RA, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in > 2 sessions). Total MVPA levels were approximately 120 min for insufficiently active, 290 min for WWs, and 540 min for RA. Comparisons between these patterns showed that even PA not meeting recommended standards was associated with a lower TyG index compared to inactivity. The study also explored significant, non-linear relationships between weekly total PA and the TyG index in non-inactive individuals, and between weekly sedentary time and the TyG index across various groups. No direct dose-response comparisons for specific PA amounts beyond pattern categorization were reported within this study's primary findings.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized discovery metabolomics and lipidomics to investigate plasma glycosphingolipids and other lipid metabolites as potential biomarkers for distinguishing aggressive from indolent prostate cancer (PCa) in treatment-naïve African-American and European-American men. The findings indicate that specific glycosphingolipid species, particularly trihexosylceramide and tetrahexosylceramide, along with other sphingolipids and triglycerides, are significantly associated with PCa aggressiveness. A five-sphingolipid signature demonstrated promising diagnostic accuracy comparable to or exceeding PSA, suggesting their utility as novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and highlighting their role in related metabolic networks and genetic alterations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery via metabolomics and lipidomics
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An observational study conducted on plasma samples from 159 men with treatment-naïve prostate cancer, utilizing ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). The study focused on identifying biomarkers for PCa aggressiveness (Grade Group 1 vs. Grade Groups 2-5, low vs. intermediate/high aggressive PCa), without administering or comparing any therapeutic interventions or doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Deep deletion profile for HEXB.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme that removes sugar moieties from tetrahexosylceramides.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic alterations in PCa tissue; correlation with PCa aggressiveness.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Putative biomarker pattern correlating with genetic alterations in PCa tissue, suggesting a role in PCa aggressiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in severe patients compared to mild patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A specific hexosylceramide lipid.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differentiating mild and severe COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of COVID-19 severity (higher in severe patients).

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean serum levels were 50.77  1 19.15 ng/mL in women and 39.58  1 9.84 ng/mL in men, indicating ~1.5-fold higher levels in women. These levels were lower than those causing vascular barrier damage ( 35  5g/mL).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Participates in the inflammatory response, attracts progenitor cells, promotes endothelial regeneration, and is abundantly expressed during atherogenesis, although high levels can promote endothelial dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sex differences in older adults, particularly in postmenopausal women in response to RONS generation, and during inflammatory response, atherogenesis, and inflammaging.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can be used to assess endothelial regeneration and the extent of damage in inflammaging, especially when jointly tested with EPCs. Highly related to the development of atherosclerosis and associated diseases (diabetes, ischemic stroke, hypertension).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to establish comprehensive reference intervals for novel circulating biomarkers of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and hepatic regeneration in healthy human volunteers. It investigated intra- and interindividual variability, as well as diurnal variation, to provide robust data for interpreting exploratory clinical DILI studies and assisting biomarker qualification by regulatory authorities.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study for establishing reference intervals of circulating biomarkers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved serum sample collection from 227 healthy volunteers in a cross-sectional study (single sample). Additionally, 25 subjects underwent weekly serial sampling over 3 weeks, and 23 subjects had intensive 24-hour blood sampling every 3 hours after a 10-h overnight fast and standardized meals. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved, as the focus was on establishing reference intervals and assessing natural variability in healthy subjects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reference intervals established; levels significantly influenced by age; intra-individual variability non-significant; consistent with previous large studies.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference intervals based on the 97.5% quantile (90% CI) and consistent with previous studies. Age was identified as a significant fixed effect contributing to interindividual variability. Intra-individual variability found to be non-significant, with no significant impact of diurnal variation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Monitors apoptotic-necrotic dynamics; associated with DILI and biological processes where age is a factor for variability.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Establishing reference ranges in healthy human volunteers, characterizing natural variability, diurnal variation, and the influence of age on serum levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential to improve DILI prediction and hepatic regeneration assessment. Age is a key factor for interindividual variability, suggesting age-stratified reference intervals are necessary for accurate diagnostic interpretation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased (P < 0.05) in the intervention group compared to baseline and control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Good cholesterol, involved in reverse cholesterol transport, removing excess cholesterol from arteries.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Rehabilitation training (RT) or aerobic exercise therapy (ET) in CAD patients after PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels indicate improved cardiovascular health, reduced risk of atherosclerosis and CAD, and improved lipid profiles.
