document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an observational cross-sectional study. Its primary objective is to assess the reliability of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and immune cell reactivity, alongside perceived pain and pressure pain thresholds, through nine repeated measurements in workers exposed to constant real-life occupational workloads. Secondary aims include assessing correlations between these biomarkers and pain measures, and comparing levels between groups with higher and lower upper-extremity physical workloads. The study also details screening for metabolic parameters to ensure participant eligibility and ultimately aims to clarify the predictive role of these biomarkers in the development of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and to inform work-related stress-recovery concepts.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exposure to real-life occupational workloads
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study compares two groups: an 'exposed group' with higher upper-extremity physical workloads (exceeding the Action Limit of TLV for HAL, with daily repetitive strain for >=4 days/week and >=20 hours/week) and an 'unexposed group' (office workers) with lower upper-extremity physical workloads (not exceeding TLV for HAL). Participants will undergo nine repeated measurements of blood samples and pain assessments once every two weeks. The study assesses reliability and compares biomarker levels between these workload groups, rather than evaluating a therapeutic dose-response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported (screening parameter).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolic blood parameter; generally indicative of lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Screening for participant eligibility to verify absence of acute infection or metabolic diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator for acute infection or metabolic diseases, used for participant eligibility.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated LRP1 expression, circulating soluble LRP1 (sLRP1) levels, and myocardial lipid content in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (IDCM) patients compared to healthy controls, and assessed the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in sLRP1 secretion. Key findings include increased circulating sLRP1, higher myocardial collagen and triglyceride content, and elevated LRP1 alpha chain expression in myocardial vessels of IDCM patients, with sLRP1 release found to be independent of the exosome pathway and not associated with blood lipid parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating disease pathogenesis and biomarker identification in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Observational and diagnostic study comparing IDCM patients (n=20 for plasma, n=9 for tissue) with age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=15 for plasma, n=5 for tissue). Myocardial tissue samples were from explanted hearts. The study also included a comparison of hypercholesterolemic and normocholesterolemic patients. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No association between sLRP1 levels and any of the lipid parameters, including HDL (r = -0.11, P = 0.67)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: High-density lipoprotein, involved in reverse cholesterol transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM), correlation with circulating sLRP1.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Circulating sLRP1 levels are not correlated with blood HDL in IDCM patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.72) or without pDPN group (P = 0.30); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.59).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport, often referred to as 'good cholesterol'.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change, suggesting no alteration in this cardiovascular risk indicator.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of early first-trimester tubular (urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1) and glomerular (eGFR) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). It concluded that elevated first-trimester urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc) and, to a lesser extent, eGFR, are associated with increased PE risk. Notably, uNGALcc, especially when combined with clinical factors like BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin, significantly improved PE prediction, indicating subclinical renal tubular and glomerular dysfunction as early markers of PE, while urinary KIM-1 and plasma NGAL were not predictive.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on diagnostic biomarker assessment for preeclampsia risk prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a prospective observational cohort study enrolling pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) and normotensive pregnant women without diabetes. Biomarkers were assessed at three gestational visits: V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks), V2 (21.7  1 1.4 weeks), and V3 (31.4  1 1.5 weeks), with primary focus on first-trimester (V1) values for preeclampsia (PE) prediction. Study groups included women with T1DM who developed PE (DM+PE+), T1DM women who remained normotensive (DM+PE-), and normotensive women without diabetes (DM-). All T1DM subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria at V1. No active intervention or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic/prognostic utility. Analysis included samples with specific attention to leukocyte-negative urine samples.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in DM+PE+ than in DM+PE 2 at V1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid transport; indicator of cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and subsequent Preeclampsia (DM+PE+), compared to those without Preeclampsia (DM+PE 2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with distinguishing clinical characteristics between DM+PE+ and DM+PE 2 groups at V1.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, prospective observational study investigated whether vitamin D metabolites (25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) and Vitamin D Binding Protein (VDBP), along with their ratios, could predict preeclampsia (PE) in women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM). The study found that higher concentrations of 1,25(OH)2D, lower concentrations of VDBP, and elevated 1,25(OH)2D/VDBP ratios in the second and third trimesters were significantly associated with and predictive of subsequent PE, while 25(OH)D, the standard metric for vitamin D status, did not predict PE.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal Prospective Observational Study on Preeclampsia Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons. Biomarker concentrations and clinical data were collected at three gestational visits: V1 (~12 weeks), V2 (~22 weeks), and V3 (~32 weeks). The study enrolled 151 women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM) and 24 non-diabetic controls, rigorously phenotyped and free of proteinuria and hypertension at enrolment. The primary analysis compared 23 T1DM women who developed preeclampsia (PE) with 24 matched T1DM women who remained normotensive. A secondary analysis compared normotensive T1DM women with non-diabetic controls. The cohort was largely vitamin D insufficient or deficient.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in T1DM women with PE (DM+PE+) than in normotensive T1DM women (DM+PE−) at the initial study visit.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport, removing cholesterol from arteries and transporting it to the liver for excretion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Initial study visit in pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM), associated with preeclampsia (PE) risk.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health; lower levels are associated with increased risk for preeclampsia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (reported in meta-analysis on post-menopausal women).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from cells back to the liver; high levels are associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein supplementation in post-menopausal women.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved cardiovascular health and reduced risk of chronic diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls, attributed to a higher prevalence of statin therapy

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: High-density lipoprotein, transports cholesterol from tissues back to the liver; protective against cardiovascular disease
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis with concurrent statin therapy
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes, with medication influencing levels

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: No significant changes in the whole group, but significant time interaction in subgroups.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes in the whole group (n=24) during the one-year training period. However, a significant time interaction (p < 0.001) was found when divided into subgroups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid metabolism; involved in reverse cholesterol transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training period in young soccer players, vitamin D supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health; variations might be influenced by training and diet.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: After 1-month of treatment, there was no significant difference in HDL levels between the high-effective Δhs-CRP (%) group (1.12 ± 0.32 mmol/L) and the low-effective group (1.09 ± 0.31 mmol/L, p = 0.432).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport, removing excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver; considered anti-atherogenic.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Statin-based lipid-lowering strategies after 1-month of treatment in patients post-PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are generally associated with lower cardiovascular risk; no significant change observed with these specific lipid-lowering strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between different physical activity (PA) patterns and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index in US adults, using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007-2018. The main findings indicate that regularly active individuals experience a substantial and significant reduction in the TyG index, offering sustained metabolic benefits. While weekend warriors and insufficiently active individuals show some improvement compared to inactive counterparts, they do not achieve comparable benefits to those who are regularly active. The association between PA and the TyG index in the regularly active group was more pronounced in males, individuals with higher education levels, and those without diabetes. A significant, non-linear, and negative relationship between weekly total PA and the TyG index was observed in non-inactive individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Activity (PA) patterns and Sedentary time
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physical activity was assessed via a questionnaire covering frequency and duration (minimum 10 uninterrupted minutes) of vigorous and moderate pursuits during a typical week. An aggregate PA score was computed (2 * vigorous PA + moderate PA). Participants were categorized into four groups: inactive (no PA), insufficiently active (< 150 min/week overall PA), weekend warriors (WWs, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in 1 or 2 sessions), and regularly active (RA, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in > 2 sessions). Total MVPA levels were approximately 120 min for insufficiently active, 290 min for WWs, and 540 min for RA. Comparisons between these patterns showed that even PA not meeting recommended standards was associated with a lower TyG index compared to inactivity. The study also explored significant, non-linear relationships between weekly total PA and the TyG index in non-inactive individuals, and between weekly sedentary time and the TyG index across various groups. No direct dose-response comparisons for specific PA amounts beyond pattern categorization were reported within this study's primary findings.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood serum (inferred from general physiological measurement)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Favorable effects on HDL-C metabolism observed when engaging in physical activity that burns approximately 1200 to 1600 kcal per week (moderate physical activity 3-5 times/week, or about 7 to 14 miles) (cited from previous studies).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport; associated with cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Moderate physical activity burning 1200-1600 kcal/week (cited from previous research).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Favorable effects on HDL-C metabolism are linked to a reduced risk of coronary heart disease mortality.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inverse effect on HDL-C (due to folic acid supplementation); did not show a positive influence on lipids (TC, TG, LDL-C) by CoQ10.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: 'Good' cholesterol, helps remove excess cholesterol from arteries.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Folic acid supplementation in patients with T2DM; CoQ10 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates potentially worsened lipid profile (with folic acid), no improvement (with CoQ10).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. The key finding is that obesity largely explains the observed association between IR and AN, with no direct causal relationship found between IR and AN when obesity is accounted for, highlighting AN's utility as a non-invasive clinical marker for obesity-driven cardiometabolic risk and its ability to predict future Type 2 Diabetes risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating cardiometabolic risk factors and a diagnostic marker
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention or dose administered. Data was collected from 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children aged 6–17 years from a family-based cohort, focusing on associations and the utility of Acanthosis Nigricans as a screening tool for cardiometabolic risk factors, including extensive clinical tests and interviews on medical history, demographic, phenotypic, and environmental variables.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: negatively correlated; suggestive inverse correlation; associated
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively correlated with AN-q (p<0.05). Genetic correlations (ρG) were suggestive in nature between AN-q and HDL-C.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport; generally protective against atherosclerosis and considered 'good' cholesterol.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Observational study in non-diabetic Mexican American children, examined as a cardiometabolic risk factor; association with AN-q and cardiometabolic risk factors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health; lower levels are associated with increased cardiometabolic risk and dyslipidemia, suggesting increased cardiovascular risk in this population.

document_context_data.document_summary: This population-based cross-sectional study investigated the association between the monocyte to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) and carotid artery disease, including carotid atherosclerotic plaque (CAP) and intima-media thickness (CIMT), in low-income, middle-aged, and elderly residents of rural China. The study identified a significant association between a higher MHR and increased CAP prevalence, particularly in females, and suggested MHR as a vital indicator for early atherosclerosis recognition. However, no significant correlation was found between CIMT and MHR after adjusting for covariates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study (population-based cross-sectional)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study focused on identifying associations of naturally occurring biomarker levels, with the Monocytes to High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Ratio (MHR) analyzed across quartiles.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood (implied as a component of MHR from routine blood tests)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hinders LDL-C oxidation and monocyte entry into the vascular wall; inhibits the expression of monocyte tissue factors by inhibiting p38 activation and inositol phosphate kinase activity; serves as a neutralizer in the process of atherosclerosis.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Endothelial or vascular protection from inflammation and oxidative stress; inhibits monocyte activity and tissue factors.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Atherosclerotic process, dyslipidemia (as a component of MHR).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Protective factor against atherosclerosis; its relative abundance (in MHR calculation) indicates atherosclerosis risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant difference (P < 0.05) between non-diabetic and diabetic groups. Specific quantitative values for changes were not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Responsible for reverse cholesterol transport, removing excess cholesterol from tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress; comparison between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are generally considered beneficial and associated with lower risk of cardiovascular disease. Lower levels are often observed in diabetic individuals and associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most studies showed no alteration; one study reported a reduction in premanifest and manifest HD subjects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: High-density lipoprotein cholesterol, involved in reverse cholesterol transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD); lipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Generally not considered a reliable peripheral biomarker for HD due to inconsistent findings, though some reductions observed in specific cohorts.

biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Synthese: Hier wuerde die konsolidierte Zuverlaessigkeits-Zusammenfassung stehen.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly differentially expressed (P<0.05) between SLE-P and SLE-NP patients. Specific direction (higher/lower) for individual subclasses is not provided in the text but they were found to be different.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in reverse cholesterol transport; different subclasses have varied functions and lipid content in lipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Novel metabolomic signature associated with subclinical atherosclerosis in women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Part of a novel metabolomic signature associated with the presence of subclinical plaque in SLE.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

Increased from T0 (1.36 
	1.8 
	µg/mL) to T1 (engraftment: 2.68 
	2.2 
	µg/mL; p=0.0042) and then decreased at T2 (inpatient discharge: 0.79 
	1.4 
	µg/mL; p<0.0001) compared to T1. Overall, increased at engraftment compared to baseline, then returned towards baseline values at inpatient release.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An acute phase reactant and a sensitive marker of systemic inflammation, produced in the liver in response to inflammation or tumors.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) during inpatient time; blood profiling at enrollment (T0), engraftment (T1), and discharge (T2); post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reliable biomarker to monitor acute and regenerative inflammation status of alloSCT patients. Elevated levels indicate an acute pro-inflammatory status, acute infections, chronic inflammation, and correlate with a reduced probability of survival before stem-cell transplantation. Levels can be reduced by training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy was significantly associated with a decreased "Δhs-CRP (%) (β = -0.253, 95% CI: [-0.501 to -0.005], p = 0.045)". It also had an indirect negative effect on Δhs-CRP via ΔLDL-C (β = -0.300, p < 0.001). Intensive statin therapy had an indirect negative effect on Δhs-CRP via ΔLDL-C (β = -0.032, p = 0.043). Increased ΔLDL-C (%) was an independent predictor of elevated Δhs-CRP (%) (β = 0.487, 95% CI: [0.15–0.824], p = 0.005). Baseline hs-CRP was 2.68 ± 2.28 mg/L in the high-effective group vs. 1.25 ± 1.28 mg/L in the low-effective group (p < 0.001). After 1 month, follow-up hs-CRP was 1.00 ± 0.95 mg/L in the high-effective group vs. 2.15 ± 2.00 mg/L in the low-effective group (p < 0.001). The median Δhs-CRP (%) was -18.6%. No significant direct association was found with different types of statins (β = 0.135, p = 0.335) or intensive statin therapy (β = -0.112, p = 0.255).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An acute-phase reactant and systemic marker of inflammation produced by the liver in response to inflammatory cytokines; mediator of inflammatory reactions and an indicator of chronic systemic inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) treatment with different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (statin monotherapy vs. statin+ezetimibe, regular vs. intensive statin therapy, different statin types) in stable coronary artery disease patients over 1 month.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictor of inflammatory response and vascular disorders; elevated levels are related to a higher incidence of cardiovascular diseases and indicate systemic inflammation. Reduced levels suggest an anti-inflammatory effect, improved cardiovascular prognosis, and potentially alleviate atherosclerotic plaque progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of post-exercise milk consumption (500 mL) versus an energy-matched carbohydrate drink on recovery from a repeated sprinting and jumping protocol in female team-sport athletes. The strenuous protocol successfully induced muscle damage, leading to post-exercise decreases in muscle function (peak torque, countermovement jump, sprint performance, rate of force development) and increases in subjective muscle soreness and tiredness. Milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function, particularly for peak torque (knee extension/flexion at 180°/s) and countermovement jump height, and reduced perceived stress (DALDA B) at various time points (24h, 48h, 72h) post-exercise. The study concluded that milk may be a valuable recovery intervention for female team-sport athletes following this type of exercise, although its effects on serum creatine kinase, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, reactive strength index, and some sprint performances were unclear.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional intervention (Milk vs. Carbohydrate drink)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants immediately consumed either 500 mL of milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g Protein, 25.5 g Carbohydrate, 5.0 g Fat) or 500 mL of an energy-matched carbohydrate drink (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g Protein, 53.6 g Carbohydrate, 0.0 g Fat) following a whole-body sport and exercise protocol designed to induce muscle damage (15x20m maximal sprints and 8 sets of 10 plyometric jumps). The milk protein dose (17g) was noted to be potentially suboptimal for maximal protein synthesis compared to other studies. No dose-response comparisons were conducted, as a single volume of 500 mL was used for both interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: hsCRP levels did not significantly increase post-exercise, and milk had an unclear effect compared to carbohydrate. Baseline: MILK 1.0 "+/-" 0.6 mg/L, CHO 1.3 "+/-" 0.6 mg/L. Relative changes from baseline showed unclear outcomes for milk vs. carbohydrate across B-2h, B-24h, B-48h, and B-72h time points.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Systemic marker of inflammation, produced by the liver as an acute phase reactant.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-repeated sprinting and jumping exercise recovery in female team-sport athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation level, often elevated due to strenuous exercise-induced stress or damage. May not fully reflect total cytokine activity or correlate with muscle soreness in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute exhaustive exercise / Symptom-limited incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single session of acute exhaustive exercise was performed by 28 male chronic heart failure (CHF) participants (mean age 59.07  1 1.79 years). The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not affected (Table 3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not affected by acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline. Baseline levels were similarly elevated in all heart failure subgroups and declined comparably, resulting in no significant difference between subgroups (LVEF improvement vs. no LVEF improvement) at FUP6.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An acute-phase reactant and a general marker of systemic inflammation and tissue injury response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), comparing LVEF recovery subgroups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation. Its comparable decline across LVEF subgroups suggests a general inflammatory response rather than a differential indicator for LVEF recovery, though prolonged or intense inflammation is linked to adverse LV remodeling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: associated with higher risk (main effect), but no interaction with CHIP or AgeAccelHG
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Main effect on risk for all-cause mortality (coefficient = 0.09, p < 1.01 	 10-3). No interaction with CHIP for all-cause mortality (coefficient = 0.076, p < 0.29) or CHD (coefficient = -0.3, p < 0.82). Stratifying by hs-CRP levels (>2 mg/L) did not distinguish risk in CHIP+/AgeAccelHG+ individuals.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Acute phase reactant, a systemic marker of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of its role as an inflammation marker in relation to CHIP, epigenetic aging, and cardiovascular/mortality outcomes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: While a general marker of inflammation and associated with mortality, it is a poor discriminator of risk in CHIP carriers compared to AgeAccelHG.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-weeks of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) pre-loading on markers of inflammation (hsCRP, IL-6), muscle damage (CK), perceived muscle soreness, tissue tenderness, and lower limb performance (squat jump peak power, hamstring flexibility) in endurance-trained female runners after a single bout of downhill running (DHR). MIPS consumption attenuated inflammation (hsCRP) three days post-DHR but did not significantly impact perceived soreness, muscle damage markers, or other performance measures.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS, NO-Shotgun®) and eccentric exercise (Downhill Running, DHR).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) was consumed daily for 28 days (4 weeks) prior to a single bout of DHR, and 30 minutes before post-testing. One serving of MIPS was 21g. A control group received an isocaloric (28g maltodextrin) placebo. The DHR protocol involved a 60-minute run at a -10% gradient, at 75% VO2max (average speed 12.03  ± 0.4 km/hr). No dose-response comparisons for either the supplement or DHR protocol were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Elevated initially, then attenuated in MIPS group.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked at 24 h post-DHR (p = 0.06). A significant decrease was observed between 24 and 48 h post-DHR (p=0.04). At 72 h post-DHR, the MIPS group showed a moderate attenuation/decrease (-38.89% of baseline) compared to the CON group which showed a moderate increase and remained above baseline.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A general marker of systemic inflammation and an acute-phase reactant, stimulated by pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammatory response to exercise-induced muscle damage; attenuation suggests a reduced inflammatory response, while an increase signifies an inflammatory response.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Montmorency cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained cyclists undergoing three consecutive days of high-intensity simulated road cycle racing. Findings consistently showed that MC attenuated post-exercise oxidative stress, indicated by lower lipid hydroperoxides (LOOH), and inflammatory responses, evidenced by reduced interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), compared to a placebo. No significant effect was found on muscle damage markers (creatine kinase) or other cytokines (TNF-α, IL-8, and IL-1-β). This suggests that MC is effective in combating oxidative and inflammatory cascades induced by metabolically strenuous exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency Tart Cherry Concentrate (MC) Supplementation in conjunction with a high-intensity, simulated road cycling exercise protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Trained cyclists consumed 30 mL of Montmorency cherry concentrate or a placebo twice daily (8 am, 6 pm) for seven consecutive days (4 days pre-trial and throughout the 3-day trial period). The exercise protocol involved three consecutive days (days 5, 6, and 7 of supplementation) of a 109-minute simulated road cycling race, which included 66 sprints (5, 10, or 15 seconds) and specific time trials (2x2 min, 1x5 min). No dose-response comparisons for the MC supplement or exercise intensity were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: hsCRP responses were significantly lower in the MC group versus PLA (p < 0.05) across all time-points after baseline (F(1,7) = 2.534, p = 0.026). The PLA group showed a sharp increase following trial 1 which remained elevated, while MC attenuated this rise, resulting in a lower hsCRP response throughout the trial duration.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An acute-phase reactant and a sensitive systemic marker of inflammation, indicating secondary inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise inflammation during repeated days high-intensity stochastic cycling following Montmorency cherry concentrate supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates attenuated systemic inflammatory responses, suggesting a reduced inflammatory cascade following exercise, with implications for combating low-grade chronic inflammation and reducing cell damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 30 mL of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) or an energy-matched placebo twice per day (8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.) for eight consecutive days, including four days pre-trial and throughout the trial period. The MC contained 73.5 mg 7L 91 cyanidin-3-glucoside, 178.8 gallic acid equivalent 7L 91 total phenolic content, and a TEAC of 0.58 trolox equivalents 7L 91. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased overall, but unchanged between groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma hsCRP significantly increased in both groups over 72 h following the trial (F(1,8)=20.298, p<0.001,  72=0.592). No significant group or interaction effects were found, indicating no difference between MC and PLA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Acute-phase protein and systemic marker of inflammation, with expression influenced by IL-6.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-prolonged intermittent sprint activity (adapted Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test) with MC supplementation vs. placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammatory response; lack of group difference suggests MC supplementation did not significantly affect this marker, despite observed IL-6 changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether pre-exercise ascorbic acid supplementation influenced antioxidant defenses, glucose metabolism, inflammation, and muscle damage in untrained healthy adults following a single bout of moderate-intensity cycling. Findings indicated that ascorbic acid supplementation reduced plasma Malondialdehyde (MDA) and increased Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP), while also modulating glucose levels and attenuating exercise-induced changes in albumin and total protein. While moderate-intensity cycling led to an increase in red blood cell Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) activity and low-grade muscle damage (Total Creatine Kinase), it did not induce systemic inflammation or lipid peroxidation. Ascorbic acid supplementation appeared to mitigate the exercise-induced increase in SOD activity but did not significantly prevent muscle damage or affect other inflammatory/damage markers such as hsCRP, LDH, CK-MB, GPx, or Catalase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supplementation combined with a single bout of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects received 1000 mg of ascorbic acid (or placebo) orally 5 minutes prior to a 30-minute indoor cycling session. Exercise intensity was set at 65–75% of maximum heart rate, which was predicted by an age-based equation. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either ascorbic acid or exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Concentrations remained unchanged in subjects with or without vitamin C supplement within 30 min post-exercise (p>0.05, implied).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An acute-phase protein and a sensitive biomarker of inflammation in the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute aerobic exercise (indoor cycling) in untrained healthy adults, with or without ascorbic acid supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change suggests that this specific exercise bout, with or without ascorbic acid, did not induce a substantial acute systemic inflammatory response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall median (IQR) at baseline was 18 (9–33) ng/L. Subphenotype 2 showed the highest median levels at baseline and elevated levels as part of Subset D. Lowest median hs-troponin T was observed in subphenotype 3 at baseline.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates myocardial injury or necrosis, serving as a marker of cardiac damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and longitudinal assessment in HFrEF patients for subphenotype identification, particularly defining Subphenotypes 2 (higher levels, worse outcomes) and 3 (lower median, but still worse outcomes).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are strongly associated with subphenotype 2, indicating significant myocardial injury and poorer prognosis. Although levels are lower in subphenotype 3, it is also linked to worse outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were observed in HDL-C levels between the FOPS and control groups at any time point.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout the study, comparing FOPS and control groups during exercise and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No differential impact of FOPS or exercise conditions was noted on this marker of cardiovascular health, suggesting its stability under these specific experimental parameters.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not explicitly reported as a change; its baseline level served as a variable in machine learning models.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Specific quantitative data or changes were not reported in the provided chunks; it was included as a blood-based biomarker in predictive models for depressive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used as a baseline blood-based biomarker in secondary analysis of EUFEST and RAISE-ETP trials, collected from patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, for inclusion in machine learning models predicting depressive symptoms and episodes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular and metabolic health; used as a variable to evaluate its contribution to predicting depressive symptoms or post-psychotic depressive episodes in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with increasing PGI/PGII quartiles. Higher MPO quartiles associated with decreased levels (P < 0.001).

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study was an observational, cross-sectional comparison involving 28 male collegiate athletes (including weight-lifting and basketball teams) who reported engaging in strength training for at least one hour per day, five times per week, versus 29 age-matched untrained controls. No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.
