document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility and limitations of Body Mass Index (BMI) compared to Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)-derived percent body fat and fasting leptin and insulin levels for diagnosing and classifying obesity in adults. It concluded that BMI significantly underestimates obesity prevalence, especially in women and with advancing age, due to its inability to distinguish lean from fat mass. The study proposed new, lower gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) and found that leptin levels, unlike insulin, enhance the accuracy of BMI estimates for adiposity, particularly in women and when DXA is unavailable. The integration of leptin and DXA is suggested for more precise obesity characterization and management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Comparison and Biomarker Analysis for Obesity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional study conducted a retrospective review of BMI calculations, DXA scans, and fasting blood levels of leptin and insulin from 9,088 adults between 1998 and 2009. Measurements for BMI, DXA (providing simultaneous muscle, bone mass, and adiposity data), and blood work (fasting leptin and insulin drawn between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm) were taken within 3 weeks of each other. The study evaluated and compared the accuracy and classification rates of these metrics for obesity, proposing new gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) based on body fat and leptin corrections. No therapeutic intervention dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lack of relationship between insulin and percent body fat. Insulin levels did not add any new information to the equation for BMI adjustment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates glucose metabolism and energy storage, but showed no relationship with percent body fat in this study.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Obesity classification and adjustment of BMI for adiposity assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Does not improve precision of BMI adjustment for obesity diagnosis; not correlated with obesity rates.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significant effect of exercise (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant effects of exercise (PBO trial) were shown (P < 0.001). No other immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding on this modulator. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of insulin to exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Regulates blood glucose levels and promotes anabolic processes/energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Reflects the metabolic response and glucose regulation during exercise. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a single 6g dose of citrulline malate (CM) supplementation on muscle recovery after a high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session in untrained young adult men, examining functional, metabolic, anabolic, and physiological markers. The findings concluded that CM supplementation does not improve the muscle recovery process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Citrulline Malate (CM) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single oral dose of 6 g of citrulline malate (CM) was administered 60 minutes pre-workout, dissolved in 200 mL water. Participants then performed a single session of high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) consisting of 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions at 90% of 10RM for leg press and hack squat exercises, with 2 min rest between sets and exercises, performed with a 1s concentric:2s eccentric cadence. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and no significant treatment × time interaction was found for any measured variables, indicating CM did not improve recovery compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes or treatment × time interactions were reported for insulin levels with CM supplementation versus placebo during the recovery period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A peptide hormone that regulates carbohydrate, fat, and protein metabolism, primarily promoting glucose uptake and storage, and acting as an anabolic agent.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blood samples collected pre- and post-exercise, and immediately after muscular fatigue tests (24, 48, and 72 h after RE session) during CM or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic regulation, nutrient partitioning, and anabolic processes crucial for recovery and muscle adaptation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels can vary depending on whether the subject had just had a meal or was fasted overnight. Specific quantitative data not provided in this context.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates blood glucose levels and metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Feeding status (fed or fasted).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates variability requiring consistent feeding conditions for reliable measurement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated endogenous Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with rtPA, aiming to determine its association with functional outcome and compare its levels to healthy controls and at 3 months post-stroke. Key findings indicate that plasma GLP-1 levels are elevated in acute stroke patients compared to healthy individuals and remain stable at 3 months, but these endogenous levels were not associated with functional outcome. The study also highlighted insulin resistance as a predictor for unfavorable stroke outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) for ischemic stroke; the study primarily investigated endogenous biomarker levels rather than the therapeutic effect or specific dosing of rtPA itself.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: All ischemic stroke patients received conventional rtPA treatment as part of their standard care, typically on hospital day 2-4. Specific dose details of rtPA are not provided as the study focused on observational monitoring of endogenous biomarker levels and their correlation with stroke outcome, without exogenous administration or dose comparisons of GLP-1 or rtPA.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in fasting levels between acute stroke patients (13.2 values) and healthy controls (9.8 values; p = 0.20), nor between the acute phase (14.7 values) and 3 months post-stroke (14.1 values; p = 0.81) in patients. Study power was not calculated to detect these differences.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates blood glucose by facilitating glucose uptake into cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fasting state in acute ischemic stroke patients compared to healthy controls and longitudinally between acute phase and 3 months post-stroke.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Fasting insulin levels do not significantly differ between acute stroke patients and healthy controls or over 3 months post-stroke, though this finding might be limited by study power.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proof-of-concept study investigated whether a single session of High-Intensity Training (HIT) could restore impaired counterregulatory hormonal, symptomatic, and cognitive responses to subsequent insulin-induced hypoglycemia in people with type 1 diabetes and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH). The findings supported the hypothesis that IAH develops as a habituated response, demonstrating that HIT significantly amplified adrenaline responses and total symptom awareness during subsequent hypoglycemia, although it also led to a significant prolongation of cognitive reaction time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity training (HIT) compared to controlled rest
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single HIT session lasting 20 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down, with 4 x 30-second cycle sprints at 150% of maximum wattage (V̇O2peak assessment) interspersed with 2-minute recovery periods. Participants aimed for >90% peak heart rate. This was directly compared to 20 minutes of seated rest, and no dose-response comparisons for HIT were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported in this document chunk (This chunk describes methods, not comparative results of HIT vs. Rest on endogenous insulin levels).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Infusion rate of 1.5 mU kg-1 min-1 was maintained during the clamp study after initial priming. Measured endogenous levels or comparative effects were not quantified in this chunk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key hormone regulating blood glucose, promoting glucose uptake by cells and inhibiting hepatic glucose production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hyperinsulinaemic–hypoglycaemic clamp study where insulin was infused to induce controlled hypoglycaemia, following either High-Intensity Training or controlled rest.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Central to the experimental induction of hypoglycaemia in this study, allowing for the standardized assessment of counterregulatory responses in type 1 diabetes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in obese; increased post-exercise, more prolonged in obese
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Obese females had significantly higher levels than normal weight females across all time points (mean difference: 787 pg/ml, 174%, p = 0.03). It significantly increased 5 minutes post-exercise in both groups (normal weight: +108%, obese: +129%). In normal weight females, it returned to baseline by 1 hour, while in obese females, it remained elevated at 1 hour post-exercise and returned to baseline by 24 hours.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates glucose metabolism, energy storage, and postprandial glucose handling, with indirect effects on bone.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest and 5 minutes/1 hour/24 hours post-plyometric exercise (after a high carbohydrate breakfast) in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher resting levels in obese females indicate poorer metabolic health and insulin resistance. The higher and more prolonged post-exercise elevation in obese females suggests impaired metabolic recovery and potential hyperinsulinemia, indicating altered insulin sensitivity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake; involved in insulin resistance
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes and insulin resistance

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma insulin response was raised compared with placebo/control groups following acute SP supplementation and soy with carbohydrates after exercise recovery or pre-/during exercise. Soy protein and its peptides can also enhance pancreatic   ffd   cell sensitivity, promoting insulin secretion.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A hormone that regulates glucose metabolism and promotes anabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute SP or SP+CHO supplementation after endurance cycling recovery, after moderate endurance training, or pre-/during exercise; general consumption of soy protein and its peptides.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an improved glycemic response, enhanced pancreatic   ffd   cell sensitivity, and potential for increased nutrient uptake and anabolic signaling, beneficial for energy metabolism and muscle adaptation.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly different between SBMA and controls (P_adj < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone that regulates blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake by cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Adult male patients with SBMA compared to age-matched healthy controls (NIH cohort).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General health indicator; differences linked to SBMA may suggest impaired glucose metabolism or insulin sensitivity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (males), similar trend but not significant (females), unchanged (females PRE to MID)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in male COMP from PRE to MID (p < 0.001), which was statistically significant compared to male CTRL (p < 0.001). Female COMP showed a similar but not statistically significant trend in reduction. No significant change was observed within female COMP or CTRL from PRE to MID. A significant difference in insulin between female COMP and CTRL was noted at baseline (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A peptide hormone crucial for regulating carbohydrate and fat metabolism, promoting glucose uptake by cells, and fostering anabolism (e.g., protein synthesis), and regulating blood glucose levels.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) in physique athletes, leading to reduced blood glucose and altered metabolic states due to severe energy restriction.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels, especially in males, indicate increased insulin sensitivity, glucose utilization, or an energy deficit, reflecting the metabolic response and adaptation to energy deficit, potentially impacting nutrient utilization and anabolic processes. Baseline differences in females may reflect inherent physiological or metabolic status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between different physical activity (PA) patterns and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index in US adults, using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007-2018. The main findings indicate that regularly active individuals experience a substantial and significant reduction in the TyG index, offering sustained metabolic benefits. While weekend warriors and insufficiently active individuals show some improvement compared to inactive counterparts, they do not achieve comparable benefits to those who are regularly active. The association between PA and the TyG index in the regularly active group was more pronounced in males, individuals with higher education levels, and those without diabetes. A significant, non-linear, and negative relationship between weekly total PA and the TyG index was observed in non-inactive individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Activity (PA) patterns and Sedentary time
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physical activity was assessed via a questionnaire covering frequency and duration (minimum 10 uninterrupted minutes) of vigorous and moderate pursuits during a typical week. An aggregate PA score was computed (2 * vigorous PA + moderate PA). Participants were categorized into four groups: inactive (no PA), insufficiently active (< 150 min/week overall PA), weekend warriors (WWs, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in 1 or 2 sessions), and regularly active (RA, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in > 2 sessions). Total MVPA levels were approximately 120 min for insufficiently active, 290 min for WWs, and 540 min for RA. Comparisons between these patterns showed that even PA not meeting recommended standards was associated with a lower TyG index compared to inactivity. The study also explored significant, non-linear relationships between weekly total PA and the TyG index in non-inactive individuals, and between weekly sedentary time and the TyG index across various groups. No direct dose-response comparisons for specific PA amounts beyond pattern categorization were reported within this study's primary findings.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood (inferred, based on general physiological measurement)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels observed in children who engage in lower amounts of PA or have prolonged sedentary time (cited from previous studies).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates glucose metabolism; a key component of insulin resistance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children engaging in lower amounts of physical activity or having prolonged sedentary time (general knowledge/previous research).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels indicate decreased insulin sensitivity and increased insulin resistance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dropped proportionally after both matches, reaching approximately 30% of initial levels after the second match for both athletes.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (after matches).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a shift in energy metabolism during exercise, favoring glucose utilization from stores rather than uptake, reflecting a gluco-insulinic response and the high-intensity nature of a BVb competition day.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not explicitly reported as a change; its baseline level served as a variable in machine learning models.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Specific quantitative data or changes were not reported in the provided chunks; it was included as a blood-based biomarker in predictive models for depressive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of blood glucose levels and overall energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used as a baseline blood-based biomarker in secondary analysis of EUFEST and RAISE-ETP trials, collected from patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, for inclusion in machine learning models predicting depressive symptoms and episodes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General indicator of metabolic health; used as a variable to evaluate its contribution to predicting depressive symptoms or post-psychotic depressive episodes in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. The key finding is that obesity largely explains the observed association between IR and AN, with no direct causal relationship found between IR and AN when obesity is accounted for, highlighting AN's utility as a non-invasive clinical marker for obesity-driven cardiometabolic risk and its ability to predict future Type 2 Diabetes risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in both male and female COMP groups (p < 0.001) during competition preparation (PRE to MID) compared to CTRL. These decreases were associated with higher loss in FFM. Levels did not significantly change from MID to POST in COMP groups, with female COMP showing persistently lower levels compared to CTRL (p < 0.05) after MID.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Crucial hormone for muscle development, growth, cell proliferation, tissue repair, and anabolism, playing a significant role in metabolism and regulated by nutrition.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During intense energy restriction and physical training in physique athletes' competition preparation (PRE to MID) and subsequent recovery (MID to POST), specifically under conditions of reduced energy intake and low energy availability.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a potential biomarker for monitoring physiological stress and an anabolic deficit, reflecting a compromised anabolic state and correlation with loss in fat-free mass under energy restriction. Lower levels suggest a catabolic state or reduced anabolic drive.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) on individual quadriceps muscle thickness and circulating biomarkers related to muscle atrophy and hypertrophy in the early postoperative phase. It found severe atrophy in the vastus intermedius (VI) and significant reductions in other quadriceps muscle thicknesses (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Medialis Obliquus). Circulating IGF-1 levels were significantly reduced, while myostatin levels showed a slight increase with a medium effect size, contributing to the observed muscle atrophy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) surgery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fourteen recreationally active patients (10 men, 4 women) with unilateral ACL injuries underwent reconstructive surgery. Measurements were taken at a preoperative visit (PRE) and at two postoperative visits (PO1: three days post-surgery; PO2: seven days post-surgery). No dose-response comparisons or variations in surgical method/intensity were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced throughout the entire period after ACLR, with large effect sizes between PRE and PO1 (d = 0.84) and between PRE and PO2 (d = 0.82).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Promotes muscle hypertrophy by activating Akt/mTOR signaling; contributes to muscle regeneration and the healing process of connective tissue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early phase of recovery after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced levels indicate impaired potential for muscle hypertrophy and recovery, contributing to post-surgical muscle atrophy. Maintaining levels may offer a way to safely restore muscle to its pre-injury condition.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes the IMPROVE trial, a four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating a novel home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training program (along with individual components and controls) on cognitive function, physical performance, mood, and quality of life in older (≥50) ICU survivors with delirium. The study aims to identify improvements and understand the underlying pathophysiology, hypothesizing beneficial changes in neurotrophic factors (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), and a reduction in inflammatory (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, CRP) and glial activation (S-100β, GFAP) biomarkers, as well as investigating AD-related markers like APOE genotype and Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training delivered via Internet-based videoconference. The study also investigates individual components (physical exercise only, cognitive training only) and control interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a four-arm randomized controlled trial. Active cognitive training involves facilitator-led online modules (Posit Science, Inc. Brain HQ) for 45 minutes, 2 days/week for 3 months. Active physical exercise is multi-modal, seated aerobic and progressive resistance training for 45 minutes, 3 times/week for 3 months, delivered via videoconference at moderate intensity (RPE 5-6 on a 10-point scale). Control groups receive matched frequency cognitive control modules and gentle seated stretching. This protocol does not report dose-response comparisons, focusing on comparisons between the four distinct intervention arms.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hypothesized increase due to combined physical and cognitive training; specific quantitative data not reported as this is a study protocol describing intent to measure changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Functions as an anabolic hormone and neurotrophic factor, enhancing neural proliferation, angiogenesis, neurogenesis, and supporting neuron survival, growth, and differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined physical exercise and cognitive training intervention in older ICU survivors with delirium-induced cognitive impairment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cognitive function, neural function, and brain health, associated with potential for recovery from post-ICU cognitive impairment and delaying Alzheimer disease/dementias. Maximizes effects of cognitive stimulation and is a potential therapeutic target.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery and characterization for intervertebral disc degeneration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved proteomic profiling and histological grading of human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissues and matched plasma from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy. IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased significantly from pre to post in all groups, then increased from post to recovery, with overall lower levels in combined HC users at baseline and recovery compared to naturally menstruating females
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Naturally menstruating females had significantly higher IGF-1 at pre than combined HC users (p=0.002). All groups (combined HC, progestin-only HC, naturally menstruating females) showed significant decreases from pre to post (p=0.007, p<0.001, and p<0.001, respectively) after ~23 weeks of LEA. All groups also showed significant increases from post to recovery (p=0.028, p<0.001, and p<0.001, respectively), with levels comparable to pre-treatment in most cases. At recovery, IGF-1 was significantly higher in progestin-only users (p=0.028) and naturally menstruating females (p=0.002) than combined HC users. A significant group*time interaction was observed (F=3.020, p=0.025).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Insulin-like Growth Factor 1, primarily produced by the liver in response to Growth Hormone (GH), mediating the GH-IGF-1 axis. It is crucial for cell growth, metabolism, tissue repair, muscle protein synthesis, hypertrophy, and inhibition of muscle protein breakdown
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by diet and physical training in female physique athletes (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), with a comparative analysis across combined hormonal contraceptive users, progestin-only hormonal contraceptive users, and naturally menstruating females at pre, post, and recovery time points
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A comparable decrease in all groups indicates negative endocrine consequences of LEA, affecting training adaptations, muscle maintenance, and overall health, potentially due to LEA-induced GH resistance. It serves as an indicator of anabolic status and overall metabolic health, reflecting potential for tissue growth and repair, and can be a biomarker for short-term LEA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. The investigation focused on age-dependent differences in scaffold properties and their influence on BM-MSC osteogenic differentiation, rather than dose-response comparisons of a therapeutic agent.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in the protein concentration of IGF-I in DBCM produced from either young or old individuals.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Potent anabolic growth factor involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, and tissue regeneration, including bone formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of soluble factors in DBCM from young vs. old bone donors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates that IGF-I concentration in DBCM is not influenced by bone donor age, suggesting it's not the direct cause of differential osteoinductive effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective single-center study investigated the relationship between an impaired Growth Hormone (GH)-Insulin-like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) axis and cardiac wasting (reduced left ventricular mass) in 307 advanced cancer patients. The findings reveal that reduced LV mass is associated with an imbalance in the GH-IGF-I axis, characterized by higher plasma GH levels and a lower IGF-I/GH ratio, suggesting acquired GH resistance. This resistance is particularly evident in patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss, and higher baseline IGF-I was associated with a subsequent decline in relative LV mass.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and longitudinal study (with follow-up for 85 patients) assessing baseline characteristics and follow-up changes in GH-IGF-I axis parameters. No intervention or dose was administered. Patient stratification involved grouping by echocardiographic left ventricular mass/height^2 tertiles (women: <50, 50–61, >61 g/m^2; men: <60, 60–74, >74 g/m^2) and by the presence of wasting syndrome (BMI <24 kg/m^2 and ≥5% weight loss in the prior 12 months).

Levels were similar in patients with wasting syndrome. Higher baseline IGF-I (≥98.22 ng/mL) was associated with a reduction in LV mass during follow-up (r = -0.318, p=0.003).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV) with reduced left ventricular mass (cardiac wasting), presence of wasting syndrome, and during follow-up for LV mass changes.

Higher baseline levels predict a greater subsequent decline in LV mass over time, suggesting its role in cardiac wasting progression. Stable levels across LV mass tertiles and similar levels in wasting syndrome, combined with high GH, indicate impaired GH-IGF-I axis responsiveness and acquired GH resistance in advanced cancer patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels are increased by GH, but are significantly lower in osteoporotic women with poor bone quality and in subjects who sustained a stress fracture; reduced concentrations are associated with increased fracture risk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in muscle mass regulation (stimulating anabolism with GH) and positively correlated with bone quality and bone mineral density (BMD).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Training adaptations, muscle mass regulation, osteoporosis, poor bone quality, fracture risk, stress fracture development.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potentially a useful biomarker for monitoring muscle mass regulation, training adaptations, and bone quality/density; lower levels indicate poor bone health and increased risk of fracture and stress fracture development.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of various post-exercise recovery strategies (active recovery, cold water immersion, massage, and passive recovery) on subjective and objective fatigue markers in 46 recreational male runners after a competitive half-marathon. The findings indicate that cold water immersion and massage were effective in improving subjective fatigue measures, such as muscle soreness and perceived recovery/stress, compared to passive recovery. However, active recovery was largely ineffective or even detrimental, worsening subjective recovery and negatively impacting certain objective markers (creatine kinase, free-testosterone). Overall, none of the recovery interventions demonstrated beneficial effects on objective physiological markers of fatigue.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise recovery interventions (Active Recovery (ACT), Cold Water Immersion (CWI), Massage (MAS), and Passive Recovery (PAS)) following a half-marathon race.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
46 recreational male runners completed a competitive half-marathon (average time 107-116 min, 86.2%-92.9% of anaerobic threshold, 450 m altitude climb). Within 15 minutes post-race, a single application of one of four recovery protocols was performed: Passive Recovery (PAS) was 15 min sitting at rest; Active Recovery (ACT) was 15 min sub-maximal jogging at 60% anaerobic threshold; Cold Water Immersion (CWI) involved 15 min of lower limb immersion up to the iliac crest in 15 
	1
	C water, with circular leg motions every 2 min; and Massage (MAS) consisted of 20 min of classical sports massage (effleurage, petrissage, friction), split into 5 min per leg in prone and supine positions, performed by certified sports scientists. No dose-response comparisons for the overall half-marathon intensity or the recovery interventions were explicitly reported, though the CWI protocol was chosen based on existing dose-response evidence.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The half-marathon itself altered IGF-1 levels. Massage (MAS) resulted in slightly lower IGF-1 levels at 24 hours post-race compared to passive recovery (PAS) (ES = -0.34), suggesting a small harmful effect. No beneficial effects were observed for active recovery (ACT) or cold water immersion (CWI).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A growth factor that mediates cell growth, anabolism, tissue repair, and muscle regeneration, and is involved in metabolic and neurohumoral regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following a half-marathon race, particularly after massage, and generally after other recovery strategies.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anabolic potential and tissue repair processes; lower levels suggest suppressed growth and recovery mechanisms or impaired physiological recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes or specific effects reported related to the intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone promoting cell growth and proliferation, involved in anabolic processes and bone metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment in elite male rowers undergoing high or low calcium dietary interventions and intense rowing exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No specific performance or health indicator was reported related to the calcium intervention, suggesting no acute impact on IGF-1 levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes a multi-round Delphi expert consensus process to identify and prioritize 14 key biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies. The identified biomarkers encompass physiological, inflammatory, functional, and genetic/epigenetic domains. The study outlines the methodology, discusses the suitability of biomarkers for different intervention durations, and identifies future research needs regarding biomarker standardization and early life application, concluding with a preference for composite biomarkers due to the complexity of aging.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Expert consensus methodology (Delphi method) for identifying biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies (nutritional, lifestyle, or pharmacological).
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study utilized a 3-round online Delphi method, starting with 116 experts in Round 1 and concluding with 60 experts in Round 3, out of 460 invited international panel members. Consensus for statements was defined as ">=70%" agreement, with "51-69%" indicating moderate agreement and "

	<=50%" leading to removal. Initially, 460 biomarkers were suggested, leading to 20 being appraised in detail. The consensus level for the 14 recommended biomarkers ranged from 70% to 98%. The identified biomarkers were deemed more suitable for medium- (3-6 months) and long-term (">=6 months") interventions, and less suitable for acute or short-term ("<3 months") interventions, as short-term changes are likely homeostatic responses with limited long-term significance for aging. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were investigated as this was a consensus-building study on biomarker utility.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Achieved 70% agreement in expert panel consensus, classified as minimal burden, but received the lowest agreement among the 14 recommended biomarkers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates growth, metabolism, and cellular processes; involved in physiological aging processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identified by expert consensus via Delphi method for use in human intervention studies on aging and for assessment of the aging process.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential outcome measure for longevity-promoting interventions, indicator of biological age, and for harmonizing outcome measures in future intervention studies.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study was an observational, cross-sectional comparison involving 28 male collegiate athletes (including weight-lifting and basketball teams) who reported engaging in strength training for at least one hour per day, five times per week, versus 29 age-matched untrained controls. No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in strength-training athletes (324 ± 80 ng/ml) compared to untrained controls (263 ± 134 ng/ml). Negatively correlated with age (β = -34.27 ± 8.89, p <0.001) and positively correlated with height (β = 360.5 ± 167.0, p = 0.035), fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference value for healthy young males: 293 ± 114 ng/ml (comparable to reported normal value of 297 ± 10 ng/ml). Athlete group: 324 ± 80 ng/ml; Control group: 263 ± 134 ng/ml.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Downstream molecule of growth hormone (GH); increases protein synthesis in skeletal muscle, leading to accelerated regeneration and hypertrophic effects; activates muscular satellite cells and counteracts muscle function decline.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy young males (reference value determination), comparison between strength-training athletes and untrained controls, correlation analysis with age, height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure. Surrogate for GH/IGF-1 axis activation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels in athletes suggest positive association with physical training; linked to growth, muscle parameters, and overall physical activity, implying significance in athletic performance and development. Establishes normal range and provides reference for anti-doping applications.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: dynamic responses (peak at 0h for SE, minimum at 24h for MS), negatively correlated with miR-532
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peak values observed 0 h post-exercise for Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) protocol (p < 0.05), whereas minimum values observed after 24 h recovery for Maximum Strength (MS) protocol (p < 0.05). Showed a significant negative correlation with miR-532 (R = -0.33, p = 0.03).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone promoting growth, cell proliferation, anabolism, and metabolism, exerting positive effects on adaptation to resistance exercise, including muscle hypertrophy or connective tissue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Resistance Training, specifically Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Maximum Strength (MS) protocols, and general RT adaptation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for monitoring training responses and neuromuscular adaptations, indicating growth and recovery processes, and positive effects on adaptation to resistance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: undetectable in saliva samples extracted from cotton rolls
