biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Synthese: Hier wuerde die konsolidierte Zuverlaessigkeits-Zusammenfassung stehen.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed an integrative multi-platform meta-analysis of gene expression profiles from Affymetrix and Illumina datasets in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients and healthy controls to identify novel, robust diagnostic biomarkers. The analysis revealed 5 commonly differentially expressed genes and 28 novel 'gained' genes, suggesting their significant potential for early PDAC diagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Integrative meta-analysis of gene expression data for biomarker identification and diagnostic prediction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gene expression data from two independent cohorts of PDAC patients (Affymetrix: 18 PDAC patients; Illumina: 36 PDAC patients) and 18 healthy controls were integrated. Profiling was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) using Affymetrix GeneChip® Human Gene ST 1.0 Arrays and Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 Expression BeadChip microarray platforms. Data were integrated using an empirical Bayesian methodology (ComBat) for batch effect removal, and differential expression was analyzed with limma software, identifying genes with p<0.01 and at least 1.5-fold differential expression. The analysis identified 5 commonly differentially expressed genes (with individual ROC curve AUC > 0.9) and 28 novel 'gained' genes, which could discriminate PDAC patients from controls with an average sensitivity of 74.8% and specificity of 73.3% for individual gained genes, 100% sensitivity and 94% specificity for combined common genes, and 91% sensitivity and 87% specificity for combined gained genes. No dose-response comparisons were applicable as it is a diagnostic biomarker identification study.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patient samples (gene expression data); generally expressed in monocytes and macrophages.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Upregulation; identified as a differentially expressed gene with individual ROC curve showing AUC > 0.9 for distinguishing PDAC patients from healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Leads to immunosuppression, allows communication between tumor cells and macrophages, facilitates cancer progression, triggered by Toll-like receptors (TLRs).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: PDAC patients, tumor cells, chronic myeloid leukemia, metastatic cancer, inflammation, colorectal cancer.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides a clue about immune evasion by tumor cells; linked to tumor formation and growth; associated with inflammation and colorectal cancer; potential predictor for PDAC diagnosis.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Interleukin 10: Gefunden in 18 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the immediate effects of a single 20-minute Yogic Breathing (YB) session, specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam from the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, on salivary pro-inflammatory biomarkers in healthy volunteers. The study found that YB significantly reduced salivary levels of IL-1β, IL-8, and MCP-1 compared to an attention control group, with these reductions often observed at multiple time points and leading to more stable cytokine values over time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Yogic Breathing (YB), specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam (TMP) as described in the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, which included 10 minutes of Om chanting (Pranava Pranayama) followed by 10 minutes of controlled breathing (inhale for two counts, hold for eight counts, exhale for four counts).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 20-minute session, consisting of two 10-minute YB exercises, was performed by the YB group. This was compared to an Attention Control group who read for 20 minutes. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and baseline cytokine levels were collected after participants learned the technique, which might affect true pre-intervention baselines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between the Yogic Breathing (YB) and Attention Control (AC) groups were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory biomarker, mediates inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 20 min session of Yogic Breathing practice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact observed in this study for this biomarker in response to Yogic Breathing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Systemic (inferred Blood/Serum from 'systemic changes' and 'inflammatory markers')

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased within 5 days of MSC therapy, indicating MSCs lead to IL-10 production.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immunomodulation and immunosuppressive effects.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MSC immunomodulatory activities and therapy for ARDS in COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to modulating the inflammatory milieu and cytokine correction, indicating a beneficial effect on immune dysregulation and reduced inflammation in ARDS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: markedly high concentrations in critically ill patients

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characteristic feature of COVID-19 infection, especially in critically ill patients requiring ICU.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory status in COVID-19; inverse correlation with lymphocyte count attributes to hampered adaptive immune systems due to cytokine release syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in relation to some metrics, lower in others
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with CMJ values (+0.307) and 10m sprint values (+0.0071). Negatively associated with VO2 max values (-0.161) in predictive regression models (p < 0.001 for overall models). Used as a predictor in significant regression equations for fitness parameters (R2 adjusted up to 0.930).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, mediates inflammation, considered an adaptive response to increasing training loads.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer playing/training, pre-seasonal training, analyzed for its predictive ability on fitness parameters (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels predict improved explosive vertical jump ability and 10m sprint efficiency. Lower levels predict better aerobic capacity. Potential indicator for physical stress, systemic inflammation, and physiological adaptation to sports activity. Optimal levels are crucial for maintaining physiological homeostasis and preventing overtraining.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An anti-inflammatory cytokine that regulates immune response to prevent excessive inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of immune regulation and the body's attempt to dampen inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects; prominently in the acute SDD+C group compared to other groups. Significant increase in acute febrile phase compared to healthy controls (P < 0.05). Showed an increasing trend over twofold in SDD+C compared with SDD-C. Positively associated with TNF-α, VEGF, IL-18, IL-1Rα, and IL-17. Negatively correlated with RANTES.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, plays a crucial role in immune suppression and maintaining immune tolerance, involved in immune regulation to suppress immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overall acute dengue infection (healthy controls, MDF, SDD-C, SDD+C groups); correlated with other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Might be involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and is a potential marker for severity in dengue patients, consistent with immune dysregulation during dengue infection.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Low but similar levels in BD saliva compared to healthy controls; present in 100% of samples. Increased in BD saliva (ΔIL-10 = 20.35pg/ml) relative to HCs. Higher only in saliva (ΔIL-10 = 40.3pg/ml) relative to HCs for RAS. Lower in BD patients on neither COLC nor AZA (56.9 pg/ml) as compared to patients on both COLC and AZA (70.8 pg/ml). Normalized levels significantly higher in BD than in HCs. Normalized levels significantly higher in RAS than in HCs (p=0.04). Normalized levels significantly lower in patients taking both COLC and AZA than BD patients treated with only AZA (p=0.03). Positively correlated with IL-5 (p<0.0001); positively correlated with IL-12p70 (r=0.95, P<0.0001). Showed a strong correlation with IL-5. Low levels in the cohort (implied by inhibition of IFN-gamma). Lower median levels to a significant extent with COLC+AZA combination treatment. Increased in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) patients without periodontal disease compared to Healthy Controls (cited from Marques, et al. study).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, primarily involved in immune suppression and maintaining tolerance. Anti-inflammatory, immune suppression and regulation. Key immunoregulatory cytokine produced by almost all leukocytes and Th17 type cells; promotes wound healing; helps regulate the Th1/Th2 balance; inhibits T-cells from making IFN-γ.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. RAS patients relative to HCs. BD patients on neither COLC/AZA treatment compared to those on both COLC/AZA treatment. BD patients saliva. Normalised BD saliva samples. Combination treatment with COLC+AZA in Behçet's Disease patients; also plays a role in perpetuating Behçet's Disease oral inflammation and is of interest in dissecting immune dysregulation in Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus patients without periodontal disease (cited study by Marques, et al.).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a maintenance of basal local immunosuppression, despite elevated pro-inflammatory markers, or limited compensatory increase. Indicates altered immune regulatory status in BD and RAS saliva. Suggests higher anti-inflammatory activity with combination immunosuppressive therapy, which is an unusual finding. Indicates elevated immune regulatory activity in BD and RAS after protein normalization. Indicates reduced anti-inflammatory activity with combination immunosuppressive therapy. Suggests interconnected immune regulatory pathways in BD. Along with IL-5, can promote B cell proliferation and maturation leading towards a Th2 response. Low levels may indicate inhibition of IFN-gamma. Indicates response to immunoregulatory medication in Behçet's Disease; also associated with oral inflammation and immune dysregulation in Behçet's Disease and Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis. Associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Low but similar levels in BD serum compared to healthy controls. Increased in BD serum (ΔIL-10 = 11.9 pg/ml) relative to HCs. Found in high levels in active BD patient serum; not significantly increased in highly active BD compared to inactive or mild disease (reported previously).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, primarily involved in immune suppression and maintaining tolerance. Anti-inflammatory, immune suppression and regulation. Key immunoregulatory cytokine produced by almost all leukocytes and Th17 type cells; promotes wound healing; helps regulate the Th1/Th2 balance; inhibits T-cells from making IFN-γ.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Active Behçet's Disease (BD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a maintenance of basal systemic immunosuppression, or limited compensatory increase in Behçet’s Disease. Indicates altered systemic immune regulatory status in BD. Promotes wound healing; associated with disease activity (high levels in active BD).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Convalescent Plasma Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Critically ill COVID-19 patients were randomized to receive two units of high-titer, ABO-compatible convalescent plasma (total volume approximately 550 mL 
G
 150 mL) administered within 48 hours of randomization, or usual care. While no overall benefit was found (OSFD-21 OR 0.91 (0.74

1.11), mortality OR 1.01 (0.80

1.29)), differential treatment effects were observed across identified subphenotypes: subphenotype-1 showed lower hospital mortality with plasma (37.6% vs 40.5% in usual care), whereas subphenotypes-2 and -3 showed higher mortality with plasma (35.4% vs 24.1% for subphenotype-2; 34.1% vs 29.7% for subphenotype-3). No specific dose-response comparisons for plasma were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Variable levels in subphenotype-1. Significantly higher in non-survivors compared to survivors overall. Lower in seropositive overall cohort. Used to characterize subphenotypes.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in non-survivors; lower in seropositive. Not quantified in relation to treatment effect on biomarker levels directly; used to define subphenotype patterns.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Has anti-inflammatory properties and regulates immune responses; immune activating cytokine; part of complex cytokine networks, and a biomarker triad with prognostic utility.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characterization of COVID-19 subphenotypes in critically ill adults for differential treatment response to convalescent plasma therapy; associated with subphenotype-1 (dysregulated immune state); found lower in seropositive patients; found higher in non-survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a patient's immunological subphenotype which predicts differential response to convalescent plasma therapy and clinical outcomes; part of a dysregulated immune state, strongly associated with severe COVID-19; associated with seronegative status; associated with higher hospital mortality and has prognostic utility. Subphenotype patterns (2 and 3) associated with worse outcomes/poorer plasma response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An increase noted at 6 h that was associated with PGD grade 3 rather than 1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At 6 hours post-lung transplant, associated with PGD grade 3.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an association with PGD grade 3 severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Various parameters in saliva and blood changed in response to the ultramarathon. No specific quantification or direction of change was provided for IL-10 in the current study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory mediator of the immune system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of immune system response to intense physical stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased values at T2 (pT1–T2 < 0.01). Increased post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory mediator of the immune system; an anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses and regulates tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running) and immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of immune system response to intense physical stress. Suggests a counter-regulatory anti-inflammatory response to mitigate excessive inflammation induced by extreme exercise. Indicates inflammatory response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher concentrations observed in the 'high cytokine' cluster compared to the 'low cytokine' cluster. Showed greatest separation between latent class analysis classes in LeoPARDS and prominent class separation in VANISH.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis patient classification via hierarchical cluster analysis and latent class analysis in GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS cohorts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation in the 'high cytokine' cluster is associated with features of more severe disease (higher heart rates, lower PaO2:FiO2 ratios, higher fluid and norepinephrine requirements) and higher 28-day mortality in sepsis patients. Also associated with worse survival when showing prominent class separation in latent class analysis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported, this is a study protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates immune regulation and potential for dampening inflammation in neuroinflammatory conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in HCC (up to 3.78-fold, P < 0.0001) compared to control and non-malignant groups, and significantly upregulated in patients with chronic liver disease. Higher in non-cirrhotic SVRs (1.45–2-fold, P < 0.0001) compared to controls and other groups. No significant difference between cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic chronic HCV. Levels inversely correlated with Child-Pugh score (HCC) and positively with IL-12. In non-cirrhotic patients, positively correlated with Cldn1, TGF-β, IL-12, AFP, and INR, but inversely correlated with sCD163, age, FIB-4 score, and AST levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: M2 cytokine, anti-inflammatory, modulates liver fibrinogenesis, perpetuates immunosuppressive TME, central role in liver tumorigenesis, promotes immunoregulatory pathways, and acts as an 'endogenous danger signal' under hyperinflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: HCC pathogenesis, liver fibrinogenesis, chronic HCV, DAA-SVR, hyperinflammation, chronic liver disease, and mild liver cirrhosis.

Negatively correlated with Child-Pugh score, indicating an immune-homeostatic role.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) culture supernatant, PBMC (gene transcript), Patient plasma samples

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Much lower protein production and diminished gene expression levels in response to LPS stimulation compared to healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokine production and promotes immune tolerance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to LPS stimulation in children with MIS-C (both acute phase and fully convalescent) compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered innate immune functions, hyporesponsiveness to TLR4 stimulation, and lasting immune dysregulation in MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and characterized a responsive human triple-culture model of the air-blood barrier, integrating distinct macrophage phenotypes (M1, M2 wound-healing, M2 regulatory) derived from THP-1 monocytes to mimic in vivo alveolar macrophage features. The research investigated their immunological impact, particularly on epithelial barrier function and inflammatory responses in both A549/ISO-HAS-1 and H441/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture systems. It demonstrated that the M1 macrophage model induced a severe inflammatory-like response, characterized by impaired epithelial barrier integrity and increased pro-inflammatory markers, making it suitable for modeling inflammatory lung diseases. Conversely, the M2 models (M2wh and M2reg) exhibited a non-inflammatory or pro-regenerative profile, maintaining barrier integrity and thus providing a foundation for establishing a quiescent, physiological air-blood barrier model. The study also detailed the specific biomarker profiles of these differentiated macrophage subtypes and their varied responses to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation within the triple-culture system, highlighting cell line-specific differences in inflammatory outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro differentiation of human monocytic leukemia cell line THP-1 into M1 (classically activated), M2wh (wound-healing), and M2reg (regulatory) macrophage phenotypes, followed by their integration into a human triple-culture air-blood barrier model. The model consisted of alveolar epithelial cells (A549 or NCI H441) and microvascular endothelial cells (ISO-HAS-1) cultured on Transwell filter membranes. Immunological impact was subsequently assessed via Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: THP-1 cells were differentiated for 48h using specific cytokine cocktails: for M1 macrophages, 50 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 25 ng/ml TNFα; for M2wh macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, 35 ng/ml IL-4, and 20 ng/ml IL-13; for M2reg macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 20 ng/ml IL-10. Dexamethasone (1 µM) was also used in some contexts. The differentiated macrophages were seeded onto the epithelial layer of the co-culture system. Cell culture media contained 10% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS), which was reduced to 5% for the triple cultures. The triple cultures were stimulated apically with 1 µg/ml LPS (end concentration) and incubated for 24h. No explicit dose-response comparisons for LPS or macrophage cell numbers were reported; the focus was on comparing responses across macrophage phenotypes and with/without LPS stimulation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Could not be detected via ELISA (data not shown) in THP-1 cells 48h after differentiation or later in triple cultures.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cytokine that mediates anti-inflammatory responses, with distinct expression patterns in different macrophage subtypes (M1: low; M2wh: equal; M2reg: high).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro differentiation of THP-1 cells and subsequent culture in a triple culture model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of detection suggests that the established macrophage models may not fully replicate the expected cytokine production profiles of in vivo M1, M2wh, or M2reg phenotypes, or indicates assay limitations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma/Blood/Serum; conditioned media from PBMC and UC-MSC/PBMC cultures (in vitro)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Led to elevation of plasma levels. Significantly higher on day 7 in the blood of MSC patients compared to Control. Significant influx in the MSC group after final transplantation. In vitro, remarkably attenuated secretion; a drop was observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, regulates immune response and promotes immune tolerance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 patients after MSC transplantation; PBMC co-cultured with UC-MSC in vitro.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an anti-inflammatory effect or modulation of the immune response by MSCs, which could be beneficial in dampening excessive inflammation in severe COVID-19; complex immunomodulatory response with elevated levels in vivo but reduced secretion in vitro.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain homogenates, brain of AD mouse models.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Enhanced IL-10 mRNA in both sMSC and oMSC populations. Protein levels were highly variable.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: qRT-PCR and V-plex assays from 3xTg-AD mice after INA of sMSC or oMSC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Activation of anti-inflammatory gene expression (mRNA), potentially beneficial in AD pathogenesis, but inconsistent protein response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in response to hyperacute serum treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An inflammatory cytokine involved in the pathomechanism of OA.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hyperacute serum treatment on an osteoarthritic joint explant model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates decreased inflammation and potential inhibition of osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption, suggesting a beneficial effect on OA knee joint.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MSC immunomodulatory activities in ARDS, particularly in response to COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels contribute to modulating the inflammatory milieu and cytokine correction, indicating a beneficial effect on immune dysregulation in ARDS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level; Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in SDD with comorbidities. Higher in acute febrile phase of dengue patients compared to healthy controls, but lower in the acute SDD group than in the MDF group (implied by context). Showed a borderline significant decrease in SDD with comorbidity (SDD+C) group compared to SDD without comorbidity (SDD-C) group (P = 0.062), indicating near-significant fewer production. Positively correlated with IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-1β.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine, promotes Th1 cell development and IFN-γ production, antivirus-associated cytokine, plays a role in defending against DENV infection, linking innate and adaptive immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overall acute dengue infection, particularly Severe Dengue Disease (SDD) with comorbidities. Correlated with other cytokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with severe dengue disease progression with comorbidities (lower levels). Lower levels in SDD indicate an immune response inability to defend against infection, thus promoting progression to severe infection; its decrease is associated with severe dengue in comorbid patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: AFO-202 beta glucan does not stimulate the production of IL-12 (p70+40).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Th1 differentiation, pro-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: AFO-202 beta glucan administration to PBMCs and U937 cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of pro-inflammatory effect, controlled immune response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) culture supernatant, PBMC (gene transcript), Patient plasma samples

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Much lower protein production and diminished gene expression levels in response to LPS stimulation compared to healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, involved in promoting T-cell differentiation towards Th1 and Th17 phenotypes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to LPS stimulation in children with MIS-C (both acute phase and fully convalescent) compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered innate immune functions, hyporesponsiveness to TLR4 stimulation, and lasting immune dysregulation in MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine that promotes the differentiation of Th1 cells and enhances cytotoxic T cell activity, important for antiviral and antitumor immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in the context of a study involving half-marathon running and potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cellular immunity, viral infection, or autoimmune processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in BD saliva compared to healthy controls. Lower in BD saliva relative to HCs. Increased in RAS saliva. Decreased relative to HCs. Higher in BD patients not receiving any medication (did not reach statistical significance). Normalized levels significantly lower in patients taking both COLC and AZA than BD patients treated with only AZA (p=0.03). Positively correlated with IL-5 (p<0.0001); highly correlated with TNF-β (r=0.9, p<0.0001); positively correlated with IL-10 (r=0.95, P<0.0001). Found to be increased in RAS saliva. In all BD patients, normalized IL-12p70 showed a strong correlation with TNF-β in saliva (r=0.9, p<0.0001). Lower median levels to a significant extent with COLC+AZA combination treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine that promotes T helper 1 (Th1) cell differentiation and interferon-gamma production. Promotes Th1 cell differentiation and IFN-γ production. A pro-inflammatory cytokine known to drive the Th1 immune response by inducing IFN-γ and IL-2. Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. BD patients not receiving immunosuppressive medication compared to those on therapy. BD patients on combination COLC/AZA therapy compared to those on AZA monotherapy. BD patients saliva. Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS) saliva. Combination treatment with COLC+AZA in Behçet's Disease patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a localized suppression or altered Th1 immune response in the oral cavity in Behçet’s Disease. Indicates altered Th1 immune response activity in RAS and BD. Indicates altered Th1 immune response potentially influenced by immunosuppressive therapy, but without statistical significance. Indicates reduced Th1 immune response with combination immunosuppressive therapy. Suggests interconnected immune pathways involving Th1 responses in BD. Indicates a driver of the Th1 immune response. Its strong correlation with TNF-β suggests potential synergistic activity worthy of further investigation. Indicates response to immunoregulatory medication in Behçet's Disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No marked changes to serum levels relative to healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine that promotes T helper 1 (Th1) cell differentiation and interferon-gamma production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant systemic alteration in IL-12 p70 levels in Behçet’s Disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Conditioned media from PBMC and UC-MSC/PBMC cultures (in vitro)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Remarkably attenuated secretion.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in T cell differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: PBMC co-cultured with UC-MSC in vitro.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the immunomodulatory effect of UC-MSC on immune cells, reducing the secretion of this cytokine.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in response to IL-1β stimulation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An anti-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: IL-1β stimulation of bone-cartilage-synovium explant co-culture in an in vitro OA model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an anti-inflammatory response triggered by pro-inflammatory stimuli.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effect of NPN_1 (a Vicia faba hydrolysate) supplementation on strength recovery, fatigue, and muscle homeostasis markers following resistance exercise-induced delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in healthy male volunteers, concluding that NPN_1 significantly improved strength recovery, reduced fatigue, and positively modulated several plasma myokines, including suppressed myostatin expression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional supplementation with NPN_1 (PeptiStrong™, a Vicia faba hydrolysate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: NPN_1 was administered at 2.4 g/day (5 capsules) or placebo for 14 to 17 days. On day 14, delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) was induced through resistance exercise, with strength recovery, fatigue, and biomarker analysis performed at 0, 2, 48, and 72 hours post-DOMS. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated (p = 0.159) following NPN_1 supplementation compared to placebo, with significantly higher release immediately post-DOMS compared to baseline within the NPN_1 group. Values returned to baseline within 2h post-exercise for both cohorts.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Myokine that promotes muscle growth, repair, myoblast differentiation, and anti-catabolic effects, linked to increased muscle mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately after resistance exercise-induced delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS)/EIMD, with NPN_1 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with muscle anabolism and recovery; early elevation suggests a proactive reparative response and potential for muscle regeneration, contributing to improved strength recovery and reduced fatigue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with increasing age (r=0.18790; p=0.0303).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy human participants (age range 20–82 years), association with chronological aging.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the immediate effects of a single 20-minute Yogic Breathing (YB) session, specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam from the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, on salivary pro-inflammatory biomarkers in healthy volunteers. The study found that YB significantly reduced salivary levels of IL-1β, IL-8, and MCP-1 compared to an attention control group, with these reductions often observed at multiple time points and leading to more stable cytokine values over time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Yogic Breathing (YB), specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam (TMP) as described in the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, which included 10 minutes of Om chanting (Pranava Pranayama) followed by 10 minutes of controlled breathing (inhale for two counts, hold for eight counts, exhale for four counts).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 20-minute session, consisting of two 10-minute YB exercises, was performed by the YB group. This was compared to an Attention Control group who read for 20 minutes. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and baseline cytokine levels were collected after participants learned the technique, which might affect true pre-intervention baselines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between the Yogic Breathing (YB) and Attention Control (AC) groups were observed.
