matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 20 min session of Yogic Breathing practice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact observed in this study for this biomarker in response to Yogic Breathing.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively associated with CMJ values (-0.427) in a predictive regression model (p < 0.001 for the overall model). Used as a predictor in significant regression equations for fitness parameters (R2 adjusted up to 0.930).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, mediates inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer playing/training, pre-seasonal training, analyzed for its predictive ability on fitness parameters (CMJ).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels are predictive of better CMJ performance. Higher levels could indicate heightened inflammation and potential overtraining risk, negatively impacting explosive vertical jump ability. Potential indicator for physical stress, systemic inflammation, and physiological adaptation to sports activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in host defense against pathogens and in autoimmune diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of specific immune responses and inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated at 72 h post-transplant, associated with PGD3 at T48–72h (FDR-adjusted p < 0.1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine; critical for host defense against extracellular pathogens and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-lung transplant reperfusion (72h), associated with development of severe PGD (PGD3 at T48–72h).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels at 72h post-transplant are associated with severe PGD, possibly reflecting an impaired or dysregulated immune response during critical post-transplant period.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects. Significantly lower in acute dengue patients than in healthy controls (P = 0.007). Levels decreased in the convalescent phase compared to the acute, except for IL-17 itself. Positively associated with IL-10 and IFN-γ. Negatively linked with IL-6. Correlated with IL-12 and MIP-1α. Positively correlated with IL-2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in host defense and autoimmune diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute and convalescent phases of dengue infection (healthy controls, dengue patients); correlated with other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in acute dengue indicate an altered immune response pattern. Identified as a biomarker for dengue severity, with its decrease suggesting a potential immune dysregulation in dengue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Supernatants of miR-134 over-expressing cells, Supernatants from U937 or THP-1 cells

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in levels compared to control cells when miR-134 was over-expressed. Detected after miR-134 manipulation; precise quantitative data and direction of change are not provided in all article chunks.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine, reported marker of AOSD; mediates inflammation and immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: miR-134 over-expression, miR-134 mimic- or inhibitor-expressing U937 or THP-1 cells, as a disease marker for AOSD pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reported marker of AOSD, but not directly influenced by miR-134 overexpression in this context; identified as a disease marker for AOSD pathogenesis, indicating inflammatory status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed a small increase in saliva concentration in BD patients compared to serum, and implicitly compared to healthy control saliva. Higher in BD patients not receiving any medication (did not reach statistical significance); detected in almost all saliva samples tested across all groups, but no significant differences. 89.2% of samples were above the lower limits of detection; not reflected in IL-17A saliva levels compared to IL-6 in BD-MA. Significantly lower than HC in chronic periodontitis. Increased in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) patients without periodontal disease compared to Healthy Controls (cited from Marques, et al. study).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, crucial for host defense and involved in autoimmune diseases. Pro-inflammatory, mediates autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Produced by CD4+ Th17 cells, γδ T cells, NK cells, and CD3+ (CD4-/CD8-) cells. Naïve T-cells can become IL-17A secreting Th17-type cells when stimulated by IL-6 and TGF-beta. Induces IL-8 production to recruit neutrophils, contributing to inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. BD patients not receiving immunosuppressive medication compared to those on therapy. Behcet's Disease (BD) or Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS) patients; not previously measured in saliva of these patients. Chronic periodontitis. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus patients without periodontal disease (cited study by Marques, et al.).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a potential role for Th17-mediated inflammation in Behçet’s Disease. Indicates altered inflammatory response potentially influenced by immunosuppressive therapy, but without statistical significance. Recruits neutrophils whose proteases can cause detrimental damage to the mucosa. High individual IL-17A measurements with low serum IL-6 could be due to IL-17A production by non-classical Th17-type cells (γδ T cells or NK cells) which does not depend on IL-6 stimulation. Associated with inflammation and tissue damage. Associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased level detected (reported by Shen, et al.); conflicting ELISA data (Chi, et al., failed to detect); difficult to detect in current study serum (18.9% of samples above lower limits of detection).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Produced by CD4+ Th17 cells, γδ T cells, NK cells, and CD3+ (CD4-/CD8-) cells. Naïve T-cells can become IL-17A secreting Th17-type cells when stimulated by IL-6 and TGF-beta. Induces IL-8 production to recruit neutrophils, contributing to inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behcet's Disease (BD) with or without uveitis, autoimmune diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Exacerbated release can lead to destructive tissue pathologies of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. The IL-23/IL-17 pathway is crucial in several autoimmune diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine involved in pro-inflammatory responses and host defense, particularly in autoimmune diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory status and immune activation in neuroinflammatory conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study in 30,418 Chinese adults investigated the association between plasma myeloperoxidase (MPO) levels and anxiety risk, revealing a U-shaped relationship where both low and high MPO concentrations were associated with increased risk, a relationship significantly exacerbated by diabetes mellitus. The study also explored other inflammatory biomarkers for anxiety.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention or dose administration. Plasma MPO concentrations were quantified by ELISA and analyzed across quintiles (Q1:

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated levels reported in generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) patients, with an AUC value of 0.710 and a corresponding sensitivity of 77.27%.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the regulation of 23 blood-based biomarkers (including CK, IL-6, IL-17A, S100A8, BDNF, CD163, IL-1ß, and LDH) in 35 male elite athletes (badminton and soccer players) across different recovery-stress states. The primary aim was to identify markers responsive to habitual loading microcycles compared to recovered states. Key findings indicated that Creatine Kinase (CK), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) were generally higher in non-recovered states. S100A8 levels were significantly lower in non-recovered badminton players, while Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) levels were lower in non-recovered soccer players. Statistical trends were also observed for CD163 and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1ß). The study concludes that these discipline-specific biomarker responses are potentially useful for monitoring exercise and recovery to prevent overtraining and injury, though further validation is needed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise Training / Habitual Loading Microcycles
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared blood biomarker levels in elite male athletes (badminton and soccer players) during two states: 'recovered' (REC, after at least one day of rest from exercise) and 'non-recovered' (NOR, after a habitual loading microcycle). The habitual loading involved intensive, sport-specific training. For badminton players, this included four consecutive days with up to two sessions per day (50-310 min of moderate to intensive exercise daily). For soccer players, it involved high-intensity sessions with strenuous small-sided games, with at least two sessions within 48 hours. Blood samples for the NOR state were taken 12-16 hours after the last training session. The specific training content within microcycles varied and was not precisely controlled, reflecting real-world conditions. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training loads were reported within the context of the main findings, although external references to other exercise bouts (e.g., marathon, duathlon, interval training) were used to characterize biomarker behavior generally.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall, significantly higher in NOR (42.8  1 19.6 pg/mL) compared to REC (38.8  1 17.7 pg/mL) (p = 0.033; HLE 4.7 pg/mL, 95% CI [-1.2, 9.2]). Specifically in badminton players, NOR (48.5  1 25.2 pg/mL) was higher than REC (38.7  1 11.4 pg/mL) (p = 0.018; HLE 6.6 pg/mL, 95% CI [1.9, 30.1]).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation; produced by Th17 cells, critical in defense against extracellular bacterial and fungal infections, and induces various pro-inflammatory mediators (e.g., IL-1 1, IL-6).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-recovered state following habitual loading microcycles (especially in badminton players due to short-term stop-and-go movements with more anaerobic metabolism) causing an inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with a pro-inflammatory response to exercise stress and reflects exercise-sensitive inflammatory processes, potentially indicating muscle damage and suitable for athletic monitoring with discipline-specific contrasting regulations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) levels and inflammasome gene expression in monocytes from patients with septic shock caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, comparing them to healthy controls. The findings indicated that while the expression of main inflammasome genes was largely comparable between septic shock patients and healthy controls, circulating mtDNA levels were significantly elevated in septic shock patients, with even higher levels observed in those who died in the ICU. The study suggests that mtDNA could serve as an early prognostic marker for severity in septic shock from MDR pathogens.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on septic shock induced by multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 19 ICU patients diagnosed with septic shock due to documented MDR bacteria, with blood samples collected within 24 hours of diagnosis, and compared them to 20 age-matched healthy controls. The median SOFA score at ICU admission for patients was 11. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was applied or investigated; the study focused solely on characterizing the disease state and biomarker levels. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked tendency to an increased expression observed in septic shock patients, though high variability prevented statistical significance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level; Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects; significant increase in acute febrile phase (P < 0.05), markedly increased (P < 0.05) in SDD compared to MDF, and significantly higher in SDD (P = 0.002). Significantly elevated (P < 0.01) in SDD with comorbidities, showing an increasing trend over twofold in SDD+C compared to SDD-C with the most significant changes found (P < 0.01). Steadily increased significantly across all severity groups and significantly higher in severe dengue compared to healthy samples of patients with mild dengue infection. Positively associated with IL-10, TNF-α, VEGF, and IL-1Rα. Exhibited a significant negative correlation with platelets (r = 0.393, P = 0.031) and NS1 levels in the acute phase of dengue infection, where significant platelet induction caused a considerable increase in serum IL-18.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine, plays a role in innate and acquired immunity, induces IFN-γ secretion, and is involved in various inflammatory conditions such as sepsis, diabetes, metabolic syndromes, atherosclerosis, and cardiovascular disorders.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overall acute dengue infection, particularly Severe Dengue Disease (SDD) compared to Mild Dengue Fever (MDF), and especially in SDD with comorbidities. Correlated with platelets, NS1, and other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A strong and potential biomarker for predicting severe dengue disease progression, particularly when severe and with comorbid groups. It indicates immune overactivation, is associated with platelet activation, and is consistently higher in severe dengue, making it a plausible option for a dengue severity measure. It is involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and is associated with the development of comorbidities in SDD patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Individually shown predictive or diagnostic value for aGVHD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increases.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Increases vascular permeability.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ARDS, COVID-19, and COPD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Leads to tissue damage and microthrombus formation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma, Peripheral blood cells (for mRNA), THP-1 cells supernatant, miR-134 over-expressing cells, serum
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein level, mRNA level, Gene Transcript

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A negative correlation between miR-134 expression and IL-18BP mRNA levels was detected in peripheral blood cells following TLR3 ligand treatment. Lower plasma IL-18BP levels were observed in active AOSD patients who had higher miR-134 expression. Significantly lower protein levels (mean, 38.6 pg/ml) in miR-134 over-expressing THP-1 cells compared to miR-134 inhibitor-expressing cells (67.2 pg/ml, P < 0.01) and mimic control-expressing cells (52.7 pg/ml, P < 0.05) or non-transfection (50.4 pg/ml, P < 0.05). Significantly decreased IL-18BP mRNA following miR-134 upregulation associated with TLR3 ligand stimulation. Lower plasma levels in active AOSD patients (mean, 4441.6 pg/ml) compared to inactive AOSD patients (5572.5 pg/ml, P = 0.155, not statistically significant). Low rate of expression in miR-134 over-expressing cells; reduced plasma levels in active AOSD patients with high miR-134; previous studies showed lower serum levels in active AOSD vs. inactive AOSD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Target of miR-134; binds IL-18; its reduction by miR-134 is associated with elevated IL-18 levels; intrinsic inhibitor of IL-18; modulates inflammation by binding to IL-18, neutralizing its proinflammatory activity; inhibits IL-18-mediated NF-κB activation and proinflammatory cytokine production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Active Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD), following TLR3 ligand treatment, miR-134 over-expression, miR-134 mimic- or inhibitor-expressing THP-1 cells, AOSD pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates AOSD activity; targeted by miR-134, contributing to the disease pathogenesis through its effect on IL-18; negative regulation by miR-134 leads to increased free IL-18, contributing to inflammation; decreased levels contribute to increased free IL-18, promoting inflammation in AOSD; potentially associated with increased disease activity; its decline contributes to enhanced free IL-18 levels; low expression may lead to insufficient binding of IL-18; contributes to elevated free IL-18 levels and AOSD pathogenesis; involved in the biologic effect of miR-134.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Individually shown predictive or diagnostic value for aGVHD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Binding protein; inhibits IL-18 activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictive or diagnostic for acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (aGVHD).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated alterations in serum levels of tumor, cardiac, liver, and renal function markers, alongside the IL-18 rs1946518 polymorphism, in patients with breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers (BC, CRC, PCa), and myocardial infarction (MI), compared to healthy controls. It revealed significantly elevated tumor markers (CA 15-3, CA 19-9, CEA, TPSA) in cancer patients, which serve as efficient early detection biomarkers. Cardiac markers (hs-cTnT, CK-MB) were specific to MI and largely unchanged in cancer. Liver and renal markers (ALP, AST, ALT, urea, creatinine) showed varied elevations, particularly in CRC and PCa, suggesting their utility as alternative diagnostic indicators. The IL-18 -607 C/A polymorphism was identified as a risk factor for PCa (AA genotype and A allele), and also showed an Odds Ratio of 1.75 for BC, while A/C heterozygotes were linked to increased CRC risk and C allele homozygotes offered protection against CRC.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker and Genetic Polymorphism Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study focused on assessing diagnostic biomarker levels and genetic polymorphisms in various patient groups and healthy controls, without any therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated secretion of IL-18BP; no specific quantitative data provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Binds to IL-18, neutralizing its activity to modulate immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Secreted by PCa cells.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the effort of cancer cells to overcome immune surveillance.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Genetic Polymorphism (Genotype and Allele Frequency Distribution)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: For Breast Cancer (BC): No significant differences in genotype/allele frequency compared to healthy individuals (P>0.05) were reported in one chunk, while another reported an Odds Ratio (OR) of 1.75 for both C and A alleles, suggesting it as a risk factor. For Colorectal Cancer (CRC): No significant differences in genotype/allele frequency distribution compared to healthy individuals (P>0.05) in one chunk, while another indicated A/C heterozygotes exhibited an increased risk for CRC and homozygotes for the C allele were protected against CRC. For Prostate Cancer (PCa): The AA genotype significantly increased risk for PCa compared with CC (P=0.001, OR=0.033, 95% CI=0.002-0.633); a significant association for the recessive model (CC vs. AA/CA: OR=0.372, 95% CI=0.161-0.858, P=0.024) and the carrier for the mutant A allele was significantly higher in PCa patients compared with healthy volunteers (C vs A: OR=0.445, 95% CI=0.248-0.796, P=0.006).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Genetic variation affecting IL-18 gene transcription, influencing immune response and disease susceptibility.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with Breast Cancer (BC), Colorectal Cancer (CRC), and Prostate Cancer (PCa) susceptibility compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The AA genotype and carrier for the mutant A allele are significantly associated with an increased risk for PCa. For CRC, A/C heterozygotes showed increased risk while C allele homozygotes were protected. For BC, the polymorphism may be considered a risk factor based on an OR of 1.75, though some findings stated no association with susceptibility in the study population.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether baseline myocardial and systemic inflammatory burden could predict cardiac structural and functional improvement in advanced heart failure patients undergoing durable Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support. It found that lower levels of circulating inflammatory cytokines (TNF alpha, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-13, and Interferon gamma) and less activated myocardial STAT-3 inversely correlated with cardiac improvement. A two-cytokine model based on low circulating Interferon gamma and TNF alpha was identified as an effective predictor of significant reverse remodeling and post-LVAD cardiac recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Durable continuous-flow Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, used as mechanical circulatory support and combined with standard guideline-directed heart failure medications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: LVAD implantation was performed on 93 patients with advanced heart failure. Device speed was adjusted under echocardiographic guidance to optimize flow and left ventricular decompression, targeting a midline septum position and minimal mitral regurgitation. Cardiac improvement, defined as significant reverse remodeling (e.g., final LVEF >=40% or 35-40% with >=50% relative improvement), was assessed via serial echocardiography, with 11% of patients showing such improvement (responders). No explicit dose-response comparisons for LVAD speed or medication regimens were reported; the study primarily compared biomarker levels between responders and non-responders to the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower levels in responders compared to non-responders (P<0.05). Higher levels in serum of nonresponders indicate lower levels are associated with cardiac improvement.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine implicated in cardiovascular disease, contributing to systemic inflammatory burden.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline, pre-LVAD intervention in advanced chronic heart failure patients undergoing Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, comparing responders to non-responders.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower systemic inflammatory burden and lower serum levels are associated with LVAD-mediated cardiac structural and functional improvement, serving as a circulating biomarker predictive of cardiac improvement.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected at lower levels in human myocardium compared to IL-6, IL-1β, IL-7, and IL-13 (no significant difference between responders/nonresponders in tissue).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Inflammatory response in the failing human heart.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not identified as a significant differing factor between responders and nonresponders to LVAD unloading in this study regarding tissue levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-weeks of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) pre-loading on markers of inflammation (hsCRP, IL-6), muscle damage (CK), perceived muscle soreness, tissue tenderness, and lower limb performance (squat jump peak power, hamstring flexibility) in endurance-trained female runners after a single bout of downhill running (DHR). MIPS consumption attenuated inflammation (hsCRP) three days post-DHR but did not significantly impact perceived soreness, muscle damage markers, or other performance measures.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS, NO-Shotgun®) and eccentric exercise (Downhill Running, DHR).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) was consumed daily for 28 days (4 weeks) prior to a single bout of DHR, and 30 minutes before post-testing. One serving of MIPS was 21g. A control group received an isocaloric (28g maltodextrin) placebo. The DHR protocol involved a 60-minute run at a -10% gradient, at 75% VO2max (average speed 12.03  ± 0.4 km/hr). No dose-response comparisons for either the supplement or DHR protocol were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked immediately post-DHR (p = 0.03), with a significant 62.99% increase. Levels remained elevated up to 72 h post-DHR. No significant difference was reported between MIPS and placebo groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune response, muscle repair, and stimulating hepatic CRP production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory response to exercise-induced muscle damage and its activation in muscle repair processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased, then decreased, then returned to baseline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (p < 0.0001), decreased 3 hours after but remained increased compared to pre-exercise values, and returned to baseline 24 hours after (p < 0.001). Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC < 0.75 or ICC = 0.64).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates immune response, inflammation, and energy metabolism; pro-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 60-min continuous endurance exercise bouts; endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; used in exercise context for analyzing immune activation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of physiological exercise response and recovery processes, but suggests limited suitability due to moderate reliability for monitoring exercise load and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the regulation of 23 blood-based biomarkers (including CK, IL-6, IL-17A, S100A8, BDNF, CD163, IL-1ß, and LDH) in 35 male elite athletes (badminton and soccer players) across different recovery-stress states. The primary aim was to identify markers responsive to habitual loading microcycles compared to recovered states. Key findings indicated that Creatine Kinase (CK), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) were generally higher in non-recovered states. S100A8 levels were significantly lower in non-recovered badminton players, while Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) levels were lower in non-recovered soccer players. Statistical trends were also observed for CD163 and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1ß). The study concludes that these discipline-specific biomarker responses are potentially useful for monitoring exercise and recovery to prevent overtraining and injury, though further validation is needed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise Training / Habitual Loading Microcycles
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared blood biomarker levels in elite male athletes (badminton and soccer players) during two states: 'recovered' (REC, after at least one day of rest from exercise) and 'non-recovered' (NOR, after a habitual loading microcycle). The habitual loading involved intensive, sport-specific training. For badminton players, this included four consecutive days with up to two sessions per day (50-310 min of moderate to intensive exercise daily). For soccer players, it involved high-intensity sessions with strenuous small-sided games, with at least two sessions within 48 hours. Blood samples for the NOR state were taken 12-16 hours after the last training session. The specific training content within microcycles varied and was not precisely controlled, reflecting real-world conditions. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training loads were reported within the context of the main findings, although external references to other exercise bouts (e.g., marathon, duathlon, interval training) were used to characterize biomarker behavior generally.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall, significantly higher in NOR (13.7  1 3.7 pg/mL) compared to REC (12.5  1 3.8 pg/mL) (p = 0.024; mean difference 1.3 pg/mL, 95% CI [0.2, 2.4]). Specifically in soccer players, NOR (14  1 2.9 pg/mL) was higher than REC (12  1 2.5 pg/mL) (p = 0.017; mean difference 1.9 pg/mL, 95% CI [0.4, 3.5]). Also showed prolonged elevation up to two days post-match and higher levels after 90-min interval training.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation; a pleiotropic cytokine and central signal molecule of the acute-phase response, initiated by muscle damage, released by contracting muscles in response to glycogen depletion. It stimulates anti-inflammatory IL-10 and IL-1RA, and inhibits pro-inflammatory TNF- 1 and IL-1.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-recovered state following habitual loading microcycles (especially in soccer players due to higher aerobic metabolism), involving high metabolic demands and structural tissue damage after training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with a pro-inflammatory response to exercise stress and reflects exercise-sensitive inflammatory processes, indicating immune response and necessity to replenish glycogen stores and restore muscular integrity, potentially useful for athletic monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels of proinflammatory cytokines, interleukin 6, were higher after the control exercise bout than after the exercise bout preceded by a WBC session.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A proinflammatory cytokine involved in immune response and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional volleyball players (n=18) after 40-min submaximal physical exercise preceded by a single WBC session (-130°C, 2 min) vs. control exercise bout without WBC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an anti-inflammatory effect of WBC, reducing exercise-induced inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation on antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, and iron metabolism in rowers subjected to exhaustive exercise. Findings indicate that supplementation significantly strengthened antioxidant potential (TAC) and mitigated exercise-induced increases in pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-alpha), muscle damage indicators (myoglobin), and iron regulatory hormones (hepcidin) in the supplemented group. However, IL-6, ferritin, sTfR, iron, TIBC, and UIBC remained largely unaffected by supplementation or showed exercise-induced changes independent of it.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation combined with strenuous physical exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Athletes received 720 mg of highly-concentrated large cranberry extract daily (two 360-mg capsules, containing 36 mg proanthocyanidins per capsule) for 6 weeks. The control group received dyed gelatin placebo capsules containing flour. Participants performed a 2000-m rowing ergometer test at maximal effort on day 1 (pre-supplementation) and at the end of the 6-week training camp (post-supplementation), with blood samples taken pre-exercise, 1 minute post-exercise, and after a 24-hour recovery. No dose-response comparisons for cranberry extract were reported within the study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant post-exercise increase observed in both cranberry-supplemented and control groups, both prior to and after supplementation. Levels normalized after a 24-h recovery. Cranberry supplementation did not exert a significant effect (main effect, p=0.051).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates systemic inflammation as a pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune response and energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exhaustive 2000-m rowing ergometer test and 24-h recovery period, with and without 6-week cranberry supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammatory response to exertion; cranberry supplementation did not significantly modulate this particular exercise-induced inflammatory marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in the low LPC 20:0 group (p<0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine; key mediator of the acute phase response; mediates immune and inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patients with low LPC 20:0 levels in the context of COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates heightened inflammatory response in COVID-19 patients, potentially linked to lipid metabolism and disease severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the immediate effects of a single 20-minute Yogic Breathing (YB) session, specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam from the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, on salivary pro-inflammatory biomarkers in healthy volunteers. treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 20-minute session, consisting of two 10-minute YB exercises, was performed by the YB group. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the functional deficiency of endogenous interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients, a subtype of new-onset refractory status epilepticus. It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anakinra (recombinant IL1RA)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Measured at 24 ng/ml IL1RA and robustly suppressed IL1R signaling in response to 32 pg/ml IL1β.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Demonstrates that anakinra therapy effectively restores IL1R signaling inhibition, correlating with patient clinical improvement (seizure termination).

It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anakinra (recombinant IL1RA)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased IL1R activity relative to that induced by HC or MRE serum (MRE did not differ from HCs). FIRES and Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep (ESES) patient serum synergized with exogenous IL1β (32 pg/ml) to induce even more IL1R activity. The amount of IL1R signaling activity induced by serum was not completely suppressed by the addition of exogenous IL1RA in samples from FIRES and ESES patients, whereas activity was mostly suppressed in HC and MRE samples.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammatory responses, cellular signaling cascade.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: FIRES and ESES patient serum, compared to HC and MRE serum.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates dysregulated or exaggerated inflammatory signaling in FIRES and ESES; suggests resistance to IL1RA antagonism; implies presence of other serum factors driving IL1R activity or an undetected IL1β reservoir.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the expression patterns and prognostic value of the thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP)/nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome pathway and its related genes (IL1B, CASP1) in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Analyzing microarray data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), transcriptome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), and qRT-PCR data from a Jinan University (JNU) validation cohort, the study found that TXNIP and IL1B were generally upregulated, while CASP1 showed variable expression in AML patients compared to healthy individuals. Crucially, lower expression, particularly the co-expression, of TXNIP, NLRP3, and IL1B was consistently associated with a more favorable prognosis and longer overall survival (OS) in AML patients, indicating their potential as prognostic biomarkers and targets for novel AML therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prognostic Biomarker Analysis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study analyzing endogenous gene expression patterns in AML patients across multiple public (GEO: GSE13159, GSE12417; TCGA) and institutional (JNU) datasets. The study compared expression levels between AML patients and healthy individuals, and correlated expression patterns with patient outcomes (overall survival, restricted mean survival time). Patients were categorized into high and low expression groups based on median gene expression levels. No experimental intervention, therapeutic doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported or investigated.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: AML patient data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases (GSE13159 and GSE12417), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database, and Peripheral Blood (PB) samples from Jinan University (JNU) database, compared with Healthy Individuals.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher expression in AML patients compared to HIs; lower expression is associated with a favorable prognosis when co-expressed with other markers; prognostic significance not found for individual IL1B expression in GSE12417.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated in AML patients (P = 0.042 in GSE13159); No statistical significance for individual IL1B expression in GSE12417 (P = 0.574). Lower co-expression with TXNIP and NLRP3 is associated with favorable prognosis (GSE12417, P = 0.009; TCGA, P = 0.050; JNU, P = 0.026).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Active mature form (IL-1β) is cleaved from pro-IL-1β by activated CASP1; induces inflammation and cell death. A key mediator in disease progression; dysregulated secretion correlates with leukemia progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients; Prognosis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia; Expression levels in AML patients compared to healthy individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of prognosis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML); lower co-expression with TXNIP and NLRP3 predicts favorable prognosis; dysregulated levels indicate leukemia progression and poor prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine that mediates immune response and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of local inflammation and immune response in COVID-19, particularly respiratory tract inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated after elagolix treatment (mentioned in discussion as having anti-inflammatory roles)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After elagolix treatment in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure and suspected endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Has anti-inflammatory roles in endometrial receptivity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated plasma Interleukin-4 (IL4) levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and healthy controls, finding significantly decreased IL4 levels in PH patients. Lower plasma IL4 was associated with higher PH risk, greater disease severity, increased clinical worsening, and poorer survival rates, indicating its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating endogenous biomarker levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study; no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were performed. Endogenous plasma IL4 levels were measured by flow cytometry in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with PH compared with controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine, plays a role in PH pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation associated with PH pathogenesis and progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Lungs (within and surrounding CD68+ cells); Macrophages (infiltrating)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Observed within and surrounding CD68+ cells in close proximity to dying human cells in the lungs at 24 hours post-administration. Described as induced expression by infiltrating macrophages and a dramatic increase in related studies, though specific quantification not provided for the current study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, secreted by alternatively-activated (M2) macrophages, contributes to immune modulation and resolution of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Macrophage phagocytosis of dying human kidney cells in the lungs; following IV administration of dying human kidney cells in a rat cisplatin model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Presence of IL10 suggests an anti-inflammatory response, potentially released by macrophages after phagocytosing the human cells, contributing to immune modulation and stimulating renal repair by promoting inflammation resolution.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (p < 0.0001), then decreased 3 hours after RFTs (p < 0.001). Demonstrated weak reliability (ICC = 0.24, below 0.5).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, primarily expressed by monocytes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not seriously quantifiable by the ELISA method due to weak reliability and concentrations often below the limit of detection, limiting its utility as a biomarker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar at baseline between groups; no significant changes reported over time or between groups during the supplementation period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An anti-inflammatory cytokine that plays a key role in immune suppression and resolution of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed before and after the 12-week supplementation period of daily protein combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of immune regulation and anti-inflammatory processes. Assessed due to possible confounding effects on muscle mass.
