document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether baseline myocardial and systemic inflammatory burden could predict cardiac structural and functional improvement in advanced heart failure patients undergoing durable Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support. It found that lower levels of circulating inflammatory cytokines (TNF alpha, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-13, and Interferon gamma) and less activated myocardial STAT-3 inversely correlated with cardiac improvement. A two-cytokine model based on low circulating Interferon gamma and TNF alpha was identified as an effective predictor of significant reverse remodeling and post-LVAD cardiac recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Durable continuous-flow Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, used as mechanical circulatory support and combined with standard guideline-directed heart failure medications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: LVAD implantation was performed on 93 patients with advanced heart failure. Device speed was adjusted under echocardiographic guidance to optimize flow and left ventricular decompression, targeting a midline septum position and minimal mitral regurgitation. Cardiac improvement, defined as significant reverse remodeling (e.g., final LVEF >=40% or 35-40% with >=50% relative improvement), was assessed via serial echocardiography, with 11% of patients showing such improvement (responders). No explicit dose-response comparisons for LVAD speed or medication regimens were reported; the study primarily compared biomarker levels between responders and non-responders to the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower levels in responders compared to non-responders (P<0.05). Higher levels in serum of nonresponders indicate lower levels are associated with cardiac improvement.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine implicated in cardiovascular disease, contributing to systemic inflammatory burden.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline, pre-LVAD intervention in advanced chronic heart failure patients undergoing Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, comparing responders to non-responders.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower systemic inflammatory burden and lower serum levels are associated with LVAD-mediated cardiac structural and functional improvement. Higher serum levels are associated with negatively affecting LVAD-mediated cardiac improvement.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in higher levels in the human myocardium compared with IL-8, TNFα, IL-5, and IL-2, but with no significant difference between responders/nonresponders in tissue.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Inflammatory response in the failing human heart.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not identified as a differing factor between responders and nonresponders to LVAD unloading in this study regarding tissue levels.

It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in blood following treatment for 2 months with elagolix (no specific quantification)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine, part of the IL-17 axis which promotes endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 2 months of elagolix treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased level is noted as a puzzle by the authors, given its role in promoting endometriosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: markedly high concentrations in critically ill patients; increased in sera of patients with mild, moderate, or even severe forms of COVID-19

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine responsible for expansion and differentiation of various T cell subsets; immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Characteristic feature of COVID-19 infection, especially in critically ill patients requiring ICU; in sera of patients with COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory status in COVID-19; speculated as an attempt by the immune system to reverse lymphopenia and T cell exhaustion.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with IFN-γ and IL-17. No significance over the twofold decreasing trend in SDD+C compared with SDD-C.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Growth factor for T cells, important for immune cell proliferation and differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute phase of DENV infection; correlated with other cytokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of immune response during acute dengue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher in BD serum compared to healthy controls. Higher in RAS serum relative to HCs. Elevated levels reported in sera from BD patients with uveitis compared with non-uveitis patients, and in active BD cohorts compared to healthy controls. Serum samples from RAS-MA (n=2) had higher levels compared to RAS-MQ patients. High median levels observed in BD-MA serum.

T-cell growth factor, promotes immune cell proliferation and differentiation. Can be influenced by IL-6, which promotes T helper and cytotoxic T-cell proliferation by increasing IL-2 secretion. Involved in inflammatory processes and T helper and cytotoxic T-cell proliferation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. Behçet's Disease (BD) patients with uveitis or active disease. Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS) orally active (RAS-MA) and orally quiet (RAS-MQ) patients. BD orally active (BD-MA) patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: May indicate an altered systemic T-cell immune response in Behçet’s Disease and recurrent aphthous stomatitis. Indicates altered T-cell activity in RAS serum. Possibly reflects ongoing inflammatory process during oral ulceration. High serum levels may reflect ongoing inflammatory processes during oral ulceration or systemic manifestations like uveitis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in BD saliva compared to healthy controls; present in 100% of samples. Decreased in RAS saliva compared to healthy controls. Higher in BD patients not receiving any medication (did not reach statistical significance). Similar levels detected in all groups. Unchanged in saliva during oral ulceration in the study cohort.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine that promotes T-cell growth and differentiation, important for immune cell proliferation. Involved in inflammatory processes and T helper and cytotoxic T-cell proliferation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. BD patients not receiving immunosuppressive medication compared to those on therapy. Oral ulceration. General saliva samples from all groups.

Salivary IL-2 levels were not affected by oral ulceration in the study cohort, suggesting it may not be a local oral ulceration marker in saliva.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

treatment_details.dose_specificity:

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In vitro production of IL-2 decreased significantly over time during COVID-19 convalescence.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Crucial cytokine for T cell proliferation and survival, including Tregs.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment of Treg function during COVID-19 convalescence.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a decline in Treg proliferative capacity or a shift in their functional phenotype during the later stages of COVID-19 recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma; conditioned media from PBMC and UC-MSC/PBMC cultures (in vitro)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change significantly during the observation period in both groups and did not differ significantly between MSC and Control groups in plasma. In vitro, did not change significantly.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine that promotes the growth, proliferation, and differentiation of T cells, essential for adaptive immunity; T cell growth factor.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 with UC-MSC application; PBMC co-cultured with UC-MSC in vitro.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact observed on this T-cell growth factor, suggesting MSC therapy did not overtly alter T-cell proliferation signaling via IL-2 in vivo or directly in this co-culture model.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates the utility of T cell Receptor Excision Circles (TRECs) and other markers (TCR diversity, CD31, PTK7) for monitoring thymic output and T-cell reconstitution after allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT). It examines TRECs as a predictive marker for post-HSCT complications like infections, relapse, and Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD), and for clinical outcomes including overall survival. The study also explores clinical factors influencing TREC levels, such as recipient age, conditioning regimen, stem cell source and dose, and pre-transplant thymic activity, and discusses TREC's broader diagnostic utility in congenital immunodeficiencies, HIV infection, and autoimmune diseases, advocating for its inclusion in post-HSCT follow-up.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily discusses various conditioning regimens employed in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT), including total body irradiation, cyclophosphamide, busulfan, non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC), and anti-T cell serotherapy, aimed at preventing graft rejection and reducing relapse risk. It notes that a higher dose of CD34+ peripheral blood stem cells (e.g., >10^7 per kg body weight) has been associated with higher TREC levels, suggesting a dose threshold. Immunosuppressive drugs like corticosteroids and cyclosporine are mentioned in the context of GVHD prevention and treatment. However, specific dose-response relationships for HSCT or its components are not consistently reported, and the findings are often contradictory across studies due to variations in protocols and lack of randomized trials. The document focuses on monitoring applications rather than detailing specific therapeutic intervention doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: PTK7+ cells produce less IL-2 compared to the PTK7- subset.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine involved in T cell proliferation and differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Distinguishing PTK7+ from PTK7- naive T cell subsets.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Aids in identifying recent thymic emigrants (RTE) via PTK7 expression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated plasma Interleukin-4 (IL4) levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and healthy controls, finding significantly decreased IL4 levels in PH patients. Lower plasma IL4 was associated with higher PH risk, greater disease severity, increased clinical worsening, and poorer survival rates, indicating its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating endogenous biomarker levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study; no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were performed. Endogenous plasma IL4 levels were measured by flow cytometry in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with PH compared with controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine, plays a role in PH pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation associated with PH pathogenesis and progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether baseline myocardial and systemic inflammatory burden could predict cardiac structural and functional improvement in advanced heart failure patients undergoing durable Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support. It found that lower levels of circulating inflammatory cytokines (TNF alpha, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-13, and Interferon gamma) and less activated myocardial STAT-3 inversely correlated with cardiac improvement. A two-cytokine model based on low circulating Interferon gamma and TNF alpha was identified as an effective predictor of significant reverse remodeling and post-LVAD cardiac recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Durable continuous-flow Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, used as mechanical circulatory support and combined with standard guideline-directed heart failure medications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: LVAD implantation was performed on 93 patients with advanced heart failure. Device speed was adjusted under echocardiographic guidance to optimize flow and left ventricular decompression, targeting a midline septum position and minimal mitral regurgitation. Cardiac improvement, defined as significant reverse remodeling (e.g., final LVEF >=40% or 35-40% with >=50% relative improvement), was assessed via serial echocardiography, with 11% of patients showing such improvement (responders). No explicit dose-response comparisons for LVAD speed or medication regimens were reported; the study primarily compared biomarker levels between responders and non-responders to the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected at lower levels in human myocardium compared to IL-6, IL-1β, IL-7, and IL-13 (no significant difference between responders/nonresponders in tissue).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Inflammatory response in the failing human heart.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not identified as a significant predictor or indicator of cardiac improvement in this study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher concentrations observed in the 'high cytokine' cluster compared to the 'low cytokine' cluster.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Related to immune response and T-cell proliferation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis patient classification via hierarchical cluster analysis in GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS cohorts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation in the 'high cytokine' cluster is associated with features of more severe disease (higher heart rates, lower PaO2:FiO2 ratios, higher fluid and norepinephrine requirements) and higher 28-day mortality in sepsis patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study in 30,418 Chinese adults investigated the association between plasma myeloperoxidase (MPO) levels and anxiety risk, revealing a U-shaped relationship where both low and high MPO concentrations were associated with increased risk, a relationship significantly exacerbated by diabetes mellitus. The study also explored other inflammatory biomarkers for anxiety.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced in response to 2 months of OCP use (no specific quantification)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine, associated with the IL-17 axis, promotes endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 2 months of OCP use.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Promotes endometriosis and is involved in its pathogenesis; reduction suggests a direct effect on this inflammatory pathway.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the circadian rhythmicity and diurnal variation of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and healthy controls. It found that sST2 exhibits a distinct diurnal rhythm with lower values in the morning and peaks in the late afternoon. The study also compared sST2's rhythmicity to N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), which showed no diurnal rhythm, and to melatonin and cortisol, which demonstrated expected circadian patterns. These findings highlight the impact of diurnal variation on the clinical interpretation and management of sST2 levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker diurnal variation and circadian rhythm analysis for clinical monitoring and interpretation guidance
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from 16 HFrEF patients and 16 controls at seven specific time points (9 a.m., 1 p.m., 5 p.m., 9 p.m., 1 a.m., 5 a.m., and 9 a.m.) over a 24-hour period. The study focused on observational biomarker patterns and did not involve therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or standardized conditions for physical activity, meals, light exposure, or sleep duration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher concentration observed due to smoking; specific quantification not provided in the text.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates cardioprotection as part of the IL-33–ST2L pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Increased concentration in the airway epithelium due to smoking; its cardioprotective pathway is presumably inhibited by sST2 in a time-dependent manner in heart failure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Smoking status is linked to increased IL-33 concentrations; alterations in its pathway, potentially via sST2 inhibition, may lead to novel therapeutic strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An 'alarmin' cytokine, released from damaged cells to promote immune responses, often associated with type 2 immunity and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of tissue damage and immune activation, potentially relevant in lung inflammation associated with COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed an increasing trend over twofold in SDD+C compared with SDD-C. Exhibited a significant direct correlation with platelets (r = 0.523, P = 0.007).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, key regulator in humoral and adaptive immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute febrile phase of dengue infection (SDD-C, SDD+C groups); correlated with platelets.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Involved in immunomodulation during dengue progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in BD saliva compared to healthy controls. Decreased in RAS saliva compared to healthy controls. HC, BD-MQ, and BD-MA saliva had a similar IL-4 median concentration. Higher in BD patients receiving no treatment (IL-4 is a Th2 cytokine). Detectable in almost all saliva samples; RAS levels were lower than BD and HCs, but there were no significant differences between patient groups and HCs. Increased in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) patients without periodontal disease compared to Healthy Controls (cited from Marques, et al. study).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, involved in humoral immunity and T helper 2 (Th2) cell differentiation. Regulates Th2 immune responses, promotes B-cell growth and antibody production. Th2-type cytokine; stimulates B cells to proliferate and mature; considered a critical element for driving the development of Th2 immune response. Anti-inflammatory cytokine, promotes Th2 response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. HC, BD-MQ, and BD-MA patients' saliva. BD patients not receiving immunosuppressive medication compared to those on therapy. Oral mucosal tissue, Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS), Behcet's Disease (BD). Systemic Lupus Erythematosus patients without periodontal disease (cited study by Marques, et al.).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a shift in local immune balance or reduced Th2 response in Behçet’s Disease saliva and recurrent aphthous stomatitis saliva. Indicates no significant difference in Th2 immune response activity in saliva across these groups. Indicates altered Th2 immune response activity influenced by immunosuppressive therapy. May be a prominent force driving the production of antibodies in the mouth (e.g., SIgA) rather than systemically driving a Th2 response, contributing to local oral mucosal immunity. Associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No marked changes to serum levels relative to healthy controls. Detectable in only a few samples (mainly BD-MQ).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, involved in humoral immunity and T helper 2 (Th2) cell differentiation. Th2-type cytokine; stimulates B cells to proliferate and mature; considered a critical element for driving the development of Th2 immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Behçet's Disease with Mucosal Quiescence (BD-MQ).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant systemic alteration in IL-4 levels in Behçet’s Disease. Indicates activity of Th2 immune response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Convalescent Plasma Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Critically ill COVID-19 patients were randomized to receive two units of high-titer, ABO-compatible convalescent plasma (total volume approximately 550 mL 
G
 150 mL) administered within 48 hours of randomization, or usual care. While no overall benefit was found (OSFD-21 OR 0.91 (0.74

1.11), mortality OR 1.01 (0.80

1.29)), differential treatment effects were observed across identified subphenotypes: subphenotype-1 showed lower hospital mortality with plasma (37.6% vs 40.5% in usual care), whereas subphenotypes-2 and -3 showed higher mortality with plasma (35.4% vs 24.1% for subphenotype-2; 34.1% vs 29.7% for subphenotype-3). No specific dose-response comparisons for plasma were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Described as 'elevated levels'; not quantified in relation to treatment effect on biomarker levels; used to define subphenotype patterns.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a patient's immunological subphenotype which predicts differential response to convalescent plasma therapy and clinical outcomes; represents a component of a mixed immune response pattern observed in COVID-19. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated before transplant, associated with PGD3 at T48–72h (FDR-adjusted p < 0.1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine; regulates immune responses, particularly B cell activation and IgE production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-transplant, associated with development of severe PGD (PGD3 at T48–72h).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower pre-transplant levels are associated with a higher risk of developing severe PGD, possibly indicating an altered immune regulatory state.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether baseline myocardial and systemic inflammatory burden could predict cardiac structural and functional improvement in advanced heart failure patients undergoing durable Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support. It found that lower levels of circulating inflammatory cytokines (TNF alpha, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-13, and Interferon gamma) and less activated myocardial STAT-3 inversely correlated with cardiac improvement. A two-cytokine model based on low circulating Interferon gamma and TNF alpha was identified as an effective predictor of significant reverse remodeling and post-LVAD cardiac recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Durable continuous-flow Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support, used as mechanical circulatory support and combined with standard guideline-directed heart failure medications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: LVAD implantation was performed on 93 patients with advanced heart failure. Device speed was adjusted under echocardiographic guidance to optimize flow and left ventricular decompression, targeting a midline septum position and minimal mitral regurgitation. Cardiac improvement, defined as significant reverse remodeling (e.g., final LVEF >=40% or 35-40% with >=50% relative improvement), was assessed via serial echocardiography, with 11% of patients showing such improvement (responders). No explicit dose-response comparisons for LVAD speed or medication regimens were reported; the study primarily compared biomarker levels between responders and non-responders to the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in responders compared to non-responders (P<0.05). Higher levels found in serum of nonresponders, indicating lower levels are associated with cardiac improvement.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine, part of the systemic inflammatory burden.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patients with advanced heart failure undergoing Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) support.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower serum levels are associated with cardiac structural and functional improvement (reverse remodeling) following LVAD support.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the immediate effects of a single 20-minute Yogic Breathing (YB) session, specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam from the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, on salivary pro-inflammatory biomarkers in healthy volunteers. The study found that YB significantly reduced salivary levels of IL-1β, IL-8, and MCP-1 compared to an attention control group, with these reductions often observed at multiple time points and leading to more stable cytokine values over time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Yogic Breathing (YB), specifically Thirumoolar Pranayamam (TMP) as described in the ancient Tamil script Thirumanthiram, which included 10 minutes of Om chanting (Pranava Pranayama) followed by 10 minutes of controlled breathing (inhale for two counts, hold for eight counts, exhale for four counts).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 20-minute session, consisting of two 10-minute YB exercises, was performed by the YB group. This was compared to an Attention Control group who read for 20 minutes. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and baseline cytokine levels were collected after participants learned the technique, which might affect true pre-intervention baselines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between the Yogic Breathing (YB) and Attention Control (AC) groups were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory biomarker, mediates inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 20 min session of Yogic Breathing practice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact observed in this study for this biomarker in response to Yogic Breathing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Supernatants of miR-134 over-expressing cells, Supernatants from U937 or THP-1 cells

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in levels compared to control cells when miR-134 was over-expressed. Detected after miR-134 manipulation; precise quantitative data and direction of change are not provided in all article chunks.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine, reported marker of AOSD; mediates inflammation and immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: miR-134 over-expression, miR-134 mimic- or inhibitor-expressing U937 or THP-1 cells, as a disease marker for AOSD pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reported marker of AOSD, but not directly influenced by miR-134 overexpression in this context; identified as a disease marker for AOSD pathogenesis, indicating inflammatory status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. The aim was to evaluate systemic and muscle-related stress responses and recovery patterns, comparing biomarkers at 1 day (R+1) and 15 days (R+15) post-landing with pre-flight values and age-matched controls. Findings revealed a strong spaceflight-induced stress response in muscle tissue, leading to a proinflammatory state, with inflamma-miRs and myo-miR-206 mediating systemic recovery, and significant inter-individual differences in biomarker responses were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 6-month International Space Station (ISS) spaceflight exposure with in-flight countermeasure training, followed by a post-flight recovery period.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two crewmembers were exposed to approximately 6 months of spaceflight. Samples were collected pre-flight (76-79 days before) and post-flight at 1 day (R+1 / 24 hours) and 15 days (R+15) after landing. Individual molecular responses varied significantly between the two crewmembers, with crewmember A generally showing more persistent changes. Specifics of in-flight countermeasure training dose were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons for spaceflight duration were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher and dysregulated, with striking differences between crewmembers. Significantly increased at R+1 in crewmember A, then recovered, but showed no change in crewmember B.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A proinflammatory cytokine that plays a crucial role in immune responses, acute phase reactions, metabolism, and bone turnover.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-spaceflight recovery (R+1 and R+15) in crewmembers A and B, associated with a proinflammatory setting during a 6-month ISS mission.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an acute inflammatory response in crewmember A that recovered, while crewmember B showed no significant change, highlighting differing immune system responses to spaceflight. It is involved in the proinflammatory status induced by spaceflight, systemic stress/inflammation, and bone turnover, and suggests an unbalancing of homeostasis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Systemic (inferred Blood/Serum from 'systemic changes' and 'inflammatory markers')

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Clear decreases within 5 days of MSC therapy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, plays a role in acute and chronic inflammation and immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MSC therapy for ARDS in COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced inflammatory processes and potential mitigation of organ injury, supporting an immunomodulatory effect of MSC therapy, and may be linked to a decrease in cytokine release syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: markedly high concentrations in critically ill patients; increased levels correlated with increased mortality; high levels reported; between 30 and 50% of hemodialysis patients had elevated serum levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 infection, critically ill patients requiring ICU, severe COVID-19, patients with comorbid conditions (cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlated with increased mortality; indicates enhanced inflammatory process; suggests a poor prognosis in patients with severe COVID-19; most strongly associated cytokine with coronary heart disease (CHD); plays a more deleterious role in COVID-19 infection (in diabetes context); induces inflammatory state playing a significant role in dialysis-related morbidity; a key pro-inflammatory cytokine whose peak levels are associated with pulmonary complications.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cultured peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), U937 cells, and implied systemic

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: AFO-202 beta glucan does not stimulate the production of IL-6 and actually decreases IL-6 levels; decreased levels (no specific numerical quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine; commonly elevated in cytokine storms from chronic micro-inflammation; has pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory roles, immune response regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: AFO-202 beta glucan administration to PBMCs and U937 cells; AFO-202 beta glucan supplementation in conditions involving cytokine storms and hyper-inflammation, such as in COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Anti-inflammatory effect, suppression of cytokine storm, helps in regulating cytokine storms and hyper-inflammation associated with COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with CMJ values (+0.548), VO2 max values (+0.264), and RSA values (+0.300) in predictive regression models (p < 0.001 for overall models). Used as a predictor in significant regression equations for fitness parameters (R2 adjusted up to 0.930).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, mediates inflammation, induced by physical stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer playing/training, pre-seasonal training, analyzed for its predictive ability on fitness parameters (CMJ, VO2 max, RSA).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels predict improved explosive vertical jump ability, better aerobic capacity, and enhanced repeated sprint ability. Potential indicator for physical stress, systemic inflammation, and physiological adaptation to sports activity. Uncounteracted by anti-inflammatory cytokines, high IL-6 might indicate overtraining risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No difference in resting levels between groups. Increased 5 minutes post-plyometric exercise by +31% (p = 0.04) in both groups, then returned to baseline by 24 hours post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation and immune response, often secreted by muscle in response to physical stress and involved in muscle regeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest and acutely (5 minutes, 24 hours) post-plyometric exercise in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Similar acute inflammatory/metabolic response to exercise between groups, suggesting an intact exercise-induced response regardless of adiposity. Indicates a transient muscle-driven response to activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study investigating the biobehavioral impacts of sexual violence victimization and revictimization, integrated with support protocols for the participant.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single case study (N=1) involved longitudinal observation over 6 months, with data collected across five study visits (M0, M1, M3, M4, M6) following four acute sexual violence (SV) events (including vaginal rape and revictimization prior to M3 and M5 visits). Data collection included surveys, blood draws, cervicovaginal exams, and self-collected diurnal saliva samples. Integrated support protocols were provided, but no active interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: dynamic change (suppressed, then recovery, then lower than baseline)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dynamic change, showing a trend toward suppression at M1 and M3, followed by a recovery pattern/upward trend at M5, which coincided with lower perceived stress, lower depression, and increased resiliency; values at M6 were typically lower than baseline (M0), possibly indicating a return to baseline. No specific quantitative data provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine involved in the initial inflammation and healing process of the female genital tract.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In the female genital tract following sexual violence revictimization and subsequent recovery, with acute victimization prior to M3 and M5 visits.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Mediates inflammation in genital tract healing; a suppressed pattern may lead to higher susceptibility to infection, poor general immune responsiveness, and increased susceptibility to HIV and other STIs. An upward trend (immune recovery) coincides with improved mental health indicators (lower perceived stress, lower depression, increased resiliency).

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in the acute phase response and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Key marker of inflammation and cytokine storm in COVID-19, often correlated with disease severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level; Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects; significant increase in acute febrile phase (P < 0.05), being one of the top three cytokines with highest significant differences (P ≤ 0.001) in acute dengue vs healthy. Positively increased in SDD compared to MDF, with an immediate increase in SDD patients compared to MDF patients. Showed a borderline-significant pattern (higher expression) in SDD than MDF (P = 0.051). Increased in SDD with comorbidities, showing an increasing trend over twofold in SDD+C compared to SDD-C. A significant-likelihood pattern similar to IL-18 was observed (P = 0.085) in SDD+C compared to SDD-C. Positively linked with IL-8, MIP-1β, IL-15, IL-18, and MIG. Negatively linked with IL-17.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory cytokine, involved in immune response, inflammation, and hematopoiesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overall acute dengue infection, particularly Severe Dengue Disease (SDD) compared to Mild Dengue Fever (MDF), and in SDD with comorbidities. Correlated with other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with severe dengue disease progression, heightened immune response, and inflammation. It is involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and serves as a potential marker for disease severity, resembling cytokine involvement in severe dengue progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher (p=0.01) in Behçet’s disease patients with oral ulcers (BD-MA) than healthy controls (HCs). Evident increase in BD saliva levels compared to healthy controls. Significantly higher in BD and RAS patients compared to HCs, however only IL-6 reached a significant increase in BD-MA saliva compared with HC (p=0.04). Significantly higher in the saliva of BD patients with ulcers (BD-MA) than those without (BD-MQ, p=0.03). Normalized IL-6 salivary levels significantly higher only in BD-MA. Normalized levels significantly higher in BD than in HCs. Plays a role in perpetuating Behçet's Disease oral inflammation. Increased in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) patients without periodontal disease compared to Healthy Controls (cited from Marques, et al. study). Increased in oral cancer compared to Healthy Controls and leukoplakia (cited from a meta-analysis).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine. Involved in acute phase reactions and immune responses. Pro-inflammatory, acute phase response, immune cell differentiation. Produced by T-cells, B cells, and macrophages; stimulates proliferation of B cells and immunoglobulins; differentiates T lymphocytes; promotes T helper and cytotoxic T-cell proliferation by increasing their IL-2 secretion. Mediates inflammation and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Oral ulceration (BD-MA) in Behçet’s disease. Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. BD-MA (active ulcers) patients relative to HCs. BD patients with ulcers (BD-MA) compared to those without ulcers (BD-MQ). Behçet's Disease oral inflammation. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus patients without periodontal disease (cited study by Marques, et al.). Oral cancer (cited meta-analysis).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates Behçet’s disease activity and inflammation; suggests potential as a diagnostic and therapeutic biomarker. Suggests elevated systemic inflammation in Behçet’s Disease. Indicates active inflammation and disease severity in BD patients with active ulcers. Indicates inflammatory activity associated with oral ulceration in BD. Indicates elevated inflammatory status in BD after protein normalization. Suggests oral mucosa inflammatory cells release IL-6 in response to oral ulceration, which could perpetuate the ulcer (decreased production of IL-6 in oral mucosa is thought to drive rapid healing). Associated with Behçet's Disease oral inflammation; of interest in dissecting immune dysregulation in Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis. Associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. Suggested as a cancer biomarker for oral cancer.
