Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar at baseline between groups; no significant changes reported over time or between groups during the supplementation period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune response, inflammation, and energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessed before and after the 12-week supplementation period of daily protein combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of inflammatory status, can be elevated during exercise and chronic conditions. Assessed due to possible confounding effects on muscle mass.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated after exercise, returning to baseline within minutes to hours; increased in synovium early after ACL injury/surgery, returning to normal by ~5 days. Levels increase from individual baselines, with high interindividual variability; no universal 'elevated' threshold.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune signaling, mediates pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory responses, involved in generalized and specific (e.g., post-ACL injury) inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise (acute bouts, training), chronic inflammation (overtraining), muscle damage-induced inflammation, infection, disease, early post-ACL injury/surgery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammation, potential biomarker for overtraining and muscle damage; useful for detecting acute stress responses and post-injury inflammatory processes (e.g., after ACL injury). Requires contextualized assessment due to pleiotropic nature and high variability, as individual fluctuations are associated with injury risk and performance decrements.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: No significant interaction with CHIP or CHIP/AgeAccelHG for overall mortality/CHD; however, alternate alleles were associated with lower risk in TET2-CHIP+/AgeAccelHG+ individuals.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant interaction between CHIP status and alternate allele count at rs2228145 for all-cause mortality (p < 0.82) or CHD (p < 0.36). No significant interactions with the combined CHIP/AgeAccelHG variable. However, TET2-CHIP+/AgeAccelHG+ with IL6R WT had HR = 11.3 (p < 2.4 	 10-29) for composite outcome, while TET2-CHIP+/AgeAccelHG+ with IL6R Mut had HR = 1.91 (p < 0.066) compared to CHIP	/AgeAccelHG	/IL6R WT (coefficient for interaction = 	1.12 per alternate allele, p for interaction < 9.6 	 10-7).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Codes for the Interleukin-6 receptor, involved in inflammatory signaling; the rs2228145 variant affects IL-6R expression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Investigation of genetic modification of CHIP/AgeAccelHG-associated risk for mortality and CHD, particularly in the context of specific CHIP-driving mutations.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Generally a poor discriminator of risk in CHIP carriers alone. However, the alternate allele of rs2228145 significantly attenuates the extremely high risk associated with TET2-CHIP+/AgeAccelHG+ status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: increased in sera of patients with mild, moderate, or even severe forms of COVID-19; found to be beneficial; proposed immune combat strategies involve increasing it.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major cytokine promoting lymphocyte expansion and possibly reversal of T cell exhaustion; responsible for expansion and differentiation of various T cell subsets; restores immune system homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Lymphopenia and lymphocyte exhaustion in COVID-19; attempt by the immune system to reverse lymphopenia and T cell exhaustion; therapeutic strategies to combat COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered to restore immune system homeostasis; beneficial for combating COVID-19 by reversing lymphopenia and T cell exhaustion.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased production (no specific numerical quantification provided)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Leads to development and survival of mature T-cells to maintain homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: AFO-202 beta glucan supplementation for immune homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Supports T-cell development and survival, crucial for maintaining immune system homeostasis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased prominently in the acute SDD+C group compared to other groups. Showed a borderline significant increase in acute dengue compared with healthy. Levels decreased in the convalescent phase compared to the acute, except for IL-7 itself. Directly correlated with IL-13 and IL-1β.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine involved in lymphocyte development and homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute and convalescent phases of dengue infection (healthy controls, MDF, SDD-C, SDD+C groups); correlated with other cytokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Might be involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and may be a potential marker for severity in dengue patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported, this is a study protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine essential for lymphocyte development and homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates aspects of immune cell regulation and development in neuroinflammatory conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates the utility of T cell Receptor Excision Circles (TRECs) and other markers (TCR diversity, CD31, PTK7) for monitoring thymic output and T-cell reconstitution after allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT). It examines TRECs as a predictive marker for post-HSCT complications like infections, relapse, and Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD), and for clinical outcomes including overall survival. The study also explores clinical factors influencing TREC levels, such as recipient age, conditioning regimen, stem cell source and dose, and pre-transplant thymic activity, and discusses TREC's broader diagnostic utility in congenital immunodeficiencies, HIV infection, and autoimmune diseases, advocating for its inclusion in post-HSCT follow-up.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily discusses various conditioning regimens employed in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT), including total body irradiation, cyclophosphamide, busulfan, non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC), and anti-T cell serotherapy, aimed at preventing graft rejection and reducing relapse risk. It notes that a higher dose of CD34+ peripheral blood stem cells (e.g., >10^7 per kg body weight) has been associated with higher TREC levels, suggesting a dose threshold. Immunosuppressive drugs like corticosteroids and cyclosporine are mentioned in the context of GVHD prevention and treatment. However, specific dose-response relationships for HSCT or its components are not consistently reported, and the findings are often contradictory across studies due to variations in protocols and lack of randomized trials. The document focuses on monitoring applications rather than detailing specific therapeutic intervention doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Used in combination with TREC for SCID screening, yielding 100% specificity. Sensitivity for IL7 alone was 85%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine involved in lymphocyte development and survival.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pilot study for screening congenital severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as part of a screening tool for SCID, improving specificity when combined with TREC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and characterized a responsive human triple-culture model of the air-blood barrier, integrating distinct macrophage phenotypes (M1, M2 wound-healing, M2 regulatory) derived from THP-1 monocytes to mimic in vivo alveolar macrophage features. The research investigated their immunological impact, particularly on epithelial barrier function and inflammatory responses in both A549/ISO-HAS-1 and H441/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture systems. It demonstrated that the M1 macrophage model induced a severe inflammatory-like response, characterized by impaired epithelial barrier integrity and increased pro-inflammatory markers, making it suitable for modeling inflammatory lung diseases. Conversely, the M2 models (M2wh and M2reg) exhibited a non-inflammatory or pro-regenerative profile, maintaining barrier integrity and thus providing a foundation for establishing a quiescent, physiological air-blood barrier model. The study also detailed the specific biomarker profiles of these differentiated macrophage subtypes and their varied responses to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation within the triple-culture system, highlighting cell line-specific differences in inflammatory outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro differentiation of human monocytic leukemia cell line THP-1 into M1 (classically activated), M2wh (wound-healing), and M2reg (regulatory) macrophage phenotypes, followed by their integration into a human triple-culture air-blood barrier model. The model consisted of alveolar epithelial cells (A549 or NCI H441) and microvascular endothelial cells (ISO-HAS-1) cultured on Transwell filter membranes. Immunological impact was subsequently assessed via Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: THP-1 cells were differentiated for 48h using specific cytokine cocktails: for M1 macrophages, 50 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 25 ng/ml TNFα; for M2wh macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, 35 ng/ml IL-4, and 20 ng/ml IL-13; for M2reg macrophages, 8 nM PMA, 100 ng/ml GM-CSF, and 20 ng/ml IL-10. Dexamethasone (1 µM) was also used in some contexts. The differentiated macrophages were seeded onto the epithelial layer of the co-culture system. Cell culture media contained 10% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS), which was reduced to 5% for the triple cultures. The triple cultures were stimulated apically with 1 µg/ml LPS (end concentration) and incubated for 24h. No explicit dose-response comparisons for LPS or macrophage cell numbers were reported; the focus was on comparing responses across macrophage phenotypes and with/without LPS stimulation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Air-blood barrier co-culture supernatant; macrophage culture supernatant; apical and basolateral compartments of co-culture/triple-culture systems

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: M1 macrophage culture showed a 47 ± 13-fold increase over unstimulated cells, while M2wh and M2reg showed slight but non-significant increases (5.1 ± 1.7-fold and 5.8 ± 2.6-fold, respectively). In A549/ISO-HAS-1 co-culture with LPS, IL-8 increased 3 ± 0.9-fold apically and 3.2 ± 0.7-fold basolaterally. M1 triple culture (tric) with A549 showed 1.8 ± 0.3-fold apical and 1.6 ± 0.3-fold basolateral increase, further increasing to 4.6 ± 1-fold apical and 3.9 ± 0.7-fold basolateral with LPS. M1 tric with H441 showed 3.2 ± 0.3-fold apical and 1.5 ± 0.1-fold basolateral increase, further increasing to 4.9 ± 0.4-fold apical with LPS (basolateral comparable). M2wh tric A549 + LPS: 2.2 ± 0.2-fold apical, 1.2 ± 0.05-fold basolateral (significant elevation). M2reg tric A549 + LPS: 2.1 ± 0.1-fold apical, 1.5 ± 0.1-fold basolateral (significant elevation). M2wh tric H441 + LPS: 2.2 ± 0.2-fold upper compartment (further elevation). M2reg tric H441 + LPS: 2.1 ± 0.1-fold upper compartment (further elevation), 1.5 ± 0.1-fold lower compartment (significant increase). Unstimulated A549/ISO-HAS-1 produced higher baseline levels (approx. 10-fold apical, 5-fold basolateral) compared to H441/ISO-HAS-1, which generally did not respond with increased IL-8 after LPS alone or in M2 triple cultures basolaterally.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chemokine that mediates inflammatory responses, recruits immune cells, particularly neutrophils, and is a key mediator of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro differentiation of THP-1 cells into M1, M2wh, and M2reg macrophages; their integration into air-blood barrier triple-culture models (A549/ISO-HAS-1 or H441/ISO-HAS-1) and subsequent stimulation with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strongly indicates pro-inflammatory activity, especially from M1 macrophages and in response to LPS, contributing to neutrophil recruitment and inflammatory processes in lung epithelial models. Differential release patterns across apical and basolateral compartments suggest specific directional signaling and can indicate barrier integrity, while cell line-specific responses highlight differences in inflammatory potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in the synovium in the early postinjury period after ACL transection (minipigs); returned to normal levels by approximately 5 days after injury or surgery.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, mediates inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early post-injury period after ACL transection (Yucatan minipigs) and after human ACL injury or surgery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory response after ACL injury; potentially indicative of exercise-induced muscle damage or overtraining in other contexts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Catheter ablation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA); Protein Level (concentration); Effect on differentiation/migration

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Gene expression significantly upregulated in differentiated fibrocytes from persistent AF compared to SR controls and paroxysmal AF groups. Plasma levels increased in both AF groups compared with the SR control group. IL-8 had no effect on promoting fibrocyte differentiation or trafficking in vitro.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine involved in neutrophil recruitment and inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF); in vitro regulation of fibrocyte differentiation and migration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased gene expression in persistent AF fibrocytes and elevated systemic levels indicate a pro-inflammatory state in AF, contributing to cardiac remodeling. However, it does not directly influence fibrocyte differentiation or migration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study investigating the biobehavioral impacts of sexual violence victimization and revictimization, integrated with support protocols for the participant.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single case study (N=1) involved longitudinal observation over 6 months, with data collected across five study visits (M0, M1, M3, M4, M6) following four acute sexual violence (SV) events (including vaginal rape and revictimization prior to M3 and M5 visits). Data collection included surveys, blood draws, cervicovaginal exams, and self-collected diurnal saliva samples. Integrated support protocols were provided, but no active interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: dynamic change (suppressed, then recovery, then lower than baseline)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dynamic change, showing a trend toward suppression at M1 and M3, followed by a recovery pattern/upward trend at M5, which coincided with lower perceived stress, lower depression, and increased resiliency; values at M6 were typically lower than baseline (M0), possibly indicating a return to baseline. No specific quantitative data provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory chemokine involved in the initial inflammation and healing process of the female genital tract.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In the female genital tract following sexual violence revictimization and subsequent recovery, with acute victimization prior to M3 and M5 visits.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Mediates inflammation in genital tract healing; a suppressed pattern may lead to higher susceptibility to infection, poor general immune responsiveness, and increased susceptibility to HIV and other STIs. An upward trend (immune recovery) coincides with improved mental health indicators (lower perceived stress, lower depression, increased resiliency).

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chemokine that recruits neutrophils to sites of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of inflammation, particularly neutrophil recruitment in lung injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study comprehensively investigated differential cytokine profiles in matched serum and saliva samples from patients with Behçet’s disease (BD) with and without oral ulcers, recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), and healthy controls (HCs). The study aimed to identify cytokine panels with diagnostic and therapeutic potential for BD, as well as to characterize the cytokine profile across different disease activity states and in response to immunosuppressive therapies. Key findings revealed that salivary cytokine levels were generally higher and more readily detectable than in serum. Specific elevated salivary cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-8, TNF-α, and IL-6, were identified in BD patients, both with and without oral ulcers, and during relapsed or quiet systemic episodes. The research also explored the impact of various immunosuppressive therapies on these cytokine concentrations and emphasized the importance of normalizing salivary cytokine levels to total protein due to altered salivary composition in BD patients. The study concluded that salivary cytokine profiling offers a less invasive and sensitive method for frequent monitoring of BD activity, progression, and treatment responses, with specific cytokine panels holding promise for differential diagnosis and predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cytokine Profiling for Diagnostic Potential; Observational study comparing disease states and the influence of immunosuppressive therapies
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concentrations of 12 cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, TNF-β) were measured using the Human Th1/Th2 11-Plex FlowCytomix™ kit with IL-17A. Samples were matched serum and saliva from N=20 Behçet's disease (BD) patients, N=6 recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients, and N=10 healthy controls (HCs), utilizing 25 µl sample volumes. BD patients received either single therapy (ST) (prednisolone, azathioprine, or colchicine, N=9) or a combination of therapies (CT) (prednisolone, azathioprine, colchicine, and/or Cyclosporin A, N=8), compared to patients not on any medication (N=3). Specific dosages for medications were not reported, and no dose-response comparisons for therapeutic interventions were conducted, as the primary focus was on biomarker expression and assay performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher (p=0.02) in Behçet’s disease patients with oral ulcers (BD-MA) than healthy controls (HCs). Significantly higher (p ≤ 0.05) in BD patients without oral ulcers (BD-MQ) than HCs. Significantly higher only in quiet (BD-Q) systemic episodes (p=0.02). Present in 100% of BD saliva samples. A marked increase compared to healthy controls. Higher in RAS saliva relative to HCs; ΔIL-8 = 575 pg/ml in RAS saliva. Increased in BD saliva (ΔIL-8 = 178.2pg/ml) compared to HCs; group median levels of salivary IL-8 in BD (MA and MQ) were higher than HCs. More than 2-fold lower in BD patients not receiving any medication (did not reach statistical significance). Lower in BD patients on neither COLC nor AZA (572.8 pg/ml) as compared to patients on both COLC and AZA (835.6 pg/ml). Normalized levels significantly higher in BD than in HCs; significantly higher in BD-Q (quiescent) than HCs (p=0.02). Elevated in BD and RAS saliva compared to HCs. Increased in RAS saliva but not serum. Elevated in Behçet's Disease patients without oral ulcers compared to Healthy Controls; increased detection in Behçet's Disease-related oral inflammation. Increased in oral cancer compared to Healthy Controls and leukoplakia (cited from a meta-analysis).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine involved in neutrophil priming and activation, pro-inflammatory cytokine. Recruits neutrophils and other immune cells to the site of inflammation. Mediates inflammation and recruits immune cells. A potent chemokine that elicits a strong immune response, recruiting neutrophils, activating leukocytes, and enhancing adherence of circulating leukocytes to endothelial cells during inflammation. Also suggested as an inducer of matrix metalloproteinase, which may contribute to ulcer development.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Oral ulceration (BD-MA, BD-MQ) and quiet systemic episodes (BD-Q) in Behçet’s disease. Behçet’s Disease (BD) patients compared to healthy controls. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. BD patients relative to HCs and across disease sub-groups (MA and MQ). BD patients not receiving immunosuppressive medication compared to those on therapy. BD patients on neither COLC/AZA treatment compared to those on both COLC/AZA treatment. Behçet's Disease (BD) and Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS) patients, compared to Healthy Controls (HCs), during active/inactive disease, with/without vascular symptoms, and during oral ulceration. Differentiation between 'normal' saliva content and orally asymptomatic Behçet's Disease patients; Behçet's Disease oral inflammation. Oral cancer (cited meta-analysis).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates Behçet’s disease activity and inflammation; suggests potential as a diagnostic and therapeutic biomarker. Indicates active inflammation and neutrophil recruitment in Behçet’s Disease and recurrent aphthous stomatitis. Suggests a compartmentalized inflammatory response in RAS, with lower systemic levels compared to local. Indicates altered inflammatory status potentially influenced by immunosuppressive therapy, but without statistical significance. Suggests higher inflammatory activity with combination immunosuppressive therapy, which is an unusual finding. Indicates elevated inflammatory status in BD, including during quiescent phases, after protein normalization. Indicates a strong immune response and heightened inflammation. During oral ulceration, it reflects mucosal damage and inflammatory cell recruitment. Increased in RAS saliva suggests RAS is a local condition. While suggested as a serological marker for BD activity, it may lack specificity alone, but combined with IL-1β in saliva, it could improve the prediction of active ulcer episodes. Useful to monitor the level of oral inflammation to deter further ulcerations and accompanying systemic manifestations; included in a potential cytokine panel to assist in differential diagnosis, predicting ulcer recurrence or systemic relapse, and monitoring treatments for Behçet's Disease. Suggested as a cancer biomarker for oral cancer.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in BD serum (ΔIL-8 = 17.6 pg/ml) compared to HCs; only BD IL-8 levels were higher in serum. Lower in RAS serum relative to HCs. Elevated in BD patient serum only. BD patients with active vascular clinical presentation showed a 4-5-fold increase over those without vascular symptoms; inactive BD patients with a history of vasculitis had 2-fold higher levels than inactive BD without vascular association. Significantly increased in serum of orally active BD patients compared to HCs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine that recruits neutrophils and other immune cells to the site of inflammation. Mediates inflammation and recruits immune cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: BD patients relative to HCs. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) patients compared to healthy controls. Behçet's Disease (BD) patients, compared to Healthy Controls (HCs), during active/inactive disease, with/without vascular symptoms, and during oral ulceration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation in BD serum. Suggests a systemic alteration in IL-8 levels, potentially indicating immune dysregulation in recurrent aphthous stomatitis. Indicates a strong immune response and heightened inflammation. While suggested as a serological marker for BD activity, it may lack specificity alone.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower baseline levels pre-transplant were associated with PGD3 at T48–72 h (p < 0.05). Differential perioperative expression correlated with PGD3 development at T48–72 h (FDR < 0.1 and p < 0.05). A decrease was generally associated with the severity of PGD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine/chemokine; potent chemoattractant for neutrophils and mediator of acute inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-transplant and post-lung transplant, associated with PGD severity, particularly PGD3 at T48–72h.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an association with PGD severity. Lower pre-transplant levels are associated with a higher risk of developing severe PGD, possibly reflecting a suppressed inflammatory response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Non-significantly increased after baseline (p = 0.10) with the highest mean at T3. No significant differences between the changes from pre- to post-exercise were identified.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory mediator of the immune system; chemokine that mediates neutrophil recruitment, involved in inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running), post-160 km ultramarathon (T2), and during recovery (T3).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of immune system response to intense physical stress. Suggests a localized inflammatory response or immune activation in the oral cavity following extreme exertion. Saliva-specific reference values are needed for proper interpretation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased values at T2 (pT1–T2 = 0.03). Increased post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory mediator of the immune system; chemokine that plays a primary role in mediating neutrophil recruitment to sites of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running) and immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of immune system response to intense physical stress. Indicates acute systemic inflammation and mobilization of immune cells in response to extreme physical stress. Offers potential for innovative monitoring of exercise and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed the greatest separation between latent class analysis classes in LeoPARDS. Showed prominent class separation in VANISH. Significantly higher in SRS1 than SRS2 (FDR <0.05) in both GAinS and VANISH. Used in ARDS models for classification. High levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, chemokine involved in neutrophil recruitment and pro-inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis patient classification via latent class analysis in LeoPARDS and VANISH, comparison between SRS1 and SRS2 subphenotypes in GAinS and VANISH, and classification in ARDS models; used in evaluating inflammatory groups in sepsis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation is associated with worse survival in sepsis (lowest in latent class analysis class 3 in LeoPARDS with 47% survival, and class 2 in VANISH with 66% survival). Indicates a pro-inflammatory state (SRS1 subphenotype) and a hyperinflamed state (ARDS model classification), linked to worse survival, higher levels of shock in ARDS, and higher disease severity in hyperinflamed sepsis patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a 4-biomarker panel (IL-8, IL-2Rα, TNFR1, HGF) validated for confirming aGVHD and predicting survival. Separately, associated with cGvHD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine; mediates immune responses and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Component of a panel confirming acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (aGVHD) and predicting survival; associated with chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease (cGVHD).

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level; Protein Concentration; Cytokine Level

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects; significant increase in acute febrile phase (P < 0.05), being one of the top three cytokines with highest significant differences (P ≤ 0.001) in acute dengue vs healthy. Markedly increased (P < 0.05) in Severe Dengue Disease (SDD) compared to Mild Dengue Fever (MDF), significantly higher in SDD (P = 0.037) and showing an increasing trend over twofold in SDD with comorbidities (SDD+C) compared to SDD without comorbidities (SDD-C). Positively linked with IL-6, MIP-1β, IL-15, and MIP-1α, and showed a marked positive relationship with NS1 (r = 0.475, P = 0.011).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Proinflammatory chemokine, mediates neutrophil chemotaxis and inflammation, involved in neutrophil recruitment and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Overall acute dengue infection, particularly Severe Dengue Disease (SDD) compared to Mild Dengue Fever (MDF), and in SDD with comorbidities. Correlated with NS1 and other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with severe dengue disease progression and heightened inflammation. It is involved in dengue Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and serves as a potential marker for disease severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Montmorency cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained cyclists undergoing three consecutive days of high-intensity simulated road cycle racing. Findings consistently showed that MC attenuated post-exercise oxidative stress, indicated by lower lipid hydroperoxides (LOOH), and inflammatory responses, evidenced by reduced interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), compared to a placebo. No significant effect was found on muscle damage markers (creatine kinase) or other cytokines (TNF-α, IL-8, and IL-1-β). This suggests that MC is effective in combating oxidative and inflammatory cascades induced by metabolically strenuous exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency Tart Cherry Concentrate (MC) Supplementation in conjunction with a high-intensity, simulated road cycling exercise protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Trained cyclists consumed 30 mL of Montmorency cherry concentrate or a placebo twice daily (8 am, 6 pm) for seven consecutive days (4 days pre-trial and throughout the 3-day trial period). The exercise protocol involved three consecutive days (days 5, 6, and 7 of supplementation) of a 109-minute simulated road cycling race, which included 66 sprints (5, 10, or 15 seconds) and specific time trials (2x2 min, 1x5 min). No dose-response comparisons for the MC supplement or exercise intensity were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No group or interaction effects were found for IL-8; no differences were present between groups, although a main effect of time was found (F(1,7) = 15.411, p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chemokine that mediates inflammation and the recruitment of neutrophils to sites of inflammation and tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Responses to repeated days high-intensity stochastic cycling, not significantly affected by Montmorency cherry concentrate supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant impact on this specific inflammatory marker observed under the study conditions, suggesting MC did not alter IL-8 levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 30 mL of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) or an energy-matched placebo twice per day (8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.) for eight consecutive days, including four days pre-trial and throughout the trial period. The MC contained 73.5 mg 7L 91 cyanidin-3-glucoside, 178.8 gallic acid equivalent 7L 91 total phenolic content, and a TEAC of 0.58 trolox equivalents 7L 91. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased overall, but unchanged between groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma IL-8 significantly increased in both groups over 72 h following the trial (F(1,8)=4.905, p=0.010,  72=0.259). No significant group or interaction effects were found, indicating no difference between MC and PLA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemotactic cytokine that recruits neutrophils to sites of inflammation, involved in inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-prolonged intermittent sprint activity (adapted Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test) with MC supplementation vs. placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory response; lack of group difference suggests MC supplementation did not significantly affect this marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased after fisetin usage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to senolytic treatment (fisetin) in human participants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated plasma levels are characteristic.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Recruits neutrophils to lungs via CXCR1/2 interaction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COPD, early IPF; COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlates with the severity of COVID-19 and IPF.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes the IMPROVE trial, a four-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating a novel home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training program (along with individual components and controls) on cognitive function, physical performance, mood, and quality of life in older (≥50) ICU survivors with delirium. The study aims to identify improvements and understand the underlying pathophysiology, hypothesizing beneficial changes in neurotrophic factors (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), and a reduction in inflammatory (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, CRP) and glial activation (S-100β, GFAP) biomarkers, as well as investigating AD-related markers like APOE genotype and Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Home-based combined physical exercise and cognitive training delivered via Internet-based videoconference. The study also investigates individual components (physical exercise only, cognitive training only) and control interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a four-arm randomized controlled trial. Active cognitive training involves facilitator-led online modules (Posit Science, Inc. Brain HQ) for 45 minutes, 2 days/week for 3 months. Active physical exercise is multi-modal, seated aerobic and progressive resistance training for 45 minutes, 3 times/week for 3 months, delivered via videoconference at moderate intensity (RPE 5-6 on a 10-point scale). Control groups receive matched frequency cognitive control modules and gentle seated stretching. This protocol does not report dose-response comparisons, focusing on comparisons between the four distinct intervention arms.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Hypothesized decrease due to combined physical and cognitive training; specific quantitative data not reported as this is a study protocol describing intent to measure changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine mediating immune signaling and inflammatory responses, relevant to systemic inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Combined physical exercise and cognitive training intervention in older ICU survivors with delirium-induced cognitive impairment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory status and neuroinflammation; a hypothesized decrease suggests an improved inflammatory environment and may contribute to delaying Alzheimer disease/dementias. Delirium is considered a cytokine-mediated inflammatory syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the functional deficiency of endogenous interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients, a subtype of new-onset refractory status epilepticus. It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anakinra (recombinant IL1RA)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Large increases in patients with acute encephalitis and refractory, repetitive partial seizures (AERRPS).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chemokine that mediates inflammation and immune cell recruitment.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patients with acute encephalitis and refractory, repetitive partial seizures (AERRPS), a condition similar to FIRES.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate significant neuroinflammation and immune cell recruitment in the CNS, contributing to disease pathology in FIRES-like conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated plasma Interleukin-4 (IL4) levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and healthy controls, finding significantly decreased IL4 levels in PH patients. Lower plasma IL4 was associated with higher PH risk, greater disease severity, increased clinical worsening, and poorer survival rates, indicating its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating endogenous biomarker levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study; no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were performed. Endogenous plasma IL4 levels were measured by flow cytometry in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with PH compared with controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory cytokine, plays a role in PH pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) pathogenesis and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation associated with PH pathogenesis and progression.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-lung transplant reperfusion (over 72h), associated with severity of PGD, particularly PGD3 at T48–72h.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar and in a normal range (<1.25) in both complicated and uncomplicated COVID-19 patient groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the extrinsic pathway of coagulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 uncomplicated and complicated phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a normal extrinsic coagulation pathway in COVID-19 patients within this study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher in HCC patients than non-cirrhotic HCV patients (P < 0.0001) and cirrhotic responders (P = 0.0007). Non-malignant patients had higher INRs than healthy controls (P < 0.0001), except for non-cirrhotic HCV patients. Significant increase in cirrhotic patients in both chronic HCV and SVR groups compared to non-cirrhotic groups (P < 0.0001 for both).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of HCC, non-malignant (HCV, SVR), and healthy control groups; comparison between cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher INR indicates impaired liver synthetic function and increased risk of bleeding, common in advanced liver disease and HCC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document outlines the protocol for the PROSAP-A randomized controlled trial, investigating the effects of preoperative insomnia treatment (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia or Sleep Education Therapy) on acute and long-term postoperative pain control, brain health, and physical recovery in patients undergoing total knee or hip arthroplasty. The study aims to assess various patient-reported outcomes (e.g., opioid use, quality of recovery, sleep, mood, quality of life), objective measures (e.g., actigraphic sleep, quantitative sensory testing for pain, neurocognitive function), and blood biomarkers (e.g., inflammatory, monoamine, genetic mediators) across preoperative and postoperative phases to determine the impact on pain intensity, opioid use, sleep quality, mental health, and functional recovery. The document also details the recruitment, randomization, blinding, and data collection plans for this prehabilitation approach.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Preoperative Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) and Sleep Education Therapy (SET) as an active comparator.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Both interventions are delivered over 4 weeks in a hybrid format, comprising a digital self-guided platform and weekly telehealth video sessions (up to 60 minutes). CBT-I sessions are conducted with a psychologist and include sleep restriction and stimulus control, while SET sessions are with a research nurse. A video-assisted booster session is provided 1-2 weeks postoperatively. No dose-response comparisons are reported as these are fixed intervention protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mouse heart tissue (assessed by Masson's Trichrome and Sirius Red staining)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Attenuated by mCRAMP peptide treatment in TAC mice.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Accumulation of excessive extracellular matrix in the cardiac interstitium, a hallmark of heart failure and cardiac remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: TAC-induced heart failure (HF) with mCRAMP peptide supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced cardiac remodeling and improved cardiac health and function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tendency for a decrease in the verum group (p = 0.053, ES = 0.348).
