document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between markers of gut damage, permeability, and microbial translocation (I-FABP, REG3α, LPS, BDG) and cognitive function (performance-based B-CAM and self-reported PDQ) in a cohort of 80 ART-treated men living with HIV. The findings indicate that bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocation and higher regenerating islet-derived protein 3 α (REG3α) levels are significantly associated with increased self-reported cognitive difficulties, while fungal translocation (BDG) and intestinal fatty acid binding protein (I-FABP) did not show consistent or significant associations with cognitive outcomes. The study concluded that bacterial but not fungal translocation was associated with cognitive difficulties in ART-treated men living with HIV.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were men living with HIV, receiving ART for an average of 12 years (range 6.6–17.8 years), with HIV viral load below or equal to 50 copies/mL. The study focused on biomarker associations within this ART-treated cohort and did not report specific ART dose, intensity, or duration details, nor were dose-response comparisons investigated.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant differences in plasma levels (median 963-1088 pg/mL across B-CAM groups; 1038 vs. 931 pg/mL, p=0.97 between PDQ groups) were found. Not associated with either performance-based (B-CAM) or self-reported (PDQ) cognitive abilities in multivariable analyses. Plasma levels vary daily in ART-treated PLWH.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Released into circulation upon gut epithelium cell death, serving as a marker of gut integrity/damage and microbial translocation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Men living with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy, in relation to performance-based cognitive ability (B-CAM) and self-reported cognitive difficulties (PDQ).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Did not show an association with either performance-based or self-reported cognitive difficulties in ART-treated men living with HIV in this study, suggesting it may not be a reliable indicator of cognitive impact in this specific context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prolonged exercise under heat stress (used in cocoa flavanols study)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates intestinal epithelial damage and increased permeability, which can compromise gut barrier function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the functional deficiency of endogenous interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients, a subtype of new-onset refractory status epilepticus. It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anakinra (recombinant IL1RA)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced protein levels in FIRES patient PBMCs compared to healthy controls, corresponding to a 21-fold decrease in total IL1RN mRNA levels. Reduced expression of intracellular IL1RA isoforms was observed in the index patient's PBMCs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates IL1R signaling internally; intracellular forms of IL1RA can be secreted in response to specific triggers and serve as acute response molecules to antagonize IL1R signaling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) in the index patient, comparing PBMCs to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced and aberrant expression of intracellular IL1RA contributes to the observed impairment in inhibitory function and the overall functional deficiency in IL1RA in FIRES pathogenesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

The findings indicate that 3-month volumetric imaging can serve as an early biomarker to predict long-term sensitivity to everolimus, which demonstrated a cytostatic effect by decreasing VS growth rates, stabilizing tumors, and improving time to progression, while generally maintaining hearing and quality of life, despite not achieving significant tumor shrinkage in all cases.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Everolimus (mTORC1 inhibitor), with some cases also involving Bevacizumab as a subsequent or alternative treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral everolimus was administered daily for 52 weeks (12 months) to NF2 patients with progressive VS. Adult participants (18+) received 10 mg/day, and adolescents (16-17) received 3 mg/day. Doses could be reduced (e.g., to 5 mg/day for adults) due to toxicity, such as grade 3+ or grade 2 oral ulcers. While no formal dose-response comparisons were reported, the treatment period was continuous for 52 weeks, with some patients re-challenged with everolimus after discontinuation, and others receiving bevacizumab if everolimus failed to control growth.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of wearing exercise compression stockings (CS) on intramuscular pressure (IMP), muscle tissue oxygenation, and early blood biomarkers for muscle damage (myoglobin, creatine kinase) in the tibialis anterior muscle during a 10-km treadmill run in healthy recreational runners. Findings indicated that CS use significantly elevated IMP, reduced muscle tissue oxygenation, and increased serum myoglobin, suggesting non-beneficial muscle effects and no prevention of early exercise-induced muscle damage. Creatine kinase levels and systemic blood pressure remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise with Compression Stockings
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty healthy recreational runners performed two identical 10-km treadmill runs at a self-selected speed (10-12 km/h, no inclination) in a randomized crossover design, once with knee-high compression stockings (manufacturer-stated 25 mmHg at ankle) and once without. The intervention involved wearing CS during rest, running, and a post-run recovery period. No dose-response comparisons for compression levels were conducted, only with/without CS comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Applying CS at rest elevated baseline IMP by 24 	 1.1 mmHg (p < 0.001). During running, IMP was significantly higher by 22 	 3.1 mmHg on average with CS compared to without CS (p < 0.001), representing an average increase of between 10 and 50 mmHg in the same individuals. IMP remained significantly higher throughout the post-run period when CS were used (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the pressure within muscle compartments, indicating mechanical load, tissue compression, and potential influence on blood flow and oxygen delivery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During rest, a 10-km treadmill run (10-12 km/h), and post-run recovery while wearing exercise compression stockings (CS).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated IMP indicates heightened pressure within the muscle compartment, suggesting potential for reduced blood flow, decreased muscle oxygenation, and adverse effects on muscle function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CHIP was associated with 2.92 years of age acceleration (p < 9.3 	 10-26) as measured by IEAA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A measure of biological age acceleration independent of cell composition, partly driven by cell division.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis of epidemiological cohort data for associations with CHIP and clinical outcomes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an indicator of biological aging and is used to predict clinical outcomes; its acceleration is strongly associated with CHIP.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: iNKT reconstitution has been correlated with improved outcomes. Elevated levels of iNKT cells within the graft have been linked to subsequent increased numbers in HCT recipients. Higher iNKT-containing graft doses have shown a correlation with a reduced incidence of aGVHD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Diverse immunologic functions, capable of suppressing T-cell proliferation and IFN-γ production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-HCT immune reconstitution, association with aGVHD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlated with improved outcomes. Higher iNKT-containing graft doses linked to reduced aGVHD incidence. Deserves further investigation in the HCT setting.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and optimized a portable, economical, and sensitive biosensor for rapid thrombin activity detection, leveraging a blood coagulation-inspired fibrin hydrogel system with a personal glucometer readout; the principle involves thrombin-mediated fibrinogen cleavage and invertase immobilization, and the method's analytical performance, selectivity, and reliability in serum samples were thoroughly evaluated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Development and optimization of a portable biosensor and in vitro enzymatic assay for thrombin activity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The biosensor was optimized for thrombin detection, achieving a linear range of 0–0.8 U/mL with an LOD of 0.04 U/mL. Optimal conditions included a fibrinogen concentration of 10.0 mg/mL, thrombin-fibrinogen incubation for 5.0 min, invertase concentration of 1.0 mg/mL, sucrose concentration of 7.5 mg/mL, and invertase-sucrose incubation for 5.0 min at an enzymatic reaction temperature of 40–50 °C. Recovery rates in serum samples ranged from 92.8% to 107.7%, and repeatability was 7.0% RSD. The study focused on diagnostic method development, so no therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Free in solution, then immobilized within fibrin hydrogel

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower (free concentration, as thrombin activity increases)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The concentration of free invertase in solution decreases as thrombin activity increases, due to encapsulation within the fibrin hydrogel. This decrease is proportional to thrombin activity. An optimal concentration of 1.0 mg/mL was used in the assay.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose, thereby generating the measurable signal in the assay.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Serves as the signal transducer enzyme in the assay; its activity is modulated by the immobilization state, which is controlled by the thrombin-mediated formation of fibrin hydrogels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A critical element in the signal generation cascade, directly linking thrombin activity to the final glucose readout.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the low calcium (CON) group, iCa decreased with each exercise session, being ~4.5% and 2.4% lower than CAL after EX1 and EX2, respectively. The high calcium (CAL) intake maintained iCa concentrations above CON for ~7 hours, spanning the exercise and recovery periods (P < 0.001 for CAL vs CON, also for adjusted iCa).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for muscle contraction, nerve transmission, hormone secretion, and bone mineralization, playing a critical role in maintaining overall calcium homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During repeated, strenuous (two 90-min sessions separated by 150 min) non-weight-bearing rowing ergometer exercise, comparing high (~1000 mg) versus low (<10 mg) preexercise calcium meal intake.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased iCa indicates a disruption in calcium homeostasis, triggering PTH release and bone resorption. Maintaining iCa levels through preexercise calcium intake stabilizes conditions, supporting musculoskeletal and physiological function, and safeguarding long-term bone health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (after TBI, with PAD4 overexpression, with STING activation), lower (with Cl-amidine, with STING inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI significantly increased Iba-1-positive cells (p < 0.001). Cl-amidine significantly reduced Iba-1-positive microglia/macrophage numbers (p < 0.001). Upregulation was observed with PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.05) and in the TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group (p < 0.01). STING antagonist C-176 significantly decreased Iba-1 levels (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1, widely used as a marker for microglia/macrophages and their activation, which is part of the neuroinflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, PAD4 overexpression, STING activation, or STING inhibition.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates microglial/macrophage activation. Its reduction signifies inhibited activation and reduced neuroinflammation, while its increase suggests aggravated neuroinflammation and contributes to brain injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain homogenates, brain of AD mouse models.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Brain content of Iba-1 positive microglia remained unchanged.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Western blot analyses from 3xTg-AD mice after INA of sMSC or oMSC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No observable change in microglial cell numbers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation on antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, and iron metabolism in rowers subjected to exhaustive exercise. Findings indicate that supplementation significantly strengthened antioxidant potential (TAC) and mitigated exercise-induced increases in pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-alpha), muscle damage indicators (myoglobin), and iron regulatory hormones (hepcidin) in the supplemented group. However, IL-6, ferritin, sTfR, iron, TIBC, and UIBC remained largely unaffected by supplementation or showed exercise-induced changes independent of it.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation combined with strenuous physical exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Athletes received 720 mg of highly-concentrated large cranberry extract daily (two 360-mg capsules, containing 36 mg proanthocyanidins per capsule) for 6 weeks. The control group received dyed gelatin placebo capsules containing flour. Participants performed a 2000-m rowing ergometer test at maximal effort on day 1 (pre-supplementation) and at the end of the 6-week training camp (post-supplementation), with blood samples taken pre-exercise, 1 minute post-exercise, and after a 24-hour recovery. No dose-response comparisons for cranberry extract were reported within the study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Supplementation with cranberry extract did not exert a significant effect on serum iron (main effect, p = 0.516). However, a significant post-exercise increase in serum concentrations of iron was documented in both the cranberry-supplemented athletes and the controls at Trial II.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral for oxygen transport and various metabolic processes. Elevated levels can trigger free radical-mediated processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Strenuous physical exercise at Trial II, with and without 6-week cranberry supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of circulating iron levels; cranberry supplementation had no discernible effect on its levels, but post-exercise elevation may trigger oxidative stress and inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Deficiency rates up to 31% in female and some athletes. Reference ranges typically 50–175 µg·dL⁻¹, but with high daily variation (10–26%). Insufficient levels are defined when serum ferritin <12 µg·L⁻¹.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral for oxygen transport, hemoglobin synthesis, oxidative phosphorylation, aerobic metabolism, and cardiovascular endurance performance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Athletes (especially females), inadequate nutritional intake, iron deficiency, physical performance, endurance, training programs/cycles, general health (infection, personal stress), pre-competition.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates nutritional deficiency; insufficient levels hinder oxygen transport, aerobic metabolism, and endurance performance, preventing adaptations to training. Deficiency can lead to fatigue, anemia, cognitive impairment, immune deficiencies, and increased risk of upper respiratory infections. Tracking and supplementation can improve endurance performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between iron status and renal outcomes, specifically progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), in 111 pre-dialysis patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven Diabetic Nephropathy (DN). It found that reduced serum transferrin is an independent predictor of ESRD, and identified increased iron and transferrin deposition in renal tubular epithelial cells of DN patients, suggesting a pathological role for altered iron metabolism in disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the prognostic value of iron status and related biomarkers in Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. Serum markers were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, immunoradiometric assay, and colorimetric methods. Additionally, histological analysis involved immunohistochemical staining for transferrin and Perl's blue staining for iron in kidney biopsy specimens from DN patients and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or active treatments were investigated; the study focused on correlation and predictive value.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Kidney Tissue (DN kidney biopsies, tubular epithelial cells)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Deposited in a granular pattern in the tubular epithelial cells in DN, but not in controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral, but free iron can cause nephrotoxicity through production of cell-damaging reactive radicals (Fenton reactions), ferroptosis (programmed cell death), and iron-induced RAS activation. Involved in iron homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression, investigated in renal biopsy specimens from T2DM patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggested as a potential mechanism contributing to DN progression via nephrotoxicity and cell damage. Indicates a source of iron that could act on renal tubular cells, providing evidence for the role of excess tissue iron in kidney disease progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased during recovery; deficiency may be associated with negative outcomes
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Recovery plasma concentrations showed a tendency to increase regardless of sex and competitive distance during the 10 weeks, coinciding with a decrease in ferritin. Deficiency may be associated with negative outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral and micronutrient critical for hemoglobin formation, oxygen transport, and various metabolic processes in athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring recovery effectiveness in swimmers, preventing mineral deficiency due to insufficient recovery, and in the context of inflammatory states during a 10-week preparatory training stage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Deficiency may lead to anemia and impaired sports performance. Combined with ferritin and blood morphology, it helps avoid iron deficiencies, anemia, and adverse inflammatory states; its sequestration during inflammatory states can lead to 'anemia of inflammation'.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between routine plasma biomarker levels and recovery efficiency in elite professional soccer players over an entire eleven-month competitive match season, including seasonal variations and differences based on player position and cumulative match time. It concluded that a panel of AST, CK, LDH, and creatinine can effectively monitor recovery, adaptation, and overtraining risk, particularly in active positions like midfielders who may also be prone to iron and magnesium deficiencies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competitive professional soccer matches and regular intense training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An eleven-month competitive season, comprising 44 league and cup matches (23 autumn, 21 spring), typically one to two matches per week. Fasting capillary blood samples were collected 17-24 hours after each match. The study compared player positions (midfielder/defender vs. goalie/substitute, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups), noting significant differences in cumulative match time and physical demands. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for training intensity, but adaptation to increasing training load was observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in midfielder/defender groups, decreasing trend over season, varied by season/group
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally lower in the midfielder/defender group compared to the goalie/substitute group, especially in the spring round for midfielders compared to autumn. A decreasing trend was observed over the season, with significant decreases in midfielders over the entire season (R=-0.33, P<=0.05) and for the midfielder/defender group (R=-0.15, P<=0.05). However, it also increased significantly with time in the spring round for the midfielder/defender group, and showed a positive correlation with cumulative game time for defenders (R=0.23, P<=0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An essential micronutrient vital for oxygen transport (hemoglobin), energy metabolism, and various cellular processes. Its levels reflect the body's physiological stress response, and its deficiency is linked with anemia.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout an eleven-month professional competitive soccer match season, including post-match recovery, regular intense training, and conditions of insufficient recovery time and mineral deficiency. Comparisons were made between different player positions (midfielder/defender, goalie/substitute, individual midfielder and defender subgroups), considering cumulative game time, seasonal variations (autumn vs. spring rounds), and the prolonged intensive physical activity of active players like midfielders.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Deficiency can impair athletic performance, and its measurement can be an additional tool for monitoring recovery efficiency. Levels indicate physiological stress, increased iron utilization/loss, altered iron metabolism, or inflammation due to intense exercise. It suggests dynamic changes in iron status, reflecting recovery, dietary intake, or red blood cell turnover. Midfielders, experiencing prolonged intensive activity, are more prone to deficiencies, warranting screening for health reasons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case-control study investigated plasma levels of 16 trace elements and 27 AMD-associated genetic variants in 236 individuals with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and 236 age-matched controls. The primary findings revealed significantly elevated plasma levels of barium and cadmium, and reduced levels of chromium in nAMD patients, suggesting that an imbalance of these trace elements, influenced by environmental and lifestyle factors, may play a role in nAMD pathogenesis. No association was found between the AMD-associated genetic variants and trace element levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational biomarker association study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Plasma levels of 16 trace elements (including arsenic, barium, calcium, cadmium, cobalt, chromium, copper, iron, magnesium, manganese, molybdenum, lead, antimony, selenium, vanadium, and zinc) were quantitatively measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in 236 nAMD patients and 236 age-matched controls. Two additional elements (Al, Ni) were initially measured but excluded due to inadequate accuracy/reproducibility. This was a cross-sectional, observational study, and no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported or applicable. Patients with nAMD may have received past anti-angiogenic drug injections, but details regarding dose, intensity, or duration were not the focus of this study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: No significant difference reported between nAMD patients and controls in this study.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma levels were measured in this study; however, specific quantitative findings for Fe in nAMD patients vs. controls were not reported as significant. Prior research suggests iron supplementation is associated with nAMD in a dose-response manner.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Implicated in increasing chronic oxidative stress and decreasing antioxidant defense systems.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Plasma measurements in nAMD patients and controls. Prior research links iron supplement use to nAMD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential association with Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) based on prior research, particularly regarding supplementation, but direct association from this study's measurements not specified in provided chunks.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower (in ESRD patients), Higher (associated with diabetes/DN)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower baseline concentrations in ESRD patients (median 10.17  5mol/L, IQR 8.00-15.70) compared to non-ESRD patients. matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral; component of iron stores. Essential component of heme, involved in oxygen transport and various enzymatic reactions. Dysregulation of iron homeostasis is a major factor in DN development.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Index of iron stores; associated with diabetes and DN progression via inflammation and oxidative stress. Lower levels are associated with ESRD, but not an independent significant predictor; lower levels coincide with lower transferrin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease in both groups following 14 days of bed rest intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral involved in oxygen transport (hemoglobin), energy metabolism, and DNA synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 14 days of bed rest intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of iron status; decreased levels may suggest altered metabolism or potential deficiency during bed rest.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in ITG (prevented decline in CG)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Iron Supplementation Group (ITG) showed significant increases, with values of T1: 116.0 ± 21.6 µg/dL vs. T2: 116.7 ± 14.4 µg/dL, representing a 0.60 ± 8.64% change. Control Group (CG) showed a decline from T1: 108.6 ± 39.6 µg/dL to T2: 98.9 ± 15.8 µg/dL, representing a -8.93 ± 10.35% change. Group-by-time interaction was significant (p = 0.018).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential micronutrient for oxygen transport (hemoglobin), energy production, and various enzymatic reactions; involved in physical performance and metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España) with 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Prevention of decline and improvement indicates better hematological status, instrumental for athletic performance, endurance capacity, and decreasing fatigue and muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review discusses the practical application, limitations, and recommendations for blood biomarker profiling and monitoring in high-performance athletes, aiming to optimize physiology, nutrition, training, recovery, and prevent injury/illness. It covers various physiological and procedural factors affecting analysis, the importance of individualized reference ranges, the utility of specific nutritional and stress-related biomarkers (e.g., Omega-3 Index, carotenoids, redox status, glutamine, sex and thyroid hormones, IGF-1, cortisol, iron, tHbmass, inflammatory markers, CK, urea, melatonin, vitamins), and considerations for managing energy availability, training load, and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Comprehensive Blood Biomarker Profiling and Monitoring for Athlete Management, Nutritional Intervention, and Training Adaptation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The therapeutic approach involves comprehensive blood biomarker profiling (infrequent screening for deficiencies, several months apart) and monitoring (frequent assessment of adaptation/recovery, days or weeks apart) in athletes. This strategy is tailored to individual needs, sport, sex, and training context, utilizing individualized adaptive ranges and critical difference thresholds. It includes careful consideration of pre-analytic factors (e.g., posture, tourniquet use, centrifugation time, time of day, psychological stress, fasting status, menstrual cycle day, hydration status, duration/intensity/mode of prior exercise) and minimizing blood draw volumes, such as the removal of an average of 180 ml (range 82–314 ml) of blood in a simulated altitude study which negated hypoxia-induced erythropoiesis and aerobic performance gains. Specific interventions include targeted dietary/antioxidant supplementation (e.g., Omega-3 to increase OM3I from ~4.5% to ~6%, N-acetylcysteine for low red blood cell glutathione, Vitamin C for low plasma concentrations), iron supplementation for deficiency (e.g., ferritin < 12 ng mL−1 leading to dramatic increases in tHbmass), and nutritional adjustments for energy availability management (e.g., during persistently excessive endurance exercise, 8 weeks of gross energy deficiency, or carbohydrate restriction impacting testosterone/cortisol responses). The monitoring is applied across various contexts like intense exercise, eccentric loading, single matches, long-haul travel, sleep loss, and season-long competitive demands, with biomarker responses proportional to the imposed stress and recovery status.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Iron Status Markers (Iron, Ferritin, MCV, MCH, Reticulocytes, Hepcidin)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Level/Status, Protein Concentration, Red Blood Cell Parameter, Peptide Hormone Concentration, Deficiency status

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identification of iron deficiency; low iron status compromises erythropoietic effects. Females are more susceptible due to menstrual blood loss (< 36.5 ml to > 72.5 ml per cycle). Severe iron deficiency is defined as ferritin < 12 ng mL−1. Total hemoglobin mass (tHbmass) is around 40% higher in endurance athletes and can be dramatically increased via supplementation when ferritin < 12 ng mL−1. MCV and MCH provide an indication of compromised erythropoiesis due to iron deficiency. Reticulocyte variables can provide evidence of compromised iron status. Hepcidin shows promise as a highly informative addition to an iron panel; it interacts with exercise, iron deficiency, and iron overload.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for oxygen transport (via hemoglobin in red blood cells), energy metabolism, and metabolic processes. Ferritin is an iron storage protein. MCV and MCH indicate red blood cell volume and hemoglobin content, respectively. Reticulocytes reflect recent erythropoietic activity. Hepcidin regulates iron absorption and systemic iron homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-performance physiology, training interventions, nutritional strategies, altitude training, menstrual blood loss in females, endurance athletes, iron deficiency corrected via supplementation, general health and nutrition screening, RBC data in the context of iron deficiency, monitoring iron status in athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identification of deficiency; low status compromises erythropoietic effects of altitude and endurance performance, impacting training tolerance. Indicates compromised health and potentially reduced athletic performance due to impaired oxygen transport. Ferritin is a key indicator for iron deficiency, with levels below 12 ng mL−1 indicating severe deficiency requiring intervention. MCV, MCH, and reticulocytes indicate compromised red blood cell production due to iron deficiency. Hepcidin is highly informative for assessing an individual’s propensity to absorb iron. Optimal tHbmass enables greater maximal oxygen-carrying capacity and higher aerobic power; compromised tHbmass indicates sub-optimal aerobic power. Haemoglobin concentration is a poor indicator of true oxygen-carrying capacity (tHbmass) due to susceptibility to plasma volume shifts. Supports athlete health, nutrition, and performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: hiPSC, hESC, somatic cells, certain types of normal tissue
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (Gene Transcript or Protein Level - previously demonstrated)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently up-regulated in early and late passage cells of both hiPSC lines (by ESI-MS e) and confirmed by Western blot analysis. All selected proteins were confirmed to be up-regulated in hiPSC and hESC compared to somatic cells. Expressed only in certain types of normal tissue. Over-expression in hESC or hiPSC was demonstrated previously by gene expression or proteomic analysis. Included in a panel of markers confirmed to be differentially expressed in analyzed hiPSCs compared to somatic cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly stated, inferred as related to metabolism and potentially pluripotency. Involved in stemness maintenance and regulation of pluripotency.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Proposed novel pluripotency marker identification and validation; tissue specificity analysis. Stemness maintenance and regulation of pluripotency in hESC and hiPSC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate novel pluripotency marker for hiPSCs/hESCs; shows tissue-specific expression. Marker for stemness and pluripotency in hESC and hiPSC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: present; associated with higher ACACA expression, increased sensitivity to TOFA, and cell growth defect upon ACACA inhibition

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with bed rest in either group.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar decrements in isokinetic peak torque measures were observed in both BCAA-CHO and CHO groups at 60°/s (p<0.001 for time, p=0.94 for interaction) and 120°/s (p=0.021 for time, p=0.17 for interaction), indicating no beneficial effect of BCAA-CHO supplementation on muscle function recovery.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures dynamic muscular strength and power of the quadriceps.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following three consecutive high-intensity resistance training bouts (barbell back squat protocol).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of muscle function and recovery from intense exercise; sustained decrements suggest incomplete recovery, not mitigated by BCAA-CHO supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, observational study aimed to identify and externally validate the association of different pathological computed tomography (CT) features, specifically intracranial injury patterns and hemorrhage subtypes, with adverse outcomes and long-term functional recovery (up to one year post-injury) in mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) patients across two large cohorts, demonstrating that these CT features hold significant and distinct prognostic implications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of the prognostic value of pathological computed tomography (CT) features in mild traumatic brain injury
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study analyzing diagnostic head CT findings performed within 24 hours of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) in two large cohorts (TRACK-TBI and CENTER-TBI). CT imaging utilized modern standards (e.g., 64-320 detector rows, <0.3s gantry rotation, <1s whole-head acquisition) to improve diagnostic accuracy, and images were evaluated by board-certified neuroradiologists. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on diagnostic and prognostic features.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly associated with incomplete recovery (GOSE scores <8) up to 6 months post-injury: 2 weeks (OR, 2.01 [95% CI, 1.19-3.39]), 3 months (OR, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.00-2.35]), 6 months (OR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.01-2.43]). A trend toward significant association was observed at 12 months (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 0.90-2.03]; P = .14).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents bleeding into the subarachnoid space (the space between the arachnoid membrane and the pia mater covering the brain and spinal cord), typically caused by trauma in this context.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-traumatic brain injury (TBI) recovery assessment, evaluated at 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts incomplete recovery up to 6 months post-TBI, with a trend indicating continued association up to 1 year.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) that effectively discriminates COVID-19 patients from healthy individuals with high efficiency (AUC=0.91, 86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, involved in amino acid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 diagnosis (discriminating COVID-19 patients from healthy controls).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A key component of a highly efficient diagnostic panel for COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Notable differences between groups at 98 days, at the statistical limit (p < 0.001).
