matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention at 98 days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentiating metabolite indicating the impact of the dietary intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Displayed decreasing trends throughout the protocol. Athlete 1 exhibited a decrease, returning to basal values after short recovery 1, and dropped to 70% of the initial concentration before the second match. Athlete 2 showed a mirroring effect during the first match. Both athletes responded similarly during the first match but diverged in the second match.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An essential branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) important for muscle protein synthesis and energy production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (short recovery 1, before second match, during first and second matches).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle protein turnover and utilization of BCAAs for energy during exercise, with divergent responses in the second match suggesting individual metabolic differences and indicating metabolic response to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: sex-specific changes, lower (improved resistance in females post-MID)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A significant difference was noted in the changes in isometric fatigue profile between sexes from PRE to MID (p < 0.05). Isometric fatigue decreased in female COMP from MID to POST (p < 0.05), indicating improved resistance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The rate at which muscle force output declines during sustained or repeated contractions.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Across the PRE to MID phase for both sexes, and from MID to POST for female COMP.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Highlights sex-specific adaptations or responses in endurance capacity or susceptibility to fatigue during the activity phase. A decrease indicates improved fatigue resistance or recovery in female COMP.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased from PRE to MID in female (p < 0.001) and male (p < 0.01) COMP, and in male CTRL (p < 0.05). Isometric force was also lower in COMP compared to CTRL in both sexes (p < 0.001 and p < 0.05, respectively).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A main effect of time was observed (p = 0.003) as both groups experienced decrements. A group*time interaction approached significance (p = 0.06), but no between-group differences were observed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for a two-phase randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigating the efficacy and acceptability of high-frequency, low-load Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) in UK military personnel with lower limb musculoskeletal injuries where persistent pain is the primary limiting factor. Phase One will compare 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) BFR-RT over one week to determine the most effective and acceptable pressure for pain reduction. Phase Two will then compare this optimal BFR-RT protocol against usual care over three weeks to evaluate its impact on pain modulation, function, and other rehabilitation outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) compared to standard rehabilitation (usual care).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Phase One involves 7 BFR-RT sessions over 5 days (1 week) comparing 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) (n=28). Each session for the affected limb includes unilateral leg press and knee extension, performed at 20% of 1-Repetition Maximum (1RM) with a protocol of 1 set of 30 repetitions followed by 3 sets of 15 repetitions, with 30-second rest between sets (continuous inflation) and a 3-minute reperfusion period between exercises. Phase Two involves 21 BFR-RT sessions over 15 days (3 weeks) for the BFR group (n=26), utilizing the optimal LOP determined in Phase One. The control group in Phase Two receives usual care. The study aims to compare high vs. low BFR pressures (40% vs. 80% LOP) and their acceptability, but as this is a protocol document, no dose-response results are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Enhanced muscle function and recovery following muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study characterized pediatric Philadelphia-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients with kinase fusions in Japan, identifying 29 such patients from a cohort of 373. These patients presented with distinct clinical features including male predominance (22/7), older mean age at onset (8.8 years), high mean white blood cell count at diagnosis (94,200/μl), and a high proportion of National Cancer Institute high-risk (NCI-HR) cases. Genetic analysis revealed various kinase fusions (ABL1, PDGFRB, JAK2, IgH-EPOR, NCOR1-LYN, CRLF2) and a high prevalence of IKZF1 deletion (16/22 patients). Kinase fusion-positive patients demonstrated inferior outcomes, including high rates of prednisolone poor response (44.8%), induction failure (12.9%), and significantly inferior 5-year event-free survival rates (48.6±9.7%) compared to fusion-negative patients, suggesting clinical similarities to Ph+ ALL and underscoring the need for advanced stratification and targeted therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy for B-Cell Precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (BCP-ALL)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients were treated under various conventional chemotherapy clinical trial protocols (e.g., JACLS-ALL02, TCCSG, CCLSG, KYCCSG studies), which included initial prednisolone (PSL) therapy. Some patients received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs like imatinib, dasatinib) are discussed as potential targeted therapies for kinase fusion-positive patients. However, specific drug doses, durations, or detailed regimens for any treatment were not provided or directly investigated within this study; the heterogeneity of protocols was noted as a limitation. The study focused on clinical outcomes in relation to kinase fusion status.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with CRLF2 rearrangement; JAK-class rearrangements (including JAK2) are potential targets for JAK2 inhibitors. Lower prevalence suggests other genetic alterations may be involved or less frequency than previously noted.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exceptionally strong association for a single mutation in several clocks, most extreme being PhenoAge (10.01 years, p < 9.7 	 10-6).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in cell signaling pathways; mutations are strongly associated with myeloproliferative neoplasms and contribute to clonal hematopoiesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CHIP-related epigenetic age acceleration, specifically showing a very strong association with PhenoAge clock acceleration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strong association with increased PhenoAge acceleration, which is a predictor of mortality risk incorporating hematological variables, suggesting a link to myeloproliferative neoplasm and related hematological abnormalities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mesoangioblasts, shPW1 AdmMABs vs Ctl AdmMABs, non-competent AdmMAB clones, human MABs (hMABs), human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Expression Level, Gene expression (mRNA, microarray), Protein level, Transmigration assay (in vitro)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Modulated (leading to impaired function), Upregulated (in absence of PW1/Peg3), Lower (with blocking antibody), Rescued transmigration
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression is modulated by lack of PW1/Peg3, which abrogates vessel wall crossing. Robust increase in the absence of PW1/Peg3, pronounced at both mRNA and protein levels, and upregulated in non-competent clones. JAM-A blocking antibody resulted in a 1.5-fold rescue in transmigration (mouse shPW1 AdmMABs) and almost twofold rescue in non-competent hMABs. In vivo, JAM-A function impairment led to a decrease in shPW1 AdmMABs inside vessels and an increase in the interstitium 6 hours post-injection.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates trans-vessel migration as a tight junction molecule. Regulates junction tightening, involved in cell adhesion and extravasation. Repression of JAM-A promotes MAB extravasation and transmigration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Mesoangioblast ability to cross the vessel wall and engraft into damaged myofibres, particularly in the context of PW1/Peg3 absence. MAB trans-vessel migration, MAB extravasation. Absence of PW1 in MABs, JAM-A blocking antibody treatment in shPW1 AdmMABs, transmigration assays on HUVECs. Therapeutic intervention for impaired MAB migration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with mesoangioblast ability to cross the blood vessel wall and engraft into damaged myofibres; its modulation by lack of PW1/Peg3 indicates impaired migratory potential. Upregulation in shPW1 AdmMABs contributes to their inability to cross the vessel wall, thereby impairing muscle engraftment. Targeting JAM-A can restore migratory capacity of dysfunctional MABs, enhancing their therapeutic potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screening in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells, primarily Nalm6 B-ALL, to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of panobinostat resistance and action. Key findings reveal mitochondrial activity as a driver of panobinostat resistance and SIRT1 expression as a critical determinant of sensitivity. Panobinostat treatment abrogates mitochondrial activity in ALL cells, contributing to resistance, while enhancing mitochondrial function (via rosiglitazone or SIRT1 overexpression) sensitizes ALL cells to panobinostat by activating the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. The investigation identifies the SIRT1-mitochondria-PMAIP1 pathway as central to panobinostat response and suggests that higher SIRT1 expression or mitochondrial hyperactivity could indicate patient benefit from panobinostat therapy. The study also details various methods used, including cell culture, gene modulation techniques, drug sensitivity assays, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and flow cytometry.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily investigated Panobinostat, a pan-histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, often in combination with genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening or SIRT1 modulation. Other HDAC inhibitors (chidamide, vorinostat) and conventional chemotherapeutic agents (l-asparaginase, cytarabine, 6-mecaptopurine, vincristine, dexamethasone, daunorubicin) were mentioned for comparative or contextual analysis. Rosiglitazone, a PPAR   γ activator, was used to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and enhance panobinostat sensitivity.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Panobinostat was frequently used at 10 nM for durations of 24 hours (for RNA sequencing, combination treatments) or 14 days (for CRISPR screening), leading to 60-80% cell death and significant proliferation inhibition in Nalm6 cells. Gradient concentrations were employed for drug sensitivity assays. Rosiglitazone was administered at 31.25 µM for 24 or 48 hours. Dose-response comparisons for panobinostat sensitivity were analyzed using Sanger GDSC1 IC50 data across 576 diverse cancer cell lines. No specific doses or dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for other HDAC inhibitors or conventional chemotherapeutic agents.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Among the top hits (Figure 1B; supplemental Figure 2C-F); disturbing expression had no effect in validation (Figure 1C-H).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lysine acetyltransferase; involved in acetylation modification.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening during 14-day panobinostat treatment (10 nM).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a potential regulator of panobinostat resistance in CRISPR screening, but direct disturbed expression did not confer resistance in validation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association of common germline genetic variants, particularly those exhibiting differential allelic expression (DAE), with breast and ovarian cancer risk in a large cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. It identified a new modifier locus at 11q22.3 significantly associated with breast cancer risk, specifically in BRCA1 carriers, and explored potential functional implications through eQTL and chromatin analyses. While several other SNPs showed nominal associations with breast or ovarian cancer risk and specific breast cancer subtypes (ER-negative/ER-positive), most associations did not retain statistical significance after multiple testing correction.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic Association Study and Epidemiological Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational epidemiological study involving genetic risk assessment, not a therapeutic intervention. It analyzed ~320 genotyped SNPs and additional imputed SNPs across a cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. Statistical significance was set at p < 1.5 × 10^-4 after Bonferroni adjustment for multiple testing, and imputation considered SNPs with r^2 > 0.30. eQTL analysis was performed using gene expression data from normal and tumor breast tissues. No dose-response comparisons were reported as it is not a treatment study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 1.5% of variation in expression attributable to SNP rs4753834 (p = 8.6 × 10^-4, r^2 = 0.015)

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: eQTL analysis in breast cancer tissue.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates genetic influence on gene expression in breast cancer.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript, Gene Transcript (Persistence), Gene transcript level (wbRNA via RNA-Seq)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower / persistence of expression / returned to baseline in MIS-C; remained decreased in COVID-19
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in COVID-19 and MIS-C compared with controls. Observed at post-acute time point; returned to baseline in MIS-C 1 month post-hospitalization but remained decreased in COVID-19. Exhibits persistence of gene expression. Elevated wbRNA levels returned to baseline in MIS-C at 1 month post hospitalization but not in COVID-19 at 1 month post hospitalization.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: NK cell surface receptor, involved in immune response; reflects cellular activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 and MIS-C disease states compared with controls, longitudinally post-hospitalization; longitudinal sampling in MIS-C and COVID-19 patients at 1 month post hospitalization.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Consistent with lower expression reported in severe COVID-19. Potential target biomarker to discriminate between MIS-C, COVID-19, and other hyperinflammatory conditions; may indicate persistent immune dysregulation and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection ("long COVID") in COVID-19 patients, distinguishing them from MIS-C recovery; may be a useful target biomarker to discriminate among MIS-C, COVID-19, and other hyperinflammatory conditions due to persistence of expression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathological landscape, subclonal evolution, and dynamics of gene fusions, specifically KMT2A/AFDN and a novel CCDC32/CBX3, along with chimeric RNA variants, in 16 adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) patients undergoing treatment. It aimed to understand treatment resistance and relapse mechanisms by monitoring cytogenetic, RNA-seq, and genome-wide changes from diagnosis to relapse. The research identified the CCDC32/CBX3 fusion as a new therapeutic vulnerability that promotes cell cycle progression and contributes to AML pathogenesis and treatment resistance, highlighting its prognostic significance and the necessity of advanced molecular profiling for cryptic gene fusion detection.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (including high-dose cytarabine (HIDAC) and (7+3) induction chemotherapy) and Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (for Patient 7).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient 7 received HIDAC chemotherapy followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient 20 received (7+3) induction chemotherapy followed by HIDAC consolidation. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study primarily focused on biomarker monitoring and molecular changes rather than specific treatment efficacy across different doses. The study also included functional validation of gene fusion in vitro, which is not a treatment per se but part of the investigation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased during relapse (4.7-fold higher) compared to initial diagnosis, and increased by 1.3-fold after treatment compared to before treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in gene regulation and chromatin remodeling as a histone methyltransferase; wild-type counterpart to the KMT2A/AFDN fusion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: AML relapse; following (7+3) induction chemotherapy and HIDAC consolidation in AML patient 20.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates dynamic expression changes of the wild-type gene during AML relapse and represents part of the treatment-driven gene expression changes in AML patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. It further characterized 56 proteins with sustained changes, linking them to cardiometabolic traits and responses to a 20-week aerobic exercise training program. The research aimed to biochemically characterize acute exercise protein kinetics, finding enrichment for coagulation-related proteins post-exercise and MYC targets, and noting both concordant and discordant protein responses between acute and chronic exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute treadmill exercise and chronic aerobic exercise training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise consisted of symptom-limited treadmill stress testing in 75 middle-aged adults, following a standard Bruce protocol with plasma protein quantification at baseline, peak exercise (mean 90% predicted peak heart rate, 9.6 METs), and 1-hour post-exercise. Chronic exercise involved a 20-week aerobic training program with three sessions per week, with intensity and duration gradually increased based on individual VO2max. Acute exercise intensity and duration varied, making it difficult to effectively analyze specific exertion thresholds or dose-response comparisons for the acute protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multi-phase, multi-center study developed and validated a machine learning-enabled blood-derived exosomal RNA profiling platform (ETR.sig) for noninvasive multi-cancer detection and localization, demonstrating its robust potential for accurate diagnosis, tumor origin classification, and prognostic assessment across eight primary cancer types.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery and validation for multi-cancer detection and prognosis using exosomal RNA signatures.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This multi-phase, multi-center study involved a discovery phase (818 participants, 8 cancer types, 194 healthy controls, exoRNA-seq), a screening phase (245 participants, TaqMan qPCR), and a validation phase (1,385 participants). Machine learning (Random Forest and LASSO algorithms) was applied to refine 33 initial candidate biomarkers down to 12 exosomal tumor RNA signatures (ETR.sig). Diagnostic models were built with stratified random sampling (7:3 or 8:2 training/validation splits, tenfold cross-validation). Filtering criteria for differential gene expression included |log2FC|>1 and P<0.05 for bulk RNA-seq, and P<0.01 with FC ≥1.4 or ≤−1.6 for multi-cancer exoRNA-seq. The study focused on diagnostic development and biomarker identification, thus no therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the feasibility and biological correlations of simultaneously quantifying perfusion, permeability, and novel contrast leakage effects in brain gliomas using dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) with a single contrast injection. The research detailed the methodology for acquiring and processing MRI data from 38 adult-type diffuse glioma patients, focusing on parameters like TRATE, ΔR2,ss*, ΔR1,ss, ADC, nrCBV, PSR, Ktrans, and ve. Key findings demonstrate that dynamic SAGE-EPI enables the simultaneous assessment of these parameters, providing new metrics that correlate with previous treatment exposure, IDH status, and Ki67 expression, offering advantages like shorter scan times and reduced contrast agent use, and revealing distinct differences in contrast agent dynamics and tissue properties between treatment-naïve and recurrent gliomas, as well as between IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype tumors. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

Also identified as a protein with 'large weights' in the organ aging models, indicating significant predictive power, though no explicit direction of change for individual levels was detailed.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Implied role in longevity and kidney aging. Suggests a potential causal role in organ aging and is associated with organ-specific disease risk, contributing to the prediction of mortality and functional decline.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in both EXE and EXO trials, peaking during the recovery phase at 38.5°C (EXE: p < 0.0001, from 52.9 nM to 83.7 nM; EXO: p < 0.05, from 52.6 nM to 65.7 nM). Concentrations steadily increased during the heating phase of the EXE trial and reached their peak during recovery. Unlike most other metabolites, KYNA did not revert to baseline levels upon returning to homeostatic temperatures. Detected in concentrations higher than the LLOQ of 5 nM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neuroprotective metabolite of the kynurenine pathway, involved in tryptophan degradation, neurological and psychiatric disorders, immune responses, cardiovascular function, and energy metabolism. It acts as an antagonist at glutamate receptors and modulates neurotransmission. Skeletal muscle is a major source of peripheral KYNA, with exercise stimulating PGC-1α expression and KAT enzyme activity, leading to increased peripheral KYNA levels.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Core temperature increases induced by exogenous heating (hot water immersion, 44°C) or exertional heating (exercise/cycling at 60% VO2max in a 30°C room), until rectal temperature reached 39°C, followed by a recovery phase. Samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential disease biomarker whose fluctuations are important for assessing dysfunction. It indicates a potential neuroprotective response or modulation of neuronal excitability during recovery from heat stress. Higher plasma KYNA levels are hypothesized in EXE due to unique skeletal muscle activation. Its sustained elevation post-recovery may be due to relatively slow elimination via urine and is implicated in various diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Key and significant metabolite hits within the tryptophan pathway (pathway significantly influenced by hemp fiber supplementation, p < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences observed between groups 55 days after starting the dietary intervention (p < 0.002).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, cross-over study investigated the effects of acute cocoa flavanol (CF) intake on exercise-induced changes in antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress, inflammation, nitric oxide (NO) production, exercise performance, and recovery in well-trained male cyclists. Findings showed acute CF intake increased systemic epicatechin levels and total antioxidant capacity (TEAC/UA and UA), but did not significantly affect exercise-induced lipid peroxidation (MDA), inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α), or NO production markers (L-arginine/ADMA, citrulline). While CF intake showed a tendency for improved late-stage performance in the first time trial, overall exercise performance and recovery were not significantly enhanced.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received an acute dose of either 903.75 mg of cocoa flavanols (CF) or a placebo (15 mg CF) in chocolate milk prior to exercise. The exercise protocol involved two 30-minute time trials (TT1 and TT2) performed at a workload equivalent to 75% of peak power output, separated by a 100-minute passive recovery. No explicit dose-response comparisons were conducted beyond the high-CF vs. placebo design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytotoxic and immunomodulatory effects of chemotherapeutic agents (cisplatin, oxaliplatin, pemetrexed) on malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) cell lines, both alone and in allogeneic co-culture with healthy donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). The primary aim was to assess the impact of these agents on the expression of immune checkpoints (PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3) and their ligands (PD-L1, PD-L2, galectin-9) to inform rational combination strategies with immune checkpoint blockade. While chemosensitivity varied by cell line (e.g., NCI-H2818 more sensitive to cisplatin and oxaliplatin, no response to pemetrexed), the expression of immune checkpoints and their ligands on MPM cells and PBMCs was mostly downregulated or unaltered, with only TIM-3 on PBMC co-cultured with NCI-H2731 showing significant alteration after cisplatin treatment. The findings generally showed no clear trend or significant changes, highlighting interexperimental variability and suggesting complex interactions relevant for designing optimal immunotherapy combination schedules.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (cisplatin, oxaliplatin, pemetrexed, and combinations thereof for the core study; other agents like decitabine, doxorubicin, paclitaxel, panobinostat, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone were mentioned for contextual comparison from literature).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Desired inhibitory concentrations (IC values: IC20, IC40, IC50, IC60) for cisplatin, oxaliplatin, and pemetrexed were determined via SRB-assay across three MPM cell lines (NCI-H2818, NCI-H2795, NCI-H2731). Specific concentration ranges tested were cisplatin (0-50  5M), oxaliplatin (0-50  5M), and pemetrexed (0-10  5M). For further co-culture experiments, IC20 values were typically used, with 0.05  5M specifically mentioned for pemetrexed. All treatments were applied for 72 hours. Susceptibility to cisplatin and oxaliplatin was cell-line dependent (e.g., NCI-H2818 was significantly more sensitive to both), while pemetrexed showed no cytotoxic response in any cell line. No significant difference in cell survival was observed between cisplatin and cisplatin + pemetrexed treatment groups. PBMC were co-cultured with MPM cells at a 10:1 (Effector:Target) ratio. The study acknowledged significant interexperimental variability and inconsistency in effects on immune checkpoint expression across different studies and agents.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific quantification provided, but identified as 'MEK inhibitor-specific biomarkers'.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identified by MiSL as a novel genetic biomarker for MEK inhibitors in lung squamous cancer, not represented in existing cell lines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predictive biomarker for MEK inhibitor sensitivity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased the age gap association with dementia severity (FIBA-); primarily expressed in oligodendrocytes. Shown to be crucial for neuronal health in mouse models.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primarily expressed in oligodendrocytes, crucial for neuronal health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's disease, cognitive decline, brain aging mechanisms.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Involved in brain aging, but its contribution (or higher levels) decreases the model's association with dementia severity. Important for neuronal health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the functional implications of heterogeneity in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), focusing on an endodermally biased pluripotent substate. Using a GATA6-GFP reporter line and single-cell functional/transcriptomic analyses, the research identified distinct, interconvertible hESC substates defined by differential expression of GATA6 and SSEA3. GATA6-positive hESCs, while retaining long-term self-renewal and pluripotency (often alongside OCT4 and SOX2 co-expression), exhibited a higher propensity and bias towards spontaneous endoderm and mesoderm differentiation, with downregulation of ectodermal genes. SOX17 was identified as a potential driver for this endoderm-biased substate.

Cells were cultured in KO/SR on MEF feeders or E8 medium. hESC substates, defined by differential GATA6 and SSEA3 expression (e.g., 3+/6-, 3+/6L, 3+/6H, 3-/6+), were isolated by Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS). These sorted cells were subjected to single-cell cloning, gene expression analysis (qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing), high-content clonogenic assays, and differentiation protocols, including a spin-embryoid body (EB) system, without external therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for differentiation-inducing factors. The focus was on intrinsic marker expression and resultant lineage bias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association of common germline genetic variants, particularly those exhibiting differential allelic expression (DAE), with breast and ovarian cancer risk in a large cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. It identified a new modifier locus at 11q22.3 significantly associated with breast cancer risk, specifically in BRCA1 carriers, and explored potential functional implications through eQTL and chromatin analyses. While several other SNPs showed nominal associations with breast or ovarian cancer risk and specific breast cancer subtypes (ER-negative/ER-positive), most associations did not retain statistical significance after multiple testing correction.

Statistical significance was set at p < 1.5 × 10^-4 after Bonferroni adjustment for multiple testing, and imputation considered SNPs with r^2 > 0.30. eQTL analysis was performed using gene expression data from normal and tumor breast tissues. No dose-response comparisons were reported as it is not a treatment study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced expression observed in sorafenib-treated cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated metallothioneins (MTs) as potential dynamic biomarkers for Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) and other Lysosomal Storage Diseases (LSDs) with nervous system involvement. It identified significant overexpression of MT genes and proteins, including specific isoforms (MT1A, MT1E, MT2A, MTE, MT1P3-C20ORF127), in T lymphocytes and brain tissue of MLD patients and various LSD mouse models. MT levels correlated with disease progression, nervous tissue damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation, and decreased upon therapeutic treatment. In vitro experiments elucidated that MT expression is regulated in response to proinflammatory and pro-oxidative stimuli and through microglia-astrocyte crosstalk, supporting their role as dynamic markers of disease pathology, progression, and therapeutic response in LSDs.

General therapeutic treatment in mice resulted in decreased biomarker levels, but specific treatment types, doses, intensity, or duration details were not provided. In vitro studies applied experimental conditions such as 10ng/ml lipopolysaccharide, 100
M H2O2-1mM L-buthionine-sulfoximine, 1mM Trolox, 10
M dexamethasone, and 10% serum from WT and GLD mice to primary cortical astrocytes and astrocyte/microglia cocultures for 6 or 24 hours; these were experimental conditions and not patient treatments.
