document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. The study also explored genetic associations with cerebellar gray matter volume, linking several genetic variants to cardiovascular disease and other health indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of early brain injury and cognitive impairment following aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH) using MRI and cognitive assessments.

An additional 27 paired healthy controls were recruited for comparison. No specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study of SAH's natural course and sequelae.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review explores the application and convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Systems Biology (SysBio) in advancing stem cell research and therapeutics development. It details how these computational approaches, including advanced bioinformatics and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) analysis, enable integrated analysis of large-scale multi-omics data, enhance understanding of stem cell behavior and heterogeneity, facilitate the identification of specific markers and therapeutic targets, and optimize clinical trial design for improved safety and efficacy. The review also highlights strategies for addressing challenges like tumorigenicity and proposes frameworks for integrating SysBioAI to improve therapy performance and product development, particularly for Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs), induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs), Embryonic Stem Cells (ESCs), and CAR-T cell therapies, including a predictive model for optimal MSC doses in cartilage repair.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The document primarily reviews the application of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Systems Biology (SysBioAI) in optimizing various stem cell-based therapies, including Mesenchymal Stem Cell (MSC) therapy for cartilage repair, CAR-T cell therapy, and the broader development of iPSCs and ESCs. It focuses on conceptual and methodological frameworks for computational analysis rather than a single specific therapeutic method investigated by the authors.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

These variants were also associated with considerably more pronounced lymphopenia (P < 0.05) and a 4-fold higher median neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported as a change from intervention; used to determine Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT) as a 1 mmol rise above minimum lactate equivalent.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase after each bout of exhaustive exercise. Baseline values did not differ between bouts. Showed the second highest percentage increment after cf n-DNA, reaching about half and one-fourth of cf n-DNA's increment after the first and third bouts, respectively.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism; accumulates during high-intensity exercise, marker of metabolic stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After each of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the intensity of exercise and the extent of anaerobic energy production, reflecting metabolic stress and fatigue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a single 6g dose of citrulline malate (CM) supplementation on muscle recovery after a high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session in untrained young adult men, examining functional, metabolic, anabolic, and physiological markers. The findings concluded that CM supplementation does not improve the muscle recovery process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Citrulline Malate (CM) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single oral dose of 6 g of citrulline malate (CM) was administered 60 minutes pre-workout, dissolved in 200 mL water. Participants then performed a single session of high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) consisting of 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions at 90% of 10RM for leg press and hack squat exercises, with 2 min rest between sets and exercises, performed with a 1s concentric:2s eccentric cadence. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and no significant treatment × time interaction was found for any measured variables, indicating CM did not improve recovery compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma lactate levels increased significantly (p < 0.001) immediately post-exercise and remained elevated at 24, 48, and 72 h in both CM and placebo conditions, with no significant differences between treatments (treatment × time p = 0.456).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis, indicating metabolic stress and fatigue, but also an energy substrate and a waste product associated with lactic acid production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blood samples collected pre- and post-exercise, and immediately after muscular fatigue tests (24, 48, and 72 h after RE session) during recovery from a single high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session with CM or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Metabolic indicator of acute exercise intensity, anaerobic metabolism, and subsequent metabolic recovery; CM supplementation did not show beneficial effects on lactate reduction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proof-of-concept study investigated whether a single session of High-Intensity Training (HIT) could restore impaired counterregulatory hormonal, symptomatic, and cognitive responses to subsequent insulin-induced hypoglycemia in people with type 1 diabetes and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH). The findings supported the hypothesis that IAH develops as a habituated response, demonstrating that HIT significantly amplified adrenaline responses and total symptom awareness during subsequent hypoglycemia, although it also led to a significant prolongation of cognitive reaction time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity training (HIT) compared to controlled rest
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single HIT session lasting 20 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down, with 4 x 30-second cycle sprints at 150% of maximum wattage (V̇O2peak assessment) interspersed with 2-minute recovery periods. Participants aimed for >90% peak heart rate. This was directly compared to 20 minutes of seated rest, and no dose-response comparisons for HIT were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked rise during HIT, specifically a 12-fold increase from 0.95 (0.09) to 12.28 (0.78) mmol/l (p <0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A metabolic by-product of anaerobic glycolysis, reflecting high-intensity exercise and energy demand, which can serve as an energy substrate and is involved in various metabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During HIT intervention in individuals with type 1 diabetes and IAH.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms the acute metabolic impact and effectiveness of the HIT intervention, indicating a significant metabolic challenge and reliance on anaerobic energy pathways.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then reduced but remained elevated
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (from 1.9 to 13.5 mmol.L^-1, always exceeding 10 mmol.L^-1) and decreased by 30 min post-exercise, but remained above baseline (>2.8 mmol.L^-1) for all participants (p<0.01). No significant differences were observed between novice and experienced individuals in the magnitude of change (p<0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, indicator of metabolic stress; involved in energy metabolism, byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT); acute 'Cindy' workout session.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute metabolic stress and the extent of anaerobic energy contribution during high-intensity exercise, reflecting fatigue. High levels indicate significant work intensity and high anaerobic demand.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral venous lactate concentrations in hospitalized patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 and mild ambulatory COVID-19 patients, comparing these levels to non-SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia and malaria cases. Findings indicate that lactate levels are significantly higher in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, decrease during recovery, and remain elevated in a subgroup with prolonged viral positivity, suggesting lactate's utility in risk stratification and monitoring disease severity and course.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Monitoring of COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study comparing peripheral venous lactate concentrations in two groups: 18 hospitalized patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 and 16 ambulatory patients with mild COVID-19. Lactate levels were monitored longitudinally on days 1, 7, 14, and 28 for hospitalized patients, and days 1, 14, and 28 for ambulatory patients. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median whole blood lactate levels were 3.3 mmol/L in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 1.4 mmol/L in ambulatory patients on day 1 (P = 0.002).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and cellular stress, often associated with tissue hypoxia or increased metabolic demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between hospitalized moderate to severe COVID-19 patients and mild ambulatory COVID-19 patients at disease onset.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates more severe disease in hospitalized COVID-19 patients at disease onset, useful for risk stratification.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median whole blood lactate levels were 1.9 mmol/L in hospitalized patients and 1.5 mmol/L in ambulatory patients on day 28 (P < 0.0001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and cellular stress, often associated with tissue hypoxia or increased metabolic demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between hospitalized moderate to severe COVID-19 patients and mild ambulatory COVID-19 patients at later stages of recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates persistent metabolic differences between hospitalized and ambulatory COVID-19 patients even at later stages of recovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median whole blood lactate levels in hospitalized patients decreased significantly from 3.3 mmol/L (day 1) to 1.9 mmol/L (day 28) during clinical course and recovery (P = 0.008).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and cellular stress, often associated with tissue hypoxia or increased metabolic demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clinical course and recovery in hospitalized moderate to severe COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improvement in clinical condition and recovery from COVID-19; useful for monitoring disease progression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently elevated in four hospitalized patients with prolonged SARS-CoV-2 viral positivity on day 7.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and cellular stress, often associated with tissue hypoxia or increased metabolic demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hospitalized COVID-19 patients with prolonged SARS-CoV-2 viral positivity (beyond day 7).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with delayed viral clearance and potentially more persistent disease activity or metabolic dysfunction in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Moderately elevated compared to non-SARS-CoV-2 infections; median level of around 4 mmol/L for severe COVID-19 (CURB-65 ">= 4"); levels > 5 mmol/L associated with severe disease and fatal outcomes in malaria.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and tissue hypoxia, reflecting processes like decreased oxygen diffusion in lungs (COVID-19 pneumonia) or microvascular obstruction (malaria).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hospitalized patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia (CURB-65 >= 4) and comparison to severe systemic infections like malaria.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severe disease, predicts fatal outcomes (especially in severe systemic infections), and reflects a longer course of illness in COVID-19. Useful for general risk stratification and understanding distinct pathophysiological processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study investigated the ergogenic effects of acute pre-exercise homemade chicken broth (CB) ingestion, rich in histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) like carnosine and anserine, on high-intensity cycling performance in recreationally-trained men. The study found a significant 5.2% improvement in 8-minute time trial mean power and elevated plasma carnosine and anserine levels following CB supplementation. However, the ergogenic effect was not mediated by changes in acid-base balance or red blood cell glutathione status, indicating alternative mechanisms may be at play.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute pre-exercise nutritional supplementation (homemade chicken broth or placebo soup)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested either 8 mL/kg body weight of homemade chicken broth (CB), providing 46.4 mg/kg body weight of total histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) (specifically 15.6 mg/kg BW carnosine and 30.8 mg/kg BW anserine), or an equivalent volume of a placebo soup. The supplement was administered 25-40 minutes prior to an 8-minute high-intensity cycling time trial, following a warm-up. No dose-response comparisons were made, only CB versus placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant effects of chicken broth supplementation were observed on blood lactate levels. During the time-trial, lactate levels naturally increased from 1 to 16 mmol/L.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, serving as an energy substrate and associated with muscle fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During an 8-min high-intensity cycling time-trial following acute pre-exercise chicken broth ingestion.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Unchanged lactate levels suggest that the ergogenic effect of chicken broth is not due to altered lactate production or clearance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by approximately 3.7-fold in response to CCombat exercise, returning to basal levels during recovery. Post-CCombat lactate showed a positive correlation with post-CCombat glucose (r s 0.52). Lactate during short and long recovery correlated positively with urate (r s 0.50 10.74).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolic marker, product of anaerobic glycolysis, indicating glycolytic pathway demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During and post-CCombat exercise, including short and long recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the intensity of anaerobic metabolism and high energetic demand of cyclic exercise, associated with myokinase activity and uremia maintenance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Exercise-induced changes are being investigated (in current study protocol).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes from baseline will be collected and analyzed; measured via Lactate Plus, Nova Biomedical at rest, 5 min into treadmill test, every 2-3 min until exhaustion, and 3 min after test completion.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, indicating increased glycolysis and exercise intensity; also an indicator of endurance capacity and metabolic efficiency.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week probiotic intervention during endurance treadmill test; collected during V̇O2 max and time-to-exhaustion tests.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects anaerobic energy contribution and exercise fatigue, influencing running performance and fuel use patterns during running.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of low (0.625 mg) and high (2.5 mg) doses of phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation on full squat performance, muscle damage, protein breakdown, metabolic response, and perceived exertion in resistance-trained males. It concluded that high-dose PC favorably influenced squat performance, reduced active muscle perceived exertion, and attenuated muscle damage compared to placebo, suggesting an ergogenic effect primarily with the higher dose.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation during resistance training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received oral phenylcapsaicin (PC) supplementation 45 minutes before exercise, with conditions including a low dose (LD) of 0.625 mg, a high dose (HD) of 2.5 mg, and a placebo (PLA) of maltodextrin. The resistance exercise protocol involved full squat sets of 3x8 repetitions at 70% 1RM, with lifting velocity monitored. The high dose (HD) demonstrated superior biochemical and mechanical anti-fatigue effects compared to the low dose and placebo, indicating a dose-response relationship where higher doses were more effective.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant differences for time (pre-post comparisons) (F = 269.62, p < 0.001); no significant differences for condition (F = 1.49, p = 0.23) or condition × time interaction (F = 0.94, p = 0.34). Post-exercise lactate levels tended to be lower in HD conditions compared to PLA and LD, though non-significant.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, often associated with exercise intensity and fatigue; also described as a potent endogenous inhibitor of TRPV1 activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre- and post-resistance training (SQ exercise), 90 seconds after the last squat set, after phenylcapsaicin supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects metabolic stress during exercise; no significant effect of PC supplementation on lactate levels was observed, though a non-significant trend towards lower levels in HD might suggest modulated sarcoplasmic calcium efflux channels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively investigates the potentials, pitfalls, and practical applications of blood-based biomarkers for objective individualized monitoring of training load, recovery, and health status in elite sports. It evaluates the utility and limitations of established markers like creatine kinase (CK), lactate, C-reactive protein (CRP), urea, myoglobin, and various leukocyte populations, detailing their physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise, kinetics, and implications for muscle damage, immune function, and inflammation. The document also addresses methodological considerations, confounding variables, the need for individual reference ranges, and statistical approaches for interpreting biomarker changes, concluding with recommendations for best practices in their sport-specific use.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-based biomarker monitoring in conjunction with physical exercise and training load management in elite sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review focuses on the application and interpretation of blood-based biomarkers for athlete monitoring across various exercise loads, including strenuous, resistance, high-intensity, submaximal, acute physical stress, soccer matches, ultradistance races, and long-term intensive endurance exercise. Biomarker responses are noted to depend on exercise modality, intensity, duration, and individual factors such as ethnicity and body composition. While specific exercise regimens like 30 minutes of endurance running (65% vs 85% of VO2max) showed CRP increases, no single standardized dose-response is consistently reported or compared across all biomarkers. The document emphasizes the need for individual reference levels, standardized collection, and careful consideration of confounding variables, particularly in managing workload by adjusting training when physiological parameters exceed baseline.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Varies with exercise intensity and nutritional aspects; site-dependent differences observed; changes
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Varies significantly with exercise intensity and nutritional aspects (e.g., low-carbohydrate availability shifts thresholds). Site-dependent differences exist (e.g., earlobe vs. fingertip during graded exercise). It correlates well with RPE during high-intensity soccer exercise but not submaximal cycling, and reflects aspects of acute psychophysiological response.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Produced by skeletal muscles to remove pyruvate, regenerate NAD+ for ATP regeneration, and contribute to metabolic proton buffering; serves as an indicator of acute psychophysiological response to exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During, before, and after various types of exercise including acute, submaximal rowing, graded, high-intensity soccer, submaximal cycling, repeated high-intensity training, physiological exercise testing, and under conditions of low-carbohydrate availability.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Valuable for determining intensity thresholds, measuring acute exercise intensity, and assessing the efficacy of training sessions. It is a useful, load-sensitive variable in acute exercise, but a consistent sampling site is crucial due to site-dependent differences. Lower levels from glycogen depletion should not be misinterpreted as training improvement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Promoted the reduction of exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers; decreased by 12% (p = 0.003) and decreased compared with control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: By-product of anaerobic metabolism, an indicator of muscle fatigue during intense exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise-induced, specifically high-intensity and high-speed running performance; moderate resistance training with SP supplementation; moderate endurance training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Delayed fatigue, improved endurance performance, and enhanced metabolic efficiency in active individuals and athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed predictive models using a novel machine learning pipeline to identify viable intrauterine pregnancies (Live Normally Sited Pregnancies, LNSP) in symptomatic women, differentiating them from combined adverse outcomes (CAO) such as miscarriage, pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). The models integrate serum metabolite levels (untargeted 1H NMR profiling) with plasma hormone concentrations (β-hCG and progesterone) and clinicodemographic data, finding that a composite biomarker provides superior predictive accuracy (0.79). The aim is to offer a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic test to reduce diagnostic burden and improve outcomes in early gestation by accurately identifying LNSP and excluding conditions associated with maternal morbidity and mortality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker identification and predictive model development using machine learning, untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, and hormone assays.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 370 symptomatic pregnant women (≤10 weeks gestation), presenting with abdominal pain and/or vaginal bleeding. A single blood sample was collected upon first emergency presentation; plasma was used for β-hCG and progesterone concentration measurements, and serum for untargeted metabolomic profiling. Nine key metabolite signals were identified. Random forest models were constructed and compared: a model using metabolite signals alone yielded 0.68 accuracy, β-hCG and progesterone alone yielded 0.71 accuracy, and the combined model achieved the best predictive accuracy of 0.79. Model performance was assessed using an independent validation cohort. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic accuracy for pregnancy outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: While identified as significantly perturbed in tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP) versus live normally-sited pregnancy (LNSP) in a previous study, it was not significantly different in the cohort examined in this study between tEP and LNSP controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolite, primarily involved in anaerobic energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP) and live normally-sited pregnancy (LNSP) controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not validated as a differentiating biomarker in this specific cohort, despite conflicting findings from previous research.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time course of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and conventional muscle damage markers in response to mechanically demanding muscle-damaging drop jump exercise without significant metabolic stress in healthy males. It found that cfDNA levels increased acutely and with a delayed response up to 72 hours post-exercise, correlating strongly with primary muscle damage indicators (low-frequency fatigue, MVIC torque, P20/P100 torque) and delayed-onset muscle soreness. This suggests cfDNA is a sensitive marker for acute loss of muscle function after mechanical stress, offering insights into primary and secondary muscle damage responses.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Muscle-damaging exercise (Drop Jumps)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fourteen participants performed 50 intermittent drop jumps once, from heights of approximately 0.5 m (ranging from 30.37 ± 5.55 cm to 36.39 ± 6.83 cm) with 20-second rest intervals between each jump. This protocol was designed to be mechanically demanding, inducing sufficient primary and secondary muscle damage, without placing the organism under significant metabolic stress. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease immediately post-exercise (from 1.52 ± 0.29 to 1.21 ± 0.35 mmol/L, P = 0.016); decrease still evident 45 min post-exercise (1.2 ± 0.28 mmol/L, P = 0.012).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis, typically indicating metabolic stress, but also used as a substrate for energy production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately and 45 minutes post-exercise after 50 Drop Jumps (exercise designed to be without metabolic stress).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The observed decrease confirms that the exercise protocol did not induce significant metabolic stress and suggests accelerated lactate uptake and utilization by muscles, rather than accumulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased considerably during the games, particularly in the second match. Athlete 2 showed a 75% increase compared to Athlete 1's 21% increase after the second match, and a 45% higher increase overall after the second match. The first match did not significantly impact Athlete 1's lactatemia considerably.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, reflecting glycolytic energy production and exercise intensity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition Day (during/post-matches).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a classic marker of exercise-induced metabolic stress and the activation of anaerobic energy pathways during intense physical activity, corroborating the high-intensity nature of competition and suggesting cumulative strain and fatigue accumulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Samples collected immediately prior to and following the completion of the 3000m race. Specific quantitative data on changes not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic glycolysis and metabolic stress during exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately prior to and following a 3000m time trial.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with exercise intensity, fatigue onset, and anaerobic capacity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced accumulation (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis, accumulating during intense exercise and contributing to muscle fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation during resistance training and following exercise, in both human and animal studies.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates improved anaerobic capacity, delayed onset of fatigue, and faster recovery post-exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes the development, optimization, and validation of a portable, low-cost, and 3D-printed electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor capable of simultaneously detecting glucose and lactate in real serum. The biosensor integrates interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) within a bipolar electrochemical system and leverages a smartphone-based readout, demonstrating high sensitivity, reproducibility, and accuracy within physiologically relevant ranges, thereby offering a scalable and field-deployable solution for point-of-care metabolic monitoring and biomedical diagnostics.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Development, fabrication, optimization, and validation of a 3D-printed electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor for diagnostic purposes.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The biosensor was fabricated using dual-extrusion FDM 3D printing (0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer height, 40 mm/s printing speed, 220 °C nozzle, 60 °C heated bed, 100% infill) and featured six pairs of interdigitated electrodes. Operational parameters were optimized for voltage (3-10 V, with signal saturation observed beyond optimal), luminol concentration (4 mM), pH, and enzyme concentrations (glucose oxidase at 10 mg/mL, lactate oxidase at 50 U/mL, with 90-120 s incubation). This optimization led to detection limits of 0.1 mM for glucose (linear range 0.1-5.0 mM) and 80 µM for lactate (linear range 0.1-4.0 mM), with real serum recovery rates of 95–102%. Interdigitated electrodes provided approximately a 2.5-fold increase in luminescence signal compared to planar electrodes. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported as the study focused on diagnostic device performance.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Real human serum and target analyte solutions (for biosensor characterization).
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: ECL Signal Intensity Measurement (Enzyme-coupled Electrochemical Luminescence Biosensing for concentration detection/monitoring).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ECL signal intensity is directly proportional to lactate concentration, quantified in Relative Light Units (RLU) and measured via smartphone camera. The sensor exhibited a detection limit of 80 µM (0.08 mM), a strong linear correlation (R² = 0.9453) in the range of 0.1 mM to 4.0 mM (with saturation beyond 4 mM), and 95-102% recovery rates in real serum. In human serum, it measured 1.27 mM compared to 1.30 mM by a clinical method (97.69% accuracy), demonstrating reproducible and reliable quantification across varying concentrations.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis, a key metabolite in energy metabolism, and an important indicator of tissue hypoxia, metabolic stress, and energy status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Real-time monitoring for chronic diseases, sepsis, trauma, and physiological stress scenarios, validated through the development and characterization of a 3D-printed, smartphone-integrated ECL biosensor in analyte solutions and human serum.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Critical for assessing metabolic status, detecting physiological stress, and diagnosing systemic complications. The low LOD (80 µM) enables early detection of subtle metabolic shifts, with values ≥ 2 mM being clinically actionable in conditions such as sepsis, ischemia, trauma, and sports physiology, making it suitable for real-time point-of-care testing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased only during the EXE trial, peaking at 39°C (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: By-product of anaerobic metabolism, reflecting energy demand and metabolic stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exertional heating (EXE) heat stress trial induced by core temperature increases, with samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments up to 39°C and subsequent decrease until 37.5°C.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased anaerobic glycolysis and metabolic strain during acute heat stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased 0 h post-exercise compared to pre-exercise levels across all protocols: SE (9.0 ± 0.5 mmol·L−1 vs. 1.2 ± 0.1 mmol·L−1, p < 0.05); MH (10.6 ± 0.6 mmol·L−1 vs. 1.1 ± 0.1 mmol·L−1, p < 0.05); MS (4.8 ± 0.4 mmol·L−1 vs. 1.1 ± 0.1 mmol·L−1, p < 0.05). Levels nearly decreased to baseline by 1 h post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to acute Muscular Strength Endurance (SE), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH), and Maximum Strength (MS) Resistance Training protocols.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates intensity of anaerobic metabolic activity during exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-of-day-dependent physiological, physical, and psychological responses of higher-weight men to a Walking Football Match (WFM). Findings revealed that evening WFM led to significantly lower glycemia, mean blood pressure (MBP), and heart rate recovery after 1 minute (HRR60s) compared to morning sessions, suggesting potential safety and metabolic benefits for higher-weight individuals when exercising in the evening. Most other parameters, including HRV, lactate, SpO2, and various physical performance metrics, showed no significant diurnal variation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Walking Football Match (WFM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a single session of 5 vs. 5 Walking Football Matches (WFM) on artificial turf fields. Each session lasted approximately one hour, comprising a 10-min warm-up, two 20-min playing periods separated by a 10-min passive recovery, and a 5-min cool-down. Matches were performed in randomized order, either in the morning (6:30 a.m. - 8:30 a.m.) or in the evening (5:00 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.), with 7 days between sessions. The activity was classified as moderate intensity (4.85-4.9 METs), with participants averaging around 2500-2600 steps per session and a cadence of approximately 63.8 steps/min. The study primarily focused on time-of-day effects, with no explicit dose-response comparisons regarding WFM intensity or duration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased after the WFM at both morning and evening sessions. A previous study revealed a significant increase of around 157% post-session. No significant diurnal variation noted.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of glycolytic pathway activity and energy metabolism during exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After Walking Football Match, in both morning and evening sessions in higher-weight men.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Highlights the high intensity of WFM, indicating significant demand on the glycolytic pathway.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Release of lactate from cells, a byproduct of glycolysis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates disturbed energy metabolism and potentially increased anaerobic glycolysis in ME/CFS patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and evaluated a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol in collegiate athletes, demonstrating that it significantly enhances the recovery of cardiovascular and biochemical biomarkers (heart rate, lactic acid, and creatine kinase) compared to regular training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 4-week intervention included a Taekwondo-specific HIIT protocol compared to a control group receiving regular Taekwondo training. The HIIT was structured in two phases: Weeks 1-2 involved six rounds of four kicking techniques (21s work, 12s rest, 1.75:1 WRR) at 85% HRmax; Weeks 3-4 increased to eight rounds of the same techniques (24s work, 8s rest, 3:1 WRR) at 90% HRmax. Both phases included 1-minute rest between rounds. The control group performed regular Taekwondo training (90 min/session, 5 times/week) at 70-80% HRmax. Significant differences were observed between the groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant (p ">= 0.05) post-intervention reductions and faster clearance were observed in the HIIT group compared to the control group. The HIIT group showed significant changes at E5 and E24 within the group, and significant differences at PostE5 and PostE24 between groups, indicating rapid LA recovery. Detection range for blood LA was 0.5-40 mmol/L, with a coefficient of variation ">= 1.5%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism, byproduct of energy production, and a biomarker of fatigue and exertion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise recovery during and after a Taekwondo-specific High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) protocol.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved lactate clearance, reduced metabolic stress, and enhanced recovery capacity, contributing to sustained maximal effort and reduced fatigue in competitions.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Lactate Dehydrogenase: Gefunden in 28 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute exhaustive exercise / Symptom-limited incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single session of acute exhaustive exercise was performed by 28 male chronic heart failure (CHF) participants (mean age 59.07  1 1.79 years). The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels (Table 3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased muscle damage following acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated circulating myomesin 3 fragments as a novel biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage, finding that plasma levels significantly increased 96 hours after acute eccentric exercise in humans and positively correlated with established muscle damage biomarkers (CK, Mb, LDH) and muscle symptoms (tenderness, DOMS).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Eccentric Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention involved nine healthy males performing 10 sets of 40 repetitions of one-leg calf-raise exercise (total 400 repetitions) with a load corresponding to half their body weight. Ankle ROM was maintained between 20 0 dorsiflexion and 15 0 plantar flexion, at a speed of 60 counts/min (1 repetition/s); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Percent changes positively correlated with myomesin 3 fragments (R = 0.674, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytosolic enzyme that leaks into the blood following sarcolemma damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute eccentric exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Established biomarker for muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated urinary proteins responsive to acute eccentric calf-raise exercise in healthy males, identifying an N-terminal fragment of titin. The urinary titin fragment significantly increased 96 hours post-exercise and correlated strongly with established blood biomarkers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion), proposing its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Eccentric Calf-Raise Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute, single-leg calf-raise exercise (right leg) involving repetitive eccentric muscle contractions. The protocol consisted of 10 sets of 40 repetitions (total 400 repetitions) with 3-minute rest between sets, performed at 60 counts/min. Ankle joint range of motion was maintained between 20° dorsiflexion and 15° plantar flexion, with an exercise load approximately half the subject's body weight. Samples were collected before and up to 96 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant correlations between changes in urinary titin fragment concentrations and changes in serum LDH after acute eccentric exercise. Positive correlation between titin fragment at 48 h and LDH at 72 h (r = 0.91, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established marker of muscle damage, indicating muscle cell injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After acute eccentric exercise; exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher, indicating muscle damage. Highest increases observed compared to other sports. Significant differences found during periods of significant reduction in training load or match congestion/intensity (e.g., playoff season).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme released from damaged cells, indicating muscle cell damage and tissue breakdown.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise (over preseason and season), periods of match congestion and intensity (e.g., playoff season), periods of significant reduction in training load, and sports with higher eccentric loads.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Sensitive tool for detecting changes in muscle damage levels. Useful for monitoring physical state during the season, especially during congested matches or decreased training/match load, to adjust training/recovery programs and minimize injury risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No changes in the values of selected immune system parameters: muscle enzymes: lactate dehydrogenase (LAD) were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy metabolism, whose elevated levels can indicate cell and tissue damage, particularly muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Italian national rugby team members (n=10) after cryotherapy (5 sessions/week, once a day, -110°C/2 min).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant muscle damage or recovery effect was detected by this cryotherapy protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A leucine/carbohydrate beverage did not affect serum lactate dehydrogenase at 24 h, 48 h, or 72 h following exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy metabolism, elevated levels in blood can indicate tissue damage, including muscle.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 6 sets of heavy back squats.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage; no effect of BCAA-CHO suggests muscle fibers were damaged irrespective of supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. The investigation focused on age-dependent differences in scaffold properties and their influence on BM-MSC osteogenic differentiation, rather than dose-response comparisons of a therapeutic agent.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: BM-MSCs cultured in Decellularized Bone Conditioned Media (DBCM)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: LDH assays confirmed BM-MSCs viability in DBCM from both young and old donors.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytosolic enzyme released upon cell membrane damage, serving as a marker for cellular cytotoxicity and viability.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of the effect of decellularized bone conditioned media on MSC viability and potential cytotoxicity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms biocompatibility of DBCM from both age groups, supporting its use for cell-based therapies by demonstrating maintained cellular viability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether pre-exercise ascorbic acid supplementation influenced antioxidant defenses, glucose metabolism, inflammation, and muscle damage in untrained healthy adults following a single bout of moderate-intensity cycling. Findings indicated that ascorbic acid supplementation reduced plasma Malondialdehyde (MDA) and increased Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP), while also modulating glucose levels and attenuating exercise-induced changes in albumin and total protein. While moderate-intensity cycling led to an increase in red blood cell Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) activity and low-grade muscle damage (Total Creatine Kinase), it did not induce systemic inflammation or lipid peroxidation. Ascorbic acid supplementation appeared to mitigate the exercise-induced increase in SOD activity but did not significantly prevent muscle damage or affect other inflammatory/damage markers such as hsCRP, LDH, CK-MB, GPx, or Catalase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supplementation combined with a single bout of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise
