treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects received 1000 mg of ascorbic acid (or placebo) orally 5 minutes prior to a 30-minute indoor cycling session. Exercise intensity was set at 65–75% of maximum heart rate, which was predicted by an age-based equation. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either ascorbic acid or exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activity remained unchanged in subjects with or without vitamin C supplement post-exercise (p>0.05, implied).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in anaerobic glycolysis; elevated levels in blood are often indicative of cellular damage or injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute aerobic exercise (indoor cycling) in untrained healthy adults, with or without ascorbic acid supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change suggests that this specific exercise bout, with or without ascorbic acid, did not induce significant acute muscle damage detectable by LDH.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (no significant group-by-time interaction, though ITG showed a non-significant tendency to decrease)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant group-by-time interaction was observed for circulating muscle biomarkers (p > 0.05). In ITG, differences between T1 and T2 were not significant, showing a non-significant tendency to decrease. High negative correlations observed with sFe (r = −0.944; p < 0.001), Hb (r = −0.986; p < 0.001), and FER (r = −0.643; p = 0.003).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme indicative of muscle damage, cellular breakdown, and muscle stress due to intense exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España) with 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level and muscle stress. Elevated levels suggest muscle integrity and function are compromised under prolonged, highly intensive exercise. Iron supplementation did not significantly influence this marker compared to the control group in the overall interaction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and delayed effects of the 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT) on biomarkers of muscle damage (creatinine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase), inflammation (C-reactive protein), and subjective perceptions of fatigue, recovery, and muscle soreness (DOMS, RPE, PRS) in healthy male amateur team sports players. Findings indicate that the 5mSRT significantly increased muscle damage and inflammation markers, as well as DOMS and RPE, while reducing PRS. The study concluded that a 72-hour recovery period was generally sufficient for fatigue recovery, with biomarker levels returning towards baseline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 5mSRT consisted of 6 repetitions of 30-second maximal shuttle sprints, with 35-second recovery periods between each sprint. Participants ran the greatest possible distance within 30 seconds by shuttling between cones at increasing distances (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m, etc.). Blood samples and perceptual scores were taken at rest, 5 minutes post-exercise, and 72 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons for varying test intensities or durations were reported within the protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased acutely post-exercise, then returned towards baseline.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased from pre-5mSRT (163.6  1 35.1 IU/L) to post-5mSRT (209.9  1 50.8 IU/L), a 21% increase (p < 0.001). Levels decreased to 143.9  1 36.6 IU/L at 72 h post-5mSRT, returning towards baseline (p < 0.001 compared to post-5mSRT).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in anaerobic glycolysis and energy metabolism, serving as a marker of cellular damage and intense metabolism. Elevated levels are related to disturbances in internal free calcium ions, intramuscular contractile functions, and local tissue damage with sarcomeric degeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute effect of 5-m Shuttle Run Test (5mSRT)-induced muscle damage and fatigue, with assessment at 5 minutes and 72 hours post-exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates exercise-induced muscle damage and fatigue, aiding coaches and physicians in identifying appropriate training levels and metabolic adaptations. Return to baseline within 72 hours suggests recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage in trained individuals.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between SCT (217.1            34.1 IU/L) and CON (218.5            44.7 IU/L). However, levels in both groups were elevated beyond the upper reference range (82–195 IU/L).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy production, with elevated levels indicating tissue damage or metabolic adaptation of skeletal muscle.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NCAA Division I American football players during athletic training and competition throughout the season.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels in both groups suggest general tissue damage and a high degree of metabolic adaptation associated with intensive athletic training, with no specific difference attributed to sickle cell trait status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, randomized controlled trial investigated the efficacy of post-exercise dairy-based protein supplementation versus an iso-caloric carbohydrate placebo in attenuating muscle soreness and other muscle damage markers in 323 recreational athletes following a 15-km road race. The study concluded that protein supplementation was not superior to carbohydrate supplementation for reducing muscle soreness or damage markers, and, notably, per-protocol analysis indicated higher perceived and objective lower extremity muscle soreness in the protein group 24 hours post-race, with no significant differences observed in blood markers like Creatine Kinase and Lactate Dehydrogenase between groups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation (Protein vs. Carbohydrate)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either milk protein (20% whey, 80% casein) or an iso-caloric maltodextrin carbohydrate placebo for three consecutive days post-race. The protein protocol involved 20 g immediately post-exercise and with breakfast, and 40 g prior to sleep. Compliant participants in the protein group consumed an average of 1.94-1.97 g/kg/d protein on race day and 1-2 days post-race, compared to 1.09-1.12 g/kg/d in the placebo group. The study focused on comparing protein versus carbohydrate effects, with no dose-response comparisons reported within the protein group itself.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged / Similar levels observed between protein and placebo groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were found in concentrations of LDH post-race between groups (p = 0.60). Protein group: 181 (144–200) U/L; Placebo group: 170 (147–196) U/L (ITT analysis).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism; elevated levels in blood typically indicate cell damage or tissue injury, including muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following a 15-km road race, with post-race protein or carbohydrate supplementation, measured 1-2 days post-race.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General marker for cellular damage; no difference suggests similar overall cellular integrity between groups.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the regulation of 23 blood-based biomarkers (including CK, IL-6, IL-17A, S100A8, BDNF, CD163, IL-1ß, and LDH) in 35 male elite athletes (badminton and soccer players) across different recovery-stress states. The primary aim was to identify markers responsive to habitual loading microcycles compared to recovered states. Key findings indicated that Creatine Kinase (CK), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) were generally higher in non-recovered states. S100A8 levels were significantly lower in non-recovered badminton players, while Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) levels were lower in non-recovered soccer players. Statistical trends were also observed for CD163 and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1ß). The study concludes that these discipline-specific biomarker responses are potentially useful for monitoring exercise and recovery to prevent overtraining and injury, though further validation is needed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise Training / Habitual Loading Microcycles
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study compared blood biomarker levels in elite male athletes (badminton and soccer players) during two states: 'recovered' (REC, after at least one day of rest from exercise) and 'non-recovered' (NOR, after a habitual loading microcycle). The habitual loading involved intensive, sport-specific training. For badminton players, this included four consecutive days with up to two sessions per day (50-310 min of moderate to intensive exercise daily). For soccer players, it involved high-intensity sessions with strenuous small-sided games, with at least two sessions within 48 hours. Blood samples for the NOR state were taken 12-16 hours after the last training session. The specific training content within microcycles varied and was not precisely controlled, reflecting real-world conditions. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training loads were reported within the context of the main findings, although external references to other exercise bouts (e.g., marathon, duathlon, interval training) were used to characterize biomarker behavior generally.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant increase was observed in the context of delayed recovery assessment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme that typically rises quickly after acute bouts of exercise and falls quickly thereafter.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute bouts of exercise, likely measured after a delay from the last training session.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not considered a suitable marker for delayed recovery assessment due to its rapid kinetics.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated sex differences in inflammatory response, lipid peroxidation, and muscle damage in men and women athletes following an acute resistance exercise, specifically a maximal incremental half-squat test. Results showed men exhibited a larger pro-inflammatory response (IL6) and increased lipid peroxidation (HPX) at 24 hours post-exercise compared to women at equivalent workloads, while no significant sex-based differences were observed in other muscle damage markers (CK-MB, LDH, 
	-actin).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Resistance Exercise (Maximal Incremental Half-Squat)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed half-squat exercises with five incremental intensities (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of one-repetition maximum, 1RM). Repetitions varied: 5 at 20-60% 1RM, 2 at 80% 1RM, and 1 at 100% 1RM. Rest periods between sets were 3-5 minutes. Equivalent workloads were used for men and women, but men achieved larger net loads due to greater muscle mass. No specific dose-response comparisons for biomarkers were reported across different intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between different time points nor between both sexes were found.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism, used as a marker of muscle damage and cellular stress when elevated in circulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute resistance exercise (half-squat).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant difference in muscle damage between sexes or at different time points after acute resistance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the control group, LDH significantly increased (p < 0.05) at 21 and 42 days post-baseline (e.g., T1: 312.13  1 10.81 UI/L to T3: 366.50  1 10.71 UI/L). In the intervention group, LDH showed a slight downward trend from baseline (328.59  1 5.49 UI/L) to T3 (314.14  1 4.70 UI/L), which was significantly lower (p < 0.05) compared to the control group at the end of follow-up.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in glycolysis and energy metabolism, released into circulation upon cellular/muscle tissue breakdown.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-intensity CrossFit® training program and 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD); TT supplementation may mitigate or improve recovery from muscle damage and negatively influences athletic performance/health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This descriptive, cross-sectional study investigated serum biochemical markers of muscle damage, including C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH), total Creatine Kinase (CK), Creatine Kinase-MB (CK-MB), and the CK-MB/CK ratio, in 326 adolescent athletes (aged 13-18 years, primarily soccer players) from sports centers in Tacna, Peru. The study aimed to evaluate muscle damage and inflammation related to intense physical activity, concluding that alterations in these markers are present, with specific ranges identified for elevated markers and notable correlations (e.g., a strong positive correlation between LDH and CK-MB) among the adolescent cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of physical training and activity, specifically soccer training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional study of adolescent athletes (aged 13-18 years, including soccer players) engaging in regular, intense physical activity and competitive training for at least three months. No specific training interventions or dose-response comparisons were applied or controlled by the researchers; the study analyzed pre-existing biomarker levels influenced by the athletes' own training regimes, which involve macro and microcycles and varying intensity/duration. The study notes 'different stages of training' and 'adjustment of physical load' as influencing factors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 2.5% of adolescents had low values (<200 U/L, median 209 U/L), 91.4% had normal values (200-400 U/L, with a normal range of 120-330 U/L for 10-19 years), and 6.1% had high values (>400 U/L, median 435 U/L, max 545 U/L). Elevated levels specifically varied between 390 and 450 U/L. Moderate correlation with CK (r = 0.260), moderate positive correlation with CRP (r = 0.483), and strong positive correlation with CK-MB (r = 0.780) were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme with five isoenzymes involved in anaerobic glycolysis, acting on pyruvate and lactate. It serves as an indicator of cellular damage, tissue breakdown, and muscle fiber destruction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Muscle damage assessment in adolescent athletes (including soccer players) due to intense physical activity and sports training, and associated inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate significant muscle damage, cellular damage, and necrosis, potentially predicting injuries that limit physical performance. It is useful for monitoring muscle health and shows a strong association with CK-MB levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise, with 20-45% increases after the first match and ~20% increases after the second match. Levels remained elevated by ~20% at the end of the protocol, showing incomplete normalization during short recovery sessions; increased to concentrations above post-match 1 after the second match.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in anaerobic metabolism; elevated levels can indicate myocyte damage and cellular distress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, recovery), cumulative strain from consecutive matches.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle microinjury and damage, and incomplete recovery from exercise loads; associated with low exercise tolerance, pre-clinical injury, and overtraining syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy production, commonly used as a marker for tissue and cell damage when found in blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CD administration in mice following resistance exercise, facilitating recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced levels indicate decreased muscle damage and improved recovery following resistance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the effect of oral palmitoylethanolamide (PEA, Levagen+™) on recovery from muscle-damaging leg press exercise in 28 healthy young males. The study found that while PEA supplementation did not significantly reduce perceived muscle soreness, thigh circumference, or most inflammatory and phosphoprotein markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, IL-6, IL-10, hs-CRP, TNF-α, CREB, ERK1/2, JNK, NF-κB, p38 MAPK, S6K1, STAT3, STAT5), it did significantly reduce blood myoglobin and lactate concentrations. Furthermore, PEA increased Protein Kinase B phosphorylation immediately post-exercise, suggesting aid in muscle recovery through improved metabolic efficiency and activation of anabolic/repair signaling pathways from repeat bouts of exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Supplementation with Palmitoylethanolamide (Levagen+™) combined with Resistance Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were randomized to consume either liquid PEA (167.5 mg Levagen+™ containing 150 mg PEA and 17.5 mg excipients, with 832.5 mg maltodextrin) or a matched placebo (1 g maltodextrin). Treatments were administered pre-exercise, immediately post-exercise, 24 h post-exercise, and 48 h post-exercise. The muscle-damaging exercise consisted of four sets of leg press at 80% of one-repetition maximum (1-RM) to volitional exhaustion, with 60s rest between sets, followed by a performance set at 70% 1-RM to maximal repetitions. No dose-response comparisons for PEA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Unchanged over time and no significant effect of PEA supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy production; widely distributed and released from damaged cells, serving as a general marker of cell damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Leg press exercise to volitional exhaustion, with/without PEA supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An indicator of general cell damage. Lack of change suggests minor systemic damage or insufficient sensitivity for this specific exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between routine plasma biomarker levels and recovery efficiency in elite professional soccer players over an entire eleven-month competitive match season, including seasonal variations and differences based on player position and cumulative match time. It concluded that a panel of AST, CK, LDH, and creatinine can effectively monitor recovery, adaptation, and overtraining risk, particularly in active positions like midfielders who may also be prone to iron and magnesium deficiencies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competitive professional soccer matches and regular intense training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An eleven-month competitive season, comprising 44 league and cup matches (23 autumn, 21 spring), typically one to two matches per week. Fasting capillary blood samples were collected 17-24 hours after each match. The study compared player positions (midfielder/defender vs. goalie/substitute, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups), noting significant differences in cumulative match time and physical demands. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for training intensity, but adaptation to increasing training load was observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in midfielder/defender, decreased over time, but generally increases after exercise
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activity was surprisingly highest in the goalie/substitute group compared to midfielder/defender groups. It generally showed a decreasing trend over time in various groups and phases (e.g., midfielder/defender group decreased significantly over time, R=-0.29, P<=0.05 in spring; goalie/substitute group decreased, R=-0.22 to -0.31, P<=0.05 over season). However, it is generally known to increase after exercise and endurance efforts, but for defenders, it showed a decrease in spring (R=-0.29, P<=0.05) but an increase over the total season (R=-0.23, P<=0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy metabolism (glycolysis) that catalyzes the conversion between pyruvate and lactate. It serves as an indicator of anaerobic metabolism, cellular damage, tissue necrosis, and metabolic stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout an eleven-month professional competitive soccer match season, including post-match recovery (17-24 hours post-match), regular intense training, and after exercise/endurance efforts. Comparisons were made between midfielder/defender and goalie/substitute groups, and individual midfielder/defender subgroups, considering cumulative game time and seasonal variations (autumn vs. spring rounds).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful muscle damage marker for monitoring recovery periods and efficiency, indicating cellular necrosis, tissue damage, and metabolic stress. Lower levels in active players might suggest better adaptation or less damage, while higher levels in less active players could imply poorer adaptation. Its activity might also depend on diet, potentially making it less effective as a recovery marker. Its lower interindividual variability is beneficial for assessing recovery, adaptation, and reducing overtraining risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise, then decreased 3 hours after, but remained increased 24 hours after compared to pre-exercise levels (F3 = 208.72; p < 0.001). Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC = 0.73) and was reported to have good reliability (ICC between 0.75 and 0.9) in some assessments.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in anaerobic glycolysis; often used as an indicator of tissue damage or cell lysis; indicator of cellular damage and metabolic activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 60-min continuous endurance exercise bouts; endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; used in exercise context for analyzing metabolic demands; monitoring of exercise response and recovery processes in endurance sports.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suitable as a physiological exercise response and recovery marker for monitoring athletes' load management, with good reliability. Can expand the panel of blood biomarkers to monitor load-recovery status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of D-ribose supplementation on delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) induced by plyometric exercise in untrained male college students. Findings indicate that oral administration of 15g D-ribose reduced muscle soreness, improved knee extensor function by mitigating strength reduction, lowered muscle damage markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, Myoglobin), and inhibited lipid peroxidation (Malondialdehyde), thereby accelerating DOMS recovery. However, D-ribose showed no significant effect on overall isokinetic muscle strength (flexor peak torque and total work) and modulated the time-course of antioxidant enzymes (Superoxide Dismutase) and total antioxidant capacity (TAC) without consistently showing a superior antioxidant effect compared to placebo after 48 hours.

treatment_details.therapy_type: D-ribose supplementation combined with plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: D-ribose was orally administered at 15g per dose, 1-hour before, and 1-hour, 12-hours, 24-hours, and 36-hours after exercise. A calorically equivalent placebo containing sorbitol and β-cyclodextrin was given at the same dose and times. The plyometric exercise protocol consisted of 7 sets of 20 consecutive frog hops with 90-second rest intervals between sets, performed twice with a 14-day washout period. No dose-response comparisons for D-ribose were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in PLAC after 24-h (p < 0.01) and 48-h (p < 0.01), but not in DRIB (p > 0.05). LDH was significantly lower in the DRIB group compared to the PLAC group after 24-h (p < 0.01) and 48-h (p < 0.01), with PLAC levels not returning to baseline within 48-h.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism and anaerobic glycolysis; its leakage into blood indicates muscle cell damage and disruption.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-plyometric exercise muscle damage and D-ribose supplementation effect on recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in DRIB indicate reduced muscle cell damage and accelerated restoration of membrane integrity, signifying faster muscle recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme found in almost all body tissues; elevated levels indicate tissue damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cell damage or breakdown, including lung injury in COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Fluctuated; changes with training and recovery
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fluctuated, with activity varying by competitive distance and sex. Positive correlation with CK activity observed only in the male sprint group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in anaerobic metabolism, cellular energy production, and indicates tissue damage; also involved in monitoring recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring athletes' recovery periods, particularly during a 10-week preparatory training stage in professional long-distance and sprint swimmers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Useful for monitoring recovery, with lower inter-individual variability. Evaluated for usefulness in assessing recovery effectiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-week oral garlic supplementation on 40-km cycling time trial performance, whole-body energy metabolism, exercise-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in healthy adult males. Findings indicate that garlic supplementation significantly enhanced total antioxidant capacity and attenuated oxidative stress (MDA), inflammatory response (TNF-α), and some markers of muscle damage (LDH and UA at specific time points), but it did not improve cycling performance or overall whole-body energy metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral garlic extract supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 1000 mg/day for 4 weeks (28 consecutive days) in a single-blind crossover design. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as a single dose was used.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly attenuated/decreased (p < 0.05) before exercise (0-km), at 20-km, and 40-km during the cycling challenge, significantly delaying its exercise-induced increase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in energy metabolism and anaerobic glycolysis, released into blood with cell/muscle damage, serving as a marker of muscle injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 4-wk garlic supplementation during a 40-km cycling challenge

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No meaningful differences between soy protein supplementation and an exercise-only group during a 60 min stress test.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant impact on muscular stress indicators under a 60-min stress test duration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase I/II clinical trial investigated the safety and efficacy of intravenously administered acellular human amniotic fluid (hAF) in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients with respiratory symptoms. The primary aim was to assess the impact of hAF on markers of systemic inflammation and coagulation. The study concluded that hAF administration did not result in statistically significant differences in safety or most inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, LDH) compared to placebo, although under specific analysis conditions (including last recorded values for early discharge patients), D-dimer and IL-6 showed statistically significant increases in the hAF group. Overall, hAF did not demonstrate a significant benefit in reducing inflammation or improving clinical outcomes, despite showing safety for intravenous administration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intravenous administration of sterile filtered, acellular human amniotic fluid (hAF)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 10 cc of sterile processed acellular hAF was administered intravenously once daily for up to 5 consecutive days (median 5 doses, IQR 3, 5). The hAF was sourced from a single donor per dose and underwent processing via filtration, purification, and sterilization to meet sterility guidelines. No significant dose-response comparisons were reported, and the efficacy was primarily compared against a saline placebo group. The study authors hypothesized that the tested dose might have been insufficient or administered too late in the disease course.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not statistically different from baseline to Day 6 between hAF and placebo groups. No significant differences were observed even when including last recorded values for early discharge patients or when restricted to non-ICU patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in anaerobic glycolysis; elevated levels are indicative of tissue damage or cellular injury, and can be a marker of systemic inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Changes from baseline to Day 6 following daily intravenous hAF or placebo administration in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation and cellular injury during COVID-19 infection; no significant difference observed with hAF, suggesting it did not mitigate tissue damage more effectively than placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant increase (48.89% in Medical Ward vs. 76.47% in ICU, p = 0.013).

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects disease severity in COVID-19 patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced levels demonstrated in individuals with MCI and AD compared to healthy controls, with high diagnostic accuracy for MCI and AD (>87% sensitivity, 91% specificity to distinguish AD/prodromal AD from FTD). However, some studies reported negative findings (no differences). Exercise increases both its concentration and secretion rate. Pooled AUC analysis showed significant predictive value for salivary-based AD diagnosis.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker indicative of the innate immune response, linked with central nervous system (CNS) pathways. Iron-binding glycoprotein with antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) diagnosis, distinguishing AD from other dementias; influenced by exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic biomarker for AD and MCI, with high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity; correlated with brain amyloid. It is the first established salivary biomarker for AD with regulatory approval for commercialization in Colombia. Its levels are sensitive to physical activity, requiring pre-analytical control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ significantly between the three supplementation trials.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic modifier investigation; Observational longitudinal study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is observational and investigates an intrinsic genetic factor, not an active therapeutic intervention. The 'dose' refers to the additive effects of the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage (0, 1, or 2 G alleles), which was modeled as a continuous variable. The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). No deviations from an additive effect were observed (heterozygosity indicator P > 0.05), and no traditional dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In C9orf72 presymptomatic carriers longitudinally: better language abilities (β for slope per G allele: 0.11, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.19, corrected P: 0.024).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Ability to comprehend, produce, and use language effectively.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage in presymptomatic C9orf72 carriers longitudinally.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Better scores indicate preserved language abilities, which are significant for communication and often affected in FTD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of consuming cow's milk versus an energy-matched carbohydrate solution on recovery markers and performance in twenty female team-sport athletes following repeated simulated team games (STGs). The findings indicated that 500 mL of milk consumption attenuated losses in muscle function (peak torque for knee extension and flexion), sprint performance (5m and 10m), and perceptions of stress, and helped reduce muscle soreness and tiredness, particularly after the first STG. However, for many other physiological and performance markers (e.g., CK, hsCRP, LOOHs, PCs, CMJ, HR, RPE), the effects were mostly unclear or trivial, with milk showing no clear benefit after the second STG.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional intervention (consumption of cow's milk vs. an energy-matched carbohydrate solution) combined with a multi-stage physical activity protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants consumed 500 mL of either cow's milk (910 kJ/215 kcal, 17.0 g protein, 25.5 g carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat) or an energy-matched carbohydrate solution (910 kJ/215 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 53.6 g carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat) immediately following each of two simulated team games (STG1 and STG2). The 17 g protein from milk was noted to be below the recommended 20 g threshold for maximal protein synthesis stimulation. The exercise protocol involved two ~30 minute halves of intermittent running with sprints, agility, and jumps, separated by a 10-minute half-time, with a 48-hour recovery period between STG1 and STG2. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the nutritional interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Trivial effects were seen for lap time within-group (STG1 to STG2) for both MILK and CHO. Between-group comparisons (MILK vs. CHO) were unclear.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: sMSC led to a significantly shorter latency to find the correct arm than the oMSC group (test block 4).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Time taken to complete a cognitive task, indicating efficiency and memory.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Forced choice alternation T-maze assay after INA of sMSC in 3xTg-AD mouse models.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shorter latency indicates improved cognitive performance and spatial working memory in AD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive fine-mapping analysis of 150 breast cancer risk regions using dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls of European ancestry). It identified 352 independent risk signals, containing 13,367 credible causal variants (CCVs), with 191-205 high-confidence signals and 191 likely target genes. The investigation revealed that CCVs were significantly over-represented in active gene regulatory regions, open chromatin, actively transcribed genes, and transcription factor binding sites. The study also found signals differentially associated with ER-positive and ER-negative breast cancer, and prioritized target genes through integrated computational approaches like PAINTOR and INQUISIT, collectively explaining up to 23.6% of the familial relative risk. Furthermore, it included eQTL analyses in normal and tumor breast tissue to link genetic variants with gene expression changes, and explored the enrichment of CCVs with various genomic features and their impact on specific biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic fine-mapping, risk profiling, and functional genomics analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is a genetic association and fine-mapping analysis, not an interventional therapy. It utilized dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls) of European ancestry, analyzing over 639,000 genetic variants (SNPs, deletion/insertions, CNVs with MAF ">= 0.1% or 0.005%") across 150-152 previously defined risk regions. Methodologies included stepwise multinomial logistic regression, Bayesian approaches (PAINTOR), and a gene prioritization pipeline (INQUSIT). Statistical thresholds like conditional p-values (< 10^-6 for strong evidence, < 10^-4 for moderate) and False Discovery Rate (FDR 5%) were applied. eQTL analyses involved linear regression with specific covariates, and functional characterization included enrichment analysis with histone marks and TFBS motifs (FIMO p-value threshold 10^-3). No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Case-only analysis for ER-negative status and meta-analysis combining BCAC ER-negative association results with BRCA1 mutation carriers from CIMBA.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates genetic markers predictive of increased risk for ER-negative breast cancer subtype.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Released into bodily fluids from dental alloy restorations.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Heavy metals, potential environmental toxins.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Presence of dental alloy restorations, recent dental work.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Act as confounding factors if salivary levels of these metals are being examined, requiring avoidance of sampling close to dental work.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week concurrent endurance and strength training intervention on microRNA expression and Line-1 methylation in capillary blood of sedentary, healthy adults. It aimed to develop a miRNA-based 'fitness score' to assess individual responses to diet, metabolism, and exercise, identifying significantly altered miRNAs and anthropometric data, and their correlations with genetic polymorphisms (ACE, ACTN3, FTO), dietary intake, fluid intake, and stress levels, ultimately providing information for assessing individual health, performance, and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Concurrent strength and endurance training (sports intervention)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A supervised 12-week sports intervention was conducted in 61 sedentary, healthy adults (aged 19-55 years, BMI 20-35 kg/m2). The training involved both endurance and strength exercises, with observations extending to 10 months post-intervention. No specific intensity levels, frequencies, or detailed exercise modalities were provided, and no dose-response comparisons were reported. A healthy, age- and sex-matched control group (n=20) received no intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased (p=0.000) as a result of the intervention. Participants with a TC genotype (ACTN3 gene) showed a higher gain in LBM compared to participants with a TT genotype (p=0.039).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of body composition, representing muscle and non-fat tissue mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Result of the sports intervention, influenced by ACTN3 gene polymorphism.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Direct indicator of muscle mass and physical fitness, key for athletic performance and metabolic health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Loss uniquely exhibited among males during the 21-week competition preparation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Comprises muscle, bone, and organs; contributes to strength, power, and metabolic rate.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a 21-week competition preparation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Significant for athletic performance; indicates potential catabolism if lost during weight reduction, especially if unique to one sex.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in both the protein and placebo groups; the protein group had a larger relative increase (0.93  1 1.22%) compared to the placebo group (0.44  1 1.40%, P Interaction = 0.046).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Non-fat body mass, primarily reflecting muscle, bone, and organs, crucial for strength and metabolic health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation (31g/day, achieving 1.29  1 0.28 g/kg/day total protein) combined with walking exercise in physically active older adults.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an attenuation of age-related loss of muscle mass, potentially saving 1-2 years of muscle mass decline, and contributes to improved daily life mobility and overall health benefits.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week (3-month) food-based vitamin D3 fortification intervention on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, bone turnover markers (Osteocalcin, Bone specific Alkaline Phosphatase, Procollagen type 1 amino-terminal propeptide, C-terminal crosslinked telopeptide of type 1 collagen), and muscle strength (handgrip, knee extension, chair-standing) in 143 women of Danish and Pakistani origin, aged 18-50 years, living in Denmark and at risk of vitamin D deficiency. Despite a significant increase in serum 25(OH)D concentrations in the fortified groups, the intervention did not result in significant changes in bone turnover markers or muscle strength. Baseline characteristics including anthropometrics and vitamin D status were also assessed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Food-based vitamin D fortification
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 12-week (3-month) randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled winter intervention trial. The intervention group (143 women) received 30 μg vitamin D3/day (analyzed as 29 μg/day total vitamin D content) through fortified daily foods (150g yoghurt, 60g cheese, 1 egg, 1 small crisp-bread); the placebo group received similar non-fortified products. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and the study noted potential insufficient power to detect changes in secondary endpoints.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in women of Pakistani origin
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower in women of Pakistani origin compared to Danish origin (P < 0.001)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of muscle and non-fat tissue mass, related to strength, metabolism, and overall health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline comparison between women of Danish and Pakistani origin.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates ethnic disparities in lean body mass, potentially affecting strength and metabolic health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: SP was found to provide identical or similar increases in lean mass compared to whey protein in some studies, especially at optimal protein intakes ("> 1.6 g/kg BW/day). Some studies on untrained individuals reported no difference or minimal positive effects compared to placebo, while others indicated milk/whey might be preferable for faster rates.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of muscle adaptation and overall body composition related to physical performance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein supplementation, often in response to resistance exercise, in active individuals, athletes, and untrained participants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved muscle adaptations and body composition for athletes and active individuals, with efficacy comparable to whey at sufficient intake levels.
