document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression is typically very low but promptly induced and upregulated in chronic inflammatory conditions and cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlates with the ability to produce accurate tone.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Critical area for motor speech programming.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Production of accurate tones in speech, particularly in individuals with non-fluent/agrammatic variant PPA.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with intact motor speech programming and the ability to produce accurate tones, relevant for PPA diagnosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in the verum group after intervention (p = 0.018, ES = 0.314, Q1; Q3: -0.75; 3.75) but remained within the normal range. In females, LA diameter increases age-adjusted significantly with HOMA quartiles (p=0.001). Reduced in the placebo group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of left atrial size and pressure, often reflecting left ventricular diastolic function; structural parameter of the heart.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 6 weeks of dietary intervention in the verum group.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: While increased, it remained within the normal range, implying no adverse effect on cardiac health, but indicates changes in cardiac dynamics. Increased LA diameter is a sign of diastolic dysfunction, indicating potential structural changes despite the intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery (VO2Rec) measures, especially VO2T12.5% (time to recover 12.5% of peak VO2), in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. The study suggests its regular inclusion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing protocols.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Pharmacological treatment (Aficamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Aficamten was administered for 24 weeks in a phase 3 randomized controlled trial, compared against placebo. Doses were individualized to achieve the lowest effective dose, targeting a Valsalva Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Gradient (LVOT-G) <30 mm Hg while maintaining a left ventricular ejection fraction ">=\u00ad50%. Specific daily dosages (mg) and dose-response comparisons were not detailed, but treatment led to proportional improvements in cardiac function and biomarkers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates structural changes in the heart, often associated with increased cardiac filling pressures and dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Echocardiographic structural abnormality as a diagnostic criterion for HFpEF-HDI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Diagnostic criterion for HFpEF-HDI.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant LVEF improvement occurred within 6 months in the majority of patients (over 50% showed improvement by at least one LVEF category); nearly one quarter experienced normalization to >50%. Greater LV improvements, often >=10%, were observed over time. LVEF also showed additional increases over 12 months in HFmrEF and HFrEF groups. However, LVEF worsened (P=0.002) in patients with normalized LVEF who were rehospitalized between 6 and 18 months.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the pumping efficiency of the left ventricle, indicating systolic cardiac function and ventricular remodeling (both reverse remodeling and its attenuation/reversal).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal follow-up of heart failure patients after hospital discharge for acute cardiac decompensation (ACD) with predischarge LVEF <=40%, undergoing ongoing optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), assessed over 6, 12, and 18 months.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful surrogate marker of cardiac remodeling and its reversal. Greater LVEF improvement at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) correlates with lower mortality risk and fewer all-cause or heart failure-related hospitalizations at 18 months. Its trajectory indicates myocardial capacity for repair. Worsening LVEF is a surrogate for attenuation/reversal of reverse remodeling and is associated with clinical worsening, particularly rehospitalization. document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective single-center study investigated the relationship between an impaired Growth Hormone (GH)-Insulin-like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) axis and cardiac wasting (reduced left ventricular mass) in 307 advanced cancer patients. The findings reveal that reduced LV mass is associated with an imbalance in the GH-IGF-I axis, characterized by higher plasma GH levels and a lower IGF-I/GH ratio, suggesting acquired GH resistance. This resistance is particularly evident in patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss, and higher baseline IGF-I was associated with a subsequent decline in relative LV mass.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility and limitations of Body Mass Index (BMI) compared to Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)-derived percent body fat and fasting leptin and insulin levels for diagnosing and classifying obesity in adults. It concluded that BMI significantly underestimates obesity prevalence, especially in women and with advancing age, due to its inability to distinguish lean from fat mass. The study proposed new, lower gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) and found that leptin levels, unlike insulin, enhance the accuracy of BMI estimates for adiposity, particularly in women and when DXA is unavailable. The integration of leptin and DXA is suggested for more precise obesity characterization and management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Comparison and Biomarker Analysis for Obesity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional study conducted a retrospective review of BMI calculations, DXA scans, and fasting blood levels of leptin and insulin from 9,088 adults between 1998 and 2009. Measurements for BMI, DXA (providing simultaneous muscle, bone mass, and adiposity data), and blood work (fasting leptin and insulin drawn between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm) were taken within 3 weeks of each other. The study evaluated and compared the accuracy and classification rates of these metrics for obesity, proposing new gender-specific BMI cut-points (24 for females, 28 for males) based on body fat and leptin corrections. No therapeutic intervention dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher levels observed with increased body fat; lowering of elevated levels has significant impacts.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A strong relationship exists between increased leptin and increased percent body fat. High leptin levels (>30 ng/mL) are particularly prevalent in women (91% of patients with high levels were women), where BMI tends to underestimate obesity. For individuals with BMI >25, leptin levels did not add new information to BMI adjustment. Lowering elevated leptin levels is associated with improved obesity and clinical outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A 16 kDa peptide primarily secreted by adipocytes, leptin regulates the body's energy balance, satiety, and long-term weight control by acting as a negative feedback adiposity signal. Levels rise in individuals with leptin insensitive receptors.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Obesity diagnosis and management, particularly for correcting BMI disparities with direct fat measurements, improving adiposity assessment especially in women, and in the context of hyperleptinemia or leptin insensitivity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Leptin is a useful tool in obesity management, improving the precision of BMI adjustment for diagnosis, especially in women. Elevated levels are associated with the inflammatory process, increased morbidity of obesity, and comorbidities such as chronic inflammation, type II diabetes, hypertension, and myocardial injury, particularly in individuals with leptin insensitivity. Its levels can predict improved obesity and clinical outcomes, long-term weight control, and permanent weight loss. It is also associated with increased medical comorbidities related to hyperleptinemia and sarcopenia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significant effect of exercise (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant effects of exercise (PBO trial) were shown (P < 0.01). No other immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding on this modulator. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of leptin to exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Hormone regulating energy balance, appetite, and bone metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Indicates the metabolic and hormonal response to exercise, potentially influencing energy expenditure and bone health. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in both early and advanced NASH than in healthy controls (P <0.01 and P <0.05, respectively). Elevated with no statistical difference by grade of steatosis and inflammation. Statistically higher levels compared with healthy controls in grade 2 of ballooning and the F1 group. Statistical correlation between serum levels of leptin and grades of steatosis (r=0.505, P <0.001) and inflammation (r=0.483, P <0.002); serum levels were not higher in the F4 group. Significantly correlated with all grades of histological findings (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis; P =0.001, P =0.002, P =0.004 and P =0.038, respectively).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Adipokine involved in appetite regulation, energy balance, metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis. Related to obesity; reduces development of fibrosis in liver injury models; activates multiple intracellular signaling pathways in HSCs; maintains quiescent state of HSCs by inhibitory activity of PPAR-γ.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early NASH, advanced NASH, grade 2 of ballooning, F1 fibrosis group, various grades of steatosis and inflammation in NASH.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate NASH presence and are significantly correlated with all grades of histological findings, suggesting it is a robust marker for NASH progression and related to steatosis and inflammation. Its complex role includes potentially maintaining HSC quiescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels can vary depending on whether the subject had just had a meal or was fasted overnight. Specific quantitative data not provided in this context.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates energy balance, appetite, and metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Feeding status (fed or fasted).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates variability requiring consistent feeding conditions for reliable measurement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. The aim was to evaluate systemic and muscle-related stress responses and recovery patterns, comparing biomarkers at 1 day (R+1) and 15 days (R+15) post-landing with pre-flight values and age-matched controls. Findings revealed a strong spaceflight-induced stress response in muscle tissue, leading to a proinflammatory state, with inflamma-miRs and myo-miR-206 mediating systemic recovery, and significant inter-individual differences in biomarker responses were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 6-month International Space Station (ISS) spaceflight exposure with in-flight countermeasure training, followed by a post-flight recovery period.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two crewmembers were exposed to approximately 6 months of spaceflight. Samples were collected pre-flight (76-79 days before) and post-flight at 1 day (R+1 / 24 hours) and 15 days (R+15) after landing. Individual molecular responses varied significantly between the two crewmembers, with crewmember A generally showing more persistent changes. Specifics of in-flight countermeasure training dose were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons for spaceflight duration were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher and dysregulated, with striking differences between crewmembers. Significantly increased at R+1 in crewmember A, then recovered, but showed no change in crewmember B.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primarily produced by adipose cells, it regulates energy balance, appetite, metabolism, and is involved in inflammation and bone turnover. It is also part of the stress response and homeostasis regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-spaceflight recovery (R+1 and R+15) in crewmembers A and B, associated with a 6-month ISS mission.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests an acute metabolic or physiological stress response in crewmember A that recovered, while crewmember B remained stable, indicating individual differences in metabolic adaptation to spaceflight. It is involved in systemic changes during spaceflight recovery, inflammation, bone turnover, systemic stress/inflammation, and unbalancing of homeostasis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significantly higher in obese; unchanged by acute exercise
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Obese females had significantly higher levels than normal weight females at all time points (mean difference: 13,579 pg/ml, +2.6-fold, p = 0.02). Levels did not change significantly in response to acute plyometric exercise in either group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An adipokine that regulates appetite, energy balance, fat metabolism, and has immune-modulating effects, with links to bone metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Resting levels and response to a single bout of plyometric exercise in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated resting levels in obese females are consistent with greater fat mass, indicating increased adiposity and potential leptin resistance, which can be associated with insulin resistance and potential chronic systemic inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with increasing age (r=0.2654; p=0.0023) and significantly decreased after fisetin usage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy human participants (age range 20–82 years), association with chronological aging, and response to senolytic treatment (fisetin).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the clinical relevance and efficacy of collagen X breakdown product (CXM) as a blood-based biomarker for endochondral long bone fracture repair in both healthy individuals and patients with tibia or femur fractures. It characterized CXM expression patterns, stability across demographics (age, sex), correlation with other bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, osteocalcin, leptin, sclerostin), and its utility in predicting healing prognosis (early, normal, delayed). The findings showed CXM levels are low in healthy individuals, peak around 25-35 days post-fracture, can be reliably measured via dried blood spots, and offer an earlier, quantitative indication of healing compared to traditional radiographic methods, supporting its prospective use in fracture studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of natural long bone fracture repair, with a secondary analysis of a Vitamin D3 supplementation trial (VitaShock).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on observing biomarker changes in patients with acute closed or low-grade open tibial or femoral shaft fractures (Gustilo type I or II, AO/OTA type 42), without applying a specific therapeutic dose as an intervention. For the secondary analysis of the VitaShock trial, multiple Vitamin D3 dosing strategies were assessed, but specific dose details were not provided, and no significant difference in CXM response was found compared to placebo. Longitudinal blood samples were collected at various standard-of-care clinical visits over a period up to 48 weeks post-fracture.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: negatively correlates with CXM, positively associates with BMI
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: r = -0.31, p = 0.0138 (with CXM in normal healing patients). Significant negative correlation with CXM levels at 12 weeks after fracture (r = -0.34, p = 0.005). Leptin levels significantly correlated with body mass index (BMI) (r = 0.63, p < 0.0001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Obesity biomarker. Hormone involved in energy metabolism regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fracture healing (normal healers, 12 weeks post-fracture), in the context of patient demographics and obesity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an obesity biomarker, showing an inverse relationship with CXM levels during fracture healing. May be predictive of poor healing or inhibitory of endochondral bone repair, further supporting clinical evidence that obesity is a risk factor for delayed or nonunion in fracture healing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased significantly from pre to post in all groups due to LEA; increased significantly from post to recovery in all groups but remained significantly lower at recovery than pre in naturally menstruating females
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All groups (combined HC, progestin-only HC, naturally menstruating females) showed significant decreases from pre to post (p=0.011, p<0.001, and p<0.001, respectively) after ~23 weeks of LEA. All groups significantly increased from post to recovery (p=0.002, p=0.001, and p=0.001, respectively), with levels generally returning towards baseline. However, leptin concentrations remained significantly lower at recovery than pre in naturally menstruating females (p=0.021), especially those who continued to experience LEA. There was a significant main effect for time (F=24.032, p<0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Adipokine hormone produced by adipocytes, playing a key role in appetite regulation, energy balance, and metabolism by signaling fat stores to the brain. It is upregulated when fat mass or energy balance is positive and downregulated with low energy availability
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by diet and physical training in female physique athletes, with a comparative analysis across combined hormonal contraceptive users, progestin-only hormonal contraceptive users, and naturally menstruating females at pre, post, and recovery time points
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A comparable decrease in all groups indicates negative endocrine consequences of LEA, signaling chronic energy deficit irrespective of HC use. This downregulation, which can occur even with short-term LEA, negatively affects reproductive, metabolic, and bone health, and is associated with suppression of HPO and HPT axes and activation of the HPA axis. It is an important indicator of fat mass, energy status, and metabolic regulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 3-year longitudinal study characterized the central vein sign (CVS) profiles in newly developing white matter lesions in Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients. It found that most new lesions were CVS+ (68%) and established that younger age and a higher baseline CVS+ percentage are associated with an increased likelihood of new CVS+ lesion development, thereby identifying CVS as a predictive radiologic biomarker for MS disease activity and informing clinical decisions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing the Central Vein Sign (CVS) as a diagnostic imaging biomarker in the context of Multiple Sclerosis lesion development and progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study followed adults with MS and healthy controls for a median of 3.1 years (Q1–Q3: 0.7–6.3 years). MRI scans were conducted on 3T Siemens or Philips scanners using specific submillimeter T2*-weighted, 3D millimetric T1-weighted MPRAGE/MP2RAGE, and 3D millimetric T2-weighted FLAIR sequences. The study did not involve specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons, though retrospective observations of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) changes were noted.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Newly developing Multiple Sclerosis lesions (detected via MRI)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Newly developing CVS+ lesions were larger than CVS− lesions (mean volume 59 vs 33 mm3, p < 0.001). An increased size of newly developing lesions was associated with a slightly higher likelihood of being CVS+ (OR 1.07 per each 10 mm3 increase in lesion volume, 95% CI 1.0–1.1).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the physical extent of demyelination/inflammation in Multiple Sclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Newly developing MS lesions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Larger lesion volume in MS typically indicates greater disease burden and potentially more significant neurological impact. In this study, it is associated with CVS+ status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher/slower initial increase but maintained higher levels
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Postprandial peak plasma leucine concentrations were substantially greater with whey protein compared to soy. However, branched-chain amino acids showed a slower initial increase but maintained higher levels during post-exercise recovery with an SP-based blend compared to whey protein.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acids, key signaling molecules for muscle protein synthesis and energy production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute post-concurrent exercise supplementation with whey protein vs soy protein (with/without free leucine); post-exercise recovery comparing SP-based blend with whey protein.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher plasma leucine concentrations are associated with a stronger anabolic signal, while maintained BCAA levels indicate sustained availability of building blocks for muscle repair.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed predictive models using a novel machine learning pipeline to identify viable intrauterine pregnancies (Live Normally Sited Pregnancies, LNSP) in symptomatic women, differentiating them from combined adverse outcomes (CAO) such as miscarriage, pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). The models integrate serum metabolite levels (untargeted 1H NMR profiling) with plasma hormone concentrations (β-hCG and progesterone) and clinicodemographic data, finding that a composite biomarker provides superior predictive accuracy (0.79). The aim is to offer a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic test to reduce diagnostic burden and improve outcomes in early gestation by accurately identifying LNSP and excluding conditions associated with maternal morbidity and mortality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker identification and predictive model development using machine learning, untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, and hormone assays.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 370 symptomatic pregnant women (≤10 weeks gestation), presenting with abdominal pain and/or vaginal bleeding. A single blood sample was collected upon first emergency presentation; plasma was used for β-hCG and progesterone concentration measurements, and serum for untargeted metabolomic profiling. Nine key metabolite signals were identified. Random forest models were constructed and compared: a model using metabolite signals alone yielded 0.68 accuracy, β-hCG and progesterone alone yielded 0.71 accuracy, and the combined model achieved the best predictive accuracy of 0.79. Model performance was assessed using an independent validation cohort. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic accuracy for pregnancy outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels are shown to increase in early pregnancy relative to non-pregnant women. This study did not report a specific significant difference for Live Normally Sited Pregnancies (LNSP) versus combined adverse outcomes (CAO) in its primary findings.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, involved in protein metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General changes in amino acid levels during early pregnancy.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered a general indicator of amino acid changes in early pregnancy; maternal amino acid levels are generally viewed as promising biomarkers to differentiate normal pregnancy from adverse outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified as an influential factor in group differentiation (VIP score between 1.04 and 1.75), contributing to the overall reduction in amino acids in the PFF group. Its inclusion in classic models (age, BMI, waist circumference, or cholesterol) significantly increased AUC from 76.7-78% to 100% (approaching significance).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Branched-chain essential amino acid (BCAA), critical for muscle protein synthesis, regulation of metabolism, and overall metabolic pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention, differentiating metabolic profiles between groups at 55 and 98 days, and used in predictive models to assess intervention impact from baseline to day 98.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to different health statuses, influencing group differentiation, and identified as a relevant metabolite that significantly improves the predictive power of statistical models for assessing dietary intervention impact.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Displayed decreasing trends throughout the protocol. Athlete 1 exhibited a decrease, returning to basal values after short recovery 1, and dropped to 70% of the initial concentration before the second match. Athlete 2 showed a mirroring effect during the first match. Both athletes responded similarly during the first match but diverged in the second match.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An essential branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) important for muscle protein synthesis and energy production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (short recovery 1, before second match, during first and second matches).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle protein turnover and utilization of BCAAs for energy during exercise, with divergent responses in the second match suggesting individual metabolic differences and indicating metabolic response to exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively associated with VO2 max values (-1.145) in a predictive regression model (p < 0.001 for the overall model).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: White blood cells, central to the immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer players' VO2 max performance after strenuous pre-seasonal training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels predict better aerobic capacity. Indicates immune status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant reduction (p < 0.05) in the verum group, remaining within the normal range.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Components of the immune system, involved in inflammatory and immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 6 weeks of dietary intervention in the verum group.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: May suggest a reduction in systemic inflammation, even within normal physiological limits.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during congested period), unchanged (during uncongested period)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at T3 (congested period) compared with T2 (uncongested) and T1 (baseline) (0.002 < p < 0.04, -0.78 < ES < -0.40). Resting values were unchanged after the 6-week uncongested period. Total load accounted for significant changes in variance during the congested period (r = 0.53).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: General immune response, defense against infection and inflammation, and participates in the inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Congested (T3) and uncongested (T1-T2) match play periods in elite soccer players.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels during congested periods indicate immune activation, inflammation, or physiological stress, potentially associated with fatigue and decreased physical performance. Unchanged levels during uncongested periods, coupled with performance improvements, suggest effective training and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Engraftment was defined as a leukocyte concentration >0.5 x 10^9 /L on at least three consecutive days after the transplantation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates the number of white blood cells, which are crucial for immune function and recovery of bone marrow after transplantation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used to define engraftment in the post-transplantation period (T1) in patients undergoing alloSCT.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary indicator of successful engraftment post-alloSCT, signifying bone marrow recovery and initial immune reconstitution.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes in leukocyte levels between baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) did not differ significantly between heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, and HFrEF).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: White blood cells involved in the immune system, defending the body against infection.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Changes between baseline and FUP6 in various heart failure subgroups (HFnEF, HFmrEF, HFrEF) after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant differential change or impact on health status or LVEF recovery was observed between LVEF recovery subgroups in this study, suggesting it is not a key differential indicator in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated at T2 (pT1–T2 < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: White blood cells, crucial components of the immune system involved in defending the body against infection and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a general immune activation and physiological stress response to extreme physical exertion.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), inflammatory indices, hematological markers, and performance decline in soccer players following a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). The LIST protocol induced transient changes in immune cells, inflammatory markers, and declines in performance. BC supplementation demonstrated potential in mitigating some EIMD, improving recovery of muscle power (SQJ), and attenuating post-exercise increases in inflammatory markers (CRP, CK, IL-6) compared to pre-supplementation and/or whey protein, suggesting better maintenance of performance and reduced post-exercise EIMD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Bovine Colostrum (BC) and Whey Protein (WP) supplementation in conjunction with a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A low-dose of 3.2 g/day of either bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) was administered for 6 weeks to soccer players. This consisted of 8 capsules x 400 mg per capsule. The LIST protocol was performed pre- and post-supplementation. No dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported, as only one dose was used; however, comparisons were made between pre- and post-supplementation responses, and directly between the BC and WP groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (transient, twofold increase 2h post-LIST 1, returned to baseline at 24h) after LIST. BC supplementation did not significantly affect leukocyte counts compared to pre-supplementation or WP group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: White blood cells, crucial for immune defense and inflammatory processes, component of the immune system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise. BC supplementation was evaluated for its effect on these counts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an immediate immunological and inflammatory response to strenuous exercise; BC did not significantly modulate the overall count.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 3 out of 15 (20.0%) patients in the Control group and 3 out of 13 (23.07%) patients in the MSC group had leukocytosis on day 7.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Higher-than-normal white blood cell count, usually indicative of an active immune response to infection or inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 with UC-MSC application.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects an active immune response or ongoing inflammation; similar prevalence between groups suggests comparable initial inflammatory states or response to therapy regarding this specific marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Confirmed to be up-regulated in all 9 hiPSC lines compared to fibroblasts by Western blot analysis. Widely used hESC/hiPSC marker.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Previously described hESC/hiPSC marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Validation of pluripotency markers in diverse hiPSC lines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirmed pluripotency marker for hiPSCs.
