document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated LRP1 expression, circulating soluble LRP1 (sLRP1) levels, and myocardial lipid content in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (IDCM) patients compared to healthy controls, and assessed the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in sLRP1 secretion. Key findings include increased circulating sLRP1, higher myocardial collagen and triglyceride content, and elevated LRP1 alpha chain expression in myocardial vessels of IDCM patients, with sLRP1 release found to be independent of the exosome pathway and not associated with blood lipid parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating disease pathogenesis and biomarker identification in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Observational and diagnostic study comparing IDCM patients (n=20 for plasma, n=9 for tissue) with age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=15 for plasma, n=5 for tissue). Myocardial tissue samples were from explanted hearts. The study also included a comparison of hypercholesterolemic and normocholesterolemic patients. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No association between sLRP1 levels and any of the lipid parameters, including LDL (r = 0.20, P = 0.47)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Low-density lipoprotein, transports cholesterol to cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM), correlation with circulating sLRP1.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Circulating sLRP1 levels are not correlated with blood LDL in IDCM patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased after ezetimibe treatment. Changing levels were not consistent with serum MMP-1 levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to tissues; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After ezetimibe treatment, metabolic syndrome patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lipid profile; decreased levels suggest improved lipid management. Inconsistent correlation with MMP-1 suggests complex interplay with disease activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varied (decreased in non-pDPN, unchanged in pDPN)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.19); significant decrease in without pDPN group (P < 0.05); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.87).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary carrier of cholesterol in the blood, often referred to as 'bad cholesterol'.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shows an improvement in cardiovascular risk indicator (lower LDL) in the group without pDPN, but not in the pDPN group.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant intra-group changes from baseline to 30 months (p > 0.500). No statistically significant sex differences were observed at endpoint, and no significant associations with glucose were found.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells; high levels contribute to plaque formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable LDL cholesterol levels post-COVID-19 vaccination, suggesting no significant overall changes or sex differences in LDL metabolism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol (reported in meta-analyses), with effects more pronounced in men than women.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to cells; high levels are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein supplementation in post-menopausal women and in both sexes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved cardiovascular health and reduced risk of chronic diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls, attributed to a higher prevalence of statin therapy

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Low-density lipoprotein, transports cholesterol to cells; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis with concurrent statin therapy
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes, with medication influencing levels

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant time interactions were found.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells throughout the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Competitive season and pre-season sports training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health; stability suggests no significant negative impact from training on LDL-C levels within the observed periods.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not show a positive influence on lipids (TC, TG, LDL-C) by CoQ10.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: 'Bad' cholesterol, high levels contribute to plaque buildup in arteries.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CoQ10 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No improvement in 'bad' cholesterol levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This population-based cross-sectional study investigated the association between the monocyte to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) and carotid artery disease, including carotid atherosclerotic plaque (CAP) and intima-media thickness (CIMT), in low-income, middle-aged, and elderly residents of rural China. The study identified a significant association between a higher MHR and increased CAP prevalence, particularly in females, and suggested MHR as a vital indicator for early atherosclerosis recognition. However, no significant correlation was found between CIMT and MHR after adjusting for covariates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study (population-based cross-sectional)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study focused on identifying associations of naturally occurring biomarker levels, with the Monocytes to High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Ratio (MHR) analyzed across quartiles.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood (implied by 'metabolism abnormalities' and 'elevation of blood glucose, LDL-C' in metabolic syndrome)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevation of LDL-C is a component of metabolic syndrome; the prevalence of carotid plaques was correlated with LDL-C (specific quantitative data not provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid transport, its oxidation is a process that HDL-C hinders; contributes to dyslipidemia and metabolic syndrome.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Atherosclerosis, metabolic syndrome, carotid plaque formation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with metabolic syndrome and prevalence of carotid plaques, suggesting metabolism abnormalities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant difference (P < 0.05) between non-diabetic and diabetic groups. Specific quantitative values for changes were not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells throughout the body ('bad' cholesterol).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress; comparison between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels are associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease, often observed in diabetic individuals.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most studies showed no alteration; one study reported a reduction in premanifest and manifest HD subjects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, involved in cholesterol transport to cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD); lipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Generally not considered a reliable peripheral biomarker for HD due to inconsistent findings, though some reductions observed in specific cohorts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Lipid Concentration; Metabolite / Lipoprotein Level (NMR analysis)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (though often within normal ranges); changed (for nonstandard subclasses)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Patients with atherosclerotic plaques (SLE-P) had higher serum low-density lipoprotein (LDL) levels, though for most patients these were within established normal ranges, compared to plaque-free patients (SLE-NP). Significantly differentially expressed (P<0.05) between SLE-P and SLE-NP patients for nonstandard subclasses.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary carrier of cholesterol to cells; high levels are a major risk factor for atherosclerosis; transports cholesterol to cells; different subclasses have varied atherogenic potential.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Subclinical atherosclerosis in women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (initial clinical assessment); Novel metabolomic signature associated with subclinical atherosclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a risk factor associated with the presence of subclinical atherosclerotic plaques in SLE patients. Part of a novel metabolomic signature associated with the presence of subclinical plaque in SLE.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: LDL-C levels were higher in the FOPS group compared to control in the 'no FOPS' condition (p = 0.051). A significant decrease in LDL-C was observed in the control group at 'no FOPS' but not in the FOPS group. There was also a significantly increased synthesis of LDL-C observed the morning after the test session in the FOPS group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to cells for various physiological processes; high levels are associated with increased cardiovascular risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparing FOPS and control groups under 'no FOPS' conditions and in the morning after the FOPS supplementation and exercise protocol.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates alterations in cholesterol transport and metabolism, suggesting a distinct metabolic response in the FOPS group potentially influenced by exercise and supplementation. Sustained increases could be associated with cardiovascular risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-sectional Study for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the 2019 general physical examination of 3,280 rural Chinese residents aged 45 years and older. No experimental interventions or therapeutic doses were administered; the study focused on observational correlations between biomarkers and cIMT. It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with cIMT (P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells ('bad' cholesterol).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fasting state during cross-sectional health examination; associated with carotid intima-media thickness.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strongly associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis, cardiovascular disease, and is a risk factor for carotid intima-media thickness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not explicitly reported as a change; its baseline level served as a variable in machine learning models.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Specific quantitative data or changes were not reported in the provided chunks; it was included as a blood-based biomarker in predictive models for depressive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells throughout the body; commonly referred to as 'bad cholesterol' due to its association with atherosclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used as a baseline blood-based biomarker in secondary analysis of EUFEST and RAISE-ETP trials, collected from patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, for inclusion in machine learning models predicting depressive symptoms and episodes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular and metabolic health; used as a variable to evaluate its contribution to predicting depressive symptoms or post-psychotic depressive episodes in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tended to lower values in women compared to men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol from the liver to cells throughout the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sex differences in lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, increased risk of cardiovascular events, and atherosclerosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with increasing PGI/PGII quartiles. Higher MPO quartiles associated with decreased levels (P < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transports cholesterol to cells; often referred to as 'bad' cholesterol due to its association with atherosclerosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:

D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an observational cross-sectional study. Its primary objective is to assess the reliability of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and immune cell reactivity, alongside perceived pain and pressure pain thresholds, through nine repeated measurements in workers exposed to constant real-life occupational workloads. Secondary aims include assessing correlations between these biomarkers and pain measures, and comparing levels between groups with higher and lower upper-extremity physical workloads. The study also details screening for metabolic parameters to ensure participant eligibility and ultimately aims to clarify the predictive role of these biomarkers in the development of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and to inform work-related stress-recovery concepts.

Participants will undergo nine repeated measurements of blood samples and pain assessments once every two weeks. The study assesses reliability and compares biomarker levels between these workload groups, rather than evaluating a therapeutic dose-response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy was negatively correlated with ΔLDL-C (%) (r = -0.30; β = -0.204, 95% CI: [-0.230 to -0.178], p < 0.001). Intensive statin therapy was negatively correlated with ΔLDL-C (%) (β = -0.028, 95% CI: [-0.056 to -0.001], p = 0.046), although this correlation was weak. No significant correlation was observed between different types of statins and ΔLDL-C (%) (β = -0.011, p = 0.272). Baseline LDL-C was 2.30 ± 0.95 mmol/L in the high-effective Δhs-CRP group vs. 2.22 ± 0.94 mmol/L in the low-effective group (p < 0.005). After 1 month, follow-up LDL-C levels were 1.60 ± 0.60 mmol/L in the high-effective group vs. 1.66 ± 0.61 mmol/L in the low-effective group (p < 0.001). Increased ΔLDL-C (%) was an independent predictor of elevated Δhs-CRP (%) (β = 0.487, 95% CI: [0.15–0.824], p = 0.005). ΔLDL-C (%) played an intermediary role in hs-CRP reduction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time course of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and conventional muscle damage markers in response to mechanically demanding muscle-damaging drop jump exercise without significant metabolic stress in healthy males. It found that cfDNA levels increased acutely and with a delayed response up to 72 hours post-exercise, correlating strongly with primary muscle damage indicators (low-frequency fatigue, MVIC torque, P20/P100 torque) and delayed-onset muscle soreness. This suggests cfDNA is a sensitive marker for acute loss of muscle function after mechanical stress, offering insights into primary and secondary muscle damage responses.

No dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of a structured exercise program in adult women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. The primary aim is to mitigate anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) by assessing changes in circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain, LVEF). Secondary objectives include evaluating other cardiac health parameters (blood pressure, HR, HRV, recovery HR), physical function, self-reported physical activity, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. The protocol also details the planned methodology for assessing these outcomes and administrative aspects of the study.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Structured Exercise Program (Aerobic and Resistance Training)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention group will perform a supervised exercise program three times per week, during anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT). Each 70-minute session includes a 5-minute warm-up, 60 minutes of training, and a 5-minute cooldown. Aerobic training, progressively increasing from 20 to 30 minutes at light to moderate-to-high intensity (50-80% HR reserve), combines treadmill, stationary bike, and stepping. Resistance training involves 2-3 sets of 10-12 maximal repetitions (12-RM) for upper and lower body, with progressive intensity. The program starts 1-2 days after the first chemotherapy session and continues throughout treatment. The control group receives standard breast cancer care without specific physical activity advice. No dose-response comparisons are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a novel, minimally invasive approach using hair follicle (HF) gene expression, specifically a four-gene panel (Bmp2, Daam2, Plaat1, Prss27), to assess and classify tissue thyroid hormone (TH) action. Investigating amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism (AIH) in human patients and a TH action indicator (THAI) mouse model, the study found that amiodarone treatment significantly attenuates tissue TH action under hyperthyroid conditions, leading to a mismatch between elevated serum TH levels and attenuated tissue hyperthyroidism, suggesting a protective effect of amiodarone against thyrotoxicosis at the tissue level.

Amiodarone was shown to prevent T4-induced TH action elevation in mouse tissues. Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism affected up to 10% of patients, and AIH affected 1% of patients. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for amiodarone or T4.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 12 times lower in the MSC group (p ≤ 0.05) compared to Control at week 48, with a gradual decrease from week 2 to 48 in the MSC group. In the Control group, a significant drop was observed up to week 24 and remained unchanged afterward.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of lung parenchymal damage, inflammation, and fibrotic changes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 pneumonia after triple UC-MSC transplantation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with improved lung functional status, reduced fibrotic changes, and recovery from COVID-19-related lung damage over time.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative literature review investigates biosensor approaches for continuous, real-time in vivo monitoring of molecular markers relevant to performance and health status. It highlights the limitations of current technologies and proposes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors as a generalizable, minimally invasive solution. The review details the development, validation, and attributes (generalizability, selectivity, reversibility, stability) of EAB sensors for detecting diverse targets (drugs, metabolites, hormones, proteins) in complex biological fluids and tissues. It also addresses the technological hurdles for subcutaneous placement, the correlation between interstitial fluid and systemic concentrations, and their potential for monitoring stress indicators (e.g., cortisol) and HPA/HPG axis hormones to assess overtraining syndromes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) Sensor Technology for Real-time In Vivo Molecular Monitoring
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This narrative literature review discusses the development and application of Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) sensors for continuous, real-time in vivo molecular monitoring, without an applied 'dose' in the traditional sense as it is a review of technology. EAB sensors, including 75-µm-diameter, 3-mm-long versions, have been tested in live rats for plasma monitoring (jugular vein) for up to 12 hours with few-second to sub-second resolution and clinically relevant precision. They are also adapted for minimally invasive subcutaneous placements (microneedles, indwelling needles) for interstitial fluid monitoring (e.g., brain, tumor, dermal ISF). The review highlights the importance of seconds-resolved time resolution and nanomolar limits of detection for hormones (achieved for LH and NGAL, micromolar for others). Time delays between subcutaneous ISF and plasma concentrations (e.g., 5-12 min for glucose, ~17 min for vancomycin) and correlations (strong for cortisol, <6% error for glucose) are noted, influenced by target properties. No dose-response comparisons for sensor parameters or monitoring duration were explicitly reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Stimulated by high GnRH pulse frequencies; pulsatility varies significantly
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Stimulated at high GnRH pulse frequencies (every 60 min or less). Pulsatility varies throughout the menstrual cycle: every 1 to 2 h during follicular phase, every 4 h during luteal phase, and peaks just before ovulation. In menopause or hypothalamic amenorrhea, pulsatility becomes rapid (~50 min) but can be disordered, suppressed, or non-existent. EAB sensors achieve nanomolar limits of detection.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: HPG axis function, menstrual cycle, menopause, hypothalamic amenorrhea, training and exercise recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitoring can help tailor training and inform exercise and recovery intervals; indicator of HPG axis function and integrity; dysregulation contributes to overtraining syndromes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. It also examined changes in cognitive function (attention, executive function, memory, visual ability, fine motor skills, reaction), psychological scores (anxiety, depression), and various blood biochemical markers (Estradiol, prolactin, FSH, LH, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin). The study compared patients before, one week after, and six months after completing chemotherapy to healthy controls. Key findings revealed widespread chemotherapy-induced abnormalities in resting state networks, which partly recovered by six months post-chemotherapy. These altered functional connectivities were correlated with cognitive assessment scores and blood biochemical indexes, suggesting RSNs as potential biomarkers for chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and for guiding rehabilitation. Baseline analyses also showed higher metabolic markers and psychological/cognitive scores in patients compared to controls, along with a high incidence of chemotherapy-induced amenorrhea.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (for breast cancer patients, some also received endocrine therapy)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Postoperative chemotherapy was administered to breast cancer patients, typically in six to eight courses. While specific drug names or dosages were not detailed, follow-up assessments were consistently conducted before (baseline), one week after completing, and six months after completing chemotherapy. Some patients (35.3%) also received endocrine therapy after chemotherapy, but no concurrent radiotherapy or endocrine therapy was given during chemotherapy. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference between breast cancer patients and healthy controls at baseline (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates reproductive function, including ovulation and sex hormone production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline assessment in breast cancer patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of reproductive hormone balance and pituitary function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A positive test indicated, with a level of confidence of 95%, that ovulation would occur 14–26 h later.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Triggers ovulation and stimulates the production of progesterone and estrogen in the menstrual cycle.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of ovulation for accurate timing of experimental trials in WomenNC participants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Critical for determining the precise testing window (mid-luteal phase) in naturally cycling women, which is essential for controlling hormonal variability and ensuring consistency in study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Enhances cholesterol conversion to testosterone, thereby supporting stable testosterone output crucial for muscle maintenance and recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then lower (lymphocytopenia), then returned to baseline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (2.8 to 5.9x10^3 /μL), followed by a significant decrease (lymphocytopenia, 2.2x10^3 /μL) at 30 min post-exercise, returning to pre-exercise values by 24 h (p<0.01). Experienced participants showed significantly higher post-exercise concentrations (p=0.005) and greater overall responses (p<0.05) than novice individuals. Lymphocyte activity is inhibited by cortisol increase. Significantly correlated with the number of rounds performed (r = 0.55; p = 0.006).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cell for adaptive immunity, central to adaptive immunity, mediates adaptive immune response and immune memory.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT), comparison between novice and experienced participants. Acute 'Cindy' workout session.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute changes in adaptive immune cell distribution and potential transient immune suppression (lymphocytopenia) following intense exercise. Higher response in experienced individuals might suggest a trained immune adaptation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.
