matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of viral infection or immune status; lymphopenia is a common feature in COVID-19 patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Females showed a modest but significant temporary lymphocyte surge at 24 months (T2, p=0.006). Specific quantitative values for magnitude were not provided beyond statistical significance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Type of white blood cell crucial for adaptive immunity and immune response modulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates alterations in immune response, particularly a transient sex-related difference in adaptive immunity in females post-COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower lymphocyte (LYM)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells involved in adaptive immunity, including specific defense against pathogens and regulation of immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-liver transplantation in transplant, acute rejection (AR), and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL) patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates compromised adaptive immune function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in the low LPC 20:0 group (p<0.05); negatively correlated with PC 18:1-18:1 (correlation coefficient >0.85). Given PC 18:1-18:1 is significantly lower in the acute stage of severe patients, lymphocyte count is inferred to be higher in the acute stage compared to recovery in severe COVID-19 patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main type of immune cell, crucial for adaptive immunity; crucial for immune response and host defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute vs. recovery stages in severe COVID-19 patients; patients with low LPC 20:0 levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired immune state or dysregulation in COVID-19 patients, potentially influenced by lipid metabolism; association with disease stage in severe COVID-19; inferred higher levels in acute severe stages compared to recovery, potentially reflecting immune dysregulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease (37.78% in ICU vs. 79.41% in Medical Ward, p < 0.001); lower counts associated with longer hospital stay (36.42 vs. 26.47 days, p = 0.015). Low counts were included in a predictive model for severe COVID-19 (AUC=0.825).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease severity (ICU patients vs. Medical Ward patients) and overall COVID-19 prognosis (hospital stay, risk of severe disease).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with longer hospital stay, critical disease, unfavorable evolution, increased mortality, and is a component of a panel predicting severe COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to evaluate and verify the diagnostic value of serum exosomal miRNAs, particularly miR-193b-5p and miR-511-5p, in sepsis and septic shock. It identified miR-193b-5p as a potential diagnostic biomarker, associated with inflammation and immune regulation, and a protective factor against sepsis and septic shock progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification and Disease State Analysis (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved an initial screening cohort of serum exosomal miRNA sequencing on patients with sepsis (n=6), septic shock (n=6), and healthy controls (n=3). This was followed by validation using qRT-PCR in a larger cohort of 90 participants, comprising 30 patients with sepsis, 30 with septic shock, and 30 general surgery patients serving as controls. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours of ICU admission. Comparisons were made between disease groups and controls to identify diagnostic biomarkers and understand disease progression; no specific therapeutic dose or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with miR-193b-5p (r = 0.26, P = 0.014). Significant differences (P < 0.05) identified in lymphocyte percentage and lymphocyte count (LYC) between patient subgroups based on miR-193b-5p levels (≤2.08 vs >2.08).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune cell population; immune response indicator.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis and septic shock patients; immune regulation; correlated with miR-193b-5p levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of immune status; levels significantly differ based on miR-193b-5p levels in sepsis/septic shock patients; lower levels indicate more severe inflammatory responses in sepsis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant main effect for time (p=0.42 for percentages, p=0.43 for counts) or group*time interaction (p=0.69 for percentages, p=0.47 for counts) for lymphocyte percentages or counts, indicating no differential alteration between or within groups due to supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cells of the adaptive immune system, crucial for specific immune responses, including combating infections and regulating immune memory.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following repeated strenuous resistance exercise and supplement consumption, over the duration of the study.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant changes in adaptive immune response, not differentially affected by BCAA-CHO or CHO supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant changes (P > 0.05) in hematological parameters (including WBC components) were observed throughout the experiment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, central to the adaptive immune system, responsible for specific immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, suggesting stable adaptive immune response capacity under the study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All immune-related complete blood counts demonstrated significant changes over time (p<0.001), but no significant changes between groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Types of white blood cells central to adaptive immunity, including T cells and B cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Analysis in the context of a study involving half-marathon running and potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Specific indicator of viral infections, chronic inflammation, or immune suppression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), inflammatory indices, hematological markers, and performance decline in soccer players following a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). The LIST protocol induced transient changes in immune cells, inflammatory markers, and declines in performance. BC supplementation demonstrated potential in mitigating some EIMD, improving recovery of muscle power (SQJ), and attenuating post-exercise increases in inflammatory markers (CRP, CK, IL-6) compared to pre-supplementation and/or whey protein, suggesting better maintenance of performance and reduced post-exercise EIMD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Bovine Colostrum (BC) and Whey Protein (WP) supplementation in conjunction with a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A low-dose of 3.2 g/day of either bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) was administered for 6 weeks to soccer players. This consisted of 8 capsules x 400 mg per capsule. The LIST protocol was performed pre- and post-supplementation. No dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported, as only one dose was used; however, comparisons were made between pre- and post-supplementation responses, and directly between the BC and WP groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower (significant 30% decline 2h post-LIST 1). While BC supplementation did not prevent the initial decline, a higher iAUC for lymphocytes (p = 0.017) was observed in the BC group compared to the WP group after LIST 2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell crucial for adaptive immunity, involved in specific immune responses and immune surveillance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise, and post-supplementation comparison between WP and BC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a transient shift in immune cell distribution or acute immune suppression/modulation post-exercise. Higher iAUC in BC group suggests altered lymphocyte response post-supplementation, potentially linked to immune function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Raised significantly after each exercise bout.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, crucial for adaptive immunity, involved in targeted immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately post-exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute immune system activation or response due to intense physical stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Systemic (inferred Blood/Serum from 'systemic changes' and 'inflammatory markers')

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased within 5 days of MSC therapy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells involved in adaptive immunity and host defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MSC therapy for ARDS in COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests improvement in immune function or restoration of immune balance, supporting an immunomodulatory effect of MSC therapy during inflammatory conditions like ARDS.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: SCT players had lower lymphocyte counts (1.8            0.5            10^3) compared to CON (2.3            0.9            10^3; p = 0.01). All measured values remained within the normal reference range.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell crucial for adaptive immunity, responsible for recognizing and targeting specific pathogens.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait during an entire athletic season of training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Although lower in SCT, lymphocyte counts remained within the normal reference range, suggesting that long-term conditioning and on-field practice do not clinically affect immune function in SCT players.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower proportions at T2 (pT1–T2 < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells (T cells, B cells, NK cells) central to adaptive immunity and immune memory.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests acute exercise-induced immunosuppression, redistribution of immune cells, or increased susceptibility to infection following extreme exertion.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Improved recovery; increased in both groups compared to baseline, reaching a significant difference between groups on day 28. Count doubled on day 7 in the MSC group and on day 14 in the Control group. Negatively correlated with CRP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells (T and B cells) essential for adaptive immunity, fighting infections, and viral clearance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 pneumonia after MSC therapy, compared to Control group.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved immune response/recovery, faster immune reconstitution, and attenuation of the inflammatory process.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively investigates the potentials, pitfalls, and practical applications of blood-based biomarkers for objective individualized monitoring of training load, recovery, and health status in elite sports. It evaluates the utility and limitations of established markers like creatine kinase (CK), lactate, C-reactive protein (CRP), urea, myoglobin, and various leukocyte populations, detailing their physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise, kinetics, and implications for muscle damage, immune function, and inflammation. The document also addresses methodological considerations, confounding variables, the need for individual reference ranges, and statistical approaches for interpreting biomarker changes, concluding with recommendations for best practices in their sport-specific use.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-based biomarker monitoring in conjunction with physical exercise and training load management in elite sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review focuses on the application and interpretation of blood-based biomarkers for athlete monitoring across various exercise loads, including strenuous, resistance, high-intensity, submaximal, acute physical stress, soccer matches, ultradistance races, and long-term intensive endurance exercise. Biomarker responses are noted to depend on exercise modality, intensity, duration, and individual factors such as ethnicity and body composition. While specific exercise regimens like 30 minutes of endurance running (65% vs 85% of VO2max) showed CRP increases, no single standardized dose-response is consistently reported or compared across all biomarkers. The document emphasizes the need for individual reference levels, standardized collection, and careful consideration of confounding variables, particularly in managing workload by adjusting training when physiological parameters exceed baseline.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: biphasic pattern (initial increase then strong decrease)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increase immediately after cessation of exercise, then strongly decrease for up to 36 h after exercise (potentially 50% below resting levels); T- and B-lymphocyte decreases are less pronounced and usually return to baseline level within 6 h.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune response, part of circulating WBCs.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exercise, hours after cessation of exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the immune system's response to exercise; can indicate immune suppression during recovery phases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tended toward higher values in women compared to men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sex differences in seniors, contributing to inflammatory indices (NLR, SII).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to changes in inflammatory indices (NLR, SII).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (during congested period), unchanged (during uncongested period)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower at T3 (congested period) as compared to T2 and T1 (p = 0.038, -0.48 < ES <-0.25); increased occurrence of lymphocytopenia. Resting values were unchanged after the 6-week uncongested period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key components of adaptive immunity, involved in specific immune responses and immune competence; shifts can be due to physical training or insufficient recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Congested (T3) and uncongested match play periods in elite soccer players.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower counts in conjunction with increased other immune cells can indicate heightened inflammatory stress, immunosuppression, or insufficient post-exercise recovery; may be associated with increased infection risk or overtraining and decreased physical performance. Unchanged levels with improved performance indicate effective training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased, then decreased rapidly to pre-protocol levels
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in both athletes due to matches, with a quick drop to pre-protocol/baseline levels during short recovery sessions, which were nearly sufficient to restore them. No specific numerical quantification provided for initial increase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune cells involved in adaptive immunity, viral defense, and long-term immune memory.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (post-match, short recovery).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute immune response to exercise, potentially reflecting recovery status and a classic intensity-dependent immune reaction to metabolic stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 30.4% in PGR >3 group vs 32.1% in PGR \u22643 group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells involved in adaptive immunity, including T cells and B cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Atrophic gastritis (PGR >3.0 status).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of immune status; lower counts associated with atrophic gastritis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No alterations or differences were found during or after the 6-week supplementation protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune cells crucial for adaptive immunity and fighting infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day) combined with a CrossFit training program.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that the supplementation and training program did not negatively impact immunity or blood component levels, maintaining health and performance potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes over the measuring time points. Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC values between 0.51 – 0.74).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Type of white blood cell, central to adaptive immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly responsive to exercise. Its moderate reliability, coupled with no significant changes, questions its suitability as a robust biomarker for exercise response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Fluctuated with varied peak times and significant sex differences
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fluctuated with varied peak times across groups, showing different patterns of significant changes. Highest median percentage in female sprint groups was in week 2 and long-distance in week 1. Highest absolute count in female sprint in week 4 and long-distance in week 5. In male groups, highest percentage in male long-distance in week 2 and male sprint in week 8, with highest absolute counts in week 4 for both male groups. Significant sex differences observed at specific time points.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of White Blood Cells (WBCs), essential for the adaptive immune response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negative moderate correlation with 20-meter sprint split (r = -0.44, p = 0.026). Positive moderate correlation with CMJ with hands on hips (r = 0.42, p = 0.034).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell involved in adaptive immunity and immune surveillance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase; correlation with sprint performance and CMJ performance.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher lymphocyte percentage associated with faster 20-meter sprint times and better CMJ performance, possibly indicating a robust immune system or beneficial immune profile for explosive power.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Relative decrease (

β = −5.10 

± 2.31, P = 0.03) in the diet group during the weight loss period, primarily due to increased neutrophil numbers. Percentage recovered to baseline during the weight regain period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key immune cells of the adaptive immune system, crucial for specific immune responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Weight loss period (prolonged energy deprivation and intense exercise).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered blood cell distribution and suggests T-lymphocyte mediated immunosuppression and potential immunodeficiency.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High molecular beta-glucan (H-BG) component has been found to stimulate the proliferation of lymphocytes with stronger effects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Adaptive immunity, immune cell expansion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High molecular beta-glucan (H-BG) component of AFO-202 beta glucan administration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Enhanced adaptive immune responses, stronger immune defense.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: More profound lymphopenia observed in MIS-C patients, with significantly lower lymphocyte counts (P < 0.05) in the rare LYST variant group compared to common LYST variant carriers.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reduction in key immune cells (lymphocytes), affecting immune system function. A key finding of MIS-C.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In MIS-C patients, particularly those carrying rare heterozygous LYST variants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A characteristic clinical indicator of MIS-C, correlating with disease severity. More pronounced lymphopenia is associated with more severe clinical presentations in LYST variant carriers.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower lymphocyte counts, almost two-fold lower in patients in the complicated group (though remaining within the normal range). Positively correlated with uPA/PAI-1 complex levels, which are associated with inflammatory response in severely ill patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reduction in lymphocyte count, which is a key component of the adaptive immune system and an indicator of immune system response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 complicated phase and anti-viral inflammatory response.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests immune dysregulation in complicated COVID-19, despite remaining within the reported normal range, and is associated with the anti-viral inflammatory response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lymphopenia was observed in 12 out of 14 (85.71%) patients in the Control group and 7 out of 13 (53.84%) patients in the MSC group on day 7. On day 28, 1 out of 10 (10%) patients in the MSC group had lymphopenia, whereas no lymphopenia was observed in the Control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lower-than-normal lymphocyte count, impairing adaptive immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 with UC-MSC application.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts worse outcomes in COVID-19; MSCs appear to improve lymphocyte counts and reduce lymphopenia prevalence, suggesting better immune recovery and prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels observed in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls. Identified as a key discriminating molecule.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, involved in protein synthesis, immune function, and arginine and proline metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for COVID-19 infection, differentiating patients from controls.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Notable differences between groups at 98 days (p < 0.002).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, crucial for protein synthesis, calcium absorption, and hormone production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention at 98 days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentiating metabolite indicating the impact of the dietary intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: COVID-19 Disease Progression Analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). Patients were stratified by disease severity (mild, severe), clinical stage (acute, recovery), and outcome (fatal, survival). No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in severe patients compared to mild, in the acute stage of severe patients compared to recovery, and in fatal patients compared to survival. AUC reached 0.940 for discriminating mild and severe patients; AUC 0.807 for discriminating acute and recovery stages in severe patients. Lower levels correlated with significantly lower helper T-cell count, NKT cell count, cytotoxic T-cell count, T-cell count, lymphocyte count/percentage, and NK cell count/percentage (all p<0.05). Conversely, lower LPC 20:0 correlated with significantly increased granulocyte colony stimulating factor (GCSF) and interleukin 6 (IL-6) concentrations (both p<0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A bioactive lipid metabolite of phosphatidylcholines; possesses anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and neutrophil activation; involved in LPC-mediated activation of NKT cells; generally involved in immune response, cell membrane structure, energy storage, and signaling processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease progression, severity (mild vs severe), clinical stages (acute vs recovery), and patient outcomes (fatal vs survival).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential predictive target for COVID-19 progression and outcome; associated with immune/inflammatory responses and disease severity; a possible target for therapeutic strategies; correlates with immune/cytokine indexes and NKT cell count.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document introduces and details a novel, cost-effective, non-fluorescent immunohistochemistry (IHC) method for assessing autophagy flux in fixed tissues. Utilizing MAP1LC3/LC3B and SQSTM1/p62 as core markers, the method employs diaminobenzidine (DAB) staining and bright-field microscopy. It provides a comprehensive protocol for the detection, visualization, scoring, and interpretation of these biomarkers, aiming to bridge the gap between experimental research and clinical diagnostics by offering a reliable and accessible alternative to traditional fluorescence-based techniques for understanding cellular homeostasis and disease mechanisms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Non-fluorescent Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for autophagy flux assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This methodology describes a detailed non-fluorescent immunohistochemistry protocol for assessing autophagy flux using diaminobenzidine (DAB) staining in fixed tissue samples, including commercial tissue microarray slides. The protocol involves specific steps for tissue processing, antigen retrieval (e.g., heat-induced in citrate buffer for 30 min at boiling point), blocking, primary antibody incubation (e.g., SQSTM1/p62 and MAP1LC3B/LC3B at 1:50 dilution overnight at 4°C), secondary antibody and ABC solution application, DAB substrate reaction (up to 2 min), and counterstaining. Quantification involves a scoring system based on puncta numbers (graded 0-3) and the percentage of stained cells (categorized into ranges) using bright-field microscopy, typically at 40x objective. Optimization tips include using fresh reagents, optimizing antibodies and concentrations through titration, proper tissue fixation (10% formalin for 24h), appropriate antigen retrieval (heat-induced or enzymatic with citrate or EDTA buffer), controlling background staining with hydrogen peroxide (0.3%) and normal serum/BSA, and monitoring DAB development time. This is a methodological paper, and thus no therapeutic dose-response comparisons are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (puncta staining via DAB IHC)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Puncta numbers are graded 0-3 (no to high puncta), and percentage of stained cells is categorized (0-25%, 26-50%, 51-75%, 76-100%). An increase in LC3B can reflect (A) autophagy induction or (B) a block in autophagosome-lysosome fusion or degradation; accumulation with SQSTM1 suggests a flux block; increase with SQSTM1 decrease indicates high autophagy activity. Low levels may imply efficient turnover or low induction. No specific quantitative change data from an intervention is reported as this is a methodological study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.
