matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of oxidative stress and cellular damage, particularly lipid peroxidation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Lipid Peroxidation Marker / Oxidative Stress Marker / Antioxidant Capacity

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Minimal variation was observed generally between groups. No significant difference was found in TBARS activity between cognitive impaired and cognition normal diabetics with vitamin D insufficiency. In cognitive impaired diabetics with vitamin D sufficiency, TBARS activity was slightly lower but not significant. Among non-diabetics, no difference was found, and it was slightly lower in both cognitive impaired and cognition normal subjects in both vitamin D insufficient and sufficient groups. Specific values based on percentage inhibition were noted but not quantified in detail in the findings.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures malondialdehyde (MDA) and other reactive carbonyl compounds, which are end-products of lipid peroxidation, representing the overall capacity of biological fluids to counteract reactive oxygen species and prevent oxidative damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress; cognitive impairment status in diabetics and non-diabetics with or without vitamin D insufficiency; comparison between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of oxidative stress and lipid damage. This study found no significant differences or correlations between TBARS levels and cognitive impairment across various diabetic and vitamin D status subgroups, and minimal variation between diabetic and non-diabetic groups, suggesting it may not be a sensitive peripheral indicator in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No overall anserine treatment or interaction effects were found. Moderate effect size for reduced TBARS in ANS-LD vs. PLA (d = 0.43, p = 0.17). At 24 h post-exercise, a lower TBARS was found for ANS-LD than ANS-HD (p = 0.02) and a trend towards lower TBARS in ANS-LD than PLA (p = 0.067).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of lipid peroxidation, indicating oxidative damage to cell membranes and reflecting cell membrane protection against reactive oxygen species (ROS).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Anserine supplementation following an exercise challenge (time to exhaustion).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant overall effect on lipid peroxidation, but trends towards reduced oxidative damage in the low dose suggest anserine-enhanced SOD activity protected cellular integrity from peroxidation damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Oxidative stress marker; Concentration; Metabolite of lipid peroxidation

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased immediately after exercise, then decreased
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise, then decreased 3 hours after, returning to baseline 24 hours after (F3 = 79.43; p < 0.001). Demonstrated good reliability (ICC = 0.79), and was identified as having excellent reliability (ICC > 0.9) and suitability in some assessments.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of lipid peroxidation, reflecting the level of oxidative stress; metabolite of lipid peroxidation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 60-min continuous endurance exercise bouts; endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; used in exercise context for analyzing oxidative stress; monitoring of exercise response and recovery processes in endurance sports.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suitable as a physiological exercise response and recovery marker for monitoring athletes' load management, with good to excellent reliability. Its observed correlations with MVC support its potential as a diagnostic parameter in endurance sports for assessing oxidative stress and muscle force.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated sex differences in inflammatory response, lipid peroxidation, and muscle damage in men and women athletes following an acute resistance exercise, specifically a maximal incremental half-squat test. Results showed men exhibited a larger pro-inflammatory response (IL6) and increased lipid peroxidation (HPX) at 24 hours post-exercise compared to women at equivalent workloads, while no significant sex-based differences were observed in other muscle damage markers (CK-MB, LDH, 
	-actin).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Resistance Exercise (Maximal Incremental Half-Squat)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed half-squat exercises with five incremental intensities (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of one-repetition maximum, 1RM). Repetitions varied: 5 at 20-60% 1RM, 2 at 80% 1RM, and 1 at 100% 1RM. Rest periods between sets were 3-5 minutes. Equivalent workloads were used for men and women, but men achieved larger net loads due to greater muscle mass. No specific dose-response comparisons for biomarkers were reported across different intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant differences between sexes were found using the Bonferroni test.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker for oxidative stress, indirectly estimating malondialdehyde (MDA), and an indicator of lipid peroxidation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Maximal incremental half-squat exercise test.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of significant change suggests this specific marker of oxidative stress was not significantly impacted by the exercise protocol or did not differ between sexes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels observed in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls. Identified as a key discriminating molecule.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for COVID-19 infection, differentiating patients from controls and indicating metabolic changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant in men in the validation cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery and characterization for intervertebral disc degeneration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved proteomic profiling and histological grading of human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissues and matched plasma from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy. IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase in abundance in severe compared to mild degenerated IVD tissues (AUC score of 0.748). Accurately differentiated between mild and severe degenerated IVD tissues as part of a biomarker panel.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Deficiency-causing mutations in humans lead to Keutel syndrome, a disease characterized by soft tissue calcification, strongly implicating its role in vascular calcification.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of vascular calcification and extracellular matrix alterations, major components of aging underlying early cognitive decline.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved proteomic profiling and histological grading of human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissues and matched plasma from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy. IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scientific roadmap by the Heart Failure Association comprehensively addresses the complex and heterogeneous nature of fibrosis in heart failure, aiming to improve its definition, quantification, and treatment. It reviews mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis across various etiologies like pressure overload, aging, and cardiomyopathies, emphasizing the central role of TGF-β, collagen deposition, and myofibroblast activity. The document discusses challenges in detecting fibrosis using circulating biomarkers, proposing a framework for assessment and a roadmap for future research to identify individual fibrotic mechanisms, novel therapeutic targets, and diagnostic tools. It also evaluates diverse anti-fibrotic strategies, including pharmacological agents and non-coding RNA-based treatments, highlighting the need for targeted, multi-pathway approaches given the complexity of the fibrotic process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anti-fibrotic therapies for heart failure, including established drugs like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, as well as specific anti-fibrotic agents like pirfenidone. Investigational strategies include targeting the TGF-β pathway (e.g., TGF-β inhibitors, CTGF inhibitors like FG-3019), MAPK pathways (e.g., ERK inhibitors), inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1α), neuregulin-1 administration, Matrix Metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitors, Galectin-3 inhibitors, and non-coding RNA-based treatments (microRNA and long non-coding RNAs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a review document, and as such, no specific therapeutic doses, intensities, or durations are consistently reported for any intervention, nor are dose-response comparisons detailed. While some agents like Pirfenidone and non-coding RNA modulators show utility in experimental models and clinical trials (e.g., microRNA-21 inhibitor in a Phase II trial), precise quantitative dosage or detailed treatment parameters are generally absent, reflecting a discussion of general approaches and their limitations, including a noted 'lack of precision' in current therapies. For example, MMP-12i was given 3h post-MI, but without specific dosage.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Inhibition leads to detrimental effects (prolonged inflammation, exacerbated dilatation).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inhibition by MMP-12i given at 3 h post-MI suppressed neutrophil apoptosis, leading to prolonged inflammation and exacerbated left ventricular dilatation. No direct quantification of MMP-12 activity change was provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase; its activity impacts neutrophil apoptosis and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Targeted inhibition (MMP-12i) at 3 hours post-myocardial infarction (MI) in experimental models.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Inhibition is detrimental, indicating a potentially beneficial role of MMP-12 in post-MI recovery by regulating inflammation and preventing adverse remodeling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Enhanced concentrations were triggered by IL-1β stimulation. Increased significantly during the first 3 days of hyperacute serum treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: IL-1β stimulation and early phase of hyperacute serum treatment (days 0-3) in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate cartilage and bone degradation. Initial increases during hyperacute serum treatment suggest changes in tissue remodeling, but may not reflect sustained degradation if levels stabilize later.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity. Statistically higher in advanced NASH patients compared to early NASH and controls; higher in fibrosis stage 4 (F4 group) compared to healthy controls (P<0.01); tendency to be higher in grade 1 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning, and F3 group. Some correlation with stages of fibrosis observed (P=0.051). Exhibited no difference before and after pioglitazone administration over two months.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Extracellular matrix degradation; involved in tissue remodeling and fibrosis, particularly type IV collagen.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity, advanced NASH, NASH with fibrosis stage 4 (F4), fibrosis stage 3 (F3), grade 1 steatosis, grade 3 inflammation, grade 2 ballooning. Response to pioglitazone treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of advanced NASH and progression of liver fibrosis, particularly severe fibrosis (F4), but did not reflect steatosis or inflammation. Not indicated as a biomarker for general NASH disease activity due to lack of change, and levels are not affected by short-term pioglitazone treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Catheter ablation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Gene expression significantly upregulated in differentiated fibrocytes from persistent AF compared to SR controls and paroxysmal AF groups. Plasma levels showed no significant differences among persistent AF, paroxysmal AF, and SR control groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase, involved in extracellular matrix degradation and remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF) (fibrocytes); Atrial Fibrillation and Sinus Rhythm (plasma).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased gene expression in fibrocytes from persistent AF suggests their active role in ECM degradation and remodeling, which can contribute to pathological changes in cardiac tissue. Systemic plasma levels do not show significant changes, suggesting localized changes might be more prominent.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: No therapeutic intervention was applied. This was a prospective cohort study observing disease progression across acute (1-14 days post-symptom onset, DPSO), post-acute (15-89 DPSO), and chronic (≥90 DPSO) phases. Participants were assessed for persistent arthralgia at 90 days post-symptom onset using a self-reported Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for joint pain, with plasma samples collected during initial enrollment and subsequent follow-ups between 21 and 90 days after recruitment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower levels were observed in recovered individuals compared to controls (p=0.017) and to those with persistent arthralgia (p=0.027). These lower levels were associated with recovery. While some general comparisons showed no significant differences, specific analyses for recovered versus persistent arthralgia showed a significant decrease.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase involved in extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, collagen breakdown, and tissue remodeling. Its overexpression is implicated in fibroblast-like synoviocyte migration and joint damage in chronic inflammatory diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-acute phase of Chikungunya Fever (CHIKF) infection, specifically in individuals who recovered from arthralgia compared to controls and individuals with persistent arthralgia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels are associated with clinical recovery from CHIKF and a favorable clinical trajectory, potentially indicating reduced pathological tissue remodeling and joint damage. Its specific role in CHIKF pathogenesis requires further elucidation.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to identify and validate novel protein biomarkers for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM), focusing on blood-based protein profiling. It successfully identified serum protein c-KIT as a novel biomarker capable of differentiating HCM patients from healthy controls. Furthermore, the investigation demonstrated c-KIT's involvement in cardiac remodeling and fibrosis-related processes, particularly in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HOCM), suggesting its potential role in understanding fibrotic signaling within HCM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery, identification, and functional investigation for diagnostic purposes in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 60 HCM patients (33 HOCM, 27 HNCM) and 28 healthy controls. Proteomic profiling of 92 cardiometabolic proteins in serum was conducted on a subgroup (20 HCM, 10 healthy), with c-KIT validated in the full cohort via ELISA. Myocardial c-KIT gene expression was analyzed in HOCM patient myectomies, and in vitro c-KIT silencing was performed in human cardiac fibroblasts for functional investigation. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in myectomies of HOCM patients compared to healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established fibrosis marker, involved in the degradation and remodeling of the extracellular matrix.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cardiac tissue in Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy (HOCM).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate cardiac fibrosis, which is clinically relevant for prognosis and risk assessment in HCM, particularly concerning the risk of sudden cardiac death.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels highest in subphenotype 2. Precise quantification not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Implicated in extracellular matrix remodelling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort, particularly defining Subphenotype 2.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are associated with subphenotype 2, which is linked to significantly worse patient outcomes (HR 3.43 (1.76–6.69) compared to subphenotype 1).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery and characterization for intervertebral disc degeneration
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved proteomic profiling and histological grading of human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissues and matched plasma from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy. IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most enriched (LFC = 0.70). Log2 fold change above 0.5 and significance level less than 0.05.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase-2, a zinc-dependent endopeptidase
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Plasma samples from individuals with severe degenerated IVD compared to mild degenerated IVD
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential plasma biomarker for IVD degeneration progression; shows a moderate positive correlation with histological grade

document_context_data.document_summary: This scientific roadmap by the Heart Failure Association comprehensively addresses the complex and heterogeneous nature of fibrosis in heart failure, aiming to improve its definition, quantification, and treatment. It reviews mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis across various etiologies like pressure overload, aging, and cardiomyopathies, emphasizing the central role of TGF-β, collagen deposition, and myofibroblast activity. The document discusses challenges in detecting fibrosis using circulating biomarkers, proposing a framework for assessment and a roadmap for future research to identify individual fibrotic mechanisms, novel therapeutic targets, and diagnostic tools. It also evaluates diverse anti-fibrotic strategies, including pharmacological agents and non-coding RNA-based treatments, highlighting the need for targeted, multi-pathway approaches given the complexity of the fibrotic process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anti-fibrotic therapies for heart failure, including established drugs like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, as well as specific anti-fibrotic agents like pirfenidone. Investigational strategies include targeting the TGF-β pathway (e.g., TGF-β inhibitors, CTGF inhibitors like FG-3019), MAPK pathways (e.g., ERK inhibitors), inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1α), neuregulin-1 administration, Matrix Metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitors, Galectin-3 inhibitors, and non-coding RNA-based treatments (microRNA and long non-coding RNAs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a review document, and as such, no specific therapeutic doses, intensities, or durations are consistently reported for any intervention, nor are dose-response comparisons detailed. While some agents like Pirfenidone and non-coding RNA modulators show utility in experimental models and clinical trials (e.g., microRNA-21 inhibitor in a Phase II trial), precise quantitative dosage or detailed treatment parameters are generally absent, reflecting a discussion of general approaches and their limitations, including a noted 'lack of precision' in current therapies. For example, MMP-12i was given 3h post-MI, but without specific dosage.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Deletion leads to detrimental effects (inhibition of beneficial macrophages, increased dysfunction/rupture).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Deletion inhibited M2 anti-inflammatory macrophage activation, stimulated left ventricular dysfunction, and increased cardiac rupture rates. No direct quantification of MMP-28 activity change was provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase; its presence is required for M2 anti-inflammatory macrophage activation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic deletion in myocardial infarction (MI) models.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Deletion is detrimental, indicating a crucial protective role in preventing left ventricular dysfunction and cardiac rupture by promoting M2 anti-inflammatory macrophage activation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported, this is a study protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammation and blood-brain barrier disruption in neuroinflammatory conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal cohort study investigated plasma levels of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and their tissue inhibitors (TIMPs) as potential biomarkers for persistent arthralgia in individuals diagnosed with Chikungunya Fever (CHIKF). The study aimed to identify factors and biomarkers associated with the development of chronic musculoskeletal symptoms. Key findings indicate that lower plasma MMP-2 levels are associated with clinical recovery, while elevated TIMP-2 levels during the post-acute phase are independent predictors, increasing the odds of developing persistent arthralgia in the chronic phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on the natural course and clinical outcomes of Chikungunya Fever (CHIKF) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No therapeutic intervention was applied. This was a prospective cohort study observing disease progression across acute (1-14 days post-symptom onset, DPSO), post-acute (15-89 DPSO), and chronic (≥90 DPSO) phases. Participants were assessed for persistent arthralgia at 90 days post-symptom onset using a self-reported Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for joint pain, with plasma samples collected during initial enrollment and subsequent follow-ups between 21 and 90 days after recruitment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant differences were observed between CHIK+ subjects and controls, nor between Control, Recovered, and Persistent Arthralgia groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A matrix metalloproteinase that degrades various extracellular matrix components and activates other MMPs, playing a role in tissue remodeling and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chikungunya Fever infection (acute, post-acute, and chronic phases).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not identified as a significant biomarker for persistent arthralgia or disease progression in this study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with increasing age (r=0.3035; p=0.0009) and with increasing C12FDG++ signal (r=0.1909; p=0.0489). It was uniquely correlated with C12FDG++ PBMCs in females (r=0.3242; p=0.0298) and significantly decreased after fisetin usage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy human participants (age range 20–82 years), association with chronological aging, correlation with peripheral senescence (C12FDG++ PBMCs) with sexually dimorphic correlations, and response to senolytic treatment (fisetin).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased after elagolix treatment (part of 42 DETs with similar significance levels)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metalloproteinase, involved in extracellular matrix remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After elagolix treatment in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure and suspected endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentially expressed transcript in an inflammatory array after elagolix treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study evaluated and compared the regenerative potential of different blood-derived products (EDTA-PRP, Citrate-PRP, and hyperacute serum [hypACT]) in a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model over 21 days. Key assessments included metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression (SOX9, COL2AB, COL1A1, MMP3, P21), and extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and quality, using 1% or 5% concentrations of the products. HypACT consistently demonstrated superior and more stable results for cartilage-related gene expression and tissue quality. In contrast, Citrate-PRP showed negative effects on ECM production, chondrocyte presence, and gene expression, which was partly attributed to anticoagulants and extensive platelet accumulation. Metabolic activity generally showed no significant differences among the blood products compared to controls, though some variations were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-derived products: hyperacute serum (hypACT), leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with EDTA (EPRP), and leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with trisodium citrate (CPRP).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood products (hypACT, EPRP, CPRP) were prepared from whole blood (18mL for hypACT, 16mL for EPRP, 16mL for CPRP) and used as 1% or 5% (v/v) supplementation in 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet cultures for 21 days; 10% concentration was deemed unsuitable. HypACT showed stable effects across both 1% and 5% concentrations. For EPRP, 1% was favored over 5% due to better glycosaminoglycan deposition and lower platelet accumulation, with concentration influencing specific gene expressions (SOX9, MMP3, COL2AB, COL1A1). CPRP at both 1% and 5% concentrations resulted in poor tissue quality and no increase in COL2AB production, with extensive platelet accumulation observed.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: extensive drop (lower); moderate, not significant decrease
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High production and activity are observed during OA development. A significant drop in expression was observed with 1% EPRP supplementation (p < 0.001) vs. day 0. A moderate, non-significant decrease vs. day 0 was seen with hypACT 5% and EPRP 5%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in the degradation of extracellular matrix components, including cartilage, contributing to tissue remodeling and pathological destruction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: OA development (general), and 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels indicate cartilage degradation and OA progression. Lower expression suggests reduced cartilage degradation and a more stable cartilage environment, which is generally beneficial for repair.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnosis of Sport-related Concussion (SRC) using proteomic profiling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from concussed and non-concussed collegiate athletes within 48 hours post-injury, with analyses conducted for acute (0-6 hours) and subacute (7-48 hours) phases. A highly multiplexed proteomic DNA aptamers assay targeting 1305 plasma proteins was used. The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly more abundant after SRC (P<0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in extracellular matrix degradation and remodeling; potential candidate biomarker for concussion.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sports-Related Concussion (SRC) assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential candidate biomarker for concussion.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Co-culture supernatant of osteoarthritic knee joint explants (human bone, cartilage, and synovium tissues)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Enhanced concentrations were triggered by IL-1β stimulation. Increased significantly during the first 3 days of hyperacute serum treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A primary proteolytic enzyme responsible for initiating the degradation of the extracellular matrix of cartilage and bone in osteoarthritis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: IL-1β stimulation and early phase of hyperacute serum treatment (days 0-3) in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate cartilage and bone degradation. Initial increases during hyperacute serum treatment suggest changes in tissue remodeling, but may not reflect sustained degradation if levels stabilize later.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a distinct 4-biomarker panel (CXCL9, ST2, MMP-3, OPN) for cGVHD shown to correlate with disease activity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in extracellular matrix degradation and tissue remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Component of a panel correlating with chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease (cGVHD) disease activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

Consistently higher in men (P = 6.46

												–13 in discovery cohort, P = 4.31 
												× 10
												–8 or OR 8.403 in validation cohort) after adjustment for confounders; associated with enrichment of extracellular matrix degradation pathways (FDR = 3.59

												–9).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Part of matrix metalloproteinases involved in extracellular matrix degradation and deposition, contributing to tissue remodelling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Higher in men with paroxysmal AF, associated with vascular remodelling and AF substrate formation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased vascular remodelling, extracellular matrix degradation, and potentially subclinical vascular disease in men with paroxysmal AF. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Catheter ablation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in gene expression in differentiated fibrocytes or plasma levels were observed among persistent AF, paroxysmal AF, and SR control groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase, involved in collagen degradation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Atrial Fibrillation and Sinus Rhythm patients (fibrocytes and plasma).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Unchanged gene expression in fibrocytes and systemic plasma levels suggest MMP-8 may not be a primary distinguishing factor for fibrocyte activity or a prominent circulating biomarker for AF-related ECM remodeling in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Top upregulated in MIS-C compared with COVID-19.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Related to multiple pathways, including cell-to-cell communication.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MIS-C disease state, compared with COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides insights into differential pathogenesis of MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly associated with estimated subphenotypes (p < 0.05 after correction for multiple testing), but specific change direction/magnitude not detailed for this individual protein.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with extracellular matrix remodelling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates protein involvement in patient subphenotype classification, which may relate to prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood cells / Leukocytes (inferred from gene expression analysis correlating with plasma cytokine clusters)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overexpressed by the high inflammatory phenotype; showed greatest fold changes between phenotypes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix metalloproteinase, involved in extracellular matrix degradation, inflammation, and neutrophil degranulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Distinguishing high-cytokine from low-cytokine clusters in sepsis, particularly in the high inflammatory phenotype.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a high inflammatory state, associated with greater disease severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated systemic and synovial Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) levels in early, treatment-naïve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients, both at baseline and after 6 months of conventional-synthetic Disease-Modifying-Anti-Rheumatic-Drugs (cs-DMARDs) treatment. It found that circulating PTX3 is a reliable marker of RA activity and predicts structural damage, remaining high post-treatment regardless of clinical response. Synovial PTX3 gene and protein expression correlated with local inflammation, disease activity, immune cell infiltration, ectopic lymphoid structures, and specific synovial pathotypes. While synovial PTX3 protein levels significantly decreased after cs-DMARD treatment, reflecting reduced local inflammation, this change was independent of clinical response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Conventional-synthetic Disease-Modifying-Anti-Rheumatic-Drugs (cs-DMARDs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received cs-DMARDs for 6 months; 94.1% received cs-DMARDs and 47.9% received adjunctive corticosteroid treatment. Treatment effects on PTX3 levels were assessed at 6 months and were independent of clinical response status; no specific dosages or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased (PTX3 and IL1B expression with MMP8 deficiency)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: MMP8 deficiency leads to increased disease severity, accompanied by increased expression of IL1B and PTX3 in the joints.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Matrix degradation, involved in inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: RA, joint inflammation, in the context of MMP8 deficiency.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: MMP8 deficiency is associated with worsened disease severity and increased local PTX3 expression, highlighting a link between matrix degradation enzymes and inflammation.
