document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-of-day-dependent physiological, physical, and psychological responses of higher-weight men to a Walking Football Match (WFM). Findings revealed that evening WFM led to significantly lower glycemia, mean blood pressure (MBP), and heart rate recovery after 1 minute (HRR60s) compared to morning sessions, suggesting potential safety and metabolic benefits for higher-weight individuals when exercising in the evening. Most other parameters, including HRV, lactate, SpO2, and various physical performance metrics, showed no significant diurnal variation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Walking Football Match (WFM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a single session of 5 vs. 5 Walking Football Matches (WFM) on artificial turf fields. Each session lasted approximately one hour, comprising a 10-min warm-up, two 20-min playing periods separated by a 10-min passive recovery, and a 5-min cool-down. Matches were performed in randomized order, either in the morning (6:30 a.m. - 8:30 a.m.) or in the evening (5:00 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.), with 7 days between sessions. The activity was classified as moderate intensity (4.85-4.9 METs), with participants averaging around 2500-2600 steps per session and a cadence of approximately 63.8 steps/min. The study primarily focused on time-of-day effects, with no explicit dose-response comparisons regarding WFM intensity or duration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the sex-specific relationships among total serum cholinesterase activity (CS), high-sensitive cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), and traditional hemodynamic parameters of autonomic nervous system function during exercise in apparently healthy individuals. Key findings include a positive association between serum CS and hs-cTnT detection in women, an inverse association in men, and sex-dependent predictions of exercise-hemodynamic changes and metabolic impairment by CS, providing insights for cardiovascular disease risk stratification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study using Cardiac Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent a standard Exercise ECG Stress Test (EST) according to the Bruce protocol. The study was observational, investigating associations between biomarkers and hemodynamic changes during this test; no specific therapeutic 'dose' or 'duration' of an intervention was applied or compared. Hypertensive reactions were defined as peak SBP > 205 mm/Hg in men and > 187 mm/Hg in women. Heart rate recovery rate was calculated from peak rate to recovery time.

Trend analysis revealed accumulating components of the metabolic syndrome across sex-specific quartiles of CS in men (p for trend = 0.046) and women (p for trend = < 0.001).

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased urinary metallothioneins were observed after cessation of oral cadmium exposure in an animal study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated metallothioneins (MTs) as potential dynamic biomarkers for Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) and other Lysosomal Storage Diseases (LSDs) with nervous system involvement. It identified significant overexpression of MT genes and proteins, including specific isoforms (MT1A, MT1E, MT2A, MTE, MT1P3-C20ORF127), in T lymphocytes and brain tissue of MLD patients and various LSD mouse models. MT levels correlated with disease progression, nervous tissue damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation, and decreased upon therapeutic treatment. In vitro experiments elucidated that MT expression is regulated in response to proinflammatory and pro-oxidative stimuli and through microglia-astrocyte crosstalk, supporting their role as dynamic markers of disease pathology, progression, and therapeutic response in LSDs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) and general therapeutic treatments in mouse models, alongside in vitro experimental stimulations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation involved normal hematopoietic stem cells from WT donors into globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD) mice at postnatal day 8, which led to only mild symptoms at 40 days of age, consistent with a positive treatment response; no specific dose-response comparisons were reported for HSCT. General therapeutic treatment in mice resulted in decreased biomarker levels, but specific treatment types, doses, intensity, or duration details were not provided. In vitro studies applied experimental conditions such as 10ng/ml lipopolysaccharide, 100
M H2O2-1mM L-buthionine-sulfoximine, 1mM Trolox, 10
M dexamethasone, and 10% serum from WT and GLD mice to primary cortical astrocytes and astrocyte/microglia cocultures for 6 or 24 hours; these were experimental conditions and not patient treatments.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Metallothioneins (MTs), including isoforms MT1A, MT1E, MT2A, MTE, MT1P3-C20ORF127
matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: T lymphocytes (human blood), brain tissue (human postmortem frontal cortex, mouse models for MLD, GLD, MPSI, MPSIII, SD), Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF), blood cells (human, mouse), pure mouse astrocyte cultures, astrocyte-microglia cocultures
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA expression), Protein Level (protein expression, immunoreactivity, immunoblot)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in disease states, lower after therapeutic treatment, unchanged in other neurodegenerative diseases
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly overexpressed in T lymphocytes (average 1.6-fold higher, false discovery rate <0.01) and brain (average 25.5-fold higher by qPCR, elevated immunoreactivity in white and gray matter, especially in astrocytes) of MLD patients compared to controls. Overexpression was also observed in brain tissue from other LSD patients (P<0.05 implied) and in mouse models (e.g., GLD mice showed highest levels: Mt1 5.5-fold, Mt2 8.0-fold). Levels correlated with disease progression (Pearson r = 0.617; p = 0.0432 with patient age in late infantile MLD) and dramatically increased from presymptomatic to late symptomatic stages in GLD mice. MT expression was significantly lower (P<0.05 implied) in transplanted GLD mice compared to untreated controls. In vitro, MT expression increased in response to proinflammatory (LPS) and pro-oxidative (H2O2 with glutathione depletion) stimuli, was generally increased by dexamethasone pretreatment, and blocked by Trolox (antioxidant) against oxidative stress. It also increased with microglia-conditioned medium and 10% serum from late-symptomatic GLD mice. No significant change was observed in blood/brain from EAE mice or other human inflammatory/degenerative neurologic diseases, indicating specificity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates metal homeostasis, detoxification, and protection against cellular oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Acts as a general marker of nervous tissue damage and a dynamic indicator of disease progression and therapeutic response. Plays a role in microglia-astrocyte crosstalk and mitigating LSD-associated inflammation and oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) disease progression and pathology in human patients and mouse models; various other Lysosomal Storage Disorders (LSDs) with CNS involvement (e.g., GLD, MPSI, MPSIII, SD); therapeutic treatment response (e.g., Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in GLD mice); progressive disease stages; in vitro investigation of responses to proinflammatory and pro-oxidative stimuli; microglia-astrocyte crosstalk and effects of GLD mouse serum; and specific to LSDs, showing distinction from general neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Parkinson disease, Huntington disease, EAE mice).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for monitoring neurologic disease processes, progression, and treatment response in MLD and other LSDs. It indicates nervous tissue damage, CNS involvement, and significant cellular oxidative stress/inflammatory responses. Suggests potential for clinical biomarker assay development in CSF and serves as a specific marker for MLD/LSD-related pathobiology. Correlates with disease modification following treatment and reflects astrocyte activation in neuroinflammatory processes, elucidating mechanistic links in disease pathogenesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed great potential as a biomarker; part of a group of 535 upregulated and 1200 downregulated lncRNAs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Long non-coding RNA; intricate regulatory role in MASLD pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MASLD diagnosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Promising biomarker for MASLD diagnosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multi-phase, multi-center study developed and validated a machine learning-enabled blood-derived exosomal RNA profiling platform (ETR.sig) for noninvasive multi-cancer detection and localization, demonstrating its robust potential for accurate diagnosis, tumor origin classification, and prognostic assessment across eight primary cancer types.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery and validation for multi-cancer detection and prognosis using exosomal RNA signatures.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This multi-phase, multi-center study involved a discovery phase (818 participants, 8 cancer types, 194 healthy controls, exoRNA-seq), a screening phase (245 participants, TaqMan qPCR), and a validation phase (1,385 participants). Machine learning (Random Forest and LASSO algorithms) was applied to refine 33 initial candidate biomarkers down to 12 exosomal tumor RNA signatures (ETR.sig). Diagnostic models were built with stratified random sampling (7:3 or 8:2 training/validation splits, tenfold cross-validation). Filtering criteria for differential gene expression included |log2FC|>1 and P<0.05 for bulk RNA-seq, and P<0.01 with FC ≥1.4 or ≤−1.6 for multi-cancer exoRNA-seq. The study focused on diagnostic development and biomarker identification, thus no therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Epithelial cells (in LUAD scRNA-seq), tumor tissues, cancer and normal sample-derived single cells (KIRC and LUAD).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similarly upregulated in samples from LUAD patients with LN metastasis and distant metastasis; upregulated overall in tumor tissues; widespread differences observed between cancer and normal sample-derived single cells in KIRC and LUAD; high expression in both cancer and normal tissues.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key gene involved in tumor occurrence, development, metastasis, and prognosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: LUAD patients with LN metastasis and distant metastasis, tumor tissues, KIRC and LUAD samples (cancer vs. normal).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for tumor presence and metastasis, suggesting alterations in the tumor microenvironment (TME).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with negative outcome/poor prognosis.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Alcohol metabolite; metabolic regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 patient prognosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with negative outcome (poor prognosis).

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant differences observed between groups 55 days after starting the dietary intervention (p not < 0.002).

document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an observational cross-sectional study. Its primary objective is to assess the reliability of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and immune cell reactivity, alongside perceived pain and pressure pain thresholds, through nine repeated measurements in workers exposed to constant real-life occupational workloads. Secondary aims include assessing correlations between these biomarkers and pain measures, and comparing levels between groups with higher and lower upper-extremity physical workloads. The study also details screening for metabolic parameters to ensure participant eligibility and ultimately aims to clarify the predictive role of these biomarkers in the development of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and to inform work-related stress-recovery concepts.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exposure to real-life occupational workloads
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study compares two groups: an 'exposed group' with higher upper-extremity physical workloads (exceeding the Action Limit of TLV for HAL, with daily repetitive strain for >=4 days/week and >=20 hours/week) and an 'unexposed group' (office workers) with lower upper-extremity physical workloads (not exceeding TLV for HAL). Participants will undergo nine repeated measurements of blood samples and pain assessments once every two weeks. The study assesses reliability and compares biomarker levels between these workload groups, rather than evaluating a therapeutic dose-response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document is a commentary discussing the potential of a circulating miRNA triad (miR-181a-5p, miR-146a-5p, and miR-148a-3p) as a diagnostic biomarker for age-related cognitive impairment (ACI), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's disease (AD). No specific doses were quantified, and no dose-response comparisons were reported. The commentary further notes that considerations for future therapeutic development include 'global inhibition' versus 'transient brain-specific inhibition,' without providing dose or intensity specifics for either.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to establish comprehensive reference intervals for novel circulating biomarkers of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and hepatic regeneration in healthy human volunteers. It investigated intra- and interindividual variability, as well as diurnal variation, to provide robust data for interpreting exploratory clinical DILI studies and assisting biomarker qualification by regulatory authorities.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study for establishing reference intervals of circulating biomarkers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved serum sample collection from 227 healthy volunteers in a cross-sectional study (single sample). Additionally, 25 subjects underwent weekly serial sampling over 3 weeks, and 23 subjects had intensive 24-hour blood sampling every 3 hours after a 10-h overnight fast and standardized meals. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were involved, as the focus was on establishing reference intervals and assessing natural variability in healthy subjects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reference intervals established; influenced by sex and BMI; lower intraindividual variability compared to previous studies.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reference intervals based on the 97.5% quantile (90% CI). Sex and BMI were identified as significant fixed effects in multivariable models. Intraindividual variability was 41%, lower than previously reported (94%). No significant impact of diurnal variation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enriched in the liver, acting as a mechanism-based biomarker of hepatocellular injury and regeneration; potential liver-specific alternative to ALT.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Establishing healthy reference intervals in human volunteers, assessing intra- and interindividual variability and diurnal variation, and identifying the effect of sex and BMI on serum levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential to improve DILI prediction and hepatic regeneration assessment. Reference intervals should account for sex and BMI for accurate diagnostic interpretation and clinical use.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma (circulating), Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs), U937 human monocytic cells, THP-1 human monocytic cells, miR-134 over-expressing cells

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in active disease, lower after effective treatment/remission, up-regulated by TLR3 activation
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was positively correlated with AOSD activity scores and significantly decreased after effective treatment/clinical remission (mean ± SEM, 5.30 ± 2.19 vs. 0.84 ± 0.56, P < 0.05). Significantly higher levels in active AOSD plasma (128.60 ± 47.72 fold) compared to healthy controls (5.25 ± 2.26 fold) (P < 0.01), and active AOSD (mean 6.4-fold) compared to inactive AOSD (mean 2.4-fold, P < 0.01) and controls (mean 0.3-fold, P < 0.001). Upregulated in PBMCs from active AOSD (147.70 ± 28.25 fold) compared to healthy controls (0.53 ± 0.13 fold) (P < 0.0001) and inactive AOSD (1.91 ± 0.44 fold) (P < 0.0001). Higher in active/inactive AOSD plasma/PBMCs compared to SLE patients (P < 0.01 / P < 0.0001). Significantly increased by TLR3 ligand poly (I:C) in PBMCs (3.81 ± 0.09 fold, P < 0.01) and THP-1 cells (1.92 ± 0.11 fold, P < 0.01). document_context_data.document_summary: This scientific roadmap by the Heart Failure Association comprehensively addresses the complex and heterogeneous nature of fibrosis in heart failure, aiming to improve its definition, quantification, and treatment. It reviews mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis across various etiologies like pressure overload, aging, and cardiomyopathies, emphasizing the central role of TGF-β, collagen deposition, and myofibroblast activity. The document discusses challenges in detecting fibrosis using circulating biomarkers, proposing a framework for assessment and a roadmap for future research to identify individual fibrotic mechanisms, novel therapeutic targets, and diagnostic tools. It also evaluates diverse anti-fibrotic strategies, including pharmacological agents and non-coding RNA-based treatments, highlighting the need for targeted, multi-pathway approaches given the complexity of the fibrotic process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anti-fibrotic therapies for heart failure, including established drugs like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, as well as specific anti-fibrotic agents like pirfenidone. Investigational strategies include targeting the TGF-β pathway (e.g., TGF-β inhibitors, CTGF inhibitors like FG-3019), MAPK pathways (e.g., ERK inhibitors), inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1α), neuregulin-1 administration, Matrix Metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitors, Galectin-3 inhibitors, and non-coding RNA-based treatments (microRNA and long non-coding RNAs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a review document, and as such, no specific therapeutic doses, intensities, or durations are consistently reported for any intervention, nor are dose-response comparisons detailed. While some agents like Pirfenidone and non-coding RNA modulators show utility in experimental models and clinical trials (e.g., microRNA-21 inhibitor in a Phase II trial), precise quantitative dosage or detailed treatment parameters are generally absent, reflecting a discussion of general approaches and their limitations, including a noted 'lack of precision' in current therapies. For example, MMP-12i was given 3h post-MI, but without specific dosage.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Ubiquitously expressed; clinical trial specifically in kidney fibrosis patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An inhibitor of microRNA-21 is effective in animal and clinical studies, currently in a phase II trial for kidney fibrosis. Specific quantification of effect not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Non-coding RNA playing crucial roles in the regulation of the cardiac fibroblast phenotype.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-coding RNA-based treatment strategies for fibrosis, specifically kidney fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its inhibition is a promising therapeutic strategy for fibrosis, despite its ubiquitous expression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated global microRNA (miRNA) profiles in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) primary tumor specimens to identify and validate prognostic biomarkers for disease progression, recurrence, and survival. It identified a signature of miR-652-5p and miR-7-2-3p, along with miR-3925-3p and miR-219b-3p, as significantly downregulated in Stage I progressors. Specifically, lower expression of miR-652-5p and miR-7-2-3p correlated with diminished overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with locally advanced EAC, indicating their potential as prognostic markers for tumor aggressiveness and personalized therapeutic management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prognostic biomarker identification for personalized cancer care in Esophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focused on biomarker discovery and validation, not therapeutic intervention. Global microRNA profiling was performed using miScript miRNA human miRNome PCR array on 32 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded EAC specimens (discovery set) to identify differentially expressed miRNAs (criteria: >4-fold change, p<0.05). Validation by qRT-PCR was conducted in cohorts of 15 Stage I Non-Progressors, 10 Stage I Progressors, and an independent testing set of 26 Stage II/III EAC patients. Patients in the testing set received standard neoadjuvant chemoradiation (platinum combined with 5-fluorouracil or paclitaxel) followed by surgical resection; however, specific therapeutic dosing details were not elaborated as the study's primary focus was biomarker prognosis. Progression was defined as developing metastatic disease within 3 years, and ROC curve analysis was used to establish miRNA expression thresholds for classification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated human blood-based target gene-miRNA associations in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) to identify potential protective mechanisms. Through transcriptome analysis of human blood samples (whole blood and PBMCs) from 12 ARHL patients and 12 normal hearing controls, and in vitro experiments on HEI-OC-1 cells, the study identified molecular changes. It confirmed the upregulation of IFNG in ARHL patients and demonstrated that miR-409-3p is significantly downregulated in ARHL and inversely correlates with IFNG. miR-409-3p was shown to downregulate both IFNG and p16 expression in vitro, a mechanism that promotes cell apoptosis and suppresses proliferation, suggesting a protective role for miR-409-3p in ARHL pathogenesis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Investigation of molecular mechanisms in age-related hearing loss (ARHL), involving an observational comparison of ARHL patients and normal hearing controls, complemented by in vitro cell treatments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved an observational comparison between 12 ARHL patients and 12 normal hearing controls for gene and miRNA expression profiles. In vitro experiments on HEI-OC-1 cells included treatments with IFN-γ and miR-409-3p, but specific doses or dose-response comparisons for these cell treatments were not detailed. No specific therapeutic doses or durations were applied to human subjects, as the study focused on mechanistic analysis and target identification.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human blood (whole blood, PBMCs), HEI-OC-1 cells

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly lower in ARHL patients (inversely correlated with IFNG); upregulated in senescent endothelial progenitor cells.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated (* p < 0.05) in whole blood and HEI-OC-1 cells from ARHL patients compared to normal hearing controls. Its overexpression downregulates IFNG and p16 expression. Concurrent upregulation with miR-30a-5p can replicate cellular senescence.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulates gene expression by possessing a binding site in the 3'UTR of IFNG, leading to the downregulation of IFNG and p16 signaling. This promotes cell apoptosis, suppresses proliferation, and is involved in cellular senescence. It also functions as a negative regulator of angiogenesis by targeting PPP2CA.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Significantly downregulated in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) patients, showing an inverse correlation with IFNG. It directly regulates IFNG and p16 expression in HEI-OC-1 cells and is implicated in cellular senescence and hearing loss pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Plays a significant role in ARHL pathogenesis and serves as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for human aging and hearing loss. Its downregulation is associated with ARHL, and its regulatory role suggests a protective mechanism by influencing inflammation, apoptosis, and cellular senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the potential of extracellular vesicles (EVs) and EV-encapsulated microRNAs, specifically miR-451a, as circulating biomarkers for breast cancer, addressing challenges in their quantification. It details the methods for establishing murine breast cancer models and collecting human and murine serum, followed by the isolation and characterization of EVs using techniques such as transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Western blot, and nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA). Key findings include significantly higher total and small EV numbers, and increased miR-451a copies per EV, in human breast cancer patient sera compared to healthy controls, as well as a correlation between serum EV number and tumor burden in murine models. The research highlights the critical importance of direct EV quantification over protein yield for accurate biomarker assessment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker investigation and validation for breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study comparing breast cancer patients and tumor-bearing murine models to healthy controls; no therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were administered or investigated. The focus was on quantifying circulating biomarkers.

In murine models, miR-451a copy numbers ranged from 2.92 × 10^10 to 4.54 × 10^11 copies/mL and showed a moderate correlation between serum EV number and tumour burden (rho = 0.386, p = 0.047). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic and predictive value of a circulating exosomal microRNA (miRNA) panel, specifically comprising miR-21-5p, miR-210-3p, and miR-4639-5p, as non-invasive biomarkers for monitoring post-transplant renal graft function in kidney transplant recipients. The findings demonstrated that these miRNAs were negatively correlated with eGFR and elevated in chronic allograft dysfunction, with the combined three-miRNA panel exhibiting superior diagnostic potential for predicting disease progression and long-term graft function, including future eGFR recovery, compared to individual miRNAs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-transplant renal graft function monitoring using a circulating exosomal miRNA panel
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focused on the monitoring of post-transplant renal graft function using a panel of three exosomal miRNAs (miR-21, miR-210, miR-4639). Plasma samples were collected from 58 kidney transplant recipients and 27 healthy controls at 3 months post-transplantation and during a 1-year longitudinal follow-up (at 3, 6, and 12 months). Renal function was stratified by eGFR levels (<60, 60-90, >=90 mL/min/1.73 m2) to compare chronic allograft dysfunction (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) against normal graft function (eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). No therapeutic dose-response comparisons or specific intervention details related to the transplant procedure were reported.

Significant differences also observed between 60 <= eGFR < 90 and eGFR < 60 (P < .01). AUC = 0.81 for discriminating between chronic allograft dysfunction and normal graft function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the release patterns, time course, and predictive value of circulating microRNAs (miR-499, miR-133a, miR-133b) and cardiac troponin I (cTnI) for perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI) in Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) patients. It concluded that circulating miR-499 is a novel and early biomarker for identifying PMI in cardiac surgery, demonstrating earlier elevation and superior diagnostic accuracy (higher sensitivity and specificity) compared to cTnI, particularly following on-pump CABG surgery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients underwent either on-pump (n=30 in initial phase, n=120 in prospective cohort) or off-pump (n=30) CABG surgery. Serial plasma samples were collected at seven perioperative time points: preoperatively, and 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours after aortic declamping. While no dose-response comparisons for the surgery itself were reported, comparisons were made between on-pump (involving whole heart ischemia-reperfusion) and off-pump (beating heart) procedures, revealing higher miR release in on-pump cases attributed to increased myocardial stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels rapidly increased after aortic declamping, peaking as early as 1-3 hours (e.g., 23-fold higher at 1h, 72-fold higher at 3h, 25-fold higher at 6h post-declamping vs. preoperative control) and then declined, restoring to control by 48h (2-fold, P>0.05). Peak plasma concentrations correlated significantly with cTnI (r = 0.583, P = 0.001). Levels were significantly higher in on-pump vs. off-pump groups (e.g., 72.14±4.62-fold vs. 10.89±7.26-fold at 3h, P<0.001). miR-499 was significantly independently diagnostically associated with PMI (p = 0.002) and had higher sensitivity (85.7%) and specificity (93.3%) than cTnI for PMI prediction, with an AUC of 0.939 (0.880–0.975). A threshold ΔCt value of <18.7477 at 6h indicated PMI risk, with a likelihood ratio of 12.71 (10.8–14.9).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cardiac-specific and enriched microRNA that is important for various biological and pathological processes including cell proliferation, differentiation, and development. It is involved in gene regulation and released from damaged heart or skeletal muscle tissue in response to cardiac injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI) and myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury during and after Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery, encompassing both on-pump and off-pump procedures.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A strong, novel, and early biomarker for identifying and predicting perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI) in the early postoperative period, demonstrating superior sensitivity and specificity compared to cTnI. It indicates the degree and extent of myocardial damage, appears earlier than cTnI, can be an independent risk factor for PMI, and correlates with ejection fraction and peak cTnI, suggesting a broader role in assessing morbidity and mortality risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not responsive to acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients, suggesting distinct mechanisms of circulating miRNAs response to exercise rather than a general response to tissue damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review examines the current understanding of circulating microRNAs (c-miRNAs), including muscle-specific myomiRs, as potential biomarkers for assessing physical performance capacity, training adaptation, early detection of overtraining, and monitoring health-related changes. treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review discusses a wide range of exercise durations and intensities, from acute bouts (e.g., 30 min treadmill running at 80% VO2max, acute cycling ergometer, marathon running, sprint interval training, acute eccentric exercise) to chronic training programs lasting weeks or months (e.g., 10-day endurance, 12-week endurance, 12-week resistance (5 days/week), 12-week strength, 5 months of resistance). treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased after 1 h recovery (p < 0.05) and remained elevated after 24 h recovery (p < 0.05) following Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) protocol. Displayed a significant negative correlation with Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) (R = -0.33, p = 0.03) and a significant positive correlation with Interleukin-10 (IL-10) (R = 0.42, p = 0.004).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of gene expression mediating biological responses to exercise, with potential roles in energy metabolism, inflammation, and growth factor pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) Resistance Training, particularly during early and prolonged recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential biomarker for monitoring resistance training responses, associated with anti-inflammatory responses and recovery/growth processes, indicating beneficial effects of physical exercise or tissue-remodeling.

It identified miR-193b-5p as a potential diagnostic biomarker, associated with inflammation and immune regulation, and a protective factor against sepsis and septic shock progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification and Disease State Analysis (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved an initial screening cohort of serum exosomal miRNA sequencing on patients with sepsis (n=6), septic shock (n=6), and healthy controls (n=3). This was followed by validation using qRT-PCR in a larger cohort of 90 participants, comprising 30 patients with sepsis, 30 with septic shock, and 30 general surgery patients serving as controls. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours of ICU admission. Comparisons were made between disease groups and controls to identify diagnostic biomarkers and understand disease progression; no specific therapeutic dose or dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed significantly high specificity as a diagnostic or relapse marker in AIH versus NASH, Primary Biliary Cirrhosis, or healthy controls. An EV level > 7.69 copies/µL was associated with a higher risk of relapse.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: most up-regulated miRNA

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Targets CREB1/CREB5-NF-"u03baB signaling; down-regulated in monocytes by opioid-induced immunosuppression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Elagolix treatment for unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Given its role in targeting NF-"u03baB signaling and association with immunosuppression, its up-regulation by elagolix might suggest modulation of inflammatory or immune responses, though its specific role in fertility or endometriosis has not been examined in this context.
