document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated global microRNA (miRNA) profiles in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) primary tumor specimens to identify and validate prognostic biomarkers for disease progression, recurrence, and survival. It identified a signature of miR-652-5p and miR-7-2-3p, along with miR-3925-3p and miR-219b-3p, as significantly downregulated in Stage I progressors. Specifically, lower expression of miR-652-5p and miR-7-2-3p correlated with diminished overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with locally advanced EAC, indicating their potential as prognostic markers for tumor aggressiveness and personalized therapeutic management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prognostic biomarker identification for personalized cancer care in Esophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focused on biomarker discovery and validation, not therapeutic intervention. Global microRNA profiling was performed using miScript miRNA human miRNome PCR array on 32 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded EAC specimens (discovery set) to identify differentially expressed miRNAs (criteria: >4-fold change, p<0.05). Validation by qRT-PCR was conducted in cohorts of 15 Stage I Non-Progressors, 10 Stage I Progressors, and an independent testing set of 26 Stage II/III EAC patients. Patients in the testing set received standard neoadjuvant chemoradiation (platinum combined with 5-fluorouracil or paclitaxel) followed by surgical resection; however, specific therapeutic dosing details were not elaborated as the study's primary focus was biomarker prognosis. Progression was defined as developing metastatic disease within 3 years, and ROC curve analysis was used to establish miRNA expression thresholds for classification.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Esophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC) primary tumor tissue (tumor epithelial cells from FFPE specimens, isolated by LCM or from endoscopic biopsy prior to therapy)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: MicroRNA Expression Level (quantified by miRNA microarrays and validated by qRT-PCR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated in Stage I Progressors compared to Stage I Non-Progressors (qRT-PCR p-value = .045). Lower expression was associated with statistically significant differences in Overall Survival (OS, p-value = .0356) and Progression-Free Survival (PFS, p-value = .00771). Optimal cut-off RQ value was 14.00. Non-progressors with higher miR-652-5p expression had a median survival advantage of at least 23 months.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Post-transcriptional gene regulation influencing cancer-relevant processes such as differentiation, proliferation, migration, and apoptosis. Predicted to target VHL, JUN, GAB1, and VEGFA, key players in cancer pathways including proteoglycans in cancer and TNF signaling. Functionally relevant to EAC progression and carcinogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Locally advanced Esophageal Adenocarcinoma (EAC) progression and recurrence in Stage I and resectable Stage II/III EAC patients (post-resection).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a promising prognostic marker for recurrence, diminished overall survival, and progression-free survival in patients with locally advanced EAC, indicating tumor aggressiveness and guiding therapeutic management. Predicts disease recurrence and provides survival benefit for classifying patients as Progressors or Non-Progressors.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. It further characterized 56 proteins with sustained changes, linking them to cardiometabolic traits and responses to a 20-week aerobic exercise training program. The research aimed to biochemically characterize acute exercise protein kinetics, finding enrichment for coagulation-related proteins post-exercise and MYC targets, and noting both concordant and discordant protein responses between acute and chronic exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute treadmill exercise and chronic aerobic exercise training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise consisted of symptom-limited treadmill stress testing in 75 middle-aged adults, following a standard Bruce protocol with plasma protein quantification at baseline, peak exercise (mean 90% predicted peak heart rate, 9.6 METs), and 1-hour post-exercise. Chronic exercise involved a 20-week aerobic training program with three sessions per week, with intensity and duration gradually increased based on individual VO2max. Acute exercise intensity and duration varied, making it difficult to effectively analyze specific exertion thresholds or dose-response comparisons for the acute protocol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels predict the risk of rehospitalization across all heart failure subgroups, suggesting ongoing hemodynamic stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery (VO2Rec) measures, especially VO2T12.5% (time to recover 12.5% of peak VO2), in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. The study suggests its regular inclusion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated systemic metabolic alterations in early Parkinson's disease (PD), focusing on the thyroid-liver axis, dysautonomia, and fatty acid beta-oxidation. It utilized nuclear medicine techniques (MIBG scintigraphy, DaT-SPECT) in 1,158 PD patients, combined with trans-omic analyses (serum exosome miRNA transcriptome and plasma metabolome) in de novo PD patients, and in vitro cell experiments. Key findings include sympathetic denervation of the thyroid and heart correlating with disease severity, decreased thyroxine levels, insufficient fatty acid β-oxidation, and enrichment of the PPARα axis. The research identified significantly altered exosomal miRNAs and demonstrated the association of thyroid hormone with PPARα-dependent β-oxidation regulation and enhanced mitochondrial function in muscle cells, suggesting disorganized interorgan communication as a sensitive diagnostic biomarker.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Diagnostic Study of Parkinson's Disease Pathophysiology; In vitro Hormonal Stimulation and RNA-interference.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved observational investigation and diagnostic imaging (MIBG scintigraphy, 123I-ioflupane-dopamine transporter (DaT)-SPECT) on Parkinson's disease patients; no therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were conducted on human subjects. For mechanistic insights, in vitro experiments were performed on cultured HepG2 and primary human skeletal myotubular cells, stimulated with 100 nM 3,3′,5-triiodo-L-thyronine (T3). siRNA oligonucleotides were transfected into HepG2 cells and myotubes, with experiments conducted 48 hours post-transfection. While T3 treatment showed an 'almost dose-dependent' effect on CPT1A expression in HepG2 cells, specific concentrations for siRNA knockdown were not provided, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the overall observational study or the siRNA interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) levels and inflammasome gene expression in monocytes from patients with septic shock caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, comparing them to healthy controls. The findings indicated that while the expression of main inflammasome genes was largely comparable between septic shock patients and healthy controls, circulating mtDNA levels were significantly elevated in septic shock patients, with even higher levels observed in those who died in the ICU. The study suggests that mtDNA could serve as an early prognostic marker for severity in septic shock from MDR pathogens.

The median SOFA score at ICU admission for patients was 11. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was applied or investigated; the study focused solely on characterizing the disease state and biomarker levels. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proteogenomic study investigated Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) samples from adult and pediatric patients at diagnosis, relapse, and primary resistance to identify underlying molecular characteristics. It revealed that AML relapse is consistently associated with reprogrammed energy metabolism, marked by increased mitochondrial ribosomal proteins and respiratory chain complex subunits, and a distinctive pro-inflammatory proteomic signature with higher granzymes and lower CR1/CD35. The analysis also identified increased levels of RNA splicing-related proteins, novel peptides, single amino acid alterations, and fusion peptides, highlighting potential new biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets for improving AML treatment and patient survival.

Comparisons were made between different disease states (diagnosis vs. relapse/primary resistance), but no specific therapeutic interventions or dose-response relationships for a particular therapy were evaluated or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Proteomic screening of skeletal muscle biopsies revealed UA upregulated pathways associated with mitochondria and proteins associated with mitochondrial protein-containing complexes (no specific quantification provided beyond 'upregulated').

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulation of mitochondrial health and function, including mitochondrial biogenesis and quality control.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 4 weeks of UA supplementation during short-term intensified training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved mitochondrial quality control and function, which may contribute to enhanced recovery and performance through alternative mechanisms.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in myoblasts grown in presence of serum from severe ME/CFS patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proteogenomic study investigated Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) samples from adult and pediatric patients at diagnosis, relapse, and primary resistance to identify underlying molecular characteristics. It revealed that AML relapse is consistently associated with reprogrammed energy metabolism, marked by increased mitochondrial ribosomal proteins and respiratory chain complex subunits, and a distinctive pro-inflammatory proteomic signature with higher granzymes and lower CR1/CD35. The analysis also identified increased levels of RNA splicing-related proteins, novel peptides, single amino acid alterations, and fusion peptides, highlighting potential new biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets for improving AML treatment and patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteogenomic profiling and comparative analysis of disease states
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is an observational proteogenomic analysis that investigated molecular changes associated with disease progression and resistance to current AML treatment strategies. It included unbiased, mass spectrometry-based analysis (HiRIEF LC-MS) of 119 proteomes (diagnosis, n=42; relapse, n=71; primary resistant, n=6) from 47 adult and 22 pediatric R/PR AML cases, including 38 patient-matched diagnosis-relapse pairs. Comparisons were made between different disease states (diagnosis vs. relapse/primary resistance), but no specific therapeutic interventions or dose-response relationships for a particular therapy were evaluated or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Enriched and showed higher abundance at relapse in both adult and pediatric AML. 88% of significantly altered proteins with increased abundance at relapse were mitochondria-associated. Specifically, 238 (adult) and 593 (pediatric) proteins were significantly altered (P < 0.05), with 166 (adult) and 321 (pediatric) showing higher abundance. 59 of 67 common differentially expressed proteins between adults and children were mitochondria-associated, all higher at relapse, and verified by immunoblotting.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reprogrammed and dysregulated energy metabolism with increased energy demand in relapsed AML cells, contributing to disease progression and treatment resistance; represents a potential therapeutic target.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Markers of mitophagy (Phosphorylated Parkin Ser65 site)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: UA led to a medium effect for increased markers of mitophagy (d = − 0.74), though not statistically significant for general markers. A significant time × treatment effect was detected for phosphorylated Parkin (Ser65 site) between groups (p = 0.019), but individual changes were not statistically significant (p = 0.098, d = − 0.74).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mitochondrial autophagy (mitophagy), a process for removing damaged mitochondria to maintain cellular health and quality control.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 4 weeks of UA supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a potential upregulation of mitophagy and improved mitochondrial quality control with UA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This surveillance report details malaria cases in the United States in 2018, reporting a 15.6% decrease in confirmed cases from 2017 while noting an overall increase since 1972, with 98.1% being imported cases predominantly from Africa and P. falciparum as the most common species. It describes comprehensive surveillance methodologies, diagnostic tests, and molecular analyses for antimalarial drug resistance markers, particularly for P. falciparum against pyrimethamine, sulfadoxine, chloroquine, and mefloquine, with no resistance markers for atovaquone or artemisinin. The report also investigates chemoprophylaxis adherence (found to be poor), treatment patterns for uncomplicated and severe malaria, and emphasizes the critical importance of prompt diagnosis, appropriate treatment with CDC guidelines, and continuous surveillance to prevent local transmission.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Malaria prevention (chemoprophylaxis, including Tafenoquine), diagnosis (microscopy, PCR, RDTs), and treatment for both uncomplicated and severe malaria (oral antimalarials like atovaquone-proguanil, artemether-lumefantrine, quinine; parenteral IV artesunate for severe malaria), alongside molecular surveillance for antimalarial drug resistance.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Chemoprophylaxis adherence was poor among U.S. residents with imported malaria in 2018, with 24.5% reporting use and 95.0% demonstrating non-adherence or inconsistent regimens, often due to forgetting or prematurely stopping. Tafenoquine offers an abbreviated schedule for eligible adults. For treatment, IV artesunate became the first-line for severe malaria in April 2019, replacing IV quinidine gluconate, though 52.1% of severe cases in 2018 did not receive guideline-appropriate treatment. Uncomplicated malaria treatments varied, with 91.7% receiving appropriate care, and primaquine was often used for P. vivax/P. ovale relapse prevention, though sometimes inappropriately. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported, but treatment choice was emphasized based on species, severity, patient factors (e.g., pregnancy), and CDC guidelines.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Patient specimens (clinical diagnosis and laboratory confirmation) in the United States

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 17 cases (1.1% of malaria cases) with mixed species were reported in 2018, with 82.4% PCR confirmed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Co-infection with multiple malaria parasite species, potentially complicating diagnosis and treatment due to varied clinical presentations and drug sensitivities.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Malaria surveillance in the United States, 2018, with species identification.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates complex malaria infections which may necessitate broader-spectrum treatments or more intensive monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Riociguat (Drug Treatment)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients with early treatment-naïve diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis were randomized to receive riociguat (n=60) or placebo (n=61) for 52 weeks. Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The primary endpoint, change in mRSS from baseline to week 52, did not significantly improve with riociguat vs placebo (P = 0.08). Mean mRSS was 16.8 (±3.7) at baseline, changing to 14.6 (±6.6) in the riociguat group and 15.7 (±10.5) in the placebo group at week 52.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Clinical indicator of skin thickness, fibrosis, and overall disease severity in systemic sclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial) from baseline to week 52.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects skin fibrosis and disease progression. While not statistically significant for the primary endpoint, a numerical decrease was observed with riociguat.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document outlines the protocol for the PROSAP-A randomized controlled trial, investigating the effects of preoperative insomnia treatment (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia or Sleep Education Therapy) on acute and long-term postoperative pain control, brain health, and physical recovery in patients undergoing total knee or hip arthroplasty. The study aims to assess various patient-reported outcomes (e.g., opioid use, quality of recovery, sleep, mood, quality of life), objective measures (e.g., actigraphic sleep, quantitative sensory testing for pain, neurocognitive function), and blood biomarkers (e.g., inflammatory, monoamine, genetic mediators) across preoperative and postoperative phases to determine the impact on pain intensity, opioid use, sleep quality, mental health, and functional recovery. The document also details the recruitment, randomization, blinding, and data collection plans for this prehabilitation approach.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Preoperative Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) and Sleep Education Therapy (SET) as an active comparator.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Both interventions are delivered over 4 weeks in a hybrid format, comprising a digital self-guided platform and weekly telehealth video sessions (up to 60 minutes). CBT-I sessions are conducted with a psychologist and include sleep restriction and stimulus control, while SET sessions are with a research nurse. A video-assisted booster session is provided 1-2 weeks postoperatively. No dose-response comparisons are reported as these are fixed intervention protocols.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not yet reported; proposed to respond to CBT-I.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not yet quantified; subject of future study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproducts of monoamine neurotransmitter metabolism, reflecting neurotransmitter activity; mediate the association of sleep and pain, contributing to pathophysiology when sleep is disturbed.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Relevant to pathways involved in pain and sleep processes, particularly in the context of preoperative sleep disturbance and sleep restoration via CBT-I in patients preparing for hip or knee arthroplasty.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of neurotransmitter system activity, potentially associated with pain, mood, and sleep regulation; proposed to predict postoperative pain and functional trajectories.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inhibited (no specific quantification provided).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme responsible for the breakdown of monoamine neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine), influencing mood, motivation, and fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation, particularly the action of its phenylethanoid glycosides and oligosaccharides, regulating neurotransmission and mitigating fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Inhibition leads to higher dopamine levels, improved neurotransmitter balance, enhanced neuromuscular coordination, and reduced central fatigue/anxiety, benefiting athletic performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the ability of human decidua basalis mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (DBMSCs) to protect human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) from oxidative stress and inflammation induced by hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and monocytes. The research examined various endothelial cell functions, including proliferation, adhesion, and migration, alongside monocyte adhesion and proliferation, as well as the expression of adhesion molecules and antioxidant enzymes. The findings suggest DBMSCs possess therapeutic potential for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis by shielding endothelial cells from oxidative stress-induced damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro co-culture with Human Decidua Basalis Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells (DBMSCs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC, passages 3-5) were exposed to 100 µM H2O2 for 48 hours. DBMSCs (passage 3) were co-cultured with HUVEC using three distinct methods: conditioned medium (CMDBMSC, at 1%, 5%, and 25% v/v concentrations), secretome-free direct contact (SFDBMSC, via a transwell system), and intercellular direct contact (ICDBMSC). Co-culture ratios of HUVEC to DBMSC included 1:1, 5:1, and 10:1, with a 5HUVEC:1DBMSC ratio specifically for SFDBMSC and ICDBMSC systems. Monocytes (THP-1) were also co-cultured with DBMSCs at ratios of 2.5:1, 5:1, 10:1, and 20:1 (THP-1:DBMSC), and with HUVEC at similar ratios. Experiments were primarily conducted over 48 hours, with effects often measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours. Mitomycin C at 25 µg/ml was used to inhibit cell proliferation in some experiments. No specific dose-response comparisons for DBMSCs were explicitly reported for all measured effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Endothelial cells (HUVEC) and monocytes (THP-1) in co-culture

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced (P < 0.05) adhesion of H2O2-treated monocytes to HUVEC after culturing with H2O2-untreated (UDBMSC) or H2O2-pretreated (TDBMSC) DBMSCs, indicating an inhibitory effect on monocyte adhesion to endothelial cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates cellular interactions and inflammatory responses; immune cell recruitment to sites of inflammation/injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: DBMSCs co-culture in the presence of H2O2, mitigating monocyte adhesion to HUVEC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a protective effect against inflammation and vascular damage by reducing monocyte infiltration, relevant for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Concentration; Chemokine Level; Cytokine/Chemokine Panel (Protein Level)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in all dengue cases compared with healthy subjects. Higher in acute febrile phase of dengue patients compared to healthy controls (P < 0.05), showing a borderline significant increase in acute dengue compared with healthy. Positively correlated with IFN-γ, MIP-1β, RANTES, IL-15, and MIG.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Antivirus-associated chemokine, plays a role in defending against DENV infection and recruiting monocytes, macrophages, and other immune cells to sites of inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute febrile phase of dengue infection (healthy controls, dengue patients); correlated with other cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of immune response against DENV infection and a biomarker for dengue severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed the greatest separation between latent class analysis classes in LeoPARDS. Significantly higher in SRS1 than SRS2 (FDR <0.05) in both GAinS and VANISH.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine, mediates immune cell recruitment, particularly monocytes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis patient classification via latent class analysis in LeoPARDS, and comparison between SRS1 and SRS2 subphenotypes in GAinS and VANISH.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation is associated with worse survival in sepsis (lowest in latent class analysis class 3 in LeoPARDS with 47% survival, and class 2 in VANISH with 66% survival). Indicates a pro-inflammatory state (SRS1 subphenotype).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell (UC-MSC) transplantation combined with conventional anti-viral treatment (antibiotic therapy, dexamethasone).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Triple intravenous infusion of UC-MSC at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/kg, administered on days 0, 3, and 6. The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma; conditioned media from PBMC and UC-MSC/PBMC cultures (in vitro)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged in vivo, increased in vitro
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma concentrations did not differ significantly between the MSC and Control groups overall. Levels positively correlated with total score of CT on weeks 8 (r = 0.471, p ≤ 0.005) and 48 (r = 0.499, p ≤ 0.005). Levels increased slightly during the first week but remained unchanged until day 28 in the MSC group. In vitro, a significant increase was observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine that recruits monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells to sites of inflammation and infection.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19 patients after MSC transplantation; PBMC co-cultured with UC-MSC in vitro.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with lung damage and inflammatory response; stabilized levels in vivo suggest a controlled inflammatory process, while increased levels in vitro reflect immunomodulatory effects promoting inflammatory signaling.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Uniquely correlated with C12FDG++ PBMCs in females (r=0.4737; p=0.0002) and significantly decreased after fisetin usage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy human participants (age range 20–82 years), association with peripheral senescence (C12FDG++ PBMCs) with sexually dimorphic correlations, and response to senolytic treatment (fisetin).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between iron status and renal outcomes, specifically progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), in 111 pre-dialysis patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven Diabetic Nephropathy (DN). It found that reduced serum transferrin is an independent predictor of ESRD, and identified increased iron and transferrin deposition in renal tubular epithelial cells of DN patients, suggesting a pathological role for altered iron metabolism in disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the prognostic value of iron status and related biomarkers in Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) progression.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed baseline serum iron status markers (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin, TSAT) and their association with progression to End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in 111 Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) patients with biopsy-proven DN. Serum markers were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, immunoradiometric assay, and colorimetric methods. Additionally, histological analysis involved immunohistochemical staining for transferrin and Perl's blue staining for iron in kidney biopsy specimens from DN patients and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or active treatments were investigated; the study focused on correlation and predictive value.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased transferrin upregulated monocyte chemoattractant peptide-1 expression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemokine that regulates the migration and infiltration of monocytes/macrophages, key players in inflammation and tissue injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: In vitro study of cultured proximal tubular cells, possibly reflecting direct effect of transferrin on renal cells in DN.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Upregulation is associated with recruitment of inflammatory cells and can contribute to cell death, indicating a mechanism of renal injury by transferrin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of CDH1, CDH2, MCP-1, and PAI-1 mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles (EVs) for predicting early-stage diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main findings indicate that CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression in blood EVs was significantly downregulated with the development of DN (overt and incipient stages) compared to diabetic patients without DN, suggesting a renoprotective effect and their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Raised significantly after each exercise bout.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the systemic innate immune response, specifically focusing on neutrophil phenotypes, as biomarkers to monitor exercise-induced immune changes during repetitive, prolonged walking over consecutive days (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches). It found that prolonged exercise leads to an initial systemic innate immune response, characterized by the mobilization and activation of various neutrophil phenotypes, followed by adaptation or partial normalization in subsequent days. Crucially, increased neutrophil activation, marked by high CD11b expression, was consistently associated with impaired physical feeling, slower walking speed, and a higher degree of physiological stress, suggesting its potential as a valuable marker for monitoring immune system changes and detecting overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive prolonged walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in prolonged walking over 3 consecutive days as part of a public walking event (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches), covering 30, 40, or 50 km/day at a self-selected pace. Exercise intensity on day 1 averaged 65% of maximum heart rate. While the study involved varying distances, no explicit dose-response comparisons for immune markers were reported between different daily distances. However, increased neutrophil activation (high CD11b expression) was associated with slower walking speeds (approx. 4.1-4.2 km/h across days) and predominantly occurred in participants walking 30 km (66% of this group).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased from 0.35 (0.26–0.34) × 10^6 /ml at baseline to 0.41 (0.23–0.56) × 10^6 /ml after 1 day (P < 0.005). Decreased to 0.24 (0.17–0.32) × 10^6 /ml on day 3 (P < 0.0001 vs Day 1).
