document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates targeting RARA overexpression with tamibarotene, a selective RARα agonist, in combination with azacitidine in newly diagnosed unfit non-APL acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) patients. It demonstrates that RARA-positive patients respond significantly better to tamibarotene plus azacitidine, achieving high complete remission rates, rapid response onset, and improved survival. The study also explores RARA overexpression's association with monocytic features and its link to venetoclax resistance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tamibarotene plus azacitidine combination therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In a phase 2 clinical study (NCT02807558), azacitidine was administered at 75 mg/m2 (intravenously or subcutaneously) daily on days 1-7, followed by oral tamibarotene at 6 mg/m2 per day (divided doses twice daily) on days 8-28, with each treatment cycle lasting 28 days. This combination was evaluated in 51 newly diagnosed unfit AML patients (22 RARA-positive, 29 RARA-negative). The treatment was generally well tolerated, with myelosuppression rates comparable to azacitidine monotherapy. Hypertriglyceridemia was a frequent, manageable, and reversible high-grade nonhematologic adverse event. No dose-response comparisons were reported for tamibarotene plus azacitidine. For comparative context, azacitidine monotherapy showed similar complete remission rates in RARA-high and RARA-low patients, and venetoclax resistance was evaluated in ex vivo samples without specific dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly associated with estimated subphenotypes (p < 0.05 after correction for multiple testing), but specific change direction/magnitude not detailed for this individual protein.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates protein involvement in patient subphenotype classification, which may relate to prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked increase in total content at 1 day and 3 days after TBI (p < 0.001) compared to sham.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A neutrophil enzyme associated with inflammatory response and NET formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neutrophil activity and inflammation in the brain after TBI.

The most important one and relevant one for this particular study is the U-shaped association between MPO (Myeloperoxidase) Levels and Anxiety Risk: A Cross-sectional Study in a Chinese Population. In this investigation, researchers explored how the amounts of MPO, a substance involved in inflammation, relate to the likelihood of experiencing anxiety in a specific group of Chinese adults. They discovered a unique 'U-shaped' pattern, meaning that both very low and very high levels of MPO were linked to a higher risk of anxiety. This indicates that having MPO levels in the middle range might be more protective against anxiety compared to being at either extreme. This finding is significant because it suggests that MPO could be a valuable indicator for predicting who might be at higher risk for anxiety, especially within the Chinese population, and potentially lead to new strategies for preventing anxiety that are guided by these biological markers. The study also highlighted the role of diabetes as an effect modifier, indicating that individuals with diabetes might have an even greater risk of anxiety when their MPO levels are elevated. Additionally, some texts mention the existence of other potential biomarkers for GAD like IL-17A and IL-23A, which showed superior predictive power compared to MPO in identifying anxiety in clinical settings.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Heme-containing peroxidase expressed by myeloid cells, it mediates inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and activates neuroinflammatory processes. It is a regulator of innate immune responses, contributing to neutrophil antibacterial activity and defense against pathogens, and is implicated in chronic inflammatory diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study in a large observational cohort of 30,418 Chinese adults undergoing routine health examinations, investigating the U-shaped association between plasma MPO levels and anxiety risk. Diabetes mellitus was identified as a significant effect modifier, exacerbating MPO-related anxiety risk, particularly relevant to neuroinflammatory responses. Other proinflammatory cytokines (IL-17A, IL-23A) were also mentioned in the context of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential neuroinflammatory biomarker for anxiety risk stratification and personalized interventions, especially in diabetic populations where it suggests synergistic neuroinflammatory pathways. Moderate MPO levels (around 30 ng/mL) may be optimal for neuroimmune homeostasis; both very low and very high plasma concentrations are associated with increased anxiety risk. It serves as an early warning indicator for anxiety risk, linking subclinical immune activation to disease development, though its standalone diagnostic precision is limited. IL-17A and IL-23A show promising predictive power for GAD, potentially surpassing MPO in clinical identification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood Serum (healthy cohort); Gastric Adenocarcinoma (GA) tissue (TCGA cohort)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In healthy cohort: inversely associated with PGR (\u03b2 = -0.009, P < 0.0001) and PGI (\u03b2 = -0.057, P < 0.0001). Non-linear associations and stronger effects among hypertensive individuals, smokers, and alcohol consumers. Threshold effects at MPO=24 ng/mL: Below 24 ng/mL, MPO increase associated with PGR decrease (\u03b2 = -0.089, P < 0.0001), PGI decrease (\u03b2 = -0.244, P < 0.0001), and PGII increase (\u03b2 = 0.091, P < 0.0001). Above 24 ng/mL, MPO increase associated with PGR decrease (\u03b2 = -0.003, P = 0.0032), PGI decrease (\u03b2 = -0.043, P < 0.0001), and PGII effect not significant (\u03b2 = -0.003, P = 0.1642). Each unit increase in continuous MPO associated with higher risk of PGR >3 (HR=1.003, P=0.033). Highest MPO quartile (Q4) showed nearly doubled risk (HR=1.989, P=0.00002) for PGR >3 vs Q1. In GA cohort: High MPO expression was an independent predictor of poor Overall Survival (OS) (HR = 2.781, P = 0.002, also HR = 1.43, P = 0.037) and Disease-Specific Survival (DSS) (HR = 3.667, P < 0.001, also HR = 1.67, P = 0.020), and Progression-Free Interval (PFI) (HR = 1.63, P = 0.008). Positively correlated with immune cell infiltration: macrophages (R = 0.379, P < 0.001) and dendritic cells (R = 0.377, P < 0.001). Also correlated with complement cascade, immune regulation, GPCR-related pathways, and inversely with mitochondrial protein import and oxidative phosphorylation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key enzyme in immune responses and oxidative stress, part of innate immune defense, mediates inflammation, promotes tumorigenesis and cancer progression by oxidizing DNA and creating a mutagenic environment, regulates tumor growth, metastasis, and immune-epithelial crosstalk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Healthy individuals in association with gastric mucosal injury markers; Gastric Adenocarcinoma (GA) patients in the TCGA cohort for prognostic significance and immune-regulatory mechanisms, including H. pylori-induced gastritis models and populations with smoking, alcohol consumption, or hypertension.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with markers of gastric mucosal damage, suggesting a role in gastric physiology and health status; prognostic biomarker for gastric adenocarcinoma, linked to immune dysregulation and poor survival; indicates immune cell activity in the tumor microenvironment; potential therapeutic target and monitoring biomarker for gastric mucosal injury and gastric cancer; the 24 ng/ml threshold provides a reference for clinical assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated compared with the whey and placebo groups after long-term (4-9 weeks) soy protein supplementation. However, in another context, increased in both whey and training-alone groups, but there were no significant differences with the SP group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in inflammatory responses and oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Long-term (4-9 weeks) soy protein supplementation in trained weightlifters; after training, comparing whey protein, training-alone, and SP groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects reduced inflammation and oxidative stress in some long-term contexts, but no significant difference in others.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scientific roadmap by the Heart Failure Association comprehensively addresses the complex and heterogeneous nature of fibrosis in heart failure, aiming to improve its definition, quantification, and treatment. It reviews mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis across various etiologies like pressure overload, aging, and cardiomyopathies, emphasizing the central role of TGF-β, collagen deposition, and myofibroblast activity. The document discusses challenges in detecting fibrosis using circulating biomarkers, proposing a framework for assessment and a roadmap for future research to identify individual fibrotic mechanisms, novel therapeutic targets, and diagnostic tools. It also evaluates diverse anti-fibrotic strategies, including pharmacological agents and non-coding RNA-based treatments, highlighting the need for targeted, multi-pathway approaches given the complexity of the fibrotic process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anti-fibrotic therapies for heart failure, including established drugs like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, as well as specific anti-fibrotic agents like pirfenidone. Investigational strategies include targeting the TGF-β pathway (e.g., TGF-β inhibitors, CTGF inhibitors like FG-3019), MAPK pathways (e.g., ERK inhibitors), inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1α), neuregulin-1 administration, Matrix Metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitors, Galectin-3 inhibitors, and non-coding RNA-based treatments (microRNA and long non-coding RNAs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a review document, and as such, no specific therapeutic doses, intensities, or durations are consistently reported for any intervention, nor are dose-response comparisons detailed. While some agents like Pirfenidone and non-coding RNA modulators show utility in experimental models and clinical trials (e.g., microRNA-21 inhibitor in a Phase II trial), precise quantitative dosage or detailed treatment parameters are generally absent, reflecting a discussion of general approaches and their limitations, including a noted 'lack of precision' in current therapies. For example, MMP-12i was given 3h post-MI, but without specific dosage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 'Myofibroblast persistence' is described as leading to non-resolving and progressive fibrosis. The termination of the reparative phase is identified by the disappearance of activated myofibroblasts; therefore, their persistence beyond this phase is indicative of pathology. No specific quantification provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Produce extracellular matrix components, contribute to tissue repair and fibrosis. Termination of reparative phase involves their disappearance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chronic fibrotic response in heart failure, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Leads to non-resolving and progressive fibrosis, contributing to organ damage and failure when persistence occurs beyond physiological healing.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Premature senescence of myofibroblasts was identified as an essential anti-fibrotic mechanism, implying that a lack or impairment of this process contributes to fibrosis. No specific quantification provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cellular process that can limit fibroblast activation and proliferation, thus acting as an anti-fibrotic mechanism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myocardial fibrosis in response to pressure overload.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An essential anti-fibrotic mechanism; its impairment or insufficiency contributes to pathological fibrosis, suggesting it as a potential therapeutic target.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Manuelle Synthese: Myogenic Differentiation 1 (MyoD) wurde in 25751651 gefunden. Die tatsächliche Zusammenfassung muss manuell hinzugefügt werden.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Manuelle Synthese: Hier wuerde die konsolidierte Mechanismus-Zusammenfassung stehen.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Synthese: Hier wuerde die konsolidierte Zuverlaessigkeits-Zusammenfassung stehen.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mesoangioblasts, AdmMABs (shPW1 vs Control), non-competent AdmMAB clones

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower (degraded), Absent (in non-competent clones), Accumulated (with inhibitors), Rescued (with MyoDsp3, Roscovitin), Upregulated (transcripts)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly decreased protein in the absence of PW1/Peg3; degradation occurs in mesoangioblasts when PW1/Peg3 is silenced. MyoD transcripts were present and upregulated during differentiation regardless of short hairpin RNA treatment. Protein is absent in non-competent AdmMAB clones. Inhibition of proteasome or cycE/Cdk2 function led to MyoD protein accumulation in shPW1 AdmMABs. Only MyoDsp3 forced expression led to a complete rescue of terminal myogenic differentiation. Inhibition of CyclinE-cdk2 activity by Roscovitin rescued MyoD protein in growing shPW1 cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key regulator of skeletal muscle differentiation; master transcription factor regulating the myogenic program and terminal differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myogenic differentiation of mesoangioblasts, specifically when PW1/Peg3 expression is silenced, PW1 regulatory pathway, MAB differentiation, sustained cycE expression, inhibition of CyclinE-cdk2 activity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inhibition of mesoangioblast myogenic potential and impaired muscle differentiation. Essential for skeletal muscle differentiation; its degradation impairs myogenesis, indicating dysfunctional MABs and reduced therapeutic efficacy. Its rescue suggests a means to restore MAB therapeutic function.

biomarker_summary.overall_biomarker_summary: Automatischer Platzhalter fuer Myoglobin: Gefunden in 14 Quellen. Manuelle Synthese erforderlich.
biomarker_summary.mechanisms_consensus: Details zu den Mechanismen sind in den 'aggregated_source_findings_DEBUG' enthalten.
biomarker_summary.reliability_consensus: Manuelle Aggregation der Zuverlaessigkeit ueber mehrere Studien noetig.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated circulating myomesin 3 fragments as a novel biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage, finding that plasma levels significantly increased 96 hours after acute eccentric exercise in humans and positively correlated with established muscle damage biomarkers (CK, Mb, LDH) and muscle symptoms (tenderness, DOMS).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Eccentric Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention involved nine healthy males performing 10 sets of 40 repetitions of one-leg calf-raise exercise (total 400 repetitions) with a load corresponding to half their body weight. Ankle ROM was maintained between 20 0 dorsiflexion and 15 0 plantar flexion, at a speed of 60 counts/min (1 repetition/s); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Percent changes positively correlated with myomesin 3 fragments (R = 0.464, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytosolic protein that leaks into the blood following sarcolemma damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute eccentric exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Established biomarker for muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated urinary proteins responsive to acute eccentric calf-raise exercise in healthy males, identifying an N-terminal fragment of titin. The urinary titin fragment significantly increased 96 hours post-exercise and correlated strongly with established blood biomarkers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion), proposing its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Eccentric Calf-Raise Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute, single-leg calf-raise exercise (right leg) involving repetitive eccentric muscle contractions. The protocol consisted of 10 sets of 40 repetitions (total 400 repetitions) with 3-minute rest between sets, performed at 60 counts/min. Ankle joint range of motion was maintained between 20° dorsiflexion and 15° plantar flexion, with an exercise load approximately half the subject's body weight. Samples were collected before and up to 96 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased on and after 48 h after exercise. Positive correlations with urinary titin fragment percentage change at 48 h (r = 0.98, p < 0.01) and 72 h (r = 0.67, p < 0.05). Titin fragment at 48 h correlated with Mb at 72 h (r = 0.88, p < 0.01). Mb at 48 h correlated with DOMS at 48 h (r = 0.94, p < 0.01) and 72 h (r = 0.82, p < 0.05). Mb at 72 h correlated with DOMS at 48 h (r = 0.72, p < 0.05). Negative correlation between percentage changes in Mb at 72 h and torque post exercise (r = -0.75, p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An established marker of muscle damage, indicating muscle cell injury or integrity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After eccentric exercise; exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level; correlated with DOMS and reduced muscle strength.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the release patterns, time course, and predictive value of circulating microRNAs (miR-499, miR-133a, miR-133b) and cardiac troponin I (cTnI) for perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI) in Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) patients. It concluded that circulating miR-499 is a novel and early biomarker for identifying PMI in cardiac surgery, demonstrating earlier elevation and superior diagnostic accuracy (higher sensitivity and specificity) compared to cTnI, particularly following on-pump CABG surgery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients underwent either on-pump (n=30 in initial phase, n=120 in prospective cohort) or off-pump (n=30) CABG surgery. Serial plasma samples were collected at seven perioperative time points: preoperatively, and 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours after aortic declamping. While no dose-response comparisons for the surgery itself were reported, comparisons were made between on-pump (involving whole heart ischemia-reperfusion) and off-pump (beating heart) procedures, revealing higher miR release in on-pump cases attributed to increased myocardial stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Commonly measured due to release of intracellular components into the blood. Time delay between the detection of circulating protein and ischemic damage remains a major problem.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intracellular component released into the blood following myocardial ischemia.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myocardial ischemia during cardiac surgery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of myocardial damage, but limited by time delay in detection.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum myoglobin concentrations increased over the intervention (p=0.027 for time; tendency for increase at T2 relative to T1 overall, p=0.055) regardless of supplementation (p=0.87 for group*time interaction), indicating that BCAA-CHO did not differentially alter serum myoglobin compared to CHO.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle, released into the bloodstream upon muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following three consecutive high-intensity resistance training bouts (barbell back squat protocol).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of muscle damage and integrity; increased levels indicate muscle breakdown, not mitigated by BCAA-CHO supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation on antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, and iron metabolism in rowers subjected to exhaustive exercise. Findings indicate that supplementation significantly strengthened antioxidant potential (TAC) and mitigated exercise-induced increases in pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-alpha), muscle damage indicators (myoglobin), and iron regulatory hormones (hepcidin) in the supplemented group. However, IL-6, ferritin, sTfR, iron, TIBC, and UIBC remained largely unaffected by supplementation or showed exercise-induced changes independent of it.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation combined with strenuous physical exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Athletes received 720 mg of highly-concentrated large cranberry extract daily (two 360-mg capsules, containing 36 mg proanthocyanidins per capsule) for 6 weeks. The control group received dyed gelatin placebo capsules containing flour. Participants performed a 2000-m rowing ergometer test at maximal effort on day 1 (pre-supplementation) and at the end of the 6-week training camp (post-supplementation), with blood samples taken pre-exercise, 1 minute post-exercise, and after a 24-hour recovery. No dose-response comparisons for cranberry extract were reported within the study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum concentration was modulated solely by physical exercise (main effect, p < 0.001). No significant exercise-induced changes were observed in both groups at Trial I. At Trial II (after supplementation), a significant exercise-induced increase was documented solely in the control group. The cranberry-supplemented group showed a lack of post-exercise changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein found in muscle tissue, released into circulation upon muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exhaustive 2000-m rowing ergometer test, with 6-week cranberry supplementation preventing its exercise-induced rise at Trial II.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle damage level; cranberry supplementation mitigated exercise-induced muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Leaks into circulation during muscle damage, peaking 1–3 hours after exercise; released into blood as a short-term marker of damage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle, released into circulation upon muscle cell damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Muscle damage, after exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates short-term muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether aerobic capacity predicts skeletal and cardiac muscle damage in amateur triathletes after a full-distance Ironman. It found that higher aerobic capacity was negatively associated with skeletal muscle damage biomarkers (myoglobin and creatine kinase), but no association was observed with cardiac muscle damage biomarkers (cTnT, MHC-a, NT-proBNP).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Full Distance Ironman Triathlon
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a full distance Ironman triathlon (3.8 km swimming, 180 km cycling, 42.2 km running). These amateur athletes reported training for 11.2  1 3 hours/week and had previously completed a median of 8 ultra-endurance races. Aerobic capacity was assessed one month prior to the event using a 20m shuttle-run test. The study focused on post-race biomarker levels, and no specific dose-response comparisons for varying triathlon distances or intensities were reported, though models using absolute aerobic capacity showed slightly higher predictive power for skeletal muscle damage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Post-race levels typically increase; however, a negative association was found with aerobic capacity. For myoglobin, higher aerobic capacity (mLO2*kg 11*min 11) increased adjusted r2 from 0.026 to 0.210 (F: 8.927, p = 0.005), and in absolute terms (LO2*min 11), adjusted r2 increased from 0.07 to 0.227 (F: 10.386, p = 0.003). Baseline reference < 72  5g/L.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen storage protein in muscle cells, released into circulation upon skeletal muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-full distance Ironman triathlon in amateur triathletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates skeletal muscle damage level; higher aerobic capacity is associated with reduced post-race skeletal muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the effect of oral palmitoylethanolamide (PEA, Levagen+™) on recovery from muscle-damaging leg press exercise in 28 healthy young males. The study found that while PEA supplementation did not significantly reduce perceived muscle soreness, thigh circumference, or most inflammatory and phosphoprotein markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, IL-6, IL-10, hs-CRP, TNF-α, CREB, ERK1/2, JNK, NF-κB, p38 MAPK, S6K1, STAT3, STAT5), it did significantly reduce blood myoglobin and lactate concentrations. Furthermore, PEA increased Protein Kinase B phosphorylation immediately post-exercise, suggesting aid in muscle recovery through improved metabolic efficiency and activation of anabolic/repair signaling pathways from repeat bouts of exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Supplementation with Palmitoylethanolamide (Levagen+™) combined with Resistance Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were randomized to consume either liquid PEA (167.5 mg Levagen+™ containing 150 mg PEA and 17.5 mg excipients, with 832.5 mg maltodextrin) or a matched placebo (1 g maltodextrin). Treatments were administered pre-exercise, immediately post-exercise, 24 h post-exercise, and 48 h post-exercise. The muscle-damaging exercise consisted of four sets of leg press at 80% of one-repetition maximum (1-RM) to volitional exhaustion, with 60s rest between sets, followed by a performance set at 70% 1-RM to maximal repetitions. No dose-response comparisons for PEA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall peak at +1 h post-exercise, but significantly lower for the PEA group than placebo at +1, +2, and +3 h post-exercise (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle tissue, released into circulation upon muscle cell damage (myofibrillar disruption).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Recovery from muscle-damaging leg press exercise to volitional exhaustion, with PEA supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A primary indicator of acute muscle damage; lower levels with PEA suggest a protective effect against exercise-induced muscle damage and aid in recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were unaffected by anserine dose, post-exercise time-course, or interaction effects, remaining within the normal range for healthy active participants (18.5–94.8 ng/mL).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Muscle damage biomarker; oxygen-binding protein found in muscle tissue, released into the bloodstream upon muscle injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Anserine supplementation following an exercise challenge (time to exhaustion).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anserine did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage as measured by myoglobin, suggesting maintained muscle cell integrity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Consistently higher in men (P = 2.34 
												× 10
												–4 in discovery cohort, P = 2.10 
												× 10
												–4 in validation cohort).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle tissue, typically indicates muscle degradation or stress. In this context, it is grouped with markers for vascular remodelling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Higher in men with paroxysmal AF compared to women.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates vascular remodelling in men with paroxysmal AF. Its release may be due to silent ischemia or subclinical coronary artery disease, and it may also reflect higher muscle mass in men. Its elevation with MMP-3 suggests a significant role of vascular remodelling in AF substrate formation in men.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by ~3.5-fold (119  1 21 to 369  1 62 nmol/L; p = .001) in response to the CCombat protocol, remaining elevated during short recovery and returning to pre-exercise levels within 48 hours (long recovery). Showed a high correlation with CK-MB (r s 0.66 10.86) during recovery.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein released from muscle tissue; indicator of muscle integrity and damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol-induced metabolic stress and subsequent short/long recovery periods (up to 48 hours).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates hypermetabolic stress and muscle microinjuries following intensive exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively investigates the potentials, pitfalls, and practical applications of blood-based biomarkers for objective individualized monitoring of training load, recovery, and health status in elite sports. It evaluates the utility and limitations of established markers like creatine kinase (CK), lactate, C-reactive protein (CRP), urea, myoglobin, and various leukocyte populations, detailing their physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise, kinetics, and implications for muscle damage, immune function, and inflammation. The document also addresses methodological considerations, confounding variables, the need for individual reference ranges, and statistical approaches for interpreting biomarker changes, concluding with recommendations for best practices in their sport-specific use.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-based biomarker monitoring in conjunction with physical exercise and training load management in elite sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review focuses on the application and interpretation of blood-based biomarkers for athlete monitoring across various exercise loads, including strenuous, resistance, high-intensity, submaximal, acute physical stress, soccer matches, ultradistance races, and long-term intensive endurance exercise. Biomarker responses are noted to depend on exercise modality, intensity, duration, and individual factors such as ethnicity and body composition. While specific exercise regimens like 30 minutes of endurance running (65% vs 85% of VO2max) showed CRP increases, no single standardized dose-response is consistently reported or compared across all biomarkers. The document emphasizes the need for individual reference levels, standardized collection, and careful consideration of confounding variables, particularly in managing workload by adjusting training when physiological parameters exceed baseline.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 238% increase after a soccer match; seven-fold increase immediately after a 2 × 45-min simulated soccer game; returns to baseline within 12–24 h from circulation due to rapid renal clearance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Intramuscular transport of oxygen by accepting oxygen from hemoglobin and transporting it to sites of oxidation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Physical stress in sports, acute exercise, soccer matches, myocardial infarction.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indirect marker of damage to skeletal muscle due to rapid kinetics; short-term muscle damage marker in acute settings; excessive excretion can lead to kidney damage and kidney failure due to toxic effect on renal tubules.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased post-exercise in all groups (p < 0.001), but no significant trial differences were found between supplementation groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein found in muscle tissue; released into the bloodstream upon muscle injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-2.25 h intensive cycling, following 2-week hemp fiber (high/low dose) or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of muscle damage level; the increase reflects exercise-induced muscle damage, but hemp fiber had no effect on post-exercise muscle damage differences.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of wearing exercise compression stockings (CS) on intramuscular pressure (IMP), muscle tissue oxygenation, and early blood biomarkers for muscle damage (myoglobin, creatine kinase) in the tibialis anterior muscle during a 10-km treadmill run in healthy recreational runners. Findings indicated that CS use significantly elevated IMP, reduced muscle tissue oxygenation, and increased serum myoglobin, suggesting non-beneficial muscle effects and no prevention of early exercise-induced muscle damage. Creatine kinase levels and systemic blood pressure remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exercise with Compression Stockings

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of D-ribose supplementation on delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) induced by plyometric exercise in untrained male college students. Findings indicate that oral administration of 15g D-ribose reduced muscle soreness, improved knee extensor function by mitigating strength reduction, lowered muscle damage markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, Myoglobin), and inhibited lipid peroxidation (Malondialdehyde), thereby accelerating DOMS recovery. However, D-ribose showed no significant effect on overall isokinetic muscle strength (flexor peak torque and total work) and modulated the time-course of antioxidant enzymes (Superoxide Dismutase) and total antioxidant capacity (TAC) without consistently showing a superior antioxidant effect compared to placebo after 48 hours.

treatment_details.therapy_type: D-ribose supplementation combined with plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: D-ribose was orally administered at 15g per dose, 1-hour before, and 1-hour, 12-hours, 24-hours, and 36-hours after exercise. A calorically equivalent placebo containing sorbitol and β-cyclodextrin was given at the same dose and times. The plyometric exercise protocol consisted of 7 sets of 20 consecutive frog hops with 90-second rest intervals between sets, performed twice with a 14-day washout period. No dose-response comparisons for D-ribose were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in both groups after 24-h (p < 0.01), then decreased after 48-h (p < 0.01) but remained significantly higher than baseline (p < 0.01). MB was significantly lower in the DRIB group after 24-h compared to the PLAC group (p < 0.01), with PLAC levels not returning to baseline within 48-h.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle tissue; its release into blood indicates muscle fiber damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-plyometric exercise muscle damage and D-ribose supplementation effect on recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in DRIB indicate reduced muscle fiber damage and accelerated restoration of membrane integrity, signifying faster muscle recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Abnormally high in 100% of patients with SBMA. However, exhibited variability across patient cohorts and inconsistent associations with clinical characteristics; generally failed to track disease progression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Muscle-enriched protein involved in oxygen storage in muscle tissue. Common clinical marker, typically indicative of muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Existing fluid biomarker used in SBMA clinical studies. Increased in patients with SBMA, as well as other muscle degenerative disorders like DMD and FSHD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A strong indicator of muscle degenerative disorders, specifically distinguishing SBMA (high in 100% of patients) from ALS. However, its utility for tracking disease progression or reliably correlating with clinical characteristics in SBMA is limited.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between dietary intake in the week prior to a marathon race and post-race exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) and cardiac stress (EICS) in recreational male endurance runners. It found that consumption of meat, butter, and fatty meat was positively associated with higher EIMD and EICS markers, whereas fish, vegetables, and olive oil intake showed a negative association, suggesting a protective role.

Pre-race average daily intake was 3005.7     362.5 kcal (44.8     6.2 kcal/kg), with carbohydrates at 338.3     55.1 g, protein at 130.5     24.2 g, and fat at 121.5     19.8 g. Participants showed dietary imbalances with lower than recommended servings of cereals, potatoes, dairy, vegetables, and legumes, and excess in pastries, sweets, and dried fruits. The study identified associations between food group consumption (e.g., meat, butter, fatty meat, fish, vegetables, olive oil) and post-race biomarker levels, but no specific dose-response comparisons for dietary components were explicitly reported beyond these associations. The race took place in Madrid in April 2016, with a mean dry temperature of 27     3    °C and 27     2% relative humidity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, with additional increases and eventual full recovery, but delayed peak
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increases from 20-45% after the first match, and 35-60% after the second match. Identified as the most affected marker, previously observed to increase up to ~240% after similar sports. Exhibited additional increases during short recovery sessions, with a peak delayed until short recovery where Athlete 2 showed 40% higher elevation. Recovered to initial levels before the second match and fully returned to pre-match levels during long recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This placebo-controlled, double-blind, six-arm crossover study investigated the effects of a single 60 mg Cannabidiol (CBD) supplementation versus placebo after an intensive resistance training protocol (designed to induce muscle damage) on skeletal muscle regeneration and performance in healthy, well-trained participants. The study measured muscle damage biomarkers (Creatine Kinase and Myoglobin) and neuromuscular performance (1RM Back Squat and Countermovement Jump) at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. While overall effects were small, CBD significantly attenuated increases in CK and Myo concentrations and aided in the recovery of 1RM Back Squat performance after 72 hours, but showed no significant effect on Countermovement Jump performance.

treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Participants underwent an intensive strength training protocol consisting of three sets of 12 back squats at 70% of 1RM with 150 seconds rest, and three sets of 15 drop jumps from a 45 cm box landed in a deep squat with 60 seconds rest. A single dose of 60 mg CBD solubilisat or a placebo drink was consumed directly after exercise, with effects monitored at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. Absolute strength values and training loads averaged 118.6 
± 22.6 kg. The study did not include dose-response comparisons for CBD, nor did it investigate chronic supplementation or endurance training effects, and it was suggested that the protocol might not have induced sufficient power reduction for CMJ.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No meaningful differences between soy protein supplementation and an exercise-only group during a 60 min stress test.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests no significant impact on muscular stress indicators under a 60-min stress test duration.

Levels correlated with other muscle damage biomarkers and symptoms, specifically positively correlating with percent changes in CK (R = 0.602, p < 0.01), Mb (R = 0.464, p < 0.01), LDH (R = 0.674, p < 0.01), muscle tenderness (R = 0.539, p < 0.01), and DOMS (R = 0.335, p < 0.05).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether aerobic capacity predicts skeletal and cardiac muscle damage in amateur triathletes after a full-distance Ironman. It found that higher aerobic capacity was negatively associated with skeletal muscle damage biomarkers (myoglobin and creatine kinase), but no association was observed with cardiac muscle damage biomarkers (cTnT, MHC-a, NT-proBNP).

Aerobic capacity was assessed one month prior to the event using a 20m shuttle-run test. The study focused on post-race biomarker levels, and no specific dose-response comparisons for varying triathlon distances or intensities were reported, though models using absolute aerobic capacity showed slightly higher predictive power for skeletal muscle damage.

A negative association was noted in unadjusted analyses, but its diagnostic value is not established, and no reference values are available.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study was an observational, cross-sectional comparison involving 28 male collegiate athletes (including weight-lifting and basketball teams) who reported engaging in strength training for at least one hour per day, five times per week, versus 29 age-matched untrained controls. No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.
