document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) on individual quadriceps muscle thickness and circulating biomarkers related to muscle atrophy and hypertrophy in the early postoperative phase. It found severe atrophy in the vastus intermedius (VI) and significant reductions in other quadriceps muscle thicknesses (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Medialis Obliquus). Circulating IGF-1 levels were significantly reduced, while myostatin levels showed a slight increase with a medium effect size, contributing to the observed muscle atrophy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) surgery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fourteen recreationally active patients (10 men, 4 women) with unilateral ACL injuries underwent reconstructive surgery. No dose-response comparisons or variations in surgical method/intensity were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training

No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Elevated at baseline, with partial and incomplete recovery observed, particularly among women, while overall levels increased in some groups.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), exceeding age-adjusted cut points (9.8 U/g creatinine in 1998, 16.6 U/g creatinine in 2006). Levels increased overall in some individuals (p < 0.01 in 2006). Partial recovery was observed, primarily among women, while for men, levels tended to be higher in 2006. Recovery was incomplete; the decrease in prevalence of elevated NAG (UCd > 20  5g/g creatinine group) was not statistically significant (p = 0.06). Baseline NAG was a weak predictor for future elevation (OR = 2.6).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure and its reduction over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in a human population.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates renal tubular damage and impaired kidney function. Incomplete recovery suggests ongoing or residual impairment, with potential sex-specific responses.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the critical role of PW1/Peg3 expression in determining the competence of mesoangioblasts (MABs) for therapeutic applications in muscular dystrophy. It demonstrates that PW1/Peg3 is essential for MABs' myogenic differentiation, primarily by stabilizing MyoD via regulating cyclin E levels, and for their ability to transmigrate across blood vessel walls by modulating the junctional adhesion molecule-A (JAM-A). The absence of PW1/Peg3 leads to impaired MAB function, including reduced myogenic potential and compromised vessel crossing and engraftment into damaged myofibres. The findings suggest that PW1/Peg3 levels can serve as a crucial biomarker to identify and select optimal donor MAB populations for cell therapy. The document also details the experimental methodologies, including mammalian mesoangioblast culture, genetic manipulation (shRNA knockdown of PW1), in vitro transmigration assays, in vivo MAB transplantation into scid-mdx mice, and various molecular analyses such as immunofluorescence, histology, microarray, and quantitative PCR.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesoangioblast (MAB)-based Cell Therapy, Genetic Manipulation (shRNA knockdown), and Peptide Blocking (anti-JAM-A antibodies)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized intra-arterial transplantation of 10^6 mouse MABs (control or shPW1-transduced) diluted in 50  5l of PBS, injected into the femoral artery of 5-month-old scid-mdx female mice. Genetic manipulation involved infecting shPW1 AdmMABs with lentiviral shPW1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 in the presence of polybrene (8  5g ml  1) overnight. In vivo rescue experiments included pre-incubation of control and shPW1 cells with anti-JAM-A blocking peptide BV11 (20  5g ml  1) and control IgG for 2 hours before transplantation. For human MABs, BV16 at 12  5g ml  1 was used in in vitro transmigration assays. While specific cell transplantation numbers and antibody concentrations are provided, no dose-response comparisons for PW1 manipulation or blocking antibodies were reported, with the focus being on the effects of presence/absence or blocking.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Upregulation of N-Cadherin (CDH2) in shPW1 AdmMABs.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Upregulation suggests a maintained undifferentiated state or altered cell adhesion characteristics in MABs lacking PW1.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of eukaryotic initiation factor 3a (eIF3a) in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, confirming its oncogenic function. eIF3a was found to be highly expressed in CRC patients and tissues, promoting malignant behaviors, proliferation, and tumor growth through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Silencing eIF3a inhibited these malignant characteristics, including cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest, both in vitro and in vivo, with these effects being mediated by the PI3K/AKT pathway.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic manipulation of eIF3a expression (silencing/knockdown via siRNA or shRNA, and overexpression) and pharmacological inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: eIF3a silencing was performed using si-eIF3a transfection or stable shRNA transduction in CRC cells (SW620, DLD-1), and in a nude mouse tumor xenograft model. Specific siRNA sequences were 5′-GCGAUCAUCCUGGCGUAAUTT-3′ (sense) and 5′-AUUACGCCAGGAUGAUCGCTT−3′ (antisense). eIF3a overexpression used sh-eIF3a/h-eIF3a plasmids in CRC cells. Stable eIF3a knockout cells were selected with puromycin (5 µg/mL for 7 days, then 1 µg/mL for 7 days). For xenograft models, 2 × 10^6 stable eIF3a knockout or control SW620 cells were subcutaneously injected per mouse. A specific PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, was used in combination with eIF3a modifications in CRC cells. No dose-response comparisons for eIF3a modulation were reported, but rather comparisons between manipulated and control groups.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased by eIF3a silencing; increased by eIF3a overexpression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was decreased (p < .01) upon eIF3a silencing and increased (p < .01) upon eIF3a overexpression.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels indicate inhibition of EMT and reduced metastatic potential; increased levels indicate promotion of EMT and enhanced metastatic potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. The study also explored genetic associations with cerebellar gray matter volume, linking several genetic variants to cardiovascular disease and other health indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of early brain injury and cognitive impairment following aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH) using MRI and cognitive assessments.

An additional 27 paired healthy controls were recruited for comparison. No specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study of SAH's natural course and sequelae.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the acute and 1-week effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on cardiovascular performance, autonomic control, endothelial function, and a range of molecular biomarkers (inflammatory, hormonal, oxidative stress, nitric oxide synthesis, and mitochondrial regulation) in physically inactive postmenopausal women (aged 50-70) with systemic arterial hypertension, both at rest, during submaximal aerobic exercise, and throughout recovery. The aim is to provide nutritional recommendations for optimizing cardiovascular health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with nitrate-rich beetroot juice combined with standardized submaximal aerobic exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice will be administered acutely at 140 mL (800 mg nitrate) on the first day, followed by a daily dose of 70 mL (400 mg nitrate) for 6 subsequent days. A placebo (nitrate-free) juice will serve as control. Exercise consists of a 40-minute treadmill session at a speed corresponding to 65-70% of VO2peak. The study employs a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled design with a 7-day washout period between intervention protocols. Previous research indicated lower doses (200-400 mg nitrate) were insufficient for acute cardiovascular effects, leading to the optimized dosages used here. Additionally, 40 g of whey protein will be provided before executing experimental protocols.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: N-terminal portion of the pro-hormone natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not applicable; this is a protocol description.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable; this is a protocol description of planned measurements, not actual results.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of cardiac stretch and dysfunction, elevated in heart failure.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Evaluated before and after using beet juice rich in nitrate to verify relationships with the cardiovascular system.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular stress, heart failure risk, and prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between dietary intake in the week prior to a marathon race and post-race exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) and cardiac stress (EICS) in recreational male endurance runners. It found that consumption of meat, butter, and fatty meat was positively associated with higher EIMD and EICS markers, whereas fish, vegetables, and olive oil intake showed a negative association, suggesting a protective role.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intake assessment combined with endurance running (marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Sixty-nine male recreational runners participated in a competitive marathon (42.195 km). Dietary intake for the week prior to and on race day was collected using a seven-day weighed food record. Pre-race average daily intake was 3005.7     362.5 kcal (44.8     6.2 kcal/kg), with carbohydrates at 338.3     55.1 g, protein at 130.5     24.2 g, and fat at 121.5     19.8 g. Race-day intake included 1.8     0.7 L fluid and 597.1     394.9 kcal. Participants showed dietary imbalances with lower than recommended servings of cereals, potatoes, dairy, vegetables, and legumes, and excess in pastries, sweets, and dried fruits. The study identified associations between food group consumption (e.g., meat, butter, fatty meat, fish, vegetables, olive oil) and post-race biomarker levels, but no specific dose-response comparisons for dietary components were explicitly reported beyond these associations. The race took place in Madrid in April 2016, with a mean dry temperature of 27     3    °C and 27     2% relative humidity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Post-race mean: 121.8     103.2 pg/mL. Positively associated with butter and fatty meat intake (    = 0.796; p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Peptide released from cardiac ventricles in response to stretch and stress, indicating cardiac overload.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-competitive marathon race, with levels influenced by pre-race dietary intake of butter and fatty meat.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Assesses the level of exercise-induced cardiac stress (EICS).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the circadian rhythmicity and diurnal variation of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and healthy controls. It found that sST2 exhibits a distinct diurnal rhythm with lower values in the morning and peaks in the late afternoon. The study also compared sST2's rhythmicity to N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), which showed no diurnal rhythm, and to melatonin and cortisol, which demonstrated expected circadian patterns. These findings highlight the impact of diurnal variation on the clinical interpretation and management of sST2 levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker diurnal variation and circadian rhythm analysis for clinical monitoring and interpretation guidance
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood samples were collected from 16 HFrEF patients and 16 controls at seven specific time points (9 a.m., 1 p.m., 5 p.m., 9 p.m., 1 a.m., 5 a.m., and 9 a.m.) over a 24-hour period. The study focused on observational biomarker patterns and did not involve therapeutic interventions, dose comparisons, or standardized conditions for physical activity, meals, light exposure, or sleep duration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not exhibit a diurnal rhythm, showing random fluctuations. Differences between minimum and maximum values ranged up to 76.5% in HFrEF patients within 24 hours. No significant cosinor rhythmicity (P > 0.05) was observed in either patient or control groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An important cardiovascular-related biomarker used for diagnosing heart failure, serving as a negative control for circadian rhythms in this study.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diurnal variation analysis in chronic heart failure patients (HFrEF) and healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used for diagnosing heart failure. Its absence of diurnal rhythm indicates stable levels throughout a 24-hour period, simplifying consistent measurement for diagnostic purposes, and serves as a negative control for circadian rhythmicity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of a structured exercise program in adult women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. The primary aim is to mitigate anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) by assessing changes in circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain, LVEF). Secondary objectives include evaluating other cardiac health parameters (blood pressure, HR, HRV, recovery HR), physical function, self-reported physical activity, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. The protocol also details the planned methodology for assessing these outcomes and administrative aspects of the study.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Structured Exercise Program (Aerobic and Resistance Training)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention group will perform a supervised exercise program three times per week, during anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT). Each 70-minute session includes a 5-minute warm-up, 60 minutes of training, and a 5-minute cooldown. Aerobic training, progressively increasing from 20 to 30 minutes at light to moderate-to-high intensity (50-80% HR reserve), combines treadmill, stationary bike, and stepping. Resistance training involves 2-3 sets of 10-12 maximal repetitions (12-RM) for upper and lower body, with progressive intensity. The program starts 1-2 days after the first chemotherapy session and continues throughout treatment. The control group receives standard breast cancer care without specific physical activity advice. No dose-response comparisons are reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes will be assessed as a primary outcome. Measurements will be taken at baseline (t0), 1-24 hours prior to each anthracycline-treatment cycle (t1), after the end of anthracycline-treatment (t2), and 3 months after t2 (t3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cardiac neurohormone and pro-hormone fragment released in response to myocardial wall stress and stretch, indicating cardiac dysfunction and commonly elevated in heart failure.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Structured exercise program in women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary outcome for assessing cardioprotective effect, indicating anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC), cardiac damage, and potential for heart failure.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of biomarker-based screening for the early detection of AL amyloidosis in intermediate/high-risk MGUS patients. It demonstrates that longitudinal monitoring, particularly in a cohort of 4742 MGUS patients with altered FLCr, significantly increases the timely identification of pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis, leading to earlier treatment, limited organ involvement, and significant recovery of organ function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening and monitoring strategy for AL amyloidosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Systematically integrated since 2012 in a single-center longitudinal cohort of 4742 MGUS patients, with a median follow-up of 4 years. Specifically, 1375 patients (28.9%) with altered FLCr underwent sequential biomarker monitoring. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focuses on a diagnostic screening strategy rather than a therapeutic intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected in 9 out of 22 (40.9%) pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis patients and 16 out of 38 (42.1%) MGUS cases without AL. Among those with cardiac involvement, one had a mild elevation (556 ng/L), with others at least 650 ng/L, indicating initial pre-symptomatic organ involvement.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Released in response to cardiac wall stress and volume overload, serving as a marker for cardiac dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker-based longitudinal screening for pre-symptomatic AL amyloidosis cardiac involvement or other cardiac pathologies in MGUS patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates potential cardiac involvement in AL amyloidosis, suggesting the need for further diagnostic workup. While useful, it may be suboptimal for detecting early ATTRwt heart involvement; in non-AL cases, it indicated other cardiac conditions like hypertensive cardiomyopathy or arrhythmias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether aerobic capacity predicts skeletal and cardiac muscle damage in amateur triathletes after a full-distance Ironman. It found that higher aerobic capacity was negatively associated with skeletal muscle damage biomarkers (myoglobin and creatine kinase), but no association was observed with cardiac muscle damage biomarkers (cTnT, MHC-a, NT-proBNP).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Full Distance Ironman Triathlon
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in a full distance Ironman triathlon (3.8 km swimming, 180 km cycling, 42.2 km running). These amateur athletes reported training for 11.2  1 3 hours/week and had previously completed a median of 8 ultra-endurance races. Aerobic capacity was assessed one month prior to the event using a 20m shuttle-run test. The study focused on post-race biomarker levels, and no specific dose-response comparisons for varying triathlon distances or intensities were reported, though models using absolute aerobic capacity showed slightly higher predictive power for skeletal muscle damage.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Post-race levels were elevated, with 89% of athletes showing pathological values (reference < 300 ng/L); however, no association was found between aerobic capacity and the magnitude of NT-proBNP increase.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A prohormone involved in cardiac function and regulation of blood pressure and fluid balance, released in response to increased cardiac wall stress or volume overload.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-full distance Ironman triathlon in amateur triathletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated post-race NT-proBNP levels indicate cardiac stress, but aerobic capacity does not predict its magnitude. Its clinical significance in ultra-endurance athletes is debated, potentially reflecting physiological adaptation rather than pathology.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute exhaustive exercise / Symptom-limited incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single session of acute exhaustive exercise was performed by 28 male chronic heart failure (CHF) participants (mean age 59.07  1 1.79 years). The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels (Table 3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of cardiac function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates changes in cardiac function following acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study protocol investigates the effects of early spironolactone therapy on exercise capacity, clinical worsening, and vascular inflammation in 70 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without right ventricular failure. It aims to assess changes in functional performance (6-minute walk distance, VO2 max), plasma markers of vascular inflammation, gene expression profiles in PBMCs and PAECs, neurohormonal axis activation (sympathetic nervous system, RAAS, sex hormone metabolism), and right ventricular structure and function using advanced imaging techniques, while also monitoring for safety biomarkers like serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Spironolactone therapy (Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Early treatment with spironolactone will be administered for 24 weeks in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial. The initial dose is 25 mg once daily, escalating to 50 mg daily after week 6 if serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine does not increase >50% from baseline. Dose adjustments and discontinuation are strictly tied to safety monitoring, including stopping if serum potassium increases to 5.3-5.9 mEq/L, discontinuing if it remains ">="5.3 mEq/L on two consecutive draws or immediately if ">="6.0 mEq/L, or if serum creatinine increases >50% from baseline. No formal dose-response comparisons are reported within this protocol, although drug-drug interactions with PAH-specific therapies were considered.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Will be assessed for changes post-treatment
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes from baseline between the treatment and placebo groups are compared, but no specific quantification is provided in this protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cardiac neurohormone, secreted in response to ventricular stretch and overload, indicative of heart failure.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Spironolactone therapy in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) to assess RV function.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severity of right ventricular dysfunction and prognosis in heart failure conditions like PAH and serves as a traditional measurement of disease severity in PAH.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated LL-37/CRAMP as both a potential biomarker and therapeutic agent for acute heart failure (HF) and cardiac hypertrophy. It revealed that serum LL-37/CRAMP levels are significantly decreased in acute HF patients and various preclinical models of HF. Functionally, therapeutic administration of CRAMP was found to attenuate HF and pathological hypertrophy in these models. Mechanistically, CRAMP's cardioprotective effects against hypertrophy were mediated through the inhibition of NF-κB signaling, highlighting its dual potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a protective therapeutic target for acute HF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The primary therapeutic method involved administration of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptides (CRAMP, mCRAMP, rCRAMP). Heart failure and hypertrophy models were induced using Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC) surgery, Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion, Isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, and Phenylephrine (PE) treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: CRAMP treatments included mCRAMP peptide supplementation for 2 or 4 weeks in mice, and 0.1 mg/L for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. rCRAMP was applied to neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Inducers for HF models included Ang II (1.3 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks in mice; 1 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes), Isoproterenol (30 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks in mice), and PE (100 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes). TAC surgery involved tying a 27-gauge needle parallel to the transverse aorta with 7-0 silk suture. Betulinic acid (BA) was used at 20 µM for 48 h in cardiomyocytes. Generally, no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for the various treatments, beyond the duration of supplementation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels ≥ 1,000 pg/mL used as a diagnostic criterion for acute HF. Negatively correlated with serum LL-37 levels (R=-0.174, P=0.030).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, a hormone involved in cardiac stress and volume overload response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Heart Failure (HF) patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Established clinical biomarker for acute HF diagnosis and indicator of cardiac dysfunction and severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific plasma microRNAs (miR-34a, miR-224, miR-452) and Angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) in women with diabetes and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction (LVDD) or Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF), including cohorts with impaired renal function or a history of preeclampsia. The study found distinct patterns of miR expression and Ang-2 levels associated with microvascular injury in these conditions, highlighting their relevance, particularly in women. Methodologies included echocardiography, standard blood testing, RNA isolation for microRNA profiling, and ELISA for specific plasma proteins.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study, diagnostic assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on diagnostic assessment and biomarker identification for naturally occurring cardiovascular conditions (LVDD and HFpEF) in the context of diabetes. No therapeutic interventions or dose administrations were performed or compared; the study examined existing biomarker levels in patient cohorts.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Levels measured but excluded from outcome panel for bias prevention; specific direction of change not reported as an outcome.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels available but not used for outcome determination in this context.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: N-terminal fragment of the prohormone for BNP, released in response to ventricular stretch and wall stress, indicating cardiac dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Results were available but explicitly excluded from the outcome panel's determination of HF in the UHFO-DM study to prevent incorporation bias.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A key diagnostic and prognostic marker for heart failure, though intentionally excluded from the diagnostic algorithm in this specific study context to avoid bias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Statistically significant difference observed; direction not specified.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant in women in the validation cohort.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Statistically significant in women with paroxysmal AF in the validation cohort.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall median (IQR) at baseline was 133 (46–274) pmol/L. Subphenotype 2 showed the highest median levels at baseline and elevated levels as part of Subset D, often exceeding three times the normal upper limit. Lowest median levels were observed in subphenotype 3 at baseline.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates cardiac wall stress, myocardial stretch, and ventricular dysfunction, released in response to increased ventricular pressure and volume; a key diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for heart failure severity and fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and longitudinal assessment in HFrEF patients for subphenotype identification, particularly defining Subphenotype 2 which is characterized by older patients, lower SBP, increased comorbidities (e.g., diabetes mellitus, chronic renal failure), and very high levels, often contributing to hospitalization criteria for acute or worsened HF.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are strongly associated with worse clinical outcomes, including increased risk of hospitalization due to worsening heart failure, higher heart failure severity, and poorer prognosis (HR 3.43 (1.76–6.69) for Subphenotype 2 vs. Subphenotype 1).

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated plasma Interleukin-4 (IL4) levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and healthy controls, finding significantly decreased IL4 levels in PH patients. Lower plasma IL4 was associated with higher PH risk, greater disease severity, increased clinical worsening, and poorer survival rates, indicating its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating endogenous biomarker levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study; no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were performed. Endogenous plasma IL4 levels were measured by flow cytometry in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inverse correlation with IL4 levels, indicating higher levels are associated with more severe haemodynamic compromise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of cardiac stretch and dysfunction, associated with disease severity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) disease severity and prognosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of disease severity and included in a nomogram for prognosis prediction in PH patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study established robust reference intervals for plasma dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated Matrix Gla-Protein (dp-ucMGP) in a metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population using the IDS-iSYS Ina Ktif assay. It investigated dp-ucMGP's utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The findings indicate a significant stepwise increase in plasma dp-ucMGP levels from healthy individuals to those with DM without DKD, and further to those with DKD. Higher dp-ucMGP levels were associated with renal function decline and demonstrated predictive value for DKD diagnosis and progression, showing similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting renal function decline. Additionally, the study explored associations of dp-ucMGP with various clinical parameters in healthy volunteers, noting gender differences and correlations with BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study (Observational)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study primarily focused on establishing reference intervals and evaluating the diagnostic potential of plasma dp-ucMGP across different health states (healthy, diabetes mellitus, diabetic kidney disease). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted within this study. However, the document discusses external studies on Vitamin K2 supplementation (e.g., 6 weeks of daily supplementation or 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days) as a potential therapy impacting dp-ucMGP levels.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: NT-proBNP was a significant explanatory variable associated with increasing plasma LN dp-ucMGP in participants with DM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker for cardiac function, primarily associated with heart failure and ventricular stretch.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Participants with diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiac stress or dysfunction, often elevated in kidney disease, and associated with changes in dp-ucMGP.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery (VO2Rec) measures, especially VO2T12.5% (time to recover 12.5% of peak VO2), in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. The study suggests its regular inclusion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing protocols.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Pharmacological treatment (Aficamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Aficamten was administered for 24 weeks in a phase 3 randomized controlled trial, compared against placebo. Doses were individualized to achieve the lowest effective dose, targeting a Valsalva Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Gradient (LVOT-G) <30 mm Hg while maintaining a left ventricular ejection fraction ">=\u00ad50%. Specific daily dosages (mg) and dose-response comparisons were not detailed, but treatment led to proportional improvements in cardiac function and biomarkers.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reduced with treatment; higher for diagnostic criteria
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced (P <0.005) correlating with shortening of VO2T12.5% in response to aficamten treatment. ">=125 pg/mL for HFpEF-HDI diagnostic criteria. Median 18% [8%	26%] reduction associated with a 15-second improvement in VO2 T 12.5%. A cut-point of >125 pg/mL is used in the universal definition of HF. Elevated levels. Aficamten improved VO2 T 12.5% proportionately to improvements in levels of NT-proBNP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A neurohormone released by cardiomyocytes in response to volume overload and ventricular stretch; commonly used as a marker for cardiac stress and heart failure. A natriuretic peptide used as a marker for cardiac stress and dysfunction. Hormone released by cardiac ventricles in response to stretch and stress. Hormone involved in cardiac stress and fluid balance; marker of cardiac dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Response to aficamten treatment for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). Meeting diagnostic criteria for HFpEF-HDI; also used in HF prognostication. Risk stratification for adverse outcomes. Underlying symptomatic HFpEF; risk-stratification.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates improved cardiac function and reduced cardiac stress/myocardial stretch in patients with oHCM. Diagnostic criterion for HFpEF-HDI and an indicator for patients with HF at risk of functional impairment and adverse outcomes. Reduction indicates improved cardiac function and less cardiac stress. Levels >125 pg/mL, combined with prolonged VO2 T 12.5%, further delineates risk for adverse outcomes. Elevated levels are associated with underlying symptomatic HFpEF; used for risk-stratification of individuals alongside VO2T12.5%. Associated with improved cardiac performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This prospective longitudinal study investigated Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) trajectories, associated echocardiographic and systemic changes, predictors, and prognostic implications over 18 months in heart failure patients with predischarge LVEF <=40% after acute cardiac decompensation (ACD). The study found variable LVEF trajectories, with over 50% showing improvements by at least one LVEF category within 6 months, indicating multilevel reverse remodeling. LVEF changes correlated with various parameters, were predictable from baseline characteristics (e.g., heart failure duration <1 year, female sex, higher predischarge blood pressure, baseline LVEF, lower natriuretic peptide levels), and were associated with improved clinical outcomes (lower mortality and rehospitalization rates) at 18 months. However, repeat hospitalizations were linked to the attenuation or reversal of this reverse remodeling. Biomarkers such as NT-proBNP, MR-proANP, cardiac troponin I, hs-CRP, and interleukin-6 showed significant changes, often decreasing with LVEF improvement, while others like hemoglobin, leukocytes, and renal/hepatic function parameters showed no differential changes across LVEF recovery subgroups.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT) for Heart Failure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMT) as tolerated throughout the 18-month follow-up, with uptitration to target doses as per the Interdisciplinary Network Heart Failure (INH) study protocol. The study focused on observing LVEF trajectories and biomarker changes in response to ongoing GDMT rather than comparing specific therapeutic interventions or doses. No explicit dose-response comparisons for individual GDMT components were reported, but proportions of patients taking each substance class were high and increased at 6-month follow-up (FUP6).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declined markedly at 6-month follow-up (FUP6) compared to baseline. Lower baseline levels were identified as a significant predictor for LVEF improvement (P<0.05). At FUP6, levels were significantly lower in patients with improved LVEF versus those with persistent HFrEF; HFrEF patients had NT-proBNP levels twice as high as HFmrEF and HFnEF subgroups. Abnormal, albeit lower, levels were still observed in HFnEF at FUP6 despite apparent normalization of LV systolic function.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Natriuretic peptide and biomarker of cardiac wall stress and heart failure severity, associated with cardiac function and neurohormonal activation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and 6-month follow-up (FUP6) measurements in heart failure patients after Acute Cardiac Decompensation (ACD) undergoing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapies (GDMT), particularly in relation to LVEF improvement and as a predictor for clinical outcomes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower baseline levels predict a higher likelihood of LVEF improvement. Persistent abnormal levels at FUP6, even with improved LVEF, suggest ongoing myocardial stress and serve as a predictor for clinical outcomes and renal dysfunction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). The treatment also showed complex immunomodulatory effects, including altered levels of several cytokines (e.g., increased IP-10, MIP-1α, G-CSF, IL-10, while IL-6, MCP-1, and RAGE remained mostly unchanged in vivo but exhibited changes in vitro) and specific miRNAs, as well as influencing PBMC activation and proliferation in vitro.

The average cell viability was 87.8% ± 5.1% before infusion. This was combined with conventional anti-viral treatment including dexamethasone and antibiotic therapy. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dysregulated m6A RNA and enzyme profiles observed in HCC; notably fosters MASLD development through adipogenesis, lipid metabolism, inflammation, and insulin resistance; plays a crucial role in hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication and immunity, thereby contributing to HBV-induced HCC pathogenesis. Analogous mechanisms implicated in hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and m6A-mediated immune system suppression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Post-transcriptional RNA modification, affecting gene expression, regulating adipogenesis, lipid metabolism, inflammation, insulin resistance, viral replication, and immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MASLD development, HBV replication, HBV-induced HCC pathogenesis, HCV infection, m6A-mediated immune system suppression, chronic hepatitis, HCC progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Pivotal in MASLD development and HBV/HCV-induced HCC pathogenesis; dysregulation correlates with HCC progression, indicating potential for CLD diagnoses and therapeutic interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sorafenib treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Underscores the indispensable role of the G3P shuttle in metabolic adaptation to maintain glycolysis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study characterized pediatric Philadelphia-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients with kinase fusions in Japan, identifying 29 such patients from a cohort of 373. These patients presented with distinct clinical features including male predominance (22/7), older mean age at onset (8.8 years), high mean white blood cell count at diagnosis (94,200/μl), and a high proportion of National Cancer Institute high-risk (NCI-HR) cases. Genetic analysis revealed various kinase fusions (ABL1, PDGFRB, JAK2, IgH-EPOR, NCOR1-LYN, CRLF2) and a high prevalence of IKZF1 deletion (16/22 patients). Kinase fusion-positive patients demonstrated inferior outcomes, including high rates of prednisolone poor response (44.8%), induction failure (12.9%), and significantly inferior 5-year event-free survival rates (48.6±9.7%) compared to fusion-negative patients, suggesting clinical similarities to Ph+ ALL and underscoring the need for advanced stratification and targeted therapies.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients were treated under various conventional chemotherapy clinical trial protocols (e.g., JACLS-ALL02, TCCSG, CCLSG, KYCCSG studies), which included initial prednisolone (PSL) therapy. Some patients received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs like imatinib, dasatinib) are discussed as potential targeted therapies for kinase fusion-positive patients. However, specific drug doses, durations, or detailed regimens for any treatment were not provided or directly investigated within this study; the heterogeneity of protocols was noted as a limitation. The study focused on clinical outcomes in relation to kinase fusion status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) levels and inflammasome gene expression in monocytes from patients with septic shock caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, comparing them to healthy controls. The findings indicated that while the expression of main inflammasome genes was largely comparable between septic shock patients and healthy controls, circulating mtDNA levels were significantly elevated in septic shock patients, with even higher levels observed in those who died in the ICU. The study suggests that mtDNA could serve as an early prognostic marker for severity in septic shock from MDR pathogens.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on septic shock induced by multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 19 ICU patients diagnosed with septic shock due to documented MDR bacteria, with blood samples collected within 24 hours of diagnosis, and compared them to 20 age-matched healthy controls. The median SOFA score at ICU admission for patients was 11. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was applied or investigated; the study focused solely on characterizing the disease state and biomarker levels. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Comparable to that of healthy patients without infection; no significant difference from controls, though a small trend toward increased expression was observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of the inflammasome; acts as a cytosolic pattern recognition receptor involved in mounting a proinflammatory immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Septic shock due to Multidrug Resistant (MDR) pathogens infection.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant difference from healthy controls, suggesting no pronounced dysregulation in gene expression or possibly an 'abnormal normality' / exhausted inflammatory response in this context of septic shock.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the expression patterns and prognostic value of the thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP)/nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome pathway and its related genes (IL1B, CASP1) in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Analyzing microarray data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), transcriptome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), and qRT-PCR data from a Jinan University (JNU) validation cohort, the study found that TXNIP and IL1B were generally upregulated, while CASP1 showed variable expression in AML patients compared to healthy individuals. Crucially, lower expression, particularly the co-expression, of TXNIP, NLRP3, and IL1B was consistently associated with a more favorable prognosis and longer overall survival (OS) in AML patients, indicating their potential as prognostic biomarkers and targets for novel AML therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prognostic Biomarker Analysis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study analyzing endogenous gene expression patterns in AML patients across multiple public (GEO: GSE13159, GSE12417; TCGA) and institutional (JNU) datasets. The study compared expression levels between AML patients and healthy individuals, and correlated expression patterns with patient outcomes (overall survival, restricted mean survival time). Patients were categorized into high and low expression groups based on median gene expression levels. No experimental intervention, therapeutic doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported or investigated.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: AML patient data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases (GSE12417), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database, and Peripheral Blood (PB) samples from Jinan University (JNU) database, compared with Healthy Individuals.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower expression is associated with a longer overall survival and favorable prognosis.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: AML patients with low NLRP3 expression had a longer overall survival (OS) (GSE12417 dataset, P = 0.004); lower expression associated with favorable prognosis (GSE12417, P = 0.009; TCGA, P = 0.050; JNU, P = 0.026). Lower expression predicted better OS (1-year OS: NLRP3 low vs. NLRP3 high 79% vs 44%, HR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.24 to 0.79, P = 0.004 in GEO dataset).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of the NLRP3 inflammasome; activated by elevated TXNIP in the presence of high ROS; induces NLRP3 oligomerization, recruiting ASCs and pro-caspase-1 to assemble inflammasomes, leading to chronic inflammation and tumor progression. Important intermediator between stressful stimuli and inflammatory responses; deregulation implicated in tumor progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients; Prognosis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of prognosis in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML); overexpressed and highly activated in AML bone marrow leukemia cells and correlated with poor prognosis; lower expression predicts longer overall survival and favorable prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic utility of specific long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in Schizophrenia (SZ) patients, aiming to identify potential biomarkers and their association with psychiatric symptoms. A panel of three lncRNAs (NONHSAT089447, NONHSAT021545, and NONHSAT041499) was identified as significantly upregulated in the plasma/peripheral blood of SZ patients, demonstrating diagnostic value for SZ and correlating with positive symptoms and overall disease severity. These findings suggest these lncRNAs could serve as potential biomarkers for the diagnosis and differential diagnosis of SZ, with NONHSAT021545 showing particular association with positive symptom severity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker identification and diagnostic evaluation for Schizophrenia
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational/diagnostic study comparing 96 schizophrenia patients (first-episode or no antipsychotic medication for at least three months) with 48 healthy controls, and also with patients diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Expression levels of ten specific lncRNAs were initially screened, with three validated, in plasma samples using quantitative real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Psychiatric symptoms were assessed using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) and Global Assessment Scale (GAS). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly performed within this study, though some referenced findings mention lncRNA changes post-antipsychotic treatment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated/overexpressed in Schizophrenia patients compared to healthy controls, MDD patients, and GAD patients (P < 0.05). Part of a diagnostic panel (AUC = 0.689, P < 0.001; sensitivity: 77.1%, specificity: 58.3%) and individually predicted SZ with an AUC between 0.603–0.689 (P < 0.05). Plasma expression levels/ΔCT values significantly correlated with Positive subscale score and Global Assessment Scale total score (rSp: -0.401 to 0.311, P < 0.01). Accounted for 11.3% of the Positive subscale score variance and 11.6% of the Global Assessment Scale total score variance. Mean positive subscale score was 16.82 ± 4.96 in the lower positive symptoms group (n=50) vs. 27.35 ± 3.76 in the higher positive symptoms group (n=46).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key factor in gene regulation, involved in brain development and the pathogenesis of psychiatric diseases; contributes to the pathogenesis of Schizophrenia, though specific mechanisms are currently unclear.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Schizophrenia (SZ) diagnosis, pathogenesis, and symptom severity (particularly positive symptoms); prediction of positive symptom severity; differential diagnosis from healthy controls, Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic biomarker for Schizophrenia and for its differential diagnosis; strongly associated with psychiatric symptom severity (Positive subscale score) and global functioning (GAS total score); effectively predicts the severity of positive symptoms; implicated in the pathogenesis and development of positive symptoms associated with Schizophrenia.
