document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cerebral (venous output, arterial concentration), systemic and transcerebral circulation (net exchange)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Apnea markedly increased net cerebral output (v > a), which was especially pronounced, and more so in normoxic (NX) conditions. More marked elevations in arterial concentrations during hyperoxic (HX) apnea. Linear relationships were observed between apnea-induced reductions in PaO2/SaO2 and increased NF-L gradient in NX (r = 0.770/0.557, P = 0.009/0.045).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cytoskeletal protein specific to neurons; indicator of axonal damage and biomarker for hypoxic brain damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Apnea (Normoxic and Hyperoxic), particularly during NX apnea and linked to hypoxemia, also in breath-hold diving and patients with hypoxic brain damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects increased leakage across the blood-brain barrier and increased neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, identifying hemodynamic stress and hypoxemia's contribution to BBB disruption. Increased systemic appearance demonstrates superior prognostic accuracy for hypoxic brain damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute blood protein levels of Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP), Ubiquitin C-terminal Hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1), Neurofilament Light Chain (NF-L), and tau in US military cadets after concussions incurred during combative training. It aimed to validate these biomarkers for concussion diagnosis and management in military settings, given the challenges of traditional symptom-based assessments for mild traumatic brain injury (TBI). The findings revealed significant acute increases in GFAP and UCH-L1, with GFAP showing more prolonged elevation and NF-L levels indicating persistent differences, suggesting ongoing axonal injury and potentially incomplete biological recovery despite symptom resolution. These patterns were largely consistent with those observed in sport-associated concussions, while tau levels showed no significant changes in this specific context.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Concussion sustained during combative training exercises
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Concussions occurred during combative training exercises (e.g., boxing, self-defense, martial arts) among military service academy cadets. This multicenter prospective case-control study compared 67 concussed cadets to 36 matched contact-control cadets who participated in the same training but did not incur a concussion. Biomarker levels were assessed at baseline, acute postinjury (<6 hours), 24-48 hours postinjury, asymptomatic postinjury, and 7 days after return to activity. No specific dose or intensity of head impacts was quantified, and no dose-response comparisons for concussion severity were reported, as the 'dose' refers to the concussion event itself.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the concussion group compared to the contact-control group (mean difference in natural log values, 0.309; 95% CI, 0.105-0.513; P = .003). Levels were elevated from less than 6 hours after injury up to 7 days after return to activity, with group differences observed at all postconcussion assessment points. Lower limit of quantification was 0.241 pg/mL.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Brain injury-associated protein, indicating physiological changes and ongoing axonal injury following concussions and traumatic brain injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute concussion incurred during combative training among US military service academy cadets, with persistent elevation observed from early post-injury to 7 days after return to activity, potentially indicating ongoing axonal injury.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential objective biomarker for concussion diagnosis, injury identification, and recovery assessment in military combative training. It indicates ongoing axonal injury and serves as a subacute concussion biomarker with value days after injury, potentially identifying incomplete biological recovery and suggesting neuronal damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This multicentre longitudinal GENFI study investigated the disease-modifying effects of common variants within TMEM106B (specifically the rs1990622 G allele dosage) on disease endophenotypes in genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) caused by GRN, C9orf72, or MAPT mutations. The study aimed to longitudinally examine the interactive effects between the TMEM106B-rs1990622 genetic polymorphism, FTD mutations, clinical status (presymptomatic/symptomatic), and time on brain imaging (grey matter volume), serum biomarkers (NfL), and cognitive/behavioural measures. Findings consistently demonstrate that the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele confers protective effects, likely in an additive manner, on multiple endophenotypes, including reduced grey matter atrophy, lower serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels, and better cognitive and behavioural outcomes, predominantly in GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers, and reduces the risk of conversion to clinical FTD in GRN carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic modifier investigation; Observational longitudinal study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is observational and investigates an intrinsic genetic factor, not an active therapeutic intervention. The 'dose' refers to the additive effects of the TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage (0, 1, or 2 G alleles), which was modeled as a continuous variable. The protective effects varied across genetic FTD groups (GRN, C9orf72, MAPT mutations), specific biomarkers, disease stage (presymptomatic vs. symptomatic), and over time (baseline vs. longitudinal). No deviations from an additive effect were observed (heterozygosity indicator P > 0.05), and no traditional dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In C9orf72 presymptomatic carriers: lower NfL levels at baseline; however, no difference over time. In GRN presymptomatic carriers longitudinally: lower serum NfL levels over time (β for slope per G allele: -3.10, 95% CI: -4.75, -1.39; P: 0.0003). In GRN symptomatic carriers: lower NfL levels at both baseline (β per G allele: -27.86, 95% CI: -37.44, -18.30; P: 2.53 × 10^-8) and over time (β for slope per G allele: -6.43, 95% CI: -10.43, -2.43; P: 0.002). Past EASO GRN group: Lower levels of serum NfL over time than converter counterparts. No effects on serum NfL were observed in MAPT carriers. Elevated blood levels with wide variability were generally observed in presymptomatic FTD mutation carriers, potentially predicting conversion to clinical FTD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker of axonal damage, neuroaxonal injury, and neurodegeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic Frontotemporal Dementia (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT mutations) in presymptomatic and symptomatic carriers, modified by TMEM106B-rs1990622 G allele dosage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neuroaxonal damage and disease progression in FTD; lower levels suggest reduced neurodegeneration, reduced axonal damage, and a protective effect. May predict short-term risk of conversion to clinical FTD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol details a prospective observational longitudinal study to develop and validate the Imperial Comprehensive Cognitive Assessment in Cerebrovascular Disease (IC3), a novel digital tool for detecting post-stroke cognitive deficits. The study aims to recruit 300 acute stroke patients and longitudinally investigate the relationship between cognition, psychosocial status, MRI brain imaging, and various blood biomarkers (including NFL, GFAP, brain-derived tau, phosphorylated tau forms, Aβ42/40 ratio, apolipoprotein E genotype, and polygenic risk scores) over 12 months post-ictus. The overarching goal is to identify reliable multimodal recovery indicators, patients at risk of progressive cognitive decline, and facilitate personalized therapy allocation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational longitudinal study for post-stroke cognitive impairment monitoring, biomarker identification, and validation of a novel digital cognitive assessment tool (IC3).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a 12-month longitudinal observational design involving repeated measures collected at baseline (0-15 days post-stroke), 3, 6, and 12 months post-ictus. It includes a digital cognitive assessment (IC3) comprising 22 tasks, lasting 60-70 minutes, administered via web-browser. Blood samples are collected from 200 patients and MRI imaging from 300 patients (at 3 and 12 months), along with 50 age-matched controls. No therapeutic dose comparisons are reported as it is an observational and diagnostic tool development protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Aimed to be characterized over the first year after stroke; expected to increase to a peak at 3 months post-stroke, with group differences between patients and controls.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aimed to be quantified over the first year after stroke and related to MRI measures and cognitive/functional outcomes; expected to detect group differences between patients and controls (Cohen’s d=0.38 at baseline, 0.58 at 3-months); correlations between NFL and time of sampling of acute blood (r^2=0.10); correlations between NFL and WMHV (r=0.32); relationship between peak plasma NFL and binary functional outcomes (R^2=0.28).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker and indicator of neuroaxonal injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-stroke cognitive outcome and recovery trajectory over the first year after stroke; after acute stroke, specifically acute and postacute phases (up to 3 months and longitudinally).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Aimed to identify novel biomarkers associated with poststroke cognitive outcome and recovery trajectory, and as an indicator of neuroaxonal injury; a primary predictor of cognition and functional outcomes post-stroke, and related to white matter hyperintensities (WMHV).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantified with a customized Neurology 4-plex A platform. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Structural protein of neuronal axons, released into biofluids upon neuronal damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Plasma AD biomarker analysis in study populations 2 and 3.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential blood-based biomarker for neuroaxonal damage and neurodegeneration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated brain and blood biomarker signatures in both rat models exposed to repetitive low-level blast and human veterans exposed to IED blasts, aiming to identify antemortem evidence of tauopathy and neuronal injury related to neurobehavioral syndromes. Key findings include chronic increases in hyperphosphorylated tau (p-tau) immunoreactivity and abnormal perivascular p-tau accumulation in specific brain regions of blast-exposed rats from 6 weeks to 12 months post-injury. In human veterans, a significant subset (50%) with multiple blast exposures exhibited excessive cortical [18F]AV1451 tau ligand retention, indicating tauopathy, which correlated with higher circulating plasma neurofilament light (NfL) levels, suggesting neuronal injury. The study also explored cortical diffusivity analysis and [18F]AV45 amyloid PET imaging, finding no significant amyloid pathology but identifying microstructural cortical disruption linked to tau pathology. Additionally, increases in stathmin 1 in the amygdala of blast-exposed animals were associated with increased anxiety. The findings collectively suggest a link between blast injury, tauopathy, neuronal injury, and associated neurobehavioral complaints, highlighting potential biomarkers for diagnosing long-term neuropsychiatric sequelae of mTBI.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blast exposure (Mild Traumatic Brain Injury - mTBI)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Rats received three repetitive low-level blast exposures (74.5 kPa/10.8 psi, 4.8 ms duration, 175.8 kPa ms impulse) administered one per day for 3 consecutive days using a shock tube. Human veterans reported histories of multiple blast exposures from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), ranging from 1 to 50 or more, all associated with at least one mTBI. The study primarily focused on the effects of these exposures rather than varying doses, and no dose-response comparisons were reported. Diagnostic procedures included MRI (3-Tesla Siemens Biograph MR system) and PET imaging (370 MBq [18F]AV45 and 370 MBq [18F]AV1451 injected, with image acquisition approximately 60-80 min post-injection for 20 min durations).

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein level (concentration, via ultrasensitive Simoa platform, digital ELISA)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Humans: Elevated levels observed in plasma of veterans displaying excess [18F]AV1451 retention. Plasma NfL levels were highest among veterans who exhibited [18F]AV1451 retention versus tau-negative veterans (Mann-Whitney test, p = 0.031). Higher plasma NfL also correlated with high cortical diffusivity scores. No overall difference in human plasma NfL when all veterans were compared to controls. Rats: No difference in serum at 10 months post-blast. At 4 months post-blast, 5 out of 10 blast-exposed rats had serum levels >100 pg/mL compared to 1 out of 6 controls; means were different if one outlier was removed from the control group (p < 0.02).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A component of the neuronal cytoskeleton, released into biological fluids upon axonal damage; serves as a biomarker for neuroaxonal injury and neurodegeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Human veterans exposed to IED blasts (particularly those displaying tauopathy or high cortical diffusivity scores); rats after blast exposure, both with neurobehavioral syndromes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests an association linking blast injury, neuronal injury, and tauopathy. Identified as a potentially informative parameter for diagnosing CTE during life. Indicates axonal damage and is associated with tauopathy and microstructural disruption in the brain in blast-exposed veterans. In rats, it serves as a potential early indicator of injury and may play a role in monitoring post-concussive recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently found raised in CSF and plasma; identified as a 'most promising' marker, correlating with disease onset and progression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A structural component of the neuronal cytoskeleton; its release into biofluids indicates axonal and glial damage or degeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD) onset and progression; neuronal and glial degeneration in HD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Most promising marker for HD onset and progression, reflecting CNS pathology, useful for trials involving CNS-delivery of disease-modifying agents, and correlating with disease onset and brain atrophy.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not exhibit differences between SBMA versus control (P_adj > 0.05). In contrast, reduction in NfL protein levels in the blood was the basis for FDA accelerated approval of the ALS therapeutic tofersen (QALSODY).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates motor neuron degeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Biomarker of choice in ALS studies for assessing therapeutic efficacy (e.g., tofersen treatment). Comparison between SBMA patients and controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates motor neuron degeneration and correlates with clinical outcomes in ALS. However, it is not a distinguishing biomarker for SBMA versus control, suggesting that muscle biomarkers may be more indicative of SBMA disease status than neuronal biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated plasma extracellular vesicle neurofilament light chain (EV NfL) as a biomarker for Parkinson's disease (PD) progression in early-to-mid stage patients and healthy controls. While no significant differences in overall EV NfL levels were observed between groups over time, changes in plasma EV NfL levels significantly correlated with worsening motor symptoms, specifically with UPDRS Part II, Part III adjusted-total, and akinetic-rigidity subscores, suggesting its potential to monitor disease progression and neuronal damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study for Parkinson's disease progression monitoring and biomarker validation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, longitudinal study involving 55 patients with Parkinson's disease (PwP) and 58 healthy controls (HCs), followed for an average of 3.96 and 2.25 visits, respectively. Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated, and EV Neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels were quantified using an immunomagnetic reduction assay. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were administered, as the study focused on monitoring natural disease progression and biomarker association.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Correlated with motor symptom progression; generally elevated or increased with disease progression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
No significant differences in plasma EV NfL levels were observed between Parkinson's disease patients (PwP) and healthy controls (HCs) over time or at baseline. However, changes in plasma EV NfL levels significantly correlated with motor symptom progression: positively associated with changes in UPDRS Part II scores, and significantly correlated with adjusted-total UPDRS Part III scores (
 = 0.257, P = 0.006) and akinetic-rigidity (AR) subscores (
 = 0.273, P = 0.004) at each follow-up time point. The assay detection limit was 0.0033 to 1000 pg/mL. NfL levels were not associated with overall change in UPDRS III, MMSE, MoCA, or predictive of subsequent clinical progression.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Neurofilament light chain is a cytoskeletal protein predominantly found in neuronal axons, providing structural support. Elevated levels in bodily fluids indicate neuronal damage, axonal degeneration, and neurodegenerative processes, as it is released into the extracellular space and bloodstream in response to injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal follow-up of early-to-mid stage Parkinson's disease (PD) progression, focusing on neuronal damage, axonal degeneration, and changes in motor symptoms (UPDRS Part II and Part III scores).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential valuable biomarker for tracking and reflecting motor symptom progression, severity, and neuronal loss in Parkinson's disease (PD). It is useful for monitoring disease severity, evaluating therapeutic interventions, and guiding clinical trials by indicating underlying axonal damage and neurodegeneration. It may be a more stable and specific indicator than UPDRS for progression monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study (cross-sectional analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional observational study utilizing baseline data from 129 community-dwelling cognitively healthy older adults (aged 65+) enrolled in the Age-Well trial. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered; the study focused on analyzing associations between naturally occurring biological markers and neuroimaging values.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (concentration, measured via SIMOA, log transformed for analysis)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with higher %CST (  = .195; P = .020; 95%CI [0.170; 0.220]), though this association did not meet the threshold for multiple comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A structural protein of neuronal axons; its presence in plasma indicates axonal damage or neurodegeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with higher %CST in cognitively healthy older adults; blood-based biomarker related to AD pathophysiology; also potentially impacted by kidney function.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels suggest increased axonal damage or neurodegeneration, a general marker associated with neurological conditions and AD physiopathology risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to characterize circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) in the plasma of patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) compared to healthy controls. Key findings include significantly higher plasma NfL and GFAP in RRMS patients, with GFAP also elevated in NMOSD patients. RRMS patients exhibited lower EV density and increased mean EV size compared to controls, with larger EVs (>150nm) primarily contributing to this. Furthermore, specific EV surface markers (CD29, CD31, CD40, CD44, CD49c, CD69) showed changes in RRMS patients, notably correlating negatively with NfL/GFAP levels and positively with time since the last relapse, suggesting their potential as biomarkers for disease stabilization and reduced immune cell activity, independent of current treatments.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing biomarkers in patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD) undergoing existing pharmacological treatments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 96 participants (52 RRMS, 19 NMOSD, 10 MOGAD, 15 healthy controls). RRMS patients received natalizumab (n=33), dimethylfumarate/glatiramer acetate (n=12), or no treatment (n=7). NMOSD patients were treated with rituximab, and MOGAD patients had various heterogeneous treatments. While existing treatments were noted, no specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated by the study itself. Biomarker measurements were performed using SIMOA, SP-IRIS, cryo-EM, Western blotting, NTA, and multiplex flow cytometry. The study concluded that current treatments did not significantly influence the observed EV marker levels or composition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) than in healthy controls (HCs) (Figure 2, A and B), suggesting prominent axonal damage. No significant difference for NfL z-score between RRMS, NMOSD, and MOGAD groups (Figure 2A). NfL z-scores were adjusted for age based on a large reference cohort.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Structural protein of neurons, released into circulation following Central Nervous System (CNS) neuronal damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CNS neuron damage and disease activity in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered a potential surrogate biomarker of neuronal damage and disease activity in demyelinating diseases of the CNS, indicating prominent axonal damage in RRMS. Useful for following disease activity and linked to a negative correlation with certain EV markers in RRMS, suggesting an association with low disease activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not specifically quantified in the provided text; its increase has been linked to axonal injury.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Linked to axonal injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: General brain injury context; blast exposure during training events.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Facilitates identification of axonal injury, elucidates pathophysiological mechanisms related to brain trauma, and serves as a potential biomarker for brain injury assessment and risk stratification.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigates plasma neurofilament light protein (p-NFL) as a screening biomarker for neurodegeneration in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (ND-CNS-LCH), comparing its utility with cerebrospinal fluid neurofilament light protein (CSF-NFL). It also explores p-NFL's correlation with CSF-NFL and its response to mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway inhibitor (MAPKi) treatment, suggesting p-NFL may be useful for screening and therapeutic monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Screening Method using Biomarker Measurement, and Mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway inhibitors (MAPKi) monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on diagnostic screening, comparing paired plasma (p-NFL) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF-NFL) samples from 10 LCH patients (19 samples). CSF-NFL was measured by ELISA (abnormal ≥380 ng/l) and p-NFL by Simoa assay (LOQ 2 ng/l). Additionally, p-NFL levels were monitored in response to mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway inhibitor (MAPKi) treatment, observing changes upon initiation and discontinuation, though specific dose or duration comparisons for MAPKi were not detailed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Normal reference value < 380 ng/l; abnormal defined as ≥380 ng/l. Levels ranged from 130–1000 ng/l. In 9 samples, CSF-NFL was abnormal (≥380 ng/l). Changes generally followed p-NFL trends, with one noted exception.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker of neuroaxonal damage; promising marker to monitor neurodegeneration in CNS-Langerhans cell histiocytosis (ND-CNS-LCH).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis, screening, and monitoring of neurodegeneration in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (ND-CNS-LCH), including its correlation with p-NFL.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered a 'gold standard' biomarker for detecting and monitoring neurodegeneration in ND-CNS-LCH, though its invasive collection method (lumbar puncture) is a limitation. Elevated levels are associated with neurodegeneration.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher, lower, reduced, increased, or undetectable, often correlating with CSF-NFL.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Clinically validated lower limit of quantification was 2 ng/l; levels ranged from <2–15 ng/l. A threshold of p-NFL ≥ 2 ng/l showed 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity for identifying abnormal CSF-NFL (≥380 ng/l). Specifically, 9 samples with abnormal CSF-NFL correlated with p-NFL ≥ 2 ng/l, and 80% of samples with normal CSF-NFL had p-NFL < 2 ng/l (P < 0.001). All 9 symptomatic patients had p-NFL ≥ 2 ng/l, compared to 2 of 10 asymptomatic patients. All samples from patients with neuroradiologically verified neurodegeneration or active non-neurodegenerative CNS lesions also had p-NFL ≥ 2 ng/l. Levels were reduced after initiating MAPKi and increased after discontinuation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of neuroaxonal damage; serves as an indirect indicator reflecting CSF-NFL levels.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Screening for neurodegeneration in Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH); monitoring response to mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway inhibitors (MAPKi); and in patients with cognitive/neurological symptoms, neuroradiologically verified neurodegeneration, or active non-neurodegenerative CNS lesions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful and less invasive screening test for neurodegeneration in LCH; p-NFL ≥ 2 ng/l indicates the need for further CSF-NFL evaluation, while p-NFL < 2 ng/l suggests CSF-NFL may not be immediately necessary. Levels also reflect the efficacy of MAPKi treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study, part of the Concussion Assessment, Research, and Education (CARE) Consortium, investigated the utility of plasma biomarkers (total tau, GFAP, and Nf-L) for predicting return-to-sport (RTS) duration following sport-related concussion (SRC) in collegiate athletes. It aimed to differentiate athletes returning to sport in less than 14 days versus 14 days or more post-injury. The findings indicated that higher total tau concentrations at 24-48 hours post-injury and at symptom resolution, and lower GFAP concentrations acutely post-injury, were associated with a protracted RTS (>=14 days). Nf-L was not significantly associated with RTS duration in this cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery and return-to-sport (RTS) trajectories.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 127 NCAA collegiate athletes who sustained an SRC. Plasma biomarker levels (total tau, GFAP, Nf-L) were measured at baseline, 0-21 hours, 24-48 hours post-injury, and at the time of symptom resolution. The study compared biomarker concentrations between athletes who returned to sport in less than 14 days versus those who took 14 days or more; no therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in plasma Nf-L levels at 6 and 14 days post-SRC relative to baseline concentrations, and no significant associations with RTS duration after Bonferroni adjustment, despite a statistical interaction (F 1.9, 144.0 = 3.34; P = .04; p2 = 0.042).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects axonal damage due to injury or degeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery monitoring in collegiate athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Limited utility for discriminating or predicting RTS duration in this collegiate athlete SRC cohort due to lack of significant association and potentially limited sensitivity in milder cases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, natural history study investigated Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) patients (mild, moderate, severe) and healthy controls, aiming to determine if extracellular vesicle (EV) concentrations of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light (NfL), measured 1 year post-injury, could distinguish patient groups and correlate with TBI severity or 1-year and long-term recovery outcomes (GOS-E). The study found that blood-derived EV GFAP and NfL concentrations were generally higher in TBI patients 1 year post-injury compared to controls, correlating with injury severity and poorer 1-year recovery outcomes, although EV GFAP also showed an association with long-term improvement. Attempts to quantify EV UCH-L1 and EV tau were unsuccessful due to insufficient data quality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and its long-term biomarker profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Biomarker measurements were performed 1 year after TBI, with patient groups classified by TBI severity (mild, moderate, severe). This was a natural history study, and no specific therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher in TBI patients compared to controls 1 year post-injury, though direct comparisons between TBI severity groups and controls did not reach statistical significance. Elevated EV NfL levels were associated with lower 1-year Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended (GOS-E) score (p < 0.05;   = -0.738, p = 0.017).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Axonal protein associated with damaged axons; suggestive of neuroaxonal damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) 1 year post-injury.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates TBI presence, related to injury severity and poor recovery outcomes. Associated with worse 1-year clinical outcomes (lower GOS-E). Serves as a valuable chronic biomarker for TBI and neuroaxonal damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported, this is a study protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported, this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A structural protein of neurons, released upon neuronal damage or degeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroinflammatory conditions (MS, NMOSD, MOGAD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of neuronal injury and disease progression in neuroinflammatory conditions, highlighted as an exploratory outcome for NMOSD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive power of Neuroimmune Guidance Cue (NGC) gene expression profiles from peripheral blood monocytes for classifying cardiovascular disease (CVD) patients versus healthy individuals. Utilizing various machine learning methods, including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and Stochastic Gradient Boosting, the research aimed to identify key biomarkers for CVD prediction. The findings indicated that expression levels of SEMA6B, SEMA6D, and EPHA2 in circulating monocytes were predictive of CVD outcomes, with machine learning models demonstrating high accuracy and sensitivity in discriminating between healthy individuals and CVD patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Predictive modeling for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction using machine learning on biomarker expression profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved profiling transcriptomes of purified CD14+ monocytes from 368 subjects in the CIRCULATING CELLS study cohort, utilizing 60 mL EDTA blood samples with stringent RNA quality control (RIN > 9) and Illumina BeadStation for hybridization. Various machine-learning methods (including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, Stochastic Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, Partial Least Square, Bagged CART, and Random Forest) were applied to gene expression data to classify CVD patients and healthy individuals. Model performances were compared, with linear discriminant analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and stochastic gradient boost models yielding perfect or near-perfect sensibility and specificity, and some models achieving up to 100% accuracy in classification. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on predictive modeling and biomarker analysis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Alleviated by NET inhibition with Cl-amidine. Effectively attenuated microglia-mediated neuroinflammation by Cl-amidine. Significantly attenuated by NET inhibition via STING. Overexpression of PAD4 aggravated neuroinflammation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory response within the brain tissue, mediated by microglia/macrophages, contributing to TBI pathophysiology.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); influenced by NET inhibition with Cl-amidine and PAD4 overexpression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A key pathophysiological process in TBI associated with neuronal cell death and other adverse outcomes. Alleviation indicates a positive therapeutic effect for TBI management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.

Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the discovery of novel traumatic brain injury (TBI) biomarkers using autoimmune profiling in both rat models and human patients. It details methodologies for sample preparation, protein analysis via 2D gel electrophoresis, immunoprofiling, and the development of an immunosorbent electrochemiluminescence assay (IEA) for peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6). The main findings establish PRDX6 as a candidate TBI biomarker, showing its astrocytic expression, TBI-induced autoantibody reactivity in rats, gender differences in baseline human plasma levels, and a significant, persistent approximately fourfold elevation of circulating PRDX6 in humans following mild-to-moderate TBI, which is proportional to injury severity and independent of imaging findings. The study also acknowledges S100B and GFAP as other relevant TBI indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) injury model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human TBI was observed as mild-to-moderate (median GCS 15), with plasma collected at 4-24 hours and 2-7 days post-injury; no direct manipulation or controlled dose was applied, though PRDX6 response correlated with injury severity. In rat models, severe CCI injury was induced using a stereotaxic impactor with a 5 mm impactor at a 20-degree angle to a depth of 2 mm at 5 m/sec with a dwell time of 500 msec to maximize autoimmune response. No specific dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported for either human TBI or rat CCI, beyond PRDX6 response proportionality in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Concentrated in platelets.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An established brain biomarker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cerebral (venous output, arterial inflow) and transcerebral circulation (net exchange)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Apnea reversed NSE output (v > a) to uptake (a > v) during apnea. This was observed exclusively in normoxic (NX) conditions. A relationship was observed between the elevation in PaCO2 and decrease in NSE gradient in HX (r = 0.739, P = 0.015). Molecular weight 47.3 kDa. No detectable hemolysis (<100 mg of free Hb/L) observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glycolytic enzyme found in neurons, involved in neurotrophic regulation of neuronal survival, differentiation, and neurite regeneration through activation of specific signaling pathways; indicator of neuronal integrity or damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Apnea (Normoxic and Hyperoxic), specifically in normoxic (NX) conditions and HX apnea with elevated PaCO2 during breath-hold diving.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Uptake suggests altered neuronal metabolism or efflux across the blood-brain barrier, potentially reflecting contributions from extracerebral sources to foster neuronal repair in response to injury, representing an authentic, counter-intuitive observation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. document_context_data.document_summary: The INVICTA study outlines its comprehensive methodology to assess the impact of repetitive subconcussive blast exposure (RSCBE) during military heavy weapons training on brain function and molecular changes. The study aims to identify acute and long-term effects, develop and validate a risk stratification system (RATING tool), and ensure uniform data collection for future comparisons and meta-analyses. It investigates relationships between blast exposure and various clinical, physiological, and neuroimaging outcomes, including specific blood biomarkers, to predict individual risk and inform military decision-making regarding performance readiness and return-to-duty.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive Subconcussive Blast Exposure (RSCBE) during Heavy Weapons Training (HWT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants are exposed to blast overpressure during military Special Operations Heavy Weapons Training (HWT), involving firing weapons like the Carl Gustav recoilless rifle, Light Anti-Armor Weapon (LAAW), and AT-4 anti-tank rocket. Exposure is quantified using wearable blast sensors (e.g., Black Box Biometrics Gen 7 Blast Gauge System) mounted on helmets, shoulders, and chests, which record full waveforms for blast pressures exceeding ~6.9 kPa (1.0 psi) and define significant exposure at > ~27.6 kPa (4.0 psi). Incident peak overpressure and impulse are estimated using the FAST-CT algorithm. The study assesses naturally occurring exposure in RSOs conducting 6 training courses per year over a 2-year tour, with no controlled dose administration or explicit dose-response comparisons reported as findings, but aims to explore relationships between exposure extent and outcomes.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Facilitates identification of neuronal cell body injury and elucidation of pathophysiological mechanisms related to brain trauma.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI induced significant neuronal loss in ipsilateral CTX (p < 0.001), hippocampal CA1 (p < 0.001), and hippocampal DG (p < 0.05). document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased the age gap association with dementia severity (FIBA-); expressed in neurons. Proposed as a CSF biomarker for AD.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's disease, cognitive decline, brain aging mechanisms.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Involved in brain aging, but its contribution (or higher levels) decreases the model's association with dementia severity. Proposed as a CSF biomarker for AD.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether post-exercise branched chain amino acid and carbohydrate (BCAA-CHO) supplementation, compared to carbohydrate-only (CHO) supplementation, could mitigate performance decrements, muscle damage, and soreness, or alter immunological markers following three consecutive days of high-intensity resistance training (back squats) in resistance-trained males. The findings consistently indicated that BCAA-CHO did not significantly improve lower body strength, isometric/isokinetic torque, neuromuscular activation (EMG), perceived muscle soreness, or reduce levels of muscle damage markers like myoglobin, creatine kinase, and lactate dehydrogenase. However, BCAA-CHO supplementation did attenuate the exercise-induced increase in monocyte percentages, suggesting a modulated immune or inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Post-exercise nutritional supplementation (branched chain amino acids + carbohydrates vs. carbohydrates only) combined with a high-intensity, high-volume resistance training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Resistance training involved three consecutive days of 10 sets of 5 repetitions at 80% of 1RM barbell back squat, with a 5% weight reduction if repetitions could not be completed. Participants received two servings of either BCAA-CHO (3g L-leucine, 1g L-isoleucine, 2g L-valine, 2g non-sugar carbohydrates) or CHO (42g carbohydrates, predominantly sugars) immediately after each lifting bout and on a recovery day. Supplements were provided in 600 mL of tap water. The study compared these two supplementation types, reflecting a real-world application, but reported no further dose-response comparisons or standardization for overall carbohydrate or calorie content.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant main effect for time (p=0.95 for percentages, p=0.84 for counts) or group*time interaction (p=0.46 for percentages, p=0.40 for counts) for neutrophil percentages or counts, indicating no differential alteration between or within groups due to supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary phagocytic cells of the innate immune system, rapidly responding to infection and acute inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following repeated strenuous resistance exercise and supplement consumption, over the duration of the study.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant changes in acute inflammatory response, not differentially affected by BCAA-CHO or CHO supplementation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of nicorandil on cardiorenal injury in patients with type I Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) complicated by Coronary Heart Disease (CHD). It concluded that nicorandil significantly improved both cardiac function (evidenced by increased LVEF and decreased BNP) and renal function (evidenced by decreased Scr, Cys-C, KIM-1, NGAL, and IL-18) compared to conventional treatment, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic tool for improving prognosis and rehabilitation in type I CRS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nicorandil
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received 24 mg/d nicorandil intravenously for 1 week, administered as 4 mg/h by intravenous drip. This dosage is consistent with standard heart failure treatment (2–6 mg/h) and previous studies, and a pharmacokinetic study indicated no need for dose adjustment in patients with impaired renal function. The treatment was an add-on to conventional therapy for patients with type I CRS complicated by coronary heart disease, resulting in significantly improved outcomes for various cardiac and renal biomarkers compared to conventional treatment alone.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in both nicorandil and conventional treatment groups (P < 0.05); significantly more decreased/improved in the nicorandil group compared to conventional treatment (P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates reduced renal injury and inflammation, improved kidney function, and direct protection of renal tubular cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative literature review investigates biosensor approaches for continuous, real-time in vivo monitoring of molecular markers relevant to performance and health status. It highlights the limitations of current technologies and proposes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors as a generalizable, minimally invasive solution. The review details the development, validation, and attributes (generalizability, selectivity, reversibility, stability) of EAB sensors for detecting diverse targets (drugs, metabolites, hormones, proteins) in complex biological fluids and tissues. It also addresses the technological hurdles for subcutaneous placement, the correlation between interstitial fluid and systemic concentrations, and their potential for monitoring stress indicators (e.g., cortisol) and HPA/HPG axis hormones to assess overtraining syndromes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) Sensor Technology for Real-time In Vivo Molecular Monitoring
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This narrative literature review discusses the development and application of Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) sensors for continuous, real-time in vivo molecular monitoring, without an applied 'dose' in the traditional sense as it is a review of technology. EAB sensors, including 75-µm-diameter, 3-mm-long versions, have been tested in live rats for plasma monitoring (jugular vein) for up to 12 hours with few-second to sub-second resolution and clinically relevant precision. They are also adapted for minimally invasive subcutaneous placements (microneedles, indwelling needles) for interstitial fluid monitoring (e.g., brain, tumor, dermal ISF). The review highlights the importance of seconds-resolved time resolution and nanomolar limits of detection for hormones (achieved for LH and NGAL, micromolar for others). Time delays between subcutaneous ISF and plasma concentrations (e.g., 5-12 min for glucose, ~17 min for vancomycin) and correlations (strong for cortisol, <6% error for glucose) are noted, influenced by target properties. No dose-response comparisons for sensor parameters or monitoring duration were explicitly reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: EAB sensor achieves nanomolar limits of detection.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Important target for monitoring health and performance status; nanomolar detection achieved by some EAB sensors indicates potential for meaningful monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise and decreased within 30 min post-exercise for all participants (p<0.01). NCR in the novice group was significantly higher post-exercise (p=0.021) than in experienced participants.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the interaction between immediate immune and neuroendocrine stress responses; offers a view of cortisol-independent increase of neutrophils.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Useful for 30-minute post-exercise collection due to cortisol's delayed effect on neutrophil induction.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher NCR in novice participants post-exercise suggests a differential acute stress response related to training experience.

The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels observed as part of extensive heterogeneity in TOO profiles in moderate to severe MIS-C cohort.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates neutrophil cell death or injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Moderate to severe MIS-C cohort.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Consistent with systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement in MIS-C.
