document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in women, higher in men
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced in older women (0.055  1 0.030) compared to men (0.090  1 0.047), indicating a two-fold lower ratio in women. Values were 0.55  1 0.026 for CRP < 3 mg/L and 0.074  1 0.048 for CRP  3 3 mg/L. Optimal threshold: 0.064 (AUC = 0.636, specificity 52.6%, sensitivity 77.6%, OR = 3.82).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A composite biomarker indicating systemic inflammatory status by combining inflammatory (neutrophils) and lipid (HDL) markers.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Aging, specifically in older adults with chronic inflammation, demonstrating sex-specific differences in inflammatory and lipid profiles.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shows average diagnostic potential for clinical prognosis in vascular dysfunction and cardiovascular diseases in older patients with chronic inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during congested period), unchanged (during uncongested period)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Greater at T3 (congested period) compared to T2 and T1 (0.001 < p < 0.015, -1.01 < ES < -0.21); resting values were unchanged after the 6-week uncongested period. Negatively correlated with YYIRL1 performance (r = -0.56; p = 0.02) and VO2max (r = -0.56; p = 0.02) after the congested period. Positively correlated with competitive load (r = [0.59–0.64]; p < 0.001), training load (TL) (r = [0.65–0.68]; p < 0.001), session rating of perceived exertion (S-RPE) (r = [0.65–0.68]; p = 0.001), and training volume (r = [0.60–0.61]; p = 0.001). Training load accounted for changes in NLR values (r = 0.50).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An integrative immune cellular marker reflecting systemic inflammation, immune stress, and ongoing inflammatory processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Congested (T3) and uncongested match play periods in elite soccer players, and its association with workload parameters.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased values indicate heightened inflammatory status, exercise-induced strain, and potential immune suppression, often linked to decreased physical performance and heightened risk of illness. Useful for monitoring training, regulating training intensity and competitive load, preventing overtraining, and monitoring aerobic physical fitness. Unchanged levels with improved performance indicate effective training.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes over the measuring time points. Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC values between 0.51 – 0.74).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An inflammatory marker, reflecting systemic inflammation and immune status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly responsive to exercise. Its moderate reliability, coupled with no significant changes, questions its suitability as a robust biomarker for exercise response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) / CrossFit 'Cindy' workout
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower, then higher, then returned to baseline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased significantly immediately post-exercise compared to baseline (p<0.01), then rose above pre-exercise and post-exercise values at 30 min post-exercise (within the normal range of 0.78–3.58). Returned to pre-exercise values at 24 h. No group differences were found in NLR, but at 30 min post-exercise, it was higher than pre-exercise only for the experimental group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of systemic inflammation and physiological stress; prognostic marker with distinct meanings between healthy and disease states.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Post-exercise, particularly when cortisol actions prevail.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased NLR at 30 min post-exercise, especially in the experimental group, corroborates the hypothesis that cortisol promotes a pro-neutrophil, anti-lymphocyte environment. Reflects immune modulation and physiological stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review investigates immune dysregulation in COVID-19 patients with comorbidities, identifying key pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune markers associated with increased mortality. It proposes immune-enhancement strategies, particularly focusing on the immune-modulating properties of Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan, which stimulates various immune cells and beneficial cytokines while reducing inflammatory markers to counter hyper-inflammation and immune dysregulation characteristic of severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional Supplementation with Aureobasidium pullulans strain (AFO-202) beta 1,3-1,6 glucan
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The AFO-202 beta 1,3-1,6 glucan is a soluble exopolysaccharide derived from Aureobasidium pullulans strain AFO-202, composed of both high and low molecular weight components. It is investigated as a nutritional supplement with proven safety over two decades. No specific quantitative dosage (e.g., mg/kg), regimen details, or dose-response comparisons are reported across the analyzed texts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: increased

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a poor prognosis in patients with severe COVID-19; reflects an enhanced inflammatory process.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower in women, higher in men
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced in older women (2.29  1 2.03) compared to men (2.93  1 2.24). Values were 2.44  1 2.01 for CRP < 3 mg/L and 3.23  1 2.44 for CRP  3 3 mg/L. Optimal threshold: 1.67 (AUC = 0.655, specificity 77.2%, sensitivity 53.3%, OR = 3.87).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week daily curcumin supplementation (2g/day) on inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), blood count, and brain-derived neurotropic factor (BDNF) levels in middle-aged amateur long-distance runners. Overall, curcumin supplementation did not significantly affect CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, or blood count. However, IL-1β levels unexpectedly increased in the curcumin group, while BDNF levels showed a notable 21% increase in the curcumin group, contrasting a 5% decrease in the placebo group.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Curcumin supplementation alongside regular endurance training and an incremental treadmill running test.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 6-week daily supplementation of 2g curcumin extract. Each dose consisted of two capsules (500mg turmeric extract standardized to 95% curcumin, 10mg black pepper extract standardized to 95% piperine per capsule) taken twice daily. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but effects were compared between curcumin and placebo groups during specific exercise trials and recovery periods.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Varied significant changes across time points within both groups; no clear effect of curcumin relative to placebo on overall ratio.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant differences were observed between the respective measurements at rest, at 3 minutes post-test, and 1 hour post-test during both first and second trials for both CUR and PLA groups, with a large effect size. The study results do not clearly support the use of NLR as a reliable marker for diagnosing exercise-induced inflammation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Assesses systemic inflammation and reflects changes in primary immune cell populations (neutrophils and lymphocytes) affected by exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Amateur middle-aged long-distance runners during preparatory training period, at rest, 3 minutes post-test, and 1 hour post-test, in response to strenuous exercise and exercise-induced inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Can be used to assess systemic inflammation and potentially monitor the health status of athletes; reflects immune cell mobilization. However, the study results did not clearly support its use as a reliable marker for diagnosing exercise-induced inflammation in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The median neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was 4-fold higher in rare LYST variant heterozygous carriers than in common LYST variant carriers of MIS-C patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of systemic inflammation and immune status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clinical laboratory test in MIS-C patients, particularly those carrying rare LYST variants, compared to those with common LYST variants.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A key marker of disease severity in many pathologies. Rare LYST variants are associated with more severe clinical presentations in MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased post-exercise in the three arms of the study (all-time effects p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of systemic inflammation and physiological stress response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-intensive 2.25-hour cycling bout, irrespective of hemp fiber supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased physiological stress and inflammation following vigorous exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, the primary responder to bacterial infection and acute inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of bacterial infection or acute inflammation; low levels (neutropenia) can indicate immune compromise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex connection between chronic sleep disturbance (CSD) and cognitive progression in elderly individuals not living with dementia. It found that CSD significantly impacts cognitive function, increasing the risk of cognitive decline. Key findings indicate that activated neutrophil pathways are enriched in cognitively progressive CSD subjects, leading to increased blood neutrophil levels. High tau burden (t-tau and p-tau) mediates the influence of neutrophils on cognitive function, exacerbating CSD-related left hippocampal atrophy. Elevated CSF inflammatory factors (ICAM1, VCAM1, TNFR2, TGFβ1) were observed in cognitive progression associated with CSD, correlating with brain tau burden. The study concludes that activated neutrophil pathways triggering tau pathology likely underlie the mechanism of cognitive progression in CSD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chronic Sleep Disturbance (CSD)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated Chronic Sleep Disturbance (CSD) as a condition in elderly individuals, classifying 784 participants into a normal sleep group (528) or a CSD group (256) based on the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI)-sleep subitem, defining CSD by 8 aspects including difficulty falling asleep and excessive daytime sleepiness, and also by self-reported sleep difficulties at baseline and at least twice during 6-month follow-up intervals over 14 years. CSD was treated as a chronic condition; no specific dose, duration, severity, or induction method for CSD was reported, nor were dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Cell Level, Percentage, Gene transcript/pathway enrichment (GSEA), Pathway involvement/activation, Cell Count/Level

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased blood neutrophil level (percentage) observed, reflecting activated neutrophil pathways, and correlated with cognitive progression in CSD. Higher in cognitively progressive subjects with CSD (adjusted p < 0.05); risk of cognitive progression increased with increasing levels, with a threshold of 61.633 for blood neutrophil percentage. Significantly enriched (adjusted p < 0.05) for activation pathways. Increased in cognitively progressive subjects with CSD; a higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was associated with a greater risk of subsequent dementia (from Framingham Heart Study reference); impacted annual change in cognitive function independently of CSF t-tau and p-tau levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: First-line innate immune cell, marker of ongoing non-specific inflammation. Mediates immune response, inflammation, host defense, and various cellular processes. Capable of inducing release of toxic substances and inflammatory cytokines. Mediates neuro-immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cognitive progression of chronic sleep disturbance (CSD) in elderly individuals. Cognitively progressive elderly subjects with Chronic Sleep Difficulties (CSD) and Chronic Sleep Deprivation (CSD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates activated neutrophil pathways in CSD-related cognitive progression. Mediates the influence on cognitive function and exacerbates CSD-related risk of left hippocampal atrophy. Associated with an increased risk of cognitive progression, including higher risk of subsequent dementia. Significantly affects cognitive progression and potentially triggers tau pathology.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower neutrophil (NEU)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary immune cells involved in acute inflammation and bacterial infection defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-liver transplantation in transplant patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates compromised innate immune function.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the systemic innate immune response, specifically focusing on neutrophil phenotypes, as biomarkers to monitor exercise-induced immune changes during repetitive, prolonged walking over consecutive days (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches). It found that prolonged exercise leads to an initial systemic innate immune response, characterized by the mobilization and activation of various neutrophil phenotypes, followed by adaptation or partial normalization in subsequent days. Crucially, increased neutrophil activation, marked by high CD11b expression, was consistently associated with impaired physical feeling, slower walking speed, and a higher degree of physiological stress, suggesting its potential as a valuable marker for monitoring immune system changes and detecting overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repetitive prolonged walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants engaged in prolonged walking over 3 consecutive days as part of a public walking event (e.g., Nijmegen 4 Day Marches), covering 30, 40, or 50 km/day at a self-selected pace. Exercise intensity on day 1 averaged 65% of maximum heart rate. While the study involved varying distances, no explicit dose-response comparisons for immune markers were reported between different daily distances. However, increased neutrophil activation (high CD11b expression) was associated with slower walking speeds (approx. 4.1-4.2 km/h across days) and predominantly occurred in participants walking 30 km (66% of this group).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased from 4.0 (3.1–5.3) × 10^6 /ml at baseline to 7.9 (6.0–9.4) × 10^6 /ml after 1 day (P < 0.0001). Partially normalized to 6.6 (5.4–7.8) × 10^6 /ml on day 2 (P < 0.005 vs Day 1) and to 5.8 (4.6–7.2) × 10^6 /ml on day 3 (P = 0.816 vs Day 2).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: First responders of the innate immune system, involved in inflammation and fighting bacterial infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prolonged moderate walking exercise (Nijmegen 4 Day Marches), after 1, 2, and 3 consecutive days.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes significantly to the systemic innate immune response induced by exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant changes (P > 0.05) in hematological parameters (including WBC components) were observed throughout the experiment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, crucial for the innate immune response, especially against bacterial infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, suggesting stable acute immune response capacity under the study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant (P < 0.05) increase in the diet group during the weight loss period, accounting for most of the increase in WBCs. Augmented neutrophil numbers were observed after the diet. Numbers recovered to baseline during the weight regain period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary immune cell of the innate immune system, involved in combating infection and acute inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Weight loss period (prolonged energy deprivation and intense exercise).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered blood cell distribution and potential immune system response to physiological stress; may contribute to immunosuppression or HSC aging phenotype.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher proportion at T2 (pT1–T2 = 0.02).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Phagocytic immune cells, serving as first responders to infection and acute inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an acute inflammatory response and immune system mobilization following extreme endurance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An expansion of neutrophils; an inverse correlation between neutrophil and lymphocyte numbers has been documented in severe cases of COVID-19.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Innate immune response, phagocytosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe acute COVID-19 illness.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to immunopathology, excessive tissue infiltration, and acute respiratory distress syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly fewer neutrophils were observed in women compared to men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary immune cells involved in acute inflammation, mediating immune response and secreting inflammatory mediators.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sex differences in seniors, contributing to various inflammatory indices (NLR, SII, NHR), and reflecting inflammatory response and immunoaging.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammation development; a high number promotes inflammation and neutrophilia inhibits immune response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during congested period), unchanged (during uncongested period)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at T3 (congested period) compared with T2 and T1 (0.002 < p < 0.04, -0.78 < ES < -0.40); increased occurrence of neutrophilia. Resting values were unchanged after the 6-week uncongested period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Granulocyte mediating innate immune response and inflammation, reducing infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Congested (T3) and uncongested match play periods in elite soccer players.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Changes indicate inflammatory processes or stress related to training load and insufficient post-exercise recovery; increases may compensate for decreased functionality during high-intensity training, impacting the immune system. Unchanged levels with improved performance indicate effective training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Raised significantly (up to 200-250%) during match 1, remained high until the end of match 2, and exhibited a slower decrease during long recovery.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary immune cells involved in acute inflammation and bacterial defense.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated beach volleyball competition (during matches, long recovery).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute inflammatory response and immune activation due to exercise, reflecting a classic intensity-dependent immune reaction to metabolic stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Comparable across sexes and timepoints (p = 0.194), indicating no significant sex-specific changes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Type of white blood cell, crucial for innate immunity, primarily targeting bacterial and fungal infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests stable innate immune dynamics with no significant sex-specific alterations.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes over the measuring time points. Demonstrated moderate reliability (ICC values between 0.51 – 0.74).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Type of white blood cell, critical for innate immune response and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not significantly responsive to exercise. Its moderate reliability, coupled with no significant changes, questions its suitability as a robust biomarker for exercise response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, critical for the innate immune response, primarily fighting bacterial infections.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase in professional soccer players, assessed at baseline and post-PS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not reported in this study, but generally indicates immune function and response to infection/inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased during the heating phase of both EXE and EXO trials (EXO: p < 0.05). In the EXO trial, NAM returned to normal during recovery, whereas in the EXE trial, levels remained suppressed during the recovery phase (p < 0.01). Post-intervention levels were significantly different between trials (p < 0.01). Detected in concentrations higher than the LLOQ of 50 nM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Form of Vitamin B3, a precursor to NAD+ and involved in energy metabolism, DNA repair, and anti-inflammatory processes. Intimately connected with NAD+; NAD+ generated via the kynurenine pathway may influence NAM levels.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Heat stress (EXE and EXO trials) induced by core temperature increases, with samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments up to 39°C and subsequent decrease until 37.5°C, particularly during heating and recovery phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates changes in NAD+ metabolism and cellular energy status, potentially reflecting metabolic demand or stress-induced consumption, possibly influenced by acute exercise and modulated by aryl hydrocarbon receptor stimulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No measurable presence in the athletes' urine during the whole study (from  148 to +48 h).

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: linked to increased nitrate/nitrite-reducing activity

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Microbial metabolic pathway that converts nitrate to nitrite, impacting nitric oxide production
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low-carbohydrate high-fat (LCHF) diet in elite race walkers
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased activity suggests enhanced potential for nitric oxide generation, which can influence cardiovascular function and performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates current and potential blood and urine biomarkers for osteoarthritis (OA), focusing on markers derived from type II collagen and aggrecan to reflect joint tissue turnover. The review details their molecular targets, measurement methods, and diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic utility in assessing cartilage degradation, bone turnover, and disease progression, including responses to treatments. It highlights both established and preclinical markers, emphasizing the complexities of cleavage sites, the need for multi-protease inhibition strategies, and further biomarker validation, while noting a continued lack of operationalized in vitro diagnostics and markers for patient endotyping.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Osteoarthritis (OA) biomarker investigation, Doxycycline treatment, Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT), Cathepsin K inhibition, Collagen hydrolysate supplementation, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced remodeling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic dose or intervention protocols are primarily reported, as this is a narrative review focusing on biomarkers for Osteoarthritis and their utility in drug development and patient management. However, some treatments were mentioned: Doxycycline was investigated in a randomized controlled trial in 120 obese knee OA patients (specific dose/duration not detailed). Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) was examined for its effect on knee OA patients (specific dose not detailed). Cathepsin K inhibition reduced CTX-I by more than 90% (specific inhibitor dose/duration not reported). Collagen hydrolysate administration led to a modest decrease in CS846 and an elevation in PIIANP (specific dose/duration not reported). No dose-response comparisons were generally reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of low (LV-HIIT) and high (HV-HIIT) volumes of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on vascular-endothelial function, oxidative stress, and atherosclerosis markers in patients after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The 16-week supervised HIIT programs, regardless of volume, led to a volume-dependent enhancement in endothelial function (FMD) and a decrease in oxidative stress (ox-LDL). A reduction in vascular wall thickness (cIMT) was also observed, with LV-HIIT proving sufficient to initiate favorable adaptations and reduce cardiovascular risk. The study also assessed anthropometric and other cardiovascular markers, comparing HIIT groups to an active control.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Unsupervised Physical Activity Recommendations (Active Control, AC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) with two volumes: Low Volume (LV-HIIT) and High Volume (HV-HIIT), and an Active Control (AC) group. LV-HIIT involved 8 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-minute total session. HV-HIIT involved 16 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-40 minute total session. Both supervised HIIT groups exercised 2 non-consecutive days per week for 16 weeks (32 sessions) on treadmills and cycle ergometers, with intensity individualized based on cardiorespiratory fitness, ventilatory thresholds, beat-to-beat HR, and the Böarg scale. The AC group received individualized recommendations for unsupervised physical activity, advised to perform at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity 5–7 days per week for 16 weeks. FMD and ox-LDL changes were volume-dependent (HV-HIIT showing greater effects), while cIMT reduction was similar between LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT, indicating a volume-independent effect for cIMT and confirming LV-HIIT's effectiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the acute and 1-week effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on cardiovascular performance, autonomic control, endothelial function, and a range of molecular biomarkers (inflammatory, hormonal, oxidative stress, nitric oxide synthesis, and mitochondrial regulation) in physically inactive postmenopausal women (aged 50-70) with systemic arterial hypertension, both at rest, during submaximal aerobic exercise, and throughout recovery. The aim is to provide nutritional recommendations for optimizing cardiovascular health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with nitrate-rich beetroot juice combined with standardized submaximal aerobic exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice will be administered acutely at 140 mL (800 mg nitrate) on the first day, followed by a daily dose of 70 mL (400 mg nitrate) for 6 subsequent days. A placebo (nitrate-free) juice will serve as control. Exercise consists of a 40-minute treadmill session at a speed corresponding to 65-70% of VO2peak. The study employs a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled design with a 7-day washout period between intervention protocols. Previous research indicated lower doses (200-400 mg nitrate) were insufficient for acute cardiovascular effects, leading to the optimized dosages used here. Additionally, 40 g of whey protein will be provided before executing experimental protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study focuses on developing and validating MiSL, a computational algorithm for identifying mutation-specific synthetic lethal partners and predictive genetic biomarkers in cancer. This involves synthetic lethality-based targeted therapy approaches, computational analysis (MiSL pipeline), and various experimental validation methods including gene knockdown (shRNA, siRNA), CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, pharmacological inhibition (e.g., ACACA inhibitors, AKT1-inhibitor MK-2206), and xenograft models.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The MiSL algorithm analyzed approximately 3,000 primary tumor samples from 12 TCGA cancer datasets, predicting 145,891 synthetic lethal partners for 3,120 mutations, utilizing specific criteria for genomic alterations and statistical thresholds (e.g., Fisher's exact test P value <0.05). Experimental validation involved shRNA screens (54,020 shRNAs targeting 11,194 genes, >20% reduction in reads for SL hits, 16 population doublings), doxycycline induction (1 µg ml⁻¹ for 3-12 days), siRNA (25 nM siGLS), and drug treatments with dose-response IC50 curves (e.g., 2 µM TOFA for ACACA inhibition; IDH1 R132-mutated AML blasts IC50 1.1 µM vs 6 µM for wild-type; MK-2206 for AKT1 inhibition with PIK3CA mutated breast cancer cell lines sensitive at IC50 <1 µM). Specific shRNA knockdown efficiencies were assessed, but general dose-response comparisons for all therapeutic interventions were not explicitly detailed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.
