document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significantly lower in obese at rest; higher post-exercise in both groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Obese females had significantly lower resting levels compared to normal weight females (mean difference: 3,326 pg/ml, -23%, p = 0.04). Both groups showed a progressive increase post-exercise, significantly higher by 24 hours post-exercise (+12%, p = 0.02) compared to pre-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A marker of bone formation and mineralization, produced by osteoblasts and involved in bone turnover.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Resting levels and response 24 hours post-plyometric exercise in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower resting levels in obese adolescents suggest blunted bone formation and turnover, potentially hindering normal bone growth. The exercise-induced increase indicates a beneficial anabolic bone response.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not affected by exercise in the PBO trial or by CHO ingestion during exercise in the immediate (P = 0.343) or short-term (P = 0.786) recovery periods. No concomitant effect on circulating OC concentrations with CHO feeding during exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone involved in bone formation and mineralization, a marker of coupled bone turnover, capable of suppressing IL-6 release, and important in the relationship between bone remodeling and energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During and after strenuous exercise (120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max) with PBO or CHO feeding.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant indicator in this context, suggesting stable osteocalcin levels regardless of exercise or CHO intake, and it was not involved in the observed effects of CHO feeding on bone turnover.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 12-week (3-month) food-based vitamin D3 fortification intervention on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, bone turnover markers (Osteocalcin, Bone specific Alkaline Phosphatase, Procollagen type 1 amino-terminal propeptide, C-terminal crosslinked telopeptide of type 1 collagen), and muscle strength (handgrip, knee extension, chair-standing) in 143 women of Danish and Pakistani origin, aged 18-50 years, living in Denmark and at risk of vitamin D deficiency. Despite a significant increase in serum 25(OH)D concentrations in the fortified groups, the intervention did not result in significant changes in bone turnover markers or muscle strength. Baseline characteristics including anthropometrics and vitamin D status were also assessed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Food-based vitamin D fortification
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 12-week (3-month) randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled winter intervention trial. The intervention group (143 women) received 30 μg vitamin D3/day (analyzed as 29 μg/day total vitamin D content) through fortified daily foods (150g yoghurt, 60g cheese, 1 egg, 1 small crisp-bread); the placebo group received similar non-fortified products. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and the study noted potential insufficient power to detect changes in secondary endpoints.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant change after 12 weeks of vitamin D fortification (P > 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of bone turnover, particularly bone formation, reflecting bone remodeling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12-week intervention with vitamin D fortified foods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone formation activity and overall bone health. Lack of significant change suggests the intervention did not notably affect bone formation, possibly due to adequate baseline vitamin D status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated teriparatide (TPTD) as an adjunct therapy for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), finding it significantly shortened treatment periods, reduced surgical interventions, improved bone mineral density in the lumbar spine and femur neck, and favorably altered bone turnover markers (CTX, OC, 25-OH-vitamin D, calcium).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Teriparatide (TPTD) administration for Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (MRONJ)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Teriparatide (Forsteo®) was administered as a 20 µg daily subcutaneous injection for >3 months and up to 24 months. Patients also received 1,000 IU/day of oral Vitamin D. TPTD treatment led to significantly shorter surgical recovery periods (3.89 ± 2.71 months vs 6.64 ± 6.38 months, p = 0.030) and fewer surgical procedures (average 1.26 vs 1.82, p = 0.049) in surgical patients compared to non-TPTD counterparts. The overall treatment period was also shorter in the TPTD group (5.5 months vs 6.75 months in non-TPTD), though not statistically significant.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in both TPTD and non-TPTD groups post-treatment, with OC levels being higher in the TPTD group (33.653, p = 0.012) and showing greater increases compared to the non-TPTD group. Significantly increased only in the surgical treatment group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone formation marker, produced by osteoblasts, indicating osteoblast activity and bone turnover.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MRONJ treatment with or without Teriparatide (TPTD), with conservative or surgical approaches, and following discontinuation or substitution of osteoporosis drugs.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced bone metabolism, positive treatment response, and a greater potential for more effective MRONJ treatment, particularly in the TPTD group, suggesting enhanced bone formation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 2-year prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in bone remodeling and turnover markers in children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from diagnosis through chemotherapy. It revealed that ALL onset significantly slows bone remodeling, with significantly lower bone turnover markers at diagnosis compared to controls. During chemotherapy, particularly the induction phase, these markers increased, suggesting a recovery of bone turnover, and a potential balance in active bone remodeling by the end of therapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Risk-adapted multiagent antileukemic chemotherapy, specifically for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), including Glucocorticoid (GC) therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 2-year prospective longitudinal study involved chemotherapy according to international AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 and ESPhALL 2017 protocols, with patients stratified by risk (standard, intermediate, high). The treatment included induction, reinduction/delayed intensification (two phases of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy), and a maintenance phase. Blood sampling was conducted at 5 time points (T0-T4) from diagnosis until treatment cessation. No specific numerical drug dosages were reported, but it was noted that different glucocorticoid doses did not significantly alter bone marker profiles after intensive therapy phases.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: initially lower at diagnosis compared to controls, then increased during treatment, followed by a slight decrease towards the end of therapy
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower at diagnosis compared to controls (p < 0.001), then showed a significant increase during treatment from 23.6 (17.1–28.2) ng/mL at onset to 122.4 (97.4–143.0) ng/mL at T3 (p < 0.001), particularly at T0-T1, followed by a slight decrease at T4 (end of therapy).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A non-collagenous marker reflecting osteoblast activity and bone formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls, and during various chemotherapy treatment phases (T0-T4), especially during induction (T0-T1) and towards the end of therapy (T4).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates decreased bone formation at the onset of leukemia, followed by an increase during induction chemotherapy reflecting changes in osteoblast activity, with a subsequent decrease at the end of therapy suggesting a potential balance and recovery of active bone remodeling in growing children.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to evaluate bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome (NS) to understand their bone status and explore genotype-phenotype correlations. It revealed increased bone resorption in NS patients, evidenced by significantly elevated serum C-telopeptides of type I collagen (CTX) levels, and a non-significant increase in RANKL. The study also discussed the influence of RAS/MAPK signaling pathway alterations and SHP2 protein on osteoclastic activity and the effects of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment on bone parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Case-Control Study evaluating bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome, including an analysis of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment effects.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional, case-control study compared 28 children with Noonan Syndrome to 35 healthy controls. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was administered to the main cohorts. Within the NS cohort, some subjects had received or were receiving rhGH therapy, but no specific dosages, duration, or dose-response comparisons for rhGH treatment were reported, and no significant differences in bone parameters were found between treated and untreated subjects in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were found between NS patients and controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone formation marker secreted by osteoblasts, reflecting osteoblast activity and involvement in bone mineralization.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children with Noonan Syndrome (NS).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not a significant indicator of altered bone formation in this cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the clinical relevance and efficacy of collagen X breakdown product (CXM) as a blood-based biomarker for endochondral long bone fracture repair in both healthy individuals and patients with tibia or femur fractures. It characterized CXM expression patterns, stability across demographics (age, sex), correlation with other bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, osteocalcin, leptin, sclerostin), and its utility in predicting healing prognosis (early, normal, delayed). The findings showed CXM levels are low in healthy individuals, peak around 25-35 days post-fracture, can be reliably measured via dried blood spots, and offer an earlier, quantitative indication of healing compared to traditional radiographic methods, supporting its prospective use in fracture studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of natural long bone fracture repair, with a secondary analysis of a Vitamin D3 supplementation trial (VitaShock).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on observing biomarker changes in patients with acute closed or low-grade open tibial or femoral shaft fractures (Gustilo type I or II, AO/OTA type 42), without applying a specific therapeutic dose as an intervention. For the secondary analysis of the VitaShock trial, multiple Vitamin D3 dosing strategies were assessed, but specific dose details were not provided, and no significant difference in CXM response was found compared to placebo. Longitudinal blood samples were collected at various standard-of-care clinical visits over a period up to 48 weeks post-fracture.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: positively correlates with CXM (in normal healing patients), lower in nonunions
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: r = 0.26, p = 0.0411 (with CXM in normal healing patients). Lower expression in nonunions (cited from prior studies).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Bone turnover marker, established biomarker for bone formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fracture healing, normal healing conditions, nonunion conditions.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone turnover in the context of fracture healing. Associated with bone formation, and positively correlated with CXM during normal fracture healing; lower expression is associated with nonunion, suggesting its role in assessing delayed healing.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effect of NPN_1 (a Vicia faba hydrolysate) supplementation on strength recovery, fatigue, and muscle homeostasis markers following resistance exercise-induced delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in healthy male volunteers, concluding that NPN_1 significantly improved strength recovery, reduced fatigue, and positively modulated several plasma myokines, including suppressed myostatin expression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional supplementation with NPN_1 (PeptiStrong™, a Vicia faba hydrolysate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: NPN_1 was administered at 2.4 g/day (5 capsules) or placebo for 14 to 17 days. On day 14, delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) was induced through resistance exercise, with strength recovery, fatigue, and biomarker analysis performed at 0, 2, 48, and 72 hours post-DOMS. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower expression/concentration in the NPN_1 group compared to placebo over the study course (p = 0.009), implying NPN_1 mitigated the increase seen in placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in muscle-bone crosstalk, metabolic regulation, and muscle adaptation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exhaustive exercise (DOMS induction)/EIMD, with NPN_1 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower increase with NPN_1 might indicate a more favorable state of muscle metabolism, reduced catabolic signaling, and a potential mechanism for reduced fatigue.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of human bone donor age on the osteoinductive capacity of decellularized bone scaffolds and their conditioned media (DBCM), and their ability to promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). The main findings indicate that older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media exhibit superior osteoinductive capacity, enhancing osteogenic differentiation of BM-MSCs, which is potentially linked to reduced IGFBP1 bioavailability and increased porosity/altered trabecular architecture in aged bone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro assessment of human decellularized bone scaffolds and conditioned media for osteoinductive capacity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study's primary variable was the age of the human bone donor (young: ≤50 years, range 34–49; old: ≥70 years, range 72–84). Decellularized bone cubes (1 cm³) were obtained from human femoral heads. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) from both young (≤50 years, range 44–49) and old (≥70 years, range 72–81) donors were seeded onto these scaffolds (0.5x10^6 BM-MSCs per cube) or cultured in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM) for up to 28 days. The investigation focused on age-dependent differences in scaffold properties and their influence on BM-MSC osteogenic differentiation, rather than dose-response comparisons of a therapeutic agent.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) cultured on decellularized bone scaffolds and in decellularized bone conditioned media (DBCM)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally increased in all BM-MSC/scaffold/DBCM combinations compared to controls. BM-MSCs (both young and old donor) cultured on old donor bone scaffolds or in old donor DBCM consistently showed significantly higher gene expression for RUNX2, Osteopontin, and Osteocalcin compared to young donor bone or DBCM. A notable exception was that old donor BM-MSCs showed no significant increase in Osteocalcin expression, indicating impaired late-stage differentiation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates the activation and progression of osteogenesis, the process of bone formation and maturation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Osteogenic differentiation of young and old donor BM-MSCs seeded on decellularized human bone scaffolds from young or old donors, and in conditioned media derived from these scaffolds.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Enhanced osteogenic differentiation, particularly by older donor bone scaffolds and their conditioned media, suggests superior osteoinductive capacity for bone tissue engineering. Impaired late-stage differentiation in old donor BM-MSCs indicates potential limitations for these cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a protein network involved in extracellular matrix, cartilage development, and osteoblast signaling pathways, implicated in vascular calcification and early cognitive decline.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in extracellular matrix, cartilage development, and osteoblast signaling pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Vascular calcification, extracellular matrix alterations, early phases of cognitive decline.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Component of a protein network indicating vascular calcification and extracellular matrix alterations as a major component of aging that underlies early cognitive decline.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Co-culture supernatant of osteoarthritic knee joint explants (bone-cartilage-synovium tissues)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (due to IL-1β stimulation), then higher (after hyperacute serum treatment)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: IL-1β stimulation inhibited its secretion. In response to hyperacute serum treatment, concentrations were significantly elevated, indicating enhanced production.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glycoprotein involved in bone mineralization, cell adhesion, and collagen binding, secreted by regenerating chondrocytes, osteoblasts, and bone marrow progenitor cells; crucial for bone and cartilage matrix formation and serves as a tissue remodeling marker.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Inhibition by IL-1β stimulation and subsequent enhanced production during hyperacute serum treatment in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Initial inhibition by IL-1β indicates a negative effect on cartilage and bone remodeling. Enhanced production due to hyperacute serum suggests promotion of bone remodeling, repair, and overall enhanced regenerative processes in bone and cartilage, indicating a beneficial effect on OA knee joint health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scientific roadmap by the Heart Failure Association comprehensively addresses the complex and heterogeneous nature of fibrosis in heart failure, aiming to improve its definition, quantification, and treatment. It reviews mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis across various etiologies like pressure overload, aging, and cardiomyopathies, emphasizing the central role of TGF-β, collagen deposition, and myofibroblast activity. The document discusses challenges in detecting fibrosis using circulating biomarkers, proposing a framework for assessment and a roadmap for future research to identify individual fibrotic mechanisms, novel therapeutic targets, and diagnostic tools. It also evaluates diverse anti-fibrotic strategies, including pharmacological agents and non-coding RNA-based treatments, highlighting the need for targeted, multi-pathway approaches given the complexity of the fibrotic process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anti-fibrotic therapies for heart failure, including established drugs like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, as well as specific anti-fibrotic agents like pirfenidone. Investigational strategies include targeting the TGF-β pathway (e.g., TGF-β inhibitors, CTGF inhibitors like FG-3019), MAPK pathways (e.g., ERK inhibitors), inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1α), neuregulin-1 administration, Matrix Metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitors, Galectin-3 inhibitors, and non-coding RNA-based treatments (microRNA and long non-coding RNAs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a review document, and as such, no specific therapeutic doses, intensities, or durations are consistently reported for any intervention, nor are dose-response comparisons detailed. While some agents like Pirfenidone and non-coding RNA modulators show utility in experimental models and clinical trials (e.g., microRNA-21 inhibitor in a Phase II trial), precise quantitative dosage or detailed treatment parameters are generally absent, reflecting a discussion of general approaches and their limitations, including a noted 'lack of precision' in current therapies. For example, MMP-12i was given 3h post-MI, but without specific dosage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: At later time points, it contributes to the progression of fibrosis as a fibroblast-specific factor. No quantification of levels or contribution provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Fibroblast-specific factor contributing to the progression of fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Later stages of fibrosis progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its contribution to fibrosis progression identifies it as a potential target for anti-fibrotic therapies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Multifunctional glycoprotein involved in ECM remodeling and inflammation. Upregulation reflects its role in promoting inflammation, tissue injury, and fibrosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 and COPD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlates with disease severity and outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Improvements reported across various measures (e.g., significant increases in TAC, TAS, ORAC (p < 0.05)), indicating enhanced intrinsic antioxidant defense.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protection against oxidative stress and maintenance of cellular redox homeostasis, representing the sum of all antioxidants.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation (6 mg to 100 mg before exercise or 5 mg after exercise) in highly trained athletes to counteract exercise-induced RONS overproduction.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved overall antioxidant defense against free radicals and enhanced cellular protection, leading to reduced oxidative damage and improved recovery from exercise-induced stress.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated the Expanded Multimodal Analysis (EMMA) framework for the ultra-early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs). EMMA integrates cfDNA methylation (DMRs), copy number variations (CNVs), and fragmentation features (FSRs) derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and detection rates across all ESCC stages and IENs compared to single-modal approaches. The study also demonstrated the utility of cfDNA methylation markers for molecular subtyping of ESCC, revealing associations with distinct molecular subtypes, tumor microenvironments, gene expression profiles, and survival outcomes, thus offering potential for dynamic molecular monitoring and therapeutic guidance to improve patient survival.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Method Development and Biomarker-based Molecular Subtyping
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on the development and validation of diagnostic methods for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) and precancerous lesions (IENs) using multimodal cfDNA analysis. This involved Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) of 460 cfDNA samples (230 patients with non-metastatic ESCC/precancerous lesions and 230 matched healthy controls) to identify optimal differentially methylated regions (50 DMRs), copy number variations (153 recurrent CNV regions), and fragmentation features (83 FSRs). Machine learning models (ESCC-cfMeth, DMR plus CNV, and EMMA) were developed with 10-fold cross-validation in a discovery cohort and validated in independent cohorts. The study also explored biomarker-based molecular subtyping of 155 ESCC patients into three groups based on cfDNA methylation. ESCC patients underwent surgery or endoscopic resection, and IEN patients underwent endoscopic resection for sample collection, but no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were investigated, as the study's primary aim was diagnostic and prognostic marker development.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of total dietary antioxidant intake and capacity on body antioxidant mechanisms and exhaustive exercise-induced oxidative damage in ultra-endurance athletes. It examined physiological responses, including oxidative stress biomarkers (8-iso PGF2a, TOS, TAS, OSI) and lactate levels, during and after a combined cycling and treadmill exhaustive exercise protocol. Key findings indicated that higher dietary antioxidant intake was negatively correlated with pre-exercise total oxidant status and post-exercise increases in 8-iso PGF2a, while positively correlating with post-exercise increases in total antioxidant status and blood lactate concentrations. A higher dietary antioxidant capacity also positively influenced antioxidant defense and blood lactate removal (in both sexes) and running time to exhaustion (in males), but did not affect post-exercise heart rate recovery or perceived exertion.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Exercise and Dietary Antioxidant Intake Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ultra-endurance athletes underwent an acute exhaustive exercise protocol comprising 45 minutes on a cycle ergometer at 65% VO2max, immediately followed by a treadmill test at 75% VO2max to volitional exhaustion (median running time ~26-27 min, RPE 19). document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review discusses the practical application, limitations, and recommendations for blood biomarker profiling and monitoring in high-performance athletes, aiming to optimize physiology, nutrition, training, recovery, and prevent injury/illness. It covers various physiological and procedural factors affecting analysis, the importance of individualized reference ranges, the utility of specific nutritional and stress-related biomarkers (e.g., Omega-3 Index, carotenoids, redox status, glutamine, sex and thyroid hormones, IGF-1, cortisol, iron, tHbmass, inflammatory markers, CK, urea, melatonin, vitamins), and considerations for managing energy availability, training load, and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Comprehensive Blood Biomarker Profiling and Monitoring for Athlete Management, Nutritional Intervention, and Training Adaptation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The therapeutic approach involves comprehensive blood biomarker profiling (infrequent screening for deficiencies, several months apart) and monitoring (frequent assessment of adaptation/recovery, days or weeks apart) in athletes. This strategy is tailored to individual needs, sport, sex, and training context, utilizing individualized adaptive ranges and critical difference thresholds. It includes careful consideration of pre-analytic factors (e.g., posture, tourniquet use, centrifugation time, time of day, psychological stress, fasting status, menstrual cycle day, hydration status, duration/intensity/mode of prior exercise) and minimizing blood draw volumes, such as the removal of an average of 180 ml (range 82–314 ml) of blood in a simulated altitude study which negated hypoxia-induced erythropoiesis and aerobic performance gains. Specific interventions include targeted dietary/antioxidant supplementation (e.g., Omega-3 to increase OM3I from ~4.5% to ~6%, N-acetylcysteine for low red blood cell glutathione, Vitamin C for low plasma concentrations), iron supplementation for deficiency (e.g., ferritin < 12 ng mL−1 leading to dramatic increases in tHbmass), and nutritional adjustments for energy availability management (e.g., during persistently excessive endurance exercise, 8 weeks of gross energy deficiency, or carbohydrate restriction impacting testosterone/cortisol responses). The monitoring is applied across various contexts like intense exercise, eccentric loading, single matches, long-haul travel, sleep loss, and season-long competitive demands, with biomarker responses proportional to the imposed stress and recovery status.

Response to exercise is a well-established method to assess oxidative stress (OS) and predict adaptation; overloaded athletes display a diminished plasma antioxidant response to an exercise test. Modifiable through diet. Increased exercise-associated lipid peroxidation with exercise (a type of OS biomarker) on a low antioxidant diet. Vitamin insufficiencies increase OS. Significant changes observed in relation to workload across various time points of the season in elite soccer players; periods of oxidative stress (OS) occur in association with periods of higher training loads and competition. OS has been termed a 'molecular switch' for upregulating antioxidant systems. Red Blood Cell Glutathione (GSH): low/high levels (not quantified numerically).

Regulates oxidative stress and antioxidant defense; acts as a 'molecular switch' for upregulating antioxidant systems for adaptation. GSH is a ubiquitous antioxidant enzyme, involved in redox status.

Diminished response indicates adaptation issues or predicts lack of adaptation in overloaded athletes. Increased OS is associated with decreased physical performance. Identifying a blood redox profile can identify individuals whose physical performance may be enhanced through the correction of redox 'deficiency' with appropriate antioxidant treatment. In the 'low' GSH group, NAC improved both aerobic and anaerobic capacity. In the 'high' GSH group, NAC had an adverse effect on aerobic performance. Measuring biomarkers of redox status may aid in individualization and frugal use of antioxidant supplementation. Indicates capacity to train and recover, propensity for successful adaptation, informs recovery needs; identifies maladaptation (performance plateau) and fatigue; associated with healthy adaptation and avoidance of disease when balanced.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the acute and 1-week effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on cardiovascular performance, autonomic control, endothelial function, and a range of molecular biomarkers (inflammatory, hormonal, oxidative stress, nitric oxide synthesis, and mitochondrial regulation) in physically inactive postmenopausal women (aged 50-70) with systemic arterial hypertension, both at rest, during submaximal aerobic exercise, and throughout recovery. The aim is to provide nutritional recommendations for optimizing cardiovascular health.

The study employs a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled design with a 7-day washout period between intervention protocols. Previous research indicated lower doses (200-400 mg nitrate) were insufficient for acute cardiovascular effects, leading to the optimized dosages used here. Additionally, 40 g of whey protein will be provided before executing experimental protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated (p < 0.001, main treatment effect) for both ANS-LD (p < 0.01) and ANS-HD (p < 0.001) compared with PLA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of low (LV-HIIT) and high (HV-HIIT) volumes of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on vascular-endothelial function, oxidative stress, and atherosclerosis markers in patients after an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The 16-week supervised HIIT programs, regardless of volume, led to a volume-dependent enhancement in endothelial function (FMD) and a decrease in oxidative stress (ox-LDL). A reduction in vascular wall thickness (cIMT) was also observed, with LV-HIIT proving sufficient to initiate favorable adaptations and reduce cardiovascular risk. The study also assessed anthropometric and other cardiovascular markers, comparing HIIT groups to an active control.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Unsupervised Physical Activity Recommendations (Active Control, AC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) with two volumes: Low Volume (LV-HIIT) and High Volume (HV-HIIT), and an Active Control (AC) group. LV-HIIT involved 8 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-minute total session. HV-HIIT involved 16 minutes of high-intensity exercise (R3) within a 20-40 minute total session. Both supervised HIIT groups exercised 2 non-consecutive days per week for 16 weeks (32 sessions) on treadmills and cycle ergometers, with intensity individualized based on cardiorespiratory fitness, ventilatory thresholds, beat-to-beat HR, and the Böarg scale. The AC group received individualized recommendations for unsupervised physical activity, advised to perform at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity 5–7 days per week for 16 weeks. FMD and ox-LDL changes were volume-dependent (HV-HIIT showing greater effects), while cIMT reduction was similar between LV-HIIT and HV-HIIT, indicating a volume-independent effect for cIMT and confirming LV-HIIT's effectiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced content.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Normoxic (NX) apnea.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates severe systemic hypoxemia and the severity of the hypoxemic-hypercapnic challenge.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery (VO2Rec) measures, especially VO2T12.5% (time to recover 12.5% of peak VO2), in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. The study suggests its regular inclusion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing protocols.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Pharmacological treatment (Aficamten, a cardiac myosin inhibitor)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Aficamten was administered for 24 weeks in a phase 3 randomized controlled trial, compared against placebo. Doses were individualized to achieve the lowest effective dose, targeting a Valsalva Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Gradient (LVOT-G) <30 mm Hg while maintaining a left ventricular ejection fraction ">=\u00ad50%. Specific daily dosages (mg) and dose-response comparisons were not detailed, but treatment led to proportional improvements in cardiac function and biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In MGH-ExS patients, a longer VO2T12.5% (">=35 seconds) was associated with elevated exercise pulmonary capillary wedge pressure to cardiac output slope (P <0.0001). For each 15-second increase in VO2T12.5%, the hazard ratio for heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death was 1.54 (95% CI, 1.35	1.76; P <0.001). In SEQUOIA-HCM, baseline was 45	20 seconds and improved 8 seconds (95% CI, 	12 to 	5 seconds; P <0.001) with aficamten vs. placebo at 24 weeks. Aficamten-treated participants were 3.7 times more likely to improve VO2T12.5% by ">=15 seconds (OR, 3.7 [95% CI, 1.9	6.9]; NNT=4.8). Initial mean	SD 29	17 seconds in MGH-ExS cohort. Prolonged (">=35 seconds) associated with HR 2.52 [1.76	3.62] for adverse outcomes, modestly attenuated to 1.76 [1.20	2.60] (P=0.003) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. An average relative magnitude of 18% improvement was observed in response to aficamten treatment. VO2T12.5% ">=35 seconds predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization. No significant increase in diagnostic certainty based on comparison of ROC AUC values (P >0.05 for VO2T50% and VO2T25% versus VO2T12.5%) beyond this point.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery, an indicator of metabolic resilience and cardiac performance. Captures metabolic consequences of increasing metabolic rate during exercise, provides a quantitative measure of metabolic resilience, and reflects cardiocentric exercise limitations. Indicator of early oxygen uptake recovery kinetics, reflecting the efficiency of the cardiovascular system to restore baseline metabolic state after exercise. Integrates cardiovascular and metabolic responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-exercise oxygen uptake recovery during cardiopulmonary exercise testing; response to aficamten treatment for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). Post-exercise recovery in patients with dyspnea on exertion (DOE), established severe heart failure (HF), and symptomatic oHCM. Early recovery from incremental ramp exercise; aficamten treatment in oHCM patients; differentiation of HFpEF-HDI from NCD. Dyspneic individuals with HFpEF; symptomatic oHCM; cardiac myosin inhibition treatment (aficamten); evaluation of cardiac reserve capacity during exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects cardiac performance during exercise, predicts heart failure event-free survival, indicates cardiospecific limitations to exercise capacity, and is a potential endpoint for cardiac interventions. Prolonged VO2Rec is linked to worse cardiac output augmentation during exercise and increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes (HF hospitalization and all-cause death), independent of peak VO2. It serves as a sensitive noninvasive surrogate for identifying impaired cardiac performance during exercise. Discriminates impaired central cardiac function in HFpEF-HDI (AUC 0.72 vs 0.63 for VO2 T 0%, P <0.001). Prolonged VO2 T 12.5% (">=35 seconds) predicts increased risk for heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death. Improvement with aficamten treatment is associated with reduced NT-proBNP, hs-cTnI, and LVOT-G. Identifies impaired cardiac performance in HFpEF, predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, risk-stratifies individuals with impaired peak VO2 or elevated NT-proBNP with underlying symptomatic HFpEF, indicates responsiveness to cardiac-specific treatment, and prolonged VO2T12.5% relates to elevated filling pressures. Should be considered for inclusion in standard CPET protocols; promising noninvasive measurement for defining impaired cardiac performance in human cardiac drug development randomized controlled trials.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the physiological and biochemical responses, including oxygen uptake, power output, and arterial lactate concentrations, during two maximal incremental cycle ergometer tests performed 24 hours apart in female Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) patients compared to healthy controls. The findings revealed that previous exercise deteriorates physical performance and increases lactate accumulation in ME/CFS patients, while it improves lactate handling in healthy subjects, indicating a disturbed metabolic response to exertion in ME/CFS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Repeated Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), specifically maximal incremental ramp tests.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two maximal incremental ramp tests (CPET 1 and CPET 2) were performed 24 hours apart on a cycle ergometer. Each test included a 2-min resting phase and 2 min of unloaded pedaling, followed by a linear increase in power output until volitional exhaustion. Increment rates were individually set (10-24 W/min for ME/CFS patients; 15-30 W/min for controls) to reach VO2peak within 8-12 min. Arterial lactate concentrations were measured every 30 seconds during exercise. Blood sampling during CPET 1 amounted to approximately 150–200 mL. No specific dose-response comparisons for different fixed exercise intensities were reported beyond the comparisons between the two repeated tests.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of different cycling exercise intensities (70% and 90% of ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and cadences (30-110 rpm) on cardiopulmonary, metabolic, and skeletal muscle oxygenation responses in healthy participants. While higher intensity and cadence led to increased cardiorespiratory and metabolic activity, skeletal muscle oxygenation (measured by tissue saturation index and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis was not substantially affected, suggesting it may not be a primary factor in self-selected cadence at moderate exercise intensity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cycling Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed cycling exercise at two intensities (70% and 90% of the ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and five cadences (30, 50, 70, 90, and 110 rpm), with each bout lasting 4 minutes in a randomized sequence, interspersed with active recovery. While cardiopulmonary and metabolic responses increased with higher intensity (90% Tvent) and higher cadences (especially 110 rpm), skeletal muscle oxygenation (TSI and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis showed no significant dose-response across the tested intensities or cadences.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.
