document_context_data.document_summary: This review comprehensively explores Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) as crucial mediators of intercellular communication, highlighting their dual roles in health and disease. It examines their potential as personalized diagnostic biomarkers across various conditions including viral infections, cancer, neurological, kidney, autoimmune, metabolic, and pro-thrombotic diseases. The document also investigates EVs as promising therapeutic agents, drug delivery vehicles, and regenerative therapeutics, discussing their involvement in disease pathogenesis (e.g., spreading misfolded proteins, facilitating viral replication) and their protective functions (e.g., neuroprotection, inflammation regulation, aggregate prevention, tissue repair). Challenges in EV isolation, standardization, and clinical translation are also addressed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, EV-based drug delivery, and EV modulation/depletion.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily reviews the conceptual and potential applications of EVs as therapeutics, drug delivery vehicles, and methods for EV modulation or depletion across various diseases (e.g., neurodegenerative, cancer, age-related conditions). While neuroprotection was observed with therapeutically administered EVs in in vitro models, and EV depletion via Hemopurifier™ is noted for cancer, specific dose regimens, intensities, or durations for most EV therapies or dose-response comparisons are not detailed. Mentions of 'lowering the infusion rate' for immune evasion and administering 'EVs from young mice to old mice' are qualitative examples without precise quantitative data.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detectable in ADn in Braak stages I to VI and 'pre-Braak' stage 0. Consistently exhibited p-tau pathology. Preferential spread between vesicular glutamate transporter type 2-containing subcortical terminals and ADn dendrites.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Misfolded and modified form of tau protein, a hallmark of tauopathies, involved in neurodegeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early stages of tau pathology, spatial navigation disruption, neurodegeneration.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Heightened vulnerability of ADn to p-tau likely contributes to disorientation, serving as an early sign of dementia and a potential target for identifying individuals at risk of memory impairments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol details a prospective observational longitudinal study to develop and validate the Imperial Comprehensive Cognitive Assessment in Cerebrovascular Disease (IC3), a novel digital tool for detecting post-stroke cognitive deficits. The study aims to recruit 300 acute stroke patients and longitudinally investigate the relationship between cognition, psychosocial status, MRI brain imaging, and various blood biomarkers (including NFL, GFAP, brain-derived tau, phosphorylated tau forms, Aβ42/40 ratio, apolipoprotein E genotype, and polygenic risk scores) over 12 months post-ictus. The overarching goal is to identify reliable multimodal recovery indicators, patients at risk of progressive cognitive decline, and facilitate personalized therapy allocation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational longitudinal study for post-stroke cognitive impairment monitoring, biomarker identification, and validation of a novel digital cognitive assessment tool (IC3).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study is a 12-month longitudinal observational design involving repeated measures collected at baseline (0-15 days post-stroke), 3, 6, and 12 months post-ictus. It includes a digital cognitive assessment (IC3) comprising 22 tasks, lasting 60-70 minutes, administered via web-browser. Blood samples are collected from 200 patients and MRI imaging from 300 patients (at 3 and 12 months), along with 50 age-matched controls. No therapeutic dose comparisons are reported as it is an observational and diagnostic tool development protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Aimed to be characterized over the first year after stroke, with an expectation of being raised and showing longitudinal change over a 1-year period.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Aimed to be quantified over the first year after stroke and related to MRI measures and cognitive/functional outcomes; expected to detect any true change in mean over a 1-year period with an effect size of 0.41.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Biomarker of Alzheimer’s disease; involved in neurodegeneration and related to tau pathologies and neurodegenerative dementias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the impact of sleep quality improvement, specifically through treatment for sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), on neuropsychological symptoms and Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer's. The study found that sleep treatment significantly improved sleep quality, neuropsychological scores (including MoCA, HRSD-24, and HAMA), and reduced blood Aβ 42/40 ratio and Tau-pT181 levels. It highlighted that a complete recovery of sleep quality is crucial for full improvement in cognitive and depressive symptoms and Aβ 42/40 ratio, and identified blood Aβ 42/40 ratio as a significant predictive factor for sleep quality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sleep quality improvement for sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) using continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) ventilation, alongside standard donepezil treatment for Alzheimer's disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-month sleep treatment was administered, primarily continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) ventilation for sleep-disordered breathing, in conjunction with donepezil (5-10 mg, every night). The study emphasized that a complete recovery of sleep quality (PSQI score "less than or equal to" 5 post-treatment) was crucial for achieving full improvements in neuropsychological scores (MoCA, HRSD-24) and blood Aβ 42/40 ratio, although Tau-pT181 levels significantly reduced in both completely recovered and partially recovered patients. No specific CPAP pressure settings or dose-response comparisons for CPAP itself were reported beyond the impact of overall sleep recovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients with sleep-disordered breathing compared to non-SDB cases. After 6-month sleep treatment, blood levels were significantly reduced overall, and notably, this reduction was observed in both completely recovered (PSQI ">=" 5) and partially recovered (PSQI > 5) patient subgroups. Levels showed a strong correlation with PSQI scores and other neuropsychological scores (HAMA, HRSD-24).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key component of microtubule assembly, regulated by phosphorylation. Phosphorylated tau protein at T181 (Tau-pT181) is a biomarker for neurofibrillary tangles and neurodegeneration, both pathological hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease. Its aberrant aggregation is a major pathogenic factor in AD development and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-month sleep treatment (CPAP) for sleep-disordered breathing in patients with mild-moderate cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease, and in correlation with overall sleep quality.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A crucial indicator of Alzheimer's disease pathology and neurodegeneration; lower levels are associated with improved neuropsychological status. It is associated with sleep-disordered breathing in MCI patients due to Alzheimer's disease and suggests a potential link between sleep disturbance and Tau-pT181 accumulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated blood-derived DNA methylation-based prediction models, including epigenetic scores (epi-LIBRA, epi-CAIDE) and a Multivariate Methylation Risk Score (MMRS), to assess and predict cognitive impairment and dementia (including AD and MCI) in various independent cohorts. The MMRS showed notable predictive capacity for MCI and prospective cognitive decline in AD and Parkinson's disease, and enhanced prediction when combined with traditional biomarkers, though individual epi-CAIDE and epi-LIBRA models performed poorly for AD and MCI status prediction. The study also detailed data preprocessing for various dementia risk factors, CSF biomarkers (amyloid- , tau, p-tau), whole blood DNA methylation profiling, and polygenic scores, aiming to investigate cognitive status and dementia.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Model Development and Validation using Epigenetic Markers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the development and validation of DNA methylation-based predictive models (including MMRS, epi-CAIDE, epi-LIBRA) for cognitive impairment and dementia. Whole blood genome-wide DNA methylation data, genotyping, and CSF biomarkers were utilized from various cohorts (EXTEND, EMIF-AD MBD, PPMI, ADNI, BASE-II) with different age ranges (40-75,  60 years). Models were constructed using machine learning techniques (e.g., ElasticNet, Random Forest, sPLS-DA, RF-RFE) with hyperparameter optimization via cross-validation. The study focused on predictive modeling and model performance comparisons, rather than therapeutic interventions or traditional dose-response relationships.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of tau pathology, relevant for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and cognitive impairment. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Estimated combined hazard ratio of 2.08 when combined with CognitionBrain age gap for dementia progression. Individuals with fluid biomarker levels two standard deviations above average had a 75% probability of dementia progression within five years. Levels were measured using the Lumipulse G 1200 platform.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's disease, dementia progression; measured in the context of clinical dementia and healthy control subjects for diagnostic and cognitive status determination.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts future dementia progression, additive to CognitionBrain age gap for risk prediction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly elevated in the saliva of individuals with AD. Increased in AD patients, with statistically significant results when using ELISA or Western blot assays. However, no significant correlation with CSF tau or brain measures, showing significant variation and relatively low sensitivity and specificity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive study investigated alpha-synuclein (αSN) as a potential diagnostic and monitoring biomarker for Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM). It evaluated αSN immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies and its concentration in serum and muscle homogenates, comparing IBM patients to other myopathies and healthy controls. The findings suggest αSN immunoreactivity in muscle is a promising diagnostic marker, while serum αSN levels could serve as a monitoring biomarker, correlating with disease duration and clinical severity in IBM. The study also explored the diagnostic utility of other established and emerging biomarkers in IBM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational/Diagnostic Biomarker Investigation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved a multimodal assessment of alpha-synuclein (αSN) levels and immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies, muscle tissue homogenates, and serum samples from various cohorts. Muscle biopsies (N=63, including 19 IBM, 21 other inflammatory myopathies, 20 other myopathies, 3 healthy controls) were analyzed by immunohistochemical staining. Serum samples (N=156, including 11 IBM, 25 other inflammatory myopathies, 53 hereditary myopathies, 30 mitochondriopathies, 37 healthy controls) were assessed by ELISA. Muscle homogenates were also examined (N=17 IBM, N=19 other inflammatory myopathies, N=5 hereditary myopathies, N=2 healthy controls). IBM patients were stratified by disease severity (IBMFRS) and disease duration for serum αSN analysis. No interventional dose or therapeutic comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic and monitoring biomarker evaluation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the transferability and performance of European-derived Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS) across diverse global populations, demonstrating consistent associations with AD risk and biomarkers and improved prediction in non-European ancestries when including the APOE region, while also detailing the comprehensive methodological framework for generating these scores.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Application, evaluation, and methodological development of Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study developed and evaluated polygenic scores (PGS) for Alzheimer's disease (AD). PGS ALZ was derived from 83 independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) excluding the APOE locus, and an APOE-inclusive PGS was also generated. Associations were assessed across various PGS ALZ strata (e.g., 0–2% vs. 98–100% relative to 40–60% reference). Cross-ancestry polygenic risk scores (PRS COMB) were constructed using the Bayesian PRS-CSx method, integrating GWAS summary statistics from European, African American, Latin American, and East Asian populations, and evaluated across different sparseness values and both with and without the APOE region. Methodological details included stringent variant quality control (e.g., R^2 < 0.3 excluded), imputation with TOPMed reference panel, ancestry determination, population structure adjustment using principal components (first 14 PCs), and clumping criteria (P-value threshold of 1 x 10^-3 and R^2 of 0.05).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with an increment in p-tau levels, irrespective of APOE adjustment. The highest levels were observed in the 80–100% PGS ALZ stratum, and the lowest levels in the 0–20% PGS ALZ stratum, compared to the 40–60% reference stratum.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Phosphorylated form of tau, a specific marker for neurofibrillary tangle pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Association with PGS ALZ in 13,051 individuals, with and without APOE adjustment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher CSF p-tau levels are indicative of neurofibrillary pathology and increased risk for Alzheimer's disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased tau aggregation, with aggregates possessing structural properties akin to PHFs.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Abnormal phosphorylation of tau is proposed to reduce conformational flexibility, preceding and being necessary for the development of PHFs and NFTs, driving tau fibrillization and aggregation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Genetic code expansion to express phosphoserine-harboring proteins, AD etiology.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased tau aggregation with PHF-like structural properties indicates a pathological state; abnormal phosphorylation is a key event in AD etiology and disease progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neurodegeneration and cognitive decline; associated with increased numbers of CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between critically short telomeres (%CST) and various brain and blood markers related to aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in 129 cognitively healthy older adults from the Age-Well trial. The research specifically examined the influence of the APOE ε4 genotype on these relationships. Key findings indicate that while %CST is linked to age-related alterations in white matter integrity and specific hippocampal subfield volumes (subiculum, DG, CA1), it does not show a direct association with AD pathophysiological processes in the general healthy older adult population. However, higher %CST significantly increases AD susceptibility in APOE4 carriers, likely due to enhanced vulnerability to age-related effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated plasma levels observed, used to characterize MCI subjects with increased CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells and for subgrouping participants (p-tau217+). Measured with an in-house assay of University of Gothenburg. Specific quantitative results are not provided.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Riociguat (Drug Treatment)

Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (after TBI, with STING activation), lower (with Cl-amidine, with STING/IRE1α inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased at 3 days after TBI (p < 0.001). Significantly decreased by Cl-amidine treatment (p < 0.01). Remarkably increased by 2'3'-cGAMP pretreatment (p < 0.05). Significantly downregulated by STING antagonist C-176 (p < 0.001) and IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, STING activation (2'3'-cGAMP), STING inhibition (C-176), or IRE1α inhibition (Kira6).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased phosphorylation indicates activation of the JNK pathway, correlating with neuroinflammation and neuronal damage. Decreased phosphorylation indicates inhibition of this pathway, contributing to neuroprotective effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: p70S6k Thr389 phosphorylation (S6K1) generally showed similar signaling between whey and soy protein. However, one study indicated whey did not enhance S6K1 phosphorylation at 300 min post-exercise, while a soy-dairy blend led to a more sustained rise at 5h post-exercise compared to whey.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study established robust reference intervals for plasma dephosphorylated-uncarboxylated Matrix Gla-Protein (dp-ucMGP) in a metabolically healthy adult Caucasian population using the IDS-iSYS Ina Ktif assay. It investigated dp-ucMGP's utility as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The findings indicate a significant stepwise increase in plasma dp-ucMGP levels from healthy individuals to those with DM without DKD, and further to those with DKD. Higher dp-ucMGP levels were associated with renal function decline and demonstrated predictive value for DKD diagnosis and progression, showing similar ability to urine albumin:creatinine ratio (uACR) in detecting renal function decline. Additionally, the study explored associations of dp-ucMGP with various clinical parameters in healthy volunteers, noting gender differences and correlations with BMI, CRP, GGT, TSH, and haemoglobin.

However, the document discusses external studies on Vitamin K2 supplementation (e.g., 6 weeks of daily supplementation or 90 µg daily for 270 ± 12 days) as a potential therapy impacting dp-ucMGP levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

The research established VO2T12.5% as an easily derived, reliable, non-invasive biomarker that reflects cardiac performance, predicts heart failure hospitalization and all-cause death, and tracks with invasive hemodynamic indices. It differentiates impaired cardiac function in HFpEF and is modifiable by aficamten treatment in oHCM patients, improving proportionally to cardiac function and a reduction in cardiac biomarkers, indicating its utility as a prognostic and treatment response indicator. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Only affected in the EXE trial, showing significant increases during heating and peaking at 38°C during recovery (p < 0.001). Concentrations steadily increased, with post-intervention levels remaining significantly different from baseline (p < 0.001) and from EXO trial levels (p < 0.05). Did not revert to baseline levels upon returning to homeostatic temperatures. Detected in concentrations higher than the LLOQ of 5 nM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolite of the kynurenine pathway, involved in tryptophan degradation, iron chelation, and modulation of immune function. PGC-1α induces ACMSD, the enzyme responsible for PIC production; elevated levels suggest increased acetyl-CoA synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Core temperature increases induced by exertional heating (exercise/cycling at 60% VO2max in a 30°C room), until rectal temperature reached 39°C, followed by a recovery phase. Samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential disease biomarker. Reflects kynurenine pathway activity and suggests elevated acetyl-CoA synthesis for energy generation. document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the impact of sleep quality improvement, specifically through treatment for sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), on neuropsychological symptoms and Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer's. The study found that sleep treatment significantly improved sleep quality, neuropsychological scores (including MoCA, HRSD-24, and HAMA), and reduced blood Aβ 42/40 ratio and Tau-pT181 levels. It highlighted that a complete recovery of sleep quality is crucial for full improvement in cognitive and depressive symptoms and Aβ 42/40 ratio, and identified blood Aβ 42/40 ratio as a significant predictive factor for sleep quality.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sleep quality improvement for sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) using continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) ventilation, alongside standard donepezil treatment for Alzheimer's disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-month sleep treatment was administered, primarily continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) ventilation for sleep-disordered breathing, in conjunction with donepezil (5-10 mg, every night). The study emphasized that a complete recovery of sleep quality (PSQI score "less than or equal to" 5 post-treatment) was crucial for achieving full improvements in neuropsychological scores (MoCA, HRSD-24) and blood Aβ 42/40 ratio, although Tau-pT181 levels significantly reduced in both completely recovered and partially recovered patients. No specific CPAP pressure settings or dose-response comparisons for CPAP itself were reported beyond the impact of overall sleep recovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall improvement was significant after 6-month sleep intervention. 53 cases (82.8%) achieved complete sleep recovery (PSQI ">=" 5), while 10 cases showed partial improvement (PSQI > 5 post-treatment). One patient's score increased. A complete recovery was critical for improvements in MoCA, HRSD-24, and Aβ 42/40 ratio. PSQI scores correlated significantly with HRSD-24, HAMA, blood Aβ 42/40 ratio, and Tau-pT181 levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures subjective sleep quality across multiple domains, vital for clearing pathogenic molecules and impacting disease progression, especially in the context of Alzheimer's disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 6-month sleep intervention (CPAP) for sleep-disordered breathing in MCI patients due to Alzheimer's disease.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A direct indicator of sleep quality and recovery from sleep-disordered breathing. It strongly correlated with neuropsychological scores (HRSD-24, HAMA) and AD biomarkers (Aβ 42/40 ratio, Tau-pT181 levels) and is critical for improving cognitive and mood symptoms.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document outlines the protocol for the PROSAP-A randomized controlled trial, investigating the effects of preoperative insomnia treatment (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia or Sleep Education Therapy) on acute and long-term postoperative pain control, brain health, and physical recovery in patients undergoing total knee or hip arthroplasty. The study aims to assess various patient-reported outcomes (e.g., opioid use, quality of recovery, sleep, mood, quality of life), objective measures (e.g., actigraphic sleep, quantitative sensory testing for pain, neurocognitive function), and blood biomarkers (e.g., inflammatory, monoamine, genetic mediators) across preoperative and postoperative phases to determine the impact on pain intensity, opioid use, sleep quality, mental health, and functional recovery. The document also details the recruitment, randomization, blinding, and data collection plans for this prehabilitation approach.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Preoperative Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) and Sleep Education Therapy (SET) as an active comparator.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Both interventions are delivered over 4 weeks in a hybrid format, comprising a digital self-guided platform and weekly telehealth video sessions (up to 60 minutes). CBT-I sessions are conducted with a psychologist and include sleep restriction and stimulus control, while SET sessions are with a research nurse. A video-assisted booster session is provided 1-2 weeks postoperatively. No dose-response comparisons are reported as these are fixed intervention protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a novel, minimally invasive approach using hair follicle (HF) gene expression, specifically a four-gene panel (Bmp2, Daam2, Plaat1, Prss27), to assess and classify tissue thyroid hormone (TH) action. Investigating amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism (AIH) in human patients and a TH action indicator (THAI) mouse model, the study found that amiodarone treatment significantly attenuates tissue TH action under hyperthyroid conditions, leading to a mismatch between elevated serum TH levels and attenuated tissue hyperthyroidism, suggesting a protective effect of amiodarone against thyrotoxicosis at the tissue level.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Amiodarone treatment and Thyroid Hormone Status Modulation (Hypothyroid, Euthyroid, Hyperthyroid, T4 Administration)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human patients were treated with amiodarone for at least 4 weeks prior to sampling, with comparisons made between hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid groups; specific human amiodarone doses were not reported. In the mouse model, amiodarone was administered at 1.35 g/kg in chow for 8 weeks, and T4 was administered intraperitoneally at 166.7 ng/bwg/day for 2 days to induce hyperthyroidism. Amiodarone was shown to prevent T4-induced TH action elevation in mouse tissues. Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism affected up to 10% of patients, and AIH affected 1% of patients. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for amiodarone or T4.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Regulated by both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism; specifically 2.7- to 6.5-fold higher in hyperthyroid cases compared to hypothyroid cases.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression level is highly influenced by TH status and correlated with serum-based TH status. Part of a 4-gene model that showed high predictive performance for tissue TH status.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of tissue thyroid hormone signaling and action (TH-responsive gene).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Human tissue TH signaling assessment across hypothyroid, euthyroid, and hyperthyroid states, particularly in amiodarone treatment or discrepancies between serum and tissue TH levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Allows assessment of tissue TH action/status, reflecting serum-based TH status at the tissue level. It is part of a 4-gene panel used to categorize tissue TH status, serving as a complementary tool for clinical scenarios with unexplained discrepancies between routine serum parameters and clinical symptoms, and aids in treatment decisions for amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated altered T-cell reactivity and functional changes in adaptive immune cells across early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, including preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). Using high-dimensional mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays, alongside multimodal imaging and fluid biomarker analysis (including AD-related biomarkers and anti-viral antibody titres), the research characterized immunophenotypes and function of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in blood and CSF. Key findings include: preclinical AD subjects showed an emergence of CD4+ T helper cell responses to amyloid-β peptide, early CSF enrichment of CD8+ TEMRA cells, and a less immunosuppressive peripheral regulatory T cell gene signature. Conversely, MCI subjects exhibited increased frequencies of peripheral CD8+ TEMRA/effector cells with a pro-inflammatory gene profile and generally decreased antigen responsiveness. The study highlights the complexity of adaptive immune changes, suggesting potentially beneficial roles for specific CD4+ T-cell responses in preclinical AD and harmful involvement of CD8+ T-cells in MCI, also considering immune tolerance and epitope mismatch in AD pathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational, Cross-sectional, and Diagnostic Study (Immunological Profiling)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and diagnostic study focused on immunological profiling and disease progression in early Alzheimer's Disease (AD) stages, specifically preclinical AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). No therapeutic interventions were applied. The study involved comprehensive analyses of blood and CSF from three distinct study populations (n=9, n=30, n=44), categorized based on CSF Aβ42/40 ratios (brain Aβ-negative/positive), Aβ PET imaging (FMM Centiloid >12 for Aβ positivity), and plasma p-tau217 levels (p-tau217+ and p-tau217-). Methodologies included high-dimensional mass cytometry, single-cell RNA-sequencing, ex vivo T-cell secretome analysis, and antigen presentation assays. Additionally, multimodal imaging, fluid biomarker analysis (plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP; CSF Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau), anti-viral antibody titres (VZV, CMV, EBV, HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG/IgM with defined thresholds: VZV IgG >100 mIU/ml, CMV IgG >=6 AE/ml, HSV-1 IgG >1 S/CO, HSV-2 IgG >1 S/CO), and APOE genotyping were performed to characterize the study cohorts. No dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive performance of amyloid-PET, plasma p-tau217, Aβ42/40, and p-tau217/Aβ42 for longitudinal cognitive and functional decline over 3.5 years in a community-based cohort of 225 older adults, including cognitively unimpaired and mild cognitive impairment individuals. The research assessed how these biomarkers and their specific thresholds impact sample size estimation for Alzheimer's disease clinical trials, concluding that combining plasma p-tau217 with Aβ42/40 or Aβ-PET with p-tau217, alongside multi-domain cognitive assessments, significantly reduces required sample sizes, especially for preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating biomarker assessment for optimizing Alzheimer's disease clinical trial design and participant selection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, longitudinal cohort study over 3.5 years, not a therapeutic intervention. Participants were followed annually with cognitive assessments and received baseline biomarker quantification. Aβ-PET imaging utilized approximately 140 MBq [18F]-flutemetamol to calculate global Aβ SUVR. Plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, and p-tau217 were quantified using customized Simoa platforms. The primary focus was on identifying optimal baseline biomarker thresholds (e.g., Aβ-PET SUVR > 1.27 / ~14-34 Centiloids; plasma Aβ42/40 < 0.063; plasma p-tau217 > 1.53 pg/mL; plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 > 0.25) and inclusion criteria to detect a 30% slowing in cognitive decline over 3 years with 80% statistical power in hypothetical clinical trials. No dose-response comparisons for actual treatments were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (ratio of amyloid beta peptides)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Predicted decline across multiple cognitive domains. When combined with plasma p-tau217, cut-offs yielded the lowest sample size estimates for detecting a 30% slowing in cognitive outcomes, particularly effective in preclinical AD. In the total cohort, it was not significantly associated with cognitive decline in most domains, predicting decline in only two tasks after FDR correction. Lowest predictive threshold for MEM-EF-PS composite was Aβ42/40 < 0.063. In MCI, strongest decline was in CERAD delayed recall (β = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.21), predicting decline in three tasks after FDR correction. In CU, lower plasma Aβ42/40 predicted faster decline in the Boston Naming Test but was not significant after FDR correction. Single-biomarker use alone resulted in sample size estimates > 5000 per arm in CU individuals.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the processing of amyloid precursor protein and amyloid-beta peptide aggregation in the brain; a lower ratio indicates increased amyloid pathology and distinguishes abnormal from normal amyloid-beta status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of longitudinal cognitive and functional decline over 3.5 years in a community-based sample of older adults (cognitively unimpaired and mild cognitive impairment); used as a prescreening tool and eligibility criterion for optimizing clinical trials targeting early Alzheimer's disease stages.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High performance in predicting cognitive decline; holds significant potential as a (pre)screening tool for clinical trials to identify individuals with a high likelihood of Aβ pathology and enrich trial populations at increased risk of cognitive decline. A weaker predictor of cognitive decline compared to p-tau217, but crucial for reducing sample size requirements in preclinical AD clinical trials, especially when combined with p-tau217.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated in TBI mice at 3 days post-TBI (p < 0.01) compared to sham. Substantially reduced after Cl-amidine treatment at 3 days after TBI (p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Extracellular DNA, often associated with cell death, inflammation, or NETosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Cl-amidine treatment after TBI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates cell damage, inflammation, and NET formation in the circulation after TBI. Its reduction by Cl-amidine suggests a decrease in these pathological processes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated endogenous Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with rtPA, aiming to determine its association with functional outcome and compare its levels to healthy controls and at 3 months post-stroke. Key findings indicate that plasma GLP-1 levels are elevated in acute stroke patients compared to healthy individuals and remain stable at 3 months, but these endogenous levels were not associated with functional outcome. The study also highlighted insulin resistance as a predictor for unfavorable stroke outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) for ischemic stroke; the study primarily investigated endogenous biomarker levels rather than the therapeutic effect or specific dosing of rtPA itself.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: All ischemic stroke patients received conventional rtPA treatment as part of their standard care, typically on hospital day 2-4. Specific dose details of rtPA are not provided as the study focused on observational monitoring of endogenous biomarker levels and their correlation with stroke outcome, without exogenous administration or dose comparisons of GLP-1 or rtPA.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Fasting plasma and plasma during 75g OGTT

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher (during OGTT in stroke patients vs. controls; during acute OGTT vs. 3 months post-stroke OGTT); Unchanged (fasting in stroke patients vs. controls).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: During a 75g OGTT, levels were higher in acute stroke patients (7.8 values) compared to healthy controls (6.1 values; p < 0.001), and higher during the acute phase (8.0 values) compared to 3 months post-stroke (7.4 values; p = 0.015). Fasting levels did not differ significantly between acute stroke patients (5.3 values) and healthy controls (5.6 values; p = 0.33).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary energy source for the body, regulated by insulin.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fasting state and during a 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) in acute ischemic stroke patients compared to healthy controls, and longitudinally between acute phase and 3 months post-stroke.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates increased post-challenge plasma glucose levels and transiently higher post-challenge levels during the acute phase of ischemic stroke, which are detrimental to outcome and associated with increased hemorrhagic transformation risk. Fasting levels do not differ significantly.

document_context_data.document_summary: This proof-of-concept study investigated whether a single session of High-Intensity Training (HIT) could restore impaired counterregulatory hormonal, symptomatic, and cognitive responses to subsequent insulin-induced hypoglycemia in people with type 1 diabetes and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH). The findings supported the hypothesis that IAH develops as a habituated response, demonstrating that HIT significantly amplified adrenaline responses and total symptom awareness during subsequent hypoglycemia, although it also led to a significant prolongation of cognitive reaction time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: High-intensity training (HIT) compared to controlled rest
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single HIT session lasting 20 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down, with 4 x 30-second cycle sprints at 150% of maximum wattage (V̇O2peak assessment) interspersed with 2-minute recovery periods. Participants aimed for >90% peak heart rate. This was directly compared to 20 minutes of seated rest, and no dose-response comparisons for HIT were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Actively controlled to specific levels (e.g., euglycaemia, then hypoglycaemia).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Maintained at 4–6 mmol/l (euglycaemia) for the first 30 minutes of the clamp, then reduced over 30 minutes to a final level of 2.5 mmol/l (hypoglycaemia), and maintained at 2.5 mmol/l for 60 minutes, before being returned to the euglycaemic range.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The body's primary energy source, with tightly regulated levels essential for cellular function, especially in the brain.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Hyperinsulinaemic–hypoglycaemic clamp study where glucose levels were precisely controlled to induce euglycaemia and then controlled hypoglycaemia (2.5 mmol/l), following either High-Intensity Training or controlled rest.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The primary indicator of hypoglycaemia and the target variable for assessing the efficacy of counterregulatory hormone responses and associated symptoms/cognitive function in diabetes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This article updates the redox theory of aging, proposing that aging results from a decline in gene-exposome interaction plasticity due to cumulative exposure memory. It emphasizes the critical role of redox networks, particularly thiol/disulfide balance (e.g., plasma cystine to glutathione ratio), as an interface between an individual and the environment, influencing health, disease etiology, and resilience. The theory links compromised redox networks to increased oxidative stress biomarkers like hydroxynonenal and reactive carbonyls, and discusses the predictive power of the plasma CySS/GSH ratio for all-cause mortality in conditions like coronary artery disease, while also exploring implications for regenerative medicine, multimorbidity, and personalized health management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document is a comprehensive review and theoretical discussion of the redox theory of aging, its mechanisms, and implications, including the prognostic utility of specific biomarkers. No direct therapeutic interventions were investigated.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this is a review article and theoretical discussion; it does not report on experimental studies involving specific therapeutic doses, intensities, durations, or dose-response comparisons for any intervention. It discusses observational findings and the predictive power of naturally occurring biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: become oxidized with aging

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Maintenance of redox networks
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Aging
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts death in coronary artery disease (CAD) patients; suggests a way to measure resilience of redox networks in aging and disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Antibodies that play a critical role in the adaptive immune system
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Astaxanthin supplementation post-exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Countering reductions suggests an immune-normalizing effect, beneficial for immune function and reducing post-exercise immune suppression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of nonpharmacological thermal therapies, specifically Mud Bath Therapy (MBT) versus Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA), on the endurance of loaded inspiratory muscles and associated inflammatory/metabolic markers in patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The aim was to compare their effects on endurance time (ET) and plasma IL-6 concentration following an inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge. The findings indicated that MBT significantly improved ET, suggesting a training effect and physiologic adaptive mechanisms in respiratory muscles. Both thermal interventions were found to be safe, as they did not significantly alter baseline IL-6, CRP, or ACTH levels. However, an IRB challenge systematically increased IL-6 levels in both groups, indicative of altered respiratory muscle glycogen utilization and a measurable inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Thermal therapy, including Mud Bath Therapy (MBT, also referred to as Mudpack Balneotherapy or medicinal clay applications as passive warm-up) and Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Both MBT (n=22) and LTA (n=19) groups completed 12 sessions over 2 weeks. MBT involved daily mud pack application at 38-42°C for 20 minutes, followed by a thermal bath at 38°C for 8-15 minutes, and 60 minutes of bed rest, with optional access to thermal swimming pools once or twice daily for unsupervised leisure activities (each not exceeding 30 minutes). LTA consisted of 12 sessions over 2 weeks of unsupervised leisure activities (bathing, walking, swimming) in thermal swimming pools twice daily (each not exceeding 30 minutes). An inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge was performed at approximately 40% of maximal inspiratory pressure both pre- and post-intervention. No formal dose-response comparisons for the thermal therapies were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased after inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge as a metabolic consequence.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and metabolic efficiency of respiratory muscles, reflecting biochemical adaptations.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge and thermal interventions in COPD patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a training effect, stemming from metabolic consequences and biochemical adaptations in respiratory muscles, which contributes to increased endurance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled pilot study protocol investigates the effects of early spironolactone therapy on exercise capacity, clinical worsening, and vascular inflammation in 70 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without right ventricular failure. It aims to assess changes in functional performance (6-minute walk distance, VO2 max), plasma markers of vascular inflammation, gene expression profiles in PBMCs and PAECs, neurohormonal axis activation (sympathetic nervous system, RAAS, sex hormone metabolism), and right ventricular structure and function using advanced imaging techniques, while also monitoring for safety biomarkers like serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Spironolactone therapy (Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Early treatment with spironolactone will be administered for 24 weeks in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial. The initial dose is 25 mg once daily, escalating to 50 mg daily after week 6 if serum potassium is <5.0 mEq/L and serum creatinine does not increase >50% from baseline. Dose adjustments and discontinuation are strictly tied to safety monitoring, including stopping if serum potassium increases to 5.3-5.9 mEq/L, discontinuing if it remains ">="5.3 mEq/L on two consecutive draws or immediately if ">="6.0 mEq/L, or if serum creatinine increases >50% from baseline. No formal dose-response comparisons are reported within this protocol, although drug-drug interactions with PAH-specific therapies were considered.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Change in placebo-corrected plasma markers of vascular inflammation will be measured. Specific quantitative changes will be determined post-treatment as this is a study protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates the presence and severity of inflammatory processes within the vascular system and endothelial dysfunction, a key component of PAH pathology.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early spironolactone therapy in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) without clinical right ventricular failure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Secondary endpoint to evaluate the anti-inflammatory effects of spironolactone and indicates the level of vascular inflammation, a factor in PAH progression.
