document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: increased significantly (p < 0.05) and with a tendency to increase (p > 0.05)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Hormone primarily involved in sleep-wake cycles and antioxidant activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation for bioavailability assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms successful absorption and systemic presence of exogenous melatonin.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of early first-trimester tubular (urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1) and glomerular (eGFR) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). It concluded that elevated first-trimester urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc) and, to a lesser extent, eGFR, are associated with increased PE risk. Notably, uNGALcc, especially when combined with clinical factors like BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin, significantly improved PE prediction, indicating subclinical renal tubular and glomerular dysfunction as early markers of PE, while urinary KIM-1 and plasma NGAL were not predictive.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on diagnostic biomarker assessment for preeclampsia risk prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a prospective observational cohort study enrolling pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) and normotensive pregnant women without diabetes. Biomarkers were assessed at three gestational visits: V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks), V2 (21.7  1 1.4 weeks), and V3 (31.4  1 1.5 weeks), with primary focus on first-trimester (V1) values for preeclampsia (PE) prediction. Study groups included women with T1DM who developed PE (DM+PE+), T1DM women who remained normotensive (DM+PE-), and normotensive women without diabetes (DM-). All T1DM subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria at V1. No active intervention or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic/prognostic utility. Analysis included samples with specific attention to leukocyte-negative urine samples.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (between groups); significant temporal increase with gestation observed only in DM+PE+ women (P = 0.015).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ significantly at any visit between any of the three study groups and did not predict preeclampsia (PE). No significant differences reported for predictive utility. Did not contribute to the prediction model.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Generally an early and sensitive biomarker for acute and chronic kidney disease, indicating systemic inflammation or renal insult; protective against ischemic and nephrotoxic injuries.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy (V1: 12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not useful in predicting preeclampsia in this specific context, showing no clear-cut changes and having no predictive value (AUC = 0.546). Less sensitive biomarker of early renal insult compared to uNGAL in this specific context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated plasma NET biomarkers correlated with worse outcomes in TBI patients. No specific numerical value.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicators of neutrophil extracellular trap formation, which contribute to inflammation and adverse outcomes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) in patients
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlated with worse neurological outcomes, including elevated intracranial pressure and worse neurological function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single bout of moderate-intensity continuous exercise, specifically at lactate threshold (LT) intensity, on renal hemodynamics and kidney injury biomarkers in middle-aged men. The main findings indicate that this type of exercise effectively maintains renal blood flow (RBF), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and filtration fraction (FF), and crucially, does not induce renal injury based on biomarker analysis. However, transient changes were noted in renal cross-sectional area and resistance indices, along with an increase in plasma noradrenaline in the recovery phase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Moderate-intensity continuous exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of 30 minutes of aerobic exercise was performed using a cycle ergometer, precisely at lactate threshold (LT) intensity (corresponding to 36% VO2max). The study involved middle-aged men (38 	 8 years) with well-maintained renal function (eGFR 	 60 ml/min/1.73m2). Renal hemodynamics and biomarker levels were evaluated at rest, immediately after exercise, and during 30-minute and 60-minute recovery phases. Participants were allowed free hydration during and after the experiment. No dose-response comparisons or chronic effects were investigated in this acute study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased after exercise (194 	 57 vs. 550 	 221 pg/ml, p = 0.009) and remained significantly higher in 60-min after exercise (194 	 57 vs. 404 	 99 pg/ml, p = 0.009) compared to before exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with the regulation of renal hemodynamics; exhibits a strong vasoconstrictive effect; indicator of sympathetic nervous system activity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Continuous exercise at LT intensity and recovery phase.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increasing noradrenaline following moderate-intensity continuous exercise contributes to a decrease in Cross-sectional Area (CSA), but this enhanced sympathetic nervous system activity does not induce a decrease in RBF.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm controlled study investigated the comparative rehydration efficacy of electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) versus standard purified water (CON) on various hydration biomarkers in healthy adults following moderate exercise-induced dehydration. The primary finding was that ALK water significantly reduced high-shear whole blood viscosity and enhanced its restoration to pre-exercise baseline levels compared to CON water, while other markers like plasma osmolality, bioimpedance, and body mass showed no significant difference.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral rehydration therapy after exercise-induced dehydration, comparing electrolyzed high-pH alkaline water (ALK) with standard purified water (CON).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants exercised in a warm environment (30 °C, 70% relative humidity) until a 2.0 ± 0.2% body weight loss was achieved due to perspiration (mild dehydration). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive performance of amyloid-PET, plasma p-tau217, Aβ42/40, and p-tau217/Aβ42 for longitudinal cognitive and functional decline over 3.5 years in a community-based cohort of 225 older adults, including cognitively unimpaired and mild cognitive impairment individuals. The research assessed how these biomarkers and their specific thresholds impact sample size estimation for Alzheimer's disease clinical trials, concluding that combining plasma p-tau217 with Aβ42/40 or Aβ-PET with p-tau217, alongside multi-domain cognitive assessments, significantly reduces required sample sizes, especially for preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating biomarker assessment for optimizing Alzheimer's disease clinical trial design and participant selection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, longitudinal cohort study over 3.5 years, not a therapeutic intervention. Participants were followed annually with cognitive assessments and received baseline biomarker quantification. Aβ-PET imaging utilized approximately 140 MBq [18F]-flutemetamol to calculate global Aβ SUVR. Plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, and p-tau217 were quantified using customized Simoa platforms. The primary focus was on identifying optimal baseline biomarker thresholds (e.g., Aβ-PET SUVR > 1.27 / ~14-34 Centiloids; plasma Aβ42/40 < 0.063; plasma p-tau217 > 1.53 pg/mL; plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 > 0.25) and inclusion criteria to detect a 30% slowing in cognitive decline over 3 years with 80% statistical power in hypothetical clinical trials. No dose-response comparisons for actual treatments were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Predicted decline across multiple cognitive domains. Stronger AD biomarker abnormality (higher p-tau217) was associated with faster cognitive decline, with strongest decline in CERAD delayed recall (β = -0.10, 95% CI: -0.14 to -0.07). Predicted decline in eight tasks after FDR correction in the total cohort. Lowest predictive threshold for MEM-EF-PS composite was p-tau217 > 1.53 pg/mL. In MCI, strongest decline was in TMT-B (β = -0.17, 95% CI: -0.24 to -0.09). When combined with plasma Aβ42/40, cut-offs yielded the lowest sample size estimates for detecting a 30% slowing in cognitive outcomes in CU individuals. Sample size estimates were similar for p-tau217 combined with Aβ42/40 or Aβ SUVR. Slightly outperformed Aβ SUVR in predicting decline in the total cohort and MCI subsample. Levels below the limit of quantitation (LOQ) were set at LOQ/2 (43% of participants).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Distinguishes abnormal from normal amyloid-beta status, predicts amyloid-beta accumulation, and indicates tau pathology (neurofibrillary tangles) associated with Alzheimer's disease progression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prediction of longitudinal cognitive and functional decline over 3.5 years in a community-based sample of older adults (cognitively unimpaired and mild cognitive impairment); used as a prescreening tool and eligibility criterion for optimizing clinical trials targeting early Alzheimer's disease stages.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High performance in predicting cognitive decline, even in preclinical stages; holds significant potential as a (pre)screening tool for clinical trials to identify individuals with a high likelihood of Aβ pathology and enrich trial populations at increased risk of cognitive decline. It is a strong predictor of decline, particularly sensitive to semantic and visuospatial-construction tasks, and highly effective in reducing clinical trial sample sizes, especially when combined with other AD biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma thiols were consistently higher at all timepoints after acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) ingestion compared to placebo, irrespective of group (all p < 0.001; d = 1.45 to 2.34), and remained elevated during exercise. No between-group differences were observed in endogenous thiol levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This substudy of the REST trial investigated the effects of lower tidal volume ventilation facilitated by veno-venous extracorporeal CO2 removal (vv-ECCO2R) compared to standard care in patients with moderate-to-severe acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF). The study aimed to evaluate plasma biomarkers of systemic inflammation and lung injury, such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-18 (IL-18), and potential heterogeneity of treatment effect based on inflammatory phenotypes. Key findings indicated no overall difference in day 3 plasma CRP, but a greater increase in plasma IL-18 in the intervention group. Notably, baseline IL-18 levels and inflammatory phenotypes were found to identify subgroups of patients who may benefit from lower tidal volume ventilation facilitated by vv-ECCO2R, demonstrating differential treatment responses and outcomes like ventilator-free days and 90-day mortality.

Plasma samples were collected at baseline and day 3 for biomarker analysis. No explicit dose-response comparisons for different levels of the intervention were reported; however, treatment responses were observed to vary based on patient phenotypes (baseline interleukin-18 levels and inflammatory status).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated plasma protein biomarkers (including cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and cell death markers) to identify unique expression patterns associated with the severity and duration of Primary Graft Dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation. It identified several strong biomarker candidates, such as IP-10, MIP-1B, RANTES, M30, M65, IL-1Ra, PDGF-BB, G-CSF, IL-4, MIP-1A, IL-17, IL-9, IL-1B, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-alpha, sRAGE, and PAI-1, which are informative for early detection, predicting clinical course, and monitoring treatment efficacy of PGD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Lung transplantation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 40 consecutive lung transplant patients (February 2018 – May 2019). Blood samples were collected immediately pretransplant (T0) and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transplant/reperfusion, with PGD severity scored using 2016 ISHLT guidelines. Biomarker analysis involved a bead-based multiplex assay for 27 plasma proteins (cytokines, growth factors, chemokines) and enzyme-linked immunoassay for cell injury markers (M30, M65, sRAGE, PAI-1). Statistical methods included pairwise comparisons, sensitivity, and temporal analyses. An immunosuppression regimen of basiliximab, solumedrol, and mycophenolate (induction) and tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil (maintenance) was used. Intraoperative extracorporeal life support (ECLS), ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP), and postoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) were considered for severe PGD (PGD3). No specific dose-response comparisons for transplantation or immunosuppression were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Varied (downregulated/upregulated at T0, no significant post-T0 trends)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were different in pairwise comparison only at 6-h time point. Downregulated when comparing PGD2 versus 1 at T0 and upregulated when comparing PGD3 versus 2 at T0. No significant differences in sensitivity or temporal analyses for overall PGD development.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Marker of endothelial dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-transplant (T0) and 6 hours post-lung transplant, associated with PGD grades.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates endothelial dysfunction, with inconsistent and time-point specific correlation to PGD severity, not a strong general predictor in this study.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Similar active PAI-1 levels in sera of COVID-19 patients and healthy individuals, with nearly average values in the complicated phase (despite increased total PAI-1 protein). A non-significant trend towards higher levels was found in healthy Europeans (26.28 
G2 11.68 IU/ml) compared to healthy Japanese (20.2 
G2 5.2 IU/ml). Weakly correlated with IL6 (r=0.42, p<0.01) and CRP (r=0.36, p<0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1, which inhibits fibrinolysis by blocking plasminogen activators, thus contributing to hypofibrinolysis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease progression (complicated phase), inflammatory response, and ethnic differences in baseline levels between Japanese and Caucasians.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: While high PAI-1 levels are generally reported to predict COVID-19-associated thrombosis and tissue fibrosis, active PAI-1 did not significantly increase in COVID-19 patients in this study, and only weakly reflects the inflammatory response. A discrepancy between PAI-1 antigen and activity levels was noted, with lower activity in Japanese potentially contributing to a lower thrombosis risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of CDH1, CDH2, MCP-1, and PAI-1 mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles (EVs) for predicting early-stage diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main findings indicate that CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression in blood EVs was significantly downregulated with the development of DN (overt and incipient stages) compared to diabetic patients without DN, suggesting a renoprotective effect and their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. These mRNAs inversely correlated with markers of kidney damage like creatinine and albuminuria. In contrast, CDH1 mRNA showed no significant change across groups, and while PAI-1 mRNA decreased in some diabetic groups, its diagnostic utility for early DN was not clearly established, according to the authors' results. The study also explored the expression of these and other related biomarkers in urine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 196 participants (35 overt DN, 53 incipient DN, 62 DM, and 46 healthy controls) with type 2 diabetes. The study focused on characterizing mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles and other clinical markers across different stages of diabetic nephropathy and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in incipient DN group (0.70-fold change) and DM group (0.58-fold change) compared to control. However, authors' results did not indicate a strong role in early detection of DN.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Incipient diabetic nephropathy and diabetic patients (DM) compared to healthy controls; early-stage diabetic nephropathy prediction.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Observed decrease in expression is associated with incipient diabetic nephropathy and the diabetic state. While potentially a predictor of renal fibrosis, its diagnostic utility for early-stage DN in this study was not significant.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mentioned as 'measured' during acute phase response; not quantitatively specified, but indicates an increase.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated large-scale plasma proteomic changes in 75 middle-aged adults during acute treadmill exercise and up to 1-hour post-exercise, identifying 765 proteins changed at peak and 128 at 1-hour post-exercise. It further characterized 56 proteins with sustained changes, linking them to cardiometabolic traits and responses to a 20-week aerobic exercise training program. The research aimed to biochemically characterize acute exercise protein kinetics, finding enrichment for coagulation-related proteins post-exercise and MYC targets, and noting both concordant and discordant protein responses between acute and chronic exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute treadmill exercise and chronic aerobic exercise training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise consisted of symptom-limited treadmill stress testing in 75 middle-aged adults, following a standard Bruce protocol with plasma protein quantification at baseline, peak exercise (mean 90% predicted peak heart rate, 9.6 METs), and 1-hour post-exercise. Chronic exercise involved a 20-week aerobic training program with three sessions per week, with intensity and duration gradually increased based on individual VO2max. Acute exercise intensity and duration varied, making it difficult to effectively analyze specific exertion thresholds or dose-response comparisons for the acute protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased 1-h post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-h post-acute exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of reduced fibrinolytic activity, contributing to an overall procoagulant state post-exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This surveillance report details malaria cases in the United States in 2018, reporting a 15.6% decrease in confirmed cases from 2017 while noting an overall increase since 1972, with 98.1% being imported cases predominantly from Africa and P. falciparum as the most common species. It describes comprehensive surveillance methodologies, diagnostic tests, and molecular analyses for antimalarial drug resistance markers, particularly for P. falciparum against pyrimethamine, sulfadoxine, chloroquine, and mefloquine, with no resistance markers for atovaquone or artemisinin. The report also investigates chemoprophylaxis adherence (found to be poor), treatment patterns for uncomplicated and severe malaria, and emphasizes the critical importance of prompt diagnosis, appropriate treatment with CDC guidelines, and continuous surveillance to prevent local transmission.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Malaria prevention (chemoprophylaxis, including Tafenoquine), diagnosis (microscopy, PCR, RDTs), and treatment for both uncomplicated and severe malaria (oral antimalarials like atovaquone-proguanil, artemether-lumefantrine, quinine; parenteral IV artesunate for severe malaria), alongside molecular surveillance for antimalarial drug resistance.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Chemoprophylaxis adherence was poor among U.S. residents with imported malaria in 2018, with 24.5% reporting use and 95.0% demonstrating non-adherence or inconsistent regimens, often due to forgetting or prematurely stopping. Tafenoquine offers an abbreviated schedule for eligible adults. For treatment, IV artesunate became the first-line for severe malaria in April 2019, replacing IV quinidine gluconate, though 52.1% of severe cases in 2018 did not receive guideline-appropriate treatment. Uncomplicated malaria treatments varied, with 91.7% receiving appropriate care, and primaquine was often used for P. vivax/P. ovale relapse prevention, though sometimes inappropriately. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported, but treatment choice was emphasized based on species, severity, patient factors (e.g., pregnancy), and CDC guidelines.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Presence of infection when species is unknown
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 11 cases (5.0%) with unknown species reported were PCR confirmed to the Plasmodium genus level.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Parasitic genus responsible for malaria in humans, confirming infection even if specific species cannot be determined.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Imported malaria cases with initially unknown species.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms a malaria infection, guiding initial management even if species is not yet determined.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Dramatically down-regulated upon reprogramming; quantification data by ESI-MS e correlated well with detection by Western blot analysis. Highly expressed in PBMC.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates somatic cell state; down-regulation is a marker of successful reprogramming to pluripotency.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study evaluated and compared the regenerative potential of different blood-derived products (EDTA-PRP, Citrate-PRP, and hyperacute serum [hypACT]) in a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model over 21 days. Key assessments included metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression (SOX9, COL2AB, COL1A1, MMP3, P21), and extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and quality, using 1% or 5% concentrations of the products. HypACT consistently demonstrated superior and more stable results for cartilage-related gene expression and tissue quality. In contrast, Citrate-PRP showed negative effects on ECM production, chondrocyte presence, and gene expression, which was partly attributed to anticoagulants and extensive platelet accumulation. Metabolic activity generally showed no significant differences among the blood products compared to controls, though some variations were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-derived products: hyperacute serum (hypACT), leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with EDTA (EPRP), and leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with trisodium citrate (CPRP).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood products (hypACT, EPRP, CPRP) were prepared from whole blood (18mL for hypACT, 16mL for EPRP, 16mL for CPRP) and used as 1% or 5% (v/v) supplementation in 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet cultures for 21 days; 10% concentration was deemed unsuitable. HypACT showed stable effects across both 1% and 5% concentrations. For EPRP, 1% was favored over 5% due to better glycosaminoglycan deposition and lower platelet accumulation, with concentration influencing specific gene expressions (SOX9, MMP3, COL2AB, COL1A1). CPRP at both 1% and 5% concentrations resulted in poor tissue quality and no increase in COL2AB production, with extensive platelet accumulation observed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher platelet accumulation was observed with 5% EPRP. Extensive platelet accumulation was noted with 1% and 5% CPRP, particularly after 21 days of cultivation with 5% CPRP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A cellular component of blood products, involved in signaling, coagulation, and potentially influencing tissue response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Supplementation of OA chondrocyte pellets with 1% and 5% EDTA-PRP (EPRP) or Citrate-PRP (CPRP).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High accumulation might detrimentally alter forming tissue quality and explain discrepancies in metabolic activity, suggesting it is a detrimental factor for tissue quality in PRP treatments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fluctuated; no significant difference between sprint and long-distance female swimmers. Varied peak/trough times across male groups (e.g., lowest median in ML group in 10th week, highest in MS group at same time). A decrease in peak values was observed from the beginning to the end of the training program.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional swimming training period and recovery, especially during training programs focused on motor performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower in SCT players (197.9            48.0            10^3) compared to CON (278.7            78.1            10^3; p = 0.03) specifically at post-season.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Represents an observed difference in platelet levels in SCT players at post-season compared to controls, indicating a potential hematological alteration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower counts in HCC patients compared to both control (P = 0.0008) and non-malignant patients (P < 0.0001). Significant reduction in cirrhotic patients (both chronic HCV and SVR) compared to non-cirrhotic groups (P < 0.0001 for both). Lower in cirrhotic SVRs compared to other non-malignant groups (P = 0.01–<0.0001). No significant differences between non-/cirrhotic chronic HCV and SVR groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for blood clotting and hemostasis; low levels can indicate bone marrow issues or splenic sequestration, often seen in portal hypertension and cirrhosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis and assessment of liver cirrhosis in HCV patients. Comparison of HCC patients with control and non-malignant patient groups, and comparison between non-/cirrhotic chronic HCV and SVR groups. Used as a component in the FIB-4 index formula.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower platelet count (≤ 150/mL) combined with splenomegaly indicates clinically significant portal hypertension and suggests liver cirrhosis severity. Indicates hematological alteration; thrombocytopenia is associated with liver disease and HCC, and can reflect impaired clotting ability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated Nogo-B protein expression in liver tissues and its plasma levels in patients with liver cirrhosis, correlating them with various clinical parameters. Findings indicated that Nogo-B is highly expressed in fibrotic/cirrhotic liver tissues and its plasma levels are significantly elevated in cirrhotic patients, showing a positive correlation with Child-Pugh scores and liver fibrosis stage. The research suggests that plasma Nogo-B could serve as a novel surrogate marker for assessing liver functional reserve.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on liver cirrhosis progression and biomarker correlation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention. It involved 24 patients with fibrotic/cirrhotic liver specimens (12 Metavir F2, 12 Metavir F4) and 10 healthy controls for immunohistochemical analysis of liver tissue. For plasma Nogo-B analysis, 301 patients with hepatic cirrhosis (comprising 152 with hepatitis B cirrhosis, 83 with alcoholic cirrhosis, and 66 with primary biliary cirrhosis) and 153 healthy controls were enrolled. Patients were further classified into Child-Pugh classes A, B, and C to assess correlation with disease severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant correlation with plasma Nogo-B levels (r = -0.24, P = 0.739), excluding patients with splenic embolization and splenectomy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in blood clotting; levels can be affected by portal hypertension and thrombocytopenia.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of portal hypertension and thrombocytopenia in patients with hepatic cirrhosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates thrombocytopenia and severity of portal hypertension; lack of correlation with Nogo-B suggests Nogo-B does not reflect portal hypertension severity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a computational model to explain and predict changes in red blood cell parameters (RDW-CV%, Hb, MCV) during iron and folate deficiencies, highlighting RDW-CV% as an early and useful indicator for both conditions, especially in resource-limited settings for detecting folate deficiency to prevent foetal damage, and suggesting its inclusion in routine blood analyses.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Computational diagnostic modeling for nutritional deficiencies.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A computer model simulated red blood cell (RBC) formation and destruction, assuming a 120-day RBC lifespan. It used standard haematological parameters (normal Hb lower limit 110 g/l, upper normal RDW-CV% 15%) and specific parameters for normal haemopoiesis (RBC/day 40000, MCV 90, SD of MCV 10, MCH 30), iron-deficient haemopoiesis (RBC/day 30000, MCV 60, SD of MCV 7, MCH 18), and folate-deficient haemopoiesis (macrocytic pattern). Simulations ran for up to 180 days, incorporating shifts between normal and deficient states to predict changes in blood parameters. No direct therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported within the study, as it focused on diagnostic prediction.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Malaria.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The best discriminator for malaria compared to RDW-CV%.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: May represent the transition from CLD to fibrosis

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in hemostasis and wound healing; count can reflect liver disease status
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Transition from Chronic Liver Disease (CLD) to fibrosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for the transition from CLD to fibrosis

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized a multi-omics approach to investigate molecular pathways mediating immunosuppression in healthy female physique athletes undergoing prolonged intensive physical training and low-energy availability for substantial fat mass loss, followed by weight regain. The findings revealed significant alterations across various immune parameters, including dysregulated hematopoiesis, suppressed immune cell proliferation (both T- and B-lymphocytes), attenuated systemic inflammation, reduced antibody-mediated function (decreased total IgG levels and altered IgG glycosylation towards pro-inflammatory activity and reduced affinity), and suppressed IgE-dependent immune reactions. Most immune system parameters, including blood cell distribution and cytokine/chemokine profiles, showed significant changes during weight loss and largely reverted to baseline during the weight regain period, highlighting that the method of weight loss distinctly modulates the immune system.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive physical training combined with a physique competition diet leading to substantial weight loss and subsequent weight regain
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The intervention involved 25 healthy female physique athletes undergoing a vigorous 2- to 5-month progressive competition diet routine. This entailed a weight loss period averaging 21.1 

± 3.1 weeks, achieved through approximately 18% decreased energy intake and 15% increased exercise (METh/wk), resulting in about 29% decreased energy availability. This was followed by a weight regain period averaging 18.4 

± 2.9 weeks, during which exercise decreased and energy intake increased. Measurements were taken at baseline (PRE), immediately after weight loss (MID), and after weight regain (POST). No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced counts observed during the weight loss period. Counts recovered back to baseline during the weight regain period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for blood clotting and wound healing.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Weight loss period (prolonged energy deprivation and intense exercise).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a wider effect on blood cell proliferation and hematopoiesis.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated changes in cellular immune inflammation markers (NLR, PLR, SII), various blood cell counts (leucocytes and their subsets, platelets), and physical fitness parameters (VO2max, YYIRL1 performance, sprint, jump tests) in elite male soccer players over a 12-week period, including both uncongested and congested match play phases. It found that a congested match play period significantly altered immune cell counts and inflammation markers, leading to increased leucocyte, neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, and monocyte counts, and higher NLR, PLR, and SII, with concurrent decreases in lymphocyte counts and aerobic physical fitness. These immune inflammation markers were negatively correlated with physical fitness (YYIRL1 performance, VO2max) and positively correlated with workload parameters, suggesting their utility for monitoring training intensity, competitive load, and aerobic physical fitness, and for preventing overtraining.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Elite Soccer Training and Congested Match Play
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifteen elite male soccer players were monitored for 12 weeks, comprising a 6-week uncongested match play period (30 training sessions, 45 hours training volume, 6 matches with 350±53.5 minutes average playing time) followed by a 6-week congested match play period (24 training sessions, 36 hours training volume, 10 matches with 629.6±133.9 minutes average playing time). Players typically trained five times per week and played one match per week, with the congested period exposing them to up to eight matches per month. Physical fitness tests (Squat Jump, Countermovement Jump, 20-meter sprint, Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test level 1) and blood samples were taken at T1 (week 1), T2 (week 7), and T3 (week 13). Workload parameters (Global load, Training load, Competitive load, Training volume, Session-Rating of Perceived Exertion) were recorded and compared. The congested period showed significantly increased total and competitive loads and decreased training load, training volume, and Session-RPE compared to the uncongested period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for varying levels of congestion beyond the two defined periods were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change during the competitive periods (congested or uncongested).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in hemostasis, blood clotting, and exhibit pro-inflammatory properties.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During competitive periods (congested and uncongested) of elite soccer match play and training programs.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that changes in leucocyte subsets and derived ratios (like NLR, PLR, SII) are more sensitive indicators of competitive stress than changes in platelet count alone.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute and cumulative effects of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise on circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (cf n-DNA), cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf mt-DNA), muscle damage, and metabolic markers in healthy, average-trained men. It found a remarkable and tremendous increase in post-exercise cf n-DNA without tolerance development, a moderate post-exercise increase in cf mt-DNA, and a significant decrease in baseline cf mt-DNA over the study period. The research also observed cumulative muscle damage (indicated by CK, AST, ALT), dehydration effects on blood cell counts, elevated white blood cell counts, and increased metabolic markers after exercise. Circulating cf n-DNA was highlighted as a highly sensitive indicator for monitoring acute exercise effects, surpassing traditional muscle injury and metabolic markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Treadmill Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Eleven healthy, average-trained men performed three repeated bouts of treadmill exercise to volitional exhaustion, separated by 72 hours (3 days) of resting. Each bout was at a speed corresponding to 70% of the individual's maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max), with a constant treadmill inclination of 1.5%, and involved increasing treadmill velocity by 2 km/h every 3 minutes until exhaustion. Participants were allowed to drink mineral water. The intensity of each bout was comparable to a half-marathon in terms of cf n-DNA response. The study assessed cumulative effects and tolerance development over repeated bouts, but no explicit dose-response comparisons for changes were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase after each bout, increasing by about 50 x10^3 cells/µL. Percentage increment was always many times lower than cf n-DNA.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in hemostasis (blood clotting) and contribute to inflammatory and immune responses. Contain functional mitochondria that can be released upon activation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After each of three repeated bouts of exhaustive treadmill exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a physiological stress response, possible minor vascular damage, or inflammatory processes. Platelet activation and degranulation could contribute to the post-exercise rise in cf mt-DNA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study aimed to identify biomarkers for predicting severe dengue disease progression and cytokine release syndrome (CRS) by evaluating an integrated multiplex panel of cytokines/chemokines and clinical parameters in adult dengue patients. Researchers compared various severity groups (mild, severe without/with comorbidities, and healthy controls) across acute and convalescent phases. Key findings highlighted how specific markers like IL-18, IL-8, IL-6, and IFN-γ are altered in severe dengue, particularly with comorbidities, and their correlation with clinical indicators such as platelet counts and NS1. The study also characterized demographic and clinical parameters across patient groups, confirming the utility of a 24-plex cytokine/chemokine panel designed based on extensive literature review.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on biomarker identification and monitoring for dengue disease progression and severity
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study on 30 adult dengue patients (mean age 61.6 years, 17 male, 13 female) categorized into three severity groups based on WHO criteria (1997 and 2009): Mild Dengue Fever (MDF, n=10), Severe Dengue Disease without comorbidities (SDD-C, n=10), and Severe Dengue Disease with comorbidities (SDD+C, n=10). Six healthy controls were also included. A 24-plex panel of cytokines/chemokines was used to measure plasma levels, along with clinical blood parameters. Blood samples were collected during the acute febrile phase (before 6 days from disease onset) and the convalescent phase (9-18 days from disease onset). No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on natural disease progression and biomarker correlation with severity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased levels reported. Decreased platelets were significantly (P < 0.05) associated with increased IL-18. Significant difference observed in overall acute dengue compared to convalescent dengue (P < 0.01). Peaked in the acute phase of the MDF group and decreased as the disease progressed to severe. The increased level in the severe group exceeded that in the MDF group in the convalescent phase. Exhibited a significant negative correlation with NS1 (P < 0.01) and IL-18 (r = 0.393, P = 0.031). Showed a significant direct correlation with IL-4 (r = 0.523, P = 0.007), RANTES (r = 0.563, P = 0.001), and IL-13 (r = 0.569, P = 0.002). Significant platelet induction caused a considerable increase in serum IL-18.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for hemostasis and blood clotting, also plays a role in immune responses. Contains the IL-18 gene that is transcribed when activated, leading to aggregation, adherence to endothelium, and triggering phagocytosis by macrophages.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dengue disease, acute and convalescent phases of dengue infection across MDF, SDD-C, and SDD+C severity groups. Specifically associated with increased IL-18 levels and correlated with NS1 and various cytokines/chemokines.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels (thrombocytopenia) are a clinical characteristic of dengue severity and are associated with increased IL-18. Indicates involvement in disease progression and immunomodulation in response to DENV infection. Severe thrombocytopenia is associated with severe dengue (SDD).

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly lower in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Small blood cells that help the body form clots to stop bleeding
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tended toward higher values in women compared to men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in blood clotting and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sex differences in seniors, contributing to inflammatory indices (NLR, SII).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to changes in inflammatory indices (NLR, SII).

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (F2.48 = 342.75; p < 0.001), decreased 3 hours after (p < 0.001), and remained significantly different compared to pre-exercise at 24 hours (p < 0.046). Demonstrated excellent reliability (ICC = 0.86).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cell fragments involved in blood clotting and wound healing.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High reliability, suggesting suitability as a blood-based biomarker for monitoring physiological exercise response and recovery status in endurance athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Increased after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.39). Significantly increased after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.039). Meaningfully augmented post-PS training program. Positive moderate correlation with weight (r = 0.41, p = 0.042).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates blood clotting, wound healing, and inflammatory responses; exercise-activated PLT contributes to the release of growth factors and proinflammatory mediators.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after intense physical exertion; post-PS training program, intensification of the exercise program, strenuous exercise; correlation with body weight.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological stress or adaptive response to intense exercise; adaptative changes in the whole organism and metabolism, informing optimal management of stimulus/recovery; associated with improved exercise performance due to the release of ergogenic mediators and stimulus for augmenting performance-improving nitric oxide.
