document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the cytokine changes, tissue viability, and remodeling markers in an in vitro osteoarthritic knee joint explant co-culture model (comprising cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) in response to hyperacute serum treatment. The findings demonstrate that hyperacute serum induces cell proliferation, shifts the cytokine milieu towards a less inflamed state, and improves tissue remodeling in the osteoarthritic joint model.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hyperacute Serum Treatment and IL-1β Stimulation in an in vitro explant co-culture model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Osteoarthritic knee joint explants (cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial membrane) were stimulated with IL-1β as an inflammatory trigger, then treated with 10% hyperacute serum containing medium. The treatment lasted up to 5 days, with supernatants collected on days 3 and 5. Comparisons were made against human serum albumin-treated controls. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either hyperacute serum or IL-1β beyond their observed effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 2-year prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in bone remodeling and turnover markers in children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from diagnosis through chemotherapy. It revealed that ALL onset significantly slows bone remodeling, with significantly lower bone turnover markers at diagnosis compared to controls. During chemotherapy, particularly the induction phase, these markers increased, suggesting a recovery of bone turnover, and a potential balance in active bone remodeling by the end of therapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Risk-adapted multiagent antileukemic chemotherapy, specifically for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), including Glucocorticoid (GC) therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 2-year prospective longitudinal study involved chemotherapy according to international AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 and ESPhALL 2017 protocols, with patients stratified by risk (standard, intermediate, high). The treatment included induction, reinduction/delayed intensification (two phases of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy), and a maintenance phase. Blood sampling was conducted at 5 time points (T0-T4) from diagnosis until treatment cessation. No specific numerical drug dosages were reported, but it was noted that different glucocorticoid doses did not significantly alter bone marker profiles after intensive therapy phases.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher and significantly elevated in ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key regulator of osteoclastogenesis (bone resorption cells), essential for osteoclast formation, activation, and survival, thus promoting bone resorption, as part of the RANKL/OPG/RANK axis. Leukemia cells produce high levels of RANKL.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with increased bone resorption and B-ALL cell-mediated bone damage and bone pathology in ALL, indicating dysregulation in bone remodeling due to leukemia, possibly from direct effects of leukemic blasts on bone metabolism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of a structured exercise program in adult women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. The primary aim is to mitigate anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) by assessing changes in circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain, LVEF). Secondary objectives include evaluating other cardiac health parameters (blood pressure, HR, HRV, recovery HR), physical function, self-reported physical activity, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. The protocol also details the planned methodology for assessing these outcomes and administrative aspects of the study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anserine supplementation (oral intake)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. While both doses conferred antioxidant benefits, some dose-dependent effects were observed, particularly for cell damage markers (GPT, CKMB) and haematological parameters (MCV, MCHC) which were more pronounced with the high dose.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The highest red blood cell (RBC) counts in the female groups were observed in the middle of the study (4th–6th week). In male swimmers, RBC count fluctuated, with the highest values at the beginning and end of the study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All immune-related complete blood counts demonstrated significant changes over time (p<0.001), but no significant changes between groups.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated a stepwise, serum- and feeder-free protocol for differentiating human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) into hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) and red blood cells (RBCs). It specifically examined the effect of enforced HOXB4 expression on this process. While HOXB4 activation increased the production of multipotent HPCs (peaking around days 6-10, characterized by CD34, CD43, and Runx1C-GFP expression) and immature erythroid cells, it ultimately failed to promote the maturation, efficient enucleation, or expansion of adult-like RBCs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enforced expression of HOXB4 in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized a tamoxifen-inducible HOXB4-ER T2 expression system within H1 hESCs, under a CAG promoter. HOXB4 activation was induced with tamoxifen for varying durations: 10 days for HPC assessment, days 10-24 for RBC maturation, or days 0-24 for overall differentiation and expansion. This was integrated into a multi-step, serum- and feeder-free differentiation protocol lasting at least 17 days, involving sequential addition of various growth factors and cytokines (e.g., BMP4, VEGF, Wnt3a, Activin A, GSK-3 2 inhibitor VIII, FGF- 1, SCF, IGF2, TPO, Heparin, IBMX, Hydrocortisone, Flt3L, IL-3, IL-11, EPO, IGF1) at specific concentrations and time points. No quantitative dose-response comparisons for either HOXB4 activation or the overall differentiation protocol were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review discusses the practical application, limitations, and recommendations for blood biomarker profiling and monitoring in high-performance athletes, aiming to optimize physiology, nutrition, training, recovery, and prevent injury/illness. It covers various physiological and procedural factors affecting analysis, the importance of individualized reference ranges, the utility of specific nutritional and stress-related biomarkers (e.g., Omega-3 Index, carotenoids, redox status, glutamine, sex and thyroid hormones, IGF-1, cortisol, iron, tHbmass, inflammatory markers, CK, urea, melatonin, vitamins), and considerations for managing energy availability, training load, and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Comprehensive Blood Biomarker Profiling and Monitoring for Athlete Management, Nutritional Intervention, and Training Adaptation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The therapeutic approach involves comprehensive blood biomarker profiling (infrequent screening for deficiencies, several months apart) and monitoring (frequent assessment of adaptation/recovery, days or weeks apart) in athletes. This strategy is tailored to individual needs, sport, sex, and training context, utilizing individualized adaptive ranges and critical difference thresholds. It includes careful consideration of pre-analytic factors (e.g., posture, tourniquet use, centrifugation time, time of day, psychological stress, fasting status, menstrual cycle day, hydration status, duration/intensity/mode of prior exercise) and minimizing blood draw volumes, such as the removal of an average of 180 ml (range 82–314 ml) of blood in a simulated altitude study which negated hypoxia-induced erythropoiesis and aerobic performance gains. Specific interventions include targeted dietary/antioxidant supplementation (e.g., Omega-3 to increase OM3I from ~4.5% to ~6%, N-acetylcysteine for low red blood cell glutathione, Vitamin C for low plasma concentrations), iron supplementation for deficiency (e.g., ferritin < 12 ng mL−1 leading to dramatic increases in tHbmass), and nutritional adjustments for energy availability management (e.g., during persistently excessive endurance exercise, 8 weeks of gross energy deficiency, or carbohydrate restriction impacting testosterone/cortisol responses). The monitoring is applied across various contexts like intense exercise, eccentric loading, single matches, long-haul travel, sleep loss, and season-long competitive demands, with biomarker responses proportional to the imposed stress and recovery status.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: Red Blood Cell & Haemoglobin Parameters (RBC Populations, tHbmass, Haemoglobin Concentration, Blood Cell Counts)
matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood, Bone marrow (release) and blood (circulation), Blood sample
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Population Status, Release rate and count, Mass measurement, Protein Level (mass), Cell count, Concentration measurement, Protein Concentration

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Status of red blood cell populations (no specific quantitative value provided beyond general assessment). RBCs are released from bone marrow at > 2 million per second; each cubic milliliter of blood contains 4–6 million RBCs. Small blood losses via phlebotomy are naturally replenished rapidly. Environment- or training-induced gains in total haemoglobin mass (tHbmass) can be reversed with blood loss (e.g., 180 ml phlebotomy to negate hypoxia-induced erythropoiesis). Endurance athletes have around a 40% higher tHbmass than the general population. Blood cell counts are diluted due to hypervolemia associated with endurance training, giving a false impression of anaemia. Haemoglobin concentration is poorly correlated with tHbmass since it is dependent upon blood volume and is susceptible to dilution from plasma volume expansion.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary function is oxygen transport throughout the body and maintaining total blood volume, crucial for endurance performance. tHbmass reflects the total oxygen-carrying capacity. Haemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. Blood cell counts are indicators of blood volume status and oxygen-carrying capacity, used in the diagnosis of anemia.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-performance physiology, endurance performance, training interventions, natural physiological processes and blood loss, simulated altitude research study with phlebotomy, endurance athletes, altitude training, iron deficiency, general blood testing in athletes, plasma volume expansion (e.g., with heat acclimation or prolonged exercise), endurance training-induced hypervolemia in athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates oxygen carrying capacity and potential for anemia, which directly impacts endurance performance and the ability to tolerate training load. Essential for maintaining oxygen carrying capacity; rapid replenishment after minor blood losses among non-athletes. tHbmass directly impacts aerobic performance; blood loss can negate aerobic performance gains. Enables greater maximal oxygen-carrying capacity and higher aerobic power; indicates sub-optimal aerobic power if compromised. Blood cell counts can lead to misinterpretation of physiological status, specifically giving a false impression of anaemia when true red blood cell mass may be normal, thus masking or misrepresenting health status. Haemoglobin concentration is a poor indicator of true oxygen-carrying capacity (tHbmass) due to susceptibility to dilution effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This exploratory study investigated α-synuclein-positive extracellular vesicles (α-synuclein-EVs) and poly (ADP-ribose) (PAR) levels in the plasma of Parkinson disease (PD) patients. The aim was to evaluate these as non-invasive biomarkers for PD diagnosis, severity, and progression, comparing PD patients to unaffected controls, Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Key findings showed significantly higher α-synuclein-EV levels in PD patients, which could distinguish them from controls and other neurodegenerative diseases. Detectable PAR plasma levels were associated with higher α-synuclein-EV levels in PD patients, suggesting a PARP-1/α-synuclein cross-talk in systemic circulation. The study also determined that α-synuclein-EVs do not primarily originate from red blood cells. While α-synuclein-EVs showed potential as a diagnostic marker and an initial correlation with disease severity (UPDRS scores) in a discovery cohort, this correlation was not consistently replicated in the larger cohort, indicating that single timepoint levels may not reliably predict disease severity. Longitudinal studies are suggested to evaluate their role as markers of disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker identification, assessment, and characterization for Parkinson Disease (PD) and related neurodegenerative conditions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study focused on biomarker analysis, not a therapeutic intervention. Plasma samples were collected from 57 PD patients (discovery cohort 20, replication cohort 37), 20 unaffected individuals, 20 Alzheimer's disease patients, and 20 dementia with Lewy bodies patients. All cohorts were age/sex matched. α-synuclein extracellular vesicles were quantified from platelet-free/poor plasma using nanoscale flow cytometry, and poly ADP-ribose levels were determined using sandwich ELISA kits. No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median RBC-EV concentration was 6,593 EVs/µl (range 1,200–26,827) in the PD group, significantly higher compared to AD dementia and DLB groups (p = 0.059). Unaffected controls (CU): 2,910 EVs/µl (range 1,200–6,453); AD dementia: 4,017 EVs/µl (range 0–10,340); DLB: 3,480 EVs/µl (range 480–13,340).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Extracellular vesicles derived from red blood cells are involved in intercellular communication and reflect the state of red blood cells. Investigated to understand the origin of α-synuclein EVs.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of Parkinson's disease from AD dementia and DLB, specifically when investigating the origin of plasma-derived α-synuclein-EVs.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated concentration in PD patients compared to AD and DLB. However, analysis of α-synuclein+CD235a+ EVs indicated that peripheral α-synuclein EVs do not primarily originate from RBCs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Dynamic changes over the one-year cycle, including significant decreases in both groups and a subsequent increase in the placebo group (GP).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant group or group x time effect from vitamin D supplementation was observed. Dynamic changes included a significant decrease (p < 0.05) in the supplemented group (GS) and the placebo group (GP), with a subsequent significant increase in RBC noted between T3 and T4 in the placebo group (GP).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main cellular component responsible for oxygen transport and cellular oxygenation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training cycle in young soccer players, competitive and pre-season training periods, influenced by high training loads, 8-week vitamin D supplementation, and home isolation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates oxygen-carrying capacity and erythropoietic response to training demands. Changes were primarily influenced by training loads, with home-based training during isolation potentially supporting cellular oxygenation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower counts in HCC patients compared to both control (P = 0.001) and non-malignant patients (P = 0.0008–<0.0001). No significant differences between non-cirrhotic and cirrhotic chronic HCV or SVR groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Oxygen transport, maintaining tissue oxygenation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison of HCC patients with control and non-malignant (chronic HCV and SVR) patient groups, and comparison between non-/cirrhotic chronic HCV and SVR groups.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates hematological alteration in HCC patients. Lower counts suggest anemia, a common complication in cancer.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant changes (P > 0.05) in hematological parameters were observed throughout the experiment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary function is oxygen transport in the blood.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, suggesting stable oxygen carrying capacity under the study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 80 mg/day oral iron supplementation on hematological parameters, muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, Mb), and cortisol levels in elite male cyclists during a 3-week stage race (Vuelta a España). It concluded that iron supplementation effectively prevented declines in iron metabolism and hematological profiles (serum iron, ferritin, hemoglobin, hematocrit, TSI, TP, RBC), significantly reduced accumulated stress (cortisol), and significantly lowered Creatine Kinase (CK) levels within the supplemented group, thereby contributing to optimal recovery and performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Iron Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 80 mg/day of oral iron (800 mg of iron protein succinylate, e.g., Ferplex 40®), administered as two 40 mg doses per day (during breakfast and dinner). The supplementation lasted for a 4-week period, starting one week before and continuing throughout the 3-week Vuelta a España stage race. No dose-response comparisons were reported, but a control group received no oral iron.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ITG showed significant increases between T1 (4.8 ± 0.3 × 10^6/µL) and T2 (5.3 ± 0.2 × 10^6/µL; p < 0.05). Group-by-time interaction showed significant differences (p < 0.001; η2p = 0.815) in favour of ITG. CG did not show significant differences between T1 and T2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Transport of oxygen from the lungs to tissues and carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Oral iron supplementation during a 3-week professional cycling stage race.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Directly correlates with oxygen-carrying capacity, which is fundamental for aerobic endurance performance and recovery in athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the test-retest reliability and suitability of various subjective, muscle force, and blood-based physiological markers (including oxidative stress markers, hormones, cytokines, and haematological parameters) for monitoring exercise response and recovery processes in endurance athletes after strenuous endurance exercise bouts, concluding that TBARS and IL-1RA exhibited the best reliability and suitability.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous Endurance Running Field Tests (RFTs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two identical 60-minute continuous endurance running field tests (RFTs) were performed, separated by a four-week recovery period. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of running at an intensity corresponding to 95% of Heart Rate (HR) at Individual Anaerobic Threshold (IAT), followed by 20 minutes at 110% of HR at IAT to ensure exhaustion. Biomarkers were measured before, immediately after, 3 hours after, and 24 hours after each bout. No dose-response comparisons for varying exercise intensities or durations were reported, but reliability was compared between trained and untrained subgroups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately after exercise (p < 0.001), decreased 3 hours after (p < 0.001), and remained significantly different compared to pre-exercise at 24 hours (p < 0.001). Demonstrated good reliability (ICC = 0.84).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Red blood cells, primarily responsible for oxygen transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Endurance running field tests (RFTs) and subsequent recovery phases; haematological markers during physiological exercise response and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High reliability, suggesting suitability as a blood-based biomarker for monitoring physiological exercise response and recovery status in endurance athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No alterations or differences were found during or after the 6-week supplementation protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary transporters of oxygen to tissues.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day) combined with a CrossFit training program.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that the supplementation and training program did not negatively impact oxygen transport capacity or blood component levels, maintaining health and performance potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary function is oxygen transport throughout the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of anemia, erythrocytosis, or general hematological health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positive large correlation with CMJ with hands on hips performance (r = 0.65, p = 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the variation in red blood cell size, indicative of erythropoiesis and inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase; correlation with Countermovement Jump (CMJ) performance.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher RCDW associated with better CMJ performance, suggesting adaptive hematological changes or a physiological state supporting explosive power.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased at T1 compared to T0 (p=0.0004); not significantly different to T0 at T2.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the variation in red blood cell volume or size (anisocytosis)
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) at engraftment time point T1
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates red blood cell system status and heterogeneity post-alloSCT.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Showed different patterns of changes; suggested to decrease at end of training cycle
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed different patterns of changes across all groups. Suggested to decrease at the end of a training cycle, but increased erythropoiesis was not observed in this study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the variation in the size of red blood cells, indicating heterogeneity, and related to red blood cell parameters and erythropoiesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional swimming training period and end of training cycle.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Changes may suggest erythropoiesis decreases. Part of blood morphology assessment for monitoring recovery and provides general health information.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective study analyzed 4054 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to investigate the association of preoperative red blood cell distribution width (RDW) and hemoglobin-to-RDW ratio (HRR) with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). The findings demonstrated that elevated RDW and decreased HRR were robustly and independently associated with a higher risk of CA-AKI, suggesting their utility for early risk identification.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Coronary Angiography (CAG) or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) involving contrast media administration.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study retrospectively analyzed 4054 patients undergoing CAG or PCI. Patients received contrast media as part of standard clinical practice. Excessive contrast media was defined as exceeding a calculated maximum dose (5 mL × weight (kg)/Scr at baseline (mg/dL)). However, no dose-response comparisons for RDW or HRR associations with varying contrast media doses or procedural specifics were reported in relation to CA-AKI risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher in patients who developed CA-AKI (median 13.9% [IQR 13.2%, 14.9%]) compared to those without (median 13.5% [IQR 12.9%, 14.2%], p < 0.001). Positively associated with serum creatinine (Scr) elevation (multivariable β = 2.496, 95% CI = 1.784–3.208, p < 0.001). High RDW (≥13.8%) was significantly associated with a higher risk of CA-AKI (multivariable RR = 1.540, 95% CI = 1.345–1.762, p < 0.001). The normal reference range for RDW is 11.0%–14.5%.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the heterogeneity of circulating erythrocytes; serves as an indicator of systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, or erythropoiesis dysfunction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Preoperative measurement in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and associated with the development of contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: An independent and robust risk factor for CA-AKI, valuable for early identification and prognostication of cardiovascular and renal diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: A longitudinal study investigated hematological responses and hydration status in NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait (SCT) compared to controls (CON) over a two-year period, encompassing an entire athletic season and pre-season training. The study found that SCT players exhibited altered hematological profiles, including higher red cell distribution width (RDW), elevated serum uric acid, and greater creatine kinase (CPK) levels at pre-camp and throughout the season. Furthermore, SCT players showed altered hydration status with lower pre- and post-practice urine electrolytes and specific gravity, but higher sweat sodium, potassium, and chloride concentrations, indicating differences in fluid balance and electrolyte regulation during intensive training. These findings suggest potential implications for kidney function and muscle damage in SCT players during long-term conditioning and highlight the importance of careful hydration management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Collegiate American Football Training and Competition (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This longitudinal study observed NCAA Division I American football players over two consecutive years, encompassing an entire athletic season. This involved 17 consecutive practices in year 1 and 16 practices in year 2 between pre-camp and post-camp, followed by 13 weekly in-season competitions between post-camp and post-season. Hydration status was specifically assessed during pre-season training camp practices conducted under hot and humid environmental conditions (average 26.8            1.9 °C WBGT and 68.9            11.1% relative humidity). The study focused on the physiological responses to sustained physical activity and environmental exposure inherent to standard collegiate football regimens, with no explicit dose-response comparisons for varying training intensities.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Hematological index of red blood cell size variation

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: SCT players had greater RDW (14.3            0.9%) compared to CON (13.4            0.9%, p = 0.02) across all study visits (pre-camp, post-camp, post-season). The RDW value of SCT players was near the upper reference limit.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the variation in red blood cell size (anisocytosis).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NCAA Division I American football players with sickle cell trait throughout an entire athletic season (pre-camp, post-camp, post-season).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered hematological responses, a greater degree of red cell anisocytosis, and larger variation of red blood cell morphology in SCT players, potentially suggesting underlying red blood cell stress or early signs of pathology associated with microcirculatory changes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed a computational model to explain and predict changes in red blood cell parameters (RDW-CV%, Hb, MCV) during iron and folate deficiencies, highlighting RDW-CV% as an early and useful indicator for both conditions, especially in resource-limited settings for detecting folate deficiency to prevent foetal damage, and suggesting its inclusion in routine blood analyses.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Computational diagnostic modeling for nutritional deficiencies.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A computer model simulated red blood cell (RBC) formation and destruction, assuming a 120-day RBC lifespan. It used standard haematological parameters (normal Hb lower limit 110 g/l, upper normal RDW-CV% 15%) and specific parameters for normal haemopoiesis (RBC/day 40000, MCV 90, SD of MCV 10, MCH 30), iron-deficient haemopoiesis (RBC/day 30000, MCV 60, SD of MCV 7, MCH 18), and folate-deficient haemopoiesis (macrocytic pattern). Simulations ran for up to 180 days, incorporating shifts between normal and deficient states to predict changes in blood parameters. No direct therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported within the study, as it focused on diagnostic prediction.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: RDW-CV% (Red Cell Distribution Width - Coefficient of Variation)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Normal RDW-CV is 12%, with an upper limit of 15%. In iron deficiency/recovery, it increases rapidly from 11.2% to 18.3% (after 30 days) and to 21.3% (after 50 days), remaining high until a uniform cell population is established or rising again during iron repletion. In short-term folate deficiency, it rises rapidly beyond normal and stays elevated for over 100 days post-correction. It can also be high if iron is limiting in combined deficiencies. RDW-CV% is often normal in thalassaemia minor, anaemia of thalassaemia, and anaemia of chronic illness, but is low in malaria.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the variability in red blood cell size (anisocytosis), indicating heterogeneity in RBC populations.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early iron deficiency, recovery from iron deficiency, short-term folate deficiency, recovery from folate deficiency, iron supplementation, combined iron and folate deficiency (iron-limiting), thalassaemia minor, anaemia of thalassaemia, anaemia of chronic illness, and malaria.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an early indicator of iron and folate deficiencies, often preceding changes in other anaemia parameters. Useful for detecting folate deficiency to prevent foetal damage. Indicates a mixed population of red blood cells (e.g., during recovery or combined deficiencies). Helps differentiate iron deficiency from thalassaemia or anaemia of chronic illness (where it's typically normal). Associated with malaria, though less discriminatory than platelet count. Reported with 77.1% sensitivity for iron deficiency anaemia and 49.2% for iron deficiency anaemia plus latent iron deficiency, with 90.6% specificity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the expression characteristics of cuproptosis markers, oxidative stress indexes, copper metabolism, and hepatic fibrosis in Wilson disease patients, concluding that conventional chelation therapy significantly improves these abnormal markers and may reverse hepatic fibrosis progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Conventional chelation therapy using sodium dimercaptosulphonate (DMPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Sodium dimercaptosulphonate (DMPS) at 20 mg 7kg 7−1 was administered intravenously once daily for 6 days per course, dissolved in 5% glucose or 0.9% sodium chloride solution, with calcium gluconate (20 mL) given intravenously once daily for 2 days during intervals. This regimen consisted of four 8-day courses of treatment, totaling 32 days; no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Before treatment: 49.28  1 25.55  5mol 7L 7−1 (WD patients) vs control 24.70  1 12.01  5mol 7L 7−1 (P < .001, up-regulated); After treatment: decreased from 49.28  1 25.55  5mol 7L 7−1 to 34.09  1 15.02  5mol 7L 7−1 (P < .001), with levels stated as not significantly different compared to control after treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A major endogenous antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Wilson's disease patients (compared to control) and after conventional chelation therapy.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels before treatment suggest a compensatory increase in response to oxidative stress in WD. Reduction after treatment, leading to levels stated as not significantly different from control, suggests alleviation of oxidative stress and improved antioxidant status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This article updates the redox theory of aging, proposing that aging results from a decline in gene-exposome interaction plasticity due to cumulative exposure memory. It emphasizes the critical role of redox networks, particularly thiol/disulfide balance (e.g., plasma cystine to glutathione ratio), as an interface between an individual and the environment, influencing health, disease etiology, and resilience. The theory links compromised redox networks to increased oxidative stress biomarkers like hydroxynonenal and reactive carbonyls, and discusses the predictive power of the plasma CySS/GSH ratio for all-cause mortality in conditions like coronary artery disease, while also exploring implications for regenerative medicine, multimorbidity, and personalized health management.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document is a comprehensive review and theoretical discussion of the redox theory of aging, its mechanisms, and implications, including the prognostic utility of specific biomarkers. No direct therapeutic interventions were investigated.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the oxidative stress and genotoxicity in gas station refueling workers exposed to long-term, low levels of atmospheric BTEX in Nanning, China, comparing them to office workers. It found significantly higher BTEX levels in refueling areas, which, despite being generally below occupational limits, were associated with reduced antioxidant capacity (lower T-SOD and GSH) and increased oxidative stress (higher MDA and 8-OHdG) and DNA damage (higher micronucleus rate, tail moment, and Olive tail moment) in refueling workers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Long-term occupational exposure to BTEX (Benzene, Toluene, Ethylbenzene, Xylenes) compounds in gas station refueling workers, compared to office workers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Long-term occupational exposure to low levels of atmospheric BTEX, with refueling workers exposed for an average of 8.7 years. BTEX concentrations in refueling areas were significantly higher than in office areas (p < 0.001), with mean ambient air concentrations including Benzene (60.03 vs 16.86 µg/m3), Toluene (317.76 vs 89.93 µg/m3), Ethylbenzene (113.85 vs 12.09 µg/m3), m-xylene (40.91 vs 28.44 µg/m3), p-xylene (57.51 vs 10.62 µg/m3), and o-xylene (37.18 vs 15.67 µg/m3). These levels were generally below current occupational exposure limits, but fixed environmental monitoring may underestimate actual exposure. No specific dose-response analysis for individual BTEX compounds was reported in human subjects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of anserine supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress, cellular damage, and haematological biomarkers in ten healthy men. Anserine, at both low and high doses, enhanced antioxidant activity by significantly increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and preserving catalase (CAT) activity, while elevating glutathione disulfide (GSSG) and consequently lowering the GSH/GSSG ratio. Although anserine had no significant effect on glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT), myoglobin, or thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), the high dose transiently elevated glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and creatine kinase isoenzyme (CKMB). Furthermore, high-dose anserine increased mean cell volume (MCV) and decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration (MCHC), indicating altered red blood cell parameters. The findings suggest anserine preserves cellular homeostasis and protects cell integrity through enhanced antioxidant activity, potentially augmenting exercise-induced adaptive responses and recovery in healthy men.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten healthy men were administered anserine orally 1 hour prior to an exercise challenge (running time trials to volitional exhaustion, approximately 40 minutes at 50% V̇O2peak). Participants received either a low dose (ANS-LD) of 15 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, a high dose (ANS-HD) of 30 mg·kg⁻¹·bw⁻¹, or a placebo (PLA, corn starch) on three separate occasions in a randomized, placebo-controlled, repeated-measures design. Blood samples were collected at rest, 5 minutes, 60 minutes, and 24 hours post-exercise. Exercise performance (Time-to-Exhaustion) showed no significant difference between conditions. document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (p < 0.05) concentration after melatonin supplementation (e.g., 5 mg for 30 days after exercise).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation (e.g., 5 mg for 30 days or general indirect antioxidant mechanisms) in highly trained athletes to improve glutathione homeostasis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced antioxidant defenses and an extra adaptation of antioxidant systems for intense exercise, leading to improved cellular antioxidant capacity and detoxification.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated upon sorafenib exposure and in sorafenib-treated cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

document_context_data.document_summary: This article updates the redox theory of aging, proposing that aging results from a decline in gene-exposome interaction plasticity due to cumulative exposure memory. It emphasizes the critical role of redox networks, particularly thiol/disulfide balance (e.g., plasma cystine to glutathione ratio), as an interface between an individual and the environment, influencing health, disease etiology, and resilience. The theory links compromised redox networks to increased oxidative stress biomarkers like hydroxynonenal and reactive carbonyls, and discusses the predictive power of the plasma CySS/GSH ratio for all-cause mortality in conditions like coronary artery disease, while also exploring implications for regenerative medicine, multimorbidity, and personalized health management.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. The study also explored genetic associations with cerebellar gray matter volume, linking several genetic variants to cardiovascular disease and other health indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of early brain injury and cognitive impairment following aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH) using MRI and cognitive assessments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 27 good-grade SAH patients (WFNS 1 and 2) underwent MRI scanning and comprehensive cognitive assessment at three time-points: within the first 72 hours (acute phase), at 5-10 days (subacute phase), and at 3 months (chronic phase) post-SAH. An additional 27 paired healthy controls were recruited for comparison. No specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study of SAH's natural course and sequelae.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cerebellum (measured via MRI VBM, specifically lobule VII: Crus II, Crus I, VIIb and VIIIa)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Patients who later developed cognitive impairment at 3 months post-SAH already showed a significant apparent higher GM volume in an overlapping cerebellar region (extending into lobules VIIb and VIIIa) at scan 1 (acute phase). This acute measure discriminated patients with vs. without cognitive impairment with 84% accuracy (sensitivity 82%, specificity 86%, AUC 0.805). Persistent and significantly higher GM volume in patients compared to controls (mainly lobule VII: Crus II, Crus I, and VIIb) was observed at 3 months, with cognitively impaired patients having higher GM volumes (Cohen's d = 0.72).

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A promising risk stratification biomarker for predicting future cognitive impairment at 3 months post-SAH, even in patients initially appearing clinically good grade. Persistent abnormalities are linked to worse cognitive outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally higher in recovered/recovering patients compared to severely ill acute cases. No significant difference in asymptomatic recovery compared to seronegative controls. Greater suppressive function observed in recovering subjects compared to severe acute disease.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Immune regulation, preventing excessive immune responses and autoimmunity by suppressing effector T cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between recovered and severely ill COVID-19 patients, comparison of Treg cytokine release and suppressive function between previously asymptomatic COVID-19 patients and seronegative controls, recovery from severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher function indicates more effective immune control and better recovery outcomes. Normalization in asymptomatic recovery suggests successful immune resolution. Impaired function in severe cases contributes to immunopathology.

The findings revealed significantly elevated CD4/CD8 ratios in sarcoidosis lymph nodes compared to BAL fluid and lung cancer metastases, and a higher ratio in stage I sarcoidosis than stage II, aiding in differential diagnosis and understanding disease immunopathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic analysis of lymphocyte profiles using flow cytometry on samples obtained via Endobronchial Ultrasound-guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) from mediastinal lymph nodes and Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) fluid.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Single cell suspensions were prepared from EBUS-TBNA samples of mediastinal lymph nodes (from 26 sarcoidosis and 16 lung cancer patients) and BAL fluid (50 ml saline instilled/retrieved three times). Flow cytometric analysis targeted surface markers (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19, CD25) and FoxP3 expression on 1-3x10^4 cells per antibody combination. EBUS-TBNA was performed five to six times per patient. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the procedure was for diagnostic sampling.
