document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reported to be increased after boxing matches in which the athlete sustained direct or repetitive blows to the head. Also found to be increased in concussed hockey players.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Glial cell biomarker, indicating brain injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Concussion sustained during boxing matches or in hockey players.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic and recovery marker for brain injury/concussion.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the discovery of novel traumatic brain injury (TBI) biomarkers using autoimmune profiling in both rat models and human patients. It details methodologies for sample preparation, protein analysis via 2D gel electrophoresis, immunoprofiling, and the development of an immunosorbent electrochemiluminescence assay (IEA) for peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6). The main findings establish PRDX6 as a candidate TBI biomarker, showing its astrocytic expression, TBI-induced autoantibody reactivity in rats, gender differences in baseline human plasma levels, and a significant, persistent approximately fourfold elevation of circulating PRDX6 in humans following mild-to-moderate TBI, which is proportional to injury severity and independent of imaging findings. The study also acknowledges S100B and GFAP as other relevant TBI indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) injury model
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human TBI was observed as mild-to-moderate (median GCS 15), with plasma collected at 4-24 hours and 2-7 days post-injury; no direct manipulation or controlled dose was applied, though PRDX6 response correlated with injury severity. In rat models, severe CCI injury was induced using a stereotaxic impactor with a 5 mm impactor at a 20-degree angle to a depth of 2 mm at 5 m/sec with a dwell time of 500 msec to maximize autoimmune response. No specific dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported for either human TBI or rat CCI, beyond PRDX6 response proportionality in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Responses in serum titers of anti-S100B antibodies were proportional to the number and severity of hits experienced. S100B protein levels increase in blood in response to TBI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A long-recognized TBI biomarker, highly expressed in astrocytes. Released upon repetitive disruption of the blood-brain barrier, leading to immune activation and autoantibody formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Repeated sub-concussive hits to the head (e.g., in collegiate football players); Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate TBI biomarker; autoantibodies against S100B correlate with changes in brain structure detected by diffusion tensor imaging, indicating its role in TBI assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationship between serum S100B protein levels and disease severity in hospitalized Covid-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infected) patients. It revealed that increased S100B serum concentrations significantly correlate with Covid-19 disease severity, intensity of care, inflammatory processes, and several inflammatory and organ damage markers, suggesting S100B as a novel biomarker for monitoring disease course and prognosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on the progression of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Covid-19) in hospitalized patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received standard care following WHO guidelines. Disease severity was quantified using a Covid-score and categorization into High Intensity Care (HIC) or Low Intensity Care (LIC) wards. No specific intervention doses or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased levels significantly correlated with Covid-19 disease severity (p < 0.006 for intensity of care; correlation with Covid-Score 0.61, p < 0.01; Multiple R-squared values for clinical risk score 0.4369 and 0.3751). Mean values: 8.80 ".10.24 ng/mL in High Intensity Care (HIC) vs 0.62 ".10 ng/mL in Low Intensity Care (LIC) (p < 0.006). Samples below detection limit of 0.1 ng/mL were assigned 0 ng/mL.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Calcium-binding protein that acts as a Danger-Associated Molecular Pattern (DAMP) molecule, involved in inflammatory processes, interacts with the RAGE receptor to initiate intracellular signaling, stimulates pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion, and participates in pulmonary inflammatory processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: SARS-CoV-2 infection (Covid-19 patients) in relation to disease severity and progression.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Represents a marker of clinical severity in SARS-CoV-2 infected patients, indicates inflammation and potential organ damage, and is useful for monitoring disease course, prognosis, and potentially as a therapeutic target.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of extreme static apnea on blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and neurovascular unit (NVU) protein exchange in ultra-elite breath-hold divers, aiming to distinguish between hypoxemic- and hypercapnic-induced stress. Findings revealed that hypoxemia, independently of hypercapnia, is a critical stimulus contributing to increased BBB permeability and neuronal-gliovascular reactivity, leading to a net cerebral output of NVU proteins. This suggests transient NVU dysfunction rather than structural damage, with evidence of active repair mechanisms and highlighting hemodynamic stress as a key factor in BBB disruption.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Maximal static apnea (voluntary asphyxia) and breath-hold diving
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten ultra-elite breath-hold divers performed two maximal dry apneas: Normoxic Normoventilation (NX) with an average apnea duration of 5m 6s (range: 3m 37s to 6m 49s), resulting in severe hypoxemia and hypercapnia; and Hyperoxic Hyperventilation (HX) with an average apnea duration of 15m 59s (range: 9m 39s to 21m 2s), preceded by 15 min of 100% O2 hyperventilation (targeting PET CO2 ~20 mmHg), which alleviated hypoxemia while compounding hypercapnia. Biomarker measurements were taken at baseline (pre-apnea) and at the apnea breakpoint, coinciding with the most severe hypoxemic-hypercapnic stress. NVU protein output was more pronounced in NX compared to HX (P < 0.05). Serial measurements for temporal dynamics and maximal rates of transcerebral protein flux were ethically constrained by blood volume loss, thus no specific dose-response comparisons were reported; however, biomarker output partially recovered post-NX, suggesting transient rather than sustained effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Serum, systemic and transcerebral circulation (net exchange via arterial and internal jugular venous sampling)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Marked elevations (P < 0.05 vs. baseline) in net cerebral output (v > a). Output was more pronounced in normoxic normoventilation (NX) compared to hyperoxic hyperventilation (HX) (P < 0.05 vs. HX). Apnea-induced elevations in venous S100B were comparable to a submaximal (~30%) BBB disruption. Global cerebral output was ~17 pg/min, systemic accumulation ~12 pg/min, and turnover rate ~6 pg/min. A relationship was observed between apnea-induced elevation in IJVP and the increase in the S100B gradient in NX (r = -0.579, P = 0.049). Levels partially recovered after NX.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Calcium-binding astrocytic protein, found at the perivascular brain space; a molecular reporter of increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, reflecting glial synthesis and extravasation, involved in gliovascular reactivity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Maximal dry apnea and breath-hold diving (before, during, and post-NX recovery) under normoxic and hyperoxic conditions, particularly severe apneic hypoxemia-hypercapnia (NX condition) and elevated IJVP.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of blood-brain barrier permeability and glio-vascular damage; reflects increased neuronal-gliovascular reactivity. Indicates transient neurovascular unit (NVU) 'dysfunction' (not structural 'damage'), highlights active repair mechanisms, and is implicated in transient loss of motor control ('samba'). Peak concentrations were generally below pathologic thresholds for traumatic brain injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly associated with estimated subphenotypes (p < 0.05 after correction for multiple testing), but specific change direction/magnitude not detailed for this individual protein.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Patient subphenotype classification in a cardiac cohort.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates protein involvement in patient subphenotype classification, which may relate to prognosis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant increase in S100A9 levels (in lung and plasma); elevated serum S100A8/S100A9 levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Calcium-binding proteins, major DAMPs (Damage-Associated Molecular Patterns) released during lung injury. Inflamed lung tissues release IL-17, which provokes neutrophils to produce S100A8/A9, inducing apoptosis of alveolar epithelial cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: LPS-induced ARDS mice, patients with COVID-19-related ARDS; COPD and IPF.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlates with disease severity of COVID-19; negative correlation between COPD lung function and S100A8/S100A9 levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified by both MALDI-TOF/TOF and ESI–MS e. In silico digestion yields Lys-ending/Arg-ending peptide ratio of 1.6.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identification and characterization of hiPSC pluripotency markers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Candidate pluripotency marker for hiPSCs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathological landscape, subclonal evolution, and dynamics of gene fusions, specifically KMT2A/AFDN and a novel CCDC32/CBX3, along with chimeric RNA variants, in 16 adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) patients undergoing treatment. It aimed to understand treatment resistance and relapse mechanisms by monitoring cytogenetic, RNA-seq, and genome-wide changes from diagnosis to relapse. The research identified the CCDC32/CBX3 fusion as a new therapeutic vulnerability that promotes cell cycle progression and contributes to AML pathogenesis and treatment resistance, highlighting its prognostic significance and the necessity of advanced molecular profiling for cryptic gene fusion detection.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (including high-dose cytarabine (HIDAC) and (7+3) induction chemotherapy) and Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (for Patient 7).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient 7 received HIDAC chemotherapy followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient 20 received (7+3) induction chemotherapy followed by HIDAC consolidation. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study primarily focused on biomarker monitoring and molecular changes rather than specific treatment efficacy across different doses. The study also included functional validation of gene fusion in vitro, which is not a treatment per se but part of the investigation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline (unstimulated) mRNA levels were close to significance (P = 0.06) for being higher in MIS-C patient cells relative to healthy controls. Higher levels were observed in fully convalescent children (>30 days after hospital admission).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Negative regulator of TLR signaling, involved in dampening cytokine production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline (unstimulated) in MIS-C patients compared to healthy controls, persisting in convalescent children.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potentially associated with dampened TLR responses and TLR hyporesponsiveness. Indicates lasting immune dysregulation in convalescent MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated immune subphenotypes and biomarker differences in critically ill adult COVID-19 patients from the REMAP-CAP trial. It identified three distinct subphenotypes based on biomarker patterns, revealing differential treatment effects of ABO-compatible convalescent plasma therapy on hospital mortality and organ support free days (OSFD-21). Seronegative patients showed significantly higher hospital mortality, with specific biomarker profiles varying by serostatus within subphenotypes. The findings suggest that convalescent plasma therapy should be avoided in subphenotypes 2 and 3 and emphasize the importance of patient selection based on host immune response for COVID-19 immunotherapy.

1.11), mortality OR 1.01 (0.80

No specific dose-response comparisons for plasma were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study identified a robust signature of 40 novel and reproducible plasma and serum protein biomarkers associated with Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) in multiple human cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. These proteins, many of which are muscle-enriched, correlated with clinical severity and functional traits, outperformed existing clinical markers like CK, and showed mechanistic links to androgen receptor gene regulation and muscle pathology, indicating their potential as early predictors of treatment effects and for tracking disease progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery and Disease Characterization (Observational Study)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was primarily an observational study focused on biomarker identification and disease characterization in Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy (SBMA) across human patient cohorts and AR113Q mouse models. No therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were conducted. Plasma and serum samples were collected from SBMA patients and healthy controls, with protein levels measured using targeted proteomic approaches (Olink platforms). Longitudinal plasma samples were also collected from male AR113Q mice (12-28 weeks of age), and secondary mechanistic analyses included public data from female mice treated with Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to investigate AR links.

matched_biomarker_details.biomarker_name: SBMA-associated protein signature (a set of 40 proteins)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Mixed (many increased, some like RGMA, MSTN, ART3 decreased)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 40 highly reproducible SBMA-associated proteins identified out of nearly 3,000 measured; robustly enriched in gene sets of skeletal muscle expression, mitochondrial processes, and calcium signaling. The differential abundance was highly correlated across cohorts (r = 0.78, P < 0.0001). Differentiated SBMA patients from controls with an average AUC of 0.94 (SD = 0.06). Many outperformed currently used clinical laboratory tests (e.g., creatine kinase [CK]) in distinguishing patients from controls, with 20 of 40 proteins showing more significant association than CK (P_adj < 4.6 × 10–5) and 31 of 40 proteins showing less variability than CK (coefficient of variation < 49.8%).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Enriched in gene sets associated with skeletal muscle expression and function, RNA Binding, Mitochondrion, and Calcium Signaling, reflecting disease features in SBMA. Many are enriched in skeletal muscle and tongue tissue expression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identification in SBMA patients compared to healthy controls (NIH, UCL Discovery, and independent replication cohorts); also investigated in AR113Q preclinical mouse model.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential for use as early predictors of treatment effects in clinical trials and for distinguishing SBMA patients from controls. Correlated with clinical and functional traits in patients, including inverse correlation with 'walking' and 'stairs' subscales of SBMAFRS and 6MWT, indicating higher levels correlate with increased disease severity and lower limb impairment; also correlated with thigh MRI muscle fat fraction (MFF).

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery Method: Nano-omics integrative proteomics workflow utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas for glioblastoma (GB).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved inducing murine glioblastoma by stereotactic injection of 50,000 GL261 cells into the striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Liposomes (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000) were prepared at a final lipid concentration of 25 mM and administered intravenously at a lipid dose of 0.125 mM/g body weight (equivalent to 5 mg/kg doxorubicin-loaded liposomes) 10 minutes prior to blood collection in mice. In human validation, ex vivo nanoparticle corona analysis was performed on pre-operative plasma samples from 10 high-grade glioma patients. Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. Matched resected tumor tissue from human patients was analyzed by LCM-coupled LC:MS/MS. No specific dose-response comparisons for nanoparticle application or tumor cell inoculation were reported for therapeutic purposes, as the focus was on biomarker discovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Progressively upregulated with increasing disease burden; upregulated in tumour tissue; upregulated in human plasma (Supplementary Fig 6)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum pathway and phagosome pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Increasing Glioblastoma (GB) disease burden in mice and human patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for Glioblastoma (GB) progression.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated innate immune functions in children with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 exposure. It revealed a persistent, genetically modulated Toll-like receptor (TLR)-tolerant phenotype in peripheral blood cells, characterized by severely dampened cytokine responses (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-12p40, IL-10) and elevated gene expression of negative regulators of TLR signaling (SOCS1, TOLLIP, SHIP1, SARM1) both acutely and in convalescence. The study also identified increased plasma zonulin levels, indicating gut leakage. Critically, children carrying rare heterozygous variants of the lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) gene exhibited reduced TLR hyporesponsiveness, alongside lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, altered energy metabolism, more profound lymphopenia, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, indicating a more severe inflammatory profile. The findings suggest a link between genetic background, immune refractory states, and the clinical spectrum of MIS-C, with implications for long-term monitoring.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was primarily an observational and diagnostic study of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) pathogenesis, involving in vitro cellular stimulation as an experimental challenge. Patients received standard MIS-C treatment (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin), but this was determined not to be the cause of observed immune hyporesponsiveness.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: For in vitro experiments, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from MIS-C patients were stimulated ex vivo with Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists, specifically lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at 50 ng/mL. LPS stimulation was performed for 4 hours for gene expression analysis and for 24 hours for multiplex cytokine analysis. No dose-response comparisons or clinical therapy doses for patients were specifically reported or compared. Endotoxin-free water served as a vehicle control for in vitro stimulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline (unstimulated) mRNA levels were higher in MIS-C patient cells relative to healthy controls, observed prior to treatment and in fully convalescent children (>30 days after hospital admission).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Negative regulator of TLR signaling, involved in dampening cytokine production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline (unstimulated) in MIS-C patients, independent of MIS-C treatment, compared to healthy and febrile non-MIS-C controls, persisting in convalescent children.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with dampened TLR responses and TLR hyporesponsiveness (endotoxin tolerance-like state). Distinguishes MIS-C from Kawasaki disease. Indicates lasting immune dysregulation in MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify novel diagnostic plasma biomarkers for sport-related concussion (SRC) by investigating proteomic changes in collegiate athletes. It found 338 differentially abundant plasma proteins after SRC, with a combination of erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 (EPB41) and alpha-synuclein (SNCA) demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy, especially when measured more than 6 hours post-injury. The study also noted acute increases in cardiac-related proteins (troponin T, troponin I, and FABP3) post-SRC, suggesting physiological stress.

The study focused on biomarker discovery for diagnosis rather than a therapeutic intervention, thus no specific dose comparisons for a therapeutic agent were reported, nor was a 'dose' of concussion administered or compared.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association of common germline genetic variants, particularly those exhibiting differential allelic expression (DAE), with breast and ovarian cancer risk in a large cohort of 15,252 BRCA1 and 8,211 BRCA2 mutation carriers. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated imaging and cognitive biomarkers of early brain injury in good clinical grade aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) patients, and explored their ability to predict long-term cognitive impairment. It quantified global and regional brain volume, white matter volume, CSF volume, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values at acute (<72h), subacute (5-10 days), and chronic (3 months) phases post-SAH. Key findings include significantly higher global and regional brain volume and restricted water diffusion (lower ADC) acutely, persistent abnormalities in posterior cerebellar volume at 3 months correlating with worse cognitive outcomes, and the ability of acute cerebellar gray matter changes to predict cognitive impairment at 3 months with 84% accuracy. The study also explored genetic associations with cerebellar gray matter volume, linking several genetic variants to cardiovascular disease and other health indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of early brain injury and cognitive impairment following aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH) using MRI and cognitive assessments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 27 good-grade SAH patients (WFNS 1 and 2) underwent MRI scanning and comprehensive cognitive assessment at three time-points: within the first 72 hours (acute phase), at 5-10 days (subacute phase), and at 3 months (chronic phase) post-SAH. An additional 27 paired healthy controls were recruited for comparison. No specific therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were investigated, as this was an observational study of SAH's natural course and sequelae.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated genomic variants associated with thiazide-like diuretic (chlorthalidone and hydrochlorothiazide)-induced glucose changes in hypertensive patients, specifically focusing on genetic predictors in Black and White participants from PEAR and PEAR-2 studies. It identified and replicated the intronic single-nucleotide polymorphism (rs9943291) in the HMGCS2 gene as strongly associated with increased glucose levels following both chlorthalidone and hydrochlorothiazide treatment. The analysis noted a more potent effect of chlorthalidone on glucose increase, particularly in white participants, indicating a genetic predisposition to thiazide-induced hyperglycemia.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chlorthalidone and Hydrochlorothiazide (thiazide/thiazide-like diuretics)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Hypertensive patients received either sequential monotherapy with chlorthalidone for 8 weeks (PEAR-2 study) or randomized monotherapy with hydrochlorothiazide (PEAR study), both at protocol-specified doses. Chlorthalidone demonstrated a more potent effect on adverse glucose response and induced higher mean glucose changes compared to hydrochlorothiazide, with adverse metabolic events observed within 9 weeks. The difference in glucose change between the two diuretics was statistically significant in white participants (P=0.0002) but not in black participants. No specific mg/dose details were provided, and no dose-response comparisons for the drugs themselves were reported, as the study focused on genetic variants influencing treatment response.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chlorthalidone treatment in Black individuals
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with increased blood glucose levels, potentially indicating higher risk of chlorthalidone-induced hyperglycemia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the functional implications of heterogeneity in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), focusing on an endodermally biased pluripotent substate. Using a GATA6-GFP reporter line and single-cell functional/transcriptomic analyses, the research identified distinct, interconvertible hESC substates defined by differential expression of GATA6 and SSEA3. GATA6-positive hESCs, while retaining long-term self-renewal and pluripotency (often alongside OCT4 and SOX2 co-expression), exhibited a higher propensity and bias towards spontaneous endoderm and mesoderm differentiation, with downregulation of ectodermal genes. SOX17 was identified as a potential driver for this endoderm-biased substate.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Human Embryonic Stem Cell (hESC) Substate Characterization and Differentiation Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study utilized the Shef4 hESC line, which was genetically modified with a GATA6-GFP reporter via Zinc Finger Nuclease-mediated homologous recombination. Cells were cultured in KO/SR on MEF feeders or E8 medium. hESC substates, defined by differential GATA6 and SSEA3 expression (e.g., 3+/6-, 3+/6L, 3+/6H, 3-/6+), were isolated by Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS). These sorted cells were subjected to single-cell cloning, gene expression analysis (qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing), high-content clonogenic assays, and differentiation protocols, including a spin-embryoid body (EB) system, without external therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for differentiation-inducing factors. The focus was on intrinsic marker expression and resultant lineage bias.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the molecular determinants of hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs) and hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) by generating a GATA2w/eGFP reporter in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The reporter accurately marks endogenous GATA2 expression, which is critical for endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT). A key finding is the identification of ITGB3 (CD61) as a reliable novel positive surface marker that precisely labels functional HECs with superior hemogenic potential, both in hESC/hPSC differentiation in vitro and in embryonic day 10 mouse embryos in vivo. The research provides a robust platform for dissecting hematopoiesis and facilitates the generation of functional hematopoietic stem cells in vitro.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Gene targeting using TALENs, in vitro human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation, and in vivo mouse embryo analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GATA2w/eGFP reporter was generated in H1 hESCs via gene editing (TALENs, electroporation of 1 μg linearized vector and 2.5 μg of each TALEN plasmid into 1 × 10^6 H1 cells, puromycin selection at 0.5 μg/mL, and Cre recombinase (400 ng per 1 × 10^6 cells) for cassette removal). In vitro differentiation involved hPSC blood differentiation protocols using co-culturing with OP9 stromal cells or AGM-S3 co-culture. Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) treatment was applied for 5 days. Cell seeding used Y-27632 (10 μM). CFU assay medium contained 100 ng/mL recombinant murine stem cell factor, 10 ng/mL recombinant murine interleukin-3, 10 ng/mL recombinant human interleukin-6, and 3 U/mL human erythropoietin, with endothelial cell assays using 100 ng/mL vascular endothelial growth factor. In vivo analysis included mouse embryos at E10.0, E11, E12, E14, with fractionation of endothelial cells based on CD61 expression (CD61 high, CD61 low, and CD61 − subpopulations). No specific dose-response comparisons for differentiation conditions or therapeutic interventions were reported beyond qualitative observations of effect.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Downregulated in the eGFP+ cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Vital endothelium gene.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Transcriptome analysis of GATA2/eGFP+ HECs during hESC blood differentiation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its downregulation in HECs (GATA2/eGFP+ cells) suggests a transition away from a pure endothelial identity towards a hemogenic one.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study evaluated and compared the regenerative potential of different blood-derived products (EDTA-PRP, Citrate-PRP, and hyperacute serum [hypACT]) in a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model over 21 days. Key assessments included metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression (SOX9, COL2AB, COL1A1, MMP3, P21), and extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and quality, using 1% or 5% concentrations of the products. HypACT consistently demonstrated superior and more stable results for cartilage-related gene expression and tissue quality. In contrast, Citrate-PRP showed negative effects on ECM production, chondrocyte presence, and gene expression, which was partly attributed to anticoagulants and extensive platelet accumulation. Metabolic activity generally showed no significant differences among the blood products compared to controls, though some variations were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-derived products: hyperacute serum (hypACT), leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with EDTA (EPRP), and leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with trisodium citrate (CPRP).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood products (hypACT, EPRP, CPRP) were prepared from whole blood (18mL for hypACT, 16mL for EPRP, 16mL for CPRP) and used as 1% or 5% (v/v) supplementation in 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet cultures for 21 days; 10% concentration was deemed unsuitable. HypACT showed stable effects across both 1% and 5% concentrations. For EPRP, 1% was favored over 5% due to better glycosaminoglycan deposition and lower platelet accumulation, with concentration influencing specific gene expressions (SOX9, MMP3, COL2AB, COL1A1). CPRP at both 1% and 5% concentrations resulted in poor tissue quality and no increase in COL2AB production, with extensive platelet accumulation observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A chondrogenic-related gene and transcription factor crucial for chondrocyte differentiation and cartilage formation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher expression indicates enhanced chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage matrix production; lower (non-significant) suggests less effective chondrogenesis or impaired cartilage regeneration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study introduces MiSL (Mining Synthetic Lethals), a novel computational algorithm that identifies mutation-specific synthetic lethal (SL) partners and predictive genetic biomarkers by mining pan-cancer human primary tumor data. MiSL was applied to 12 different cancers, predicting numerous SL partners and demonstrating its utility in precision oncology. Key validations include the identification of ACACA as a novel druggable SL partner for the IDH1 mutation in AML and glioma, and PIK3CA mutation as a predictive biomarker for AKT1 inhibitors in breast cancer. The algorithm also integrates functional screens like shRNA data to rank gene essentiality and detect genomic alterations and differentially expressed genes, aiding in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of acute and long-term (16 weeks) heavy resistance exercise, with and without angiotensin II type I receptor blocker (losartan) supplementation, on serum C-terminal agrin fragment (CAF) levels in healthy older men. The findings indicate that 16 weeks of exercise alone did not affect CAF, but losartan supplementation led to an increase in CAF levels. Conversely, a single bout of heavy resistance exercise acutely lowered serum CAF. The study emphasizes drug interaction and the timing of blood sampling relative to exercise as crucial factors influencing CAF turnover and interpretation in neuromuscular research.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute exercise (1EX) consisted of a single bout of unilateral heavy resistance exercise targeting the quadriceps muscles (5 sets of 12 concentric repetitions at 70% 1RM followed by 4 sets of 6 eccentric repetitions at 110% 1RM). Losartan (100 mg daily) or placebo was administered from Day -10 to Day 7 for 1EX. Long-term exercise (48EX) involved 48 sessions over 16 weeks (3 sessions/week) of progressive heavy resistance exercise, with loads gradually increasing from 67% to 86% of 1RM, 3 to 5 sets, and 15 to 6 repetitions. Losartan for 48EX was 50 mg/day for the first week, then 100 mg/day for the remaining 15 weeks. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either exercise or medication regarding biomarker outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased cfRNA burden observed from Schwann cells in MIS-C.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Schwann cells are involved in peripheral nervous system myelination and support. Increased burden indicates PNS cell death.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MIS-C disease state.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that peripheral nervous system damage may be a common feature of MIS-C.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study clinically validated C12FDG as a flow cytometry-based biomarker for detecting senescent peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T cells in humans. It investigated the association of C12FDG+ cells with chronological age, sex, and various serum senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) biomarkers. Findings revealed that C12FDG++ PBMCs and T cells increase with age, are elevated in males and patients with mild to moderate osteoarthritis, and decrease following fisetin treatment. The C12FDG platform shows promise as a quantifiable clinical tool for assessing healthy aging, age-related orthopedic decline, and the efficacy of senolytic therapies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Senolytic therapy using the flavonoid fisetin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fisetin was administered at 100 mg/day to a small subgroup of 10 participants, with longitudinal analysis performed. While dose consistency was self-reported, specific duration details or comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not systematically reported in this study, though future controlled trials are acknowledged as necessary to determine the optimum senolytic dosing regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with increasing age (r=0.3002; p=0.0030) and with increasing C12FDG++ signal (r=0.2066; p=0.0457). This correlation with age was lost in females. Levels were significantly decreased after fisetin usage.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glycoprotein secreted by osteoblasts, associated with the inhibition of bone formation; it is a biomarker related to aging and the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Chronological aging (20–82 years), C12FDG++ PBMC (senescence), and senolytic drug fisetin usage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with osteoporosis; its reduction by senolytics (fisetin) indicates a potential to improve bone health in humans and serves as a biomarker of aging and senescence.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the clinical relevance and efficacy of collagen X breakdown product (CXM) as a blood-based biomarker for endochondral long bone fracture repair in both healthy individuals and patients with tibia or femur fractures. It characterized CXM expression patterns, stability across demographics (age, sex), correlation with other bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, osteocalcin, leptin, sclerostin), and its utility in predicting healing prognosis (early, normal, delayed). The findings showed CXM levels are low in healthy individuals, peak around 25-35 days post-fracture, can be reliably measured via dried blood spots, and offer an earlier, quantitative indication of healing compared to traditional radiographic methods, supporting its prospective use in fracture studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of natural long bone fracture repair, with a secondary analysis of a Vitamin D3 supplementation trial (VitaShock).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on observing biomarker changes in patients with acute closed or low-grade open tibial or femoral shaft fractures (Gustilo type I or II, AO/OTA type 42), without applying a specific therapeutic dose as an intervention. For the secondary analysis of the VitaShock trial, multiple Vitamin D3 dosing strategies were assessed, but specific dose details were not provided, and no significant difference in CXM response was found compared to placebo. Longitudinal blood samples were collected at various standard-of-care clinical visits over a period up to 48 weeks post-fracture.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: variable correlation (positive in early healers, negative in delayed healers), increases with age
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Correlation with CXM transitioned from positive in early healers to negative in delayed healers. Showed a significant correlation between increasing levels with increasing age (r = 0.46, p = 0.0007). An overall significant relationship with CXM was not consistently observed across all analyses.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulator of bone formation/resorption (implied).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Early and delayed fracture healing; associated with aging; general fracture healing assessment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Dynamic role in fracture healing prognosis, with its correlation to CXM varying based on healing trajectory. Also serves as an age-related bone marker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study compared inflammatory cytokines, adipokines, and bone markers at rest and in response to plyometric exercise in obese versus normal-weight adolescent females. Key findings indicate that obese adolescents did not show evidence of resting inflammation or differences in bone resorption, but exhibited blunted bone formation (lower osteocalcin) and a differential sclerostin response to exercise compared to normal-weight controls. Acute exercise generally induced an anti-inflammatory and anabolic bone response in both groups, though insulin and sclerostin responses differed with adiposity, suggesting a unique systemic regulation dependent on adiposity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bout of high-impact plyometric exercise, totaling 120 jumps across 5 circuits (3 sets of 8 repetitions per station with 3 min recovery), lasting 30 minutes. The protocol included box, lunge, tuck jumps, single leg hopping, and jumping jacks. Box jump height was adjusted for body mass (40 cm for normal weight, 25 cm for obese) to ensure safety and sufficient loading. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher post-exercise in obese; unchanged or slightly lower in normal weight; unchanged at rest
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar between groups at rest. In obese females, there was a significant increase 5 minutes post-exercise (+26% to +29%, p = 0.04) that returned to baseline by 1 hour. In normal weight females, there was no significant change (or a non-significant decrease of -13%, p = 0.08) immediately post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Osteocyte-secreted factor that inhibits bone formation by inhibiting Wnt signaling, promotes adipogenesis, and plays a role in bone-adipose tissue crosstalk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest and acutely (5 minutes, 1 hour) post-plyometric exercise in obese vs normal weight adolescent females.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The differential exercise-induced response (increase in obese, no change in normal weight) suggests an adiposity-dependent systemic regulation. An increase in sclerostin post-exercise in obese females could potentially blunt bone formation and indicate an unfavorable metabolic response, potentially promoting advanced skeletal maturation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute response of serum sclerostin and bone turnover biomarkers (B-ALP, CTX) to a single session of whole-body vibration (WBV) exercise, both with and without blood flow restriction (BFR), in healthy untrained adult males. The findings indicated that adding BFR to WBV did not significantly affect serum sclerostin or CTX levels up to 24 hours post-exercise. However, a differential response was observed for bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (B-ALP), which was significantly lower 24 hours post-exercise in the combined WBV and BFR group compared to WBV alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Whole-body Vibration (WBV) exercise with and without Blood Flow Restriction (BFR)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two experimental conditions: (i) WBV alone, consisting of ten 1-minute bouts of whole-body vibration (30 Hz frequency, 2 mm peak-to-peak displacement, 3.6 g peak acceleration) with 30-second recovery between bouts. Participants stood barefoot in an isometric semi-squat position (130° knee angle). (ii) WBV with lower-body Blood Flow Restriction (BFR). For the WBV+BFR condition, a 13-cm-wide pneumatic cuff was applied to each thigh and inflated to 110 mmHg (estimated ~60% blood flow restriction) for the entire 1-minute duration of each vibration bout, with full deflation during the 30-second recovery intervals. No dose-response comparisons for varying WBV parameters or BFR pressure were reported within the study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant time × condition interaction (p>0.05). Specifically, no statistically significant main effect of condition (p=0.14; ηp2=0.22), time (p=0.43; ηp2=0.08), and no significant condition × time interaction (p=0.68; ηp2=0.05) for serum sclerostin up to 24 hours post-exercise.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Osteocyte-derived secreted glycoprotein that regulates bone formation by inhibiting osteoblast activity and promoting osteocyte apoptosis; involved in mechanosensitivity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute bout of whole-body vibration (WBV) exercise with and without blood flow restriction (BFR).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates no acute change in bone formation inhibition or bone mechanosensitivity in response to the tested whole-body vibration exercise protocols with or without blood flow restriction, suggesting no additional short-term benefit for optimizing bone health via this mechanism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This 2-year prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in bone remodeling and turnover markers in children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from diagnosis through chemotherapy. It revealed that ALL onset significantly slows bone remodeling, with significantly lower bone turnover markers at diagnosis compared to controls. During chemotherapy, particularly the induction phase, these markers increased, suggesting a recovery of bone turnover, and a potential balance in active bone remodeling by the end of therapy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Risk-adapted multiagent antileukemic chemotherapy, specifically for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), including Glucocorticoid (GC) therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The 2-year prospective longitudinal study involved chemotherapy according to international AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 and ESPhALL 2017 protocols, with patients stratified by risk (standard, intermediate, high). The treatment included induction, reinduction/delayed intensification (two phases of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy), and a maintenance phase. Blood sampling was conducted at 5 time points (T0-T4) from diagnosis until treatment cessation. No specific numerical drug dosages were reported, but it was noted that different glucocorticoid doses did not significantly alter bone marker profiles after intensive therapy phases.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower at diagnosis compared to controls
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls (p = 0.023).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Secreted by osteocytes, it inhibits the Wnt/β-catenin pro-osteoblastogenic pathway and Wnt signaling, thereby inhibiting bone formation and regulating osteoblastogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ALL children at diagnosis compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels in ALL children at diagnosis suggest altered bone formation signaling and dysregulation of bone formation pathways, potentially contributing to suppressed bone turnover observed in a context of overall slowed bone remodeling.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to evaluate bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome (NS) to understand their bone status and explore genotype-phenotype correlations. It revealed increased bone resorption in NS patients, evidenced by significantly elevated serum C-telopeptides of type I collagen (CTX) levels, and a non-significant increase in RANKL. The study also discussed the influence of RAS/MAPK signaling pathway alterations and SHP2 protein on osteoclastic activity and the effects of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment on bone parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Case-Control Study evaluating bone turnover and remodeling markers in children with Noonan Syndrome, including an analysis of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment effects.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This cross-sectional, case-control study compared 28 children with Noonan Syndrome to 35 healthy controls. No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was administered to the main cohorts. Within the NS cohort, some subjects had received or were receiving rhGH therapy, but no specific dosages, duration, or dose-response comparisons for rhGH treatment were reported, and no significant differences in bone parameters were found between treated and untreated subjects in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences were found between NS patients and controls (Assay range 0–240 pmol/L).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inhibits bone formation by blocking the pro-osteoblastogenic activity of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children with Noonan Syndrome (NS).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not a significant indicator of altered bone status in this cohort, suggesting its inhibitory effect on osteoblasts is not altered.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma (component of CognitionArtery model) and Vascular Tissue

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased in the plasma of people with vascular calcification. Negative regulator of WNT signalling that drives calcification.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Negative regulator of WNT signalling, drives calcification, primarily expressed in vascular smooth muscle cells, pericytes, and fibroblasts.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Aging, vascular calcification, early phases of cognitive decline (as a component of CognitionArtery model).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of vascular calcification and extracellular matrix alterations, major components of aging underlying early cognitive decline.
