document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the functional deficiency of endogenous interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients, a subtype of new-onset refractory status epilepticus. It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anakinra (recombinant IL1RA)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Gene Transcript Expression Level (real-time polymerase chain reaction)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No reduced expression of secreted IL1RA isoforms in the index patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inhibits IL1R signaling extracellularly.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) in the index patient.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of change in secreted isoforms, in contrast to reduced intracellular isoforms, helps characterize the specific nature of IL1RA deficiency in FIRES pathogenesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. Proteomic analysis revealed UA upregulated mitochondrial pathways and downregulating inflammatory pathways in skeletal muscle. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Urolithin A (UA) supplementation combined with altitude training and structured exercise challenges.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Competitive male distance runners received 1000 mg/day of Urolithin A or placebo for 4 weeks, concurrent with an intensified altitude training camp (~1700–2200 m). The regimen included weekly downhill running bouts and 3000 m time trials. No dose-response comparisons for UA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Unusually high log2 fold change of 7.1 in UA group when normalized relative to placebo, considered significantly regulated (nominal p-value < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Protein, part of general proteomic changes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 4-week UA supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Part of proteomic changes observed with UA supplementation, though noted as an outlier.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher during acute stress but lower with prolonged stressful stimuli or increased physical training demands, showing a decline or reduction of ≥65%. Reductions are associated with escalated training intensity/volume and congested schedules, and a trend of lower concentrations is seen in players with higher URTI instances.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Antimicrobial protein secreted by mucosal cells under sympathetic nervous system control, acting as a barrier against viral infections and an immunological marker tied to infection risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute stress, prolonged stressful stimuli, increased physical training demands, escalated training intensity/loads, intensive training periods (e.g., 4-week), high training load, increased training intensity/volume, and congested schedules in athletes (e.g., soccer players).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Pivotal biomarker for evaluating overtraining, psychological stress, and upper respiratory tract health status, used for monitoring chronic fatigue. Lower levels indicate increased vulnerability and risk for upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and symptoms (URTSs), instrumental in identifying excessive training workloads and suggesting necessary workload adjustments to mitigate URTI risks.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a 9-week randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial investigating the ergogenic effects of a 6-week daily probiotic supplementation on high-intensity endurance running performance in healthy non-elite athletes (N=32). Primary objectives include assessing the impact on time-to-exhaustion, while secondary objectives involve evaluating perceived exertion, blood chemistry (glucose, lactate), immune and stress biomarkers (cortisol, alpha-amylase, sIgA), cold and flu symptoms, gastrointestinal health (symptoms, stool characteristics, microbiota composition), and body composition. The study hypothesizes increased running time-to-exhaustion and reduced gastrointestinal/cold/flu symptoms with probiotic intervention.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Probiotic supplementation (intervention) with standardized exercise testing protocols
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week intervention period involves daily oral supplementation of 5 billion colony-forming units (CFU)/day of a specific probiotic capsule taken with a meal. The study is preceded by a 2-week pre-baseline and followed by a 1-week washout period. Participants are considered compliant if they take at least 80% of the supplement. Exercise testing includes a modified Bruce V̇O2 max treadmill test and a time-to-exhaustion treadmill endurance test conducted at 85% of V̇O2 max heart rate. No dose-response comparisons are reported in this study protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Changes in immune activity are being investigated (in current study protocol); historically, 'maintained' concentrations were observed in elite athletes.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes from baseline will be collected and analyzed (in current study protocol); historically, 'maintained concentrations' were reported from a 14-week Lactobacillus intervention (20 billion CFU) in elite athletes.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key component of mucosal immunity, providing frontline defense against pathogens.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 6-week probiotic intervention and post-intervention treadmill endurance testing in non-elite runners (current study protocol); 14-week Lactobacillus intervention in elite athletes (historical reference).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Biomarker of immune activity; historically, maintained levels suggested preserved mucosal immunity, reducing risk of upper respiratory infections. Expected to indicate immune health status, potentially influenced by probiotic supplementation and physical activity in the current study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Secretion rate is not affected by exercise. Levels are elevated due to acute infections, including COVID-19. Diurnal patterns have been described.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary antibody in mucosal immunity, defending against pathogens.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise, acute infections (e.g., upper respiratory tract infections, COVID-19), and diurnal variations.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of mucosal immune status; requires noting recent infections and standardizing sampling times for accurate interpretation, though its secretion rate is stable with exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed an integrative multi-platform meta-analysis of gene expression profiles from Affymetrix and Illumina datasets in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients and healthy controls to identify novel, robust diagnostic biomarkers. The analysis revealed 5 commonly differentially expressed genes and 28 novel 'gained' genes, suggesting their significant potential for early PDAC diagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Integrative meta-analysis of gene expression data for biomarker identification and diagnostic prediction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gene expression data from two independent cohorts of PDAC patients (Affymetrix: 18 PDAC patients; Illumina: 36 PDAC patients) and 18 healthy controls were integrated. Profiling was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) using Affymetrix GeneChip® Human Gene ST 1.0 Arrays and Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 Expression BeadChip microarray platforms. Data were integrated using an empirical Bayesian methodology (ComBat) for batch effect removal, and differential expression was analyzed with limma software, identifying genes with p<0.01 and at least 1.5-fold differential expression. The analysis identified 5 commonly differentially expressed genes (with individual ROC curve AUC > 0.9) and 28 novel 'gained' genes, which could discriminate PDAC patients from controls with an average sensitivity of 74.8% and specificity of 73.3% for individual gained genes, 100% sensitivity and 94% specificity for combined common genes, and 91% sensitivity and 87% specificity for combined gained genes. No dose-response comparisons were applicable as it is a diagnostic biomarker identification study.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patient samples (gene expression data).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Upregulation; identified as a novel gained gene, differentially expressed and capable of discriminating between PDAC patients and healthy controls (individual ROC curves showed average sensitivity 74.8% and specificity 73.3%).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly stated.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: PDAC patients, development of different gastrointestinal tumors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Related to the development of different gastrointestinal tumors.

document_context_data.document_summary: This case study from The THRIVE Study investigates the biobehavioral impacts of repeat sexual violence victimization and recovery in a single acute survivor over 6 months. It details the longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health biomarkers, revealing dysregulated hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity and a correlation between suppressed cervicovaginal immune biomarkers and increased adverse mental health. The findings underscore the value of monitoring cervicovaginal immune functioning and HPA axis dysregulation in coordination with mental health changes following repeated sexual trauma, with implications for HIV susceptibility.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study investigating the biobehavioral impacts of sexual violence victimization and revictimization, integrated with support protocols for the participant.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review systematically examines the therapeutic potential of gamma ("\u03b3") neuromodulation as a non-pharmacological strategy across a range of neurological and psychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, epilepsy, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, schizophrenia, and depression. It investigates various neuromodulation techniques (such as rTMS, tACS, tDCS, neurofeedback, DBS, VNS, optogenetic stimulation, and rhythmic sensory stimulation) to regulate neuronal oscillations, particularly \u03b3 oscillations and cross-frequency coupling. The document highlights the role of \u03b3 neuromodulation in improving cognitive, emotional, and motor functions by addressing oscillatory imbalances, reducing pathology (e.g., amyloid-\"\u03b2" accumulation), improving seizure control, and sharpening executive functions, while also discussing the physiological mechanisms, intervention outcomes, and the need for further research into specific treatment strategies and precision medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Various neuromodulation techniques are investigated, including gamma (\u03b3) neuromodulation, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and olfactory bulb-driven closed-loop neuromodulation), Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS - including responsive DBS and high-frequency DBS of the habenula, fornix, posterior cingulate cortex, subthalamic nucleus, and anterior nucleus of the thalamus), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), optogenetic neuromodulation, Rhythmic Sensory Stimulation (RSS), multisensory \u03b3 stimulation, \u03b3 Knife Surgery, \u03b3 Entrainment Using Sensory Stimulation (GENUS), and high-frequency modulation.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review synthesizes existing literature and, as such, generally lacks specific dose-response data from new interventions. However, various dose details are mentioned for different neuromodulation techniques. Optogenetic stimulation increased cortical \u03b3 band oscillations (GBO) by entraining at approximately 40 Hz, with inhibition reducing GBO power. Multisensory \u03b3 stimulation was applied at 40 Hz, and 40 Hz \u03b3 entrainment via sensory stimulation (light flicker or sound) reduced amyloid plaques and tau pathology. rTMS is described as enhancing high-frequency oscillations (\u03b3, \u03b2) and reducing low-frequency rhythms (\u03b1, \u03b8, \u03b4), with low-frequency rTMS for epilepsy showing uncertain effectiveness. tACS synchronizes neuronal oscillations, directly entraining \u03b3 oscillations through phase-locked sinusoidal currents, sometimes targeting frontal areas. tDCS delivers low-level electrical currents to adjust cortical excitability. Neurofeedback (including EEG-neurofeedback and multisensory stimulation with operant conditioning) allowed for self-modulation of \u03b3-band synchronization, achieving up to 71% accuracy in enhancing neural synchronization in preclinical AD and older adults, with success rates for \u03b3 modulation varying (approximately 75%). DBS was applied to the fornix for AD, the posterior cingulate cortex for PD, the subthalamic nucleus (STN) for \u03b3 activity modulation, the subgenual cingulate or ventral striatum, and bilaterally to the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) for epilepsy, which reduced seizures by 40.5% at 3 months and 75.0% at 5 years. VNS aimed at desynchronizing epileptiform activity in the \u03b3 band. \u03b3 neuromodulation involved a rapid transition from an over-activated Cross-frequency coupling (CFC) pattern to an inhibited-activated state during stimulation, which remained significantly weakened post-stimulation. High-frequency modulation and high-frequency DBS of the habenula were also mentioned. The document notes a significant gap in research addressing specific, detailed treatment strategies with \u03b3 neuromodulations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced by 40.5% at 3 months and by 75.0% at 5 years

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. document_context_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of a structured exercise program in adult women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. The primary aim is to mitigate anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) by assessing changes in circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain, LVEF). Secondary objectives include evaluating other cardiac health parameters (blood pressure, HR, HRV, recovery HR), physical function, self-reported physical activity, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. The protocol also details the planned methodology for assessing these outcomes and administrative aspects of the study.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Structured Exercise Program (Aerobic and Resistance Training)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention group will perform a supervised exercise program three times per week, during anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT). Each 70-minute session includes a 5-minute warm-up, 60 minutes of training, and a 5-minute cooldown. Aerobic training, progressively increasing from 20 to 30 minutes at light to moderate-to-high intensity (50-80% HR reserve), combines treadmill, stationary bike, and stepping. Resistance training involves 2-3 sets of 10-12 maximal repetitions (12-RM) for upper and lower body, with progressive intensity. The program starts 1-2 days after the first chemotherapy session and continues throughout treatment. The control group receives standard breast cancer care without specific physical activity advice. No dose-response comparisons are reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the predictive power of Neuroimmune Guidance Cue (NGC) gene expression profiles from peripheral blood monocytes for classifying cardiovascular disease (CVD) patients versus healthy individuals. Utilizing various machine learning methods, including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and Stochastic Gradient Boosting, the research aimed to identify key biomarkers for CVD prediction. The findings indicated that expression levels of SEMA6B, SEMA6D, and EPHA2 in circulating monocytes were predictive of CVD outcomes, with machine learning models demonstrating high accuracy and sensitivity in discriminating between healthy individuals and CVD patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Predictive modeling for cardiovascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction using machine learning on biomarker expression profiles.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved profiling transcriptomes of purified CD14+ monocytes from 368 subjects in the CIRCULATING CELLS study cohort, utilizing 60 mL EDTA blood samples with stringent RNA quality control (RIN > 9) and Illumina BeadStation for hybridization. Various machine-learning methods (including Linear Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayesian, Stochastic Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, Partial Least Square, Bagged CART, and Random Forest) were applied to gene expression data to classify CVD patients and healthy individuals. Model performances were compared, with linear discriminant analysis, Naïve Bayesian, and stochastic gradient boost models yielding perfect or near-perfect sensibility and specificity, and some models achieving up to 100% accuracy in classification. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on predictive modeling and biomarker analysis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved clinically relevant outcomes, indicating potential for disease prevention/treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document introduces and details a novel, cost-effective, non-fluorescent immunohistochemistry (IHC) method for assessing autophagy flux in fixed tissues. Utilizing MAP1LC3/LC3B and SQSTM1/p62 as core markers, the method employs diaminobenzidine (DAB) staining and bright-field microscopy. It provides a comprehensive protocol for the detection, visualization, scoring, and interpretation of these biomarkers, aiming to bridge the gap between experimental research and clinical diagnostics by offering a reliable and accessible alternative to traditional fluorescence-based techniques for understanding cellular homeostasis and disease mechanisms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Non-fluorescent Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for autophagy flux assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This methodology describes a detailed non-fluorescent immunohistochemistry protocol for assessing autophagy flux using diaminobenzidine (DAB) staining in fixed tissue samples, including commercial tissue microarray slides. The protocol involves specific steps for tissue processing, antigen retrieval (e.g., heat-induced in citrate buffer for 30 min at boiling point), blocking, primary antibody incubation (e.g., SQSTM1/p62 and MAP1LC3B/LC3B at 1:50 dilution overnight at 4°C), secondary antibody and ABC solution application, DAB substrate reaction (up to 2 min), and counterstaining. Quantification involves a scoring system based on puncta numbers (graded 0-3) and the percentage of stained cells (categorized into ranges) using bright-field microscopy, typically at 40x objective. Optimization tips include using fresh reagents, optimizing antibodies and concentrations through titration, proper tissue fixation (10% formalin for 24h), appropriate antigen retrieval (heat-induced or enzymatic with citrate or EDTA buffer), controlling background staining with hydrogen peroxide (0.3%) and normal serum/BSA, and monitoring DAB development time. This is a methodological paper, and thus no therapeutic dose-response comparisons are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Fixed tissue sections (e.g., commercial tissue microarrays, neural cell bodies)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Protein Level (puncta staining via DAB IHC)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Typically lower due to degradation, or accumulation, indicating different autophagy statuses
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Puncta numbers are graded 0-3 (no to high puncta), and percentage of stained cells is categorized (0-25%, 26-50%, 51-75%, 76-100%). Its degradation and decrease in puncta number indicate active flux. Accumulation with LC3B suggests a block in flux, while a decrease with increased LC3B indicates high autophagy activity. No specific quantitative change data from an intervention is reported as this is a methodological study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key marker in the autophagy pathway, binding to LC3B and degraded within lysosomes, thus indicating active autophagy flux and lysosomal turnover, crucial for cellular degradation and recycling.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Autophagy flux assessment in fixed tissue sections, relevant for cellular homeostasis, disease mechanisms (e.g., cancer, neurodegeneration), and responses to various treatments or stressors via DAB-based IHC.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the degradation efficiency and lysosomal turnover during autophagy, critical for cellular waste removal, cell health, and disease pathology. Combined with LC3B, it provides insights into autophagy flux, including potential blocks or high activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive study investigated alpha-synuclein (αSN) as a potential diagnostic and monitoring biomarker for Inclusion Body Myositis (IBM). It evaluated αSN immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies and its concentration in serum and muscle homogenates, comparing IBM patients to other myopathies and healthy controls. The findings suggest αSN immunoreactivity in muscle is a promising diagnostic marker, while serum αSN levels could serve as a monitoring biomarker, correlating with disease duration and clinical severity in IBM. The study also explored the diagnostic utility of other established and emerging biomarkers in IBM.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational/Diagnostic Biomarker Investigation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved a multimodal assessment of alpha-synuclein (αSN) levels and immunoreactivity in muscle biopsies, muscle tissue homogenates, and serum samples from various cohorts. Muscle biopsies (N=63, including 19 IBM, 21 other inflammatory myopathies, 20 other myopathies, 3 healthy controls) were analyzed by immunohistochemical staining. Serum samples (N=156, including 11 IBM, 25 other inflammatory myopathies, 53 hereditary myopathies, 30 mitochondriopathies, 37 healthy controls) were assessed by ELISA. Muscle homogenates were also examined (N=17 IBM, N=19 other inflammatory myopathies, N=5 hereditary myopathies, N=2 healthy controls). IBM patients were stratified by disease severity (IBMFRS) and disease duration for serum αSN analysis. No interventional dose or therapeutic comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic and monitoring biomarker evaluation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Accumulation identified; considered the most accurate degenerative marker among histological features. More common in biopsies that also show other histological features of advanced disease (e.g., rimmed vacuoles). Previous studies report highly variable sensitivity (12.5%–91%) and specificity (18%–100%) for IBM diagnosis. The pathology observed in IBM is specifically noted as not present in PM-Mito.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Muscle degeneration and diagnostic utility in Inclusion body myositis (IBM), particularly in advanced stages and for differentiation from PM-Mito.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Accurate degenerative marker for IBM, but its value may be limited in early disease stages. document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Metabolic syndrome, dyslipidemia in diabetic mice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Deficiency is associated with metabolic syndrome and dyslipidemia; supplementation can mitigate dyslipidemia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in patients with severe COVID-19 and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), focusing on clinical outcomes, lung functional status, hematological parameters, cytokine levels, and miRNA expression profiles. The findings demonstrated that UC-MSC therapy was safe, improved lung lesions over a one-year follow-up by reducing fibrosis and markers of lung damage (CT score, Surfactant D, sRAGE), hastened lymphocyte recovery, and modulated inflammation (decreased ESR, CRP, banded neutrophils). document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of 4 weeks of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on running performance, recovery, and mitochondrial biomarkers in highly trained male distance runners during an altitude training camp. Findings showed that UA supplementation significantly lowered post-exercise muscle damage (Creatine Kinase tAUC after a 3000 m time trial) and ratings of perceived exertion, while also showing a large within-group increase in VO2max. However, UA did not significantly improve 3000 m running performance directly. The study also assessed physiological adaptations including running economy, body composition, and hemoglobin mass.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

Athlete 2 showed immediate decrease after match 2, then increase during short recovery 2. Both experienced significant declines during the long recovery phase, dropping to 78% for Athlete 1 and 109% for Athlete 2 (relative to initial concentration for Athlete 1 and final concentration for Athlete 2).

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated proteomic and histological changes in human intervertebral disc (IVD) tissue and matched plasma samples to identify biomarkers for disc degeneration progression. It compared mild and severe degenerate IVD tissues from individuals undergoing lumbar discectomy, employing mass spectrometry, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. The main finding was the identification of AEBP1 as a significant tissue marker for monitoring degeneration severity, with increased levels in severe IVD. While other matrisomal proteins (TNC, MGP, COL12A1, COL6A2, COL6A3, TGFBI) and complement system proteins (C4A, C3, CFB, CFH) were also elevated in severe IVD, and some plasma proteins (A2M, F13B, MMP2, IGF1) showed changes, plasma biomarkers exhibited a weak correlation with tissue degeneration.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery and characterization for intervertebral disc degeneration

IVD tissues were categorized into mild (Grades 4-7) and severe (Grades 10-12) degeneration based on the Sive et al. histological grading system (n=35 samples, 18 mild, 17 severe). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the focus was on characterizing disease states and identifying associated biomarkers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. The aim was to evaluate systemic and muscle-related stress responses and recovery patterns, comparing biomarkers at 1 day (R+1) and 15 days (R+15) post-landing with pre-flight values and age-matched controls. Findings revealed a strong spaceflight-induced stress response in muscle tissue, leading to a proinflammatory state, with inflamma-miRs and myo-miR-206 mediating systemic recovery, and significant inter-individual differences in biomarker responses were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: 6-month International Space Station (ISS) spaceflight exposure with in-flight countermeasure training, followed by a post-flight recovery period.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two crewmembers were exposed to approximately 6 months of spaceflight. Samples were collected pre-flight (76-79 days before) and post-flight at 1 day (R+1 / 24 hours) and 15 days (R+15) after landing. Individual molecular responses varied significantly between the two crewmembers, with crewmember A generally showing more persistent changes. Specifics of in-flight countermeasure training dose were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons for spaceflight duration were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A serine protease inhibitor and acute phase protein, involved in anti-inflammatory response and acting as a stress and antioxidant protein. It is a validated target of miR-126-3p.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post 6-month spaceflight (R+1 and R+15) observed in muscle biopsy during recovery, associated with muscle tissue changes and increased inflamma-miR levels in astronaut A.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a strong stress response and tissue-related anti-inflammatory response in muscle tissue following spaceflight, linked to inflammatory regulation via miR-126-3p, and shows differences in stress and antioxidant proteins post-spaceflight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated serum phosphate (S-phosphate) and magnesium (S-magnesium) levels in Ethiopian children aged 6-59 months recovering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM), including those with edema or severe wasting, when treated with therapeutic diets (F-75, F-100, or diluted F-100). The study assessed baseline biomarker levels, their correlation with serum albumin, and their response to different stabilization diets. Key findings include a high prevalence of hypophosphatemia at admission, which often remained subnormal at discharge and could hinder recovery. S-magnesium levels were often high at admission and typically increased to above normal by discharge, suggesting it may not be a limiting nutrient in F-100. Stabilization with diluted F-100 did not lead to lower S-phosphate or S-magnesium levels compared to F-75, and in fact, resulted in higher adjusted mean levels of both at the start of treatment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Therapeutic feeding and nutritional intervention for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Children aged 6-59 months with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) received therapeutic feeding and medical management over an average of 16 days, following Ethiopian guidelines across stabilization, transition, and rehabilitation phases. Standard therapeutic diets included F-75 (100 kcal/kg/day, 560 mg/L phosphorus, 85 mg/L magnesium) for stabilization and F-100 (130-200 kcal/kg/day, 579 mg/L phosphorus, 154 mg/L magnesium) for transition and rehabilitation. Due to a national F-75 shortage, 25 (35%) children were stabilized with diluted F-100 (75 kcal/100 mL), which provided 57 mg/kg/day of phosphorus compared to 73 mg/kg/day from pre-mixed F-75. The median duration for stabilization was 6 days, transition 2 days, and rehabilitation 6 days. The study compared the effects of stabilization with F-75 versus diluted F-100 on serum phosphate and magnesium levels, finding that diluted F-100 did not cause lower levels and in some instances resulted in higher initial levels of these biomarkers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with both S-phosphate (0.02, 95% CI: 0.01; 0.03 mmol/L, P < 0.001) and S-magnesium (0.02, 95% CI: 0.01; 0.02 mmol/L, P < 0.001) at admission. No specific numerical quantification provided for albumin levels themselves.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Maintains oncotic pressure, transports hormones and fatty acids, and acts as a buffer. General indicator of nutritional status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) at admission.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with initial S-phosphate and S-magnesium levels, serving as a general marker of nutritional health status and severity of malnutrition in SAM.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated systemic and synovial Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) levels in early, treatment-naïve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients, both at baseline and after 6 months of conventional-synthetic Disease-Modifying-Anti-Rheumatic-Drugs (cs-DMARDs) treatment. It found that circulating PTX3 is a reliable marker of RA activity and predicts structural damage, remaining high post-treatment regardless of clinical response. Synovial PTX3 gene and protein expression correlated with local inflammation, disease activity, immune cell infiltration, ectopic lymphoid structures, and specific synovial pathotypes. While synovial PTX3 protein levels significantly decreased after cs-DMARD treatment, reflecting reduced local inflammation, this change was independent of clinical response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Conventional-synthetic Disease-Modifying-Anti-Rheumatic-Drugs (cs-DMARDs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients received cs-DMARDs for 6 months; 94.1% received cs-DMARDs and 47.9% received adjunctive corticosteroid treatment. Treatment effects on PTX3 levels were assessed at 6 months and were independent of clinical response status; no specific dosages or dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with PTX3 expression, indicating a link between acute-phase reactants and local inflammation in the synovium.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of acute phase response and systemic inflammation, especially relevant for evaluating chronic disease states or prolonged/severe inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically reduced by 72.3% at day 7 in the CD133+ cell-treated group compared to cisplatin-injured group. In the CD133- treated group, values were lower but not statistically significant. Cell treatments failed to restore levels back to baseline by day 14.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Metabolite used as an indicator of renal function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Amelioration of cisplatin-induced renal injury by CD133+ or CD133- cell therapy in nude rats.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower sCr levels indicate improved renal function, though considered less accurate than FITC-sinistrin t 1/2.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationships between serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (sUCHL1), tau (sTau), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP) levels with disease activity and disability in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and the effects of inebilizumab on these biomarkers. It found that all four biomarkers increase during NMOSD attacks, reflecting CNS damage. Specifically, sNfL was the strongest predictor of post-attack disability worsening, while sGFAP was superior in predicting future attacks. Treatment with inebilizumab attenuated biomarker elevations during attacks and reduced sNfL and sGFAP levels over time.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Inebilizumab (anti-CD19, B-cell-depleting monoclonal antibody)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were randomized to receive intravenous inebilizumab 300 mg or placebo (saline) on days 1 and 15 of a 28-week randomized controlled period (RCP), followed by an open-label follow-up period of at least 2 years. No specific dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes were reported, but inebilizumab treatment was associated with attenuated biomarker elevation during attacks and reduced biomarker levels over time compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly during NMOSD attacks and during the days before an attack, with mean concentrations increasing above an elevated level (>170 pg/mL). Levels returned to baseline after >7 days post-attack. Predicted upcoming attacks. Elevated at baseline versus healthy donors and RRMS patients (30% of AQP4+ participants had >170 pg/mL). Elevated baseline sGFAP in AQP4+ participants correlated with a Hazard Ratio of 2.56 for an adjudicated NMOSD attack. Treatment with inebilizumab was associated with lower levels than placebo, showing significantly lower levels in the absence of attack and smaller elevations during attacks.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An abundant cytoskeletal intermediate filament in astrocytes, released into CSF and serum following astroglial injury; a primary astrocytopathy marker, reflecting glial damage, CNS tissue injury, and inflammatory damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: NMOSD attacks (acute and preceding), inebilizumab treatment, prediction of upcoming attacks, baseline in NMOSD (AQP4+, MOG+, double-negative) and RRMS patients, post-attack recovery, evaluation of CNS damage in NMOSD patients, and subclinical disease activity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Superior predictor of upcoming NMOSD attacks and attack severity compared to sNfL, sTau, and sUCHL1. Associated with NMOSD attack severity, inflammatory damage, and disability worsening, including EDSS scores. May indicate subclinical disease activity. Lower levels with inebilizumab treatment indicate reduced astrocytic damage and attenuated attack-related elevation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Throughout exercise and recovery periods, with FOPS supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of differential impact on overall hormone regulation suggests that FOPS primarily influences metabolic substrates directly rather than acutely altering major hormonal signaling, implying alternative mechanisms for metabolic modulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated serum phosphate (S-phosphate) and magnesium (S-magnesium) levels in Ethiopian children aged 6-59 months recovering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM), including those with edema or severe wasting, when treated with therapeutic diets (F-75, F-100, or diluted F-100). Key findings include a high prevalence of hypophosphatemia at admission, which often remained subnormal at discharge and could hinder recovery. S-magnesium levels were often high at admission and typically increased to above normal by discharge, suggesting it may not be a limiting nutrient in F-100. Stabilization with diluted F-100 did not lead to lower S-phosphate or S-magnesium levels compared to F-75, and in fact, resulted in higher adjusted mean levels of both at the start of treatment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated blood-derived DNA methylation-based prediction models, including epigenetic scores (epi-LIBRA, epi-CAIDE) and a Multivariate Methylation Risk Score (MMRS), to assess and predict cognitive impairment and dementia (including AD and MCI) in various independent cohorts. The MMRS showed notable predictive capacity for MCI and prospective cognitive decline in AD and Parkinson's disease, and enhanced prediction when combined with traditional biomarkers, though individual epi-CAIDE and epi-LIBRA models performed poorly for AD and MCI status prediction. The study also detailed data preprocessing for various dementia risk factors, CSF biomarkers (amyloid- , tau, p-tau), whole blood DNA methylation profiling, and polygenic scores, aiming to investigate cognitive status and dementia.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during preparation), lower (males during recovery), unchanged (females during recovery)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Differed between sexes at baseline in COMP (p < 0.001). Increased in both female (p < 0.05) and male (p < 0.001) COMP from PRE to MID, with male COMP differing significantly from CTRL (p < 0.001). From MID to POST, SHBG levels decreased in male COMP (p < 0.05), while male CTRL increased (p < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in female groups from MID to POST.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels, particularly when combined with lower testosterone, indicate reduced availability of free (bioavailable) testosterone, exacerbating catabolic effects and impacting androgen-dependent functions. document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increases in response to exercise training. Increased SHBG and decreased testosterone may indicate insufficient recovery. Low SHBG may merely represent an individual's chronic diet.

Low SHBG, potentially linked to high-fat and high-protein diets, may be a sign of suboptimal capacity to adapt to training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals.
