matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, suggesting a stable anabolic state under the study conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Demonstrated significant changes over time and from baseline, peaking (elevated or depressed) 60-min post-run. Specific group differences or quantification of change between groups were not provided.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone involved in muscle repair and growth; a primary sex hormone involved in muscle growth, bone density, and reproductive health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Half-marathon race and 48-h recovery; potential supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of anabolic/catabolic balance and physiological stress from exercise; indicator of anabolic status, recovery, and overall reproductive and metabolic health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant changes observed for Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) protocols, with peak values observed 0 h post-exercise (p < 0.05). A component of the Testosterone/Cortisol ratio, which was positively correlated with miR-133a.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone involved in muscle growth and repair, and contributes to the anabolic-catabolic balance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Resistance Training, specifically Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) protocols.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for monitoring training responses and neuromuscular adaptations, indicating anabolic response to exercise, and used to understand acute program variables and recovery phases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased levels are accompanied by decreased performance, energy, or strength, often in context of dysregulation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone promoting protein synthesis, red blood cell production, and glycogen replenishment, while reducing protein breakdown; involved in endocrine regulation and long-term dysregulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Long-term dysregulation, overtraining, and endocrine regulation of muscle repair/adaptations during a training season.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Integrates with other markers to assess health and overtraining status; decreased levels suggest excessive training volume and insufficient recovery, potentially benefiting from reduced training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a single 6g dose of citrulline malate (CM) supplementation on muscle recovery after a high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session in untrained young adult men, examining functional, metabolic, anabolic, and physiological markers. The findings concluded that CM supplementation does not improve the muscle recovery process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Citrulline Malate (CM) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single oral dose of 6 g of citrulline malate (CM) was administered 60 minutes pre-workout, dissolved in 200 mL water. Participants then performed a single session of high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) consisting of 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions at 90% of 10RM for leg press and hack squat exercises, with 2 min rest between sets and exercises, performed with a 1s concentric:2s eccentric cadence. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and no significant treatment × time interaction was found for any measured variables, indicating CM did not improve recovery compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific significant changes or treatment × time interactions were reported for individual testosterone levels with CM supplementation versus placebo; only the Testosterone:Cortisol ratio was analyzed for significance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A primary anabolic steroid hormone essential for muscle growth, tissue repair, and overall anabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blood samples collected pre- and post-exercise, and immediately after muscular fatigue tests (24, 48, and 72 h after RE session) during CM or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Anabolic hormone level, influencing muscle protein synthesis, recovery, and adaptation to resistance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively associated with VO2 max values (+41.224) and RSA values (+19.14) in predictive regression models (p < 0.001 for overall models). Used as a predictor in significant regression equations for fitness parameters (R2 adjusted up to 0.930).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone, involved in muscle growth, recovery, energy metabolism, and supports healthy muscle development; modified by physical stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer playing/training, pre-seasonal training, analyzed for its predictive ability on fitness parameters (VO2 max, RSA).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels predict better aerobic capacity and repeated sprint ability. Indicates anabolic metabolism and acute/prolonged physical stress response. Useful tool in early detection of overtraining, especially when considered in ratio with cortisol; used to predict fitness parameters.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot clinical cohort study investigated physiological and immunological changes in male ultramarathon runners in response to a 160 km ultramarathon, collecting saliva and blood samples at baseline, immediately post-race, and after an 8-11 day recovery period. The study assessed the utility of saliva for non-invasive monitoring and found significant alterations in various hormones, cytokines, and blood cell counts in both saliva and blood, indicating pronounced physiological stress and immune response to extreme endurance exercise. Specifically, statistically significant changes were observed in several blood parameters and salivary cortisol, with longitudinal changes in testosterone (p=0.02) and alpha-amylase (p=0.03) showing significant differences between blood and saliva.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Ultramarathon Running (Strenuous Exercise)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 160 km ultramarathon event ('Berliner Mauerweglauf'), completed within 30 hours by male runners. Parameters were measured at three time points: baseline (T1), immediately post-race (T2), and after an 8-11 day recovery period (T3); no dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased at T2 (p = 0.26, non-significant in absolute values); however, the T2/T1 ratio for saliva (1.1) showed a significant difference compared to blood (0.3) (p = 0.02). Ratios to the baseline differed significantly when comparing changes between saliva and blood.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone involved in muscle growth, repair, overall physiological function, energy balance, and reproductive function; an important part of the HPA axis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running) and immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of physiological and endocrine response to intense exercise, with notable differences between blood and salivary measurements. May indicate an acute catabolic state or hormonal imbalance following extreme endurance exercise. Indicates physiological stress and recovery, potentially related to anabolic-catabolic balance and adaptation to exercise load.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased from T1 to T2 (pT1–T2 < 0.01). The T2/T1 ratio for blood (0.3) was significantly different compared to saliva (1.1) (p = 0.02). Blood testosterone significantly decreased post-ultramarathon. Ratios to the baseline differed significantly when comparing changes between saliva and blood.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone crucial for muscle repair, growth, and maintaining anabolic balance; involved in overall physiological function and energy balance; an important part of the HPA axis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Intense physical stress (ultramarathon running), immediately post-160 km ultramarathon (T2), and ultraendurance events.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitored as an indicator of physiological and endocrine response to intense exercise, with notable differences between blood and salivary measurements. Indicates a pronounced catabolic state and potential impairment of recovery or muscle repair processes following extreme endurance exercise. Offers potential for innovative monitoring of exercise and recovery. Indicates physiological stress and recovery, potentially related to anabolic-catabolic balance and adaptation to exercise load.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative literature review investigates biosensor approaches for continuous, real-time in vivo monitoring of molecular markers relevant to performance and health status. It highlights the limitations of current technologies and proposes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors as a generalizable, minimally invasive solution. The review details the development, validation, and attributes (generalizability, selectivity, reversibility, stability) of EAB sensors for detecting diverse targets (drugs, metabolites, hormones, proteins) in complex biological fluids and tissues. It also addresses the technological hurdles for subcutaneous placement, the correlation between interstitial fluid and systemic concentrations, and their potential for monitoring stress indicators (e.g., cortisol) and HPA/HPG axis hormones to assess overtraining syndromes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) Sensor Technology for Real-time In Vivo Molecular Monitoring
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This narrative literature review discusses the development and application of Electrochemical Aptamer-Based (EAB) sensors for continuous, real-time in vivo molecular monitoring, without an applied 'dose' in the traditional sense as it is a review of technology. EAB sensors, including 75-µm-diameter, 3-mm-long versions, have been tested in live rats for plasma monitoring (jugular vein) for up to 12 hours with few-second to sub-second resolution and clinically relevant precision. They are also adapted for minimally invasive subcutaneous placements (microneedles, indwelling needles) for interstitial fluid monitoring (e.g., brain, tumor, dermal ISF). The review highlights the importance of seconds-resolved time resolution and nanomolar limits of detection for hormones (achieved for LH and NGAL, micromolar for others). Time delays between subcutaneous ISF and plasma concentrations (e.g., 5-12 min for glucose, ~17 min for vancomycin) and correlations (strong for cortisol, <6% error for glucose) are noted, influenced by target properties. No dose-response comparisons for sensor parameters or monitoring duration were explicitly reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Declines over the course of the day
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Declines 20 to 25% in young males, but only ~10% in older males over the course of the day. Plasma half-life is less than 20 min.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Exerts system-wide effects including red blood cell production, glycogen replenishment, bone metabolism, and muscle protein synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: HPG axis function (in males), age (young vs. older males), training and exercise recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Monitoring muscle status can help tailor training and inform exercise and recovery intervals; dysregulation contributes to overtraining syndromes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Effects are contradictory: some studies reported fluctuations related to SP, while a 41-study meta-analysis reported no significant effect of SP or soy extracts on total or free testosterone. Other findings include lowered serum testosterone after 2 weeks of SP, no alteration after 12 weeks of SP-based blend, but a significant increase after 4 weeks of soy peptides and 4 months of soy peptides. The testosterone/estradiol ratio increased across all groups with SP and whey.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary male sex hormone, involved in muscle growth, bone density, and well-being; influences anabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein or soy peptide supplementation (2 weeks to 4 months) in various active individuals and athletes, sometimes with resistance training; general soy protein, soy foods, or isoflavone extracts supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Inconsistent effects mean no clear indication of consistent benefit or detriment for muscle adaptation or overall health, though some contexts showed increases with soy peptides or an improved androgenic balance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease in both groups following 14 days of bed rest intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A primary sex hormone involved in muscle growth, bone density, and overall metabolic function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 14 days of bed rest intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of hormonal balance, muscle mass maintenance, and overall anabolic status; decreased levels can impact physical performance and health during bed rest.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Altered, with significant alterations observed in response to training and competition loads. Acute increases typically follow intense exercise, with significantly different baseline levels and larger magnitudes of change in males compared to females. Specific direction of alterations caused by chronic training load remains unclear.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anabolic hormone, crucial for anabolic/catabolic balance, reflecting metabolic strain, physiological adaptation, and recovery responses to training load.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Physiological loads from intensive training, competition loads (TL and CL), and training load-induced stress across competitive seasons in professional male team athletes. Used for chronic fatigue monitoring.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects measurable physiological strain and anabolic/catabolic balance. Provides useful information for athlete monitoring to detect dysfunctional physiological responses, acting as an indicator of fatigue. Helps optimize performance, mitigate injury and overtraining risks, and indicates physiological adaptation. Interpretation, especially with cortisol ratio, necessitates sex-specific reference ranges.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower levels reported in individuals with incident cognitive impairment and AD. However, collection using cotton rolls resulted in falsely elevated levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Sex steroid playing a role in brain function and involved in reproductive and anabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease pathophysiology and cognitive impairment; sensitive to saliva collection methods (cotton rolls).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Alterations linked to cognitive decline and AD-related pathology, suggesting a potential diagnostic marker, but measurements are highly sensitive to collection methods.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of 8 weeks of daily 5g Cistanche deserticola (CD) extract supplementation, combined with progressive high-intensity resistance training, on muscle strength and recovery in both untrained and resistance-trained male participants. The study found that CD supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength (1RM bench press and squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF in untrained), and facilitated post-exercise recovery by modulating hormonal responses (increased testosterone, reduced cortisol) and decreasing markers of stress and inflammation (reduced CRP and CK levels) in both cohorts. Mechanistic insights suggest CD's role in improving energy metabolism, reducing muscle degradation, enhancing antioxidant defense, modulating neurotransmission, and regulating endocrine axes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation combined with a progressive resistance training program.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 5 g of CD extract daily, administered in two sachets (after breakfast and lunch) for 8 consecutive weeks, alongside a placebo group. A standardized resistance training program was completed three times per week for eight weeks. This program involved 4 sets of 10-12 repetitions at 65-70% of 1RM for weeks 1-4, and 4 sets of 6-8 repetitions at 80% of 1RM for weeks 5-8. Maximal strength (1RM bench press/squat, MVIC) and endurance (RTF bench press) were assessed. No dose-response comparisons for CD were reported, only comparison to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in untrained CD group (773.77 	 130.01 ng/dL vs. PLAC 636.49 	 98.85 ng/dL; p < 0.01) and in trained CD group (846.15 	 141.26 ng/dL vs. PLAC 732.16 	 117.27 ng/dL; p < 0.05). Overall, statistically significant improvements, also enhanced synthesis.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary male sex hormone and anabolic steroid, promoting muscle growth, strength, bone density, and recovery processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cistanche deserticola (CD) supplementation (5g daily for 8 weeks) combined with progressive resistance training; modulation of the Hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG) axis by CD components.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced anabolic capacity, improved muscle repair and recovery, contributing to increased muscle strength and overall athletic performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Significant increases after the PS phase (p = 0.001, 
D72 = 0.76). Increased after the PS phase, contrasting with previous studies that reported a reduction.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A primary anabolic hormone involved in muscle growth, bone density, and overall energy; indicates anabolic status; used in the evaluation of anabolic and catabolic balance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training phase; after intense physical exertion and intensification of training demands.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anabolic status and a hormonal response to exercise, potentially linked to muscle repair and adaptation; crucial for establishing anabolic/catabolic balance during PS for soccer performance; informs optimal management of stimulus/recovery.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly differed between male and female COMP at baseline (p < 0.001). Decreased significantly in male COMP from PRE to MID (p < 0.01) and compared to CTRL (p < 0.05), with a significant difference in change between sexes (p < 0.05). No significant changes were observed in female COMP groups. Levels in male COMP increased from MID to POST, recovering back to baseline (p < 0.001), also significant compared to CTRL (p < 0.05). Female CTRL showed a decrease from MID to POST (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A key anabolic steroid hormone involved in muscle protein synthesis, growth, bone density, red blood cell production, and male reproductive health. In females, it contributes to bone health, mood, and libido, and is regulated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (dieting, energy restriction, intense training) in physique athletes and subsequent recovery phase.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels in males suggest a catabolic state, physiological stress, or HPG axis disruptions, potentially impairing muscle anabolism, recovery, and overall male health. Its recovery indicates a return of anabolic hormonal balance. Stability in females suggests different hormonal responses. Overall, it plays a critical role in maintaining muscle mass and optimizing performance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Stable in combined HC users; significantly decreased from pre to post in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females, with some recovery in both groups but remaining lower than pre in naturally menstruating females at recovery
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In combined HC users, total testosterone concentrations showed no significant change over time. In progestin-only HC users, concentrations decreased significantly from pre to post (p=0.005) and then increased significantly from post to recovery (p=0.011). In naturally menstruating females, concentrations decreased significantly from pre to post (p<0.001) and increased significantly from post to recovery (p<0.001), but remained significantly lower than pre at recovery (p=0.043). At post, concentrations were lower in progestin-only HC users (p=0.004) and naturally menstruating females (p<0.001) compared to combined HC users. A significant group*time interaction was observed (F=3.819, p=0.015).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Sex steroid hormone (androgen), influenced by the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis and energy availability, involved in muscle growth, bone density, libido, and energy metabolism in females, and serves as a precursor for estradiol biosynthesis
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by diet and physical training in female physique athletes, with a comparative analysis across combined hormonal contraceptive users, progestin-only hormonal contraceptive users, and naturally menstruating females at pre, post, and recovery time points
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Maintenance in combined HC users suggests suppressed HPO axis function, potentially helping to maintain baseline concentrations despite LEA. A decrease in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females indicates LEA-induced HPO axis suppression, influencing muscle anabolic potential, bone health, and overall vitality. Lower testosterone is associated with LEA and training-related menstrual dysfunction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of acute preexercise calcium intake on bone turnover markers and calcium homeostasis in elite male rowers during a day with multiple strenuous, non-weight-bearing training sessions. The findings indicate that consuming a calcium-rich meal before training stabilizes ionized calcium levels, reduces the postexercise parathyroid hormone response, and attenuates the increase in bone resorption markers (e.g., β-CTX-I) over a sustained 7-hour period, thereby supporting long-term bone health and reducing the risk of bone stress injuries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary calcium supplementation (via whole foods/meals) in conjunction with repeated, strenuous, non-weight-bearing rowing exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Elite male rowers (n=16) participated in two trials, one week apart, each involving two 90-min rowing ergometer sessions (EX1, EX2) separated by 150 minutes. Before each trial, participants consumed either a high calcium meal (~1000 mg, CAL) or an isocaloric low calcium meal (<10 mg, CON). Each exercise session consisted of three 30-minute sets at 90-100% of individual 2 mmol·L−1 capillary blood lactate power (mean 255-260W). Calcium was provided acutely before training sessions. No dose-response comparisons were reported beyond the high versus low intake, nor for exercise intensity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes or specific effects reported related to the intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Assessment in elite male rowers undergoing high or low calcium dietary interventions and intense rowing exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No specific performance or health indicator was reported related to the calcium intervention, suggesting no acute impact on testosterone levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the time-course changes of circulating microRNA (c-miRNA) profiles and conventional biomarkers (anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory cytokines, muscle damage markers) in healthy young men following three distinct acute resistance training (RT) protocols: muscular strength endurance, muscular hypertrophy, and maximum strength. The findings revealed protocol-dependent dynamic responses in several c-miRNAs (miR-208b, miR-532, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-206, miR-181a, miR-21, miR-221) and traditional biomarkers (e.g., Testosterone, Cortisol, IGF-1, CK, Lactate, IL-10), with specific c-miRNAs correlating with hormonal and inflammatory markers. These results suggest the utility of c-miRNAs as novel biomarkers for monitoring RT-induced adaptations and physiological stress, while some markers like IL-6, hs-CRP, miR-1, miR-146a, and miR-378 showed no significant changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Resistance Training (RT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Three distinct acute resistance training protocols were administered to healthy young men: Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) (3 sets of 16–20 repetitions at 40% of 1RM with 1-minute rest), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) (3 sets of 12 repetitions at 70% of 1RM with 2-minute rest), and Maximum Strength (MS) (4 sets of 6 repetitions at 90% of 1RM with 3-minute rest). Each protocol included five exercises (bench press, squat, pulldown, overhead press, standing dumbbell curl), and the total workload was kept as similar as possible across groups. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, 1 hour, and 24 hours post-exercise. The protocols differed in acute program variables, with relative intensity identified as a key factor influencing c-miRNA responses; however, direct dose-response comparisons among protocols were not made as participants differed for each protocol.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: dynamic changes (peaking for SE/MH, declining for MS), positively correlated with miR-133a
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked for Muscular Strength Endurance (SE) and Muscular Hypertrophy (MH) protocols, whereas declining to minimum for Maximum Strength (MS) protocol after 24 h recovery (p < 0.05). Showed a positive correlation with miR-133a (R = 0.59, p = 0.02) for the MS protocol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the balance between anabolic and catabolic states, indicating anabolic/catabolic balance and muscle adaptation potential.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute Resistance Training, specifically Muscular Strength Endurance (SE), Muscular Hypertrophy (MH), and Maximum Strength (MS) protocols.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Conventional biomarker for monitoring training responses and neuromuscular adaptations, potentially related to recovery status or overtraining risk, and indicative of stressful training (overreaching) when correlated with miR-133a.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the physiological and psychological impacts of intense competition preparation, involving rigorous energy restriction and physical training, on male and female physique athletes. Across a 46-week period including a 21-23 week preparation phase and a recovery phase, the study assessed hormonal changes (e.g., IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, SHBG, insulin, cortisol, FSH, ACTH, estradiol), energy dynamics (energy intake, energy availability), body composition (body mass, fat mass, muscle size, lean mass, fat-free mass), muscle strength (isometric and concentric force, fatigue profiles), bone health (Z-scores), mood states (POMS), and reproductive function. Key findings revealed significant reductions in anabolic hormones (IGF-1, IGFBP-3, testosterone, free testosterone), increased catabolic markers (SHBG, cortisol), and decreased energy availability and muscle strength in both sexes, with males often showing more pronounced hormonal and psychological stress responses (e.g., increased fatigue and tension, decreased T/C ratio). While bone mineral density remained stable, many adverse changes largely reversed during the post-competition recovery phase with increased energy availability. The study suggests IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 as potential biomarkers for monitoring physiological stress and provides insights for optimizing training and nutritional strategies to minimize adverse effects.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Competition preparation in physique athletes, involving intense energy restriction, physical training, and self-managed diet and exercise regimens.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved a longitudinal assessment over 46 weeks, including an average 21-23 week competition preparation phase (PRE to MID) characterized by intense energy restriction and physical training, followed by a 3-5 month recovery phase (MID to POST) with increased energy availability. Participants self-managed their diet and exercise, with resistance training quantified as total weekly sets and aerobic training as total minutes per week, and average training load by metabolic equivalents (METs). Measurements were taken at PRE, MID (one week before competition), and POST (23 weeks after competition). While strategies like adequate energy availability and individualized nutrition were discussed, no specific intervention doses were administered by researchers, and no explicit dose-response comparisons for training or diet components were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in male COMP from PRE to MID (p < 0.001), with a -50.4 	17.8% decrease, which was more pronounced (p < 0.01) compared to female COMP (6.8 	53.5%) and significant compared to male CTRL (p < 0.001). No significant changes were observed in female groups. From MID to POST, the T/C ratio increased in male COMP (p < 0.01), indicating recovery, and this change was significant compared to CTRL (p < 0.001), with a significant difference between sexes (p < 0.001) in COMP.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the balance between anabolic (testosterone) and catabolic (cortisol) processes, often used as an indicator of training stress and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During competition preparation (prolonged training, energy restriction) in physique athletes and the subsequent recovery phase with increased energy availability.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A significant decrease indicates increased catabolic stress, potential overtraining, or inadequate recovery, potentially linked to greater psychological stress and fatigue. A more pronounced decrease in males highlights greater disruption of anabolic processes. An increase during recovery indicates a shift towards an anabolic state and recovery from physiological stress, serving as a valuable marker for optimizing training loads and recovery strategies.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the correlations between immune, haematological, and endocrinological markers and fitness parameters in 28 young male soccer players (age: 13.0 ± 0.2 years, BMI: 19.5 ± 2.2 kg/m2). It assessed if these physiological parameters could predict fitness values (including Countermovement Jump (CMJ), 10m sprint, VO2 max, Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA) total time, and RSA index) using multiple linear regression, both at baseline and following a pre-seasonal training period. The study demonstrated that these biomarkers can predict physical performance in various fitness tests.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sports Activity/Exercise and Baseline Physiological Evaluation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved 28 young male soccer players undergoing regular sports activity and a brief but intense pre-seasonal soccer training period. Data collection included comprehensive anthropometric and physical evaluations (CMJ, 10m sprint, VO2 max estimated via Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIRT1), RSA total time and index) and blood/salivary sample collection. Evaluations were performed at baseline over three days before the competitive season and once after the pre-seasonal training. No experimental dose-response comparisons were reported for either training intensity or therapeutic interventions, as the study focused on observational prediction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively associated with RSA index (-78.84) in a predictive regression model (p < 0.001 for the overall model).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the anabolic/catabolic balance; often used as an indicator of training stress and recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Youth soccer players' RSA index performance after strenuous pre-seasonal training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower ratios predict better RSA index. This ratio helps evaluate the player’s individual capacity to maintain physiological homeostasis; significant alterations indicate potential overtraining and increased injury risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to synthesize and analyze scientific evidence on biomarkers used for monitoring chronic fatigue and physiological responses to training and competition loads in professional male team sport athletes. It synthesizes evidence across 28 studies, covering muscle damage markers, anabolic/catabolic hormones, inflammatory markers, immunological markers, and oxidative stress markers. The review concluded that professional team sports induce significant alterations in these biomarkers, reflecting physiological strain, muscle damage, oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunosuppression, with effects generally larger and more prolonged after official matches than training. It emphasizes that a comprehensive analysis of these biomarkers provides a holistic understanding crucial for managing athlete fatigue, optimizing performance, and mitigating risks of overtraining, injury, or disease. The review also highlights the importance of establishing sex-specific reference ranges and monitoring strategies for biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physiological loads from intensive training and competition in professional male team sports.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The systematic review analyzed responses to varying physiological loads experienced by professional male team sport athletes during official matches and training sessions across competitive seasons (e.g., 4-week intensive training, 6-month seasons, 12-week periods, consecutive matches over 1-week). Biomarker data was collected from sports including basketball, soccer, handball, futsal, rugby, Australian football, volleyball, netball, and water-polo. Responses were generally larger and more prolonged after official matches compared to training, with recovery times ranging from 24 hours to several days post-exercise. The review also considered the impact of congested fixture schedules, high-intensity efforts, and sports with high eccentric loads, noting variability based on playing position, game time, and specific sporting discipline, but did not provide specific quantitative doses for training or matches.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Altered, with significant alterations observed in response to training and competition loads. Changes show moderate evidence. Described as a particularly sensitive and reliable index, though variability is contingent on the period and sporting discipline.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Balances anabolic and catabolic processes, reflecting metabolic strain, physiological stress, adaptation, and recovery responses to training load.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Physiological loads from intensive training, competition loads (TL and CL), and training load-induced stress across competitive seasons in professional male team sport athletes. Used for gauging training stress and fatigue levels, varying by playing position and game time.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects measurable physiological strain and serves as a particularly sensitive and reliable marker for gauging training stress and fatigue levels, more so than cortisol alone. It is vital for monitoring and managing athlete fatigue, helping optimize performance and mitigate risks of non-functional overtraining, injury, or disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A prolonged decrease. A 30% decrease in T:C has been suggested as an indicator of insufficient recovery, whereas a value of 0.35 × 10⁻³ has been considered to be the threshold of overtraining.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicates the anabolic-catabolic balance in the body, reflecting the balance between muscle building and breakdown processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Monitoring training stresses, especially in male athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Considered more sensitive to training stresses than either measure alone. A prolonged decrease is associated with detriments to performance through increased proteolysis and decreased protein synthesis. Serves as an indicator of insufficient recovery and a threshold for overtraining, linked to poor performance outcomes and suboptimal training adaptations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a single 6g dose of citrulline malate (CM) supplementation on muscle recovery after a high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session in untrained young adult men, examining functional, metabolic, anabolic, and physiological markers. The findings concluded that CM supplementation does not improve the muscle recovery process.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Citrulline Malate (CM) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single oral dose of 6 g of citrulline malate (CM) was administered 60 minutes pre-workout, dissolved in 200 mL water. Participants then performed a single session of high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) consisting of 3 sets of 8–12 repetitions at 90% of 10RM for leg press and hack squat exercises, with 2 min rest between sets and exercises, performed with a 1s concentric:2s eccentric cadence. No dose-response comparisons were reported, and no significant treatment × time interaction was found for any measured variables, indicating CM did not improve recovery compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Hormone Ratio (derived from individual hormone concentrations)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum testosterone: cortisol ratio did not differ between CM and placebo conditions during the recovery period at 24, 48, and 72 h post-exercise (treatment × time p = 0.970; time p = 0.947), indicating no significant treatment × time interaction.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the balance between anabolic (testosterone) and catabolic (cortisol) hormonal states, influencing muscle protein synthesis and breakdown, and serving as an indicator of physiological stress and recovery status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Blood samples collected pre- and post-exercise, and immediately after muscular fatigue tests (24, 48, and 72 h after RE session) during recovery from a single high-intensity resistance exercise (RE) session with CM or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Anabolic indicator commonly used to assess recovery status, potential for muscle adaptation, and risk of overtraining or chronic stress; absence of differences with CM supplementation suggests no effect on muscular regeneration markers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased across all groups (SPs and whey combined with resistance training); within-group analysis showed significant increases with soy supplementation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An indicator of androgenic balance, impacting muscle development and other androgen-dependent processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-athletic healthy men supplemented with different combinations of SPs and whey in conjunction with a resistance-training program.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: May indicate an improved androgenic balance, potentially beneficial for muscle development and anabolism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized discovery metabolomics and lipidomics to investigate plasma glycosphingolipids and other lipid metabolites as potential biomarkers for distinguishing aggressive from indolent prostate cancer (PCa) in treatment-naïve African-American and European-American men. The findings indicate that specific glycosphingolipid species, particularly trihexosylceramide and tetrahexosylceramide, along with other sphingolipids and triglycerides, are significantly associated with PCa aggressiveness. A five-sphingolipid signature demonstrated promising diagnostic accuracy comparable to or exceeding PSA, suggesting their utility as novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and highlighting their role in related metabolic networks and genetic alterations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery via metabolomics and lipidomics
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An observational study conducted on plasma samples from 159 men with treatment-naïve prostate cancer, utilizing ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). The study focused on identifying biomarkers for PCa aggressiveness (Grade Group 1 vs. Grade Groups 2-5, low vs. intermediate/high aggressive PCa), without administering or comparing any therapeutic interventions or doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most closely associated with high-aggressive PCa; levels proved different between Grade Group 1 and Grade Groups 2–5 in treatment-naïve patients, yielding AUC 0.815 (0.716–0.896, 95% CI).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A glycosphingolipid with structural roles in cellular membranes, critical roles in cancer signaling and biology, involved in glycosphingolipid synthesis and metabolic networks, with its biosynthesis involving B3GALNT1.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prostate Cancer (PCa) aggressiveness (high-aggressive, low vs. intermediate-high aggressiveness, Grade Group 1 vs. 2-5) in treatment-naïve patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential diagnostic biomarker for aggressive PCa, contributing to PCa aggressiveness assessment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Th17 cell expansion; promoting a pro-inflammatory Th17 cell profile; a positive correlation between IL-6 and Th17.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory immune response.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Severe acute COVID-19 illness.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Linked to decreased relative Treg frequency, promoted by IL-6 surge, contributes to immunopathology.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between thalamic volume and heart rate recovery following an orthostatic challenge in older adults from The Irish Longitudinal Study on Aging (TILDA). It consistently found that smaller thalamic volume is associated with slower heart rate recovery, suggesting that thalamic structural integrity is a potential risk marker for autonomic dysfunction, cardiovascular events, and sudden cardiac death, while also differentiating its contribution from other subcortical brain regions.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Orthostatic Challenge (Active Standing Test)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in this observational study underwent an active stand protocol where they lay supine for 10 minutes, then stood quickly and remained standing for 3 minutes. Beat-to-beat heart rate and blood pressure were monitored, with heart rate recovery (HRR) specifically measured between 10 and 30 seconds post-standing (HRR 10|30s). This study focused on correlating brain volume with physiological response, thus no therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Structural measurement (volume) via multimodal brain magnetic resonance imaging

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower (smaller volume) is associated with slower heart rate recovery and higher cardiovascular risk; Higher (larger volume) is associated with faster heart rate recovery.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Smaller thalamic volume was associated with slower heart rate recovery (-1.4 bpm per 1 cm^3 thalamic volume, 95% CI -2.01 to -0.82; p < .001 in bivariate analysis, and 0.82 bpm slower in multivariable modeling, CI 95 -1.49 to -0.13; p = .01). Participants with smaller thalamic volumes had a mean heart rate recovery -2.7 bpm slower than participants with larger thalamic volumes (95% CI -3.89 to -1.61; p < .001). Specifically, individuals in the first tertile (smaller thalamic volumes) had a mean HRR 10|30s decline of -5.75 bpm (CI 95 -6.56 to -4.94; p < .001), while those in the third tertile (larger thalamic volumes) showed a mean decline of -8.51 bpm (CI 95 -9.31 to -7.70; p < .001), indicating faster recovery with larger volume. Thalamic volume was also 0.56% lower per additional year of age, and 3% to 4% lower with diabetes and heavy alcohol consumption.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The thalamus is an integrative brain region involved in sensory and motor signal relay, consciousness, and is central to maintaining optimal autonomic control and the complex autonomic response to standing. It reflects the structural integrity of the central autonomic network, cortico-thalamic connectivity, neural density, and contributes to motor, cardiopulmonary, and allostatic interoceptive functions.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional analysis in older individuals (aged ">=50 years") undergoing an orthostatic challenge, and association with aging, diabetes, and heavy alcohol intake.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Thalamic volume serves as an indicator of the structural integrity of the central autonomic network and neural correlates of homeostatic flexibility and autonomic cardiovascular function. Smaller volume is associated with higher cardiovascular risk, autonomic dysfunction, and is a potential clinical biomarker for stratifying individuals at risk of cardiovascular events, sudden cardiac death, cognitive decline, and increased disease burden in conditions like epilepsy and multiple sclerosis.
