document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Regulate MMP activity, maintaining ECM homeostasis. Inflammatory mediators promote TIMP-1 expression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ARDS, COVID-19, COPD, and IPF.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated TIMP-1 levels are linked to fibrosis, whereas lower levels are associated with proteolysis and fluid leakage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not change with NASH disease activity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inhibitors of metalloproteinases.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease activity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not indicated as a biomarker for NASH disease activity due to lack of change.

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated the predictive impact of free and complexed forms of urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), along with other inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers, for COVID-19 severity and the development of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Japanese adults. It revealed that elevated free, non-complexed PAI-1 antigen, and low circulating uPA and uPA/PAI-1 complex levels were associated with increased COVID-19 severity and ARDS, particularly in the complicated phase. These fibrinolytic changes correlated with heightened inflammation (e.g., TNF
Gα, IL1
Gβ, IL6, CRP), endothelial dysfunction (suPAR, sVCAM1), and clinical outcomes like lymphopenia, suggesting a "fibrinolysis-sleeper/shutdown" state in severe COVID-19.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on COVID-19 Disease Progression
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a retrospective observational study involving 69 hospitalized Japanese adults with COVID-19 and 20 healthy donors, comparing biomarker levels across uncomplicated, complicated, and critical disease phases. No therapeutic intervention or dose comparisons were reported, focusing instead on naturally occurring changes during disease progression and noting ethnic differences in biomarker profiles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Higher in COVID-19 patients regardless of clinical phase compared to healthy individuals, but not associated with COVID-19 severity or ARDS development in this study. No correlation with plasmin/
Gα2AP complex (Spearman rs=0.0068).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A complex formed between tPA and PAI-1, involved in regulating fibrinolysis. Increases are linked to myocardial infarction.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease, specifically in relation to fibrinolysis regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not found to be a predictive biomarker for COVID-19 severity or ARDS development in this study. While higher in COVID-19 patients, its functional consequences are unclear, though it may suggest a low thrombosis risk for Japanese when considered with other markers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of different cycling exercise intensities (70% and 90% of ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and cadences (30-110 rpm) on cardiopulmonary, metabolic, and skeletal muscle oxygenation responses in healthy participants. While higher intensity and cadence led to increased cardiorespiratory and metabolic activity, skeletal muscle oxygenation (measured by tissue saturation index and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis was not substantially affected, suggesting it may not be a primary factor in self-selected cadence at moderate exercise intensity.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cycling Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed cycling exercise at two intensities (70% and 90% of the ventilatory threshold, Tvent) and five cadences (30, 50, 70, 90, and 110 rpm), with each bout lasting 4 minutes in a randomized sequence, interspersed with active recovery. While cardiopulmonary and metabolic responses increased with higher intensity (90% Tvent) and higher cadences (especially 110 rpm), skeletal muscle oxygenation (TSI and its oscillations) in the vastus lateralis showed no significant dose-response across the tested intensities or cadences.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Tissue oxygenation index (measured via near-infrared spectroscopy)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
TSI was not different between 70% and 90% Tvent exercise intensities and across cadences (30-110 rpm). No significant difference in changes from baseline, with mean 
				TSI values averaging ~4% and not varying with intensity or cadence. Not substantially affected during short-duration cycling at moderate intensity.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall index of skeletal muscle oxygenation, reflecting the balance between oxygen delivery and extraction, and between oxygen supply and demand.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cycling at moderate exercise intensities (70% and 90% Tvent) across various cadences (30-110 rpm) for short durations (4 min per cadence), with testing in randomized sequences and active recovery periods.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests that skeletal muscle oxygenation is not an important negative feedback signal in the choice of self-selected cadence during cycling at moderate exercise intensity under these conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated urinary proteins responsive to acute eccentric calf-raise exercise in healthy males, identifying an N-terminal fragment of titin. The urinary titin fragment significantly increased 96 hours post-exercise and correlated strongly with established blood biomarkers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion), proposing its potential as a non-invasive biomarker for exercise-induced muscle damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Eccentric Calf-Raise Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Acute, single-leg calf-raise exercise (right leg) involving repetitive eccentric muscle contractions. The protocol consisted of 10 sets of 40 repetitions (total 400 repetitions) with 3-minute rest between sets, performed at 60 counts/min. Ankle joint range of motion was maintained between 20° dorsiflexion and 15° plantar flexion, with an exercise load approximately half the subject's body weight. Samples were collected before and up to 96 hours post-exercise. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Excretion rates were 5.1  1 2.3 pg/min (Pre) and increased significantly to 77.6  1 23.0 pg/min 96 hours after eccentric exercise (p < 0.01). Other time points include 2.2  1 0.6 pg/min (2h), 4.2  1 1.5 pg/min (4h), 4.0  1 1.4 pg/min (24h), 12.9  1 8.6 pg/min (48h), and 56.9  1 22.0 pg/min (72h).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Structural sarcomere protein of striated muscle, essential for passive and active contractility and myofibril elasticity, linking the Z-line to the M-line. Released into circulation upon skeletal myofiber disruption.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute eccentric calf-raise exercise involving repetitive contractions, leading to exercise-induced muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential non-invasive biomarker of muscle damage, reflecting and correlating strongly with established serum markers of muscle damage (CK, Mb, LDH, ALD) and muscle symptoms (DOMS, reduced muscle strength, and range of motion).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Context of circulating cells/plasma (implied by association with circulating miR-134 and effects in peripheral blood cells), Cells (U937 or THP-1)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: associated with increased miR-134, lower (due to knockdown)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An increased miR-134 level is significantly associated with the activation of Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3). TLR3 ligand treatment in peripheral blood cells led to changes in IL-18BP mRNA levels. Reduced due to lentivirus-based RNA interference (knockdown efficiency validated by QRT-PCR); precise quantification not provided for knockdown.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates immune responses; its activation is linked to increased miR-134 expression; Toll-like receptor, recognizes viral double-stranded RNA, involved in innate immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Activation in the context of AOSD, TLR3 ligand treatment leading to specific molecular changes, lentivirus-based RNA interference (TLR3 knockdown), AOSD pathogenesis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates involvement in the pathogenic mechanisms of AOSD through its association with miR-134 and downstream effects on IL-18BP; demonstrates successful experimental manipulation (knockdown) of TLR3 gene expression for functional studies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the oxidative stress and genotoxicity in gas station refueling workers exposed to long-term, low levels of atmospheric BTEX in Nanning, China, comparing them to office workers. It found significantly higher BTEX levels in refueling areas, which, despite being generally below occupational limits, were associated with reduced antioxidant capacity (lower T-SOD and GSH) and increased oxidative stress (higher MDA and 8-OHdG) and DNA damage (higher micronucleus rate, tail moment, and Olive tail moment) in refueling workers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Long-term occupational exposure to BTEX (Benzene, Toluene, Ethylbenzene, Xylenes) compounds in gas station refueling workers, compared to office workers
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Long-term occupational exposure to low levels of atmospheric BTEX, with refueling workers exposed for an average of 8.7 years. BTEX concentrations in refueling areas were significantly higher than in office areas (p < 0.001), with mean ambient air concentrations including Benzene (60.03 vs 16.86 µg/m3), Toluene (317.76 vs 89.93 µg/m3), Ethylbenzene (113.85 vs 12.09 µg/m3), m-xylene (40.91 vs 28.44 µg/m3), p-xylene (57.51 vs 10.62 µg/m3), and o-xylene (37.18 vs 15.67 µg/m3). These levels were generally below current occupational exposure limits, but fixed environmental monitoring may underestimate actual exposure. No specific dose-response analysis for individual BTEX compounds was reported in human subjects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean concentration in refueling air: 317.76 µg/m3 versus 89.93 µg/m3 in office areas (significantly higher). Below the recommended occupational limit of 100 ppm (375 mg/m3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Environmental pollutant; solvent.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Occupational exposure in gasoline station refueling areas.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates occupational exposure level, associated with potential health risks for workers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document synthesizes the proceedings of the Tau2024 Global Conference, showcasing interdisciplinary advancements in tau-associated brain disorders. Key areas covered include the pathophysiology, molecular mechanisms, and brain microenvironments of tauopathies, as well as global perspectives highlighting genetic, socioeconomic, and linguistic diversity's impact on conditions like Frontotemporal Lobe Dementia and Primary Progressive Aphasia. The conference reviewed cellular mechanisms, advanced tau-PET, CSF, and blood-based biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease and other tauopathies, alongside discussions on therapeutic strategies such as antisense oligonucleotides, immunotherapy, senolytics, OGA inhibitors, and novel intrabody approaches aimed at reducing tau levels and aggregates.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The conference proceedings discussed a range of therapeutic advancements for tauopathies, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy, tau immunotherapy (e.g., bepranemab), anti-tau-PEST intrabody therapy, pharmacological inhibition of PERK, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) inhibition (e.g., FNP-223).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Specific dose details varied by therapy: BIIB080 (ASO) demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction of approximately 60% in CSF tau. Anti-tau-PEST intrabodies reduced eGFP-tau by 70-78% in cellular models and endogenous tau by 38-58% in organoids over 21 days. A PERK inhibitor and nanobody constructs were effective in animal models without specific dose reporting. Bepranemab, senolytics (dasatinib plus quercetin), and FNP-223 (OGA inhibitor) were evaluated in early-phase human trials with various administration routes (IV, oral) and were generally well-tolerated, but detailed dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported across all interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher incidence of tone errors observed

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of difficulties in grammatical comprehension, expression, and speech sound production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Non-fluent/agrammatic variant Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA) in individuals speaking tonal languages (Mandarin and Cantonese).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates specific linguistic impairment in PPA, affecting communication in tonal language speakers.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the molecular relevance of GBA1 pathogenic variants (N370S and L444P) in Gaucher disease (GD) patients (GD1, GD3) on Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT), GBA1 carriers, and healthy subjects by analyzing glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb1), α-synuclein mRNA, total protein, and oligomer levels. Key findings included significantly elevated Lyso-Gb1 levels in GD patients and neuronopathic GD, substantially higher α-synuclein mRNA levels in GD3 patients and L444P carriers, but no statistically significant differences in total α-SNCA protein or oligomer levels between groups after multiple comparison adjustment. The research also explored correlations with disease severity, GBA1 variants, aging, and ERT impact, suggesting links to Parkinson's disease risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Gaucher disease patients (65 total: 47 GD1, 18 GD3) were treated with ERT. Doses varied, generally ranging from 15–60 U/kg, with an average of 30 U/kg bm/every other week. While Lyso-Gb1 showed a varied correlation with ERT dosing (the coefficient of determination (R2) for treatment response dropped to 0.16 for high doses >35 U/kg bm/every other week), no consistent dose-response comparisons were reported for all analyzed markers. Blood samples were collected during annual clinical follow-up visits.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma, Blood samples (in this study); also noted in neurons (mouse model) and cerebrospinal fluid (previous study).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Slightly elevated in healthy controls but not significant; decreased in GD patients; negative correlation with age among GD3 patients.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The median concentration was highest in the control group (1.34 ng/mL), with GD patients having 0.16 ng/mL and GBA1 carriers 0.54 ng/mL. The difference between GD patients and controls was statistically significant (p = 0.0075) before multiple comparison adjustment but not after. A moderately negative linear correlation with age was found among GD3 patients (r = -0.52, p = 0.029), and levels were observed to decrease with ERT duration (partially supported). Mouse models showed an increase in α-SNCA concentration with GCase deficiency, while a previous study on cerebrospinal fluid revealed decreased α-SNCA levels among GBA1 pathogenic variant carriers. Correlation with age was also reported in supplementary materials.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Plays a role in the etiopathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases, particularly Parkinson's disease. Increased concentration and polymerization can lead to neurotoxicity, and GBA1 pathogenic variants are risk factors for PD.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Gaucher disease (GD) patients, GBA1 variant carriers, GCase deficiency, aging, duration of Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) treatment, and comparison to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential indicator of neurotoxicity and risk for Parkinson's disease. Although not statistically significant after adjustment, lower levels were observed in GD patients. Its levels are influenced by age and ERT duration in GD patients, with a negative correlation with age in GD3 patients suggesting a potential disease-related dynamic.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study primarily investigated the effects of physical exercise combined with whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) on oxidant/antioxidant balance and other physiological parameters in 16 high-level kayakers. It found an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in GPx activity, decreased TBARS, and variable urea levels, with no significant changes in MDA, CD, protein carbonyls, vitamin E, cortisol, testosterone, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), or hematological parameters. The document also reviews findings from other studies, indicating that WBC generally increases overall antioxidant capacity, helps normalize oxidant/antioxidant balance during intensive exercise, and exhibits anti-inflammatory effects, potentially enhancing recovery and performance during training.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Exercise Combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In the primary study, 16 kayakers underwent specialized physical training twice daily for 19 days. For the first 10 days, this was combined with Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) sessions administered twice daily (morning pre-exercise stimulation and afternoon post-exercise recovery). Each WBC session lasted 3 minutes (excluding a 30-second adaptive vestibule at -60°C) with chamber temperatures gradually decreasing from -120°C to -145°C. The document also refers to other studies using varying WBC protocols, including 10 sessions at -130°C for 3 minutes (once daily), 5 sessions/week at -110°C for 2 minutes, and single sessions at -130°C for 2 or 3 minutes, either with or without exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No statistically significant changes (P > 0.05) were observed throughout the experiment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall capacity of antioxidants in the body to neutralize free radicals.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During a training cycle involving combined physical exercise and WBC, followed by exercise-only in kayakers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change observed, suggesting stable overall antioxidant status under the study conditions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Negatively correlated with GPx at baseline (r = -0.697, P < 0.05); negatively correlated with TBARS on Day 5 (r = -0.710, P < 0.01) and Day 19 (r = -0.683, P < 0.01); negatively correlated with MDA on Day 19 (r = -0.634, P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall capacity of antioxidants in the body to neutralize free radicals, and its relationship with specific oxidative stress markers and antioxidant enzymes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Kayakers during a training cycle involving intensive exercise and WBC sessions (baseline, Day 5, and Day 19).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Statistically significant negative correlations are evidence for correct physiological functions, indicating a healthy balance between oxidative stress and antioxidant capacity within the organism.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Effect of Time (  = 3.43 mmol·L⁻¹, [1.38, 5.49]) and a Time by Supplement effect (  = − 3.09 mmol·L⁻¹ [− 6.04, − 0.14]). It was not clear whether TAC was statistically higher after the 1-km cycling TT (i.e., timepoint 'post') in the NAC trial compared to the placebo trial (p = 0.089; mean difference (MD) [95% CI] = 0.45 mmol·L⁻¹ [− 0.07, 0.97]; d = 0.36).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall measure of antioxidant defense system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During/after exercise with NAC or placebo.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher TAC indicates better overall antioxidant defense. The unclear effect with NAC suggests limited or non-significant impact on overall antioxidant capacity in this context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blinded, crossover study investigated the comparative effects of 1-week supplementation with tomato powder, isolated lycopene, or placebo on total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and exercise-induced lipid peroxidation biomarkers (MDA, 8-isoprostane) in well-trained male athletes. The study concluded that tomato powder was significantly more effective than pure lycopene in enhancing resting TAC and reducing the post-exercise elevation of lipid peroxidation biomarkers, suggesting that tomato powder's benefits are due to the synergistic interaction of lycopene with other bioactive components.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Nutritional supplementation (Tomato powder, Lycopene supplement, Placebo) combined with exhaustive exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received 1-week supplementation with either tomato powder (containing 30 mg lycopene, 5.38 mg beta-carotene, 22.32 mg phytoene, 9.84 mg phytofluene, and implied vitamin C and E per serving), pure lycopene (30 mg), or a placebo (dextrose and 3g tomato powder). Each subject underwent three exhaustive exercise tests (incremental treadmill protocol until failure) after each 1-week supplementation period. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported; the study focused on comparisons between the different supplement types and the placebo.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (at rest after tomato powder ingestion)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Resting TAC increased by 12% following tomato powder ingestion compared to other treatments (P = 0.04). No significant difference in TAC response to exhaustive exercise was found between treatments (P > 0.05). Improved antioxidant capacity was observed with tomato powder administration, but not with pure lycopene.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the body's total antioxidant defense system, comprising both endogenous and exogenous antioxidants, defending against oxidative stress and reactive oxygen species (ROS).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: At rest, following 1-week tomato powder ingestion, and during exhaustive exercise, after 1-week supplementation with tomato powder, lycopene, or placebo in well-trained male athletes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates antioxidant status; higher TAC suggests a stronger antioxidant defense system, providing protection against oxidative stress, supporting better recovery and overall health in athletes.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation on antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, and iron metabolism in rowers subjected to exhaustive exercise. Findings indicate that supplementation significantly strengthened antioxidant potential (TAC) and mitigated exercise-induced increases in pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-alpha), muscle damage indicators (myoglobin), and iron regulatory hormones (hepcidin) in the supplemented group. However, IL-6, ferritin, sTfR, iron, TIBC, and UIBC remained largely unaffected by supplementation or showed exercise-induced changes independent of it.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation combined with strenuous physical exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Athletes received 720 mg of highly-concentrated large cranberry extract daily (two 360-mg capsules, containing 36 mg proanthocyanidins per capsule) for 6 weeks. The control group received dyed gelatin placebo capsules containing flour. Participants performed a 2000-m rowing ergometer test at maximal effort on day 1 (pre-supplementation) and at the end of the 6-week training camp (post-supplementation), with blood samples taken pre-exercise, 1 minute post-exercise, and after a 24-hour recovery. No dose-response comparisons for cranberry extract were reported within the study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: decreased post-exercise at Trial I in both groups; significantly higher resting, post-exercise, and post-recovery levels in supplemented group at Trial II compared to controls; significant post-exercise decrease in supplemented group at Trial II from a higher baseline.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Modulated both by physical exercise (p < 0.001) and cranberry supplementation. Prior to supplementation (Trial I), both groups showed a significant post-exercise decrease. At Trial II, cranberry-supplemented athletes had significantly higher resting, post-exercise, and post-recovery levels of TAC than controls. Supplemented athletes also showed a significant post-exercise decrease in serum TAC at Trial II, but maintained overall higher levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the overall antioxidant defense potential of plasma against reactive oxygen species and combats oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Strenuous physical exercise (2000-m rowing test) and 6-week cranberry supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher baseline and post-exercise levels with supplementation suggest improved antioxidant defense, mitigating exercise-induced oxidative damage and indicating strengthened antioxidant potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 36-hour survival training, which included moderate to low physical activity and complete sleep deprivation, on oxidative stress and muscle damage biomarkers in young, healthy men. The training impaired enzymatic antioxidant defense (GPx, SOD), increased lipid peroxidation (LHs), and induced muscle damage (CK). A subsequent 12-hour recovery period, including overnight sleep, was found to be sufficient to normalize these markers and restore blood prooxidant-antioxidant homeostasis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Survival Training (combined with moderate to low intensity physical activity and sleep deprivation)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 36-hour survival training regimen for young, healthy men, involving moderate to low physical activity such as a 12-km march, 6 hours of rowing, 4 hours of kayaking, running, swimming, climbing, solving special tasks, and navigation in wild terrain. Ambient temperatures ranged from 8°C at night to 30°C during the day. The average heart rate was 80-90 beats/min (40-45% age-predicted HR max), with individual variations from 70-80 beats/min during march to 120-130 beats/min during rowing or kayaking. Participants experienced complete sleep deprivation and consumed approximately 3800 ± 120 kcal daily. This was followed by a 12-hour recovery period, including overnight sleep. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher than baseline and compared to the control group at 24h, 36h of survival training, and following the 12-h recovery (p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the overall antioxidant defense system of the body and its capacity to scavenge free radicals.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During 36-hour survival training with sleep deprivation and subsequent 12-hour recovery.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the body's response to counteract oxidative stress, suggesting an increased demand for antioxidant defense and overall antioxidant status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effect of D-ribose supplementation on delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) induced by plyometric exercise in untrained male college students. Findings indicate that oral administration of 15g D-ribose reduced muscle soreness, improved knee extensor function by mitigating strength reduction, lowered muscle damage markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, Myoglobin), and inhibited lipid peroxidation (Malondialdehyde), thereby accelerating DOMS recovery. However, D-ribose showed no significant effect on overall isokinetic muscle strength (flexor peak torque and total work) and modulated the time-course of antioxidant enzymes (Superoxide Dismutase) and total antioxidant capacity (TAC) without consistently showing a superior antioxidant effect compared to placebo after 48 hours.

treatment_details.therapy_type: D-ribose supplementation combined with plyometric exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: D-ribose was orally administered at 15g per dose, 1-hour before, and 1-hour, 12-hours, 24-hours, and 36-hours after exercise. A calorically equivalent placebo containing sorbitol and β-cyclodextrin was given at the same dose and times. The plyometric exercise protocol consisted of 7 sets of 20 consecutive frog hops with 90-second rest intervals between sets, performed twice with a 14-day washout period. No dose-response comparisons for D-ribose were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased then normalized in DRIB, sustained increase in PLAC
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly in both groups after 24-h (p < 0.01). TAC remained significantly elevated in PLAC after 48-h (p < 0.01), but not in DRIB (p > 0.05) at 48-h (though DRIB TAC was still significantly higher than before exercise, p < 0.01).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Reflects the overall capacity of the body's antioxidant defense system to neutralize free radicals.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-plyometric exercise oxidative stress and D-ribose supplementation effect on antioxidant defense.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the body's overall capacity to counteract oxidative stress. DRIB intervention modulates the duration of elevated TAC post-exercise, suggesting an altered or potentially more efficient antioxidant defense mechanism compared to sustained elevation in PLAC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-week oral garlic supplementation on 40-km cycling time trial performance, whole-body energy metabolism, exercise-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage in healthy adult males. Findings indicate that garlic supplementation significantly enhanced total antioxidant capacity and attenuated oxidative stress (MDA), inflammatory response (TNF-α), and some markers of muscle damage (LDH and UA at specific time points), but it did not improve cycling performance or overall whole-body energy metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral garlic extract supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 1000 mg/day for 4 weeks (28 consecutive days) in a single-blind crossover design. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as a single dose was used.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased/enhanced (p < 0.05) compared to placebo both before and during the 40-km cycling challenge period.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Represents the body's overall antioxidant defense capacity, involving antioxidant enzymes and whole-body antioxidant defense system for scavenging free radicals and resisting oxidative damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 4-wk garlic supplementation during a 40-km cycling challenge
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced systemic antioxidant capacity and reduced oxidative stress, crucial for preventing muscle damage, delaying the onset of high oxidative stress, and reducing exercise-induced inflammation during high-intensity exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased 1-8% from pre-run levels in placebo over 48-h recovery, and increased 15-39% in tart cherry group. A linear increase in antioxidant activity/TAS at 24 and 48-h of recovery was statistically different (p=0.046) from placebo and pre-run levels, culminating in a greater TAS activity at 48-h recovery in the tart cherry group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Redox balance, neutralization of free radicals; indicator of the body's antioxidant defense system and overall capacity to counteract reactive oxygen species (ROS) production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Short-term powdered tart cherry supplementation during recovery from a half-marathon run.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates better maintained redox balance, enhanced capacity to counteract oxidative stress post-exercise, and potential reduction in secondary muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 6-week Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation (770 mg/day) on muscle metabolism, inflammation, and antioxidant biomarkers in trained male CrossFit® athletes. The study concluded that TT supplementation could attenuate CrossFit® training-induced oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation by modulating levels of LDH, CRP, and TAS, while other muscle damage and inflammatory markers remained unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tribulus terrestris L. (TT) supplementation combined with a structured CrossFit training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Tribulus terrestris (TT) was supplemented orally at 770 mg/day (2 capsules of 385 mg, 72.64% TT extract at 40% saponins) for 6 weeks, taken daily after workouts. The CrossFit training program involved 3 high-intensity sessions per week on alternate weekdays (4.5 hours/week total), including specific warm-ups, Workouts of the Day (WODs) like 'Grace' and 'Fran', and cool-downs. The TT dose was within the reported safety range of 250-9000 mg, and no dose-response comparisons were reported in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the intervention group, TAS was significantly increased (p < 0.05) at 21 and 42 days post-baseline (e.g., T1: 1.34  1 0.07 mmol/L to T3: 1.48  1 0.05 mmol/L). The control group showed no significant change. Significant differences (p < 0.05) were observed between the intervention and control groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of the body's overall antioxidant defense capacity, evaluating the dynamic balance between antioxidant system and prooxidants, protecting against oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-intensity CrossFit® training program and 6-week Tribulus terrestris supplementation (770 mg/day).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the body's capacity to counteract oxidative stress; TT supplementation enhanced antioxidant defense, potentially promoting better cellular health and recovery during intense training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of total dietary antioxidant intake and capacity on body antioxidant mechanisms and exhaustive exercise-induced oxidative damage in ultra-endurance athletes. It examined physiological responses, including oxidative stress biomarkers (8-iso PGF2a, TOS, TAS, OSI) and lactate levels, during and after a combined cycling and treadmill exhaustive exercise protocol. Key findings indicated that higher dietary antioxidant intake was negatively correlated with pre-exercise total oxidant status and post-exercise increases in 8-iso PGF2a, while positively correlating with post-exercise increases in total antioxidant status and blood lactate concentrations. A higher dietary antioxidant capacity also positively influenced antioxidant defense and blood lactate removal (in both sexes) and running time to exhaustion (in males), but did not affect post-exercise heart rate recovery or perceived exertion.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exhaustive Exercise and Dietary Antioxidant Intake Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ultra-endurance athletes underwent an acute exhaustive exercise protocol comprising 45 minutes on a cycle ergometer at 65% VO2max, immediately followed by a treadmill test at 75% VO2max to volitional exhaustion (median running time ~26-27 min, RPE 19). Dietary antioxidant intake was assessed using the Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP) assay, with a median intake of 16.6-17.2 mmol/day, categorized as moderate-to-high. document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated a multilayer perceptron (MLP) machine learning model for the early postnatal differential diagnosis of choledochal cysts (CC) and cystic biliary atresia (CBA). The model utilized routinely available clinical parameters, including biochemical markers (Total bile acid, Total bilirubin, γ-glutamyl transferase, Aspartate aminotransferase, Alanine aminotransferase, Direct bilirubin, and Taurodeoxycholate) and ultrasonographic measurements (Longitudinal and Transverse diameters of cysts), from a retrospective cohort of 319 patients. The MLP model achieved high diagnostic performance (95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and AUC of 0.990 for differentiating CBA from CC), aiming to facilitate timely surgical intervention for CBA and improve patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Model Development (Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective study involved the analysis of clinical features from 319 patients (< 60 days old at surgery) with hepatic hilar cysts (274 CC, 45 CBA) treated between 2011 and 2022. It focused on developing a diagnostic model rather than a therapeutic intervention. Biochemical markers and ultrasonographic measurements were compared, and key diagnostic features were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Eleven machine learning models were developed and compared, with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) model showing optimal performance: 95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.990. The model utilized seven routine clinical parameters (GGT, TBA, DBIL, TBIL, ALT, LDC, and TDC) as input variables. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the congenital biliary atresia (CBA) group than in the choledochal cysts (CC) group. Tanaka et al. reported that when patients with hilar cysts have a TBA > 111 mol/L, the diagnosis of CBA over CC should be considered. Contributes positively toward CBA diagnosis in the LASSO model, demonstrating the highest absolute coefficient magnitude among positive contributors.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Key discriminatory marker for CBA, indicating severe cholestasis due to complete biliary obstruction and poor development of intrahepatic bile ducts. Serves as a distinguishing factor for CBA.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated peripheral immune signatures, specifically serum sCD163, IL-10, IL-12, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) Cldn1 and TGF-β expression levels, in various patient cohorts including healthy controls, chronic HCV (cirrhotic/non-cirrhotic, treatment-naïve and DAA-SVR), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. The primary aim was to characterize clinicopathological and molecular profiles, assessing their associations with hepatocarcinogenesis risk and their prognostic capacity for HCC in cirrhotic Egyptian HCV patients before and after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, ultimately identifying these markers as novel non-invasive predictors for HCC, even in cases with normal conventional markers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) therapy for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, primarily involving a 12-week period of sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin, were administered to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) in HCV patients. The study's focus was on the SVR outcome and the observational analysis of biomarker levels across different patient groups (including those post-DAA treatment), rather than on specific DAA dose-response comparisons or detailed treatment protocols.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of short-term powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation on markers of muscle damage, inflammation, oxidative stress, and muscle soreness in aerobically trained individuals undergoing a half-marathon run. Findings indicate that supplementation attenuated muscle catabolism (creatinine, urea/BUN, total protein), reduced physiological stress (cortisol), lessened immune and inflammatory stress (IL-2, IL-6, IL-13), better maintained redox balance (antioxidant activity, TAS), and reduced muscle soreness, ultimately enhancing endurance performance and recovery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Powdered Montmorency tart cherry supplementation and endurance running (half-marathon race)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested capsules containing 480 mg of powdered Montmorency tart cherries (CherryPURE®) once daily for 10 days (7 days pre-race, race day, and 2 days post-race), compared to a 480 mg rice flour placebo. This 480 mg supplement is equivalent to 51.3 mL (17.4 fl oz) of tart cherry juice, providing 991 mg of phenolic compounds and 66 mg of anthocyanins. The intervention was evaluated in the context of a stressful endurance challenge: a half-marathon run (21.1 km). No dose-response comparisons were reported, but the supplementation significantly affected physiological responses and race performance compared to placebo.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of liver function, bile duct obstruction, or hemolytic conditions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study evaluated the usefulness of a panel of biochemical and hematological variables for assessing training loads and recovery effectiveness in young professional long-distance and sprint swimmers over a 10-week preparatory training period. It identified an optimal panel including creatine kinase (CK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea (U), total bilirubin (TB), direct bilirubin (DB), and ferritin concentrations, which collectively provide crucial information for monitoring post-training effort and recovery, regardless of sex or competitive distance. The study also highlighted the importance of ferritin, iron, and blood morphology in preventing deficiencies, anemia, and inflammatory states.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study monitoring biochemical and hematological recovery variables in young professional swimmers during a training program
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Data was collected over a 10-week preparatory training stage involving 27 male and female swimmers, aged 15-18 years, categorized by competitive distance (sprint: 50-100m; long-distance: 400-800m). Measurements included enzyme activities (ALT, AST, LDH, ALP, CK), metabolite concentrations (Cr, CRP, ferritin, TB, DB, urea, iron), and various capillary blood morphology parameters. The study primarily focused on observing responses to ongoing training loads and recovery, rather than comparing specific training "doses."

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased at beginning of training, then decreased significantly; tendency to increase in female groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed a tendency to increase in female groups during the study. Generally, increased at the beginning of the training program, then significantly decreased to below baseline after 2–3 weeks, regardless of sex and competitive distance.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Byproduct of heme breakdown, generally associated with liver function and red blood cell breakdown, functioning as a potential anti-inflammatory and antioxidant.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-training effort, recovery profiles after physical effort, beginning of the training program, and training adaptation after a break in professional long-distance and sprint swimmers.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Provides a good overview of post-training effort, helps assess recovery, and indicates hemolysis (e.g., footstrike hemolysis) when increased. Serves as a marker of training adaptation after a break and can assess the extent of training without excessive intravascular hemolysis. Recommended for an optimal monitoring panel.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers for predicting the effectiveness and diagnosing complications (acute rejection (AR) and ischemic-type biliary lesion (ITBL)) in liver transplant patients. Using MALDI-TOF MS, LC-MS, ELISA, and Western blot, the study found that ACLY, FGA, and APOA1 protein levels were significantly lower in pre-transplant, AR, and ITBL patients compared to healthy controls, showing modest recovery post-transplantation. These dysregulated proteins, implicated in glucolipid metabolism and the clotting cascade, are proposed as novel non-invasive and early diagnostic and prognostic indicators for liver transplantation outcomes and complications. Additionally, the study noted changes in clinical parameters such as blood cell counts, liver synthesis markers (CHO, ALB, FIB), and liver damage markers (GGT, TBIL, PT, ALT, AST) in transplant patients and those with complications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Liver Transplantation (Orthotopic)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study focuses on orthotopic liver transplantation, investigating outcomes and complications (acute rejection, ischemic-type biliary lesion) in patients. While no specific dose-response comparisons for the transplantation procedure were reported, the study did note that the anhepatic phase was significantly longer in ITBL patients (57.60 ± 7.28 minutes vs 45.88 ± 8.43 minutes for excellent patients, p = 0.0377) and warm ischemia time was longer in AR patients (14.57 ± 7.28 minutes vs 9.63 ± 0.86 minutes for healthy transplant patients, p = 0.0996). Samples were collected pre-transplant, 14 days post-transplant, and within 48 hours of complication onset, including grafts from extended criteria, donation after death, and partial/suboptimal donors.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-liver transplantation in transplant patients compared to healthy controls.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers to differentiate Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases in human patients. The findings indicated that methylation levels of OPCML and HOXD9 in serum cfDNA were significantly higher in CCA patients compared to those with other biliary diseases. The study concluded that OPCML and HOXD9, especially when combined, demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity, making them promising differential biomarkers for CCA, improving diagnostic accuracy and preventing misdiagnosis.

Methylation levels were quantified using methylation-sensitive high-resolution melting (MS-HRM) assay on bisulfite-modified serum cfDNA (20 µL, <1 µg), with detection limits of 1.56% (lower) and 50% (upper). Their potency was evaluated using ROC curves. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported, as this was a diagnostic study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased only in the exercise group; although both groups showed a decrease, the exercise group had the highest change in magnitude following 14 days of HDBR.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Energy storage, insulation, hormone production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 14 days of Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR) with an exercise countermeasure.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Metabolic health, body composition changes during inactivity and exercise, with exercise showing a greater beneficial impact on fat loss.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased borderline significantly more in the protein group compared with the placebo group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Overall mass of the body, influenced by fat, lean mass, and water content.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: General indicator of body mass changes in response to dietary and exercise interventions.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study investigated the effects of 6-month potassium citrate (K citrate) supplementation (30 mEq/day), in combination with calcium and vitamin D, on bone turnover markers and urinary metabolic profiles in 40 postmenopausal women with osteopenia. The study found that while bone turnover markers (CTX and BAP) decreased in both K citrate and placebo groups, K citrate significantly enhanced these beneficial effects, particularly in a subgroup of patients with pre-existing low-grade acidosis (low urine pH and/or low potassium and citrate excretion). K citrate also improved urinary pH, citrate, and potassium excretion. The study concluded that K citrate is beneficial for osteopenic women with documented potassium/citrate deficits and low-grade acidosis, but its indiscriminate use is not recommended without such evidence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Potassium Citrate (K citrate) supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Daily oral supplementation with 30 mEq of K citrate (in two tablets) for 6 months. This was administered in addition to daily calcium carbonate (500 mg day   ⁻¹) and vitamin D (400 IU day   ⁻¹) for all subjects (K citrate and placebo groups). The K citrate treatment showed significant benefits in subjects with evidence of low-grade acidosis (low 24h-citrate excretion or low fasting-morning urine pH) compared to the placebo, with significant changes observed as early as 3 months. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported, and adherence rates were approximately 90% for both groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential mineral for bone health, muscle contraction, nerve signaling, and blood clotting.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: K citrate supplementation in postmenopausal women with osteopenia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of calcium metabolism and overall bone health status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the tissue origins of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in healthy mice using tissue-specific knockout models and its utility as a biomarker following paracetamol (APAP) overdose in both mice and humans. It found that cfDNA predominantly originates from blood cell lineages in healthy mice. Following APAP overdose, total and hepatocyte-derived cfDNA, as well as ALT and AST levels, significantly increased in mice (peaking at 8 hours), while albumin and bilirubin remained unaffected. In human APAP overdose patients, total cfDNA and liver-specific cfDNA (via methylation analysis) also significantly increased, especially in those with biochemical evidence of liver injury, demonstrating cfDNA's potential as a clinical biomarker for distinguishing overdose patients, assessing liver injury severity, and monitoring treatment efficacy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Paracetamol (APAP) Overdose; N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mice received intraperitoneal (IP) APAP at 350 mg/kg body weight, with samples collected at 8, 24, and 48 hours post-dosing (optimal cfDNA peak at 8 hours, liver damage most severe at 24 hours). Human patients presented with APAP overdose, with a subset receiving N-acetylcysteine (NAC) at 500-900 mg/kg body weight 20-40 hours after initial overdose. Patient groups were stratified by liver injury severity (normal vs. raised ALT); no specific APAP dose comparisons were performed in humans.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by ~100-fold in APAP-dosed mice compared to saline-injected mice, peaking at 8 hours post-dose; greater than 100-fold increase also observed in hepatocyte-specific knockout mice. Sufficient cfDNA input for duplicate ddPCR measurements was 20 ng.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of general cellular breakdown, cell death, or loss of nuclear DNA into circulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: APAP-induced acute liver injury in C57BL/6 and hepatocyte-specific knockout mice.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Sensitive indicator of cellular damage; candidate biomarker for stratification of APAP overdose patients, indicating acute tissue damage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by an average of more than 236-fold in APAP overdose patients with biochemical evidence of liver injury (raised ALT); increased by an average of 18-fold in patients without biochemical evidence of liver injury (normal ALT); decreased after N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of general cellular breakdown, cell death, or loss of nuclear DNA into circulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: APAP overdose in human patients; response to NAC treatment.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential clinical biomarker in APAP overdose for distinguishing patients from healthy volunteers, for assessing severity of liver injury, and for monitoring the efficacy of treatment. Reflects exposure to APAP and overall cellular damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Highest mean levels found in children with MIS-C (4.12 ng/µL, p < 0.03 by Mann-Whitney U test) compared with pediatric COVID-19, adult COVID-19, or controls. Subset of MIS-C patients (n=3) showed >10 ng/µL. Significantly higher mean levels in more severe pediatric and adult COVID-19 cases compared to nonsevere cases and controls (p < 0.05 by Mann-Whitney U test). Significant positive correlation with C-reactive protein (CRP) levels in the blood (Pearson correlation; R = 0.29, p = 0.049).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: General indicator of cell death and tissue injury.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Children with MIS-C, pediatric and adult COVID-19 (severe vs. nonsevere), and controls; patients with MIS-C/COVID-19.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates widespread tissue injury, useful for monitoring and quantification of tissue injury and cell death; mirrors systemic inflammation markers, indicating utility for evaluating general tissue injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.
