matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid metabolism, cardiovascular risk factor.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Medical risk factor control, general health monitoring in patients with stable coronary heart disease.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fat utilization during exercise reduces resting levels of total cholesterol (59)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of lipid profiles, involved in cardiovascular health
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fat utilization during exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cardiovascular health profiles

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varied (decreased in non-pDPN, unchanged in pDPN)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.06); significant decrease in without pDPN group (P < 0.01); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.79).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential component of lipid metabolism, vital for cell membrane structure and steroid hormone synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shows an improvement in metabolic health (lower total cholesterol) in the group without pDPN, but not in the pDPN group.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A lipid essential for cell membrane structure, hormone production, and vitamin D synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase in professional soccer players, assessed at baseline and post-PS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not reported in this study, but generally indicates cardiovascular health and metabolic status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: lower in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls, attributed to a higher prevalence of statin therapy

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential lipid for cell membranes and hormone production; indicator of cardiovascular risk
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis with concurrent statin therapy
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes, with medication influencing levels

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported in the study findings.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential component of cell membranes and a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels are generally associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy of a multimodal exercise countermeasure (including high-intensity interval training, low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises) in attenuating musculoskeletal deconditioning, cardiovascular fitness level reduction, and muscle strength loss during 14 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) in healthy older adults. The research, conducted as a 2-arm randomized controlled trial, also examined the effects on body composition, vertical jump performance, tilt tolerance, and various blood parameters including hormones, inflammatory markers, and lipid profiles. While the exercise intervention helped maintain aerobic fitness (V̇O2peak) and resulted in a greater decrease in total body fat mass, it was largely ineffective in preventing reductions in total and leg lean mass, knee extension strength (isometric and isokinetic), and orthostatic intolerance. Both groups experienced significant reductions in several blood parameters (serum iron, total cholesterol, HDL-chol, LDL-chol, parathyroid hormone, testosterone) and increases in white blood cells and C-reactive protein. Alanine transaminase and cortisol showed differential responses, increasing in the exercise group while decreasing in controls.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Head-down bed rest (HDBR) with or without a multimodal exercise countermeasure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent 14 days of continuous 6-degree Head-Down Bed Rest (HDBR). The exercise countermeasure group performed 3 sessions per day, totaling 60-75 minutes of physical exercise daily, individually adjusted for intensity. This multimodal intervention included high-intensity interval training (HIIT), low-intensity cycling, or strength exercises for the lower and upper body. The control group received passive physiotherapy consisting of passive range-of-motion exercises. All exercises and activities were completed in a head-down tilt or horizontal position. No specific dose-response comparisons for varying exercise parameters were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease in both groups following 14 days of bed rest intervention.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid molecule vital for cell membrane structure, hormone production, and vitamin D synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Following 14 days of bed rest intervention.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of lipid metabolism; changes can reflect metabolic adaptation or risk factors for cardiovascular health during bed rest.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decreases (p < 0.05) reported in the melatonin group, with moderate overall modulating effects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A lipid essential for cell membranes and as a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids; high levels associated with cardiovascular risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation in highly trained athletes to improve lipid profile.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health and lipid metabolism, which can impact overall physiological function and long-term health by improving lipid profile.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Patients with atherosclerotic plaques (SLE-P) had higher serum total cholesterol levels, though for most patients these were within established normal ranges, compared to plaque-free patients (SLE-NP).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential lipid for cell membranes and steroid hormone synthesis; high levels are a risk factor for atherosclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Subclinical atherosclerosis in women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (initial clinical assessment).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a risk factor associated with the presence of subclinical atherosclerotic plaques in SLE patients; however, routine measurements often classified high-risk patients as low-risk due to values falling within normal ranges, highlighting poor predictive power.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with increasing PGI/PGII quartiles. Higher MPO quartiles associated with decreased levels (P < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential lipid for cell membranes and hormone synthesis; an indicator of cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Stratification by Pepsinogen Ratio (PGI/PGII) quartiles; association with MPO levels across quartiles.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health. Levels are interpreted in conjunction with LDL and HDL.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant intra-group changes from baseline to 30 months (p > 0.500). No statistically significant sex differences were observed at endpoint, and no significant associations with glucose were found.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential component of cell membranes, precursor to steroid hormones and bile acids.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable lipid metabolism post-COVID-19 vaccination, suggesting no significant overall changes or sex differences in total cholesterol.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not show a positive influence on lipids (TC, TG, LDL-C) by CoQ10.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Sum of all cholesterol types in the blood; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: CoQ10 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: No improvement in overall cholesterol levels.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High levels (> 200 mg/dL) found in 72% of the sample, with levels ~20% higher in women compared to men.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of cell membranes and a precursor for steroids and bile acids.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Vascular aging.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Strongest biomarker of vascular aging; high levels are a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-sectional Study for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the 2019 general physical examination of 3,280 rural Chinese residents aged 45 years and older. No experimental interventions or therapeutic doses were administered; the study focused on observational correlations between biomarkers and cIMT. It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Positively correlated with cIMT (P < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for cell membranes, hormone production, and vitamin D synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fasting state during cross-sectional health examination; associated with carotid intima-media thickness.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular risk and a risk factor for carotid intima-media thickness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A greater decrease in TCH levels was observed in the control group at 'no FOPS' condition, but not in the FOPS group. There was also a significantly increased synthesis of TCH observed the morning after the test session in the FOPS group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An essential structural component of cell membranes and a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Comparing FOPS and control groups under 'no FOPS' conditions and in the morning after the FOPS supplementation and exercise protocol.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered overall cholesterol metabolism, with a less pronounced decrease in the FOPS group during the 'no FOPS' condition and increased synthesis post-exercise, suggesting a distinct and complex metabolic response to FOPS and exercise. Sustained increases could be associated with cardiovascular risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. It summarizes findings related to metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, endocrine (melatonin, cortisol, growth hormone), and neuronal/glial degeneration pathways, including promising markers like neurofilament light chain. The document also highlights the importance of standardized protocols, independent validation, and considers pre-analytical and analytical variables (e.g., sampling time, feeding state) that influence biomarker reliability, noting the current lack of clinically validated biomarkers but expressing optimism for future discoveries.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Review and evaluation of wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD) progression and pathology
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Not applicable, as this document is a comprehensive review of biomarkers, their changes, and factors influencing their measurement in HD, rather than an experimental study of a specific therapeutic intervention or its dose.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Most studies showed no alteration; one study reported a reduction in premanifest and manifest HD subjects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential lipid involved in cell membrane structure and precursor for steroids.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Huntington's Disease (HD); lipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Generally not considered a reliable peripheral biomarker for HD due to inconsistent findings, though some reductions observed in specific cohorts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. It also examined changes in cognitive function (attention, executive function, memory, visual ability, fine motor skills, reaction), psychological scores (anxiety, depression), and various blood biochemical markers (Estradiol, prolactin, FSH, LH, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin). The study compared patients before, one week after, and six months after completing chemotherapy to healthy controls. Key findings revealed widespread chemotherapy-induced abnormalities in resting state networks, which partly recovered by six months post-chemotherapy. These altered functional connectivities were correlated with cognitive assessment scores and blood biochemical indexes, suggesting RSNs as potential biomarkers for chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and for guiding rehabilitation. Baseline analyses also showed higher metabolic markers and psychological/cognitive scores in patients compared to controls, along with a high incidence of chemotherapy-induced amenorrhea.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (for breast cancer patients, some also received endocrine therapy)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Postoperative chemotherapy was administered to breast cancer patients, typically in six to eight courses. While specific drug names or dosages were not detailed, follow-up assessments were consistently conducted before (baseline), one week after completing, and six months after completing chemotherapy. Some patients (35.3%) also received endocrine therapy after chemotherapy, but no concurrent radiotherapy or endocrine therapy was given during chemotherapy. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the breast cancer group than in the healthy control group at baseline (P < 0.05). Increased changes after chemotherapy were negatively correlated with decreased within-network connectivity in the supplementary motor area for Central Network (r = -0.484, P = 0.049). Improved cholesterol metabolism was observed six months later, but the levels were still in the abnormal range compared to the Healthy Control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential lipid for cell membrane structure and steroid hormone synthesis; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Cholesterol metabolism is vital for vascular health and cognitive function.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline assessment and post-chemotherapy changes in breast cancer patients, correlated with within-network functional connectivity.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic health and cardiovascular risk. Elevated baseline levels are associated with breast cancer. Changes after chemotherapy are linked to brain functional connectivity changes, suggesting a contribution to chemotherapy-related cognitive dysfunction. Lower lipid levels are speculated to positively impact cognitive improvement and reduce the risk of vascular-related cognitive impairment.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A lipid essential for cell membranes and hormone production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular risk and general metabolic status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lowered total cholesterol (reported in meta-analyses), with effects more pronounced in men than women. Note that isolated isoflavone extracts, unlike soy protein, did not significantly lower total cholesterol.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Sum of all cholesterol in the blood; a key indicator of cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Soy protein supplementation in post-menopausal women and in both sexes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved cardiovascular health and reduced risk of chronic diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Lipid-depleted (LD) serum (FBS-LD), FBS, Isolated VLDL and LDL

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Virtually absent in lipid-depleted (LD) serum compared to standard FBS. Reduced levels in culture medium enhance sorafenib's efficacy.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major exogenous lipid component, essential for cell membrane structure and involved in various metabolic processes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Medium containing 10% FBS-LD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced levels in culture medium enhance sorafenib's efficacy, though it was considered less critical than triglycerides as a driver of resistance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly decreased (P < 0.05) in the intervention group compared to baseline and control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key lipid in blood, involved in lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health; high levels contribute to atherosclerosis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Rehabilitation training (RT) or aerobic exercise therapy (ET) in CAD patients after PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels indicate improved cardiovascular health, reduced risk of atherosclerosis and CAD progression, and improved lipid profiles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant time interactions were found.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for cell membranes and steroid hormone synthesis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Competitive season and pre-season sports training.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic and cardiovascular health, showing stability despite training variations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study retrospectively investigated the effect of different statin-based lipid-lowering strategies (including various statin types, statin combined with ezetimibe, and intensive vs. regular statin therapy) on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in 3653 patients with stable coronary artery disease who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. The findings indicate that statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy significantly reduced hs-CRP levels, with this reduction being indirectly mediated by a decrease in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Statin-based lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, ezetimibe)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated three statin-based lipid-lowering strategies administered for 1 month: 1) different types of statins (atorvastatin vs. rosuvastatin); 2) statin combined with ezetimibe therapy (regular statin dose + ezetimibe 10 mg/day or greater); and 3) intensive statin therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg or greater/day or rosuvastatin 20 mg or greater/day) vs. regular statin therapy (atorvastatin 20 mg/day or rosuvastatin 10 mg/day). Statin combined with ezetimibe therapy and intensive statin therapy further reduced hs-CRP levels compared to routine statin use, with statin+ezetimibe showing a stronger LDL-C reduction effect. No significant difference was observed among different statin types regarding their direct effect on hs-CRP reduction.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: After 1-month of treatment, TC was lower in the high-effective Δhs-CRP (%) group (3.42 ± 0.79 mmol/L) compared to the low-effective group (3.52 ± 0.84 mmol/L, p < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Total amount of cholesterol in the blood, comprising HDL, LDL, and VLDL; essential for cell membrane structure and precursor for steroid hormones.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Statin-based lipid-lowering strategies after 1-month of treatment in patients post-PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease; reduction contributes to improved cardiovascular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study aimed to develop and validate a female-focused predictive atherosclerosis risk signature based on serum metabolites in patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), addressing the inadequacy of established cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk scores. It investigated metabolomic and clinical features associated with subclinical plaque status, developing and validating a 35-metabolite/5-clinical trait signature (UCLH-40) and a refined 5-feature panel (including age, glycine, M-LDL-C, IDL-C, and omega-6/omega-3 ratio) that accurately classifies SLE patients with/without subclinical atherosclerosis, predicts atherosclerosis progression, and identifies elevated CVD risk, thereby outperforming existing risk assessment tools.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic/Prognostic Biomarker Discovery and Validation for Atherosclerosis Risk Stratification (via Metabolomics and Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, diagnostic study that did not involve therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons for treatments. Its primary focus was on developing and validating predictive biomarker signatures. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance platform (≥250 metabolites). Various machine learning models (e.g., univariate logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator LR, random forest, neural network, support vector machine, and eXtreme gradient boost) with 10-fold cross-validation were used to analyze metabolomic data and clinical traits. Model performance was assessed by AUROC (>0.7 for inclusion), sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Vascular ultrasound was used for carotid/femoral intima-media thickness assessment of subclinical atherosclerosis. The study discusses the implications for guiding statin therapy or lifestyle modifications but does not directly test them, noting that standard statin prescriptions may be insufficient due to normal lipid ranges in SLE patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly different (P<0.05) between SLE-P and SLE-NP patients, identified as a molecule linked to atherosclerosis. Elevated in patients with SLE-P (P <0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Storage form of cholesterol, transported within lipoproteins; involved in cholesterol metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Novel metabolomic signature associated with subclinical atherosclerosis in women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus; Subclinical plaque status in adult Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) patients (SLE-P vs. SLE-NP).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Part of a novel metabolomic signature associated with the presence of subclinical plaque in SLE. Associated with subclinical plaque status and increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in SLE patients. Identified as statin-responsive in previous pharmacological studies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether pre-exercise ascorbic acid supplementation influenced antioxidant defenses, glucose metabolism, inflammation, and muscle damage in untrained healthy adults following a single bout of moderate-intensity cycling. Findings indicated that ascorbic acid supplementation reduced plasma Malondialdehyde (MDA) and increased Ferric Reducing Ability of Plasma (FRAP), while also modulating glucose levels and attenuating exercise-induced changes in albumin and total protein. While moderate-intensity cycling led to an increase in red blood cell Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) activity and low-grade muscle damage (Total Creatine Kinase), it did not induce systemic inflammation or lipid peroxidation. Ascorbic acid supplementation appeared to mitigate the exercise-induced increase in SOD activity but did not significantly prevent muscle damage or affect other inflammatory/damage markers such as hsCRP, LDH, CK-MB, GPx, or Catalase.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) supplementation combined with a single bout of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects received 1000 mg of ascorbic acid (or placebo) orally 5 minutes prior to a 30-minute indoor cycling session. Exercise intensity was set at 65–75% of maximum heart rate, which was predicted by an age-based equation. No dose-response comparisons were reported for either ascorbic acid or exercise intensity.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased in both placebo and ascorbic acid groups post-exercise
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A main effect of exercise (p < 0.05) was observed. Levels increased immediately after exercise (p = 0.019) and remained high at 30 min post-exercise (p = 0.004) in the placebo group. Activity also increased at 30 min post-exercise in subjects ingesting ascorbic acid.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: An enzyme primarily found in muscle tissue, involved in energy production; elevated levels indicate muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute aerobic exercise (indoor cycling) in untrained healthy adults, with or without pre-workout ascorbic acid supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates exercise-induced muscle damage. Ascorbic acid supplementation did not significantly prevent this acute muscle damage.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, prospective observational study investigated whether vitamin D metabolites (25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) and Vitamin D Binding Protein (VDBP), along with their ratios, could predict preeclampsia (PE) in women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM). The study found that higher concentrations of 1,25(OH)2D, lower concentrations of VDBP, and elevated 1,25(OH)2D/VDBP ratios in the second and third trimesters were significantly associated with and predictive of subsequent PE, while 25(OH)D, the standard metric for vitamin D status, did not predict PE.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal Prospective Observational Study on Preeclampsia Prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons. Biomarker concentrations and clinical data were collected at three gestational visits: V1 (~12 weeks), V2 (~22 weeks), and V3 (~32 weeks). The study enrolled 151 women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM) and 24 non-diabetic controls, rigorously phenotyped and free of proteinuria and hypertension at enrolment. The primary analysis compared 23 T1DM women who developed preeclampsia (PE) with 24 matched T1DM women who remained normotensive. A secondary analysis compared normotensive T1DM women with non-diabetic controls. The cohort was largely vitamin D insufficient or deficient.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in T1DM women with PE (DM+PE+) than in normotensive T1DM women (DM+PE−) at the initial study visit.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Exogenous insulin administered to regulate blood glucose levels in individuals with Type 1 Diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Initial study visit in pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes (T1DM), associated with preeclampsia (PE) risk.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates insulin requirement, potentially reflecting insulin resistance or disease severity, and is a factor in assessing preeclampsia risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of early first-trimester tubular (urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1) and glomerular (eGFR) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). It concluded that elevated first-trimester urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc) and, to a lesser extent, eGFR, are associated with increased PE risk. Notably, uNGALcc, especially when combined with clinical factors like BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin, significantly improved PE prediction, indicating subclinical renal tubular and glomerular dysfunction as early markers of PE, while urinary KIM-1 and plasma NGAL were not predictive.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on diagnostic biomarker assessment for preeclampsia risk prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a prospective observational cohort study enrolling pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) and normotensive pregnant women without diabetes. Biomarkers were assessed at three gestational visits: V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks), V2 (21.7  1 1.4 weeks), and V3 (31.4  1 1.5 weeks), with primary focus on first-trimester (V1) values for preeclampsia (PE) prediction. Study groups included women with T1DM who developed PE (DM+PE+), T1DM women who remained normotensive (DM+PE-), and normotensive women without diabetes (DM-). All T1DM subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria at V1. No active intervention or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic/prognostic utility. Analysis included samples with specific attention to leukocyte-negative urine samples.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in DM+PE+ than in DM+PE 2 at V1.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Exogenous regulation of blood glucose.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and subsequent Preeclampsia (DM+PE+), compared to those without Preeclampsia (DM+PE 2).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as a covariate in the mathematical model to predict PE risk; associated with distinguishing clinical characteristics between DM+PE+ and DM+PE 2 groups at V1.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the utility of Endothelial Progenitor Cells (EPCs), Circulating Endothelial Cells (CECs), and their ratio, alongside C-peptide, as early biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction in children with newly diagnosed Type 1 Diabetes (T1D). The study aimed to assess their association with clinical state, residual insulin secretion, and the occurrence of partial remission, revealing that T1D patients exhibit higher EPC levels compared to controls. Worse clinical conditions, including higher glucose and lower C-peptide, were linked to increased EPC mobilization and less favorable EPC/CEC ratios, while higher CEC levels were associated with partial remission. The findings highlight the potential of these biomarkers to reflect endothelial injury and repair processes in T1D children.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This was an observational study assessing biomarkers in children with newly diagnosed Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) and their clinical progression, rather than an interventional study. The document also discusses various T1D management strategies, including insulin pump therapy, multiple daily injections, metformin, ACE inhibitors, statins, diet, and physical activity, and their influence on biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: As an observational study, there were no controlled therapeutic doses. Patients received routine outpatient care, including insulin therapy (dose not a controlled variable, but DIR < 0.5 U/kg/24 h was a criterion for partial remission). The study noted that increased EPC levels were more pronounced with insulin pump therapy compared to multiple daily injections, and discussed the potential effects of other treatments (metformin, ACE inhibitors, statins) on biomarker levels without specific dose comparisons from this study's direct findings.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Partial remission defined as < 0.5 U/kg/24 h

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Measures the exogenous insulin needed to maintain glycemic control.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Newly diagnosed T1D; assessed at discharge, 3, 6 months, 1st and 2nd year follow-up; used to define partial remission.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the degree of exogenous insulin dependency and is a criterion for partial remission in T1D.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study investigated the ergogenic effects of acute pre-exercise homemade chicken broth (CB) ingestion, rich in histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) like carnosine and anserine, on high-intensity cycling performance in recreationally-trained men. The study found a significant 5.2% improvement in 8-minute time trial mean power and elevated plasma carnosine and anserine levels following CB supplementation. However, the ergogenic effect was not mediated by changes in acid-base balance or red blood cell glutathione status, indicating alternative mechanisms may be at play.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute pre-exercise nutritional supplementation (homemade chicken broth or placebo soup)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Subjects ingested either 8 mL/kg body weight of homemade chicken broth (CB), providing 46.4 mg/kg body weight of total histidine-containing dipeptides (HCDs) (specifically 15.6 mg/kg BW carnosine and 30.8 mg/kg BW anserine), or an equivalent volume of a placebo soup. The supplement was administered 25-40 minutes prior to an 8-minute high-intensity cycling time trial, following a warm-up. No dose-response comparisons were made, only CB versus placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant effect of chicken broth supplementation was observed on red blood cell reduced glutathione (GSH, p = 0.771) or oxidized glutathione disulphide (GSSG, p = 0.267) levels. No main effect of time or supplement was present.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A major antioxidant system protecting cells from oxidative damage and maintaining cellular redox balance.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After pre-exercise chicken broth supplementation and a high-intensity cycling time-trial, sampled at fasted, pre-warm-up, and post-exercise time points.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Unaffected by CB supplementation, suggesting it does not significantly alter the glutathione status in red blood cells under the study conditions, and thus is not a primary mediator of the observed performance effects through antioxidant capacities.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the influence of oral contraceptive (OC) use on physiological, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses to fixed-intensity and sprint cycling in recreationally trained women, comparing them to naturally cycling women. It also examined the acute effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation on these responses and 1-km cycling time trial performance. Key findings showed that women using OC had elevated oxidative stress (higher MDA, lower GPx) and inflammation (higher CRP) biomarkers, as well as increased ventilation, during exercise. While NAC supplementation increased plasma thiols, it only blunted exercise-induced malondialdehyde increases in naturally cycling women, not in OC users, and did not improve cycling performance in either group. This suggests an increased strain on the endogenous antioxidant system in women using OC during exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation and cycling exercise (fixed-intensity and sprint time trial).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Twenty recreationally trained women completed five exercise trials, including two double-blind crossover intervention trials where participants acutely supplemented with NAC or a placebo. NAC was administered orally in a total dose of 105 mg·kg⁻¹ of body mass, given as 70 mg·kg⁻¹ 60 minutes prior to exercise and 35 mg·kg⁻¹ 30 minutes prior. The exercise protocol involved 40 minutes of fixed-intensity cycling at 105% of the gas-exchange threshold (GET), immediately followed by an all-out 1-km cycling time trial. No dose-response comparisons for NAC were reported beyond the acute vs. placebo comparison.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically lower in the NAC trial compared to the placebo trial at the end of the 40-min cycling task (p = 0.005; MD = − 0.47 µmol·L⁻¹ [− 0.79, − 0.16]; d = − 0.40) and after the 1-km cycling TT (p < 0.001; MD = − 0.80 µmol·L⁻¹ [− 1.20, − 0.41]; d = − 1.01), irrespective of group. An effect of Time (  = 1.71 µmol·L⁻¹ [0.24, 3.16]), Supplement (  = − 0.29 µmol·L⁻¹ [− 0.56, − 0.02]), and a Time by Supplement interaction (  = -4.19 µmol·L⁻¹ [− 6.24, − 2.09]) were observed.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major endogenous antioxidant, involved in detoxification and redox regulation as part of the non-enzymatic endogenous antioxidant defense system.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During and after fixed-intensity cycling and 1-km cycling time trial, with acute N-acetylcysteine (NAC) or placebo supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower total glutathione during the NAC trial compared to placebo might suggest increased utilization during exercise or altered synthesis/breakdown pathways, requiring further investigation into reduced and oxidized glutathione levels for complete interpretation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document critically analyzes current evidence on the use of neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and blood biomarkers to assess neuroplasticity in response to cardiovascular exercise (CE) in post-stroke individuals. It investigates how various CE interventions, including continuous and high-intensity interval training, modulate biomarkers like corticospinal excitability, brain activity and volume, and circulating growth factors. While many biomarkers respond to CE, often showing changes associated with functional recovery and normalization of excitability, the response is variable and not consistently linked to functional improvements. The review highlights significant methodological limitations, such as inadequate standardization of training parameters, small sample sizes, and inconsistent reporting of associations with functional outcomes, precluding objective quantification of CE's neuroplastic effects. It concludes that a consensus on optimal biomarkers for monitoring CE-induced neuroplasticity is currently lacking, emphasizing the need for more rigorous research to determine CE's reparative capabilities and guide its evidence-based implementation in stroke rehabilitation.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiovascular Exercise (CE), Conventional Exercise, Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill training, Stepping exercise, Cycling exercise, Upper-limb ergometry training, Multimodal Exercise Program. Non-invasive brain stimulation (anodal tDCS, intermittent theta burst stimulation) was also used as a priming agent in some contexts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The reviewed literature encompasses a wide range of acute and chronic CE interventions, with significant heterogeneity in intensity (light, moderate, vigorous), duration (single bouts from 5 to 30 minutes; chronic protocols from 4 weeks to 6 months), and type (e.g., treadmill, cycling, ergometry, walking HIIT). Comparisons were made between different intensities and exercise types, and against various control groups (e.g., resting, standard therapeutic activity, stretching). While some dose-response relationships were investigated (e.g., HIIT often evoked larger changes in corticospinal excitability than MICT, and moderate intensity walking promoted greater BDNF elevation than light intensity), overall, studies suffered from 'inadequate standardization of training parameters' and a 'lack of reporting of associations with functional outcomes'. Only 34% of studies utilized exercise tests for individualized workloads. This variability in methodology, combined with incomplete information regarding patient characteristics and the absence of consensus on optimal intervention parameters, makes it challenging to quantitatively compare results or establish clear dose-response relationships for neuroplasticity post-stroke. The optimal timing for CE introduction after stroke, and its precise dose-response relationship in modulating neuroplasticity, remain unclear.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Larger increases exhibited by the High-intensity Interval Training (HIIT) group during a graded exercise test, compared to Moderate-intensity Continuous Training (MICT), after 12 weeks of cycle ergometry.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cerebral blood flow, oxygenation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12 weeks of cycle ergometry (HIIT vs MICT) post-stroke.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests increased or more efficient brain oxygen utilization in response to HIIT, indicating potential neural adaptations.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational cohort study, conducted in a non-diabetic hypertensive population (N=14,393), investigated the prospective relationship between baseline and changing serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels and the risk of new-onset diabetes and impaired fasting glucose (IFG). The study found that higher serum ALP levels, both at baseline and with increasing levels over time, are significantly associated with an increased risk of new-onset diabetes and IFG. This association is particularly strong in individuals with lower total homocysteine (<10 µmol/L) or higher fasting glucose (≥5.9 mmol/L) levels.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antihypertensive treatment (Enalapril ± Folic Acid, or other antihypertensive drugs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily oral doses of 10 mg enalapril and 0.8 mg folic acid (single pill combination) or 10 mg enalapril only, as part of the primary study, and other antihypertensive medications were used. This study was an observational cohort analysis of biomarker associations, not an intervention to modify ALP. It investigated the relationship between baseline serum biomarker levels (ALP, tHcy, FG) and incident diabetes, including a dose-response evaluation for baseline ALP levels and changes in ALP levels over a median follow-up of 4.5 years. Specific thresholds for effect modifiers were identified as lower tHcy (< 10 µmol/L) and higher FG (≥ 5.9 mmol/L).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Participants with higher ALP levels had lower baseline tHcy levels. A stronger positive association between baseline ALP and new-onset diabetes was found in participants with tHcy < 10 µmol/L (per SD increment of ALP; adjusted OR, 1.24; 95% CI: 1.10, 1.40) compared to those with tHcy ≥ 10 µmol/L (adjusted OR, 1.03; 95% CI: 0.96, 1.10; P-interaction = 0.007). Lower tHcy levels (< 10 µmol/L) significantly strengthened the association between higher serum ALP and increased new-onset diabetes risk, while elevated tHcy levels may attenuate this positive relation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Total homocysteine is an amino acid derived from methionine metabolism. Elevated levels are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, and other metabolic disorders.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline total homocysteine levels in hypertensive patients, acting as a modifying factor for the association between serum ALP and new-onset diabetes risk.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower baseline tHcy levels (< 10 µmol/L) are associated with a stronger positive link between baseline ALP levels and the risk of new-onset diabetes. Optimal tHcy levels, in combination with ALP and FG, may be a better strategy for primary diabetes prevention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of aberrant N-glycosylation profiles of serum immunoglobulins (Igs) for urothelial carcinoma (UC), including bladder cancer (UCB) and upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). It identified five UC-associated aberrant N-glycan changes, notably the accumulation of asialo-bisecting GlcNAc type N-glycans in UC patients. A novel diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore), derived from a combination of these five N-glycans, demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (92.8% sensitivity, 97.2% specificity, AUC 0.969) for discriminating UC patients from healthy volunteers and prostate cancer patients, outperforming traditional diagnostic methods like urine cytology and hematuria. The dNGScore also showed utility in detecting urine cytology-negative cases and was associated with UCB invasiveness.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Biomarker Identification (N-glycomics analysis)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on diagnostic biomarker discovery, not therapeutic doses. High-throughput N-glycomics was used to quantify 32 types of N-glycan levels on serum immunoglobulins from 10-μL aliquots of purified Ig fractions. A diagnostic N-glycan Score (dNGScore) was established using a specific formula involving five N-glycans (m/z 1606, 1769, 2074, 2118, 2423) and a cut-off of -0.0955 points. No therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in urothelial carcinoma (UC) patients compared to healthy volunteer (HV) and prostate cancer (PC) patients.
