document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) on individual quadriceps muscle thickness and circulating biomarkers related to muscle atrophy and hypertrophy in the early postoperative phase. It found severe atrophy in the vastus intermedius (VI) and significant reductions in other quadriceps muscle thicknesses (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Medialis Obliquus). Circulating IGF-1 levels were significantly reduced, while myostatin levels showed a slight increase with a medium effect size, contributing to the observed muscle atrophy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) surgery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fourteen recreationally active patients (10 men, 4 women) with unilateral ACL injuries underwent reconstructive surgery. Measurements were taken at a preoperative visit (PRE) and at two postoperative visits (PO1: three days post-surgery; PO2: seven days post-surgery). No dose-response comparisons or variations in surgical method/intensity were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not exhibit any significant differences between the three time points. Showed decreases with small effect sizes at PO1 and PO2 compared with PRE, and a tendency to decrease within a week.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Cytokine closely related to myostatin; directly induces muscle atrophy and severely reduces muscle force generation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with muscle atrophy; observed tendency to decrease in the early phase might indicate complex or delayed roles after ACLR.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory, epigenetic, and molecular changes in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure (UEETF) and suspected endometriosis. It evaluated the predictive value of endometrial BCL6 and SIRT1, compared GnRH agonist treatment to controls, and conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing GnRH antagonist (elagolix) to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for two months. The findings characterized changes in inflammatory gene and miRNA expression in blood following treatments and suggested that medical suppression of suspected endometriosis could improve implantation success rates by addressing underlying inflammatory and epigenetic factors.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Medical suppression, including GnRH agonist, orally active GnRH antagonist (elagolix), and Oral Contraceptive Pills (OCPs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: GnRH agonist was administered for two months prior to embryo transfer and compared to a no-treatment control, showing significantly improved ongoing pregnancy/live birth rates (68.1% vs. 35.7%, p=0.02). In a pilot randomized controlled trial, elagolix (200 mg BID) and OCPs (Orthocyclin) were each administered for 2 months before embryo transfer. Elagolix treatment was associated with a trend toward higher pregnancy and live birth rates (100% pregnancy, 60% live birth) compared to OCPs (60% pregnancy, 20% ongoing/delivered), though statistical significance was not reached due to small numbers. Elagolix also dramatically altered the inflammatory milieu in blood compared to OCP suppression. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported within the treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased with OCP treatment (part of 3 DETs with p < 0.01)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Anti-inflammatory cytokine, plays a role in endometriosis pathogenesis, suppresses or promotes endometrial cancer depending on CD73 expression.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After OCP treatment in women with unexplained euploid embryo transfer failure and suspected endometriosis.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Plays a role in endometriosis pathogenesis; can suppress or promote endometrial cancer; observed increase after OCPs requires further investigation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates targeting RARA overexpression with tamibarotene, a selective RARα agonist, in combination with azacitidine in newly diagnosed unfit non-APL acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) patients. It demonstrates that RARA-positive patients respond significantly better to tamibarotene plus azacitidine, achieving high complete remission rates, rapid response onset, and improved survival. The study also explores RARA overexpression's association with monocytic features and its link to venetoclax resistance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Tamibarotene plus azacitidine combination therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: In a phase 2 clinical study (NCT02807558), azacitidine was administered at 75 mg/m2 (intravenously or subcutaneously) daily on days 1-7, followed by oral tamibarotene at 6 mg/m2 per day (divided doses twice daily) on days 8-28, with each treatment cycle lasting 28 days. This combination was evaluated in 51 newly diagnosed unfit AML patients (22 RARA-positive, 29 RARA-negative). The treatment was generally well tolerated, with myelosuppression rates comparable to azacitidine monotherapy. Hypertriglyceridemia was a frequent, manageable, and reversible high-grade nonhematologic adverse event. No dose-response comparisons were reported for tamibarotene plus azacitidine. For comparative context, azacitidine monotherapy showed similar complete remission rates in RARA-high and RARA-low patients, and venetoclax resistance was evaluated in ex vivo samples without specific dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Attained by 72% of RARA-positive patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Signifies improved bone marrow function and erythropoiesis, reducing the need for external blood product support.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Outcome following tamibarotene plus azacitidine treatment in newly diagnosed unfit RARA-positive AML patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Attainment of transfusion independence reflects significant hematologic improvement and enhanced quality of life for patients with RARA-positive AML.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive observational study utilized plasma proteomics and machine learning to develop and validate a framework for measuring organ-specific biological aging, termed 'e-ageotypes', in humans. Analyzing 4,778 proteins from 5,676 adults across five independent cohorts, the research revealed that accelerated aging in specific organs (including heart, brain, kidney, muscle, liver, adipose, pancreas, lung, and immune system) is significantly associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality and various age-related diseases, such as heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, diabetes, and cognitive decline. The study's methodology involved defining 'extreme agers' (individuals with highly accelerated organ aging), clustering them into distinct ageotypes, and identifying key protein biomarkers (e.g., REN, KL, NPPB, TNNT2, CPLX1/2) that contribute to these aging profiles and offer prognostic utility for disease risk and progression.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study on Biological Aging via Plasma Proteomics and Machine Learning
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study involved the quantification of approximately 4,778 plasma proteins using SomaScan assays (v.4 and v.4.1) in 5,676 adults from five independent cohorts. Machine learning models (LASSO regression-based chronological age predictors) were developed and validated to estimate biological (organ-specific) age, referred to as 'age gaps' or 'e-ageotypes', for 11 major organs (adipose tissue, artery, brain, heart, immune tissue, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, and pancreas) and the whole organism. Models were trained on 1,398 healthy participants from the Knight-ADRC cohort and tested across the full cohort. Age gaps were calculated using local regression, z-scored per model and cohort, and adjusted for age and sex. Associations with various age-related phenotypes, future mortality, heart disease, clinical biochemistry markers, and cognitive decline were assessed using linear models or Cox proportional hazards models, with multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method, 5% false discovery rate). No therapeutic intervention or dose comparison was performed.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study systematically investigated distinct host responses, cellular injury, and tissue damage in pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA) from 228 patients. It revealed unique molecular signatures distinguishing MIS-C from COVID-19, including increased multiorgan involvement and pyroptosis-related gene enrichment in MIS-C, alongside shared and distinct pro-inflammatory pathways. The analysis highlighted the complementary insights provided by cfRNA and wbRNA profiling, demonstrating varying biomarker trajectories, such as persistent immune dysregulation in COVID-19 compared to MIS-C resolution.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study characterizing and differentiating disease states of pediatric COVID-19 and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) through comprehensive molecular profiling.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study involved longitudinal analysis of 402 blood samples from 228 pediatric patients (MIS-C, COVID-19) and controls, utilizing next-generation sequencing of plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA), cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and whole-blood RNA (wbRNA). Samples were collected at acute, 1-month, and 3-month post-hospitalization time points. While some patients received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), it was not a tested intervention, and its administration was found not to significantly confound observed molecular differences. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were conducted or reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated a chemically defined, serum-free protocol for the in vitro transdifferentiation of pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells into functional hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) over five days. The research examined morphological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional changes, concluding that successful transdifferentiation, facilitated by extracellular matrix proteins like fibronectin or laminin, is independent of serum.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro pancreatic progenitor cell transdifferentiation to hepatocyte-like cells
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Clonal pancreatic progenitor AR42J-B13 cells were cultured for five days in a differentiation medium containing 100 nM Dexamethasone, 10 ng/ml Oncostatin M, 20 ng/ml HGF, 20 ng/ml FGF-2, 1% ITS+ (insulin, transferrin, selenous acid), 0.2% BSA, 4.4 mM nicotinamide, 1 µM copper sulphate, 30 µg/ml ascorbic acid, and 1 µg/ml heparin. Cells were grown on uncoated plastic, laminin-coated (2 µg/cm2), or fibronectin-coated (5 µg/cm2) substrata, with or without 5% FBS supplementation. The study primarily focused on the effectiveness of serum-free conditions facilitated by ECM proteins, rather than dose-response comparisons for individual components, finding no significant difference in transdifferentiation potential between fibronectin and laminin substrata.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Undifferentiated cells lacked expression. Strongly induced in 95.7 ± 1.5% of cells exposed to differentiation medium, with punctate cytoplasmic staining, confirming increased levels.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Confirms hepatocytic conversion at the protein level and a hepatocyte phenotype of transdifferentiated cells.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers to differentiate Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) from other biliary diseases in human patients. The findings indicated that methylation levels of OPCML and HOXD9 in serum cfDNA were significantly higher in CCA patients compared to those with other biliary diseases. The study concluded that OPCML and HOXD9, especially when combined, demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity, making them promising differential biomarkers for CCA, improving diagnostic accuracy and preventing misdiagnosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-based differential diagnosis using cfDNA methylation analysis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on evaluating serum cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation levels of OPCML, HOXA9, and HOXD9 as diagnostic biomarkers. Methylation levels were quantified using methylation-sensitive high-resolution melting (MS-HRM) assay on bisulfite-modified serum cfDNA (20 µL, <1 µg), with detection limits of 1.56% (lower) and 50% (upper). Their potency was evaluated using ROC curves. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons for treatment were reported, as this was a diagnostic study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Sensitivity of 76.8% and specificity of 93.8% (as reported by Liu et al. [53]).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: General protein, investigated as a potential biomarker for CCA in previous studies.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis between CCA and benign hepatobiliary diseases (as reported by Liu et al. [53]).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential diagnostic biomarker for CCA as reported by previous studies.

document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduction observed in AD subjects, further validated in MCI and AD subjects using Western blot analysis.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) subjects.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Novel protein biomarker candidate for AD, associated with AD pathogenesis.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study developed and validated a multilayer perceptron (MLP) machine learning model for the early postnatal differential diagnosis of choledochal cysts (CC) and cystic biliary atresia (CBA). The model utilized routinely available clinical parameters, including biochemical markers (Total bile acid, Total bilirubin, γ-glutamyl transferase, Aspartate aminotransferase, Alanine aminotransferase, Direct bilirubin, and Taurodeoxycholate) and ultrasonographic measurements (Longitudinal and Transverse diameters of cysts), from a retrospective cohort of 319 patients. The MLP model achieved high diagnostic performance (95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and AUC of 0.990 for differentiating CBA from CC), aiming to facilitate timely surgical intervention for CBA and improve patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic Model Development (Machine Learning)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This retrospective study involved the analysis of clinical features from 319 patients (< 60 days old at surgery) with hepatic hilar cysts (274 CC, 45 CBA) treated between 2011 and 2022. It focused on developing a diagnostic model rather than a therapeutic intervention. Biochemical markers and ultrasonographic measurements were compared, and key diagnostic features were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Eleven machine learning models were developed and compared, with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) model showing optimal performance: 95.8% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 96.3% specificity, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.990. The model utilized seven routine clinical parameters (GGT, TBA, DBIL, TBIL, ALT, LDC, and TDC) as input variables. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the feasibility and biological correlations of simultaneously quantifying perfusion, permeability, and novel contrast leakage effects in brain gliomas using dynamic spin-and-gradient-echo echoplanar imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) with a single contrast injection. The research detailed the methodology for acquiring and processing MRI data from 38 adult-type diffuse glioma patients, focusing on parameters like TRATE, ΔR2,ss*, ΔR1,ss, ADC, nrCBV, PSR, Ktrans, and ve. Key findings demonstrate that dynamic SAGE-EPI enables the simultaneous assessment of these parameters, providing new metrics that correlate with previous treatment exposure, IDH status, and Ki67 expression, offering advantages like shorter scan times and reduced contrast agent use, and revealing distinct differences in contrast agent dynamics and tissue properties between treatment-naïve and recurrent gliomas, as well as between IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype tumors. Specifically, ΔR1,ss shows potential as a quantitative biomarker for blood-brain barrier breakdown, and TRATE captures unique cytoarchitectural information dependent on cell volume fraction and cell size.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dynamic Spin-and-Gradient-Echo Echoplanar Imaging (dynamic SAGE-EPI) for diagnostic imaging of brain gliomas, sometimes in the context of previous cancer treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single bolus of Gadavist (Gadobutrol) contrast agent was administered at approximately 0.1 mL/kg (rate ~4 mL/s) for the dynamic SAGE-EPI. This imaging technique reduces scanning time (~3 min) and contrast dose compared to traditional separate acquisitions for perfusion and permeability imaging. The study also analyzed the effects of previous, unspecified cancer treatments (e.g., radiation, chemoradiation) on imaging metrics, but no specific dose or duration details for these prior treatments were reported, nor were any dose-response comparisons for imaging parameters.

matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: MRI metric (Transverse Relaxivity at Tracer Equilibrium), a quantitative biomarker reflecting T2*-leakage effects normalized to estimated contrast agent concentration.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varies (higher in TN-IDH wt, lower with previous treatment)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower TRATE (p = 0.002) observed in IDH wild-type gliomas with previous treatment exposure. TRATE values above 142 mM−1 s−1 were exclusively seen in treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas. It was significantly higher in treatment-naïve IDH wild-type gliomas compared to recurrent IDH wild-type gliomas (p=0.002). TRATE strongly correlated with ΔR2,ss* in TN-gliomas (p=0.004, r=+0.71) and moderately in R-gliomas (p=0.02, r=+0.46). It moderately correlated with ΔR1,ss in R-gliomas (p=0.04, r=−0.42) but not in TN-gliomas (p=0.32). In TN-gliomas, it correlated with ADC (p=0.04, r=−0.54) and nrCBV (p=0.02, r=+0.60). TRATE strongly inversely correlated with PSR in both TN (p<0.0001, r=−0.87) and R (p=0.0003, r=−0.68) gliomas. There was a trend towards higher TRATE in TN-IDH wt than TN-IDH m (p=0.13), and it was higher in TN-gliomas with high Ki67 expression (p=0.04). TRATE > 142 mM−1 s−1 predicted high Ki67 (>10%) with AUC = 0.84, sensitivity = 89%, and specificity = 80%. Its value also varies depending on cell volume fraction and cell size.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels were among the top positive correlates to obesity/overweight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the lipid metabolic profile and its correlation with immune/cytokine indexes in COVID-19 patients to predict disease progression, severity, and clinical outcomes. It identified several differential lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) 20:0, as potential biomarkers for discriminating between mild/severe disease, acute/recovery stages, and survival/fatal outcomes, suggesting their role in immune/inflammatory responses and as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational case-control study analyzing lipid profiles and immune/cytokine indexes in 44 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients (16 mild, 28 severe). measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in severe patients compared to mild patients, and significantly higher in fatal patients compared to survival patients. Upregulation was observed especially in those in the acute stage and with fatal outcome. A significant correlation was observed between the decrease in TAGs and the increase in cytotoxic T-cell count, suggesting harmful effects of TAGs reduction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels of these intermediates increased post-prolonged exercise (PE) and remained elevated post-time trial (TT), indicating active aerobic respiration. However, no significant differences were observed between the FOPS and control groups at any time point.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Key components of the central metabolic pathway for aerobic energy production (cellular respiration); lactate is a product of anaerobic glycolysis.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: During and after prolonged exercise and time trial periods, with and without FOPS supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased levels suggest enhanced metabolic flux through the TCA cycle due to exercise. The lack of differential effect with FOPS implies that oligopeptide supplementation did not directly alter the overall concentration or flux of these specific intermediates, suggesting its influence on lipid metabolism might occur upstream or via alternative compensatory mechanisms.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the association between different physical activity (PA) patterns and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index in US adults, using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007-2018. The main findings indicate that regularly active individuals experience a substantial and significant reduction in the TyG index, offering sustained metabolic benefits. While weekend warriors and insufficiently active individuals show some improvement compared to inactive counterparts, they do not achieve comparable benefits to those who are regularly active. The association between PA and the TyG index in the regularly active group was more pronounced in males, individuals with higher education levels, and those without diabetes. A significant, non-linear, and negative relationship between weekly total PA and the TyG index was observed in non-inactive individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Physical Activity (PA) patterns and Sedentary time
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physical activity was assessed via a questionnaire covering frequency and duration (minimum 10 uninterrupted minutes) of vigorous and moderate pursuits during a typical week. An aggregate PA score was computed (2 * vigorous PA + moderate PA). Participants were categorized into four groups: inactive (no PA), insufficiently active (< 150 min/week overall PA), weekend warriors (WWs, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in 1 or 2 sessions), and regularly active (RA, ≥ 150 min/week overall PA in > 2 sessions). Total MVPA levels were approximately 120 min for insufficiently active, 290 min for WWs, and 540 min for RA. Comparisons between these patterns showed that even PA not meeting recommended standards was associated with a lower TyG index compared to inactivity. The study also explored significant, non-linear relationships between weekly total PA and the TyG index in non-inactive individuals, and between weekly sedentary time and the TyG index across various groups. No direct dose-response comparisons for specific PA amounts beyond pattern categorization were reported within this study's primary findings.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Calculated from blood parameters (fasting triglycerides and fasting glucose)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Calculated index (formula: ln(fasting triglycerides × fasting glucose / 2) where components are in mg/dl)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (compared to inactive); higher (for weekend warriors compared to regularly active)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Compared to inactive adults, TyG indices were lower in insufficiently active (β = −0.05, P = 0.3524), weekend warriors (WWs) (β = −0.01, P = 0.9129), and regularly active (RA) adults (β = −0.110, P < 0.0001). However, when regularly active adults were the reference, WWs showed a significant TyG index increase (β = 0.11, P < 0.0001). A significant, non-linear, and negative relationship between weekly total PA and TyG index was determined in non-inactive (P for overall < 0.001, P for nonlinearity = 0.054) and regularly active (P for overall < 0.001, P for nonlinearity = 0.118) individuals, showing a gradual decreased trend with increased PA. The association was modified by diabetes, education, and gender (all P interaction < 0.05). Sedentary time also had a significant and non-linear association with TyG index across various groups (all P for overall < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A surrogate biomarker for insulin resistance and metabolic health, reflecting glucose and lipid metabolism, calculated from fasting triglycerides and fasting glucose levels. It also serves as a biomarker for the onset, progression, and prognosis of various metabolic diseases including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, sarcopenia, and malignancies.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Different patterns of physical activity (inactive, insufficiently active, weekend warriors, regularly active) and weekly sedentary time in US adults, analyzed using NHANES data (2007–2018).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: A reliable indicator for metabolic health, insulin resistance, and risk for developing diabetes, cardiovascular disease (CVD), stroke, depression, and sleep disorders. A lower TyG index indicates enhanced insulin sensitivity, better metabolic health, and reduced disease risk/improved prognosis. Regular physical activity provides sustained and significant benefits in controlling the TyG index, offering a positive impact on metabolic health.
