document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated serum levels of various biomarkers, including matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), cytokines (SDF-1α, SCGF-β, SCF-1, G-CSF, MCP-1), hormones (leptin, ghrelin), and liver enzymes (ALT, AST, γ-GTP), in patients with histologically proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The aim was to determine if these biomarkers reflect disease activity, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis progression across early and advanced NASH stages. The study also evaluated the impact of pharmacological interventions, specifically pioglitazone and ezetimibe, and lifestyle modifications on these biomarkers and the clinical course of NASH. Key findings identified serum MMP-1 as significantly higher in early-stage NASH (stage 1 fibrosis) and reflective of disease activity, while SDF-1α strongly correlated with fibrosis, steatosis, and inflammation across various stages. Pioglitazone treatment was observed to improve histological features and modulate biomarker levels, decreasing MMP-1 and increasing SDF-1α.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) disease progression and correlation with biomarkers, supplemented by pharmacological interventions and lifestyle modifications.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved both observational components, comparing serum biomarker levels in patients with histologically proven early (n=24) and advanced (n=9) NASH against healthy controls (n=14), with subgroup analysis based on histological characteristics. Pharmacological interventions included pioglitazone, administered at 15 mg daily for durations ranging from over two months to two or more years, and in some cases for 14 months concurrently with ezetimibe. Ezetimibe was also administered alone for 10 months. Other unspecified lipid-lowering and anti-diabetic agents, along with diet and physical activity, were also utilized. While changes before and after treatment were observed, comprehensive dose-response comparisons were not consistently reported, focusing more on the outcomes of specific treatment regimens.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased after ezetimibe treatment. Changing levels were not consistent with serum MMP-1 levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Form of fat stored in the body; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After ezetimibe treatment, metabolic syndrome patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates lipid profile; decreased levels suggest improved lipid management. Inconsistent correlation with MMP-1 suggests complex interplay with disease activity.

document_context_data.document_summary: This longitudinal study investigated the dynamic changes of large-scale within- and between-network functional connectivity in chemotherapy-treated breast cancer patients using resting state functional MRI. It also examined changes in cognitive function (attention, executive function, memory, visual ability, fine motor skills, reaction), psychological scores (anxiety, depression), and various blood biochemical markers (Estradiol, prolactin, FSH, LH, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin). The study compared patients before, one week after, and six months after completing chemotherapy to healthy controls. Key findings revealed widespread chemotherapy-induced abnormalities in resting state networks, which partly recovered by six months post-chemotherapy. These altered functional connectivities were correlated with cognitive assessment scores and blood biochemical indexes, suggesting RSNs as potential biomarkers for chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and for guiding rehabilitation. Baseline analyses also showed higher metabolic markers and psychological/cognitive scores in patients compared to controls, along with a high incidence of chemotherapy-induced amenorrhea.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (for breast cancer patients, some also received endocrine therapy)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Postoperative chemotherapy was administered to breast cancer patients, typically in six to eight courses. While specific drug names or dosages were not detailed, follow-up assessments were consistently conducted before (baseline), one week after completing, and six months after completing chemotherapy. Some patients (35.3%) also received endocrine therapy after chemotherapy, but no concurrent radiotherapy or endocrine therapy was given during chemotherapy. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the breast cancer group than in the healthy control group at baseline (P < 0.05). Significantly increased from baseline (t0) to one week post-chemotherapy (t1, P = 0.041), and decreased at six months post-chemotherapy (t2) without statistical significance. Decreased lipid levels were observed six months later, but the levels were still in the abnormal range compared to the Healthy Control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary form of fat storage in the body, serving as an energy source; high levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Baseline assessment and post-chemotherapy changes in breast cancer patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic health and cardiovascular risk. Elevated baseline levels are associated with breast cancer. Post-chemotherapy fluctuations are noted; lower lipid levels are speculated to positively impact cognitive improvement.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated whether painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (pDPN) influences nerve regeneration in type 2 diabetes patients undergoing intensive glycemic control with exenatide, pioglitazone, or basal-bolus insulin over a 1-year follow-up. It concluded that intensive glycemic control is associated with greater corneal nerve regeneration and an improvement in neuropathic pain severity, particularly in patients with pDPN.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Intensive glycemic control (exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received either exenatide and pioglitazone or basal-bolus insulin treatment over a 1-year follow-up period, aiming to achieve and maintain an HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). This intervention led to a significant mean HbA1c reduction (2.5% in pDPN and 3.4% in non-pDPN groups). Specific drug dosages were not detailed, and no dose-response comparisons were reported for the primary intervention. The change in Corneal Confocal Microscopy (CCM) measures was not associated with the type of treatment (P = 0.47).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varied (decreased in non-pDPN, unchanged in pDPN)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No change in pDPN group (P = 0.26); significant decrease in without pDPN group (P < 0.01); change was comparable between groups (P = 0.72).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major form of fat stored in the body, primarily used for energy.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 1-year follow-up after intensive glycemic control therapy for type 2 diabetes.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Shows an improvement in metabolic health (lower triglyceride) in the group without pDPN, but not in the pDPN group.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated LRP1 expression, circulating soluble LRP1 (sLRP1) levels, and myocardial lipid content in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (IDCM) patients compared to healthy controls, and assessed the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in sLRP1 secretion. Key findings include increased circulating sLRP1, higher myocardial collagen and triglyceride content, and elevated LRP1 alpha chain expression in myocardial vessels of IDCM patients, with sLRP1 release found to be independent of the exosome pathway and not associated with blood lipid parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating disease pathogenesis and biomarker identification in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Observational and diagnostic study comparing IDCM patients (n=20 for plasma, n=9 for tissue) with age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=15 for plasma, n=5 for tissue). Myocardial tissue samples were from explanted hearts. The study also included a comparison of hypercholesterolemic and normocholesterolemic patients. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TG content significantly increased in patients compared to controls (P = 0.026); higher in myocardium from IDCM patients than control subjects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage, involved in energy metabolism; lipid storage, energy metabolism, component of myocardial filaments.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered lipid metabolism or accumulation in the myocardium in IDCM. Characteristic hallmark of IDCM, indicative of metabolic dysfunctions including altered fatty acid uptake and oxidation in failing hearts.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study is a multidisciplinary randomized trial investigating the feasibility and effects of a Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT) for secondary prevention in 90 physically inactive patients with stable coronary heart disease. It compares PMT with a single session of exercise training advice (EX) and treatment as usual (TAU). The primary outcome is the change in individual anaerobic threshold, with secondary endpoints including endothelial function, biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress, and various psychological measures. The study hypothesizes that PMT will lead to greater improvements in physical fitness than EX and TAU, and EX will be superior to TAU, particularly benefiting patients with mental or psychosocial distress.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Psychodynamic Motivation and Training program (PMT), individualized advice in exercise training (EX), and treatment as usual (TAU) for lifestyle modification and psychological support in patients with coronary heart disease.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study randomizes 90 patients into three groups (n=30 each) over a six-month follow-up. Treatment as Usual (TAU) involves standard recommendations. Exercise Training (EX) consists of one session of individualized exercise advice (ACSM/AHA guidelines, individualized heart rate zones) aiming for 300 minutes moderate or 150 minutes vigorous training/week. The Psychodynamic Motivation and Training (PMT) program includes 2-8 sessions of individual psychodynamic psychotherapy (max 400 minutes/patient over six months), tailored to individual needs, in addition to the EX advice, also aiming for 300/150 minutes training/week. Home-based exercise training is unsupervised. The study aims to explore optimal dosage but no formal dose-response comparisons between interventions are reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not reported in this document chunk. Intended to measure change.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported in this document chunk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Lipid metabolism, energy storage, cardiovascular risk factor.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Medical risk factor control, general health monitoring in patients with stable coronary heart disease.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study was an observational, cross-sectional comparison involving 28 male collegiate athletes (including weight-lifting and basketball teams) who reported engaging in strength training for at least one hour per day, five times per week, versus 29 age-matched untrained controls. No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in myostatin transgenic mice; higher in diabetic patients with lower myostatin.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not specifically quantified beyond 'lower' or 'higher'.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Energy storage, lipid metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Myostatin transgenic mice; diabetic patients with lower myostatin levels.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower TG in myostatin transgenic mice due to immature adipogenesis; high TG associated with lower myostatin in diabetic patients indicates metabolic dysregulation and metabolic syndrome risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Fat utilization during exercise reduces resting levels of triglycerides (59)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Component of lipid profiles, involved in cardiovascular health
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fat utilization during exercise
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved cardiovascular health profiles

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex causal relationships and genetic basis among Acanthosis nigricans (AN), obesity (BMI), and insulin resistance (IR) in a cohort of 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children (aged 6-17 years) from 401 nuclear families. Using variance components and mediation analysis, the research aimed to determine how AN correlates with various cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and whether IR or obesity primarily drives the association. The key finding is that obesity largely explains the observed association between IR and AN, with no direct causal relationship found between IR and AN when obesity is accounted for, highlighting AN's utility as a non-invasive clinical marker for obesity-driven cardiometabolic risk and its ability to predict future Type 2 Diabetes risk.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating cardiometabolic risk factors and a diagnostic marker
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study with no therapeutic intervention or dose administered. Data was collected from 670 non-diabetic Mexican American children aged 6–17 years from a family-based cohort, focusing on associations and the utility of Acanthosis Nigricans as a screening tool for cardiometabolic risk factors, including extensive clinical tests and interviews on medical history, demographic, phenotypic, and environmental variables.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: BMI through IR had remarkable environmental effects on lipid concentrations. The environmental partial mediation model showed a small mediation effect of HOMA-IR on triglycerides. BMI had a partial effect on lipids. Positive for both BMI and ISI (Insulin Sensitivity Index) variables; maintained on squared when attenuated by BMI.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential for energy storage, structural components of cell membranes, and signaling molecules. Dyslipidemia contributes to cardiometabolic risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Mexican American children; association with AN, BMI, and IR.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal levels (dyslipidemia) indicate increased cardiometabolic risk. The study suggests that BMI, both directly and partially mediated by IR, influences lipid profiles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the association of circulating Advanced Glycation End-products (AGEs) and soluble RAGE (sRAGE) isoforms (cRAGE, esRAGE) and their ratios with 15-year all-cause mortality and cardiovascular complications (MACE) in type 2 diabetes patients. It explored baseline demographic and biochemical characteristics, including AGEs and sRAGE isoforms, in type 2 diabetes patients compared to healthy controls, and examined their associations with diabetic complications, aging, and metabolic parameters. The study found increased circulating AGEs and sRAGE (specifically cRAGE) in type 2 diabetes, with the AGEs/cRAGE ratio predicting all-cause mortality and sRAGE associated with MACE development. A nomogram for long-term survival probability prediction, based on age, sex, HbA1c, SBP, and the AGEs/cRAGE ratio, was developed and internally validated.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and prognostic assessment study of circulating biomarkers.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A retrospective cohort study with a 15-year follow-up, investigating baseline circulating levels of AGEs and soluble RAGE isoforms in 362 type 2 diabetes patients and 125 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly increased in patients with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Major form of fat storage; indicator of lipid metabolism and cardiovascular risk
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with Type 2 Diabetes

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional observational study aimed to assess cognitive impairment and oxidative stress markers in vitamin D insufficient elderly patients, both with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The study found that cognitive impairment is more predominant in individuals with diabetes. While no overall significant relationship was established between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress, a significant association was found between GPx levels and 3MSE cognitive scores, and a significant negative correlation between fasting blood sugar (FBS) and 3MS scores, specifically in vitamin D insufficient non-diabetic individuals.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-Sectional Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study without any therapeutic intervention. Participants were categorized based on their existing health status: diabetic vs. non-diabetic (based on medical history and HbA1c levels), and serum vitamin D levels were used to classify them as vitamin D insufficient (< 29 ng/mL) vs. vitamin D sufficient (>= 30 ng/mL). Cognitive function was assessed using the modified Mini Mental Status Examination (3MS test score < 80 out of 100 indicating impairment). No dose-response comparisons or interventions were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Statistically significant difference (P < 0.05) between non-diabetic and diabetic groups. Specific quantitative values for changes were not reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage in the body, used for energy, and a major form of energy transport.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cross-sectional study investigating associations between T2DM, vitamin D deficiency, cognitive impairment, and oxidative stress; comparison between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and metabolic disorders like T2DM and metabolic syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Promoted the reduction of exercise-induced elevations and significantly decreased in both sexes (more pronounced in men) compared to control groups.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Energy storage, component of blood lipids, linked to metabolic status.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exercise-induced metabolic response following soy protein consumption; general soy protein supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Improved metabolic status, reduced metabolic stress during exercise, and improved cardiovascular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated everolimus (an mTORC1 inhibitor) as a treatment for progressive NF2-related vestibular schwannomas (VS), evaluating its impact on tumor volume, growth rate, hearing outcomes, and quality of life over 52 weeks. The findings indicate that 3-month volumetric imaging can serve as an early biomarker to predict long-term sensitivity to everolimus, which demonstrated a cytostatic effect by decreasing VS growth rates, stabilizing tumors, and improving time to progression, while generally maintaining hearing and quality of life, despite not achieving significant tumor shrinkage in all cases.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Everolimus (mTORC1 inhibitor), with some cases also involving Bevacizumab as a subsequent or alternative treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral everolimus was administered daily for 52 weeks (12 months) to NF2 patients with progressive VS. Adult participants (18+) received 10 mg/day, and adolescents (16-17) received 3 mg/day. Doses could be reduced (e.g., to 5 mg/day for adults) due to toxicity, such as grade 3+ or grade 2 oral ulcers. While no formal dose-response comparisons were reported, the treatment period was continuous for 52 weeks, with some patients re-challenged with everolimus after discontinuation, and others receiving bevacizumab if everolimus failed to control growth.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Severe grade 4 elevated

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involvement in lipid metabolism and energy storage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Everolimus treatment (adverse event in participant 10).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a severe metabolic adverse event associated with everolimus treatment, requiring medical intervention (statin therapy).

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review aimed to critically examine the effects of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and a range of circulating health biomarkers in highly trained athletes, drawing from randomized controlled trials. The review concluded that melatonin supplementation is safe and demonstrates benefits in improving antioxidant status, reducing inflammatory responses, and reversing exercise-induced liver and muscle damage. Moderate modulating effects were observed on glycemia, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and creatinine. While promising data suggest potential benefits for hematological biomarkers and hormonal responses, the direct efficiency of melatonin in improving sports performance needs further assessment; however, indirect benefits via health biomarker improvements are suggested. Melatonin was also found to counteract oxidative stress, modulate immune function, and show hepatoprotective and renoprotective properties after intense exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Melatonin Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Melatonin supplementation was investigated with doses ranging from 5 mg to 100 mg, administered acutely (1 day) or continuously for 3 to 30 days. Timing varied from 15-60 minutes before exercise to 2 hours post-exercise, 6 days post-training, 3 days before exercise, or before rest/sleep. Specific dose-response observations were mixed; for instance, 5 mg melatonin showed modest strength improvements, while 8 mg led to significant decreases, and 10 mg improved jumping performance. High heterogeneity in dosages prevented a complete meta-analysis and the establishment of a single efficient dose, though 8 mg melatonin was noted to cause significant harmful effects on strength and power compared to 5 mg and control.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decreases (p < 0.05) reported in the melatonin group, with moderate overall modulating effects.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: The main form of fat in the body, used for energy or stored as body fat; high levels associated with cardiovascular risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Melatonin supplementation in highly trained athletes to improve lipid profile.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of cardiovascular health and lipid metabolism, which influences energy reserves and overall metabolic efficiency by improving lipid profile.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review systematically evaluates the application of systems biology-driven precision sports nutrition, incorporating 'omics' platforms (e.g., nutrigenetics, metabolomics, metagenomics, proteomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, multi-omics) and wearable technologies, particularly Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM), for endurance athletes. It maps existing literature, summarizes key findings, identifies research gaps, and investigates the impact of various nutritional interventions (e.g., polyphenols, astaxanthin, nitrates, carbohydrate-protein blends, probiotics) on immune function, inflammation, metabolism, gut microbiome composition, and glycemic responses during and after exercise. The review concludes that while these technologies offer insights into individual variability and physiological responses, current evidence is often insufficient to robustly link identified biomarkers to enhanced performance, recovery, and long-term health outcomes, noting methodological limitations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This scoping review investigates precision sports nutrition strategies for endurance athletes, focusing on systems biology approaches (including various 'omics' platforms and wearable technologies like Continuous Glucose Monitoring) and a wide range of nutritional interventions. These interventions include specific foods (e.g., banana, blueberry, mango), supplements (e.g., soy protein, astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, prebiotics, probiotics, cocoa flavanols), macronutrient manipulations (e.g., carbohydrate-protein blends, oligopeptides, specific protein amounts, dietary fat, low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, low/high FODMAP diets), and their interactions with diverse exercise regimens (e.g., cycling trials, marathons, ultra-endurance events, submaximal and prolonged exercise, exercise under heat stress).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review synthesizes findings from various studies on nutritional interventions, which include specific food consumptions (e.g., banana, mango) often compared against controls or other carbohydrate sources, and supplementations (e.g., astaxanthin, beet-based nitrates, cranberry beverage, specific probiotics) with durations ranging from acute intake to 2-week periods. It also examines the effects of different macronutrient strategies (e.g., low-carbohydrate high-fat diets, carbohydrate-protein blends) and genetic variations on caffeine metabolism. The review notes that while specific interventions are detailed, it generally reports on rather than conducts dose-response comparisons, highlighting that existing studies often compare interventions against controls. A key emphasis is on the need for tailored, individual-specific strategies, robust randomized controlled trials, and better reporting of training status, dose-response relationships, and demographic stratifications in future research, as current evidence often lacks detailed dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: reductions

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of fat found in the blood, serving as an energy source and storage molecule
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 supplementation
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reductions suggest improved cardiovascular health.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study conducted a secondary analysis of data from the European First-Episode Schizophrenia Trial (EUFEST) and Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP) trials. It utilized machine learning models (support vector regressors and classifiers) to predict depressive symptom trajectories (changes in CDSS scores) and the occurrence of post-psychotic depressive episodes (PPD) at 6 and 12 months in first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The models leveraged various baseline variables including sociodemographic information, clinical assessments (e.g., PANSS, CDSS scores), neurocognitive performance, quality of life, and blood-based biomarkers, demonstrating accurate prediction and geographical generalizability across populations. The study also analyzed how factors like treatment assignment (e.g., NAVIGATE program) and antidepressant prescription influenced model misclassification and patient outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Antipsychotic medication, NAVIGATE program (psychosocial intervention), Antidepressant coadministration, and Usual community care.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants in the EUFEST trial received 1 year of antipsychotic treatment (described as "minimally antipsychotic-treated"), while RAISE-ETP participants were allocated to either usual community care or the NAVIGATE program. Antidepressant prescriptions were observed, with RAISE-ETP patients showing a higher rate (33.33%) compared to EUFEST (2.18%). The NAVIGATE program was associated with a sharper decline in depressive symptoms, especially among patients prescribed antidepressants at baseline. However, no specific doses, intensities, or durations for antipsychotics, the NAVIGATE program, or antidepressants were detailed, nor were dose-response comparisons reported for any treatment; their influence on predictive model performance and patient characteristics was primarily analyzed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Not specified as a direct change; its baseline level served as a consistently selected key predictor in predictive models.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently selected as a harmonized feature and predictor in models across both EUFEST and RAISE-ETP datasets for depressive symptoms and episodes with feature selection probability > 0.5 and cross-validated ratio (CVR) ±3. Its exclusion increased model bias, suggesting its importance for unbiased detection of symptom changes. Specific quantitative baseline levels were not provided in this excerpt.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage in the body, providing energy; associated with affective symptoms and metabolic dysfunction; high levels can be a risk factor for heart disease.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Used as a baseline blood-based biomarker in secondary analysis of EUFEST and RAISE-ETP trials, collected from patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, and consistently identified as a key predictor in machine learning models for depressive symptoms and episodes in First-Episode Psychosis (FEP) patients, validated across both EUFEST and RAISE-ETP samples.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic and cardiovascular health; used as a variable to evaluate its contribution to predicting depressive symptoms or post-psychotic depressive episodes in schizophrenia-spectrum disorder patients; a valuable biomarker for predicting and managing depressive symptoms in FEP patients, helping to ensure unbiased detection of symptom changes. Associated with immuno-metabolic dysfunction and metabolic comorbidity in psychiatric disorders.

document_context_data.document_summary: This retrospective single-center cohort study investigated sex-specific long-term alterations in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers among 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors (PCR-confirmed, symptomatic, at least two vaccine doses) over a 30-month follow-up period. The study revealed distinct physiological recovery patterns, with males exhibiting earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations and females showing more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, underscoring the need for sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Longitudinal observational study on post-COVID-19 recovery in vaccinated individuals
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study included 426 adults with PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 who received at least two doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines (mRNA BNT162b2 or inactivated CoronaVac). Participants recovered from moderate COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization but not ICU admission. Serial assessments were conducted at baseline, 18-, 24-, and 30-month post-infection. No specific therapeutic intervention doses or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on long-term physiological changes after vaccination and infection, not vaccine efficacy or specific therapeutic effects.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: fluctuated; initial higher levels in males, then decline; sustained increase in females by 30 months
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall, levels fluctuated without significant within-group variation (p = 0.5726). Males had significantly higher baseline levels (p = 0.0264) which gradually declined, while females showed a sustained and progressive increase by the 30-month (T3) timepoint. Modest positive correlations with glucose were observed in both sexes (females: r=0.23, p=0.001; males: r=0.20, p=0.021).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Involved in lipid metabolism and energy storage; main form of fat storage in the body.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Longitudinal assessment over 30 months in vaccinated COVID-19 survivors.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the stability or alterations in lipid metabolism post-COVID-19, suggesting differential metabolic recovery or lingering inflammatory responses between sexes. May reflect shared metabolic pathways such as insulin resistance.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study utilized discovery metabolomics and lipidomics to investigate plasma glycosphingolipids and other lipid metabolites as potential biomarkers for distinguishing aggressive from indolent prostate cancer (PCa) in treatment-naïve African-American and European-American men. The findings indicate that specific glycosphingolipid species, particularly trihexosylceramide and tetrahexosylceramide, along with other sphingolipids and triglycerides, are significantly associated with PCa aggressiveness. A five-sphingolipid signature demonstrated promising diagnostic accuracy comparable to or exceeding PSA, suggesting their utility as novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and highlighting their role in related metabolic networks and genetic alterations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery via metabolomics and lipidomics
treatment_details.dose_specificity: An observational study conducted on plasma samples from 159 men with treatment-naïve prostate cancer, utilizing ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). The study focused on identifying biomarkers for PCa aggressiveness (Grade Group 1 vs. Grade Groups 2-5, low vs. intermediate/high aggressive PCa), without administering or comparing any therapeutic interventions or doses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated in intermediate/high aggressive PCa patients.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary form of fat storage in the body, essential for energy and metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Prostate Cancer (PCa) aggressiveness (low vs. intermediate-high aggressiveness).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with PCa aggressiveness.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study investigated the effects of a 6-week dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination (including magnesium, potassium, B vitamins, and Coenzyme Q10) as an add-on therapy for patients with cardiac arrhythmias, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndrome components. The intervention significantly improved cardiometabolic health by reducing insulin resistance (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), improving left ventricular systolic (LVEF) and diastolic function (LV mass index, interventricular septal thickness, E/A ratio), reducing heart rate, and lowering inflammation (CrP). While beneficial effects were observed for glucose and lipid metabolism markers, premature beats and BMI remained largely unchanged.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary intervention with a specific micronutrient combination as an add-on to concomitant cardiovascular drug treatment.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dietary intervention involving 54 patients. The verum group received a specific micronutrient combination (2 tablets twice daily), including 145.8 mg magnesium, 469.2 mg potassium, 3.0 µg Vitamin B12, 400.0 µg folic acid, 48.0 mg niacin, and 60.0 mg coenzyme Q10. Other micronutrients like Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and Selenium were also part of the combination. The placebo group received microcrystalline cellulose. No dose-response comparisons were reported. Minor gastric pain was noted in one verum and one placebo patient, with no serious side effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in the verum group (p = 0.011, ES = 0.292, Q1;Q3: -0.01;0.30). Folic acid supplementation was associated with a reduction, while CoQ10 supplementation showed no positive influence on TG.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage in the body, serving as an energy source; elevated levels are a cardiovascular risk factor.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: After 6 weeks of dietary intervention in the verum group; folic acid supplementation in patients with T2DM; CoQ10 supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased levels can indicate a heightened cardiovascular risk, potentially counteracting other positive metabolic effects. Reduction with folic acid suggests improved lipid profile.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the changes in blood biochemical and hematological parameters and physical fitness outcomes in professional male soccer players following a pre-season (PS) training phase. It also analyzed the associations between these blood markers and various physical fitness measures, including sprint performance, VAMEVAL, and Countermovement Jump (CMJ) tests. Key findings revealed significant increases in platelets, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, C-reactive protein, cortisol, and testosterone, as well as significant decreases in albumin and corrected calcium after the PS phase. Overall physical fitness measures improved, and several blood biomarkers showed moderate to large correlations with specific physical performance indicators.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Professional soccer pre-season (PS) training and specific physical fitness testing
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study involved 25 professional male soccer players (28.1 
D7 4.6 years old) undergoing a regular pre-season training phase (June to October 2019) characterized by high training loads in both soccer practice and strength training, described as "intense physical exercise" and "intensification of training demands." Biological markers were assessed at baseline (June 02, 2019) and post-PS (September 19, 2019), following a 48-hour rest, with an additional acute exercise component 12 hours prior to the second blood draw. Physical fitness was assessed using standardized tests: VAMEVAL (incremental running to exhaustion), 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test (30-seconds intense running interspersed by 15-seconds rest until failure), linear sprints (5m, 10m, 15m, 20m split times), and Countermovement Jump (CMJ with hands on hips and free hands). No specific dose-response comparisons for the training or physical tests were reported as these were standardized maximal efforts.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A type of fat (lipid) found in blood; major form of fat stored by the body, serving as an energy reserve.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Pre-Season (PS) training phase in professional soccer players, assessed at baseline and post-PS.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not reported in this study, but generally indicates metabolic health and energy status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated sex-specific differences in oxi-inflammatory responses, body composition, and cardiovascular health in older adults. It aimed to assess the usefulness of serum oxi-inflammatory markers for vascular disease prediction and prevention, revealing that postmenopausal women exhibit elevated production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) leading to increased oxidative stress (oxLDLs, 3-NitroT) but also enhanced endothelial regeneration (EPCs, HMGB1). The study identified sex-specific patterns in various inflammatory (NLR, SII, NHR) and lipid markers, notably highlighting the C-reactive-protein-to-HDL ratio (CHR) as a strong predictor of endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease risk, with women generally showing reduced levels of these inflammatory indices.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cross-sectional assessment of physiological, hematological, lipid, and inflammatory markers in women (n=145) and men (n=50) aged 72.2  1 7.8 years; no intervention or dose comparison was reported, focusing on sex-specific differences.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High levels (> 150 mg/dL) found in 36% of the sample, with levels significantly more elevated (by ~20%) in women compared to men in this study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary form of fat storage in the body, used for energy.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Vascular aging, lipid metabolism, and sex-specific differences in cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High levels are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and indicate a higher risk of cardiovascular events.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigates the distinct roles of myeloperoxidase (MPO) in gastric health and gastric adenocarcinoma. It reveals an inverse and non-linear association between MPO and gastric mucosal injury markers (PGI, PGR) in a large healthy population, with a significant MPO threshold of 24 ng/ml. Furthermore, high MPO expression is identified as an independent predictor of poor prognosis in gastric adenocarcinoma, correlating with immune dysregulation, specific immune cell infiltration (macrophages, dendritic cells), and pathways involved in cell proliferation and invasion. The study also examined associations between pepsinogen ratio quartiles and various health indicators including blood pressure, diabetes, H. pylori infection, and lipid profiles.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational and Correlational Study
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational and correlational study conducted in two independent cohorts (16,943 healthy individuals and 375 gastric adenocarcinoma patients from TCGA). No direct therapeutic intervention or treatment doses were administered or compared. The study analyzed naturally occurring biomarker levels, their associations, and prognostic significance, with participants sometimes stratified by biomarker quartiles (e.g., Pepsinogen Ratio).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased with increasing PGI/PGII quartiles. Higher MPO quartiles associated with increased levels (P < 0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage in the body, used for energy; plays a role in metabolic and cardiovascular health.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Stratification by Pepsinogen Ratio (PGI/PGII) quartiles; association with MPO levels across quartiles.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic health and cardiovascular disease risk; high levels are associated with increased risk.

document_context_data.document_summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) in a rural Chinese population (N=3,280, aged 45+). The study found UHR to be a significant independent predictor and risk factor for increased cIMT and carotid intima-media thickening, with this association being particularly pronounced in older men. The findings suggest UHR's potential as a valuable marker for early detection and intervention of carotid atherosclerosis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Cross-sectional Study for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a cross-sectional study utilizing data from the 2019 general physical examination of 3,280 rural Chinese residents aged 45 years and older. No experimental interventions or therapeutic doses were administered; the study focused on observational correlations between biomarkers and cIMT. It was noted that excessively high plasma HDL-C levels (>90 mg/dL) might still increase cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline measurement only; no specific change or association with cIMT reported in this study.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat stored in the body for energy.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Fasting state during cross-sectional health examination.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated LRP1 expression, circulating soluble LRP1 (sLRP1) levels, and myocardial lipid content in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (IDCM) patients compared to healthy controls, and assessed the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in sLRP1 secretion. Key findings include increased circulating sLRP1, higher myocardial collagen and triglyceride content, and elevated LRP1 alpha chain expression in myocardial vessels of IDCM patients, with sLRP1 release found to be independent of the exosome pathway and not associated with blood lipid parameters.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating disease pathogenesis and biomarker identification in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Observational and diagnostic study comparing IDCM patients (n=20 for plasma, n=9 for tissue) with age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=15 for plasma, n=5 for tissue). Myocardial tissue samples were from explanted hearts. The study also included a comparison of hypercholesterolemic and normocholesterolemic patients. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were conducted.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No association between sLRP1 levels and any of the lipid parameters, including TGs (r = 0.15, P = 0.53)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Main form of fat storage, involved in energy metabolism.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy (IDCM), correlation with circulating sLRP1.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Circulating sLRP1 levels are not correlated with blood triglycerides in IDCM patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized controlled crossover trial investigated the impact of continuous multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS) on intraday lipid metabolism in young male cyclists. The study found that FOPS accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown, non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) uptake, and fat oxidation during both sedentary and exercise states. It also increased plasma free amino acids (FAAs) and post-exercise blood glucose, suggesting a modulation of metabolic substrate selection for improved endurance performance and cardiometabolic health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Continuous ingestion of multi-food-derived oligopeptide supplementation (FOPS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants ingested a blend of three food-derived oligopeptides (from soybean, wheat, and fish skin collagen proteins) and 6% carbohydrate with electrolytes. The total dosage was 0.5 g/kg body weight, administered in multiple servings (0.05 g/kg body weight each) throughout a one-day exercise protocol. Specifically, approximately 7g of oligopeptides were ingested 20 minutes pre-exercise, followed by continuous ingestion totaling approximately 31.5g to 35g during the 24-hour trial. The protocol included intraday fasting, 30 minutes of sitting still, 85 minutes of prolonged exercise plus a 5-minute sprint, a 60-minute recovery, and a 20-minute time trial. No dose-response comparisons for varying oligopeptide amounts were reported.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma and Serum (also implied in Adipose tissues, Liver)
matched_biomarker_details.activity_type: Lipid Concentration and Metabolic Breakdown Rate

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: FOPS significantly lowered serum/plasma TG levels post-prolonged exercise and time trial, and at subsequent fasting, compared to control. Most TGs were decreased (e.g., 45% of 101 TGs in the FOPS group vs. 3% in control at 'no FOPS' fasting condition). Average percentage changes post-TT and at fasting were -22% and -10% respectively, with FOPS. Mildly lower serum TG levels were observed within 20 minutes of initial oligopeptide ingestion. The treatment promoted whole-body TG breakdown, including rapid breakdown in adipose tissues and liver.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Primary form of energy storage, transport of lipids, and structural components of cell membranes; mobilization of stored fat for energy production.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Continuous FOPS supplementation before, during, and after prolonged exercise (PE) and time trial (TT) sessions, and during fasting and sedentary states.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Accelerated total body triglyceride breakdown and enhanced fat utilization contribute to improved lipid metabolism, sustained energy supply, and potentially enhanced endurance capacity, recovery, and cardiometabolic health by preventing fat accumulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an observational cross-sectional study. Its primary objective is to assess the reliability of systemic inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and immune cell reactivity, alongside perceived pain and pressure pain thresholds, through nine repeated measurements in workers exposed to constant real-life occupational workloads. Secondary aims include assessing correlations between these biomarkers and pain measures, and comparing levels between groups with higher and lower upper-extremity physical workloads. The study also details screening for metabolic parameters to ensure participant eligibility and ultimately aims to clarify the predictive role of these biomarkers in the development of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and to inform work-related stress-recovery concepts.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Exposure to real-life occupational workloads
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study compares two groups: an 'exposed group' with higher upper-extremity physical workloads (exceeding the Action Limit of TLV for HAL, with daily repetitive strain for >=4 days/week and >=20 hours/week) and an 'unexposed group' (office workers) with lower upper-extremity physical workloads (not exceeding TLV for HAL). Participants will undergo nine repeated measurements of blood samples and pain assessments once every two weeks. The study assesses reliability and compares biomarker levels between these workload groups, rather than evaluating a therapeutic dose-response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not reported (screening parameter).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Screening for participant eligibility to verify absence of acute infection or metabolic diseases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator for acute infection or metabolic diseases, used for participant eligibility.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of rehabilitation training (RT) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on coronary artery disease (CAD) patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It found that RT, particularly aerobic exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, significantly improved patients' exercise ability, cardiopulmonary function, lipid profiles, quantitative load indexes, and reduced anxiety and depression, ultimately enhancing overall quality of life and health status.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Rehabilitation training (RT) or Exercise Therapy (ET) combined with routine health education and standard pharmacological treatment, for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) patients post-Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Fifty CHD patients post-PCI were randomized into a control group (routine health education) and an intervention group (routine health education combined with RT/ET). ET consisted of a 5-10 minute warm-up, followed by 30-60 minutes of formal aerobic exercise (treadmill or upper body fluid resistance) performed 3-4 times per week with 1-day intervals. Exercise intensity was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (13-16 score required), and CPET involved a progressive workload increase on a stationary bike every minute for 8-12 minutes. PCI details included stenosis >80% with residual stenosis <20% post-stent deployment. Specifics for pharmacological treatment were standard. Although some dose parameters were provided for ET, detailed FITT parameters were not fully available in the provided text, and no explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for any aspect of the intervention.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: significantly decreased (P < 0.05) in the intervention group compared to baseline and control group.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Fat in blood, involved in energy storage; high levels increase cardiovascular disease risk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Rehabilitation training (RT) or aerobic exercise therapy (ET) in CAD patients after PCI.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower levels indicate improved cardiovascular health, reduced risk of metabolic syndrome and CAD progression, and improved lipid profiles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D supplementation, sunlight exposure, home isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic, and training loads on seasonal changes in 25(OH)D concentration and various blood biomarkers in young elite soccer players over a one-year cycle. It found significant seasonal variations in 25(OH)D, Hemoglobin (HGB), Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), and Creatine Kinase (CK). While 8-week vitamin D supplementation (5,000 IU/day) showed no sustained effect on 25(OH)D levels, possibly due to home isolation and seasonal factors, it did influence some biomarkers positively. Biomarkers related to morphology, lipid profile, and muscle damage varied more with training loads and seasonal factors than with supplementation alone.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Vitamin D supplementation and Sports Training.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Vitamin D supplementation involved 5,000 IU/day for 8 weeks (mid-January to mid-March 2020) in the supplemented group (n=11), compared to a placebo group (n=13) receiving sunflower oil. This supplementation had no sustained extended effect on 25(OH)D levels beyond the 8-week period, suggesting continuous dosing during deficiency is needed. Training encompassed typical competitive season volumes of 720 minutes/week (mainly aerobic and mixed aerobic-anaerobic drills), increasing to 810 minutes/week in pre-season. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for either the vitamin D or training regimen.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significant time-dependent changes in subgroups; decreased in GS between T2 and T3, then increased in T4.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes in the whole group (n=24) but significant time interaction in subgroups (p < 0.002). TG significantly decreased (p < 0.05) in the supplemented group (GS) between T2 and T3, followed by an increase in T4.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: One-year training period in young soccer players, including competitive and pre-season sports training, vitamin D supplementation, low-intensity training loads, and potential dietary influences (e.g., high-carbohydrate drinks).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of metabolic health and energy status. Decreases may reflect increased energy expenditure from training or vitamin D supplementation, while increases could be due to dietary intake during high-intensity training.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigates the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying sorafenib activity and resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells and patients. It reveals that sorafenib impairs mitochondrial function, forcing a metabolic shift towards glycolysis, leading to D-lactate accumulation, which serves as a biomarker for treatment response. In resistant cells, adaptation involves rerouting dihydroxyacetone phosphate towards glycerol-3-phosphate synthesis, extensive phospholipid remodeling to evade ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and increased reliance on exogenous triglycerides, resulting in glycerol accumulation as a marker of resistance. The study identifies D-lactate and glycerol as potential plasma biomarkers for monitoring sorafenib efficacy and resistance in HCC patients.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Sorafenib
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The primary therapy investigated was Sorafenib, a multi-kinase inhibitor for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In vitro studies used sorafenib at an IC50 of 8.5 µM for acute, 48-hour, or 7-day prolonged treatments, and 7 µM for sorafenib-resistant IR-Huh7 cells. Clinical treatment involved oral administration of 400 mg twice daily for HCC patients, with dose reductions permitted for adverse effects. Other interventions included adenoviral gene downregulation (50 MOI for Gpd1/1l, Gpd2; 20 MOI for Glo1) and supplementation with various fatty acids (SFAs, MUFAs, PUFAs) or lipoproteins (VLDL, LDL), and inhibition of Mgll with JZL184. No detailed dose-response comparisons were consistently reported for sorafenib, though Mgll inhibition showed dose-dependent effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced in lipid-depleted (LD) serum compared to standard FBS. Reduced levels in culture medium were found to enhance sorafenib's efficacy.

matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced levels in culture medium enhance sorafenib's efficacy, suggesting their crucial role in conferring resistance to sorafenib.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated systemic metabolic alterations in early Parkinson's disease (PD), focusing on the thyroid-liver axis, dysautonomia, and fatty acid beta-oxidation. It utilized nuclear medicine techniques (MIBG scintigraphy, DaT-SPECT) in 1,158 PD patients, combined with trans-omic analyses (serum exosome miRNA transcriptome and plasma metabolome) in de novo PD patients, and in vitro cell experiments. Key findings include sympathetic denervation of the thyroid and heart correlating with disease severity, decreased thyroxine levels, insufficient fatty acid β-oxidation, and enrichment of the PPARα axis. The research identified significantly altered exosomal miRNAs and demonstrated the association of thyroid hormone with PPARα-dependent β-oxidation regulation and enhanced mitochondrial function in muscle cells, suggesting disorganized interorgan communication as a sensitive diagnostic biomarker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This observational study, a secondary analysis, investigated the influence of hormonal contraceptive (HC) use on selected hormonal biomarkers and body composition metrics in 36 female physique athletes exposed to diet and physical training-induced low energy availability (LEA). Over approximately 23 weeks of LEA during competition preparation, estradiol and total testosterone concentrations remained stable in combined HC users but significantly decreased in progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females. Serum IGF-1, triiodothyronine (T3), and leptin decreased comparably in all groups, while serum cortisol concentrations remained statistically unchanged. The study concluded that exogenous hormones in combined HCs may maintain already suppressed hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian (HPO) axis function in the presence of LEA, whereas LEA-induced changes in IGF-1, T3, and leptin are comparable across all groups irrespective of HC use. Body composition changes (fat mass, body fat %, VL CSA, body mass, fat-free mass, and energy availability) were also differentially influenced.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by voluntary dietary restriction and concurrent resistance and aerobic training, with an observational comparison across hormonal contraceptive use
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent approximately 23 weeks of planned low energy availability (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21) involving voluntary energy restriction and high volumes of resistance training (~5 times/week) and aerobic training (~4 times/week, adjusted pre/post-competition). This was followed by a ~23-week recovery period, totaling ~46 weeks of observation. The study also compared physiological states across three groups (combined HC users, progestin-only HC users, and naturally menstruating females) at pre, post, and recovery time points. During recovery, energy availability differed between groups: progestin-only and naturally menstruating females maintained lower EA (< 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), while combined HC users had higher EA (> 40 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21). No dose-response comparisons for LEA intensity or specific hormonal contraceptive dosages were reported, as it was an observational study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Decreased significantly from pre to post in all groups. Combined HC users recovered to pre levels, while progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females remained significantly lower at recovery. Overall, T3 was higher in combined HC users
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: All groups (combined HC, progestin-only HC, naturally menstruating females) decreased significantly from pre to post (p<0.001, p<0.008, and p<0.001, respectively) after ~23 weeks of LEA. Combined HC users increased back to pre-treatment concentrations at recovery (p=0.009). Progestin-only HC users and naturally menstruating females remained significantly lower than pre at recovery (p=0.042 and p<0.001, respectively), despite an increase from post to recovery in naturally menstruating females (p=0.003). Overall, T3 was significantly higher in combined HC users than in progestin-only HC users (p=0.009) and naturally menstruating females (p=0.001). There was a significant main effect for time (F=28.992, p<0.001) and group (F=8.967, p<0.001).

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Low energy availability (LEA) induced by diet and physical training in female physique athletes (defined as < 30 kcal 7kg 21 FFM 7day 21), with a comparative analysis across combined hormonal contraceptive users, progestin-only hormonal contraceptive users, and naturally menstruating females at pre, post, and recovery time points. document_context_data.document_summary: This review provides updated guidelines and a consensus for standardizing pre-analytical variables in salivary biomarker studies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. It critically appraises current methodologies, identifies inconsistencies, and proposes a standardized protocol for saliva collection, processing, and storage to improve reliability for diagnostic biomarker detection and quantification. The document investigates various protein and metabolomic biomarkers in saliva, assessing their diagnostic potential for AD and Mild Cognitive Impairment, and highlights the importance of controlling factors like collection methods, centrifugation, and storage conditions for accurate measurement.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Salivary Biomarker Research and Standardization for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a comprehensive review article focusing on standardizing pre-analytical variables for salivary Alzheimer's Disease (AD) biomarker studies, rather than a therapeutic intervention or dose-response investigation. It critically discusses how inconsistent methodologies and pre-analytical factors (e.g., collection kits like Salivette vs. passive drooling, acute food intake, physical activity, stress, diurnal variations, dental restorations, freezing/thawing protocols, centrifugation speeds) influence biomarker detection and quantification, leading to conflicting findings for analytes like Aβ42, Aβ40, and AChE activity. The document proposes a standardized pre-analytical protocol, including pre-collection instructions (e.g., abstinence from food, drinks, smoking, alcohol, exercise), passive drool collection (e.g., 2 mL after 5 min pooling), and post-collection processing (e.g., immediate freezing, visual inspection, two-step centrifugation, aliquoting 100-250 µL). Various analytical methods (ELISA, Western blot, SIMOA, MS-based methods, NMR) were discussed for diagnostic marker identification, emphasizing that a universal protocol might not suit all biomarkers due to their diverse physiological roles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative proteomic analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) derived from different somatic origins (fibroblasts and peripheral blood CD34+ cells), comparing them to original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC) and human embryonic stem cells (hESC). Using ESI-MS e and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry, complemented by Western blot validation, the research aimed to characterize hiPSC proteomic profiles, identify known and novel pluripotency markers, and distinguish hiPSCs from their somatic precursors. Key findings include the identification of approximately 220 commonly up-regulated proteins in pluripotent stem cell lines, the development and confirmation of a 22-protein marker panel for hiPSC characterization, and the observation of coordinated up-regulation of proteins involved in protein synthesis, folding, RNA processing, DNA replication, DNA repair, and energy metabolism (including oxidative phosphorylation and lipogenesis) in hiPSCs. The study also identified somatic cell markers that were down-regulated upon reprogramming and highlighted specific proteomic differences between hiPSCs and hESCs, contributing to improved hiPSC quality control for therapeutic applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic characterization and comparative analysis of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and human embryonic stem cells (hESCs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a characterization study, not a therapeutic intervention, thus no 'dose' of therapy was administered. Quantitative and qualitative proteomic analyses were performed using electrospray ionization (ESI)-MS e (label-free quantification with internal reference standard) and MALDI-TOF/TOF mass spectrometry. Two hiPSC lines (iNC-01 from CD34+ cells, SB5-MP1 from fibroblasts, both generated using loxP-flanked excisable polycistronic STEMCCA lentiviral vector) and one hESC line (H9) were analyzed at earlier and later passages. Comparisons were made against their respective original somatic cells (fibroblasts, PBMC). Proteins were considered differentially expressed if expression changed by >=1.5-fold, with a maximum false discovery rate of 2% and >95% confidence. Western blot analysis was used for validation. The developed marker panel was further tested in 8-9 additional hiPSC lines or passages from different somatic origins and reprogramming techniques. Differentiation studies were conducted with embryoid bodies at 24 hours and 7 days to assess marker changes during spontaneous differentiation.

All selected proteins were confirmed to be up-regulated in hiPSC and hESC compared to somatic cells. Shown to regulate transcriptional dynamics and retroviral silencing in hESC (previous study).

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pro/anti-inflammatory status and molecular changes, including circulating microRNAs (miRs), proteasome, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), cytokines, and muscle proteomic changes, in two crewmembers after a 6-month International Space Station mission. document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the functional heterogeneity of mesenchymal and neural stem cells (MSC and NSC) to identify highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy. The research found that sMSC and sNSC exhibited superior motility and migratory potential compared to their parental non-selected cells, with podoplanin (PDPN) identified as a major regulator of this enhanced migration. In mouse models, sMSC demonstrated improved targeted migration to glioblastoma tumor sites and significantly reduced Alzheimer's disease hallmarks, including amyloid-beta pathology, cortical hyperactivity, and memory deficits, while promoting neurogenesis, neuronal survival, and synaptic integrity. PDPN overexpression in NSC also enhanced oncolytic activity against glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that stem cell motility and migration potential are key determinants of their therapeutic efficacy, with implications for developing customized cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative and oncological brain disorders.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Stem Cell Therapy (using Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSC) and Neural Stem Cells (NSC) or their highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC, sNSC)), Gene Engineering (siRNA knockdown or overexpression of podoplanin (PDPN)), and Oncolytic Virotherapy (using Oncolytic Adenovirus Ad-Delo3-RGD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Highly migrating subpopulations (sMSC and sNSC) were selected based on their superior intrinsic migration capacity. Treatments included intranasal administration (1x10^6 MSC in 40 µL PBS, applied on day 1 and 3 after pre-treatment with 100 U hyaluronidase) of oMSC or sMSC in transgenic Alzheimer's disease mouse models (APP23xPS45 and 3xTg-AD). For glioblastoma models, 1x10^5 eGFP+ murine oMSC vs. eGFP+ sMSC were stereotactically injected contralaterally to tumor cells. Neural stem cells were infected with oncolytic adenovirus (200 MOI of Ad-Delo3-RGD) for oncolytic assays. Additionally, siRNA-mediated PDPN knockdown was applied to sMSC, and transient PDPN overexpression to oNSC and oMSC. The study focused on comparing the efficacy of selected/engineered cells versus original populations, with no other explicit dose-response comparisons reported.
