document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the response of circulating miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 to an acute exhaustive exercise in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. It found that serum levels of miR-21, miR-378, and miR-940 were significantly up-regulated immediately after exercise, along with increases in CK, LDH, and NT-ProBNP. Conversely, several other miRNAs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-133b, miR-499, miR-208a, miR-208b, miR-486, miR-328, miR-126, miR-221, miR-146a, miR-155, miR-210), CK-MB, Tn-T, and hs-CRP remained unchanged. Crucially, no robust correlation was identified between changes in the circulating miRNAs and exercise capacity, muscle damage, inflammation, or cardiac function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute exhaustive exercise / Symptom-limited incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single session of acute exhaustive exercise was performed by 28 male chronic heart failure (CHF) participants (mean age 59.07  1 1.79 years). The standardized exercise protocol used revised Ramp10 programs on a bicycle ergometer where patients cycled at 60 rpm, with work increasing from 20 J/s for 2 minutes, then by 5 J/s every 30 seconds until exhaustion. No dose-response comparisons were reported for any biomarker changes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not affected (Table 3).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of cardiac muscle damage.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Not affected by acute exhaustive exercise in CHF patients.

document_context_data.document_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation on lean body mass, fat mass, muscle strength, physical performance, and various biochemical markers in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake, who were also training for a 4-day walking event. The study found that protein supplementation resulted in a larger increase in relative lean body mass and a greater reduction in fat mass compared to placebo. While both the protein and placebo groups showed improvements in physical performance and cardiorespiratory fitness due to the walking exercise, no additional between-group differences were observed in muscle strength, muscle contractile properties, or physical performance from protein supplementation. Serum urea increased in the protein group, but no adverse effects on renal function or muscle damage markers were noted, indicating protein supplementation is a safe strategy for this population.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Protein supplementation combined with walking exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Physically active older adults were randomized to receive either 31 g of milk protein concentrate daily (split into 15g at breakfast and 15g post-exercise/lunch) or an iso-caloric placebo for 12 weeks. This increased the protein group's total daily protein intake from 0.86 ± 0.23 g/kg/day upon enrollment to 1.29 ± 0.28 g/kg/day at 12 weeks. Both groups concurrently participated in walking exercise training for a 4-day walking event, covering an average of 338-391 km over 12 weeks. No dose-response comparisons for protein intake were reported, only the comparison between the protein and placebo groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly more in the protein group compared with the placebo group (P Interaction = 0.007).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Non-fat body mass specifically in the trunk region, primarily reflecting core muscle mass.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: 12 weeks of daily protein supplementation combined with walking exercise.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of regional muscle mass changes, relevant for core strength and stability.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review identifies and recommends validated biomarkers for tracking health, performance, and recovery in athletes across multiple domains including nutritional status (macronutrients, micronutrients, food allergies), hydration, muscle status (damage, endocrine response), endurance, and injury risk (concussions, stress fractures, ACL). It advocates for a comprehensive, integrative, and individualized approach to biomarker analysis, emphasizing dynamic monitoring and contextual interpretation over single markers or universal thresholds to optimize training and minimize injury and overtraining risks.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker-guided monitoring and management of athletic training, nutrition, hydration, and injury recovery
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This review primarily focuses on the diagnostic and prognostic value of biomarkers rather than specific therapeutic doses. It emphasizes frequent, individualized monitoring (e.g., pre/post-exercise, daily, seasonally, after injury/competition) to establish personalized baseline ranges and track physiological changes in response to various training loads (e.g., acute bouts, heavy strength training, challenging training weeks). While specific nutritional intake recommendations are mentioned for protein (1.3–2.0 g/kg/day) and omega-3 fatty acids (≤3 g/day for average, 6–8 g/day for elite athletes), and iron supplementation at low-moderate doses, the document does not report dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes. Instead, it provides specific thresholds for identifying deficiencies (e.g., Vitamin D >50 ng/ml, Ferritin <12 µg/L), dehydration (e.g., >-2% body mass decrease, blood osmolality ≥295 mmol/kg, USG ≥1.020), insufficient recovery (30% decrease in T:C ratio), and overtraining (T:C ratio of 0.35 × 10⁻³). The overall approach prioritizes dynamic, contextualized assessment over universal thresholds for effective athlete management.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated (no specific quantification).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Amino acid, part of patterns indicating fatigue.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Athletes; associated with fatigue and suboptimal training capacity; monitoring resting amino acids across a season.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with fatigue and suboptimal training capacity; may serve as biomarker of muscle quality/status.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study employed NMR metabolomics to investigate metabolic profiles in serum and urine from COVID-19 patients across varying disease severities (Medical Ward and Intensive Care Unit) and healthy controls. The primary aim was to identify biomarkers for COVID-19 diagnosis, severity classification, and prognosis, and to explore correlations with clinical factors like hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Key findings include the development of a highly efficient diagnostic panel (isoleucine, TMAO, glucose) and a robust severity classification panel (ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics), alongside identification of numerous individual metabolites and clinical parameters associated with infection, disease progression, hospitalization duration, and patient outcome.

treatment_details.therapy_type: NMR metabolomics-based profiling and observational study of COVID-19 infection
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This observational study analyzed 80 serum and urine samples from COVID-19 patients (34 intensive care, 46 hospitalized) and 32 from healthy controls using NMR spectroscopy. The research focused on identifying and validating metabolite-based panels for COVID-19 diagnosis and severity classification. A diagnostic panel of isoleucine, TMAO, and glucose achieved an AUC of 0.91 (86.08% sensitivity, 83.87% specificity). A severity classification panel, combining ethanol, TMAO, tyrosine, betaine, and clinical characteristics (obesity/overweight, dyslipidemia, lymphocyte count), achieved an AUC of 0.825 (84.85% sensitivity, 72.09% specificity). No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were part of the study design.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher levels observed as top positive correlates to obesity/overweight in Medical Ward patients (serum). Metabolic changes observed in ICU patients in urine.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, precursor to neurotransmitters, involved in inflammatory signals, and in arginine, proline, galactose, and glycerolipid metabolisms; metabolic regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COVID-19 disease severity (ICU vs. Medical Ward) and association with obesity/overweight.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for COVID-19 severity, indicating metabolic changes, and associated with obesity/overweight.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 2-week hemp fiber (high and low doses) or placebo supplementation on post-exercise gut permeability and plasma metabolite shifts in healthy male and female cyclists after intensive cycling. While hemp fiber did not significantly alter post-exercise gut permeability (measured by urine sugar data), untargeted metabolomics revealed that the combination of hemp fiber intake and vigorous exercise increased beneficial gut-derived metabolites and influenced pathways related to tryptophan, primary bile acid, steroid, sphingolipid, alpha-linolenic acid, arginine and proline, lipid, and amino acid metabolism.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with hemp fiber (hemp hull powder) combined with intensive cycling exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants received daily supplementation for 2 weeks with either a high dose (20 g/d) or low dose (5 g/d) of hemp hull powder, or a placebo (0 g/d). Each supplementation period concluded with a 2.25-hour intensive cycling bout performed at approximately 70% VO2max. While distinct metabolomic shifts were observed between the hemp fiber and placebo groups (R2Y = 0.987 and 0.995), no significant dose-response for gut permeability was reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Key and significant metabolite hits within the tryptophan pathway (pathway significantly influenced by hemp fiber supplementation, p < 0.05).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, precursor to serotonin and other neuroactive compounds, involved in protein synthesis and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-dose hemp fiber supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates modulation of central amino acid metabolism, potentially affecting mood, sleep, and immune function.

document_context_data.document_summary: This clinical trial investigated the impact of two distinct dietary interventions, Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF), on plasma amino acid and amine profiles in a Mediterranean female cohort (cloistered nuns). The study found that combining macronutrients significantly reduced plasma levels of amino acids and amines, particularly in the PFF group, with some recovery post-intervention. Metabolic profile analysis showed significant differences between groups at 55 and 98 days, identifying leucine, asparagine, alanine, cysteine, and creatine as key differentiating metabolites, and also observed significant alterations in EAA/NEAA and Kyn/Trp ratios.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary Intervention (Combined Macronutrient Diet)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 132-day dietary intervention with 41 participants assigned to two groups: Protein Fat (PF) and Protein Fat and Fiber (PFF). The PF group consumed 150g of pork belly (standardized to approximately 20g protein and 40g fat per 100g product) with other menu items. The PFF group consumed 200g of vegetables (cardoon or borage) along with 150g pork belly (twice a week) and other daily menu items. Total menu and physical activity were identical between groups. No dose-response comparisons beyond the defined dietary groups were reported, but effects were monitored at 55, 98, and 132 days.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Notable differences between groups at 98 days (p < 0.002) and significantly different values at 132 days (p < 0.002).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, precursor to serotonin, melatonin, and kynurenine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Dietary intervention at 98 days and 132 days (completion).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as a differentiating metabolite indicating the impact of the dietary intervention over the course of the study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This sportomics study investigated the metabolic, immune, hormonal, and amino acid responses, alongside muscle and liver injury markers, in two elite female Olympic beach volleyball athletes during a simulated competition day involving two matches. Key findings revealed significant acute physiological impacts, including electrolyte disturbances (notably hypokalemia), 20-60% increases in muscle injury markers and up to 50% for liver enzymes, elevated stress hormones (ACTH up to 4-fold, cortisol up to 3-fold), and altered energy metabolism and amino acid profiles indicative of central fatigue risk (e.g., Fischer ratio and tryptophan decreased by 60%, serotonin increased by 180%). The study emphasized distinct individual recovery kinetics, highlighted the inadequacy of short recovery sessions, and advocated for personalized monitoring due to varied biomarker responses despite similar external loads.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Two world-class female athletes participated in a simulated competition day involving two high-intensity beach volleyball matches (a two-set match in the morning and a three-set match in the afternoon), under identical environmental conditions. Blood and urine samples were collected at seven time points: pre-match, post-match, 60 minutes after each match (short recovery), and after a 15-hour long recovery. The protocol included 15-minute warm-ups. No dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, individual responses to the same protocol were highlighted, and short recovery sessions were found to be inadequate for full physiological recovery, with the second match demonstrating cumulative strain.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally decreased to a minimum of 60% of initial levels after BVb matches, with Athlete 1 showing an increasing drop in concentration. However, Athlete 2 showed a 25% increase after Match 1, with a consistent decrease after subsequent matches. Except for Athlete 1 in the first match, consistently decreased.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid and precursor for serotonin and melatonin, impacting mood, sleep, and fatigue; competes with BCAA for transport across the blood–brain barrier (BBB).
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Simulated Beach Volleyball Competition Day (during exercise, after matches).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests increased uptake of tryptophan into the central nervous system (CNS) from the bloodstream, serving as an indirect marker of central fatigue. Reflects changes in serotonin pathway metabolism, potentially influencing central fatigue or mood states during and after exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of two distinct heat stress modalities—exertional heating (exercise/cycling) and exogenous heating (hot water immersion)—on physiological responses, stress markers, and peripheral kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites in 11 young healthy males. Both modalities were designed to induce a comparable increase in core body temperature up to 39°C. The study found that heat exposure transiently induced the KP, elevating several plasma KP metabolite concentrations (Kynurenic acid, Picolinic acid, 3-Hydroxykynurenine, Quinolinic acid, Kynurenine, KYN/TRP ratio) and stress markers (Cortisol, Prolactin, Adrenaline, Noradrenaline, Lactate). These changes generally returned to baseline during recovery, suggesting adaptability of KP enzymes to physiological stressors. Differential changes were observed depending on the specific heat stress protocol and the phase (heating vs. recovery), with exertional heating often showing more pronounced effects for some markers and sustained elevation for others (e.g., KYNA, PIC in EXE). The study highlights the potential of KP metabolites as disease biomarkers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Induced Hyperthermia / Heat Stress (Exertional heating and Exogenous heating)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants underwent two distinct heat stress modalities: exertional heating (EXE) via cycling exercise at an intensity eliciting 60% VO2max in a 30°C room, and exogenous heating (EXO) via hot water immersion up to the waistline in a 44°C bath. Both trials were conducted until rectal temperature (Trec) reached 39°C (with measurements taken at every 0.5°C increment up to a maximum of 39.5°C), followed by a recovery phase to a baseline temperature of 37.5°C. The time required to reach specific temperature set points was similar in both trials. No direct dose-response comparisons were explicitly reported; however, EXE induced greater increases in stress markers and sympathetic vasomotor activity compared to EXO, suggesting differential physiological loads.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Remained stable during the heating phase of both trials. However, it exhibited a slight significant decrease during the recovery phase upon return to baseline temperature in the EXO trial (p < 0.05). Detected in concentrations higher than the LLOQ of 5 µM.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Essential amino acid, precursor for serotonin and kynurenine pathway metabolites, influencing mood and immunity.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Heat stress (EXE and EXO trials) induced by core temperature increases, with samples collected at 0.5°C rectal temperature increments up to 39°C and subsequent decrease until 37.5°C, particularly during heating and recovery phases.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Changes indicate altered availability for downstream metabolic pathways, potentially affecting neuroinflammation and mood.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the efficacy and fate of intravenously administered human kidney-derived CD133+ and CD133- cells in ameliorating cisplatin-induced nephropathy in immunodeficient rats. Both cell types similarly improved renal function and promoted regeneration, reducing acute kidney injury and histological damage. Crucially, therapeutic effects were not due to renal engraftment; instead, cells were entrapped in the lungs, underwent cell death within 24 hours, and likely mediated repair through paracrine or endocrine factors, potentially involving macrophage infiltration and IL10 secretion in the lungs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model in rats, followed by intravenous administration of human kidney-derived CD133+ or CD133- cells.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Cisplatin was administered intraperitoneally at 7 mg/100 g body weight to induce injury. Cell therapy consisted of two intravenous injections of 10^6 GFP-expressing CD133+ or CD133- cells (in 500 µl sterile PBS) via tail vein on days 2 and 7 post-cisplatin. Control groups received saline or PBS. Cells were at passage 5. A second cell injection after day 7 did not provide additional benefits. No dose-response comparisons for cell therapy were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in cell-treated groups compared to cisplatin-injured rats. Cisplatin-only: 5,400 ± 739 µm^2 (n=7); CD133+: 3,000 ± 218 µm^2 (p < .01, n=7); CD133-: 3,100 ± 301 µm^2 (p < .05, n=6); Uninjured: 1,350 ± 26 µm^2 (p < .001).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Indicator of tubular damage and dilation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Histopathological assessment of renal tissue health at day 14 following cisplatin injury and cell therapy.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced tubular luminal area indicates amelioration of acute tubular injury and dilation.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study developed and applied a Nano-omics integrative workflow, utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas, to link systemic (plasma) and localized (tumor tissue) protein changes associated with glioblastoma (GB) progression. This comprehensive proteomic investigation in GL261 murine models and human high-grade glioma patients aimed to identify GB-specific molecular pathways and peripheral blood biomarkers for early detection and disease monitoring. The methodology included inducing murine GB models, preparing and administering liposome nanoparticles in vivo or incubating them ex vivo with plasma, and subsequent proteomic analysis via mass spectrometry to identify differentially abundant proteins. The findings revealed significant plasma protein alterations, even at low tumor burden, with over 30% overlap between GB-specific plasma and tumor tissue proteomes, leading to the identification of 48 potential GB biomarker candidates across various biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker Discovery Method: Nano-omics integrative proteomics workflow utilizing nanoparticle protein coronas for glioblastoma (GB).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study involved inducing murine glioblastoma by stereotactic injection of 50,000 GL261 cells into the striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Liposomes (HSPC:Chol:DSPE-PEG2000) were prepared at a final lipid concentration of 25 mM and administered intravenously at a lipid dose of 0.125 mM/g body weight (equivalent to 5 mg/kg doxorubicin-loaded liposomes) 10 minutes prior to blood collection in mice. In human validation, ex vivo nanoparticle corona analysis was performed on pre-operative plasma samples from 10 high-grade glioma patients. Matched blood and tumor tissue samples were collected from mice at D7, D14, and D18 post-tumor inoculation, representing low, medium, and large tumor volumes. Matched resected tumor tissue from human patients was analyzed by LCM-coupled LC:MS/MS. No specific dose-response comparisons for nanoparticle application or tumor cell inoculation were reported for therapeutic purposes, as the focus was on biomarker discovery.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Log2 fold change > 10, ranked among top 5 most significant plasma differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) between Glioblastoma (GB) patients and healthy controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Associated with the cytoskeleton and extracellular matrix functional group.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: High-grade glioma patients compared to healthy controls.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for Glioblastoma (GB) detection and monitoring.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathological landscape, subclonal evolution, and dynamics of gene fusions, specifically KMT2A/AFDN and a novel CCDC32/CBX3, along with chimeric RNA variants, in 16 adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) patients undergoing treatment. It aimed to understand treatment resistance and relapse mechanisms by monitoring cytogenetic, RNA-seq, and genome-wide changes from diagnosis to relapse. The research identified the CCDC32/CBX3 fusion as a new therapeutic vulnerability that promotes cell cycle progression and contributes to AML pathogenesis and treatment resistance, highlighting its prognostic significance and the necessity of advanced molecular profiling for cryptic gene fusion detection.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chemotherapy (including high-dose cytarabine (HIDAC) and (7+3) induction chemotherapy) and Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (for Patient 7).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient 7 received HIDAC chemotherapy followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient 20 received (7+3) induction chemotherapy followed by HIDAC consolidation. No dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study primarily focused on biomarker monitoring and molecular changes rather than specific treatment efficacy across different doses. The study also included functional validation of gene fusion in vitro, which is not a treatment per se but part of the investigation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Analyses revealed potential targets for immunotherapeutic strategies.

matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Neuroblastoma (NB) patient profiles.

document_context_data.document_summary: This scoping review synthesizes existing literature on the frequency, function, and dynamics of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID, comparing them to acutely ill patients and seronegative controls. The review concludes that while Treg populations can quantitatively and functionally reconstitute during recovery, an infection-induced dysregulation often persists for several months. Findings reveal varied outcomes for total Treg frequencies, but distinct patterns for specific Treg subsets, FoxP3 expression, and cytokine production. Long COVID patients consistently exhibit significantly altered proportions of Tregs, indicating persistent immune dysregulation potentially contributing to the syndrome's pathophysiology and viral persistence, despite methodological heterogeneity across studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Scoping Review of Regulatory T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19 Convalescence and Long COVID
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This scoping review systematically investigated the frequency (e.g., absolute counts, relative frequency) and functionality (e.g., cytokine secretion, ex vivo suppressive capacity) of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and their subsets in convalescent COVID-19 patients, including those with Long COVID. Studies included comparisons across different initial disease severities (asymptomatic, mild, severe, fatal), hospitalization statuses, and various stages of convalescence (ranging from 4 weeks to ~1 year post-infection), and against acute COVID-19 cases or seronegative controls. The literature search was conducted on MEDLINE (via Pubmed) and Web of Science up to July 23, 2022. No therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were directly reported as this is a review of observational studies. The reviewed studies showed methodological heterogeneity in subject recruitment and Treg phenotyping strategies, and most subjects were likely unvaccinated and contracted wild-type SARS-CoV-2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Persistently high systemic and tissue-level concentrations of inflammatory cytokines like TNF.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Long COVID.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Could subvert the Tregs' regulatory capacity, indicating persistent inflammation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the impact of a 12-week cardiac rehabilitation program, involving moderate-intensity aerobic and resistance training, and omega-3 fatty acid supplementation, on gut barrier integrity and inflammatory biomarkers in older adults with Coronary Artery Disease. The key finding was that an increase in cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak   5 mL/kg/min) was significantly associated with a reduction in serum FABP2, indicating improved gut barrier integrity, while zonulin and inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF) did not show significant changes or associations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cardiac Rehabilitation (Aerobic and Resistance Exercise Training, and Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A 12-week moderate-intensity cardiac rehabilitation program, involving 5 days/week exercise (1 supervised in-class session, 4 at-home sessions). Supervised sessions were approximately 60 minutes, progressing from 60% to 80% of VO2peak. Omega-3 PUFA supplementation consisted of 1.9 g daily (1.2 g EPA, 0.6 g DHA) for 12 weeks, compared to a placebo. While the program had a progressive exercise intensity, no explicit dose-response comparisons between different exercise regimens or omega-3 doses were reported. The study focused on the impact of achieving a significant increase in cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak   5 mL/kg/min).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences between baseline and follow-up values (t = -1.17, p = 0.25), indicating no significant impact from the 12-week exercise or omega-3 intervention on systemic inflammation.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Inflammatory biomarker, involved in systemic inflammation and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cardiac rehabilitation (exercise training and omega-3 PUFA supplementation) in patients with Coronary Artery Disease (CAD).

document_context_data.document_summary:
This study investigated sex differences in inflammatory response, lipid peroxidation, and muscle damage in men and women athletes following an acute resistance exercise, specifically a maximal incremental half-squat test. Results showed men exhibited a larger pro-inflammatory response (IL6) and increased lipid peroxidation (HPX) at 24 hours post-exercise compared to women at equivalent workloads, while no significant sex-based differences were observed in other muscle damage markers (CK-MB, LDH, 
	-actin).

treatment_details.therapy_type: Acute Resistance Exercise (Maximal Incremental Half-Squat)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants performed half-squat exercises with five incremental intensities (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of one-repetition maximum, 1RM). Repetitions varied: 5 at 20-60% 1RM, 2 at 80% 1RM, and 1 at 100% 1RM. Rest periods between sets were 3-5 minutes. Equivalent workloads were used for men and women, but men achieved larger net loads due to greater muscle mass. No specific dose-response comparisons for biomarkers were reported across different intensities.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
No significant differences were found in the levels of TNF
	, regardless of time point and sex, and no changes were found after an acute strength test.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, initiates breakdown of damaged muscle tissue and is involved in systemic inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute resistance exercise (half-squat).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates no significant change in this specific pro-inflammatory marker after acute resistance exercise.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study aimed to establish serum reference values for myostatin and IGF-1 in healthy young males, including strength-training collegiate athletes and untrained controls, while investigating their correlations with body composition, age, and physical activity. Key findings indicated higher IGF-1 concentrations in athletes, with no significant difference in myostatin levels compared to controls. Myostatin levels were negatively correlated with age, BMI, fat mass percentage, and waist girth, whereas IGF-1 levels were positively correlated with height, fat-free mass, and estimated daily energy expenditure, and negatively with age. The document also provides context on myostatin's broader roles in muscle and lipid growth, cardiac function, and its levels in various clinical conditions and genetic polymorphisms, highlighting the relevance of these reference values for anti-doping applications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational Study / Strength Training
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study was an observational, cross-sectional comparison involving 28 male collegiate athletes (including weight-lifting and basketball teams) who reported engaging in strength training for at least one hour per day, five times per week, versus 29 age-matched untrained controls. No direct intervention or therapeutic dose was applied to investigate acute dose-response. The analysis established reference values and correlations with physiological parameters, adjusting for age and body composition. Myostatin levels in athletes did not significantly differ from controls, potentially due to sampling timing or a steady-state condition in athletes, precluding detailed dose-response comparisons within this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not quantified, only positive correlation reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Not explicitly detailed in this document chunk.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: COPD patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Its positive correlation with myostatin in COPD patients suggests a link between myostatin, muscle wasting, and systemic inflammation in this disease context.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 6-week cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation on antioxidant capacity, inflammatory markers, and iron metabolism in rowers subjected to exhaustive exercise. Findings indicate that supplementation significantly strengthened antioxidant potential (TAC) and mitigated exercise-induced increases in pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-alpha), muscle damage indicators (myoglobin), and iron regulatory hormones (hepcidin) in the supplemented group. However, IL-6, ferritin, sTfR, iron, TIBC, and UIBC remained largely unaffected by supplementation or showed exercise-induced changes independent of it.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) extract supplementation combined with strenuous physical exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Athletes received 720 mg of highly-concentrated large cranberry extract daily (two 360-mg capsules, containing 36 mg proanthocyanidins per capsule) for 6 weeks. The control group received dyed gelatin placebo capsules containing flour. Participants performed a 2000-m rowing ergometer test at maximal effort on day 1 (pre-supplementation) and at the end of the 6-week training camp (post-supplementation), with blood samples taken pre-exercise, 1 minute post-exercise, and after a 24-hour recovery. No dose-response comparisons for cranberry extract were reported within the study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Strenuous physical exercise induced significant changes (main effect, p < 0.001). At Trial I, no significant differences were found. At Trial II (after supplementation), a significant exercise-induced increase was observed solely in the control group. Cranberry supplementation did not exert an overall statistically significant effect (main effect, p = 0.118), but prevented the exercise-induced increase seen in controls.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates systemic inflammation as a pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Exhaustive 2000-m rowing ergometer test, with 6-week cranberry supplementation mitigating the exercise-induced rise at Trial II.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammation; cranberry supplementation mitigated the exercise-induced inflammatory response, suggesting it could be a marker of exercise load accumulation.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for COMMIT, a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up. It aims to investigate the impact of comorbidities, especially vascular comorbidity and related risk factors, on clinical and paraclinical parameters in patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD). The study will analyze levels of inflammation and neurodegeneration markers in blood and CSF, immune cell populations, plasma/serum proteome, cognitive functions, visual parameters, and CNS MRI findings to understand their relationship with clinical outcomes and inform future therapeutic strategies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating the impact of comorbidities on Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD), and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease (MOGAD).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This is a prospective multicenter observational study with a 3-year longitudinal follow-up, involving assessments at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 36 months. The study does not administer or test a specific therapeutic intervention; instead, it aims to analyze how existing comorbidities and their standard-of-care treatments influence disease progression and molecular parameters to inform future treatment strategies.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced (precise quantitative data not reported in this context)

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Oral antidiabetic drug treatment (metformin and pioglitazone) in Multiple Sclerosis
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduction indicates beneficial impact on MS disease progression, potentially improving outcomes in inflammatory demyelinating diseases.

document_context_data.document_summary: This pilot study aimed to investigate the effects of allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) on physical condition, muscle function, and inflammation in patients during inpatient time. It describes methods for assessing cardiopulmonary performance, body composition, muscle strength, motor skills, and various blood biomarkers (inflammatory, muscular, cardiovascular, and red blood cell parameters) at pre-transplantation, engraftment, and discharge time points. The main findings include a significant decline in grip strength and muscle function, increased levels of hsCRP and Kynurenine at engraftment, and changes in TNF-alpha, Musclin, and Galectin-3, suggesting their utility as novel biomarkers for monitoring acute inflammation, myopathy, sarcopenia, and cardiovascular health in alloSCT patients. It also noted a decline in patient physical activity adherence during the inpatient stay, without a direct correlation between steroid dosage and grip strength decline.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogenic Stem-Cell Transplantation (alloSCT)
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Patients underwent allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT), with conditioning regimens consisting of 76.9% myeloablative and 23.0% dose-reduced approaches; no non-myeloablative. The study did not report specific dose-response comparisons for alloSCT itself. Glucocorticoids were administered at an average dose of 4.5 
	3.9 mg/kg body weight per week, totaling a mean of 27.9 
	27.7 mg/kg per patient during the inpatient stay, aligning with guideline recommendations. Daily physical activity was documented and declined significantly, with endurance training decreasing from an average of 14.0 
	8.2 min/day before engraftment to 7.2 
	7.0 min/day post-engraftment, and strength training decreasing from 12.11 
	7.0 min/day pre-engraftment to 9.6 
	6.3 min/day post-engraftment. Supervised physiotherapy was offered approximately every three days. No correlation was observed between administered steroid dosage and the decline in grip strength within this study's cohort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification:
Decreased from T0 (5.0 
	3.6 pg/mL) to T1 (engraftment: 4.5 
	2.0 pg/mL; p=0.0054) and further decreased to T2 (inpatient discharge: 3.6 
	2.0 pg/mL; p=0.0003).

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pleiotropic pro-inflammatory cytokine with a central role in systemic inflammation, immune response, and cell apoptosis; plays a key role in acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (aGVHD) and mediates inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Allogenic stem-cell transplantation (alloSCT) during inpatient time; chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease (GVHD); blood profiling at enrollment (T0), engraftment (T1), and discharge (T2); during alloSCT, at T1 (engraftment time point) and inpatient release T2.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: High, chronic levels of inflammation correlate with functional limitations and reduced physical performance. It is involved in immune system activation post-transplantation and indicates inflammatory status after alloSCT. It showed a positive correlation with grip strength at T2 (r=0.41; p=0.045). TNF-alpha precedes the onset of aGVHD, peaking at its development, and can be used for discrimination of patients with and without GVHD, prediction of survival, and estimation of therapy efficacy. Combination with hsCRP and Kynurenine seems promising for GVHD prediction.

document_context_data.document_summary: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the effect of oral palmitoylethanolamide (PEA, Levagen+™) on recovery from muscle-damaging leg press exercise in 28 healthy young males. The study found that while PEA supplementation did not significantly reduce perceived muscle soreness, thigh circumference, or most inflammatory and phosphoprotein markers (Creatine Kinase, Lactate Dehydrogenase, IL-6, IL-10, hs-CRP, TNF-α, CREB, ERK1/2, JNK, NF-κB, p38 MAPK, S6K1, STAT3, STAT5), it did significantly reduce blood myoglobin and lactate concentrations. Furthermore, PEA increased Protein Kinase B phosphorylation immediately post-exercise, suggesting aid in muscle recovery through improved metabolic efficiency and activation of anabolic/repair signaling pathways from repeat bouts of exercise.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Oral Supplementation with Palmitoylethanolamide (Levagen+™) combined with Resistance Exercise
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were randomized to consume either liquid PEA (167.5 mg Levagen+™ containing 150 mg PEA and 17.5 mg excipients, with 832.5 mg maltodextrin) or a matched placebo (1 g maltodextrin). Treatments were administered pre-exercise, immediately post-exercise, 24 h post-exercise, and 48 h post-exercise. The muscle-damaging exercise consisted of four sets of leg press at 80% of one-repetition maximum (1-RM) to volitional exhaustion, with 60s rest between sets, followed by a performance set at 70% 1-RM to maximal repetitions. No dose-response comparisons for PEA were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked immediately post-exercise and declined thereafter (p < 0.05); no significant effect of PEA supplementation on reducing levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A potent pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in systemic inflammation and acute phase responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Leg press exercise to volitional exhaustion, with/without PEA supplementation.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an acute inflammatory response to exercise. Lack of reduction by PEA suggests limited anti-inflammatory effect on this specific biomarker.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for a two-phase randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigating the efficacy and acceptability of high-frequency, low-load Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) in UK military personnel with lower limb musculoskeletal injuries where persistent pain is the primary limiting factor. Phase One will compare 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) BFR-RT over one week to determine the most effective and acceptable pressure for pain reduction. Phase Two will then compare this optimal BFR-RT protocol against usual care over three weeks to evaluate its impact on pain modulation, function, and other rehabilitation outcomes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training (BFR-RT) compared to standard rehabilitation (usual care).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Phase One involves 7 BFR-RT sessions over 5 days (1 week) comparing 40% and 80% Limb Occlusion Pressure (LOP) (n=28). Each session for the affected limb includes unilateral leg press and knee extension, performed at 20% of 1-Repetition Maximum (1RM) with a protocol of 1 set of 30 repetitions followed by 3 sets of 15 repetitions, with 30-second rest between sets (continuous inflation) and a 3-minute reperfusion period between exercises. Phase Two involves 21 BFR-RT sessions over 15 days (3 weeks) for the BFR group (n=26), utilizing the optimal LOP determined in Phase One. The control group in Phase Two receives usual care. The study aims to compare high vs. low BFR pressures (40% vs. 80% LOP) and their acceptability, but as this is a protocol document, no dose-response results are reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher (elevated levels shown in persistent pain populations).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels reported in persistent pain populations; specific numerical results for this study are not provided in this protocol chunk.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Thought to be a driver for the development of pathological pain.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Acute and chronic effects of BFR-RT on inflammation, specifically in persistent pain populations.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammation and is associated with the development of pathological pain.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document describes the protocol for an exploratory, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial (CAME COVID-19 study) evaluating the efficacy of clarithromycin (400 mg/day or 800 mg/day) as an oral treatment for Japanese adult patients with mild COVID-19 pneumonia who do not require oxygen administration. The study aims to identify a new treatment strategy for mild COVID-19 and determine the number of days required to achieve a 50% or more improvement in clinical symptoms.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Clarithromycin
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Oral administration of clarithromycin is investigated in two dosage groups (800 mg/day, given as 400 mg twice daily, and 400 mg/day, given as 200 mg twice daily for 7 days) compared to a standard treatment control group. Patients are randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio, allowing for dose comparisons. Dose adjustment based on patient age, weight, and symptoms is possible. The doses are approved for other bacterial respiratory infections in Japan, and their safety is confirmed, but this is an exploratory trial as no prior dose-response data for COVID-19 pneumonia were available.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: To be determined by study outcomes; this is a protocol.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not applicable as this is a study protocol outlining planned measurements; no results are reported.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine that plays a central role in inflammation and immune regulation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Clarithromycin treatment for mild COVID-19 pneumonia.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Marker of inflammation, can contribute to systemic inflammation and organ damage in severe COVID-19.

document_context_data.document_summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing and managing immune monitoring programs in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation and cellular therapies (TCT/HCT). It highlights the critical need for standardized protocols for assay, flow cytometric, and data analysis to ensure consistent, scalable, and comparable results across multiple centers. The aim is to enhance prognosis prediction, enable early relapse detection, and improve clinical decision-making by evaluating immune reconstitution and functional recovery, as well as by identifying predictive cellular and secreted biomarkers for complications like graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), infections, viral reactivation, and relapse.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT), Transplant and Cellular Therapy (TCT), and related immune effector cell (IEC) therapies, including Genetically Modified Hematopoietic Stem Cell Therapies (GMHSCT) and CAR T-cell therapy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The document primarily focuses on immune monitoring protocols post-transplantation rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons for HCT/TCT itself. It highlights the variability in transplant platforms (e.g., T-cell depletion techniques, add backs, T-replete) and conditioning regimens (e.g., lymphocyte ablation, total body irradiation). Monitoring thresholds are mentioned for specific immune cells, such as >50 CD4+ T cells/μL within 100 days and >150 NK cells/mL at day 30 post-HCT, to indicate timely immune recovery. Recommended longitudinal sampling schedules are provided (e.g., biweekly for 3 months, then monthly/quarterly) post-HCT/GMHSCT, along with typical blood volumes (8-20 mL), but lack specific dose details for primary therapies or dose-response observations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Part of a 4-biomarker panel (IL-8, IL-2Rα, TNFR1, HGF) validated for confirming aGVHD and predicting survival. Exhibits contrasting effects on GVHD.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Soluble receptor for TNF; involved in inflammation and cell death pathways.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Post-transplant (TCT)
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Component of a panel confirming acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (aGVHD) and predicting survival; its influence on GVHD/GVL balance requires further study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated inflammatory clusters in sepsis based on plasma cytokine protein abundance and their relationship with leucocyte transcriptomic subphenotypes, utilizing data from three cohorts (UK GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS). It identified two or three inflammatory clusters across these datasets, with a 'high cytokine' cluster exhibiting elevated levels of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, which was consistently associated with worse organ dysfunction, increased disease severity, and higher mortality. The study also explored the overlap between inflammatory clusters and previously described transcriptomic subphenotypes (SRS1/SRS2) and ARDS subphenotypes, suggesting that combining cytokine protein abundance and transcriptomic data could provide complementary information for optimal sepsis patient stratification. No significant interaction between inflammatory clusters and trial treatment response for therapies like norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan was found.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Patient stratification using plasma cytokine profiling; evaluation of trial therapies including Vasopressin, Norepinephrine, Hydrocortisone, and Levosimendan in septic shock.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on patient stratification using hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis based on plasma protein abundance of 11 to 65 circulating cytokines, cytokine receptors, and regulators across three cohorts (UK GAinS: n=124, VANISH: n=155, LeoPARDS: n=484). For trial therapies, the VANISH trial compared vasopressin with norepinephrine and hydrocortisone with placebo, while LeoPARDS compared levosimendan with placebo. No specific doses or durations for these trial treatments are detailed, and the study found no detectable heterogeneity in treatment effect for norepinephrine, vasopressin, or levosimendan, noting they had no or minimal effect on circulating cytokines.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher concentrations observed in the 'high cytokine' cluster compared to the 'low cytokine' cluster.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Soluble receptor for TNF, can act as an anti-inflammatory modulator.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Sepsis patient classification via hierarchical cluster analysis in GAinS, VANISH, and LeoPARDS cohorts.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevation in the 'high cytokine' cluster is associated with features of more severe disease (higher heart rates, lower PaO2:FiO2 ratios, higher fluid and norepinephrine requirements) and higher 28-day mortality in sepsis patients, despite its anti-inflammatory potential.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the complex connection between chronic sleep disturbance (CSD) and cognitive progression in elderly individuals not living with dementia. It found that CSD significantly impacts cognitive function, increasing the risk of cognitive decline. Key findings indicate that activated neutrophil pathways are enriched in cognitively progressive CSD subjects, leading to increased blood neutrophil levels. High tau burden (t-tau and p-tau) mediates the influence of neutrophils on cognitive function, exacerbating CSD-related left hippocampal atrophy. Elevated CSF inflammatory factors (ICAM1, VCAM1, TNFR2, TGFβ1) were observed in cognitive progression associated with CSD, correlating with brain tau burden. The study concludes that activated neutrophil pathways triggering tau pathology likely underlie the mechanism of cognitive progression in CSD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chronic Sleep Disturbance (CSD)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study investigated Chronic Sleep Disturbance (CSD) as a condition in elderly individuals, classifying 784 participants into a normal sleep group (528) or a CSD group (256) based on the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI)-sleep subitem, defining CSD by 8 aspects including difficulty falling asleep and excessive daytime sleepiness, and also by self-reported sleep difficulties at baseline and at least twice during 6-month follow-up intervals over 14 years. CSD was treated as a chronic condition; no specific dose, duration, severity, or induction method for CSD was reported, nor were dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated levels observed. Higher levels in cognitively progressive subjects with CSD (adjusted p < 0.05). Significantly increased in CSF; levels correlated with CSF t-tau and p-tau.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Tumor necrosis factor receptor, involved in immune regulation, inflammation, and cell survival. A potent pro-inflammatory cytokine receptor mainly expressed in immune cells like neutrophils.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Cognitive progression of chronic sleep disturbance (CSD) in elderly subjects. Chronic Sleep Deprivation (CSD).
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with heightened inflammation and cognitive progression in CSD. Significantly associated with CSF p-tau and t-tau levels. Upregulation suggests activation of the neutrophil downstream pathway during cognitive progression; neutrophil-associated inflammatory cytokine that may induce synergistic neurotoxicity and exacerbate neurodegeneration.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates the molecular mechanisms of lung injury in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, including damage from viral, bacterial, oxidative stress, and cytokine factors. It highlights established and newly identified plasma biomarkers indicative of specific lung cell (Club, AT1, AT2, pan-epithelial, endothelial) and extracellular scaffold damage across various conditions like COVID-19, ARDS, COPD, and IPF. The review also discusses the limitations of individual biomarkers in predicting outcomes, emphasizing the enhanced predictive efficacy of combined biomarkers (e.g., ferritin and KL-6) and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven model to integrate diverse patient data for comprehensive lung injury monitoring, severity assessment, prognosis prediction, and personalized medicine.

treatment_details.therapy_type: A narrative review of lung injury mechanisms, biomarkers, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-directed lung injury evaluation and monitoring.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic intervention or dose was investigated; the document is a review of existing knowledge focusing on intrinsic pathological processes and biomarker responses. It proposes an AI-driven monitoring model, which involved analyzing diverse datasets including chest CT scans, biological pathways, and 13 blood biomarkers from 455 IPF patients, alongside demographic and clinical data. No specific dose comparisons for AI application were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma TNF- 1 levels in intensive care (ICU) patients with COVID-19 are higher than non-ICU patients; elevated levels.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Chemoattractant for neutrophils and eosinophils, boosts chemokine production, promotes vasodilation, induces apoptosis of epithelial and endothelial cells.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: ICU patients with COVID-19; ARDS, ILD, and COPD.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Facilitates inflammatory cell infiltration; associated with inflammatory roles; indicates lung inflammation and injury.

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety, efficacy, and immunologic/pulmonary responses of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy for COVID-19 associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found a favorable trend in mortality reduction (25% vs 43% in controls, not statistically significant), improved radiographic findings, and pulmonary function, with no serious adverse events and transient mild adverse events reported. The findings support the potential clinical consideration of MSC therapy for COVID-19 ARDS.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell (MSC) Therapy
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) were administered intravenously (n=115), intratracheally (n=1), or via central venous catheter (n=1) in 117 participants. Dosing varied from 1 to 10 million cells per kilogram of body weight, or uniform doses of 300 or 900 million cells, with infusion frequencies ranging from a single administration to 3-4 administrations. All MSCs were allogeneic from sources like bone marrow, umbilical cord, menstrual blood, or adipose tissue. No explicit dose-response or source comparisons were made. Follow-up ranged from 14 days to 5 years.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Systemic (inferred Blood/Serum from 'systemic changes' and 'inflammatory markers')

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Clear decreases within 5 days of MSC therapy; MSCs lead to decreased production of TNF-α.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, mediates inflammation and systemic inflammatory responses.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: MSC immunomodulatory activities and therapy for ARDS in COVID-19 patients.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased levels contribute to modulating the inflammatory milieu and cytokine correction, indicating a beneficial effect on immune dysregulation and reduced inflammation in ARDS.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study describes a multi-round Delphi expert consensus process to identify and prioritize 14 key biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies. The identified biomarkers encompass physiological, inflammatory, functional, and genetic/epigenetic domains. The study outlines the methodology, discusses the suitability of biomarkers for different intervention durations, and identifies future research needs regarding biomarker standardization and early life application, concluding with a preference for composite biomarkers due to the complexity of aging.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Expert consensus methodology (Delphi method) for identifying biomarkers of aging for use in human intervention studies (nutritional, lifestyle, or pharmacological).
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
The study utilized a 3-round online Delphi method, starting with 116 experts in Round 1 and concluding with 60 experts in Round 3, out of 460 invited international panel members. Consensus for statements was defined as ">=70%" agreement, with "51-69%" indicating moderate agreement and "

	<=50%" leading to removal. Initially, 460 biomarkers were suggested, leading to 20 being appraised in detail. The consensus level for the 14 recommended biomarkers ranged from 70% to 98%. The identified biomarkers were deemed more suitable for medium- (3-6 months) and long-term (">=6 months") interventions, and less suitable for acute or short-term ("<3 months") interventions, as short-term changes are likely homeostatic responses with limited long-term significance for aging. No specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons were investigated as this was a consensus-building study on biomarker utility.

matched_biomarker_details.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood Plasma/Serum (dry blood spot sampling also possible)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Attained "51-69%" agreement in expert panel consensus; however, suitability for field settings and minimal burden consensus was not met, and it did not meet the agreement threshold for predicting biological age better than chronological age.

matched_biomarker_details.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in systemic inflammation and mediating inflammation.
matched_biomarker_details.relevant_activity_context: Identified by expert consensus via Delphi method for use in human intervention studies on aging and for assessment of the aging process.
matched_biomarker_details.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory burden associated with aging. Its utility is limited by challenges in field testing, non-minimal burden, and its inability to predict biological age better than chronological age.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated cord blood LL37 levels in preterm neonates and their association with preterm complications, particularly bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Findings indicate that LL37 levels are lower in preterm infants compared to term neonates, positively correlate with gestational age, decrease after prenatal/antenatal steroid administration, and that higher cord blood LL37 acts as an independent protective factor against the development and severity of BPD, potentially mediated by its negative association with the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Prenatal steroid administration (investigated as a factor affecting LL37 levels)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Prenatal/antenatal steroid administration in preterm neonates was associated with decreased cord blood LL37 levels. No specific dosage, duration, or dose-response comparisons for the steroid treatment itself were reported in the context of its effect on LL37.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant correlations between TNF-a and LL37 level (R = 0.120, p = 0.230, n = 102). Measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review investigates the potential of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enclosed non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), piRNAs, circRNAs, and tsRNAs, along with N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, as stable, non-invasive diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring biomarkers for a wide range of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). These include metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD), Autoimmune Hepatitis (AIH), Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV), cholestatic liver diseases, liver fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). The document also touches upon the therapeutic potential of engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery in preclinical models to modulate inflammation and fibrosis pathways, highlighting their utility and associated challenges in clinical application.

treatment_details.therapy_type: This document primarily functions as a review investigating biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). While the main focus is on biomarker identification, the review also touches upon the therapeutic potential of Extracellular Vesicle (EV) therapy, including engineered EVs for targeted cargo delivery, and mentions pharmacological inhibition of miR-34a as a potential therapeutic strategy.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study does not report specific therapeutic doses or dose-response comparisons for most interventions, as its primary focus is on biomarker evaluation. However, preclinical models utilized various EV-based interventions, such as native and engineered EVs derived from mesenchymal/stromal stem cells (MSCs) or human liver stem cells in models of liver fibrosis, NASH, and cancer, without detailed quantitative dosing. In biomarker contexts, some observations included a dose-dependent increase in serum miR-122 and miR-192 levels in induced liver injury mouse models. Disease states and exposures examined for biomarker changes included acute and chronic alcohol consumption, autoimmune inflammation, viral infections, cholestasis, CCl4-induced liver fibrosis, lipotoxic palmitic acid treatment of hepatocytes, arsenite-induced liver fibrosis, and various human liver conditions including biliary cholangitis, biliary atresia, liver fibrosis, HCC, CCA, and GBC.

document_context_data.document_summary: This comprehensive review critically evaluates wet biomarkers for Huntington's Disease (HD), covering markers in biofluids like blood, urine, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. document_context_data.document_summary: The study investigated the effect of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction (ACLR) on individual quadriceps muscle thickness and circulating biomarkers related to muscle atrophy and hypertrophy in the early postoperative phase. It found severe atrophy in the vastus intermedius (VI) and significant reductions in other quadriceps muscle thicknesses (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Medialis Obliquus). Circulating IGF-1 levels were significantly reduced, while myostatin levels showed a slight increase with a medium effect size, contributing to the observed muscle atrophy.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of Montmorency tart cherry concentrate (MC) supplementation on recovery markers, including functional performance, muscle soreness, inflammation, muscle damage, and oxidative stress, in semi-professional male soccer players following prolonged, intermittent sprint activity. Findings suggest MC supplementation accelerates functional performance recovery (MVIC, CMJ, agility, 20m sprint), reduces muscle soreness (DOMS), and attenuates the acute inflammatory response (IL-6), but showed no significant effect on general muscle damage (CK) or oxidative stress (LOOH).

document_context_data.document_summary: This systematic review evaluates the effects of soy protein (SP) supplementation on muscle adaptations, metabolic and antioxidant status, hormonal response, and exercise performance in active individuals and athletes, often comparing it to whey protein or placebo. The review encompasses studies on protein synthesis, amino acid transport, and signaling pathways, highlighting that while some anabolic markers might be less favorable with soy, it can provide similar increases in lean mass to whey protein, especially at optimal protein intakes. SP is shown to reduce exercise-induced metabolic/blood circulating biomarkers (triglycerides, uric acid, lactate) and improve antioxidant capacity, reducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. However, its effects on hormonal responses, such as testosterone and cortisol, are inconsistent or contradictory across studies. SP supplementation also demonstrates potential benefits in improving various exercise performance indicators, including high-intensity running, maximal cardiac output, delaying fatigue, improving isometric strength, running velocity, and muscle recovery after damage. The review concludes that SP can be a viable alternative to conventional protein supplements, but emphasizes the need for further research addressing methodological limitations and consistent dosing.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Soy Protein and Soy Peptide Supplementation
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The review encompassed a wide range of soy protein (SP) and soy peptide supplementation protocols, from acute doses (e.g., 15-20g SP, 18g SP beverage, 10g essential amino acids from soy) to chronic daily intakes varying from 0.5 g/kg BW/day to 90 g/day (e.g., 33-40 g/day, 1 g/kg BW/day, 53.3 g/day). Doses were often combined with carbohydrates (e.g., 10g soy peptide + 30g sugar, 15g SP + 52.5g CHO) or matched for nitrogen/leucine content for comparison with whey protein. Durations ranged from single acute sessions to long-term interventions of 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 6 weeks, 9 weeks, 4 months, or even "12 weeks. Comparisons were consistently made against whey protein, soy-dairy blends, isoenergetic placebos, or control (exercise-only) groups. While some studies aimed for optimal protein intakes ("  1.6 g/kg BW/day), there was a notable lack of consistent dosing or explicit dose-response comparisons across the reviewed literature, indicating significant variability in intervention designs.

document_context_data.document_summary: This narrative review investigates current and potential blood and urine biomarkers for osteoarthritis (OA), focusing on markers derived from type II collagen and aggrecan to reflect joint tissue turnover. The review details their molecular targets, measurement methods, and diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic utility in assessing cartilage degradation, bone turnover, and disease progression, including responses to treatments. It highlights both established and preclinical markers, emphasizing the complexities of cleavage sites, the need for multi-protease inhibition strategies, and further biomarker validation, while noting a continued lack of operationalized in vitro diagnostics and markers for patient endotyping.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Osteoarthritis (OA) biomarker investigation, Doxycycline treatment, Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT), Cathepsin K inhibition, Collagen hydrolysate supplementation, Fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF-18) induced remodeling
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No specific therapeutic dose or intervention protocols are primarily reported, as this is a narrative review focusing on biomarkers for Osteoarthritis and their utility in drug development and patient management. However, some treatments were mentioned: Doxycycline was investigated in a randomized controlled trial in 120 obese knee OA patients (specific dose/duration not detailed). Oral salmon calcitonin (sCT) was examined for its effect on knee OA patients (specific dose not detailed). Cathepsin K inhibition reduced CTX-I by more than 90% (specific inhibitor dose/duration not reported). Collagen hydrolysate administration led to a modest decrease in CS846 and an elevation in PIIANP (specific dose/duration not reported). No dose-response comparisons were generally reported.

document_context_data.document_summary: The study describes the development and validation of hsPRO-C2, a novel high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescence immunoassay for PIIBNP (N-terminal propeptide of type IIB collagen), as a biomarker for type II collagen formation. It characterizes an antibody targeting PIIBNP and evaluates hsPRO-C2's utility by investigating PIIBNP levels in human osteoarthritic cartilage explants treated with anabolic growth factors (IGF-1, sprifermin) and comparing serum PIIBNP concentrations between healthy subjects and various patient cohorts (knee OA, pediatric, rheumatoid arthritis). The findings suggest that hsPRO-C2 effectively reflects cartilage formation, shows different biological and clinical patterns than PIIANP, responds strongly to chondro-anabolic molecules, and is significantly lower in knee OA patients, indicating its potential as a promising biomarker capable of differentiating OA patients and assessing DMOAD efficacy.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Chondro-anabolic treatment (IGF-1 and sprifermin) in human cartilage explants and comparative analysis of patient cohorts.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human osteoarthritis cartilage explants were cultured ex vivo and treated with anabolic growth factors: insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) at 100 ng/mL and recombinant human fibroblast growth factor 18 (rhFGF-18 or sprifermin) at 900 ng/mL, or vehicle, for up to ten weeks. PIIBNP levels increased 2 to 7-fold time-dependently in response to IGF-1, and significantly increased with sprifermin by day 70. No dose-response comparisons for growth factors were reported. Additionally, serum samples from cross-sectional cohorts including healthy controls, knee osteoarthritis (KL0/1 vs KL2/3/4), pediatric, and rheumatoid arthritis patients were analyzed for biomarker levels, which constituted a comparative analysis rather than a 'dose' intervention.

document_context_data.document_summary: This is an observational prospective study protocol investigating the association between loneliness, psychosocial stressors, systemic inflammation, and wound healing in older adults with chronic venous leg ulcers (CVLUs). The study aims to identify and characterize a specific biomarker profile, particularly inflammatory genes and the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity (CTRA) pathway, by comparing lonely versus non-lonely patients undergoing standard wound care over a 2-3 month period, with measurements taken at 3 time points. The ultimate goal is to enhance understanding of molecular mechanisms and develop a biopsychosocial prognostic indicator for healing potential in chronic wounds.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study during standard wound treatment for Chronic Venous Leg Ulcers (CVLUs).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients will undergo 4 weeks to 3 months of standard wound treatment, with measurements at 3 time points. Treatment levels are characterized based on wound severity: Level 1 (Grade 3 wounds) includes high compression (> 40 mmHg), debridement, antibiotics, skin substitutes, and hyperbaric oxygenation. Level 2 (Grade 2 wounds) involves moderate compression (30–40 mmHg), exudate management, and enzymatic debridement. Level 3 (Grade 1 wounds) consists of moderate compression and a moist healing environment. These treatments are applied as part of evidenced-based care and will be accounted for as covariates in the analyses; however, no specific dose-response relationships or interventions are being investigated as this is an observational study.

document_context_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the clinical relevance and efficacy of collagen X breakdown product (CXM) as a blood-based biomarker for endochondral long bone fracture repair in both healthy individuals and patients with tibia or femur fractures. It characterized CXM expression patterns, stability across demographics (age, sex), correlation with other bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, osteocalcin, leptin, sclerostin), and its utility in predicting healing prognosis (early, normal, delayed). The findings showed CXM levels are low in healthy individuals, peak around 25-35 days post-fracture, can be reliably measured via dried blood spots, and offer an earlier, quantitative indication of healing compared to traditional radiographic methods, supporting its prospective use in fracture studies.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of natural long bone fracture repair, with a secondary analysis of a Vitamin D3 supplementation trial (VitaShock).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on observing biomarker changes in patients with acute closed or low-grade open tibial or femoral shaft fractures (Gustilo type I or II, AO/OTA type 42), without applying a specific therapeutic dose as an intervention. For the secondary analysis of the VitaShock trial, multiple Vitamin D3 dosing strategies were assessed, but specific dose details were not provided, and no significant difference in CXM response was found compared to placebo. Longitudinal blood samples were collected at various standard-of-care clinical visits over a period up to 48 weeks post-fracture.
